title: Excellent add on for my GoPro's
text:

title: Battery Life Declined after a Few Months
text:
The Golf Buddy watch had performed very well through several months of use. It automatically detected every course and changes to the next hole well without needing my prompting. The color screen is clear and easy to read. The battery lasts through multiple rounds. It takes a little learning to understand how to move through screens, but nothing too hard really. I like the fact that it's a watch and I don't have to worry about losing it, which is the case with handheld and clip-on devices. From what I can tell, it's accurate. Readings have pretty much been in line with course markings. I bought it on sale during the Amazon Prime days and I'd say it's a good deal overall.

Update: After using the watch for another dozen or so rounds of golf, it continues to perform very well overall. The distances are accurate, the screen is easy to read even in bright sunlight and the battery life has been good. Usually, after 18 holes, it is at about 50% power. I have to admit, I don't understand the negative reviews, unless there are some clunker units out there. I'm not sure what people's expectations are for this kind of device; it performs the way one would expect.

Update 2: After using the device for a few months, the battery life has declined. Now, the watch barely makes it through nine holes before it is out; it is disappointing. The unit had performed so well before that. I'm not sure what the problem is exactly, but a GPS unit that does not make it more than 9-10 holes is unacceptable, especially given it's only a few months old. Given this, I would not recommend this unit.

title: Look out Garmin, this watch is amazing.
text:
I own the original Stratos and thought it was a good value. Unfortunately water must have penetrated the shell and affected its functionality. I started looking at more expensive watches thinking they must be better. Now, I am a triathlete but not at the level of an Ironman. I do appreciate a good sports watch to track my stats but I don’t want to spend a fortune to do so.

My biggest complaint with so many of these other watches is that I have to flip my wrist to see my stats. That is a major pain when riding a Tri-bike. An always on display was one of the main reasons I bought the Stratos to begin with. However, the original Stratos struggled in a few areas. I was not impressed the heart rate monitoring. The GPS was not very accurate. It also took too long to connect to the satellites. And it rarely stayed connected to my iPhone.

After reading reviews and looking at the features of the top rated watches i strugggled to pick the right watch. Then I found the Stratos 3. I wasn’t sure if it would be an improvement but for the price I had to give it a try. And I am so glad I did.

This is the best watch. The accuracy of the GPS is spot on. The heart rate measuring is much improved and the time it takes to locate the satellites is much shorter. I am so impressed with this new version. The battery life is fantastic. And thank you for keeping the always on feature. The watch also stays connected to my phone without having to reset it.

For the price you cannot go wrong. It does everything a watch 3 times the cost does and you can play your music from it so you don’t need your phone to go on a run and listen to music.

Just to be clear, I was not paid for this review. I don’t submit a lot of reviews but felt this product deserved it.

title: Okay RGB fans with fair amount of airflow for the price.  Feels compromised on build quality
text:
Comparing 3 x RGB fans Kit under $50 with good airflow (spec-wise).

The contenders are,
Pccooler Dawn Series 3M120HALO LED RGB
Cooler Master SickleFlow 120 V2 ARGB
ID Cooling XF-12025-RGB-TRIO-SNOW

Build Quality Ranking: Cooler Master > ID Cooling >>> Pccooler

Pccooler feels much cheaper in build quality compared to other two.
Cooler Master comes sleeved in white which is a nice touch. It does come with extenders which are black
ID Cooling doesn't provide sleeved cables while Pccooler is sleeved.

Airflow Ranking: Cooler Master > ID Cooling >> Pccooler
Pccooler Dawn Series 3M120HALO LED RGB is rated for a Max. Air flow of 72 CFM @ 2000 RPM
Cooler Master SickleFlow 120 V2 ARGB is rated for a Max. Air flow of 62 CFM max @ 1800 RPM
ID Cooling XF-12025-RGB-TRIO-SNOW is rated for a Max. Air flow of 74.5 CFM @ 1800 RPM

Test Method
I measured the air flow in m/s and used a calculator to do the conversion with radius of 60 mm.
An anemometer was used to measure air flow at approx. 8 inch distance from the fans.
Fans were set to max speed in BIOS.

Test Results
Pccooler CFM 36.0, RPM 2000. Cooler Master CFM 50.3, RPM 1800 and ID Cooling results: CFM 45.5, RPM 1800.
The results were a bit surprising as I expected the ID cooling to have good airflow. It seems like both
Pccooler and ID cooling are exaggerating the air flow numbers. The lowest spec Cooler Master with 62 CFM
actually turned out the winner in air flow test.

RGB intensity Ranking: Cooler Master > Pccooler >>> ID Cooling
ID Cooling utilizes a 12v RGB connector and supports changing modes using an included IR remote.
Pccooler and CM both utilize 5v ARGB headers to support RGB lighting.

ID cooling feels fairly dull in comparison to other two.
Colors are not as accurate as compared to other two either. Perhaps that's due to 12v RGB. I ain't sure about it.

Noise Ranking (spec wise): Cooler Master > Pccooler >> ID Cooling

Summary:
Overall the Cooler Master wins in all categories for me so that one's a keeper.
If you need RGB fans under $50 with good airflow go with the Sickleflow V2.

title: Best VR180 consumer camera, especially for audio
text:
I would like to correct some of the information in other reviews as well as add some of my own observations.

I'm not a "Verified Purchase" because I got mine directly from Vuze on or near day one; I do own it - I've attached some photos as proof, and one of them isn't on portrait mode because I noticed the others looked Photoshopped. If you look, you'll see that I have it on an Insta360 tripod. I own the Insta360 One X as well as the Insta360 EVO (and the KanDao Qoocam, the GoPro Fusion, a Lucid model, and a few others). I've used a number of the options on the market, and I know their pros and cons. I'd be happy to answer questions.

As a preface: if you're looking for the best 360 (as opposed to VR180) camera for your dollar, it's the One X. Period. It is better in every way (as a 360 camera) compared to the Vuze XR except for audio recording. The apps are better, the features are better, it's more portable, and so on.

However, if you want to do VR180 videos, the Vuze XR is the one to get. The only other option out there with the same resolution in this price range is the Insta360 EVO, which is a complete miss - that one is just an enormous pain to set up. The hinged mechanism is a bad design. The mics are mediocre. Don’t get me wrong - it takes decent video, but it’s awkward.

The key win for the Vuze, for me, is the audio. I have some public videos on YouTube that demonstrate what I mean; I’d post them here but Amazon does not yet handle VR180 content. Look up “Epcot Fireworks, NYE December 31, 2018 (VR180)” and you should find it. Set the resolution as high as your computer will allow. Note that this is VR180, so you’ll view it best with VR goggles, Google Cardboard, or the like, but you can watch it on a computer or smartphone. Now, to be clear: that video is of fireworks, which consumer grade cameras are terrible at recording. The Vuze isn’t any better. But… put on headphones and listen to the finale (around 20:15). It’s amazing.

Now search for my video titled "Epcot Fireworks NYE December 31, 2018 (360 Video)” - that was recorded on the One X. Listen to the finale there, too (around 19:30 - I started that camera earlier). There’s just no comparison (again: be sure to use decent headphones). Bottom line: the audio on the Vuze VR is just absolutely better than that of the One X.

I have other videos, usually noted as “VR180 Ambient”, that show off some daytime capabilities of the camera. It’s a really good VR180 camera. Photos are great, too. All the uploaded videos were recorded with one of the first couple of firmware revisions, since they were done just weeks after the camera came out, and they still turned out well.

As far as ease of use: as mentioned above, this isn’t top-of-the-line for 360 video. It’s capable, but the One X wins unless you’re concerned mainly about audio. However, for VR180, it couldn’t be easier. One button pops it open into 180 mode. Another toggles video/photo. Another toggles play/stop. There are icons indicating what it’s doing, although they can get washed out in bright light. Since it’s a VR180 camera (at least when in that mode), you’ve not going to want to move it around. You’re going to want to put it on a tripod and leave it in one place while you record, or else viewers will get motion sickness. So, it lends itself well to manual usage. If you want to hold it, that loop by the lenses is great for making sure your fingers aren’t in the shot.

The apps are OK (iOS and Android). Somewhat of a pain, but not too bad. Insta360 wins here, too, but it’s not like Vuze apps are unusable. Just more of a hassle.

The macOS/Windows apps are also OK but not great. They are completely free, unlike what some have said. They’re slow, but encoding VR180 is inherently slow. Insta360 does a bit better here, but it’s not fantastic, either. Basically, you’re going to decide what you want to upload, then you’ll trim it, then you’ll go away for a (long) while when it processes.

Battery life isn’t great, but it’ll record while being charged - my fireworks video clearly shows it’ll record at least 20 minutes, but I’ve done about 45 without issue (but with a battery connected). You’re unlikely to want to record more than that, continuously, very often anyway.

The hardware “feel” is excellent - this feels like a better camera than the Insta360 line.

Overall: if you don’t want to do VR180, don’t get this. But if you do, this is a great camera. Yeah, it’s not perfect, but it’ll get the shot, and you’ll be able to export it. Be sure to keep the camera still while recording (learned that the hard way), and get fairly close if you can.

title: Maybe I got a dud, but the dye in these runs everywhere if you wet them.
text:
I'm very scent-allergic, and naturally when unwrapping the cloths they smelled like turpentine and brimstone, as do most cloth products these days. No biggie, I washed them off very gently in neutral-temperature water with an incredibly small amount of detergent. Lo and behold, my hands were turning black like they were running with newspaper ink! I've cleaned microfiber cloths before, I'm not a *complete* idiot, and I've never been covered in dye at the slightest provocation. Indeed, I discovered that if I get one just generally wet no-soap, the dye starts running a bit. It doesn't have to be sopping wet, more than a few drops but not drenched, and you'll get dye running. At least I do.

I got these to clean off things that are literally 1,000 times more expensive than them, and I shouldn't have tried to save money this way. I strongly recommend not to use them for cleaning off delicate camera lenses, screens, and so on. If these cloths are just a slightly better replacement for paper towels for you, then go with god and may your life be filled with gladness. But for me, they weren't just inadequate, they were outright dangerous and I went back to a much smaller set I'd gotten from Japan that are right and silky and don't run.

Again, your mileage may very, but give these a thorough test before using them on anything the price of a small car. I suppose that goes without saying, but I figured that a cloth is a cloth. All my equipment is OK, I caught it in time, how could I not? The manufacture quality was so bad that I was a bit shocked.

title: I love this new 4K Roku TV!
text:
While I initially thought 43" was a bit wider than I wanted, I bought this one because it offered 4K with HDR and ARC, which I thought would be a nice upgrade for not that much more money. I can happily say, I love this TV! The picture is crystal clear when playing higher resolution films, the colors and tint are entirely customizable, the ARC feature is a nice touch so that you can control your TV volume from the stereo by plugging in a ARC HDMI cable into the ARC port on the TV and the other end into the stereo. I used to have a "smart" HDTV, but Roku is soooo much better! It is like having cable without having to pay for it, but also having the option to buy a service with a range or channels (via one of the apps) or buying individual cable channels to watch, so it accommodates your interests in both ways. There are a few preset color/tint profiles like "Sports", "Movies," etc for you to start with, and customize, so you can just switch profile when switching venue, like when you play a dvd vs watching sports. One thing to keep in mind is that if you are playing old movies (for example) on this, then you will not really see the quality resolution as much, because it doesn't improve what isn't there. Another note, you really need high speed internet, like Cable or Fiber Optic to be able to stream in 4K. The HDR feature adds deeper/truer colors/tints to the screen image and really makes movies look more real, and not so dark or blue as often comes across on televisions. All I can say, is I would by anther Roku again, perhaps even this brand. This has been a great viewing experience! Thank you so much for making it affordable!

The TV has a USB port which can be used to either boost reception for an anttena for more remote areas or to plug in a jump drive to use in various ways. One way the USB port can be used is to enable an ability to pause or replay local tv. To activate this, you just press oause while watching tv and a menu pops up called 'Live TV Pause' and it walks you through how to set it up.

Alternatively, if you saw something on the local TV that was in progress and you wanted to watch it from the beginning, you just press star button on the remote and the Roku will list all of the channel apps you have that have it available and whether or not they are free. Just select the channel you want, and it immediately begins to play from the beginning.

Another aspect I found intesresting is that when I was binge watching a tv series and letting one episode autoplay after another, the TV actually paused and printed on the screen "Are you still there?" I guess to make sure I hadn't fallen asleep or walked away.

With a Roku, you have access to hundreds of apps to download, some free, some not. Some of these apps include: Prime Video (you have to be a Amazon Prime member), Vudu or Movies Anywhere (free access to ultraviolet movies you own on the cloud), Hoopla (free with a library account), Netflix (small monthly fee), popcornflix (free), Tubi (free), Crackle (free)" Redbox (movie rentals), Google Play Movies and TV (rent or buy movies), PBS (free), The CW (free), CW Seed (free), the Roku Channel (free), local news channels (typically free). Weather channels (typically free), sports channels typically not free), Philo (free), Fawesome (free), Filmrise (free), CCN (Classic Conedy Network) (free), AFV (America's Funniest Home Videos) (free), premium cable like STARZ or HBO (for a low monthly fee), Hulu (for a monthly fee), Sling (Rent and on demand TV from popular channels), YouTube TV (live TV with DVR storage for a monthly fee), learning apps (like TED, the Great Courses, Lynda.com, and apps to learn languages, investing, or science), history apps (like All Roads Lead to Rome, Wow I Never Knew That!), You Tube (free), Amazon Music (free music streaming app requires Amazon account, can stream Prime Music free or buy songs or play songs you own), Spotify (free music streaming), Crunchyroll (monthly fee for Anime), yoga, exercise, nutition and health apps, classic film apps (black and white), etc. Basically, there are a good variety of apps to cover things you might be interested in.

The TV was delivered fairly quickly and was undamaged. The package was surprisingly light, for it's wide bulk, and as with all new flat screen TVs, you have to be delicate with it when removing it from the box, placing it face down, and attaching its feet to avoid damaging the tube part of the screen. With large TVs like this one, it is recommended that you have two people to remove the TV from the box for setup.

title: Not a full zip-around, but great for intraday use
text:
I’ve owned many different kinds of travel backpacks. Although my luggage collection tends to be quite nice, my travel backpacks tend to be of the lower-end variety. I’ve heard great things about this brand, so I decided to give this a try. Here are some thoughts after a few daily uses along with a short weekend trip:

• Size: This is labeled as a large backpack. While it is certainly long and wide enough to fit a 15.6” laptop, the depth is not quite what I imagined as it is built to be a little flatter than most large backpacks.

• Pockets/Compartments: This is a fairly simple backpack when it comes to pockets/compartments. The front contains just one compartment. While it may seem that the front pocket extends to the bottom of the bag, it actually only goes about 6” down, so it’s designed to hold smaller items only. The interior has a three layers of “stacked” compartments. As shown in the pictures, the largest slot comfortably fits the 15.6” laptop while the middle slot can fit an iPad 7 that has a fairly bulky keyboard case on it. The smallest of the three slots contains a zipper that opens into a half closed / half mesh pocket. Lastly, there is a small slot opposite the mesh, along with the rest of the bag to hold additional items. As noted above, this is slightly on the flatter end though it does comfortably fit my two computers, travel headphones, and rolled up lightweight jacket.

My only complaint with the design is that this is not a full zip-around. This is because one side has a sleeve to hold a water bottle. To be honest, I would have preferred the traditional side compartment and kept the full zip-around in order to make it easier to organize the interior contents.

• Comfort and Look: On the contrary, this is perhaps my favorite aspect of the bag. I got the Stargazer Blue and absolutely love the color. It just screams “chic”! This is also very comfortable when worn, as the shoulder straps and back of the bag are very well-padded.

• Durability: As noted, this is well-padded and made of a solid polyester fabric material. As I intend to wear this for walks to/from the office and daytrips, I believe this should hold up just fine.

In summary, I love the color and comfort. I’m not a huge fan of the water bottle slot because it prevents the full zip-around, but I support I can live with it. It’s not quite as deep of a bag as I would prefer for weekend trips, but I believe this is a great size from intraday use. If that fits your needs, go ahead and give it a try!

It feels like all the subconscious techniques I've been using since childhood just flowed so much better with this on. And I didn't even realize they hadn't been doing that before! title: Premium Sound Quality -- Basic Feature Set
text:
4-star audio quality but 3-stars for missing features found in this price range. Well balanced neutral audio. Good soundstage. Good fit but they stick out more than most earphones and have sharp edges. Glossy touch controls work as advertised but easy to activate when reseating earphones. Very good audio quality at expense of features found on similar priced earphones. Earphone case is "boxy", slick and slippery for ease of putting into pockets. Earbuds drop into charger magnetically for secure charging. USB-C and battery/reset button on back. Matches Jabra cases in size and feel. Right earbud is master and connects to the left. Using a single bud for a call or any other reason requires the right earbud.

Sound quality slightly better than Jabra Elite 65 and 75 models. Sound quality slightly better than AirPod Pros at similar price but lack active noise cancellation, transparency mode, adaptive EQ, ability to connect two sets of earphones for simultaneous playback, and auto pairing with Apple products. Good clarity and details in most types of music. Warm sound stage that is easy to listen to. Mids sometimes lack emphasis. However I find these a very good earphone if audio performance is your priority.

Initially earphones would not pair with my iPhone XS. Had to reset with back button then they paired and stayed paired in later use. Smart Control App took 30 minutes to update firmware. App has several good functions for earphone adjustments and control. Equalizer has two modes. One is basic with bass, mid, and treble adjustments. Other mode has some sort of graph adjustment which I never figured out.

In summary, you get premium sound quality in an otherwise mid-range earphone. Especially so since so many reputable audio companies are in this arena with more feature packed earphones. If Sennheiser knocks $30-$40 off their price or you can find them discounted these would be a good value.

Pros:
- Premium Sound Quality (large 7mm drivers; neutral, balanced, open soundstage, high clarity across frequency range)
- Touch Controls Can be Customized (volume control available on the earbuds)
- Smart App for firmware updates, control customization, EQ, earphone on/off, and more. Not required but useful
- Good battery life at about 6-7 hours which I achieved (with case about 20 hrs total advertised)
- Earbuds held in case magnetically (easy to put in and stay in to ensure they charge correctly)
- Okay for making phone calls
- Can get a tight seal for great sound
- SBC, AAC, and AptX codecs, Bluetooth 5.1 supported
- Once paired to iPhone XS they stay paired, re-pair automatically, and work over long distance

Cons:
- Lacks Features of other earphones in same price range
- No Active Noise Cancellation (passive noise reduction only)
- No Transparency Mode (Ambient/Hear Through Mode)
- No Wireless Charging (USB-C wired charging only)
- No Auto pause when you remove earbud
- Earbuds are large, somewhat heavy, and stick out (with sharp edges). Required twisting and pushing firmly into ear to get good fit.
- Touch/tap controls on earbuds easy to mistakenly engage when reseating earbuds in ear
- Not water resistant (at least not listed anywhere I could find)
- Can't figure out how to power off earbuds without putting into case or using on/off in Smart App

title: This is the best sub-$100 class-D amp I've tested
text:
If you're looking for a desktop amp, you're likely in awe of the glut of cheap Chinese chip amps. I did a lot of research and purchased several of them, as well as a dedicated high-quality bluetooth receiver to compare audio quality against. Remember that you're looking at very low-cost desktop chip amps powering 8Ω speakers -- this isn't going to be in the same ballpark of quality of traditional analog amps. If your expectations are adjusted, you'll love this little guy.

1. Connectivity

Bluetooth: It's hard to find a bluetooth amp under 100 bucks with aptX HD. This is a big selling point. Qualcomm's aptX HD codec gets you a high-enough bitrate that using bluetooth instead of a wired connection can actually get you decent results. When it is stable, the sound quality is quite good without noticeable latency or syncing issues when paired with videos. I did notice with this receiver that the bluetooth connection seemed to suffer from some occasional crackles. I'm wondering if there's interference coming into play. I'm close to docking a star for the interference, but I have to determine if it's something in my setup first. I'll try to update when I have a better sense of the issue. UPDATE: I purchased a second unit and this one is not having the same problem with bluetooth signal drops. I'm happy to report that it's working perfectly.

Aux in (3.5mm jack): sounded great plugged into my turntable (with pre-amp). No hiss or notable issues to speak of.

Noe that when bluetooth connects, it takes precedence over line-in. There's no switch to choose inputs.

RCA/Optical/Coax: I didn't realize this when purchasing the unit, but these connections are all *outputs*, not inputs. The only inputs to the amp are bluetooth and 3.5mm. I haven't tested the output ports.

2. Audio quality

As an amplifier it does the job well. I'm not sure what chips they're using, but there's no noticeable clipping or distortion at 50-70% volume and it's plenty loud. The sound is warm and clean, not overly processed-sounding. I didn't notice any issues with hissing until I got up to 90%+ volume; at lower volumes, I couldn't detect anything. I'm pretty sure the amp can deliver the 50Wx2 on the box.

3. Controls

The plastic bass and treble knobs provide some ability to dial in the sound, though their effects are not as prominent as I've heard in some other amps. There's an impossible-to-see small circle on each dial to indicate where it is set. I would've liked to see painted lines. That said, all three knobs have a nice click of resistance when you get to the 50% setting, which helps you orient yourself without even looking at them. I noticed a slight lag to the effect of moving the knobs, which I later realized is due to the fact that the controls seem to make changes in "steps" rather than a linearly.

-

Overall, I'm quite happy with the quality of this unit, especially considering its cost. You're just not going to get better sound from your bluetooth devices to your speakers for under $100.

title: Decent Budget Unit
text:
I was looking for an Android Auto capable multimedia head unit to put in my 17 year old truck. I also didn't want to spend over $250. This unit meets all of my expectations, which were fairly low. There are some issues with it, but it will be fine. First, the good;

- Looks nice installed. Fits in the location well, almost looks OEM.
-All functions work and are not glitchy. Android auto loads up, Bluetooth maintains a solid connection.
-Sound quality is better than the OEM Head unit I replaced.

The install was straight forward. One connection was to the parking brake signal, which is required to open up Android Auto. I learned on some forums that you can connect this wire to ground, and circumvent this restriction. Much more user friendly, and easier than splicing into some obscure wire under the dash. All the wires were clearly labeled on the harness, although the directions had some of the colors wrong on the camera hookup. Not a big deal, just not very good directions.

The bad...

- The screen frequently looks washed out. The mounting location on my truck (2003 Toyota Tacoma) is lower than ideal, which accounts for some of this issue, but it is still a bit washed out when I look at it straight on. This is most apparent when using Android Auto, and not so much when using the home screen for the unit. This makes using Google Maps almost impossible, as you cannot see the map at all. Waze displays much better because the map has more contrast to it, especially in night mode. The backup camera also looks washed out, but (barely) adequate.

- Minimal adjustment options for the display on the settings for the HU. Increasing contrast may help this display's functionality, but you only get an adjustment for brightness.

- USB plug in is not on the unit itself. It is a cord emerges from behind the unit.

All in all, it is a decent unit for the money. It does what I wanted it to do without bugs.

title: Perfect little alarm clock with modern features
text:
Hello, I highly recommend this alarm clock for its quality and modern features. I found this product while looking for a small alarm clock that would not take up too much time on my nightstand. What I didn't expect was all of the advanced features in such a small package. These are the features I really like:
1. Unlike my iPhone, the time always shows in big numbers that I can see from across the room.
2. It has 2 USB ports which I use to charge my phone and my fit bit at the same time.
3. It has a battery backup - AAA batteries which I have plenty of. Not those dang button batteries which don't last.
4. It is super easy to set the time and the two alarms using the silver round dial on top. I have one alarm set for the work week and one for the weekend to get me up and to the gym.
5. MY ABSOLUTE FAVORITE FEATURE - Is the sound quality of the alarms themselves. You can wake up to an alarm, or there are much more pleasant alarms - birds singing, ocean waves, spa-type music, and a few more. I wake up to the birds which start off soft on a low volume and get increasingly louder until you turn it off. For such a little clock, I am amazed at the quality of the sounds that come out of it. The birds and the ocean sounds are so crisp and clear, it is a pleasure to wake up to.

So, while I used to use my phone as an alarm clock, I am a definite convert. I don't have to worry about this clock having enough charge or losing it. And I can keep an eye one the time as I get ready without having to unlock my homescreen. I went ahead and bought another for my teenage daughter who was reluctant at first, but like me, now wakes up to birds chirping every morning.

This clock has more features (FM radio, ambient temperature reading, etc.), I'm just writing about the ones I like. BTW, no one is paying me to do this. I just appreciate this product that much.

title: Soooo Close.
text:
I wanted to love this tablet so so bad, but It falls just short. Today the market is oversaturated with crappy tablets that you can get for next to nothing. It seems like every company out there had to stick their fingers in the tablet market. Examples being, RCA, Polaroid, Packard Bell, and the laughable ONN. All which should've never seen the light of day. So when I was looking at the Black Friday deals on amazon, and first noticed a 10 inch HD tablet for $100?!?! I knew one of two things, it was either going to be a solid "MEH" or a good tablet.. Here is what I think....

First I want to talk about the things I liked.
-The screen is sharp, crisp and clear. I have watched numerous shows, and movies on it and it has worked better than I thought it would.
-Sound quality is great, again for being a $150 (regular price) tablet with sound quality like that, is very very good.
-Processor speed is very good for the price, and it seems to respond very well. I did notice some slow down when I was running a couple apps at once.

Dislikes.
-Speaker location. Both speakers, on the same side, can make the sound muffled with you have it propped in a case or leaning against something.
-Ram. The tablet itself could use maybe one more gig of ram, that would help greatly. With the overall speed and responsiveness of the tablet itself.
-The biggest downfall, beyond so many things is the OS itself. The tablet runs on some janky version of Android, which you would think would be great however, No Google Play. That is the largest downfall that this tablet has and its quite a significant one as well. If Google, and Amazon could make nice and make the Play Store available, this tablet would easily be a 5/5. Until then I sadly have to give it a 2/5. It's just hard for me to give it anymore than that.

If you are on a budget but want a good HD screen, and you won't miss the Google Play store, then this is definitely the tablet for you. If you are someone who needs HD display, Great sound, And the Play store, I recommend going after a good Samsung tablet.

title: Dropped The Connection Twice Within One Week of Receiving It
text:
I take it as a bad sign when a device simply stops working, and this router simply stopped working twice over a one week period. No power failure, no service failure, just a router failure. The signal dropped and a red light lit up on the panel. Once might have bee a fluke, but twice means it's going back.

Remember that any router (or any electronic device) built "by" any company is composed of hundreds of parts that come from different vendors at different times and may be put together at any factory in China and nobody has any real quality control over any step of the process. Check the history of failures on reviews like these for the best prediction of future performance.

I am going to try another TP-Link model that has a lower rate of less-than-5-star reviews, if only because the price is so much better. I'll update this if that one fails also.

title: Honestly Comparable to my Edifiers
text:
I am actually blown away by these speakers. As I pulled them out of the box, I immediately saw that they were fashioned to look a lot like Edifier speakers, just a little smaller. The remote is the exact same shape and size as my Edifier remote, but it has a few more options on it to further control these speakers, further proving Edifier was their benchmark, so I had high hopes for them.

Problems began once I pulled the grill off them, though. As soon as I saw the speaker and tweeter, I was convinced they'd sound like trash compared to my Edifiers because the tweeter was of 'obviously' inferior quality, and the speaker cone was also not nearly as quality looking as my Edifier's. To really put the last nail in their coffin, the power brick is directly attached to the plug, which wouldn't be a big deal if it weren't huge and made of super flimsy feeling plastic. I was wholly convinced these would be garbage, if I'm honest.

Boy was I surprised when I got them hooked up and playing my music! My only remaining complaints after hearing them is the plug thing, and that Bluetooth was a little too easy to connect in my opinion. There needs to be some security keeping my neighbors from connecting to them, but there isn't. Anyone within range can connect and take over what's being played. This is their only real drawback, though. Considering their sound and that they come with Bluetooth at all I'm forgiving them and not taking stars off for them.

The 'cheery' (I'm sure they misspelled cherry) wood is nice looking, and the grills compliment the look. The knobs are recessed into the right side of the right speaker, exactly like my Edifiers, and are of high quality. The speakers put out really good sound for their compact size. They actually have more bass than my Edifiers, and the only real advantage the Edifiers have is they're a little less tinny (but honestly only a little bit) and they look much better with the grills off, which I don't take off because it leaves your cones exposed to dust and damage, so that's not an advantage in my case.

For what these cost, ~$35 less than the Edifier R1280T's to which I'm comparing them, they come with Bluetooth which the more expensive Edifiers don't have and sound almost as good, possibly better depending on your priorities. I have to say, I'm very impressed with them for the price.

title: Recommended: Two successful transfers in two days
text: This is not the cheapest USB to SATA transfer cable you can buy. If you look, you can get just a cable for maybe ten or even fifteen dollars less. The difference is the Apricorn software. I used this kit to transfer Windows 10 systems on my laptop and my wife's laptop to Samsung SSDs. Samsung provides its own transfer software and I now have a comparison. On my laptop, I transferred the contents of a 1 Terabyte hard disk to a 1 Terabyte Samsung SSD. The transfer went without a hitch. It went so well that I immediately ordered a 256 Gigabyte Samsung SSD from Amazon for my wife's laptop. This time I used Samsung's data transfer software with the Apricorn transfer cable. It failed. Samsung's software complained about the condition of the hard disk. Then I used the Apricorn software. That also failed, but it was because my wife's PC went to sleep in the middle of the transfer. Your PC cannot decide to sleep during the transfer process. The third transfer, using the Apricorn software, succeeded. The PC immediately booted from the newly filled SSD. I bought the Apricorn kit because I'd had success years ago with Apricorn's IDE drive transfer kit. They've still got it. Recommended.

title: Excellent low-cost A/V receiver
text:
This is a good budget A/V receiver. I didn't want a lot of bells and whistles to get lost in--just something simple and functionally intuitive. Like any receiver out of the box, you need to learn about the sound adjustments and experiment accordingly. I employ a 2.1 setup (two large towers and a 10-inch subwoofer). I prefer to manually set up the sound rather than the automatic method using the supplied microphone. A particular tweak I really like is the Level Calibration, which allows you to adjust the volume of each speaker set. Another thing I like about this receiver is the unamplified line-level out port. That really adds to the versatility of the unit. I use that port for a wireless headphone hookup. The remote control is intuitive.

I recommend this receiver to anyone looking for a low-cost option--that doesn't want/need a lot of bells and whistles. It has excellent sound when setup properly and is easy to use/adjust.

title: did not like at all
text: I'm not really one to leave negative reviews, but I really did not like this at all. I just got it and am returning it today. I know everyone else says this DAC is great, but I tried it on three different receivers (a vintage high powered Pioneer, and a modern Denon, and a new inexpensive Sony amp with a built in bluetooth and DAC) using Tidal tethered from my Mac and it sounded strident and harsh on all three. I listen mostly to classical and jazz, and I found the treble to be very harsh. Violins and trumpets sounded awful. But even worse, the music did not sound balanced to me - each instrument section popped out of the mix in an awkward and obtrusive way, as if the DAC were trying to isolate every different sound on the stage and make it pop separately. In comparison, the same exact tracks on vinyl sounded flowing, harmonious and much more musical, with no one instrument section glaring out to grab attention. I even thought the built-in Sony DAC+bluetooth sounded better than this D50. I think my ears might just be naive and untrained in the was of audiophilia, but I was really disappointed in the sound from this unit.

title: Great portable option
text:
So I bought this on a whim to replace an older Dell projector and occasionally watch movies in the back yard from my PC, a job it did very well. Eventually though I decided to make some additional purchases to allow the projector to travel further afield. I'm now playing Mario Kart off my Nintendo Switch in the woods while camping, projecting the image on the side of my tent. Lots of fun.

The picture quality is good. It's certainly no crystal quality ultra 4k uber HD experience, but it can project Hulu videos off my 7th Gen iPad, and video games from my PS4 and Switch well enough to easily watch and play.

I see quite a few reviews complaining about picture brightness but I've never felt like this was an issue. Maybe it's because I'm a bit older and remember the days when unless the room was as dark as pitch you couldn't use a projector. In a brightly lit room, or outside during full daylight the image is visible but I wouldn't say useable. If I turn the lights off in my room during the day I'm able to play on my Switch with ease, and of course at night the picture seems very bright. Some of this is dependent on how far you're trying to project the image though. You're definitely not going to be able to project at 120" from 12 feet away during the day.

The sound from the projector is ok I guess? It's such a tiny device I wasn't expecting much. In the woods with a few friends I've had no issues hearing what's going on, but here in Chicago the noise of the streets and nearby expressway often drowns it out. I went ahead and purchased a bluetooth portable speaker though to avoid the issue.

The one flaw, in what I would say is an otherwise solid device (and the reason for 4 out of 5 stars) is because the device is not rechargeable via USB. The USB port on the back is used only to recharge other devices from the projectors own battery. The power adapter requires 12v 2a, however, even if you can find a portable battery capable of outputting that amount of power, as you would need to be able to run the Nintendo Switch in docked mode off of a battery, the plug on the back doesn't lend itself to conversion. So far I've been unable to find anything that will convert a 3mmx1.5mm barrel plug to a USB. If you do stumble across something though, please reach out.

title: Absolutely amazing!
text:
I am pretty big into Audio. I've owned a couple desktop speaker setups, I have also heard a lot of basic desktop speakers (Aux port, non-amplified). I even have a very nice 5.1 Paradigm home audio setup and these Elacs are mind blowing!
I purchased the Elac Unifi UB5 and have them connected to a S.M.S.L AD18. Which the speakers are harder to drive, since they're 4ohm, but the S.M.S.L AD18 amplifier I paired them with, claims 80w each @ 4 ohm. Lets just say I've never been able to crank the volume all the way up. I use these for near field (about 4' away) and the amplifier volume ranges 0-60 (60=max volume). My regular volume for these are between 8-11, which I can hear plenty at that volume. I tested the speakers on various songs, movies, and games. When I tested to see how loud they would go. I got the volume up to 33 and the UB5's were WAY too loud for me (really started vibrating my keyboard), so I turned the volume back down. The bass sounds amazing, the mids sound really good, and the high's are pretty decent. The highs probably aren't as good as a horn speaker, but they sound extremely well and they don't fatigue your ears after long listening periods, as long as you don't have them cranked up loud.
Then I played with some of the pre-set EQ's with the S.M.S.L AD18 and I feel like if you have the option to change the pre-set EQ's to your preferred listening, then it'd be extremely hard to find any speakers better than these. They sound phenomenal!

title: No problems with 3.5" IDE drives
text:
I mainly bought this item for accessing old IDE hard drives from a few of my past computers. I pulled two out of my college computer (3.5" IDE drives purchased around 2006) last night, and had almost no issues getting both to mount in Windows 10.

I found it was best to:
1) connect the 44 pin adapter to the hard drive,
2) the short power cable from the adapter to the hard drive,
3) the power cord to the adapter and wall outlet,
4) connect the USB cable from the adapter to the computer, and only once everything was connected,
5) flip the power switch on the adapter.

At that point the drive starts spinning and it pops up in File Explorer. (The first time I turned it on before connecting the USB cable to the computer, and Windows did not recognize it.)

I haven't tested the SATA connection, and I don't think I have any 2.5" IDE drives to test, but I wanted to submit this review since most complaints in the other reviews I read seemed to focus on 3.5" IDE issues.

text:
This review is based on an artist and game developers perspective. This is my first review on Amazon since I like the monitor a lot and I’m willing to share my thoughts. Hope it can help someone else.

I recently upgrade 2 of my 24” 1920x1200 dell monitor to this model, because i am a game developer a lot of programs i am using have complex interface, which left me a very small working space. So I decide it’s time to upgrade the monitors.

First of all, 4k is not a option because it requires some extra GPU power to render and you have to set the OS scale to 200% to use it otherwise the text would be way too small, that defeats the whole purpose. 4k might sounds wonderful on paper but in real life it is not practical to me.

Originally i was looking for 27 in” 2k monitors, but after did some math the text would be a too small for my eyes and hard to read. 32” 2k will keep the same pixel density but enlarge the working space, I was worried 32” might be too big but it is not, perfect for my needs, in fact after a few days of use I might want to upgrade to a even bigger size in the future at some point.

I was a big Dell monitor fan before. but the quality seems went downhill over the past few year, as an artist the color accuracy is the most critical part, I had really bad experience with the last 2 dell monitors, I bought them at same time at same place but the color just won’t match even after proper color calibration, (I use Spyder5 and DisplayCAL btw). I had to going back and forth 3 times for replacement to get the best matching result but still not matching at the end. What a nightmare. But that settle me down for the past 5 yrs. so for the new one I’m considering switch to other brand. Since most monitor panels are made by LG or Samsung(i’m not sure about this) I’d like to trace down to the source and give LG a try, the result is really really good, i got 2 of this model, the color matches right out of box, after the calibration, the color accuracy only a tiny bit improvement, which mean the color already pretty good. If you don’t have the calibration gadget this monitor is the way to go. Another good thing is the pure color displayed pretty "evenly" cross the screen, I don't remember the proper word to describe it, one of my old monitor has horrible red tint on 2 corners.

The monitor has HDR built-in but I didn't turn it on (I think it is off by default) because it brighten up everything, it might be good for gaming or watching movies. But for an artist I need the color accuracy the most. The monitor also have FreeSync or GSync, which is not something that I care about, I didn’t mess with it.

The IPS “bleeding” seems well controlled on this model too. No noticeable bleeding around the edges, and edge frame is thin too.

The price is under my budget too, i used to spend double the price on monitors because of the color accuracy needs.

By no mean this is the perfect monitor, there are 2 minor complaints, One of them is the stand, it only do the up and down tilting. No height or rotate adjustment. but I'm not gonna adjust it every single day so it is not a big deal to me. The other complaint is no USB extension ports available on this monitor, but you can see in my photo, I still kept one of the Dell monitor on the left side, I use that one to connect to my drawing tablet and charging my other devices. This is the only thing I’m gonna miss the old Dell monitor. but those are just good add-on features that it is good to have but not necesary for a monitor as long as the picture quality is good.

Overall, I’m very satisfied by this LG monitor, again I’m only speaking on an artist perspective. if you are a gamer you might want to check out other people's review, but by no mean this is not a good monitor for gaming, it is just not something that I care about for a monitor.

title: Versatile Smartwatch. Well constructed, and easy to use.
text:
I pre-ordered my watch through Bestbuy, Excellent product. Great value for the price. Looks very sharp and fits my (larger) wrist perfectly. (I got the 44mm... I suggest smaller people get the 40mm)

I use it in conjunction with a renpho Bluetooth scale to keep track of my personal fitness.

I've seen small bugs where my sleep data didn't transfer completely the first time I turned my phone off at night. But restarting the watch fixed that and it hasn't happened since.

The automatic tracking is nice. I do a fair amount of walking at my job daily 10-15k steps and it adds that to my daily workout time.

I think they need to adjust the run/walk detection, even if I start running... A lot of them time it'll list it as walking. But it's just as easy for me as to manually start the run tracking.

My only issue with the watch so far is the distance tracking. I run on a track that I know is a mile around and it's typically records the distance as much shorter... off by a good tenth of a mile. I measure the same run with my phone/Nike plus and it's spot on accurate.

I'm sure the distance/GPS issues will be fixed with a update and that should also hell with people's apparent calorie burn tracking issues.

Also battery life is superb... Easy 60 hours with mild use. I through on the charger when I get home from work daily while I shower and it'll typically be full before I put it back on to go to sleep.

Sleep tracking is great... I'm a very light sleeper and it gives me clear insights into how well I actually slept.

But overall solid watch. 10/10 recommended, especially if you have a Samsung phone.

Lastly.... People complaining that they didn't receive the pre-order gift..... You guys didn't read. There were directions below the product on Amazon saying how to redeem the gift. You have to go to link below and register the watch:

https://promos.samsungpromotions.com/gwa2/Mobile

Samsung sends the charger to you directly.

title: Pros & Cons - T10 vs T6
text:
I got the last model (T10)
& ALMOST wished I'd ordered those again...

I want to stress I'm happy with both. I ordered the T6 because my T10 were stolen

Here's the breakdown:

What the T6 FIXED
(T6 pros/T10 cons)

* FIXED problem where sound would cut out on quiet parts, which was a big problem listening to podcasts (due to bad noise reduction tech)
* FIXED issue with occasional disconnecting with other ear.
* IMPROVED. Sound it's just a bit better. More dynamic range. The sound is fantastic on the T10 but it's kicked up a notch on the T6
* IMPROVED. You can now leave one in the charger if you only want to listen to one (like a podcast at work, but still need to hear your surroundings)
* NEW... T6 adds function buttons to pods, so you can change volume, skip songs, etc by touching the pods (instead of your phone). But the PROBLEM with the buttons is... (see next point in cons)

What the T6 got WRONG/made worse
(T6 cons/T10 pros)

* I like that they added buttons, however they did it very wrong. The buttons aren't physical depress buttons, they're sensitive to touch (like your phone), which is a problem because every time you adjust one you accidentally push a button. Unless you have tiny ninja fingers, it's really hard to hold just the outside where there's no button...
They're also easy to hit the button wrong, because they're so sensitive (example: easy to do a double rather than single tap)...
If you take just one out you bump a button.
I just bumped as I'm writing this. I itched my ear & didn't realize my knuckle bumped it, and the sudden music scared the bejeeezus out of me.
* The charging box sucks... It's slick looking, good quality build. But incredibly difficult to get the pods out, unless your fingers are made of tire-rubber that can grip tiny slick objects, it's a hassle to get out... The old box wasn't as pimp looking/feeling, but it was easy to just grab the pods quickly. Major design flaw for the box.

CONS THAT BOTH HAVE:
NONE! There's no consistent con

PROS that BOTH have:

* Great sound
* Great price
* comfortable & stays in
* waterproof (I use them in the shower)

The pros outweigh the cons in both sets... I think the improvements in the T6 slightly lean in favor of those over the T10 (T6: better sound, stays connected to each other, can keep one in charging box, no sound clipping on podcasts).
But the cons are very frustrating (hard to get out of charging box. Constantly pushing buttons on accident, so much so that I control them with my phone rather than the buttons).

But for this sound quality, at this price, and a very premium look & feel, the cons are worth it... If I paid premium price I'd be upset.

All around a GREAT BUY!!!! Would highly recommend, despite the two annoying design flaws.

title: Nice 100X instrument amp, needs +/- Vcc
text: I used this instrument amp for a low frequency millivolt application. it does not like single sided voltage at all (+Vcc and 0V -VCC). I had good results with +10V +Vcc and -10V -Vcc with ground and reference pins at 0V. It took a 60Hz 4.8mA voltage signal and put out 480mV at the output as measured by a scope. The gain is fixed at 100 unless you replace the 500 ohm gain resistor on the board. My input was a bit noisy but the output looked clean. I can't really find any paperwork that describes the board, so I just guessed based on the AD8221 data sheet I found online. Seems that the gain is 1 with the resistor removed and the gain is 1000 with a 50 ohm resistor. Rg=49.4k/(G-1).

title: It's a bummer
text:
If you're a PC user and purchase this tablet, prepare to feel like a worthless afterthought in Wacom's design of this somewhat-decent piece of hardware. If you're a Mac user, prepare to feel completely catered to for the brief moment you plug in the tablet with your single cable, only to feel underwhelmed thanks to the rest of the device's shortcomings when compared to its price tag.

The mess of cables I have to keep around this dock makes me mumble "a grand and a half..." every time I connect the tablet. Calling the dock a "Link Plus" feels like you're getting something extra, but really you're just getting the extra bundle of mess that makes the tablet work in 4k, as advertised. You still can't use the HDMI port though, unless you're cool with 1440p.

The 4k resolution feels largely dulled by the near-translucent screen cover.

There are no programmable buttons.

The color accuracy is much less than I'd expect from this display.

I'm having a really hard time moving from pencil and paper to this thing. It's a hard feeling to describe, but my brush control just isn't that great because it feels like the surface I'm drawing on is separated by a half-inch of glass (I suppose because it is!) There's a sort of separation of tactility that I don't experience on my non-screen tablets. It's almost like you're drawing by proxy, like you're drawing on the screen that's drawing on the canvas. I'm fully aware this could just be a "me" problem and that I'll eventually get used to it just as I got used to drawing on a regular tablet, just prepare for this feeling if you decide to buy.

The experience overall is just a bummer. The tablet's features that justify its price tag are poorly executed. If $1500 doesn't mean that much to you, you'll probably like it. It'll for sure get the job done, and it's nice to have it serve as sort of an extra monitor while you work (as opposed to a non-display tablet).

I wouldn't buy it again given what I know now. But on the other hand, I haven't sold it yet, despite the thought crossing my mind several times, so I suppose there is a part of me that really wants it to work. It's just so much extra work on top of the bank-breaking price tag.

title: Unreliable connection
text:
I use this switch to use the game keyboard and mouse on two different computers. This thing will drop my mouse connection for about a half-to-full second every minute or so, leading to a really unresponsive feel (and making it unusable for gaming). Nearly every time I click to switch computers, it just won't pick up my keyboard at all until I unplug and plug it back in. Every once in a while when I click the switch, it'll switch over to Computer B and then after a couple seconds it'll switch back to Computer A, forcing me to click the switch again.

It works fine about 95% of the time, but the moments mentioned above happen all the time and make it such an inconvenient and unreliable device.

Another small issue I have is that the inputs and outputs are on different sides. This seems fine in theory but no matter how you position this on your desk you'll always have unsightly wires running to the side or over it. Compare this design to any HDMI switch (or a router, or literally any other electronic device) - where all of the ports are on the back, and all of the wires can be hidden behind the device. The design of having the outputs on the front make sense when using it for USB Drives, but it doesn't make sense for peripherals.

title: A perfect (but too expensive) complement the already incredible Oasis
text:
First off, I understand the criticisms of this case. It's too expensive for what it is. It should be $20 or even included with the device...if we're already spending $200+ on a reader the least that Amazon could do would be to throw in a case for it.

That being said, this cover is absolutely wonderful. I've had other cases for Kindles in the past, and they've been way too bulky or unwieldy and I usually ended up taking them off for longer reading sessions. I don't think I'll be doing that with this cover any time soon.

Maybe the main reason this case works so well for me is that I felt like the Oasis itself was a little too thin, too light, and too slick to feel truly safe in my hands. This case adds just enough weight to the device, and it hugs the curves of the Oasis perfectly, the fabric adding some good grip to the back.

Even better is how the magnets in the case work. In addition to holding the cover against the Oasis' screen when it's closed, they hold the cover firmly in place when it's open, creating a nice, solid feel when reading. This handled my other issues I've had with Kindle cases that the cover would have to be held in place or flap around while reading.

Overall this case is beautiful, sleek, and a perfect complement to the Oasis, which is already a wonderful device. It's just a shame that it's too expensive.

title: Nice hardware and app, but no automation & misleading Alexa support
text:
*************************
UPDATE 10/29/2020
Not sure what changed, but viewing the live video on Fire TV suddenly works now, which is very nice!

Still disappointed that you can't control the light with Alexa/voice or use motion detection as a trigger in Alexa routines. Oddly, there is an option in the Alexa device settings to enable "Doorbell Press Announcements" and a corresponding "when pressed" trigger available in Routines, but neither seems to do anything. I thought maybe they were mapping the motion detection to an Alexa doorbell feature (which would be very clever and useful), but that doesn't seem to be the case. Even stranger is iBRIGHT does not even make a doorbell as far as can tell, so no idea what the setting or trigger could be for.
*************************

Installation was easy and build quality seems good. App setup is poorly documented, so a bit of trial and error to get it working, but once setup the app is quite nice and very easy to use. Had an extra 128GB sdcard I wasn't using, so threw that in and it works great for always on recording. Love that you don't need any monthly cloud subscription. Hardware seems good - lights, camera, motion detection and night vision all work very well. The audio features (talk and alarm) are mediocre, but I wasn't really planning to use those anyway.

So that's all great, however the "smart" features could be a lot smarter. There is no automation support, either in the iBRIGHT app or via Alexa. By that I mean that none of the functions are exposed for use in scenes/routines and no controls show up in Alexa (can't turn lights on/off in Alexa app or via voice control, for example). As far as I can tell, the only thing you can do with Alexa is ask to show the camera on an Echo Show device, which does work. But unfortunately, doesn't work on Fire TV - the iBRIGHT skill starts when you ask to view the camera on Fire TV, but eventually times out (*** this is fixed now - see UPDATE 10/29/2020 above ***). So in reality it supports a single function on a single type of Echo device. Saying it "works with Alexa" is a bit misleading.

I filled out the Contact Us form on the iBRIGHT website to ask about these issues over a week ago, but no reply.

I still think it's a good value given the low price, local storage, nice app and good hardware, so overall satisfied with it. But very disappointed there is no automation support, no real Alexa support and unresponsive customer service. If iBRIGHT resolves some of those issues it would easily be a 5 star device.

title: The longer I use it, the less I like it.
text:
My biggest grip with this product is that it keeps missing events that I am interested in.

I have my motion sensitivity set to "All Motion" but it does not record all motion. Instead, when it sense motion it records one minute and five seconds of video. Even if there is continues motion during that time, it will stop recording at the one minute, five second mark. Due to the layout of my property, very often events that I am interested in happen more then one minute and five seconds after the initial motion is detected. The result is that they are not recorded. There is a period of time before a new recording starts when there is motion but that motion is not recorded. One many occasions I have found that events that I am looking for fall into this gap between recordings.

My next grip is how hard it is to find old recordings. There is no date filter or search of any kind on the video list. Sure, a paid plan will keep 60 days of recordings, but have you tried to scroll back that far? I have. We went out of town and when we got back I wanted to look back at an event that took place about 3 weeks before. I scrolled, and scrolled and scrolled. Every time you scroll to the bottom on the list there is a delay while it loads more events. It really adds up, especially on a small screen where it is only loading 4 or 5 more events at a time. It took about 15 minutes until I was finally able to get to the date I was interested in.

Also, the app does not handle time zones well. If your phone and your camera are in different time zones, all bets are off. When traveling to the East coast, I had the app telling me that a recording was from "Today 21:09 (PST)." The problems? First, this time was in the future. It was only 19:00 in the Pacific time zone. The recording was actually from the day before. Second, Daylight Saving Time was in effect, so the correct time zone designation is PDT, not PST.

Finally (for now) downloading timestamped video just takes too many steps. First I have to find the video I want. Then I have to "share" a link. Then I have to copy and past the link. Then I can finally download a time stamped video. There is no direct download option in the web site, you can only download after a share.

I've brought all of these issue up with Ring support and always gotten a useless "we will pass that along to the developers" response. Except the time when they though reinstalling the app would fix their timezone bugs (spoiler: it didn't).

title: Cheap materials / We don't care that it broke, buy another one
text:
We had this enclosure for a few weeks before it broke. The enclosure was sitting vertically on the desk when it was accidentally tipped over and the back panel just popped off went it landed flat. This didn't fall to the floor or a few feet. This enclosure went from being upright at 90 degrees, to tipping over and laying at 180 degrees. Nothing more. This caused the mounting points for the screws to snap off of the back panel. And therefore, no longer secure the drive to the enclosure. This back panel is made of really cheap and thin plastic.

I contacted the seller about it to see if they can offer me a replacement part or exchange out the enclosure. They suggested taping or gluing it. And if this wasn't able to be done, I should just by a new one because they are "not too expensive". I probably will buy many more enclosures in the future. But when I see the name "Vantec", I'll just keep walking next time.

This was the response I received from Vantec Tech Support:
"Thanks for writing.
Is the unit still functional?
If the unit still functional, I would suggest having a proper backup of the data from the hard drive first.
If the damage is to a point that you cannot tape or glue the pieces together to continue using it, I would suggest a new replacement.
User damage is not covered in the warranty. We also do not sell as parts, replacement case because it is part of the main unit.
It is not too expensive to get a new enclosure and just move the hard drive over to the new enclosure.
If the drive is still good, all your data will still be there available to you.
You can get one here:
https://www.amazon.com/Vantec-NexStar-Drive-Enclosure-NST-328S3-BK/dp/B01JNLCC7U

If you have any further question, please don't hesitate to ask and we will do our best to answer them."

title: Not For Z87E-ITX
text:
This does not work on the ASRock Z87E-ITX even when running on the latest stable (2.50) or beta (2.70) BIOS. I doubt ASRock will support this old motherboard, but I was surprised they released a new BIOS in 2018. They should have a list of motherboard models that are supported with this TPM chip. Hopefully the release a new BIOS for this motherboard to support TPM 2.0. I cant find a TPM 1.2 chip anywhere.

Update 2/19/2021: I gave it another shot since I learned that the BIOS must be set to UEFI and CSM disabled for TPM 2.0 to work. The board still reports Support Turned Off in BIOS. I then contacted ASRock support for a modified BIOS and got it, 2.70A. If you plan to do the same, you might get an email return error. Forward the request using the same dot come email, but with support in front of the at sign. After flashing the modified BIOS, the TPM chip has all the settings visible in BIOS and Windows. There is an issue with the TPM firmware where boot up is really slow, about 2-3min just sitting at the ASRock logo. Fast or Ultra Fast boot doesnt help. I was unable to find a way to update the firmware. Theres a Dell version out there, but I was unable to apply it in Windows and DOS. I can finally use Bitlocker properly! I added a star for ASRock support providing a modified BIOS and another star for it to working. One star taken away for slow boot up and another for no way to update the firmware. I think ASRock updated their TPM website saying this does not work with Intel Series 7 and 8 chips.

text:

title: Great z490 mobo, stable with 10700k stock and oc. Affordable price.
text: The ASRock Z490M-ITX/ac worked fine when paired with a 10700k on default v1.10 bios.  I did update the bios to v1.30 after installation.  Leaving everything default/stock the 10700k worked fine.  Overclocking on this board is average but worked as well.  You can easily get 5.1 on all cores by bumping up to 1.34 volts.  But decided to keep it at 4.9 with 1.275v.  I used AIDA64 and stress tested the board for few hours.  The mobo does not have a VRM sensor so i couldn't tell how hot they were getting.  But I have a fan that blows across them.  I didn't feel any extra warmth and everything was stable. The VRM heatsink actually isn't really that bad. I had a x99 ASRock itx with an old 5820k and it ran for over 5 years and had a VRM heatsink about half the size of what is on this board.  But heck at $155 for this mobo you can't beat it.  If this one last 5 years I will be happy.  I may buy another just to keep for a backup.  The UEFI bios on this board is terrific.  Lots of options to play with and tweak. And I was surprised at just how much faster the 10700k was compared to other 9900k system. And the 10700k seems to run  cooler than my 9900k.  So in conclusion I would definitely recommend this mobo. Its stable with stock 10700k and if you are into some slight overclocking, then you should have no problems.

title: Best laptop experience for general/photo/video/music/portable use, but not a performance powerhouse
text:
The new macbooks are the best laptop experience you'll find in the market, but they are far from the strongest performing laptops you'll find, especially for the money. If you want a smooth, streamlined experience, without having to carry a mouse around, the macbook pro 16 and the Mac OS is the cream of the crop.

The colors, brightness, and clarity of the laptop are absolutely the best quality screen you'll find in a laptop.

The keyboard is great, but a bit overhyped. What it surpasses others in is build quality, there is a lot of quality control in every single key, so they feel stable, consistent, and satisfactory. But to me, they don't make or break a laptop experience.

The speakers exceed all of the hype and reviews that you hear. Go to the apple store when you can and give them a listen, they are some of the best portable speakers period.

The touchpad is arguably worth the price tag alone if you are looking to carry around your work. It is accurate and enjoyable to use, and far better than anything else on a non Apple product.

With all this said, the performance is lackluster at least for my standards. While navigating photo editing apps like Adobe are enjoyable with the trackpad, there is still quite a bit of video lag when panning, zooming, or operating large files. In the OS, windows are laggy to move around from a visual standpoint. For the same price you could get a Windows laptop that has an RTX 2070 or higher, and everything would be much more enjoyable from a snappy and visual standpoint.

This is my first macbook, and I absolutely love the user experience it provides. But despite the prestige of owning one, the build quality associated with every part of the laptop, the amazing screen and touchpad, and the portable power consistency you can get when it isn't plugged in, I have to say I'll be moving back to a Windows laptop. The biggest thing I will miss is the touchpad.

title: AMAZING... but not...
text:
I bought the Sennheiser HD-660s new and HE400i headphones on the secondhand market so that I could gauge the sound signature of both products. I went into this test fully expecting to keep the HD-660s and re-sell the HE400i but figured I would give HIFIMAN a shot based off of the good reviews I read about them. I was completely shocked to find that I MUCH preferred the sound of the HIFIMAN planar magnetic drivers over the tried and true Senn. HD platform! I sent the HD660s back.

After a few weeks of listening time with the HE400i's, I started to wonder what I was missing out on with there being much more expensive HIFIMAN products out there. After much research I pulled the trigger on the HIFIMAN Sundara. I do admit that I read some reviews about the Sundara that almost threw me off of them mentioning crappy build quality and inferior wiring/soldering, I figured since I have never been burned by faulty electronics before.. even my used gear I've bought I would be lucky again and have no problems. I finally got the Sundara's and opened them up and inspected them, they look very beautiful and are some of the best looking headphones out there I think. As I went to put them on my head I noticed the headphone band adjustment on one side was very loose and looks like it has been opened and closed so many times that the little detent that clicks into each height marker had worn them smooth and it wouldn't lock into place or click at each notch.

The sound of these headphones are incredible, I was getting goosebumps they're that good! I have paired them with the JDS Labs EL DAC/AMP stack as well as the ifi iDSD Micro Black Label and they both sound fantastic. After 3 days of listening, the left driver volume cut down to about 20%. I swapped the cables from left to right and still barely any sound. Looks to have bad wiring between the jack and the driver. I can't believe that there are so many issues with a $500 brand new pair of headphones in 3 days... I am trying my luck with one more pair and will update later, should get the replacements tomorrow. Be careful buying these and only get them if you can easily exchange them through Amazon...

***EDIT*** I ended up returning these, too worried about the build quality. I bough the Audeze LCD-2 Classics and love them, much higher build quality and I prefer the sound As well.

title: These are nothing short of incredible.
text:
Oh my goodness. These are incredible.

1) Background & Comparison:

I have had the Bose QC35 headphones for a year, and just purchased the Bose SoundSport Free (after purchasing the AirPods Pro) and love them both, but these AirPods Pro buds are SO lightweight I actually forgot I had left one in my ear at work the other day (no music playing of course). I don’t see a need for wearing my QC35s anymore because they’re heavy and large. After I purchased the AirPods Pro, purchased a pair of Bluetooth Bose Soundsport Free to compare sound and bass. Sound quality is great on the SoundSport Free model but I have issues with the size (even smalls tips hurt my ears) and they are bulky. Sorry, Bose, I really wanted to love your product but the AirPods Pro win for me due to size, ease of use, and comfort.
——

2) Fit:

My ears hurt with a lot of earbuds styles bc I have smaller ears, but the medium sized tips surprisingly fit great. There’s functionality to test the ear tip fit while you have them in your ear - I assume it tests pressure and seal that the tips make in your ear canal. They also don’t fall out and seem completely snug. I did work out in them, but haven’t run or done any kind of strenuous activity with them, but would be interested to see if they stay in while running. So far, I would assume they do based on the secure fit.
——

3) Noise cancellation & transparency mode:

I work in an open office and was completely shocked by the noise cancellation mode. It is AWESOME and really muffled out most (95%?) of the noise. I might wear these at work without playing music just so it’s quiet and I can focus better. Transparency mode is excellent for doing things around the house or wearing on a trail where I need to be cognizant of surroundings, and still want to hear my music.
——

4) Audio quality:

I feel like I don’t need to turn these up as loud as I have had to with other brands. Ear tip fit is great and sound is crystal clear. I wish they had more bass, but I do find the bass quite sufficient. I generally seek out bass in my headphones because of personal preference, and I’m happy with them. I do wish there was an equalizer to be able to adjust the settings for the use, but I’ll leave that to my music apps to do. Sound quality is great and I hope it will save my ears a little bit from not having to turn them up like I have had to with my other earbuds previously.
——

5) Conclusion:

These are amazing. Form and function are great, and most of all, they are lightweight and ease of use is excellent. Highly recommended.

title: Very nice product, needs a few more web features, here is some helpful info to change IP address
text:
This unit is very nice. I would give it a 4.5 if that was an option. It does exactly what is stated in the user manual. I would highly recommended reading the user manual carefully before purchasing it and make sure it’s going to meet your needs. I’m using the web interface, so one feature that I feel is missing is the ability to change the login password. It does have a web interface. To access it, you will need to know, the IP address, username, and password. The unit does not currently support DHCP, nor does it register its name with the LAN router.

Here is some info that I hope someone will find helpful. To change the IP address, it must be done via the RS232 port. For me, I had to purchase a USB to RS232 cable so I could communicate to it using my PC. I purchased a UGREEN USB 2.0 to RS232 DB9 Serial Cable Male. I’m running Windows 10. When I plugged in the cable to my PC, the driver did not auto load, so I needed to load the driver from the CD. One could also download the driver from prolific.com because the chipset used in the UGREEN cable is from Prolific. You should verify the driver is installed correctly by looking at device manager. In my situation, when the cable is connected to the PC, device manager adds a category called port. It also informs me that it had allocated COM4 as the communication port name for the cable.

Next you will need a terminal emulator program to send/receive information from the matrix. I picked termite rs232. One thing that I liked about termite rs232, you don’t need to install anything, just download the program to a directory (preferably a new empty one) and run it from there.

Some important tips, make sure the baud rate is set to 9600, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity, and append nothing to your transmitted text. If you send a CR or LF, it will not respond to your commands. Make sure you enter the command exactly as in the manual, case sensitive, and with the period “.” at the end of your command.
Another nice helpful hint to verify things are working ok. When the matrix powers up, it dumps a bunch of information. So if you connect RS232 cable, run the terminal emulator, and then power up the matrix, you should receive a bunch of information. If you receive the info, then you know that you are successfully communicating with the matrix and you can do things like change the IP address.
