title: Another awesome radio from Radioddity!
text:
In order to give a complete and full review of this radio, I used the GS-5B as my daily driver for the past 3-4 weeks.

1. Packaging and Enclosures:

This radio was well packaged by Radioddity. With the radio came with a Model 8800BP lithium ion battery (standard 2000 mAh), a charging cradle, an antenna, 1 power adapter for the charging cradle, an air acoustic earpiece, a belt clip, a hand strap, a programming cable, and a user manual.

2. Physical Appearance:

The radio has a very rugged feel when you hold it in your hand. It has a very attractive orange casing that makes it easy to find in the dark. The rubber gripping on the sides, and the narrowness of the radio makes it very comfortable to hold. The buttons are very easy to see with very crisp silk screening.

The radio also has a Kenwood 2-pin accessory connection on the right side, which should be very familiar with users that own a Baofeng, Anytone, or Radioddity handhelds. This is a huge advantage since it enables this radio to work with a large assortment of easily attainable accessories such as shoulder speaker-microphones, earpieces, or even an APRS cable that can be plugged into an Android phone or into a TNC.

The volume knob feels very nice between finger and thumb due to its size, and the knurling on the knob makes it easy for one to quickly do a blind tune with a single finger or thumb.

3. Flashlight:

Unlike similar radios that have a single LED “flashlight” on the top of the radio, the GS-5B has a much more practical design. The flashlight is located on the bottom, and is capable of projecting a wider and a brighter beam. What also makes this flashlight different from the others is the LED itself. Baofengs and other radios only use a through-hole PCB mounted round LED without any kind of reflectors. The GS-5B uses a much brighter surface mounted white LED, and is surrounded by a mirror-like reflective housing.

Along with the white LED, the flashlight also has 2 additional colored surface mounted red and blue LEDs that will strobe.

4. IMPROVED Display:

One of the biggest upgrades that traditional Baofeng users will notice is the much improved, full colored display. The display, which is approximately 1.5 inches diagonal, has a very crisp display that is easy to read. It features a S-meter on top, which is not found on many handheld radios today. The display also has a dual frequency display on the bottom, and in the middle shows which frequency or channel that is currently being used.

5. Battery and Charging:

This radio comes with a lithium ion battery that has the typical 2000 mAh cycle, but the battery itself is not the typical handheld battery.

The battery itself, much like the radio, is very rugged. It is secured to the radio using a metal screw on the bottom instead of using plastic tabs. One thing that I find annoying with Baofeng radios like the UV-5R is the fact when lightly dropped on the floor, the battery will pop off and you risk breaking the plastic catch/release tab. With the GS-5B, the battery is very well secured with this screw.

The radio’s battery can be charged in 3 ways: using the charging cradle with the enclosed power adapter, using the charging cradle with a micro-USB cable, or charging the battery itself directly using the micro-USB port on the battery. The utilization of a micro-USB cable alone gives the GS-5B a strong advantage since it provides users flexibility on charging methods. Almost everyone has access to a micro-USB cable and a USB charger (phone charger, USB ports in a car, ports on a computer, etc.). This also allows the user to charge the battery using a portable battery bank when hiking, or during emergency scenarios where mains power is down.

Charging time for this battery is consistent with other radios that use a battery with similar capacities. Here is a chart of approximate charging times that I’ve experienced:

Charging Cradle with Power Adapter:
- Fully drained battery – 4 to 4 ½ hours
- Half drained battery – 1 ½ to 2 hours

Charging Cradle with USB, or micro-USB on back of battery (1.0 Amp output):
- Fully drained battery – 5 to 6 hours
- Half drained battery – 3 to 3 ½ hours

Charging Cradle with USB , or micro-USB on back of battery (2.1 Amp output):
- Fully drained battery – 3 ½ to 4 hours
- Half drained battery – 1 to 1 ½ hours

6. Wired/Wireless Programming

This radio can be programmed using 1 of 2 methods: connected to a PC using a programming cable, or wirelessly using Bluetooth to a cell phone.

Radioddity provides PC programming software on their website that can be downloaded to a PC running Windows. The enclosed programming cable utilizes a USB-to-Serial chipset, and is connected to the radio’s Kenwood 2-pin plug on the right side. The cable works flawlessly between the computer and the radio. The programming software is tailored exclusively for the GS-5B, and the application is very easy to navigate. This software will allow you to program a channel list where one can enter in the transmit/receive frequencies, PL tones in either CTCSS or DCS, high or low transmit power, wide or narrowband, PTT-ID if needed, and a channel name. The Optional Feature window will present you with options that you can also find using the radio’s onboard menu. The field labels are very easy to understand and straightforward.

The radio is also programmable using its Bluetooth feature when paired to an Android phone. The Radioddity GS-5B app is available through Radioddity’s website. Personally, I find the app to be very user friendly, and I was able to grasp and understand it very quickly. The app will allow users to program channels, choose a frequency mode between the A and B VFOs, and the typical optional features that can also be found through the radio’s onboard menu. The app also saves your codeplug to your phone so you can refer to it in the future when needed. I find the Bluetooth programming feature to be an extremely huge advantage, and it is a feature many users wanted to see.

7. Battery Life

The battery life on the GS-5B, when using the provided battery, in my opinion is one of the backdraws on this radio. From my personal experience, the battery will only last 8 to 10 hours when the radio is on standby. Here is a chart of my experience with the GS-5B’s battery life:

- Fully charged, power-save mode is on, display is set to auto-off, Bluetooth is off, no transmissions/QSOs: 8 to 10 hours
- Fully charged, power-save mode is on, display is set to auto-off, Bluetooth is off, with “ragchewing” QSOs lasting anywhere from 5 to 25 minutes: 5 to 6 ½ hours
- Fully charged, power-save mode is off, display stays on, Bluetooth is off, no transmissions/QSOs: 6 to 7 hours
- Fully charged, power-save mode is off, display stays on, Bluetooth is off, with “ragchewing” QSOs lasting anywhere from 5 to 25 minutes: 4 to 5 hours

I believe this may be an isolated case with a possibility of my battery being defective. My other handheld radios with a similar battery capacity usually can stay in listening/standby mode for 24-36 hours without any transmissions made.

8. Transmit Power

The GS-5B is a dual power, dual band radio that has a maximum transmit power of 5 watts. Using my Surecom SW-102 SWR/watt meter, 2 feet of RG-58 jumper coax, and a MFJ-261 dry dummy load, I got the following readings:

VHF, High Power (146.520 MHz) – 4.2 to 4.7 Watts
VHF, Low Power (146.520 MHz) – 0.9 to 1.1 Watts
UHF, High Power (440.000 MHz) – 4.1 to 4.5 Watts
UHF, Low Power (440.000 MHz) – 0.8 to 1.0 Watts

Tests are ran with a fully charged battery, and the power readings are acceptable for a handheld radio. While with the radio being on low power hits the target of the 1 watt range, the high power falls just under 5 watts. This can be due to my testing equipment, quality of coax used, etc. since these readings can fluctuate depending on the equipment used. To get a much accurate watt/power reading, one should use an oscilloscope. Unfortunately, I do not own one.

When it comes to distance, the radio performs just like any other 5 watt handheld. I am able to key up to a VHF repeater, within line-of-sight, that is approximately 15-20 miles away with the stock antenna on high power. The same when keying a UHF repeater on high power. When switch out the stock antenna to an aftermarket antenna, I noticed no difference. The aftermarket antennas I used was the Nagoya NA-771, Diamond SRJ77CA, and a Signal Stick. When the stock antenna performs just as well with these other antennas, this comes to a huge advantage for the user. Unlike the stock antenna that comes with Baofengs, the user that uses the GS-5B will not need to upgrade their antenna.

9. Transmit and Receive Audio Quality

Once again, on a Radioddity branded radio, the GS-5B has superb audio reports when transmitting. Here are my testing conditions:

- Transmitting to repeater (VHF and UHF), both approximately 15 miles away line of sight
- Simplex transmission (VHF 146.520 MHz) to a station that is 10 miles away line of sight
- High Power

When transmitting through a repeater, I got reports stating that I was clearly audible, clear to understand, and full quieting (no background noise). When doing a simplex transmission, I was still clearly audible, clear to understand, and a little hiss in the background.

I also did this test with 3 other radios (Anytone 868, Baofeng UV-5x3, Yaesu FT65R). The GS-5B compared to these 3 radios did very well, and the audio reports of the GS-5B were similar to the Anytone and Yaesu radios.

The internal speaker on the GS-5B is also very loud and crisp, and is easy to comprehend when outdoors with a lot of environmental white noise. The air acoustic earpiece that came with the radio had superb results as well with clear receive audio, and very clear transmission audio unlike the earpieces that come with the Baofeng radios.

10. Pros and Cons:

Pros:
- Rugged and waterproof form factor
- Attractive orange color making it easy to find
- A much improved full color display that features a S-meter
- Excellent audio quality and reports
- Using a cell phone and Bluetooth to program radio using Radioddity’s app
- Improved flashlight design that makes it practical to use
- Stock antenna performs just as well as the leading aftermarket brands
- Flexible methods of battery charging

Cons:
- Battery life (again, this could just be an isolated case)

11. Conclusion

Overall, the Radioddity GS-5B is an excellent radio. I used this radio as my daily driver for the past 3-4 weeks and have been extremely pleased with it. The way the radio feels and the way it looks is amazing, and it is a pleasure doing QSOs on this radio. I see where some in the amateur radio community, through online forums, say that the GS-5B is overpriced with the $99.99 price point since it is a Chinese radio. I completely disagree. Even though this is a Chinese radio, the way it operates is on par with the Japanese-made radios such as Icom, Kenwood, and Yaesu. The build quality, transmission quality, features, Bluetooth, and programming platform options makes this radio easily price pointed for $99.99. One can find a Japanese-made radio with these similar features, but can expect to pay $75-100 more than the GS-5B.

In my opinion, this radio is a definite buy and would make a great addition to a ham station and/or emergency go-kit.

title: Believe the hype
text:
This thing is a little beast. A loud, clear, and warm sound. Practically instant setup via app, solid build, space age looks, with a nod to Moroccan wood screens in the floral design of the tweeter.

Plugs into the wall, only "portable" as in it is not very large/can be plugged in anywhere. But not totally wireless because of this. It's also rather heavy and substantial, compared to other "Portable" speakers (It's just shy of 10lbs.). Can also be connected to a modem/router via ethernet cable, which boosts the connection, apparently. I haven't felt that was necessary for my situation, as there appears to be no issues connecting via wifi or bluetooth.

With the bluetooth, you can use this as you would any other bt accessory. Over wifi, you can stream directly from apps like Spotify without relying on a bluetooth connection. And of course, you can also just hook up via optical/analog jack.

The speaker can be controlled via the touch sensors on the top of the unit, from the app, or from within apps like Spotify.

This sounds better than any bluetooth speaker I've ever heard, and it's gotta be up there with an of the stereo speakers available around the same price. So if you want to replace a stereo with something more streamlined, you should feel comfortable with this.

Besides the variety of connectivity options, the best feature is the bass. It is unbelievably rich and strong for a speaker this size, without being muddy, or harsh. In fact, it is just right at any volume I've tried, and with any kind of music. You can see the woofers pulsate, and you can feel the bass. Incredible.

Arrives securely packed. The speaker is in a unique box, featuring an elastic fabric stretched across a recessed area on either side of the interior to provide extra cushion. I'll be hanging on to that box. The power cable was in a second box, and both of these boxes are packed into the third (retail) box, which was inside a larger Amazon box (phew!)

title: I do mainly product photography and some run-n-gun commercial work
text:
So I love my GH5 and GH4's, and I was hoping this lens would give me something wide enough for some range, but would also give me additional light (As we all know the GH4/5 are not lowlight cameras)
So the Pros
- Incredibly fast, and great in low light
- Creamy Bokeh, nice orbs of light and soft
- Sharp in the corners and center evenly at 2.0 or higher
- between 3.2 - 5.6 this does a great job at sharpness
- 16mm is wide enough for an MFT but we are still in the 32mm equiv range.
- SBS this looks as good as some of my Zeiss Glass

Cons
- It's a Big Lens, and heavy
- At .1.4 corners go soft, and vary minimal focus area (To be expected)
- 16mm / 32mm is an odd focal length to work with, but has it's applications

Overall I would say if you have the money and want a faster prime this is great. If you're looking for a Wide lens and don't want to do speed boosters and adapters you should look at 8mm - 10mm mft lenses (But don't expect it to be this fast) This lens has it's applications, it's just not the best for the type of Product Photography I'm currently doing. Would high recommend this if you're looking for a faster, medium focal length, and creamy bokeh mft lens.

title: YES!  IT FITS THE 2020 M1 MACBOOK AIR
text:
Yes! The case and keyboard skin perfectly fit the NEWEST 2020 M1 MacBook Air (A2337)! What a relief! I’d been anguishing over which case to get after reading review after review of this case and other cases here on Amazon, saying the case and/or keyboard skin didn’t fit. After weeks of this nonsense, (I spent this amount of time deciding on the laptop itself!), I finally decided to pull the trigger, trust my instincts and get the dang case.

PROS: Case and accessories came on time, without any issues (dents, cracks etc I’d seen some reviewers report). However, packaging leaves a bit to be desired. There’s no bubble wrap - just a plastic envelope mailer. The case etc, was wrapped in plastic sheeting, but not much protection, but apparently it didn’t need more than that, because it was totally flaw-free.

The case came with printed installation instructions, and installed easily, without any hiccups, within seconds. The included cloth contributed to a clean installation. Everything snapped right into place.

Case is very thin, but feels capable of protection, as long as you don’t drop your laptop off a balcony or something. It’s not designed to be more than a scratch preventer IMO.

Keyboard skin fits perfectly. I’ve never used one before so I don’t have anything to compare it to, but it seems capable of preventing or minimizing liquid, crumb and dust damage.

Screen protector is a thin piece of sheet plastic that comes with a film on both sides that is (obviously) removed before application. It has a cut-out for the camera lens. It adheres to the screen without adhesive, via static electricity.

CONS: zero.

I’m totally happy with my (inexpensive) laptop protection investment. If you own the brand new 2020 M1 MacBook Air, I recommend this case kit for you!

title: A great way to upgrade performance on an older laptop
text:
A good friend of mine gave her old laptop to me. It's a 15.4 inch Toshiba Satellite A135-4487 64 bit system. This computer was new in 2006 or so, and it came with Windows Vista, DVD/CD burner, Centrinio dual core 1.66mhz processor, 4 gb of ram, and two hard drives. I installed my copy of Windows 7 Pro 64 bit on its new Kingston 240gb SSD, as Toshiba still has Windows 7 drivers available. Boot up is now in just a few seconds and program loading is blazingly fast. I have since ordered another Kingston SSD to replace the second hard drive in this computer.

Some important facts about upgrading from traditional spinning hard drives to solid state drives (SSD). The biggest bottle neck on any computer is the data throughput between the system and the hard drive. Laptop hard drives spin at 5500rpm and this slower speed coupled with the mechanical movement of read/write heads is what consumes the time. SSDs eliminate those factors. The read/write functions in an SSD are similar to those that take place in system RAM. Secondly, when doing any internal work on computers, especially laptops, remember to disconnect power and remove the battery. And just FYI, I run an SSD in my Windows 10 Pro desktop. It takes about 7 seconds from the time I turn on the computer until I am looking at my desktop.

Finally, a last word about SSDs - If you system uses IDE drives, then you will not see any great improvement in speed. The limiting factor in IDEs is the electronics itself. Be sure to check your existing drives to be SATA drives if you are looking for performance. Having said that, I put an IDE SSD in my old Dell 10 inch netbook. I did this to ensure drive reliability and reduce power consumption. While the performance increase is tiny, it is noticeable.

A word about my computers and Windows 7 - Microsoft is no longer supporting Windows 7, although it does update Windows 7 service pack 1 to what the latest was at the time of pulling support. My rationale is simple: Windows 7 runs fast on my two older laptops. Both laptops will actually run Windows 10, but the netbook maxes out at 2gb of RAM and the Toshiba at 4gb of RAM. Windows 10 Pro runs best with at least 8gb of RAM, so I get stuck with performance issues and some driver issues when using Windows 10 on these two laptops. Another alternative is to run Linux on these two laptops. Linux has a long reputation of re-energizing older computers. I recommend Linux Mint.

When you place the coin at the edge of the base so it is visible in the camera, it is so far away that the photo is distorted and the zoom will not adjust to accommodate the distance or the funky angle of the microscope. The light is only adequate close up.  Over all it was easy to set up and easy to use.  It is nice to look at the magnification on a computer screen instead of through a hand magnifier.  It's not bad for the price, but it does not really meet my needs.  It is a better quality then the two previous brands I tried and returned.

title: Helped me save my phone's pictures from certain loss, and it does other things too.
text:
I was traveling internationally earlier this year and dropped my phone onto a cement floor, permanently damaging the screen. I couldn't navigate, I couldn't change settings, I couldn't join a wifi network or even turn the cellular data back on to back things up. I was in trouble since I'd taken hundreds of pictures in recent days while traveling through Latin America and the Caribbean. Unfortunately, since I was roaming, my phone wasn't backing up to the cloud automatically, which left me reliant on wifi -- also very limited in my destinations -- but only usable with a wifi card where I had to enter a code. I packed it away, hoping I could find a solution once I returned home.
I read that my Huawei phone had a 'desktop' mode, where I could connect it to a monitor and use it like a computer but had never tried it. I was desperate so looked for a device like this, hoping it would at least give me the equivalent of an external monitor and allow me to back up my phone before sending it for repair, where a full phone reset/erase is part of their process. This arrived quickly so I plugged it into my phone's charge port (USB-C) and into an hdmi port on my television. Since the touch screen wasn't working, I also plugged in a USB mouse. Voila! The desktop came up and the mouse was moving around the screen so I turned the wifi and cellular data back on, allowing all my irreplaceable pictures to get backed up. Whew! After this ordeal, I found that this is a great product in many other ways, especially for a newer laptop that is short on USB ports. It's well-built and high performance. Great product!

title: Very good value for the amazing performance - only concern is about support and longevity
text:
So I had an Intuos 2 that remained my workhorse for 15+ years but it finally got left behind by Windows 10 so I needed a replacement. I could not afford to drop 350.00 on a new Intuos Pro medium replacement and so started researching the many affordable semi-clones. After a lot of internet research I settled on Huion H1060P (Not the 1060Plus) as the best match both for size and capability and supports tilt and has a battery-free digitizer. I was able to get it for 70.00 here and I saved 280 over Wacom. Quite frankly that deal is so good it has me seriously worried about long term viability. I don't expect a 70.00 tablet to last 15+ years like the Wacom did but I'm worried I won't get 5 out of this one. There has to have been corners cut. The build quality is good for the price but not as good as my old Intuos.

So I have used this now for about 8-10 hours. I have tried Krita (for 2d Paint) and Zbrush for 3D so far (see Zbrush model render shot above). It quite honestly has been amazing in my initial tests. No squiggles when doing diagonal line tests. The Digitizer seems to handle very well and correctly register my pressure.

Here are my concerns:
1) Longevity - As I mentioned above the performance is 95% of an intuos for 1/5 the price. That scares me. I'm worried this thing will break. I've read a lot of horror stories but so far at the very beginning of my journey this tablet is a steal for the price/performance. I hope it stays that way for 4-5 years at least.

2)3rd party support: I have not tried Photoshop yet but I've heard it has issues. That is a problem for most people buying this tablet. I have not tried it yet but I will report back if I ever buy into their subscription model. For Zbrush (my purpose for this tablet) the recent version (Zbrush 2020) appears to work perfectly. The NEWEST version (2020.1) does not work AT ALL. I have filed a support ticket but I hope this is resolved.

So in conclusion: Amazing performance for price in limited testing. I am worried it may not have a long life due ways they must have saved on the price. In a pinch I needed a tablet for Zbrush that has all the features of my old Intuos (this actually has better resolution and pressure levels) for less money and on that front it delivers so far in SPADES....on the previous version of Zbrush 2020 which is fine for now.

Final word: Totally worth the financial risk...so far

title: Rejuvenates and improves the Beats Studio line!
text:
I had an old pair of Beats Studio 2 Wireless that had been worn out - Specifically in the ear cushions. The rest of the headphones were like new, but the cracks and blown seams of the cushions made them something I didn't pull out on the airplane anymore - Embarassing how after only 3 years of moderate use, these pads were worn to this degree. I really thought I was just going to have to replace the headphones to remedy the situation, but then I found Wicked Cushions on Amazon!

Not only are these new cushions an EXACT FIT and FULL REPLACEMENT for the OEM cushions, but there are several key things that make buying these better than any others on Amazon that seem to be more of a knock-off than these:

- These are slightly thicker than OEM and are made from a seemingly more comfortable memory foam, and a seemingly better surface material that holds up better to head sweat and creasing.
- Wicked Cushions has a great warranty program and seems to back their products well.
- Wicked Cushions supports their products with EXCELLENT installation guidance online
- These are well made and more solid feeling than competitor items, and use 3M adhesive that should hold better than even the original. They also include all of the base hardware so that you can COMPLETELY remove the old cushion frame and replace with these - Some of their competitors offer a cheap "stick on" solution that mounts over the old frame, resulting in a cheap rigged fix.

The new cushions should be mounted to clean, dry surfaces (the kit will include Alcohol prep wipes) and then "clamped" for several hours to cure the adhesive. I used a few shipping boxes to "stretch" the headphones over overnight to ensure that they were compressed into the frame of the Beats so that the adhesive set in properly. No issues since! These look and feel like they're brand new!

My Beats Studio 2 Wireless are literally like new again - I've got one of my favorite pair of headphones back! I'm so excited! You will be too!

title: It can work, but manufacturing is sloppy
text: Popped it into a X-T2 and worked like a charm. Did the same with a X-T3 and the camera wouldn't turn on. I then gave it an additional push into the battery chamber and the camera turned on. Seemed like the adapter wasn't making a firm connection with the contacts in the battery compartment. Did some investigation and measured that the height of the adapter at about a half millimeter shorter than the official Fujifilm battery measured where the orange clip in the battery compartment captures the battery. A close look at the contacts on the adapter (see attached picture) have an imperfect slightly raised seam running along the contacts. Basically the adapter wasn't built close enough to the size specifications of a Fujifilm battery to work reliably in all cameras which use this size battery. It might work or it might not. I'm going to try and fix it so it works all the time. First thing I'll try is adding some plastic tape to the end to add back the missing half millimeter which should seat the adapter a little bit deeper in the battery compartment. If that doesn't do enough, I'll try to smooth out the raised seam. Unfortunately, Fujifilm discontinued their OEM version of this product so we are only left with 3rd party solutions.

title: Not even close to what I expected. VERY LITTLE BASS.
text:
Listened to it for 3 minutes, tried a couple of my BT speaker test songs, went on-line to get a return authorization.
Save your money and get the Anker SoundCore Boost 20W for single speaker use.

The Tribit MaxSound Plus 24W is also a VERY good option for a small, superior bass and fullness of sound from a small speaker. They cannot be paired but man those little speakers sound very good. They sound better than the Anker Sound Boost 20W in all ranges, but do not have as rich of bass. Depending on the song, volume, and speaker positioning, it is often a toss up of which sounds better, the Anker or the Tribit!

Or, get a PAIR of OontZ Angle 3 Ultra for $70, they play in stereo and when placed correctly, they have much better bass than the Motion.

Another good option are the OontZ Angle 3XL Ultras. Their bass is solid, but they pair and sound outstanding in stereo. AND, they cost $79 each. Head to Head with the Motion, I would take the OontZ Angle 3XL Ultra all day.

This speaker does not even come close to being worth the money being asked. I used EQ and still could not get the music to sound as rich and full as this speakers little brother, the Anker SoundCore Boost 20W.
The Motion does pair, the Anker SoundCore Boost 20W does not. Classic product rollout to force you into spending more. I have a pair of Oontz XL3 Angles that are a bit weak on bass, but when paired and listening to music ion true stereo, the Oontz speakers rock and for less than what you would pay for the Anker speaker.
With the Motion you have to keep the volume down to less than 50% to get the bass to actually have any impact. And even at the lower volumes if very weak.

Anker would have been better off making a Anker SoundCore Boost XL or II, which allows them to be pared in true stereo or dual stereo.
Okay, I have tried more songs as I am typing this and I cannot find a reason to keep this speaker. The Anker SoundCore Boost 20W sounds much better though not as loud as the Motion. The Anker SoundCore Boost 20W cannot be paired. Anker could not make the Anker SoundCore Boost 20W pairable, it would overlap and best the Motion!
Listening to "Died in Your Arms" by The Cutting Crew, and the bass is distorted, and I am playing the song at 40% without max bass EQ setting!

title: BE CAREFUL. HACKED....
text:
So I have had these camera’s for about 6 months now, and am now ready to write a review. I purchased these last July 2019 (as a recommendation from a friend) because my boyfriend’s ex-stepson was staying with us during the summer and I felt he might possibly be mistreating my dog (when no one else was home). I bought memory cards for each camera and placed 1 in the bedroom camera and 1 in the living room camera. I labeled them “bedroom” and “living room.” Fast forward to the end of October 2019 I have my son (as I was pregnant during the summer). The stepson is gone so now I decide to use these camera’s to watch the baby (if I need to run to bathroom, etc...). My baby’s grandma is also now in town for a few months to help out and started noticing clicking noises (the sound of pictures being taken) in the middle of the night on one of the cameras. We switched shifts staying up with the baby and I noticed the same thing (mostly in the early am). I logged in 1 morning (to the app) while hearing the clicks, and you can actually see a flash of light and a quick pause go off in the monitor with each click (as if someone is taking pictures). Then I also realized that these repeated clicks happen every time the baby starts crying.... it’s as if this monitor’s access is being live fed to perverted viewers who have access. Another thing I realized is that it only happened on the camera labeled “bedroom.” ☹️ I changed the labels about a month ago to camera “1” and “2”. I left them unplugged and decided to use one the other day to watch baby as I took a quick shower. The camera previously labeled “living room” worked good and no clicks. Then we rearranged the house and the camera previously labeled “bedroom” got plugged back in on accident and I didn't realize it (although it was left facing the wall). So here I am (415am) this morning and I hearing the clicks going on again for the camera previously labeled “bedroom” and then I realize it’s plugged back in.
So here are some suggestions if you have to use the camera. First off, don’t put labels such as “bedroom” or “babies room” for camera I.d’s in the app, have a good WiFi password, and also use a Face ID or password access to the app and also Another password to access the camera’s logged in. That being said... although I have done all that now, the camera previously labeled “bedroom” still gets hacked and I won’t be using it anymore at all. I was reading a computer article the other day on what the dark web is and I’m honestly pretty sure there are a ton of sickos on there with hidden, encrypted browsers watching our kids or even us. BE CAREFUL. I will now only turn on the second camera (previously labeled living room) when I hop in the shower real quick to monitor the baby in the crib. As soon as I’m done I face it back towards the wall. First sign of clicks on that camera too and I will no longer be using it. I’m absolutely disturbed by this. I actually read a review before buying this camera that another mother’s baby’s room had a man watching her daughter and she could hear him talking to the baby in the middle of the night. She also heard crunching of potato chips when she logged into the app to see what was going on. I thought that was crazy, but probably rare. Now I realize that these camera’s are hacked more often then we realize. I’m now also sure that the hackers type in keywords such as “bedroom” or “baby’s room” or what not to look for their victims. This is the only reason I am giving this camera a low star... other than that it works very well.

If my main drive malfunctions, I can just plop this ADATA ssd in and keep working until I receive a replacement.. It actually runs Windows 10 well enough that I don't feel like it's hurting me in productivity.

On the other hand, I think there are many ssds out there that are faster and probably more reliable. AS SSD Benchmark rates the ADATA at 610 while my Intel 540s comes in at 979, but costs more than twice the ADATA. Since I use the Intel ssd all day long, the extra money for the faster speed makes sense to me. But for a clone drive the ADATA is a better business decision.

title: Perfect for the home video enthusiast
text:
I got this camera to take with us on our family vacation, and it served its purpose well. I wanted something that would be easy to use, so that we could all have our videos in one place, rather than scattered amongst everyone’s phones. The picture quality isn’t perfect, but if you want the good old-fashioned home video style, this is the camera for you. It’s so easy to use, even my grandmother was able to operate it without any trouble!

The camera arrived fully charged (which was awesome bc it arrived hours before we left), and was super easy to assemble the attachments. The microphone is absolutely necessary to use if you wish to use footage with the sound. The microphone that is built in to the camera is not very good on its own, but the attachment definitely makes up for that.

The stabilizer gives the little camera a look that makes it seem more expensive than it is, which is another plus. Not to mention that it really does help stabilize the footage so you can easily walk and film without making the videos cause motion sickness while watching it lol.

The touch screen is an awesome bonus. It makes it even easier to view the videos and change around your settings.

The camera body itself looks and feels high quality. It’s lightweight, yet solid feeling (doesn’t feel cheap at all). It’s also small enough to be able to stick in the case it comes with, and easily slide into a purse or backpack.

This camera served its purpose and I am so thankful it captured our memories so easily from our trip. I will definitely be bringing it along for any of our future adventures!

title: It’s an okay soundbar
text:
I’m not going to write an in-depth review, I’m sure there are many of those already but I will tell you what I think of this speaker after about 9 months of ownership. As a soundbar, it works well enough but there are aspects of the way in which it works that aren’t terribly intuitive. Firstly, the setup seems easy enough, but you have to download an app to do it. And you have to use that app anytime you want to stream to it. The Sonos app uses its own player for the different apps you already have on your phone, like Spotify, Amazon, and so on. Which means if you’re listening to music on Spotify in your car and you want to pick up where you left off at home, you can’t do that. For one song, that isn’t a big deal but if you’re 40 songs into a playlist, 40 minutes into a podcast, or 40 chapters into an audiobook, it’s really inconvenient to have to use the Sonos app to play these things on the beam. Either it won’t remember where the apps left off or the apps won’t remember where it leaves off and it’s just a pain to use. If it’s connected to my television via arc, it should be able to stream via Bluetooth from any app.

That’s like most of my gripe with this thing but also the “night” and “voice” modes don’t work very well either. The sound in general is very mediocre. It sounds fine, but no better than many cheaper options. Even after the sound optimization the app takes 10 minutes to do when you start it up for the first time. I don’t know what it is about the night mode that these new speakers have so much trouble with. I had an old JVC surround receiver back in the late 90s that achieved a far superior night mode where it just cuts out the bass, levels out the mids, and boosts the highs. The Sonos beam does not do this well. I live in a 700 sq/foot apartment, it shouldn’t suck at this kind of thing. But it does.

And for some reason, Alexa doesn’t respond to my voice commands for the volume anymore. I don’t know if that is due to adding the arc input a couple of months after I started using it when I got a new 4K set with arc out, allowing me to control the volume from the tv remote, or if it just doesn’t work. Using the app for this was neither convenient nor precise, which was why the voice control was useful.

All and all, it’s an okay soundbar. If you want one with the best sound, buy the Sennheiser Ambeo for $2500. The Sonos is slightly more expensive than most in this class, decent sound for casuals, but after 9 months of owning this, I’m considering buying the Roku smart soundbar. It’s essentially the same thing with a built-in roku ultra 4K HDR streaming device for $180. I doubt very seriously it sounds any worse than the Sonos beam.

title: Basic cable management
text:
One set of these organizers is enough to cover one side of a typical 42U network rack; each piece is about half a rack in length.

The D-rings are simple injection-molded plastic parts, identical to the freebies that are often included with network racks. In this case, they're already screwed to a rail that connects to the rack's quick-connect slots on the side rails. The rings are on the small side, and will not be adequate for more than about 20 Ethernet cables. The rings are pretty durable, and can withstand a respectable amount of abuse without breaking.

If your rack came with plastic D-rings to screw into place, this part offers only two advantages: you don't have to screw them in, and there will probably be more D-rings per foot.

If you intend to run multiple patch panels in your network rack, you'll probably want higher-capacity wire management than this. For basic needs, it's adequate.

This is the first time I've been able to install a screen protector with no bubbles and no lint underneath it on the first try. Seriously, watch the video.

And it really feels like drawing on paper. I use Procreate, and this screen protector is having no issues picking up pressure sensitivity from the 1st generation Apple Pencil. You can definitely feel the grain—and while that might mean a more quickly worn nib in the future, it's a trade-off for the tactile feedback it gives me while drawing and sketching.

As a bonus, it makes flashcard apps like Anki much more intuitive. I'm retaining information much more easily, and I do think the tactile feedback that makes me feel like I'm flipping actual flashcards helps that.

Yes, it does give the screen a 'frosted over' look. But again, a trade-off, and not something that'll bother most artists. If you use the iPad Pro it'll definitely be more noticeable due to how it affects color, but I'm on a Early 2018 9.7" iPad and didn't lose much.

The only suggestion I have for BERSEM is to make a screen protector that completely encases the Home button, rather than just going around it, and for someone fluent in English to proofread their materials—some of it is hard to understand due to the language barrier.

If planning on taking this on portable shoots, you should find it to be an excellent choice, but plan to add an carrying case of some sort - the included one will carry the stands, but not the lighting or backdrop.
It indicates that it adjusts from 5'-10' in width. The crossbar does adjust to allow the stated width change. The backdrops, however, are a bit more of a "subject to interpretation" thing. They have a rod slot sewn in that allows it to be hung in the 6' wide arrangement easily. If you want to use it in a wide format, you'll need to use the included clamps, and that comes with a slew of hassles - definitely not a "set it and forget it" thing.

If the 6' wide format is your thing and you're in a single location or have easy other ways of packing it, then this is a simply glorious kit for the price. If you need the other factors, then you'll have to do a little bit of adjusting (thus the knock down to 4 stars).

title: Small Monitor Solution | Large TV Shows Flaws
text:
[[VIDEOID:59229e953de865e4245759c3194cf640]] I left a video so you can get a feel for how this adapter will be like, after all its for playing games. First picture is 1080, second is 720, third is my LG TV (2013) default AVI input.

At $9.99, this adapter does what it's supposed to. It converts RCA AVI to HDMI. It doesn't do the best job, but it also doesn't do the worst.

-- Image --
At 720p, the image will be more vivid, but much more blurry. At 1080p, the image will be less vivid, but a tad more sharp. If your game has text, I would suggest putting it to 1080p.

-- Audio --
The audio is mastered way beyond what it should be, and as such many sound effects will sound like they are being played by an old Nokia phone with the sound turned at full volume. Not a big problem if it is a small setup and you don't care about audio quality that much.

-- Lag --
Input lag is VERY minimal, I can barely tell any latency, for that I say kudos. Melee compatible? If you aren't Hungrybox or Mango, yes.

-- Recommend? --
For $9.99, I would recommend this to somebody who has a small monitor setup, cheaper speakers, and doesn't care about the greatest quality. It comes with a USB cable and the adapter, and for that I say it's worth $10.

If you have a large TV setup and are looking for greater quality, I would look to a more professional (albeit more expensive) solution.

title: Extremely disappointed
text:
Like some other reviewers, the main issue with this subwoofer is the lack of a power on switch. The only options are auto on or powered off. The other option is a 12-volt trigger to turn the subwoofer on and off with the receiver. However, my receiver is a Sony STR-DN1080 that does not support or have a connection for a 12 volt trigger. My receiver manual specifically says that any subwoofer auto on should be turned off. However, this subwoofer does not afford the option of simply powering on the unit. Therefore with the subwoofer set to auto on the only way it switches out of its sleep mode is if I crawl behind the tv, flip the switch from auto on to off and then back to auto. Not going to do that. Once on the subwoofer sounds ok (not nearly as good as I had hoped though). If I leave the switch to off I never get any sound to come out of the subwoofer so that switch is just a power off switch and not disabling auto on like my previous sony subwoofer. I spent hours last night playing with settings on my receiver to see if I could get this to work correctly yet no matter what I have done is if the subwoofer goes into hybernation (LED on back goes red) then the only way it will recognize the receiver is on is if I toggle the switch on the back.
I have made sure all of my speakers are setup as small on my receiver, set the fronts and center to a crossover of 80 and my surrounds at 110, connected via LFE and still the same thing.
I will be hooking back up my 15 year old Sony subwoofer that sounds fairly close to as good as this unit and allows me to disable auto power on mode. I thought a brand new subwoofer would take my home theatre up a notch but sadly this fell way short of expectations.
EDIT: I think my review may be a little unfair even though it didn't work out for my situation. While I am still very disappointed with this unit it is primarily because of the "auto on" or just off issue that doesn't work with my receiver, the unit does possess very, very powerful bass that can be awesome when watching an action movie. It did blow my old subwoofer out of the water with power and room shaking bass. My wife felt the house shake completely on the other side of the house when I was watching a movie. For my 16x12 home theatre room this subwoofer seemed a little too powerful that impacted my perception of sound quality. To be fair if I didn't have the issue with only "auto on" or off I would have kept this subwoofer and worked with dialing it in so the whole house didn't shake. The really big disappointment was the auto on not working in my setup.
I sent back the HTS 10 and got the Polk Audio DSW Pro 440 (8 inch instead of a 10 inch). The HTS 10 inch subwoofer was enormous. This subwoofer was about the same size as my old subwoofer. This clearly doesn't have the same power as the HTS 10 but has an "on" feature and also the "auto on" feature on this subwoofer works with my receiver. The 440 sounds good but isn't nearly as powerful as the HTS 10 (cannot expect it to be as powerful, just pointing it out). I am happy with the 440 but I did have to turn up the subwoorer volume to 30 (out of 40) and it still shakes my theatre room but not the entire house :)

title: Awesome solution for Macbook Pro users with a minor caveat.
text:
Like every Razer item I've purchased, it's top notch quality products and the best bang for the buck. The Razer Core X eGPU seemed quite expensive at first but if you factor in power supply, control board, and quality; it's a great bargain. I've assembled every Win PC gaming rig that I've owned and use Macbook Pros for work. I recently upgraded to 2x BenQ 4K displays since the price was right and the WFH situation made it the right time... which is how I discovered the Razer Core X / eGPUs.

My Macbook Pro (15" mid 2015) is "kind of" capable of running 2 4K monitors but noticed performance issues when the 4K resolution is scaled to 1440p. macOS shows a warning for this under display settings when changing the resolution. It's either 1080p or 4K where it doesn't bog down. Well, we all know 4K on a 27" monitor is going to make everything very tiny and the 1080p resolution is going to be in yo face but the picture quality is amazing. I prefer the 1440p with the better image quality reason I went 4K rather than native 1440p. 5K is just still super expensive.

Some folks will probably be like why dual 4K?! I'm a software engineer so the extra real estate for the IDE / Text Editor on one screen and the rest on the other is what I've always preferred. The 1440p in high def makes the text look amazing. I know, I know... folks be like, you got a 4K for TEXT and 2 of them?! ... Yes, my eyes are not the same as they were over a decade ago when I started my software development career.

Anyway, back to how I got here. The MBP was sluggish due to the GPU. My specific model is described to work with 1 5K external monitor. Makes sense, it's a 5 year old laptop GPU powering dual 4K. I needed to upgrade my GPU and researched some solutions. I was disappointed finding out there's no native macOS support for Thunderbolt 2 and eGPUs but I found purge-wrangler.sh.

After following the basic instructions from the purge-wrangler github page, it was plug and play. I installed an AMD RX580... YES, an AMD... I have not purchased a desktop AMD card ever since the whole Bitcoin mining phase, people were forced to turn to NVIDIA cards. It all works great on my MBP. Also, I have this connected to a 4 port DisplayPort KVM for dual monitors. It works, make sure to buy the official Apple TB3 to TB2 since it's bidirectional and get a TB certified cable to plug into the adapter.

# Pros
- Quality packaging as always (stickers swag) 👏
- Quality product, paint, mesh, design, etc. 🙌
- Works with MBP (15" mid 2015, and a 13" MB Air 2012) TB2 (with install scripts) - Apple's limitation 🤦‍♂️
- macOS detected my monitors supported HDR and displayed an enable/disable checkbox in the display settings where as before it didn't 🤔
- Might have the highest wattage support compared to other competitors at the time of this review. Can support most high end GPUs but double check the dimensions and power requirements! 🥇
- The swivel / lock handle design - 👌
- It can play games with the RX580 but nowhere close to what my 1070Ti on the PC can do. I'm upgrading to a 5700XT since I got a Prime Day deal on it.
- Can play fortnite, cs:go, left4dead, etc. I suggest a better card since the Razer X is designed for some serious gaming GPUs. The RX580 is an insult for what this eGPU enclosure can support. However, if you don't care about gaming in high/ultra settings, software & web development, CAD, video editing etc. then a RX580 paired with this enclosure is a great upgrade.

# Cons
- Leaving idle state, the fans spin quickly causing some fan noise. It's only like a second or two. Not that big of a deal. Might be the GPU + Enclosure combo. Will find out with the 5700XT swap.

# Neutral
- Ventilation - can be used as a mini space heater for the winter by playing games at ultra settings. Not sure how much the office will warm up during the summer. It's fall.
- Some people complained theirs "didn't power on". You have to plug in a TB3 cable. Most people will assume they would see some kind of light or power when flipping the PSU switch. Wasn't the case and it left me scratching my head a bit. My situation with purge-wrangler had me connect the cable during script install. Razers instructions were to plug in the TB cable THEN flip the PSU switch.
- Wish it came with a longer TB3 cable but they sell longer TB cables separately. That's how they can keep the price low b/c a 6.6 FT TB2 cable cost me $45 so be glad it came with one.

title: Broken (Faulty) Hinge
text:
My son has had this for only 6 months. Tried to contact seller, but i was passed my return date. They said to contact Dell so I did. They want to take it for 2 weeks (Kids School Laptop) plus charge me over $60 PLUS parts. So I guess no valid warrantee??? I'm still working with them but not much luck happening.

If you look at this unit carefully, you will see that it's only supported by a middle Bracket system for the screen. This makes the screen shift from side to side and not held with 2 brackets at the ends of the screen like most others. Every time you open and close it, there is way too much pressure on the bracket and middle portion. The rivets holding it all together fails. This is what happened with many opening and closing of our screen. Basically, the bracket gave out and busted the screen wide open, rivets fell apart, and the screen came apart and even cracked the bottom edge. It's held together with duct tape now!!!!! I saw another review for this and a class action lawsuit. I can understand why.

I don't recommend this at all. There is clearly a defect and bad design issue going on.

The system itself is good. I have no issues with it. But, to expensive and to new for me to be out $800+ with zero support!

Update: Dell has not gotten back whatsoever. Never shipped the shipping cont. No warrantee with big costs. Horrible service.
I did take it all apart myself and got my old soldering gun and super glue out. Managed to make it work somewhat. I found there is actually 2 brackets inside the one mechanism. The tension on the single middle section was the main issue, which busted the rivets out and broke the frame apart. So the hinges were workable still but just not attached to anything. So that's how I kind of fixed it. Soldered and glued the rivets back, glued the frame, and a couple pieces of electrical tape on the bottom of the screen. Had to throw out the middle section hiding the hinges.

title: The most affordable sound this good has ever been (that I've seen).
text:
I’ve spent years and years slowly accumulating, selling, trading, and updating my audio setup in order to squeeze the absolute most out of it that I can. Over the years, I’ve had ample opportunity to listen to a broad collection of speakers from all of the bang-for-the-buck usual suspects. Edifier, Audioengine, Dayton, ELAC, Emotiva, (plus all of the amplifier brands you’d expect to be discussed in the same breath with those speaker manufacturers). This process has been somewhat complicated by the fact that I don’t live near any stores where I could audition most of the stuff I’m interested in buying, so I just have to know those return policies by heart and not buy anything that I’ll be locked in to without a chance to really listen first.

I’ve either owned or known people who’ve owned pretty much all of the popular entry-level and step-up speakers from these companies. I won’t list them. If you’re on this page, you probably already know what they are.

Most of what I’ve owned thus far hasn’t really scratched the audio itch the way I’d like. I’ve gone to audio fests too many times and had my face melted off by stereos I can’t possibly afford. And, while drooling over the really fancy-pants stuff is fun, it also makes your ears a bit snobby in a way that’s hard to reverse. Every time I come home from an audio event, my own stereo sounds a bit worse. Fancy that.

For the past couple of years, I’ve focused primarily on putting together a good headphone listening setup because that’s proved the most cost-effective way to acquire satisfying sound. Sadly for me, I like listening to music for hours on end, but I don’t particularly like having headphones on my oversized noggin for hours on end. Even the most comfortable headphones I’ve found get uncomfortable after a couple of hours, although, for what it's worth, the MrSpeakers Aeon Flow Open is the closest I have to a headphone that doesn't, and it sounds great.

If that seems like the end of an overly long lead-in, that’s because it is. Vanatoo represents the first time I’ve ever heard a full sound system in this price range (IE, $600 all-in, including speakers, DAC, and amplifier) that sounds more like a baby cousin of the sound systems I've been delighted by at the audio fests than like a brother or sister of the value brand offerings we all know and love*. I’m not saying the Vanatoo T1Es sound like Magico towers with $50K of electronics behind them. That kind of hyperbole is absurd and is a popular feature of speaker review sections. The T1Es don’t sound like that. But they DO provide more of the detail, imaging, separation, resolution, and dynamics that I normally expect from higher-end gear than do any of the similarly priced offerings I’ve heard from the brands I mentioned above, specifically when you factor in the cost of amplification. The fact that the T1E accomplishes this in a very compact box with internal electronics that obviate the need to spend a bunch of extra money on a DAC or amp is just pure gravy. I expect the very precise matching of electronics with the drivers has something to do with their beautiful sound.

The T1E's bass is very well extended for such a small speaker. The mids push voices a bit forward but in a way that I enjoy. The highs are sparkly and crisp, probably more so than most other speakers in the price range, but they don't sound distorted or harsh. Good rendering of textural detail, for me, is one of the real hallmarks of a good speaker/amp combo, and the T1Es definitely do not disappoint. The microtexture of the rosin on a cello bow gliding across a string, finely-grained rendering of high-frequency fuzz in a synth note, those sorts of details bring music fully to life. I don't believe I've heard such good rendering of texture in this price range (speaker + amp + DAC cost) from anyone other than Vanatoo, headphones excluded. An iFi iDSD Nano BL with one of Massdrop's Sennheiser HD6XXs is, at $400, probably the best sound I've heard available in the mid to low hundreds (as of mid 2019).

In summary, I’d recommend getting these over getting a pair of ELAC B6.2s or Emotiva B1s or, frankly, any other famous bang-for-the-buck bookshelf speakers in this general price vicinity. The T1Es sound quite a bit better, to me, than any of the other speakers I've mentioned, and I've only ever heard any of them on DAC/amp setups that cost more than $300 which is the amount you'd have to keep your DAC and amp below in order to match the price of the T1Es. I’d also recommend the Vanatoos over any of the powered speakers in their price bracket as well. The T1E just has better tonal balance, imaging, separation, and resolution than any powered speakers I’ve heard from Edifier, Audioengine, or Klipsch, to name a few. I guess one thing I HAVEN'T done is try the Dayton B652s with a $550 amplifier, a setup which would match the T1Es' $600 price point. Something tells me that it wouldn't outdo the T1E.

Finally, here are a couple of thoughts on alternatives. I do have a pair of Vanatoo T0s in my home office, and they're easily the best setup I've experienced at the $300ish price point (again, specifically factoring in amp and DAC). If you're intending to put these speakers in a small room, say, under 150 sq ft, the T0s would probably be great for you, assuming you won't be moving them into a larger room eventually. On the other hand, if you already have a decent DAC and amp, and you're realizing that you don't necessarily need or want powered bookshelf speakers, the Goldenear Aon 2 is a bookshelf speaker that I think sounds pretty darned great for its price. If you look up reviews for them, you'll find that the critical response is a bit divided, but I think they're delightful. Just my 2 cents.

I think Schiit Audio's PYST USB cable is a great match for the T1E. Sparkly, tight, and punchy, with good texture detail, separation, and imaging. At $24 (here on Amazon), I thought they were every bit as good as Audioquest's Forest USB, which I use for my headphone setup, and PYST is only about half the price. If you're not sold on the idea of buying schmancier cables, that's totally a-OK. If you do think cables matter, I think PYST is a great USB cable to use with these that doesn't break the bank. I think it easily bests the included USB cable (although it is excellent of Vanatoo to include so many cords with the speakers) as well as Amazon Basics USB cables. So, if you believe in cables, PYST is a very reasonably priced way to make sure that your T1Es aren't being undermined by shoddy connections.

*And I DO love them. They’ve provided me with thousands of hours of better-than-Bose listening pleasure at prices for which they ought to be sainted.

UPDATE (6/25/2019): I primarily bought the T1Es for use at work. I'm pretty satisfied at the moment with my home office and living room setups, but my work listening situation wasn't ideal. I work in a creative/marketing dept., and we enjoy listening to music in our room which is a good 30 feet down the hall and isolated by several walls from any rooms that anybody else uses or works in. We all have decent desktop headphone setups at the office, but it's more fun to listen to music together while we work. The room we're listening in is about 18' x 24'. The T1Es filled the room reasonably well, and the bass response was impressive for such small speakers, but I thought it'd be fun to see how they perform with a sub, so I brought the Dayton Sub 800 that I use in my home office to work, and I have to say that offboarding the low frequencies (below 80hz) from the T1Es to the sub does allow the the overall sound to become richer and more room-filling. I adjusted the gain setting on the sub to blend the bass to levels that sound about how the Vanatoos sound without a sub. We don't listen at ear-splitting levels, but even at the slightly-above-medium volumes that we've occasionally listened to, I've found that the subwoofer assistance gives the T1Es a sense of ease and composure that they didn't have at higher volumes previously. The mid-bass, mids, and highs coming through the T1Es when the sub's attached seem seem a little more unrestrained. No surprise that the woofer vibrations are much reduced when the sub's attached. The low end on the Vanatoos without the sub is tighter and more detailed, but that's to be expected with a $99 sub.l I have to say that the little $99 Dayton sub is a pretty decent dance partner for the Vanatoos, but if you don't want to sacrifice low-end detail, and you're planning to use this with a sub long-term, I'd recommend investing in something a little nicer than the Dayton. The takeaway for me is that these really sing with a sub. Matched with, say, an RSL Speedwoofer, I think you'd have a compelling, full-range system with tight, deep bass, gorgeous mids, and sparkly highs for only $1000.

Update 12/18/2019: I've noticed that the NAD 3020 can be had from some sellers for around $300 as of this writing. That's a pretty sweet little amplifier. I haven't heard it with the ELACs or Emotivas I mentioned above, but I reckon it would sound pretty darn good, and it would cost about the same as the T1E. Much lower power, but it might be worth considering as an alternative if you don't want powered speakers. Just a thought.

title: High failure rate, test first.
text:
Using AC inputs with 24 VAC transformer secondary, unit developed unstable output that varied with load. So I tried connecting AC across one of the input rails and 0 center input (ground, from looking at the board layout). Plus side output worked fine, but minus side put out -36 and then magic smoke.

Even if this want the right way to drive the input, nothing was connected on the output but the voltmeter so this should not have happened. None of the polar components appear to be reversed.

The circuit I received is radically different than the one from the other review. The only diodes are the four in the input rectifier bridge. These connect straight to the filter (not coupling, which would be in series) capacitors, which shunt to ground.

Double checked wiring and made sure there were no shorts. Waited too long to test it.

Good thing I didn't test it in circuit, could have blown up my device.

text:
I originally tried the HS610 and liked it until I found out about the pressure sensitivity burst issue. I then found out that this product, the H1060P, did not have that issue. So I got Amazon to take back the HS610 (which they did with no problem at all) and traded it for the H1060P. I like this tablet very well. There are a couple difference from HS610 I'd like to point out as I didn't realize them until I got the H1060P. The biggest one is the HS610 has a slight texture to the surface which gives a nice paper like feel when using the pen. The H1060P has a smooth shiny surface with no texture. The pen glides completely effortlessly, unless there is some finger oil smudged on it. In that case, the pen will stop in it's tracks. I haven't had a problem with that. I just make sure not to touch the writing surface with the tips of my fingers. There is plenty of non-writing surface to grab onto. And the tablet comes with a glove. This tablet is a bit thicker than the HS610. But the H1060P does have a nice rounded edge which makes it comfortable to rest my wrist on. There is no circular button on the H1060P. This is clearly visible in the pictures. I'm just noting it because it's an important difference between the two tablets.

I'm mostly using this in GIMP. The pressure and tilt work very well in that program.
I would definitely recommend considering this tablet.

title: Quality Remote, Multiple uses
text:
This is a nice way to add some additional navigational options within your setup.

My main display is a TV and it's not as easy to manage doing repetitive tasks without having much room to properly stretch out. I also frequently use my Projector with my Nvidia Shield and this is a quick way to have better access than using the remote software.

It's easy to point and navigate as well as scroll through pages on a site, you can easily click items, make orders, control YouTube even from a distance. I like to have noise on in the house, especially if the kids are asleep and sometimes you have to be available to press OK or click skip, the range on this remote is great I can control from anywhere in the room (so long as you can see your cursor, (which you can change how it appears within windows settings)

The design is nice, it feels good in the hands, charges up via microusb so I don't have to worry about having batteries, simply take the usb receiver and attach to your device.

It's great if you work on a lot of devices and don't want to designate a full sized keyboard just to do infrequently used commands. I have a similar remote I bought to use with an emulation setup I built earlier in the year and it's great being able to access commands or type commands without having to go through the hassle of getting out a keyboard and setting it up that way, especially if you're playing the device on a couch or somewhere where it's not as practical to have a keyboard available. I wanted something like that for my PC that I could also use with my projector.

The keyboard is a QWERTY layout, my thumbs go across the keys naturally when typing (brings me back to the slider phone days), the buttons are like those on your typical remote, they have a nice solid and responsive feel.

You can use the remote like a nintendo wii mote to move around your screen and select options, if you ever used a Wii you'll know what I'm talking about, it's like that but without the trackbar and now for your PC. Voice commands work well (handy when using my shield attached to the projector).

Overall a very solid pickup, if you think something like this can enhance your life and you have ways to use it, you wouldn't be disappointed with picking this up as an option.

title: Yes. The answer is yes.
text:
I've been looking for something that produces good clean, FULL, sound for over a month now. Everywhere I went produced really low quality headphones or earbuds that touted "BIG BASS." (Red flag) All well and good except once you put those $40-$70 headphones on and find out it sounds like you're listening to a tin can on a string. People all over the world are spending, collectively, thousands of dollars, RIGHT NOW, for sound that does not live up to the amount flying out of their wallets. $40 is all you need to start on your journey of every increasing sound quality, but you have to search online, more on that below.

These in ear monitors are so good it's actually kind of creepy. When you first put them on and listen to them it feels like somebody is in the room right there with you! The bass is all here folks and it's clean, not a wobbly mess, but more importantly so is the treble! People's voices actually sound real instead of like an MP3 that been re-encoded 17 times over the course of twenty years. The cable is braided (Cool, reduces electrical interference through the wire). The cable is braided like a chain link (Really cool! It's really sturdy). The cable is detachable (Alright!!). Accidentally break the cable? Replace it cheap. The monitors themselves are sturdy, beautiful, fit comfortably, and block out external sounds very well.

It's about $150 out of your wallet. Expect to keep these two little guys for years. Also, when you're buying at this level your IEMs actually need to get broken in over time. You can search some procedures online but it basically consists of playing some music at about 50% volume capacity for some hours and then playing pink noise over night. This improves the malleability of the vibrating parts and actually increases the range of sounds that the drivers can produce. In other words, it sounds better the longer you use these not worse.

Take this from me, do not buy headphones or earbuds in retail stores unless it is a specialty store and you know exactly what you're looking for before you go in there and at what price, otherwise you are wasting your time and money. You need to shop online for this stuff and do a little research. Search "best IEM [current year™] under [dollar amount]" to get started. To start off you want to look for FORUMS or community based comment sections, not necessarily professional reviews as it's hard to know what's real or an just an ad.

Although honestly, since you're already here, you probably are already doing that, as people don't naturally find something like this unless they know what they're looking for. This is the best bang for your buck at THIS level of spending based on my research as of April 2019.

title: If it points straight at the screen, it's perfect.  The manual keystone is the issue
text: Let me start by saying, this is a really good value, period !  This projector is compact, light weight (less than 3 lbs), bright, easy to hook up to with tons of inputs, and less than $120.  There is not a zoom function, you just move it back to make it a bigger picture.  We need about 15 ft to get it to fill our 110 inch screen.  The drawback (minus one star) is that the keystone adjustment on this projector is manual.  This means that the picture gets wobbled by a mirror to get the shape back.  This causes the picture to get out of focus at the bottom (for a projector below the centerline of the screen).  You can't adjust the focus to get the whole picture in focus if you have adjusted the keystone.  We happily live with a slightly deformed picture shape at this picture quality and price.  The built in speaker is loud enough to get by if you aren't hooking up to a sound bar or amplifier so it is pretty stand alone if needed.  The elevation adjustment is a screw-type and there is not a side-to-side adjust.  As a whole, a great value.  If only the keystone actually worked.

title: If you are active in any way at all this is not the product for you
text:
Had the watch for 4 months paid for with hard earned money.
Read all of the reviews and the ads from Apple made it sound like it was pretty durable. I actually did a lot of research on this before buying asking random people that had the watch if they liked it and inquired about it.
Seriously asking random strangers for input. Asking if they felt it was durable and wouldn't break easily.
They all told me yes it was a good product and worth the investment.
Flash forward 4 months later, 4months, removing the watch at night to put on the charger like I have done for the past 4 months. It slipped out of my hand and fell. It fell not even 3 feet and hit the floor. I glanced at it briefly and it seemed fine.
Go to put it on in the morning and I notice a hair line crack. Upon closer inspection I see that the whole screen is cracked and a chip exists in the lower corner. Oh crap, We have the insurance with the service provider hopefully it is covered. No chance, the insurance for devices is a poor investment for the record.
Ok, maybe I can take it to Apple and see if they can fix it and explore my options couldn't be too much they will stand up behind their product. If I explain, after all they advertise that is for an active lifestyle, clearly a 3 foot drop should not have caused damage like this.
Wrong, basically if you are active in any way this watch will break and Apple will not step up on this.
They informed me that I could buy a new watch for $400 and send this one in for repair. After the watch is repaired then I could return it for full refund.
Hmm interesting, as if I have $400 laying around for something like this, it was suggested that I "float" the cost somehow.
So then I ask, How much will the repair be? They said $268, after the visit i was informed on 1-800-MYA-PPLE. The repair is $289.
A repair to a $400 watch which I have had for 4 months that broke from a 3 foot fall to the floor. Spend $289 to fix it and "float" $400 for a temporary replacement.
Apple, you have just created a very very upset person that will continue to tell this story to all people through all forms of media.
Your corporation has forgotten the value of a hard earned dollar and what it means to stand behind a product that you produce and sell.
Lost the care for the working people that have made you so rich.
Shame on you , Shame on you for this
Contact me at Gonetopozo@charter.net if you would like to hear my story and how Apple has forgotten the people that have filled their pockets. What would Steve Job Say?

title: Not for TVs over 60” inferior parts.
text: Mount came in a box but appeared a lot lighter then most tv mounts for a 75” tv. I should have stopped there. When the mount was used and installed with our 75” tv, we noticed 2x super Inferior parts on this mount. The first inferior part on the mount is the, “Tilt Mechanism”. The problem here is the main pic shows a small Allen key type nut to tighten that part of the bracket on the companies main photo. However that is not the case, it is a weak inferior butterfly type plastic nut that is almost impossible to get too, once the TV is mounted any higher then 4.5’. Now we have a tv that is mounted that has to be retightened every 4-5 days it does not stay put the tilt nut does not lock in place, making the top of the TV tilt down towards the floor. Not that much but enough to where it has to be adjusted again. My last mount once installed never had to be readjusted like this. Maybe the weight of the TV “71lbs” but it appears it’s a huge design flaw. The next inferior part is number 5 and 6 called extension arms. They screw into ea. other to mount tv onto the square swivel part of the bracket. These appear weak and slightly bend forward. I believe these parts should have been one solid piece of metal instead of two separate pieces, or at a minimum at least have two extra securing points on the main bracket. These bars only secure with one screw ea. top and bottom. This may have been done for shipping purposes, but I would not mount any tv larger then a 60” and weight of anything over 50lbs with this mount. I am completely unhappy with this purchase and will try to return. Now this hole tv has to be dismounted etc. lots of extra time and energy. Pay the few bucks extra and buy a stronger mount for any tv over a 60”. U won’t regret a better purchase.

The cup your ear to hear outside noise feature isn't that great, so I don't use it. But I do use the other touch controls (volume, skip track, pause/play).

Battery life is good, though it takes a long time to charge. I use them for 8 or so hours a day and only have to charge them every couple of days.

title: Better know what you are doing
text:
After seeing some Youtube videos, I got this to try to revive a Ryobi 40v battery that would no longer charge. It came with zero instructions so you do have to figure things out on your own. There's no indicators for the output either so you'll need a multimeter so you can see the actual output while making adjustments.
I had to connected to an old laptop power brick (19v 4.5A), had to try a few times before the output would actually adjust up to 40v. When charging is taking place, there is a faint clicking sound which is useful to know that it is working. Took nearly an hour to get the battery from 16v to 31v, and it is back to life. Now the Ryobi charger could charge it normally again.
Product description said to add heat dispersion if output is >4A. In my case, output would be around 2A @ 40v. I did place the module on top of a small metal box to help disperse heat, but the whole unit is hot (not just warm) to touch after an hour. So definitely be mindful of heat build up if using for extended period of time.

title: An excellent laptop in the specs I ordered - blisteringly fast
text:
I ordered this with the 20Gb RAM and the 512Gb SSD boot RAM plus 1Tb Hard drive. It loads up and shuts down in just a few seconds. My old laptop took at least 2 minutes to load up. Programs run a lot faster too than on my old 2012 Dell Vostro.
Though I've given this laptop 5 well deserved stars, I do have a couple of things against it, which I think let it down a bit. It has x2 USB2 ports... Why, in 2020 would the manufacturer still install USB2 ports when USB3 are much faster and backwards compatible with USB2? Even my old laptop made in 2012 had all USB3 ports!
Now it does also have 1 USB3 "A" port and one USB3 "C" port. Nothing I have uses a USB3-C so I bought an adapter to USB3-A and that sorted that one out easily.
Another slight downer is that it only has a Micro SD card slot and not a normal sized SD card slot so for anyone who uses normal SD cards, you'd have to buy a separate card reader. This fortunately doesn't really affect me because I can simply plug my phone or cameras directly into the computer using the USB ports.
The biggest bugbear though for me was the absence of an ethernet port. They've done this of course to make the laptop thinner and more lightweight but WiFi is nowhere near as good as a direct connection using ethernet cable.
On WiFi, I was only getting around 15Mbps on a good day. I bought an ethernet to USB3 adapter and that solved it. I now enjoy 70 to 100Mbps internet.
So those caveats aside, I still give this machine, in the configuration I bought it in, a well deserved 5 stars. Apart from the USB2 ports, the other shortfalls can be easily overcome.
