title: Good Speaker For The Price
text:
The Tronsmart Element T6 Plus is a decently sized speaker
and looks very stylish. Features of the Element T6 Plus include: IPX6 water
proofing, 3 types of EQ modes (vocals, 3D deep bass, and extra bass), speaker
pairing (for connecting two of these speakers together), battery pack for
phone charging, an SD card reader, and USB type C. The speaker is a little
larger than others at this price point, but I believe it is because they are
trying to make it a party speaker and they needed space for the battery pack
for charging devices. The device is only $69.99 which is pretty good considering
it comes with a battery pack inside it.

Sound
Let's start off with what everyone wants to know. How good is the sound? Well the
sound isn't bad, but I feel like for its size and price tag it should be better.
The 3 EQ modes do offer different types of listening and depending on the type of
music you like I would say there is a sound that works for almost any genre. It
does get loud, but the louder you go the less bass you here or feel. My favorite
EQ mode was the extra bass mode. I listen to mostly alternative rock type of music
and I found this mode the most pleasing to listen to. Now lets get something straight,
I don't think it has bad sound, I just feel like I have reviewed other speakers in the
same price range that sound either the same or a little better and most of the speakers
are smaller than this one. To me that is saying something. It is more difficult to get
good sound out of smaller speakers than to get good sound out of larger speaker. Don't
think that I don't know that different speaker sizes do different things, but in the
case of a bluetooth speaker that is trying to sound good with a specific size of speaker
for all music it would be easier to tune a larger speaker than a smaller one. JBL and BOSE
are two brands on the more expensive side, but they make my case. They have very small
bluetooth speakers in this same price range and I would argue that they sound better at
higher volumes. Those speaker don't come with a battery pack for charging devices or any
EQ features, so the Tronsmart does have some additional features that I would say still
make it a worth while purchase at this price point. Connecting two of these together would
definitely give you volume and sound quality you would want at a party.

User interface
I feel like it is important for me to talk about the way this speaker works. As with any
bluetooth speaker, you turn it on and look for it in your bluetooth settings on your phone.
Pretty straight forward. One end has a button/dial for pause/play and volume control. It
works pretty good as a pause play button, but I feel like the volume dial needs some work.
I noticed every time I went to either turn the volume up or down, that when I would turn the
dial the volume would go in both directions. If you tried to turn it up, it would go up, but
it would also go down on occasion making it hard to get it to the volume I wanted. The same
went for turning it down. I feel like the dial needs some work to make sure it is changing the
volume appropriately so that it is not a struggle to set the volume properly. This may just be
my unit, but I would guess just because of how it feels while I turn it that it's this way for
all of them. I like the idea of the dial for volume, but I want it to work better. Buttons along
the side of the speaker are labeled well and easy to navigate. Track forward and back buttons,
power button, EQ button, and the button to link two of theses speakers together.

Overview Conclusion
Overall for $69.99 I would say it is a pretty good little speaker. The average user would enjoy
the sound and volume this speaker provides. Great for the person who wants to throw some parties
and have a couple of them in different places in the house to provide a good music experience for
everyone. The battery pack inside for charging other devices is a great feature and USB type C is
fantastic. The fact that they are using the new technology is a good thing. I wish more companies
would adopt USB type C as a standard. With the speaker being IPX6 water proof, these speakers are
also great for an outdoor party. I would absolutely recommend this speaker to anyone looking for
a party speaker under $100. Audiofiles would probably not be into this speaker as much.

title: Surprisingly Good Ultra-Wide
text: I have owned several ultra-wide monitors and this LG 34WL750-B ultra-wide monitor is extremely good. The first thing that one will notice is how easy it is to unbox and setup this monitor. No tools are required. Simply take out the base, attach it to the upright column using the hand twist bolt on the base. Next, carefully take out the display, align it with the two tabs on the top of the upright column and click it into place. Assembly is complete. Attach the monitor with an HDMI cable or display port cable to your computer and you are ready to configure the display. The display comes with a CD, but not much useful content on the CD. To get the correct configuration I had to go to the LG website and download the On Screen Control software, which apparently contains the drivers as well. After my computer restarted I was able to select 3440x1440 for the resolution. This monitor can go to 60 Hz, however I was only able to select up to 50 Hz, most likely due to the video capabilities of my computer. However, the quality at 50 Hz is quite good. I originally used the HDMI cable that came with the monitor, but the monitor complained that the cable being used may cause problems, so I switched to an Ultra HTMI cable and the message went away. Something that really surprised me about this monitor is the quality of the built-in speakers, they are very nice sounding, downward facing speakers. I discovered this When I plaid a video file expecting the sound to come out of the computer speakers and was pleasantly surprised by nice quality sound coming out of the monitor. The audio is being delivered through the HDMI cable to the monitor. I give this monitor two thumbs up.

title: When you just wanna add Bluetooth to an older vehicle.
text:
Installed this in a 2002 4Runner because I was tired of using tape deck adapters to connect to my phone and play music. Now I can get in turn the truck on and it automatically connects with Bluetooth.

Unit connects quickly and starts playing right away. The buttons are easily identified and the volume knob is large enough to adjust without looking at the radio while driving.

Only issue I came across was the clock doesn’t seem to save the time you set therefore reverts back to 12:00 every time you restart it which to me is fine because to even see the clock you have to press the clock button and it just goes back to the audio screen shortly after anyways. Not sure if I wired it wrong but everything else works perfectly.

I will note for anyone installing this in a 3rd gen 4Runner that if you choose to hook up your power antenna be advised that it will raise your antenna every time you start the truck. This annoyed me to the point of disconnecting the power to my antenna. You can however get an adapter and utilize the diversity antenna to still get decent radio reception or get one of those Tacoma whip antenna mods that can be modified to delete the power antenna all together.

title: Very nice box
text:
My requirements for a new case severely limited the number of choices available, the most important requirements being that the case is capable of E-ATX motherboards, it will easily fit a Corsair H115i (preferably top-mounted), multiple internal hard drive bays, and that it has external 5.25" drive bays for my Blu-ray burner. Any of these requirements individually would limit my choices, but all requirements together made it difficult to even find any choices. This Phanteks case made the (very) short list. Before ordering, I emailed Phanteks to verify the Corsair radiator would fit on the top without removing a drive bay or anything, and they got back to me within 12 hours (kudos to their support department).

I've been assembling new systems for 24 years, and have experienced some horrible cases and some impressive cases. My last two personal systems have gone inside an Antec DF-85, which was quite versatile but didn't support E-ATX. My main HTPC is in a Silverstone LC17, and the other HTPC is in a Cooler Master. I had not heard of Phanteks before, and because of the price, I was expecting a mediocre (or even disappointing) experience.

Unboxing for the first time, I realized this Phanteks seemed just as heavy as my Antec. Unlike my Antec, this Phanteks is not flashy and/or gaudy looking, it has a very subdued yet attractive appearance: function with style. Opened the tempered glass sidepanel and pulled out the parts box, and found that the screws are all separated inside a plastic compartment organizer case...just, wow. Every other case I've unboxed came with mixed screws in a ziplock baggie, this was a very nice touch. I assumed there had to be a lot of thin metal at this price point, but the only thing that had any give, or could possibly be easily bent, was the backplate...but even that wasn't any thinner than any other backplate I've used.

I've included pictures to show that my radiator easily fit top-mounted with room to spare, I was still able to utilize the cable management holes at the top of the motherboard, and my E-ATX mobo also did not infringe too far on the cable holes to the side, either. Behind the other side panel is a somewhat elaborate cable system already in place for fans/fanhub and some power, etc. The velcro cable ties made it easy to add/re-route cables. Mounting rails for the hard drives are somewhat-thin plastic, but well designed for fast install.

One good test to determine the quality of a computer case is the number of cuts to the hands during assembly: it was 0. Edges are all either rounded or not sharp.

I normally don't think of power buttons when evaluating a case. The Phanteks power button is on the top instead of on the front (next to everything else), so there's no bending over or looking for it when first sitting down...or accidentally pushing the reset button. And it's about three times the size of most power buttons. In addition it's recessed, so I can plug my phone or tablet into the front USB port and sit my device on the top without triggering the button. HD activity LED is also on top. I don't like having all the buttons plus USB ports on the top like it is with other cases, but having just the power button is welcome.

It's not all sunshine and rose petals...there is always something. In this situation, it's the external drive bay depth: my optical drive and card reader both are slightly recessed when installed, they're not flush with the front plate. It's not much, not too noticeable. I could probably just remove the included plastic drive bay locks and use screws to fine-adjust the depth.

There are other notable touches, such as the PSU shroud, removable drive bays, magnetic dust filter on the top and slide filters on the bottom, included fans, etc. This case was so nice to work with, highly versatile, is very attractive, well designed, and quality metal. So I'm still shell-shocked about the price...

title: Tivo was exceptional ... until they changed the user interface
text:
Tivo was exceptional before. The user interface was very intuitive and easy to navigate. I've been using it for the last 17+ years, almost since the first Tivo came out.

There are a lot of pros (still), compared to many of the DVRs out there
- schedule to record videos for different shows is still really easy to do (I hope they don't change this in the future)
- the schedules shows are organized by seasons and easy to go and see whichever episode you like
- in case the episode is not available, but it is on Netflix, Hulu, etc (whichever you have), it will still show up in the correct place in the list and you can just start it like any recording
- There is a way to browse through the specified type of shows (movies, etc.) and filter down by type (action, drama, etc.)
- You can schedule a series easily.
- Many other I can't remember now.

CONS:
Now, after they changed the User Interface, the navigation is really bad and awkward, so bad that I always have hard time finding different features that used to be readily available in the main menu (when the user pressed the Tivo button on the top of the remote).
- An example would be, finding other Tivo devices that are in your household, connected to the same computer network: in the old interface, they were at the bottom of the list of My Videos, while in the new interface, still have trouble finding it. When I finally find it, after navigating back and forth through the confusing navigation and many menus, is like Christmas and getting a gift.
- Other examples: setting up different things, like channels, remotes, etc,
- The feature allowing you to transfer videos from one Tivo device to another is gone now. Now you can only do streaming, so in case you have to change your HDD (because is starting acting up after 2-3 years), you loose all your recordings because can't transfer them anymore to another Tivo device.
- Transferring videos from your computer to any of the Tivo devices is not possible anymore because Tivo Desktop Plus is gone also.
- Voice Recognition is really not good (yet). I'm suggesting that they should collaborate with some engineers from Amazon, Google or Microsoft.

Overall, I still love Tivo, but their new interface is disappointing, to say the least.

title: Poorly thought-out Bluetooth Speaker
text:
I really wanted to like this speaker. It was a great idea with very poor execution. First off, These portable Alexa speakers are basically pointless since the can't be used portably with Alexa. And If you want to use Alexa on your home WiFi good luck getting it to connect since range is ridiculously poor compared to what you would get with your phone. Say you finally get the speaker connected to WiFi and playing some music, Now you can do nothing else with the speaker unless you interact through your phone because the mics will no longer be able to hear you over the music if its above ~40% volume (it may be able to hear you if you shout). The flap on the bottom is very flimsy and after you've charged it enough times it kind of seesaws back and forth and I would not trust it to keep out water. In addition the the flap, you will most likely only be able to use the included USB cable since most all others will be too wide to fit in the tiny square hole. To add to this I've found that my unit is experiencing random power cycles where it will turn back on immediately after being turned off.

Pro's
+ Sounds fine for the size of the device (could use more bass)
+ Looks good
+ Speaker material feels rugged (minus flap)
+ Battery is good enough

Con's
- No Alexa without WiFi
- Poor WiFi connection
- Alexa cannot hear you over 40% volume
- No way to pause/skip audio from device
- Poorly designed usb flap
- Can only used included USB cable
- Speaker should save last used EQ setting.
- Random power cycles (YMMV)

I was hoping to use this shower and at the park/beach. If you wanted to be able to use voice controls in the shower, you cannot since the mics will not pick up your voice. And If you want to use it outside of your home, you will be interacting with you phone since there is no other way to control the device.

title: The Good, The Bad, The Ugly-FIXED PARTIALLY
text:
Major Update April 2, 2021. As you can read in my review below, the main problem (ugly) with this computer was the poor thermal performance and at times extremely loud fan noise. I removed the Cooler Master radiator fan and substituted the Noctua NF-A12x25 5V PWM premium quiet fan. It was a simple process. This accomplished two things. It noticeably reduced the fan noise compared to the Cooler Master fan and the CPU ran a little cooler overall. It did not completely fix the problem, but it helped somewhat. The CPU still hits 100 degrees Celsius with CPU intensive tasks, but the temps were cooler and the noise reduced with the games listed below in the review. To really solve the problem you would need to replace the radiator unit, which would be a major undertaking. It is worth the minor trouble and cost to replace the fan. I would recommend this to anyone who feels comfortable doing a radiator fan replacement. There are you tube videos showing you how to do it.

First let me start with the good. To be able to buy a computer with these specifications for under $2000 in December 2020 is a big plus. The specs are:
1) HP custom triple fan RTX 3080.
2) Core I9-10850K CPU.
3) 32 GB of DDR4-3200 HyperX Fury memory in two modules.
4) 1 TB Western Digital m2. Nvme SSD boot drive that I benchmarked at 1700 MB/sec write and 2300 MB/sec read, and a 2 TB Seagate HDD 7200 RPM storage drive. I was able to replace the Seagate HDD by going into the BIOS to configure a RAID 0 array with two much faster SSD's.
5) 750 watt Cooler Master Platinum power supply.
6) 120mm Cooler Master closed loop liquid All In One CPU cooler.
7) A solidly built, attractive case with RGB lighting with numerous configurations that can be controlled by the included Omen Command Center software.
8) It has two prewired drive cages that can accept hard drives or SSD's.
9) The performance is excellent. The 3DMark scores of >16000 for the GPU and >13000 for the CPU put this model in the top 1% of all the scores in their online database.
If I attempted to buy all the components at December 2020 street prices, it would cost almost $3000. If I could get the RTX 3080 at suggested retail price, it would bring the total down to $2100. Sadly it is almost impossible to find one now at the retail price. So getting this unit delivered within two weeks of ordering it at this price was very good.
Now for the bad:
1) Although this case design is an improvement over the previous generation Omen desktop, it still has significantly subpar thermal performance. Any demanding pc video games will cause the RTX 3080 to go above 80 degrees Celsius. Any demanding tasks for the CPU, whether a game or video editing etc., will cause the CPU temperature to go above 90 degrees Celsius. When this happens the fans ramp up their speed and become extremely loud, and I mean LOUD!!!.
2) The wiring and cable management that you can see appears untidy, sloppy and slipshod. I can even see a piece of black electrical tape used to hold down a cable so it does not touch the water radiator of the CPU cooler.
Now for the ugly:
1) The subpar thermal performance. See major update above. The unit only has one 120mm intake fan, one 92mm exhaust fan, and one 120mm exhaust fan for the radiator/CPU cooler. This results in extremely loud fans with any demanding tasks. The 120mm AIO CPU cooler is totally inadequate for the I9-10850K cooling. You really need a 240mm or bigger AIO cooling unit. When I stress tested the CPU the temperatures would go up to 98 or 99 degrees Celsius and the fans were so loud you really could not tolerate it. It even hit 100 degrees Celsius on one occasion. Over the long run this will not be acceptable. I may have to move this system to a case with better thermal performance and use a bigger CPU cooling unit in the future.
I would recommend this unit only at the sub $2000 price point. At a higher price I would look elsewhere for one that has better thermal performance. I hope this has been helpful.

Update: Playing at 4K resolution with 120 Hz refresh rate, Shadow of the Tomb Raider with HDR and ray tracing at high and all other settings at maximum resulted in 76 FPS average, 60 minimum and 120 maximum. The CPU temp was in the 90's Celsius and the GPU temp was in the 70's C. The fans were noticeable but not too loud. Playing Call of Duty Black Ops Cold War with HDR, ray tracing and all other settings at maximum resulted in a FPS range of 80 to 120 with an average of about 100. The most demanding game was Cyberpunk 2077. It was set with HDR, DLSS 2.0 at performance, ray tracing at Ultra, and all other settings at High or Ultra. The FPS range was 40-60 with an average in the high 40's. The CPU temps were in the 90's C and the GPU temps stayed in the mid to high 70's C. The fan noise was noticeable but not unduly or exceedingly loud, like when I did CPU stress tests. My recommendation for this system remains unchanged.

title: A little disappointed, but works for the price with some caveats.
text:
I've always wanted a single cable solution. I purchased this dock for my brand new Dell Precision 5750 with a Xeon W-10885M CPU and 64Gb of DDR4 Registered memory and 2TB (1TB x 2 raid 0) nvme SSD and the NVidia Quadro RTX 3000 GPU. I use 3 x 3840 x 2160 monitors and thought that I could use this dock to drive the three displays and leverage my nVidia GPU. Didnt work. The HDMI Port detects the 4K monitor as a 2560 x 1440 monitor. It detects the other two monitors as 4K monitors, but only delivers 30Hz refresh rate which is crappy. I almost returned it, but then decided to take my Razer Core X with a Quadro P4000 GPU to the thunderbolt 3 port available on this dock. It worked!! I am now able to drive three displays at 3840 x 2160 @ 60Hz which is great for desktop use. Single cable. It also charges my laptop fairly well. So I decided to keep it. Other docks DO NOT charge the Precision 5750 or the XPS 17, as these laptops do require 130W from the dock to charge them. Having a Razer Core X stowed away behind my two Dell P317Q monitors and the (center) PHL BDM4350 monitor seems to work reasonably well. The P4000 is a great card for programmer use. I am disappointed with Dell for not delivering a single cable solution that can leverage the RTX 3000 through TB3, but I have a solution that works!!
This may not be the solution for everybody, but if you are wondering if you can daisy-chain a Razer Core X or another TB3 Graphics enclosure, that will work. Note that the Razer Core X has enough power to drive pretty large graphics cards. I also have a Razer Core V2 and while that worked, it resulted in some pretty strange USB behavior when I tried to use its USB ports. So your mileage with other TB3 eGPU enclosures may vary. The P4000 is a single-slot GPU which only uses about 150W of power. But My Razer Core X has worked well with other larger cards as well including an nVidia GTX 2080ti and Radeon Vega 64 (Mac use). Unfortunately, if you have a Quadro laptop, you can use an AMD GPU, but you cannot use the GTX gpu and the Quadro GPU together. For some reason, one of the GPUs have to be disabled and this results in some system instability. If you are using Quadro, stick to Quadro or AMD. If you are using GTX then stick to GTX and AMD. Back to the topic of this dock, I didn't want the hassle of returning it as it is the only dock that gives me a single-cable solution and enables me to daisy-chain an eGPU, charge my laptop and connect my other peripherals. Working for me. YMMV.

title: Firmware update availability
text:
[[VIDEOID:38e00eba5670eaaee42ff6d9fd76a23b]] I have the older version and I mainly use it for pictures. I got rid of most of my Canon lenses when moving to Sony. I currently only have all prime lenses for my Sony a6300 and the grey market (reselling sites) has plenty of canon lenses for much less available. So I ended up getting this adapter because of the usb option to update firmware and it's price.

It's still very much cheaper than the metabones and other adapters which in my opinion are over priced and does basically the same thing.

It's feels sturdy and has good weight on it because of the metal elements. The updating may be a bit confusing as it was for me. But it was actually quite easy.

Updating the firmware:
1. Go to the manufacturer site (download site has all firmwares listed)
2. Download the updates and save to your computer.
3. connect the usb to the adapter and computer. The window should come up with a new drive letter and named E Mount.

title: easy install, quick read/write times, but runs just as hot as my old drive
text:
**** Update ****
Just died unexpectedly. Unable to boot. 2 yrs. Thumbs down.

**** Original Post ****
Purchased this as a clean install of the OS for my MBA 2011. I developed apps on the old drive and rather than archiving/formatting it so my kid can use it during this years Covid remote learning, I chose to just purchase this convenient drive with the OS already loaded.

To be transparent, my old drive had been experiencing issues where it would run hot and cause the fan to kick on all the time and I've tried all the google tricks except one (format and start over), so installing this drive is kind of a 2for.

Installation is as simple as they advertise. I have opened the back of the MBA many times to clean the fan and replace the battery so that was not new. A handful of screws and you're done. The replacement of the drive was simply another screw which held the drive in place. In my MBA 2011, the drive was right above the battery and the screwdriver that was include worked. I already had a screwdriver, but for completeness, I used the one included. Once reassembled, it booted and all I needed to do was set up the parameters of a new Mac. Wifi, Apple account, etc..

Once running, I installed a drive speed test app and sure enough I was getting roughly 400 MB/s of reads/writes where as I was getting roughly 180 before on the old drive, though it didn't noticeably speed up the boot times.

The last thing I tested was how often it would kick on the fan when being used. I installed several games that my kid plays that always triggered the fan to run quickly. Now, maybe it's not the drive, but it does prove that replacing the drive doesn't seemingly fix the fan constantly kicking on issue that many older MBAs have been experiencing.

With all this said, it's still a great purchase. It saved me a ton of time and the whole process was as simple as promised. My kid now has a fresh new Mac even if it does still run hot.

title: Exceeded all my expectations
text:
I was a bit hesitant purchasing this going in as I knew it could be a big project and was wary about quality, durability, and compatibility. It was indeed a bit challenging to install; but this is not really the fault of the unit. Due to the variations in year/model/options it is difficult for a product to truly be 'plug and play.' My case was no exception.

I have a 2005 X5 with DSP Premium sound and factory navigation. The system failed about a year ago and I finally had enough! I stripped out ALL factory equipment aside from the speakers. I purchased these passive crossovers -

Rear:

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00N9866QM/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o07__o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Front:

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00N987TC2/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o07__o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

The unit came with two wiring harnesses, in my case the flat bladed one was needed. Unfortunately, it was located under the spare tire in the rear :) I had to extend wiring as necessary and run RCAs to a four channel amp (installed in the electrical box under the spare), and to a two channel amp (for the factory sub - installed in place of the OEM amp)

This took me a LOT of time; but again this is really due to the vehicle. One oddity I had was that the buttons would illuminate when the volume was increased. I still do not understand why, but it seems to have to due with the steering wheel adapter. I disconnected the orange line (illumination) from the harness and the problem went away. I installed a rear view camera at the same time.

In the end, I couldn't be happier, this system rocks. Sound quality overall is excellent with no real noise or interference. AM & FM Radio reception is as good or better than before. Handsfree/bluetooth streaming is flawless from my Iphone 7 IOS 12.3. GPS reception typically locks on really quickly. The rearview cam triggers properly and looks excellent. Audio mutes appropriately when turn by turn directions, etc are needed. Entertainment functions halt on incoming/outgoing calls. Illumination dims nicely when the headlights are on. Steering wheel controls work just as I would want! Illumination matches the interior perfectly (this was an unexpected bonus) and the BMW boot logo is pre-loaded.

I installed a 128GB Crucial MicroSD card and have loaded it up with FLAC files - the system sounds MUCH better than factory, and the OEM subwoofer actually surprised me as well (I hated it before as it was so weak).

If I haven't made it clear, I LOVE this system. It boots fairly quickly and is very responsive. The split-screen feature is super-cool as it allows you to have both Navigation and entertainment functions at the same time. Wi-Fi performance is good; I joined it to my home so it downloads the latest podcasts as soon as I am in range so they are ready to go for next day.

At this point, all my concerns have been eradicated aside from durability. I have no issues two weeks in, time will tell how well it holds up in the extreme environment of a car interior. I purchased a 4 year extended warranty based on this; but even if the unit fails, most of the work of the installation/modification should carry over to a replacement unit.

I only have one area where I am NOT satisfied; and that is that my commute is fairly short and that limits the time I am able to enjoy this next-gen system!

text: It's hard to find a USB stick that isn't formatted as exFat or NTFS. I must have tried 6 different "free" formatting utilities - all terrible and none did the job. For whatever reason, Tesla requires the USB memory stick to use a FAT 32 file format. This stick comes pre-formatted to FAT 32. All I needed to do was make a TeslaCam folder, plug it into the USB port on my Tesla and it worked perfectly. title: Easy Setup & Excellent Video quality
text:
[[VIDEOID:dd40a249d3a6224f38e972632dc3869c]] Someone had stolen my Arlo Cams!! Sigh... this unfortunate event had forced me to shop for security cameras––again. As I was about to add the new Arlo Pro replacement cameras to my shopping cart, I had receieved an email blast from the Eufy team about the new Eufy Security E camera system. A few features that caught my eye––one, the wider recording angle, which will help me get coverage on my back door which my old Arlo couldn't have gotten. And two, it has a built-in alarm on the camera itself, which gets triggered if the camera is removed from it's mount! Why couldn't Arlo have though of this sooner?!? Security camera replacements are EXPENSIVE. Anyways, I've been a long-time user of their robovacs (still running strong after a year and a half!) so I thought, oh what the heck, I'm sure their security products should be pretty decent, why not give it a shot?
Setup: The setup was fast and easy. There is however a firmware update needed once the base stations and cameras are paired. If you already have a Eufy Home account, you can actually use the same login credentials for this. (Maybe an integrated app in the future?)
First Impressions: I'm very impressed. I've benchmarked it against my Arlo Pro camera that was mounted in my living room. See the attached pictures for a comparison between the Eufy (wide full frame images) and Arlo (with two side bars). The extra wide viewing angle was able to capture my back door (as expected), whereas the Arlo camera failed. The night shots were unquestionably clearer and crisper compared to my Arlo.
I'm still waiting for my husband to help me setting one of the Eufy cams outside (where the original Arlo cam was stolen) and see what it captures at night. I'm also curious to see how this year long battery works. The cameras are probably using Anker batteries, so I don't think the Eufy team would be toying with us about this feature. Only time will tell. I'll keep everyone updated after some more use!

title: Works great. Lacks 1 star for being a battery hog
text:
The pros:
1. The white against the black face and the white hands stand out quite well and make it easy to see the location. The numbers however are a bit on the small side so it's not the most legible. Bigger brighter numbers would have been a plus.
2. The thing that I REALLY like is that the time is automatically synced. I have several clocks and I just don't know when to trust them and when not to. It's nice to know that I will NEVER have to do that. Well until the batteries run out! :D
I am also surprised at how much I enjoy not having a very minute ticking noise (this one does not tick)

3. The timer function is quite nice. It does MULTIPLE timers. When it's greater than a minute it appears as a single notch. When the time gets below a minute it changes into the circle around the clock face which ticks down. The lights are bright so it's easy to see. The visual it provides is spot on. I set timers all the time. it is very useful for work purposes where you have to schedule things in short increments. An easy obvious reminder is visually pleasing and informative. This is by far my favorite feature.
4. Setup is just insanely good. Plug in the batteries. Then command the echo dot to setup the wall clock. And that was literally it. It paired automatically, jumped on my wireless network with no input, synced up with the correct time. I don't think it could literally be any faster to set this up.
5. Price- at the $20 bucks it sold on Cyber monday, it's close to the price of a cheap regular clock. Not to mention it comes with some mounting hardware and four AA batteries.

Room for improvement.
Let's start with the big con - this will run right through your batteries and fast. If you use the timers often I had to replace these batteries after three weeks. Plan to use rechargeable batteries and change often or you will really dislike this clock. If you don't use timers often, the batteries last about two months - not great and it is irritating.
Other nitpicks:
1. There is NO GLASS cover on this clock. Yet you are not supposed to TOUCH THE CLOCK hands. Something that a glass cover would obviously go a long way towards preventing. It just feels "weird".

2. This clock does not have a mic and it does not have a speaker. So if you ask it the time, it's your echo dot telling you the time. I think it should at least light up the clock when you ask for the time. A small speaker would be nice. I'm guessing there is going to be an echo clock plus with a fancier face, and speakers etc coming up.

3. The timer's are linked to the echo dot. So if you set a timer in the kitchen on the echo clock and go to the living room to wait, you won't be able to see it on the living room echo clock. This should be made configurable. Where you can choose to "share timers" over particular echo clocks. A sort of "link timer" feature. Currently all the echos can tell you what timers on what echos.

4. Since it can light up, I feel that the numbers and hands should also light up for clarity. Especially the numbers. You should also be able to make this echo clock light up. "Alexa light up the clock". It could have a time out function of say ten seconds or something to preserve battery.
5. A big con is that if you are a constant user of the timers, you are probably going to be changing rechargeable batteries about once every 3 to 4 weeks. The use of LED's obviously drain the batteries quickly. Yes this is very annoying, especially because you have to access the back of the clock to do it so you have to remove the clock from the wall. I plan to order some low discharge rechargeable batteries to remedy this situation and shall update.
So there you go. So far I am happy I got it. I enjoy the lack of ticking, the great synchronization and the timers. It doesn't do much else than that and it just does it.

Replacement cushions are not available, and the shape is so unique that I can't find any that would work. So I either have to buy a whole new set of headphones, or just find a different pair that I might actually be able to buy extra ear cushions for. At $40, these are the most expensive headphones I've ever purchased, and I am really upset that I can't use them anymore. Amazon support wasn't helpful, and I can't find a way to contact this manufacturer directly. I'm changing the star rating because after only 4 months these headphones are now useless. Not worth the price at all.

I've had these Wave earbuds for two months now and they are my FAVORITE. I'm a side sleeper and I always listen to something when I'm falling asleep, and these are the most comfortable earphones I have ever used! They are flat enough so they don't protrude out too far, which other side sleepers know is super uncomfortable. They also stay in place really well! I hardly ever had to adjust or reposition them. They're also much longer than other earphones I've had, which was a little weird at first and took some getting used to, but now I wholeheartedly appreciate their longer length. They are great about staying in place and not falling off from around my neck when they're not in use. I have a backup pair from another brand that I use when these are dead, and the shorter length is so annoying to me now that I'm used to the length of these. Which brings me to the battery life: the battery life on these Wave headphones is AMAZING. Since I sleep all night listening to something, I got used to my headphones dying sometime through the night. But these Wave headphones not only last all night, they also last for most of the next day too!! It's incredible! I can go at least 24-36 solid hours of near-continuous use before I have to charge again. So if you're not using them continuously, I can only imagine how long these things will last between charges. It blows my mind. And when I do need to charge them, I am equally shocked with how fast they charge! I used to get so annoyed with my previous headphones for taking so long to charge, but these are on the charger for maybe an hour or two (at the most) and they're fully charged. It's probably even less time than that, because I don't really watch the clock. I just check back after an episode of a show or something and BOOM they're fully charged. After two months, I am still tickled pink everytime I pull these off the charger because I didn't have to wait long at all. Seriously, best headphones ever.

title: Good purchase - not perfect
text:
Purchased this to finally cut the cord on our cable. We still have Sling and Netflix for shows, but really wanted the local channels. This antenna picked up 22 local stations and over 159 internet stations. Most of the local tv stations were 25-35 miles away.

Installed the antenna in the attic, mounted on a roof truss, aimed 145 degrees at the preponderance of the local station signals.

The antenna works great most of the time, especially in the morning and during the day. In the evening, not so great. During prime time almost every evening, the picture gets very pixelated on and off, especially when it gets really cloudy and/or rainy outside. Even happens with clear skies, though. To be fair to GE, our roof planks are foil lined, which I think limits the antenna’s abilities to some extent. However, since the signal is so crisp most of the day, I have a feeling the evening issues are more related to interference than to the foil lining in the roof. Also purchased an amplifier to boost the signal with no discernible difference.

Overall, satisfied with some misgivings due to evening pixelation issues.

text:
I ran two of these through 2" conduit for about 60 feet, then across some HVAC equipment and through a wall. Signal quality is much better than when I used HDMI over CatX extenders. My signal goes from a PC to an HDMI 1x4 splitter using a normal cable, then 100 feet through an attic to 2 TVs at the front of an auditorium. I have zero signal loss, zero interference, and it was an absolute breeze to set up.

Pros:
Durable wrap on the cable prevented any abrasions on pull-through
Connectors are clearly marked for Monitor and Source
Small diameter doesn't take up much space in the conduit
Less expensive than HDMI over CatX extender plus quality CatX cabling
Simple to use

Cons:
Comes double looped and wrapped in a coil. Pulling the wrong end tangles the entire thing
Very easy to kink/bend, although you have to be very rough to actually damage it
Twists really easily

Overall, as long as you treat it carefully when prepping, you won't have any problem setting this up. Will definitely look at this brand in the future.

title: Won't work with most VESA mounts
text:
Summary: Display quality is fine, but unless you own an uncommon VESA mount you will NOT be able to mount this monitor unless you DISASSEMBLE the monitor first.

I bought this because I wanted to attach it to my VESA monitor arm. EVERY VESA mount I've had (1 wall mount, 1 single arm, 1 dual arm, and 2 arm mounts at work) has a DUAL 4-screw mount pattern - a wider set of 4 screws on the outside, and a narrower set of 4 on the inside. As mentioned in the other reviews by surprised VESA purchasers, the monitor stand bracket will collide with such mounts. The manual flat-out tells you that you're out of luck and should buy another mounting bracket. You CAN remove the stand bracket, but it literally requires you to take apart the monitor case. This is not trivial and involves gingerly popping about ten plastic locking tabs with a screwdriver. If you repair Samsung monitors for a living you could probably do this in three minutes. Doing it cautiously by feel took me 15, and I never fully popped the two halves (couldn't figure out how to separate the top seam and didn't want to force it). Was able to carefully get a screwdriver in to remove the offending mount, but I wish I had purchased another monitor instead.

It is just very limited compared to something like a Roku or AppleTV. It works in a pinch if you mainly use Amazon and Netflix, though. Part of the features allows you to connect to network devices. For example, I was able to access and play media from my Synology NAS.

I also had a very weird thing happen. I had an older Panasonic BluRay player plugged into my receiver and simply unplugged it and plugged this into the same HDMI cable. My receiver completely freaked out and my speakers had a very loud sound come out. I had to turn off my amps and unplug my speakers. It literally killed that HDMI port of my receiver. However, I plugged it into a different port, with a different cable, and it worked fine. In other words, you may want to get a new HDMI cable with this player.

That being said, I got this for mainly playing discs and it is great at that! It provides the best picture I have seen on my projector, which is the main reason I wanted it! All in all, I give it four stars for my purposes. It makes me want to get more discs and see things with a level of detail I hadn't imagined. That says a lot, even with the issues I mentioned above!

title: Perfect for non-common ground amplifiers.
text: I bought this unit to facilitate adding a line-level output onto our LeGrand OnQ Digital whole-house audio system.  The individual keypad amplifiers for each room are of the non-common ground type and only have speaker level outputs (no aux or line level outputs).  One must be careful using devices like this on non-common ground amps.  Some designs use only a very simple circuit employing only resistors and can cause damage to amplifiers of that type.  I took the over off this unit when I received it and was pleased to find that it uses transformer-coupled circuits, which is the correct  method for non-common ground amps.  It works perfectly and does exactly what I wanted.  I'm using this device to drive an auxilliary  4-channel headphone amplifier in my music room. Now my musician friends and I can don headphones and play along with whatever music is being played over our home audio system, and actually hear both ourselves and the music.  Perfect for what I wanted to accomplish.

title: Sony lives up to their reputation
text:
There are plenty of places you can go online to get the detailed specs on this screen once it has been professionally reviewed. I'll give you impressions from my couch. I selected the X900H for the same reason many of you will - I wanted a great set today that will be ready for PS5 in the near future. All I can comment on is how good the set is today, one week after its release. In a word: fantastic.

I am a post-production professional. I've seen video look its absolute best in the same rooms and on the same displays as the guys who finish projects before they go out into the wild. Having experience with a professionally calibrated grading monitor, when it comes to selecting gear for my own home I'm very particular about what I choose and do patient research with the goal of coming as close as possible to that level of performance without spending a fortune. When I calibrate my personal TVs, I aim for accuracy. My living room is light controlled. I use test patterns to set the black level, the white level, and the color saturation using those old school blue THX glasses. Yeah, I'm that guy. I do it all by eye, I haven't paid to have someone come out with a Colorimeter and CALMAN and get this thing science-lab perfect, okay? On the weekends I'm a regular joe with a remote control and snacks that wants to watch some TV and wants it to look "correct". Having said all of that - I'm blown away by this TV's performance. I've got it calibrated to my liking and this thing makes content look like it's coming right out of the studio. I feel like my living room is my edit bay and this is the reference monitor.

Black levels are nearly-perfect and completely uniform. Colors are very natural. I'll save space by just saying - it lives up to Sony's reputation for image quality. I've watched blu-rays in SDR, Ultra HD blu-rays in HDR10, Netflix in Dolby Vision, Disney Plus in HDR10, PS4 games in SDR and HDR, even DVDs. They all look great. No funky colors. No weird artifacts. No need for extra words.

Read any enthusiast forum about TVs and you'll hear about blooming. I've seen it bloom once or twice during PS4Pro gaming sessions on loading screens. Never during HDR movies or normal content. You a videophile? You can tweak this TV to your heart's content. Want to change something about the picture? There's a slider for that.

I was replacing a Sony I've owned since 2008, which still looks great today, I only wanted a larger screen and wanted to go 4K. I'm very pleased with the X900H's performance. Same goes for the build quality. The design is elegant and looks great in the room. Nothing feels cheap. The packaging was safe, secure, and not wasteful. The experience with Amazon was 5 star. Placed order on a Monday, greeted the UPS man on Thursday. If I have any regrets at all about the purchase - I kinda wish I'd gotten the biggest one they make even though I don't have the space for it.

My first WP Passport drives a few years ago had the silver bodies with the rounded corners, and so far they have worked quite well, the next generation was a little bigger, back, with what seemed like a casing made of two segments, one about two thirds, the other about one third, of the length. Some of them vibrated a good deal when operating and one recently failed and froze up my computer when attached, although I'm not sure the reason. Disk utility repair did not work. Luckily I had the original drive--the silver rounded corner version, that this was a copy of but I had to waste a new disk drive of that two-piece version to make a new copy, which took about 16 hours.

Getting back to this current design, of which I purchased two 4 TB drives, I don't know how it will work, but they are recognized by my computer, and have fairly low vibration. Physically they seem to be of a sturdier construction than the last design, they are about 1/8 thinner, top to bottom, and about 1/8 inch shorter. One thing I don't particularly like is that they have no foot pads as previous ones did, however minimal they were, so these clunk down on the hard surfaces and can slip around more. Also, if you go by the side that has the label plate, which on previous versions is always on the bottom, the position of the port for the cable is reversed, so instead of being on the left side of the end and is now on the right side of the end, and the direction of the cable plug must be turned the other way to fit. Another thing is the previous generation had a rather large horizontal LED activity light, whereas this has a very small, fainter circular LED opening, but still adequate.

title: Ball Head is weakest point
text:
Like the customer service. Sadly, it's because I had same issue others did within a week of receiving. Pan friction/lock knob got stripped. They replaced entire unit immediately.
Now with second copy, I'm being extra careful with that knob, so it's holding out for now. However, the more I use this tripod, the more I realize the ball head in general is just not up to par.
What am I expecting? Avid enthusiast with typical gear tuned to that demographic. Full size DSLR with 18-300 zoom is just too much for this. Not talking about massive expensive glass here. Ball head suffers from an initial creep from desired setting to final position upon tightening, made most evident during telephoto shots. Even then, I've had blurred shots, as I watched the ball head almost imperceptibly slipping during long exposure. Just a bit spongy on the ball grip mechanism, (which takes all the torque I throw at it, unlike the pan knob. )
Legs are great - I love snap locks for speed vs twist. Metal hub that legs are attached to is what convinced me to spend a little more for this item vs competition, and for the weight vs performance, the base unit is just the ticket for a long hike or bike trip through the woods. However, it must be noted, with that same DSLR and consumer grade zoom lens, You'll need to use a remote shutter release. Period. The whole thing jiggles like jello if you touch any part of it with this mere 3 pound camera/lens attached.

So - for now, I'll deal with it, as the portability is excellent, I have a heavy pack to hang off hook and a cable shutter release. Will replace ball head soon with an Italian made unit, followed by a matching set of legs eventually.

If you're running a very light camera, or need something for flash / lighting systems, this is a very nice little tripod. Sadly, if you want better performance for your hobby equipment, you will really need to spend more. I don't think it can be done for under $100, despite my trying.

In closing, I think this is about the best pick for this price range of tripods. Just not up to par performance-wise for my expectations.

title: OLED65C8P Overall Just Better Than Average
text: First, the picture quality is fantastic, the unit looks great, is light weight, and has some great features. I would love to give this set 5 stars but there are things to me that make this tv just better than average.  The first is the HDMI ARC. I have the HDMI ARC connected to a new JBL Bar 5.1 soundbar.  I have a Roku and Blu-Ray disc player connected to the sound bar. The problem is that sometimes the TV fails to recognize the inputs on the sound bar (Roku won't show up under the list of inputs for the HDMI ARC). Sometimes I will select the Roku input and the tv will go to to the Blu-Ray and turn it on.  Very frustrating.  I believe part of the problem is how the HDMI ARC standard has been implemented. In a nutshell, I do not believe the problem would exists if I had an LG sound bar connected. Just my opinion.  Now to correct this, I was going to abandon using the HDMI ARC and connect the sound bar using the supplied digital optical cable and then connect the Roku and BD directly to the other HDMI ports.  My problem is that my TV is already mounted to the wall  and I can not pull the protective cap off the optical digital audio output to insert the optical cable.  I can reach it, but, LG uses a cap that is flush and not the kind that protrude so you can easily grab and pull out.  Needless to say, I have to remove the TV from the wall to change the set up.  Another problem is the internal streaming tuner.  I get a better connection going through Roku than the internal streaming tuner. I have found this true with every TV I have/had.  The Roku tuner is superior to TV internal streaming tuners. In regards to the tv's OTA tuner, I use to feed OTA signals to my old tv using a Tivo receiver. With this set, I have the outside antenna going directly to the LG set.  I use to pick up more OTA stations before.  I would have to say that the Tivo tuner was better that the LG OTA tuner.  LG doesn't seem to believe in documentation.  What they do have is not all that helpful.  I downloaded  the documentation from the LG website.  So, if this is the latest and greatest in tv technology I am not impressed. Granted, the picture quality is the best I ever had, I find the "smart" features lacking.  Some of my older technology out performs what this tv offers (including little plastic protective caps that you can easily be put in and out of optical ports).  As it stands , I probably would not buy another LG tv.

title: faulty battery and misrepresentation of range
text:
To summarize I had 2 problems (1 and 2 below are related);
1. The unit does not hold its charge, or that it continues to draw down at the same rate even though it has been shut off.
2. Possibly related, is that once the battery is completely drained (over night not on charger). The unit will initially start charging correctly, but will detect that it is fully charged after just a few minutes (red to blue) even though it has not charged. This can be over come by unplugging and then re-plugging in charging cord. The unit will eventually take a charge.
3. The boom mic that plugs directly into the helmet clamp had terrible audio. We had 5 riders on the mesh network and they complained my transmissions had high distortion and intermittent output (every other word, syllable, etc.). This was corrected when I installed the wired mic that glues/mounts directly onto the inside of the helmet.

I had been using a Sena 10 but decided to upgrade to the Sena 30K for a motorcycle ride from California to Alaska. This was a family trip and we had 5 people to connect, some already had the Sena 30K. This was a once in a lifetime trip. It took several days to figure out workarounds for the mic distortion and charging problems. During that time I was unable to reliably participate on the comms and interact with the other folks on the trip. I feel cheated from those days I could not interact with my sons and their families. I wasn’t able to talk about the things we were seeing, telling jokes, or even when someone needed to pull over for pictures, and that time can not be replaced, it has come and gone. And that missed opportunity is directly due to the Sena 30K quality problems.

We also found that the meshed communication is literally line of sight. If you go around a corner in the road or even have a large vehicle between riders the communication will be very poor quality to nonexistent. Usually if you could see the other rider, you could talk to them, but that was it.

title: Good value for the cost
text:
I needed a wire-style keycap puller and wanted to try throwing some o-rings on the keycaps I'm currently using on my 65% keyboard (KBD67 hotswap) to quiet it down even more for use in public, so I figured I'd check this set out as the cheapest way to kill two birds with one stone.

KEYCAP PULLER: Does what it says on the tin. Feels a little flimsy, but I found myself gripping the tool by the wires themselves instead of the plastic handle (with my middle finger between the wires to brace them open), so I'm not worried about it coming apart anytime soon. Bit of a tight fit for caps that directly abut this particular case, but a little gentle wiggling easily got it into the gap and around the cap.

O-RINGS: I had some issues due to the caps themselves (the DCS profile means no struts, so the stem height varies by row), but I was able to appreciably dampen the bottom-out sounds on R2–R4 with 2 rings per cap (3 on the spacebar), and those were the keys I was primarily concerned about. The stems on R1 were tall enough that I needed 3 rings to dampen them, so I didn't have enough rings to do all of that row.

O-RING APPLICATION: While the rings fit comfortably on MX-compatible stems and can be added or removed with your bare hands, I found it was faster and easier to use the barrel of a ballpoint pen to push each ring snugly to the base after popping it onto the end of its stem. When removing rings, 2nd and 3rd ones came off easily with just my fingers, but the 1st ones were sometimes deep enough in the cap that I needed a tweezers to pull them out, because I just couldn't get my fingers far enough in there. (May not be an issue on keycaps with struts around the stem and/or if you have longer fingernails than mine.)

BONUS: I actually received slightly more o-rings than advertised: a total of 143, if my math is right. (Though, to be greedy for a minute, I'd have liked about dozen more, so I could have fully dampened my whole board. It would be great if the set by default included ~210 rings, or enough to double up a full-size keyboard.)

Trying to look back there's a 1-2 second delay and the picture quality is so low that almost every vehicle behind you looks like a police car from the twinkling headlights and dash. There is no way to turn the monitor on and off other than unplugging the 12 volt adapter. did this allow me to see behind me during the day? Could I see it night time with this, not a chance in hell. No infrared, no night vision. Just pitch black dark nothingness.

the camera itself is attached to a transmitter and then to a power box. The wire length on this is nearly 20 ft. It's absurd to have such a long cable for a wireless camera. I just don't understand this.
the pictures and the description makes this seem like it's going to be a high-quality picture with no delay. No there is no fuzz because it is digital but the compression is so high it makes viewing objects very difficult. Not satisfied. The install took so long to tuck the wires away in to splice into the running lights I don't think it's worth the effort to remove this in order to return it. Perhaps it is?

text:
I bought the XL variant as I was grabbing at straws trying to find tips that worked for my elephant ears. Initially I gravitated to foams as they generally got a better seal than any other non-foam tip I'd tried. But they drowned out the highs too much and emphasised the bass in ways I was tiring of. And IEMs that had more subtle detail in say the highs, would have them drowned out due to the exaggerated bass, so I wasn't getting bang for buck with more pricey models (My FA7s and OH10s).

So I bought these in the hope that the seal issue I'm having with normal tips is just due to the size. Anddddd.... I was right! If you've had issues getting "large" sized tips to fit you, definitely pick these up!

Also, this is my first experience with SpinFit as far as I can tell, and the sound really is more clear due to the very flexible stems. Even with the Large CP100 variant, it sounds way better than other stock tips as I don't get as much of the muddiness that comes from the sound being directed straight into a wall in the ear, as opposed to into the canal more directly.

I'll update if they fall apart or there's something else I notice.

Update: They lose their shape a bit after a few months. Dropped to a 4 star from a 5. They're very thin so they don't keep their shape as well as thicker tips like the AZLA SednaEarfit ones, but to be fair they are a bit cheaper too. My music preference is Classic Rock and at 53 years of age, I never heard Pink Floyd's "Dark Side of the Moon" with the clarity these Sennheiser's produced.

A high powered amplifier is a must, as these are rated at 300ohms, and not your teenager's Bose or Beats. Remember, ohms is resistance and higher wattage equals "Utopia" with the HD 800 S. As mentioned above, these are an investment into your listening experience and the price shouldn't be driving you away.

I gave "Comfort" a 4 star rating, as the drivers are quite large and extend way beyond the circumference of the ears (don't let this be your deciding factor, as sound quality is stellar).

title: Comparable to my Skar Audio EVL-15" Sub!?!
text:
I've been on a Rockville Binge ever since I bought their dB45 4-channel amplifier a few months back and loved how it performed! I had recently built a new sub box for my car to drop in a Skar Audio EVL-15 2-ohm DVC sub and since that also recommends 1250 RMS to push, I ended up replacing my old Kenwood amp with a Rockville RDX-M4 1500 RMS x 1 ohm amplifier. With that being said, I've been playing the heck out of that sub/amp for a month now and I'm extremely happy with how it sounds.

So... I needed a second 15" sub for my other car... and I figured, why not the Rockville K9 15" 2-ohm DVC? :)

I've broke it in for the most part over the past week playing it in my garage sub box (not nearly as low of tuning as my car's box) and decided to swap out the Skar for the Rockville and play the same thumping music I'd been listening to to compare apples to apples. My box is 4.25 cu ft after speaker/port displacement and two 4" x 17" aeroports tuned to around 28hz.

Very happy to say that it's nearly identical! I believe the Skar still does hit a bit lower/harder than the K9 still but compared to every other sub I've owned, these 2 are in a class of their own. They both punch pretty well for 15's but that low frequency rumble is amazing on both of these subs! Extremely satisfied with this sub - especially at this price! The resistance I get on my multimeter shows the Skar between 0.9 ohms and 1.1 ohms and the Rockville is between 1.1 ohm and 1.4 ohms so there's probably a little power difference between the 2 in what my amplifier is pushing to them but it's pretty close (hopefully this is useful to anyone reading). I can tell a difference when the Skar is in my smaller/higher tuned sub box for sure - it's still more powerful than this Rockville K9, but again, for the price it's pretty darn close!

Anyways, I'm a fan of the Rockville products and will definitely be buying more of their stuff down the road! Also utilized their tech support and am happy to report they are very responsive and willing to help!

title: I want to love it, but some annoying, cheap, unnecessary choices by Supermicro make it difficult.
text:
I was very excited when I first got this case. The build quality was excellent, the aesthetics are clean and understated, and the features are functional. As I was putting my Asus H110I motherboard in it, however, I found there were no leads to connect it to. Just one 16 pin cable for the front panel that presumably is proprietary to a Supermicro mobo. Turns out I needed the CBL084L. No problem. $10 on ebay, and I can just jump the motherboard with my keys until it gets here to start it. Then I went to install my 2.5 inch hard drives, figuring there would be holes on the bottom of the drive sled for 2.5 inch drives, but no, you need to buy a separate adapter plates. That's another $50 with tax on Ebay and now I'm really stuck without a usable NAS until they get here.

I'm going to hold onto this case because it seems like it's designed better than the Chenbro alternative. Airflow definitely looks better on the Supermicro because of the use of a flex PSU. However, it's going to be hard for me to recommend Supermicro for projects like this, and I'll definitely see if there are alternatives to them for future projects. It's not like these are even expensive parts - just a few metal plates and some wires. Ffs, just put them in the box.

title: Decent Buds But Weird Fit, Inconsistent Microphone
text:
I really wanted to like these buds, and so did my girlfriend. Packaged in a modern way, everything was pointing towards this being a successful purchase. The case looked similar to my AirPods, the directions were clear and the connection was seamless. Music played really clearly from my Galaxy phone, and the buds stayed paired and reconnected when we tested turning the phone on and off. The sound was kind of tinny and not enough bass, but ok for the price of the buds.

Where the problems started occurring, however, was when we tried calling. The bud-side of the call was always clear, but for the other person, the microphone muffled the transmitted sound if the buds were too far apart, oriented imperfectly in the ear canal, or in random cases connected to one phone or the other (and also on random calls).

What's more, the buds are not really well-shaped for people with shallow ear-canals. They fit fine in my ears but in my girlfriend's they just popped right out. After prolonged use in my ears, they hurt my tragus (part of the ear that holds the bud in). A smaller size with interchangeable tips would easily solve this problem, but who knows if that is in the works for this budget bud.

A few aesthetic downsides as well. Unlike the AirPods case, the clean, lacquered finish is matte, and cheap-feeling.

I can't speak to the battery life because I didn't even use them enough to warrant a second charge. I'm sure it is fine, and I'm sure this product is a perfect solution for some people, but it just doesn't work for me.

title: High Quality Flag
text:
For those of you who are unaware, black "flags" are used in photography and videography either to block (or "flag") off light or prevent its reflection onto a particular surface (also referred to as "negative fill"). Essentially, it is an additional mechanism beyond your light modifier to give you greater control to shape your light and determine where it doesn't fall.

While many objects of all sorts of material from foam board to curtains can be used to flag off light, a good flag will generally exhibit 3 qualities:

1. It should hold its shape. This is important so that you can precisely control its effect.
2. It should not let light through. Obviously, if the idea is to block off light, you probably don't want the thing that's blocking light off to let light leak through.
3. The surface should be non-reflective. This is less of a problem (although still a bit) when it comes to straight out blocking the path of light and more of an issue with using the flag as a negative fill. An opaque, black, material with a reflective surface will still bounce some light (hence, the "reflective" surface). This is where a lot of DIY solutions will fail.

Matthews is a pretty well regarded brand so it's unsurprising that this flag is excellent at all three of these things. That having been said, there is probably a bit of a price premium that you are paying for the name so if you are on a budget, you may want to look into other options that will likely also work well. In my case, I ordered this particular flag because I'd rather not fiddle around and ship things back and forth looking for value on the dollar—at least not at this price point. If you just want something that you know will work excellently, I highly recommend this.

--------------------------

Why you might want a flag (whether you own a lighting kit or not). Beyond subject, composition, story, etc. when you get right down to it, the art of photography comes down to light. It is the presence of light that allows us to create an exposure and the absence of light that prevents it. Tools and add light such as strobes and bounce reflectors are typically the first place photographers will turn when they want to start controlling light, but for the full degree of control, you also want tools that subtract light in order to either shape it or completely remove it. This is where the flag comes into play. I would highly encourage any photographer to invest in a good flag and see the new creative options that open up. Like lights, you will probably want to get more than one as you learn, but even owning one vs. none makes a huge difference.

The second positive is the sticking portion. I used it for two drones, to help me find them in case batteries go out or a crash. It works amazingly well for that. Just walk in the general direction, make it go off when in range and voila.
Now the negatives:
I feel the effective range of the Bluetooth connection was decreased. Maybe that was the needed trade off to decrease the size of the device and thus I complain, I didn’t necessarily lower my rating.
The second issue was activating my Tile sticker. It took at least 10 attempts with both of the ones I activated. This could be an issue related to my app being a beta app, as the sticker hasn’t been released at the time of this review. That being said I cannot attest to that, thus I saved the remaining two stickers to activate when the app goes live. If my experience doesn’t improve, I will update my review and remove one star from my rating.

title: Privacy Nightmare and Poor Noise Cancellation
text:
As part of the agreement to use the app that provides full functionality of the headphones, Sony forces you to agree to allow them collect all usage information about how you use the headphones, including when and what songs you listen to. The privacy statement states that it collects your IP address (and location if enabled) and assigns each person a unique identifier and they are allowed to sell all of this information to third parties.

If you don't mind the privacy violations, you will be disappointed with the noise cancellation capabilities. I dutifully watched the in-app tutorial and the additional instructions on Sony's website about how to wear and use the headphones. I tried every single combination of the six different tips they provided, and repeatedly tried to re-seat the headphones into my ears to get the best seal possible. The noise cancellation was marginal at best. The one bright spot is the sound quality, which I judged to be better than AirPods.

In the end, I’m buying another pair of the Bose Quiet Comfort 20 Acoustic Noise Cancellation headphones. Unfortunately I left my prior pair on a flight, but they worked superbly, particularly with canceling jet engine noise at 35,000 feet. The Sony WF-1000XM3's could barely put a damper on my tiny little 5000 BTU room air conditioner.

title: Amazing product, a lot of misinformation from Lenovo Rep on Amazon
text:
Before I tell you about how good the product is, I have to give feedback on the Lenovo Rep(s). Before the product was available, I asked if the laptop had dual channel and or single channel memory. This is easily the most important specification in terms of performance for AMD laptops because the integrated graphics are very powerful, but you essentially lose half of the igpu performance with single channel memory. The rep told me (and subsequently another person) that the laptop has single channel memory. This is incorrect. I looked up the model number of the laptop on Geekbench and it clearly stated that it is dual channel. I received my laptop and checked with CPUZ, it also says dual channel.

Now some people may say "well what are you complaining for? You're mad because your laptop is better than they said it was?" No, I'm upset because the rep's job is to give correct information to consumers so that they can make good purchasing decisions. Incorrect information causes lost sales and it makes both AMD and Lenovo look incompetent. If you look through all of the questions on the Amazon product page, you will see a few other instances of incorrect information.

Just to be clear, this is a very good product in my opinion. It comes with a usb-c charger, a stylus, a mechanical shutter for the webcam, a ten keyless led keyboard. The screen is decent, obviously not something you would use for professional graphic design but it is still very good for the average user. The build quality is great, very solid. The 2 in 1 functionality is very cool in combination with the stylus.

The performance is in a completely different league from anything else in this price range. AMD's new Ryzen 4000 cpu's are insane. Benchmarked next to my 2500U, this 4500U is about 90% faster in terms of cpu performance. The igpu is up to 50% faster than the Vega 8 graphics in my 2500U. This laptop is ideal for a mixture of office work, consuming media, and light gaming. If you want something to play LoL, Dota, Rocket League, CSGO, etc or random indie games on Steam, then this laptop can do that.

For $600 there is nothing you can get from Intel that can match this performance without having a discrete Nvidia gpu. The only thing I dislike is that the SSD is 256GB, but I have a 512GB mini usb that I can use for media so it's fine.

My first impressions: highly recommend... but get your stuff together, Lenovo Rep, whoever you are.

The Optical-In works on this device, but it only is interpreted in a stereo signal. Which defeated the purpose I had for this product. Since I wanted 6 channel surround sound. Also the stereo signal from the optical playback had considerably bad interference too, as I had read in other comments.

This is coupled with a magnitude of things that don't make sense.
There is no Optical Out. The hardware is not even there although it appears to be.
You have to have a CD drive to download the software to use most of the functions.
This product is certainly not very user friendly, and that is why it has so many 1 star ratings.

However, I am deciding to keep this product.. Astonishingly enough, I am able to plug the device directly into a PS4 USB port and receive pretty quality stereo audio through my Logitech speakers. Although it is not a true surround sound experience, it is still better than the stock TV speakers for when I don't feel like wearing a headset while gaming or watching videos. title: Finally a comfortable keyboard
text:
Earlier this year I started to get severe RSI pain in my right hand--not from typing, or from moving a mouse, but specifically from mouse clicks and using a scrollwheel. I've been looking for a while for a good alternative, and I've effectively become left-handed for months. There are a lot of 'ergo' keyboards and mice out there but they really seem to be oriented for some other kind of pain that I don't have--this is really clear from vertical mice still having a completely standard scroll wheel on them.

One predecessors to this keyboard is a USB Lenovo keyboard with trackpoint, which is fairly good except for scrolling, which is terrible. I liked having the mouse buttons in the middle of the keyboard but I'd tend to use a left-handed mouse instead of trackpoint. Another is an ergo keyboard with a RollerMouse Red. The RollerMouse works wonderfully, and I still use that with a work computer, but it's not compatible with Linux and it takes up a lot of space and many keyboards aren't that comfortable to use with it. A keyboard I got right before this one is a Perixx with a scroll wheel and mouse buttons in the middle of the keyboard, but no mouse. That one really wasn't worth it, the scroll wheel hardly scrolled at all, and the rest of the keyboard was very cheap, I stopped using that keyboard within a day and went looking for another--which is when I found this one.

So how's this keyboard? It has a small removable mouseball which takes some getting used to; with my high sensitivity I tend to want to keep a finger on the mouse when clicking or just taking a finger off will jerk the pointer away from what I'm wanting to click on. For buttons it has large and easy to press right/left buttons, and then tiny and fairly stiff back/forward buttons, and then a *very* nice scrollwheel positioned for a thumb rather than a finger. I just have no complaints at all about the mouse, it's exactly what I'd wanted from every prior keyboard that I tried. I especially like that it's in the center of the keyboard as I can give my (still weak) right hand some slack when mousing around. I can use what's most comfortable. For the rest of the keyboard, I doubt these are Cherry switches but they're comfortable enough, and the keyboard as a whole feels very nice, from the soft palmrest to the soft plastic. It doesn't feel like it's made out of metal but it also doesn't feel cheap at all. I wish the keyboard were backlit and that it had some media buttons, that's all.

How about the layout? This is a JP keyboard with a layout that will unfamiliar to a US English user, not for letters which are still QWERTY, but for punctuation which varies a bit, and for having extra keys for Japanese input modes and such. As I'm comfortable touch typer I just reset the layout to ANSI standard, but there are a few extra keys I'm not sure what to do with yet, and I'm still getting used to hitting the left ALT instead of the other key that's there. I'd prefer an ANSI layout but this layout is very workable; the only thing I really don't like is the backspace key, to the point that for now I've mapped the Yen key next to it as an additional backspace.

The mouseball, although it's removable, it's not removable by finger. You're going to want some q-tips.

title: Keeps up with the competition, but half the price!
text:
Photo: a comparison of the uni adapter, a Samsung adapter and another brand bought from Amazon. The other brand is a little longer and a little bigger. The Samsung is shorter, but thicker. The Uni is in the middle, size wise.

I've had the Uni adapter for a couple weeks now and have run it through some paces. We use these adapters to run Netflix and other streaming services from our phones to our big screen TV.

In short: the Uni adapter has done just as well as any that we've ever bought, and is constructed better than the "name-brand" adapter (it has a simple plastic cable and started breaking down pretty quickly, whereas the Uni has a nice braided cable). I kept the name brand cable as an emergency backup, and then forgot about it in the console for a long while. Will probably toss it now that I have the Uni cable.

All of these adapters will overheat after a while. It's just a matter of fact. Which is why you want a few on hand to switch out if you use them very heavily. Every. Single. One. Name brand, off brand, doesn't matter. But the Uni lasts as well as any of them. And at literally 1/3 to 1/2 the price of the competition? That makes it a good buy.

If you're looking for an adapter to run HD from a phone to a tv, I'd recommend this one. Keep in mind, if you run movies, you might want to buy two.
