title: Best Gaming Monitor for High end desktops
text:
If you're looking to be competitive in any video game than latency needs to be minimized and speed need to be emphasized. A lot of people will pour all of their money into their rig and leave nothing for the monitor or skimp on the monitor completely. Considering the monitor is the most key element of the mix means that you cant go all out on a GPU/CPU and expect the monitor to just scale with it. It will soon become your Achilles heel. For competitive online play you have to have either g-sync or freesync, a high 240hz refresh and minimal latency. Most bargain monitors dont have any of those. People are generally drawn to the inexpensive monitors that look ok with a static picture perhaps, but provide no meaningful abilities for any online gaming. Most often most users pour all their money into their GPU (hey they are expensive) but without adequate hardware to use it, you're literally pouring money down the toilet. Truthfully you have to pair a GPU with a Monitor. This alienware is best suited for the higher end Nvidia cards (not AMD) as it has G-Sync (if you use AMD get a freesync monitor). It is also built for current gen cards (3090, 3080 Nvidia). If you're using an older 2 or 1 series Nvidia this monitor will be quite a waste of investment unless you plan on upgrading your card soon thereafter. Older Gen cards just wont be able to hit 240hz with low latency.

All that being said there are always pros/cons

Pros:
-Beautiful picture
-Fast refresh 240hz
-Nice case & bezel
-G-sync
-great color calibration

Cons
-Expensive
-Generates a lot of excess heat
-narrow purpose (gaming)

All in all if you are a serious competitive gamer this is your holy grail of monitors. If you are a F***lthy casual than stick with the sub 100 slow boys!

title: Pretty good sound.  Wireless charging is a good trick.  Abysmal Bluetooth connection
text:
I just bought these today, so these are my initial impressions.

First, the good:

1) The earbuds deliver good dynamic sound. Nothing that will blow you away, but very solid.
2) They're very lightweight and easy to wear.
3) I like having a carrying case with Qi charging ability.

These earbuds use buttons rather than touch controls. I'm not sure yet if that's a positive or a negative. My other wireless earbuds have touch controls, and for some functions (skipping ahead a track, for example) touch controls are good, but on touch controls, I've had either accidental touches or touches not registering, so buttons have their advantages, too.

The main place where I'm somewhat disappointed is with the Bluetooth connection. In two words: It's poor. If I leave my phone in one room, and go into another, the music stutters. It has even stopped once or twice. (Like I said, I just got these today.) In fact, as I'm typing this, the sound in my left ear is coming on and off intermittently.

I'm going to give these a chance to charge more on the charger. If performance improves, I'll come back and revise my review. But right now, I'm not happy with the performance. I gave them a 3 for sound quality because of the connection issues, but if I could, I'd give them 2 1/2.

Updated 5/122020:

I think 3/5 is a decent score for what you get. I actually kind of like the fact that it doesn't have touch controls. I have a pair with touch controls, and they're very finicky about where you touch them. So I like the fact that you click these, and you know you've clicked them.

But the Bluetooth connection issues just aren't doing it for me. I should be able to go into the next room and not lose the connection, but I can't.

title: Brilliant little drive vs. Samsung T5
text:
As a global commuter for work, size and weight of the things I carry are very important. I already own several of the little Samsung T5 drives but they're all 512GB. To support backups on a new 1TB MacBook Pro 16", I needed a larger capacity drive. Other reviews I read lead me to an interest in this little drive by Sabrent. I thought the Samsung T5 was small. This Sabrent is half the width, and a few millimeters shorter and only 1mm taller. The metal case is very solid feeling and it manages the temperature well. I thought the drive, being so small, might get a little warmer than the Samsung but in fact it runs cooler. This barely gets above room temperature even under extended write periods. I haven't verified the speed claims of the drive but I can tell you that it runs a Windows 10 image via Parallels on my Mac as though it were installed on the internal drive. No latency whatsoever. Same as the Samsung T5, in that regard.
I've not had this drive long enough to make any claims on reliability but after a few months, I'll update my review with that information. If it holds up as well as my T5 drives have, I can say I've found my new favorite hard drive.

title: 530 over the 830 (coming from Edge 500)
text:
I hemmed and hawed for awhile between the 530 and the 830, figuring why wouldn't someone want a touchscreen in 2020? I've had a touchscreen on my phone since 2008. But after asking similar questions from 530 and 830 users, and watching one particular YouTube video review of the 530, I got the 530, and definitely made the right choice. Users of the 830 reported difficulty using the screen sometimes when your hands get sweaty and gunked up. And I also like to wipe off my screen which would be problematic if it's a touchscreen. You miss a few features without the touchscreen, and that's up to you if it's necessary. I still haven't used all of the features available on the 530.

Bottom Line: It's way better than the 500. Bigger, far more contrasty screen that almost seems to display better in direct sunlight. It's incredible. I can fit what I need on one page instead of two. It connects to the satellites far quicker than my 500. And I love the auto upload to the Connect app on my phone. No longer do I need to hardwire it to my computer to upload the data. There are a lot features, so take some time to turn some on or off as needed. I watched one video that gave me good ideas to turn some stuff off.

I only gave it 4 stars because I feel that the buttons are mushy and not up to standard of Garmin products. My seemingly ancient 500 still feels better (more solid). So it's really 4.5 stars. But overall I would buy again...and may be buying my girlfriend one as she now has my hand-me-down 500.

title: Simple to set-up and use but some things to know as a MAC user
text:
First off, I'm a MAC user running Mojave 10.14.2. I was looking for my own "cloud" for home use. This unit came highly recommended from friends at work as a very easy to set-up and use unit.

It was indeed very easy to set-up and get running on a MAC but there are a few things to know.

Let me first say I'm no IT Expert, don't pretend to be, not even a home computer hobbyist. The primary use of my MAC is video editing who wanted a way to store the large number of images and videos I have without going to an external cloud service like "icloud". I'm sure if there is a better way I'm sure someone will chime in.

The following is what I found when searching the 'net on how to accomplish a few things;
1) I use my NAS for Time Machine. Synology has a really good knowledge base that walks you through the process of creating a separate Time Machine user and a separate volume for the actual Time Machine backup.
2) If you want to store your Itunes library on your NAS, its' not quite as simple as moving the Itunes music folder onto the NAS. Synology doesn't support the use of Itunes. There are a few good videos on youtube that explain how to go about moving the itunes library to the NAS. For me it was a bit complicated but doable.
3) The same situation kinda applies for the "Photos" library, in that you can't just simply move the folder to the Pictures volume on the NAS. I haven't looked up if the same process needed for the Itunes library is the same for Photo. I used this as an opportunity to go through my Photo pics and clean house. A very manual process, but it worked. Thing is with my method I've got photos store on Photo (Mac) and in Photo Station....

Overall I'm very pleased with the Diskstation and it's capabilities!

title: Worked for a month, then died.
text:
The product itself from an audio standpoint is great.
The sound is loud, crisp, deep, isolated, and they stay in your ears very well, be it while running, weight lifting, or even cone drills.

The range they have is also quite impressive. While listening to music, I left my phone to fill my water bottle about 70-80 ft away, forgot I was wearing them, but the audio never cut out. When I got back to my phone, I realized what just happened and thought, "Wow, that's actually pretty impressive."

Needless to say, there's a reason I'm giving this a 1-star review. They stopped working just over a month of using them. I sweat profusely, and by that I mean I sweat A LOT. There isn't a day my shirt isn't soaked after a workout, even when I do something mild. I try eating gratuitous amounts of salt to no avail, but I digress.

I got these thinking they'd be able to handle the amount of moisture I put out, but sadly they couldn't. Now when I plug them in, they don't even show they're charging, nor do they turn on. It was a real bummer because I loved listening to music in the gym, and was very happy with these.... until they died.

They're good if you don't sweat like Trump taking a polygraph, otherwise, find something else that's truly graded for "waterproof" and not "water-resistant".

text:

I've installed Plex and Subsonic through their App store and copied all my old media from my old external drives connected to my RPi3, and within 24 hours of unboxing this I'm already up and running again.

The 3 year warranty is nice too, although I hope I never need to use it. But 3 years on a NAS is the best I've seen, most others are only 2.

If you're looking for an inexpensive NAS to get you some fault-tolerant storage, this one from Asus seems like the cream of the crop. The *only* gripe I have so far is that I don't think I can expand the RAM in the NAS. 512 MB isn't very much, as Plex and Subsonic chew up half that even at idle. So if I ever want to integrate my Wyze cam local storage to save to the NAS down the road, I may run into some RAM problems.

title: Connection headers on wrong side of board
text:
This board is nicely made and is very compact. The only draw back I have with it is that it is made for the Pi4, which has known concerns with heat dissipation. That being said, if they placed the connection headers on the bottom of the board, instead of the top, it would have adequate clearance for heat sinks.
I put a 40 pin extension on my board, cut out a 2 pole (4 pin) header for the POE pins on the board, and am good. Additionally, the lines provided on top of the board should duplicate the pin out on the pi 40 pin connector.

title: Poorly thought out design
text:
The pro is it comes with mounting screws and holds the 2.5" drive.

But the design is not well thought out and mounts the drive too deep into the case. If I'm adapting a 2.5" drive to fit in a 3.5" drive space then the mount should mimic a 3.5 " drive. In other words, when mounted in the adapter the 2.5" drive is centered. Since the 2.5' drive is physically shorter than a 3.5 inch drive it makes the cabling hard to route. If you picture most factory built computers, the power cable ends are daisy chained and short between two stacked drives. When the drives are all identical the power cable neatly connects vertically down the row from drive to drive with very little if any slop or slack. Now try to use this adapter to put a 2.5" drive in line with other existing 3.5" drives and the power cable had to somehow bend horizontally into hole where the 2.5" drive is in order to connect to power. Then it has to bend back out to try to reach the next 3.5" drive and the distance between the connectors is just too short. All the designer of this adapter had to do was design the adapter so the 2.5" power and SATA cables are vertically aligned with where they would be if it was a 3.5" drive.

title: Arduino Pro-Mini Compatible
text:
Revised Review: I didn't care for the inconclusive way in which someone marked the voltage selection tab on the board (explained later, with photo) BUT, that said, I upgraded my 3 STARS to 5 STARS. First, I am not sure why people are selecting NANO (and really don't care since. ALL of these Pro-Mini boards loaded and worked perfectly using standard FTDI connections and using the Current Version of the IDE as of Jan 2019 set for, drum roll please: Board: PRO MINI (just as the vendor suggests.). Keep it simple. I uploaded a very large sketch that runs my RFM69HCW wireless sensor node network and these little Pro Mini boards ALL uploaded just great. I haven't connected a scope to verify the digital pin level logic to confirm that it's 5v but I assume that it is as advertised. So, I recommend that users set their Arduino IDE for Pro Mini (as the product description says), use an FTDI USB interface sold here on Amazon (Search: "TinySine Micro USB FTDI Basic Breakout Module for Arduino 3.3V/5V" ). If you do that, you can ignore any REVIEW comments that suggest needing to download any sort of drivers (assuming you already have your Arduino IDE set up).

There is one minor detail that would have downgraded this to 4-stars had it not been for the fact that the price point is offsetting (good trade-off). The headers are a little substandard quality. The metallic content of the pins lacks the composition to promote solder adhesion. Use plenty of flux to distribute heat. After the first ones, I lightly burnished the pins on the others and they soldered pretty well. Experienced users won't find this a big deal but I just mention it when I observe it. Again, I check the price point and shut up.

I hope this helps: Arduino IDE : Pro Mini (as the vendor suggests) and the FTDI USB-to-Serial adapter and you're going to enjoy this product.

Oh yes, someone asked if this is I2C compatible. YES, 100%. Just use the right pins for the library you use (A4/A5 are common). Don't forget to add external pull-up resistors. I use 4.7k for a FIRM transitions. Some people use 10k. Either will work but you MUST use something in this range (I2C bus CANNOT "float").

I will post a photo to illustrate the following point. For now, here's my comment on the SUBJECT title.

The units appear to be good quality. I will test them electrically immediately following this post and will post the results. I'm anxious to see if the bootloaders are present and working as advertised.

You will notice in the photo that there are several "options" labeled on the back. These are 5V, 3.3V, 20Mhz, 16Mhz, 10Mhz, & 8Mhz. The labeling is designed with a check-box for the vendor to use a fine-tip marker to indicate which options apply. The problem is that, in my case, the 5V option was not just checked, it was completely BLUED OUT. Since this is the ONLY label BLUED OUT, I wondered about the intended meaning. To be meaningful, ALL applicable options MUST be either MARKED or UNMARKED. The applicable 16Mhz box is NOT marked but it IS applicable. The 3.3V is NOT marked so by that logic, it IS applicable also? Is 5V marked OUT because it doesn't apply or does it? See the dilemma? It's inconsistent. It would not be a big concern if we're talking about frequency. But, illogical markings like this leave room for errors -- especially since the 5V wasn't just "checked", it was completely over-written. Logging onto Amazon to pull up my orders to see what the ad specified kinda helps. I am going to assume that the vendor intends 5V. Why the other options needing marked but that are not needs addressing by the vendor. Either mark applicable ones (ALL) or don't mark anything. Not following this rule means that the buyer must come here and sift through orders for specs (which should actually be included with the item shipped). Thus, this review.... since I was already here... Zing !!

I will update this review (and appropriate STAR rating after I have tested each unit.

title: Great 4K security camera for the money!
text:
This review is for the RLK8-410B6-5MP home security camera system with 6 bullet cameras. I paid $349 for it on sale.
I really like the way this security camera system operates and it has a very large amount of storage at 2TB. This is my first security camera set up so it took a little time figuring everything out, but I finally got it up and running and so far it’s working really well for me. Having power through Ethernet made installation a breeze! The software is a bit tricky to figure out, but from all the reviews I’ve seen, all of these security systems are a little tough to get set up right. If you aren’t tech savvy or handy with tools this probably isn’t gonna work well for you. In that case it may be best to have it installed.
I really like the fact that I can set the area that detects motion. When cars go by it triggers the alerts, so being able to set the exact area that I want to have motion detection is really helpful.
I don’t know if this is the best system out there but it works for me. The only issues I had was with the connector for the ethernet cable. The cover for that is designed for a different type of ethernet cable than the one that is sent. Those have an extra sheathing on the end so the cover won’t fit with the rubber boot installed. A nice workaround for that is to cut that end off and splice on a new connector and it will fit inside of the cover with the rubber boot. Some have complained about that but I think it’s not that big of a deal personally. I like the fact that you get 60 foot ethernet cables which covered my entire house which is about 1800 sq ft.
The cameras are crystal clear and if you use a 4K TV as a monitor I don’t think you can get a better picture. This system had six cameras but I’m adding two more and the add on cameras are not expensive at all at $35 each.
Tech support is not immediately available as some have mentioned but they do provide videos for set up. They definitely need to cover more videos for specific issues that may be encountered, but I was able to figure it out using the videos provided and a little ingenuity on my part.
Overall I’m very satisfied with this purchase!

title: Loved it for 90 days!  Then had to ship the unit back for warranty service. Wow!
text: I bought this unit for my winter home in Jan 2020.  I am a 70 year old man.  No gaming.  No wrestling on the couch. No softballs thrown in the office. I used my PC for a couple of hours a day to read the news.  When I hooked it up, it was totally satisfactory. Seemed to be a nice monitor for the money.  Very satisfied.  I unplugged the monitor in March of 2020 and returned to my regular home.  It was working fine when I left it.  I returned in November and plugged in my PC and the monitor has a large black spot with lines across it.  It was sold with a three year warranty.  I researched the Samsung warranty, described the issue on the warranty issue site and was instructed to send it back for warranty repair.  They even paid for the shipping.  I received a call today that the monitor screen was cracked and the repair fee would be $150.  I paid Amazon $171 for it new!  I explained the history of use and that the screen had never, never been struck or dropped since I opened the box.  It did not have any marks on the plastic  screen or frame, and that it only failed after sitting unplugged for seven months.  The representative finally agreed to offer the repair for $75.  I was willing until I discovered that the original warranty would be voided and the repaired unit would only carry a 90 day warranty. I told them to dispose of the item and not ship it back to me. I appreciated their offer to compromise on a repair they felt was not warranty, but I was convinced it should have been.  But why would they negate the three year warranty on a ten month old product that was factory repaired?  I believe they must have a problem in this series of monitors.  I will not buy Samsung products in the future.

title: Installed fine...the second time around.  I have some tips.
text:
This is a great product and a great seller. I messed up installing it the first time and got lots of dust underneath the screen saver.

As others have said, read and follow the directions thoroughly. I'll add a couple of tips:

-If you have them, wear those cheap vinyl gloves you can get in bulk pak from Walmart of the big box lumber stores.
-The product comes with strips to use as hinges when you pre-fit the screen saver. Make certain that these are affixed tightly so they do not pull off as you're installing it.
-I saw a tip online where rather than dab the dusting tape over the tablet's screen (it's awkward and does not get 100% coverage), you cover the tablet's screen with strips blue painter's tape (Frog tape), making certain it adheres to the entire screen. Then remove the tape, and off comes the dust with no residue! This was a great help.
-I also used painter's tape along the entire side of the screen saver as the hinge rather than the 2 provided strips. The screen saver wiggled less and was better secured that way.

As others have said, the seller was great when I had problems with the first screen saver I bought. Communication and assistance was really, really good. I see that some have had recurring dust issues when trying the installation again. Using painter's tape to remove all the dust from the entire screen eliminates that issue.

Ok; first of all, these are not bookshelf speakers. I don’t know what kind of giant medieval tomes they’re reading at Polk, but these won’t fit on any of my bookshelves, not even remotely. I had to put them on stands.

That being said; wooooow. These don’t *quite* have the warmth and musicality of say a Dynaudio (of which I own 2 pairs) costing 5 and 10 times as much, but they’re pretty close.

Extremely detailed. Maybe bordering on analytical? Every time I listen to these I remark on the detail. I think that the somewhat analytical sound makes them great for either music or movies. The right amp would warm these right up.

I’m using them in my bedroom for digital music. I’m driving them with a 50WPC AudioSource dedicated power amp, fed by a BlueSound Node 2i. All together it sounds absolutely incredible in a 13x13 bedroom with 12’ ceilings. Even at only 50WPC these can easily get party loud. (Max on the power amp and 2/3 on the Node is jazz club loud in that space.)

Bass extension is there in spades w/o getting at all flabby or muddy. High-end really adds presence in vocals and the hi-hats are right in the room with you.

If you need a great sounding pair of passive speakers, especially to do double duty as TV and HiFi speakers, and have a place to put them, I would very highly recommend them.

title: Far better than the price suggests; make sure your HDMI cable is high-bandwidth
text:
*** EDIT *** I'm seeing that folks are having issues attaining HDR and 1440p on this monitor. I already mentioned it in my initial review below, but you MUST USE A HIGH-BANDWIDTH HDMI CABLE in order for Windows to detect the HDR capabilities and the monitor's native resolution of 2560 x 1440. With standard HDMI cables, the HDR option will be grayed out, and the monitor will be blurry due to it running at lower-than-native resolutions. This is true for ALL HDR and QHD/UHD monitors, not just this one. For folks using DisplayPort, make sure you're not using a cable marked "RBR" (Reduced BitRate); this will cause the same problems.

Also note that Windows HDR is clunky as all get. Turning on HDR will make the entire screen become grey and washed out; at that point, you'll have to manually activate the monitor's HDR to "balance" things out. It's important to note that Windows HDR is NOT for general use; you only turn it on for videos and games that support it.

In any case, I've attached photos showing that I was able to attain HDR and 1440p on this monitor just fine. I did occasionally run into some "flashing" issues when I connected the monitor to a complicated workstation setup with a bunch of HDMI switchers, three monitors of different resolutions, and a DisplayLink dock, but I was able to get around it by simply switching the input a few times; I've never had this issue on my straight-to-monitor gaming setup (which is what I mainly use it for, anyway). Been playing Devil May Cry V on it (which really takes full advantage of HDR, moreso than Monster Hunter World, which I played in my original review), and it looks ABSOLUTELY AMAZING, especially for such a dirt cheap monitor. Still keeping my fingers crossed on this thing eventually exploding though... too good to be true, and all that.

*** ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW ***

I don't normally buy items that have zero reviews: that's a huge red flag for me, as that can sometimes mean that the items have been relisted due to a slew of bad reviews or something. I'm also pretty leery of items that are significantly cheaper than their competition, and this monitor was around $100 cheaper than the cheapest 1440p HDR monitor I'd seen previously; the field itself usually ranges from $400 to $700. I've also never heard of this brand, and there's almost no mention of this monitor anywhere on the web aside from a few obscure Reddit posts. All in all, I had every reason to doubt the quality of this monitor.

Yet somehow, it manages to not merely surpass my low initial expectations, it completely blew away some of my higher ones. This thing is legit.

First, the problems. You'll need to spend some time tweaking this thing's color settings. I personally prefer brighter whites and a cooler tint, and out-of-the-box the monitor was kind of yellowish and grey. After a few tweaks to the monitor settings (kicked down the red and green a few notches and kicked up the blues), I got exactly what I wanted. I retained the default contrast and brightness, which managed to provide deep blacks and bright whites after my color tweaks.

The audio output on the monitor I received doesn't seem to work. Plugging in a 3.5mm RCA to output the HDMI audio doesn't appear to do anything; the monitor insists on outputting audio from the built-in speakers, which are as meh as you'd expect. Possibly just a defect I unfortunately ended up with, but not enough of a problem for me to return it.

So for the good stuff: This thing does 2K (2560 x 1440) resolutions perfectly, just make sure you have an HDMI cable that can handle the bandwidth (and for folks with laptops, ensure that your docks/DisplayLink devices can handle it). If you plug it in and it gets stuck at 1080p without a 1440p option (as I did initially), then try switching to a newer HDMI cable. You also won't be able to take advantage of HDR without a high-bandwidth HDMI cable, so don't neglect it.

Speaking of which, the HDR on this monitor is solid; it won't change your life, and utilizing HDR on Windows 10 is just inherently clunky, but it's a strong improvement over SDR in games like Monster Hunter World, where armor details are more pronounced and shadows and light are more distinct. The HDR is strongest in videos, where it's just utter eye candy. Even without HDR, the contrast and colors pop very nicely, far better than the SDR-only monitors I currently have.

The monitor menus are plain and without frills, but are surprisingly responsive and intuitive for a "cheap" monitor. Even some of the better BenQ monitors I own have sluggish and awkward menus; this bargain, no-name Newsync monitor blows them away in this category, which is important if you're someone who spends a lot of time trying to fine-tune the perfect settings.

This monitor also has FreeSync, which I was unable to test with my Nvidia rig. Regardless, that's just another bonus for folks with compatible vid cards, on top of all the good stuff I've already mentioned.

Above all, this thing is CHEAP. As of writing, I purchased it for $219, which would be insane for even a mediocre 2K HDR monitor, yet this one manages to be pretty darn great (FreeSync support is neat, too, I guess). With no reviews, a dubiously low price, zero brand recognition and not even a Newsync website to follow, I knew this purchase would be a risk. But amazingly, it paid off, and I got a keeper for a price that simply cannot be matched. Maybe I got lucky. Here's to hoping it doesn't explode in a few weeks. Until then, five stars all the way.

title: Not Fully Baked (UPDATED: Defective Unit)
text:
Update: I believe I just received a bad unit. The Display Port connection stopped working altogether. No amount of restarts, cable swaps, and/or alternative sources (Laptop and PC) were able to bring it back. This may explain many of the issues I was encountering.

I was very excited to receive this after waiting so long for it to release.
First the Good:
This display is beautiful and well-built. SDR content is stunning. The fan doesn’t bother me, but my PC isn’t exactly silent either.
Multiple Issues:
1. Flickering Issues:
Flickering was evident in quite a few games. Downloading the latest Nvidia drivers did not make this go away. Turning “Overdrive” off completely or limiting fps to 60 made the issue go away. Not sure what “Overdrive” does but I’m sure it contributes to the high price tag.
These issues were also present on the HDMI input connected to the PS4 Pro so I’m not sure how Nvidia drivers are going to make this issue go away.
2. Visual Artifact Issues:
An interlaced pattern was very evident while running in Battlefield 5. It makes it look like a stocking is pulled over the screen (in game "film grain" was turned off).
3. HDR Issues:
Most frustrating to me personally is HDR. It doesn’t always seem to “kick-in” even though the display thinks it’s active. This was evident in Battlefield 5 and Assassins Creed Odyssey. Sometimes changing the settings in game made it activate and at other times nothing worked but a system restart. When HDR is “on” but not really on, games look washed out and dim.
4. Power Issues:
At one point the display would not power back on. I had to unplug it and reconnect for it to boot up.
When it’s working, it’s amazing. There are just far too many issues to justify this purchase though. Hoping ACER can work them out quickly. If so, I’ll come back to update my review.

title: Best laptop I've owned in years despite thermal issues - UPDATE 05/20/2019
text:
UPDATES 05/20/2019 - original review below.

After a few weeks with the laptop, I have noticed some issues with the laptop. Namely, thermal and WiFi. I've dropped by review from 5 to 4 stars.
None of these issues are deal breakers and I still love this laptop, but let me explain so you are aware going in.

Thermal: the intel i7 processor on this machine is a beast and it produces a lot of heat. Unfortunately, the design of the laptop is so thin that it has no great way to dissipate heat. When the i7 goes up to nearly 4GHz (the turbo boost on it) it usually throttles (clocks down) because the temps of the processor will go up to 90 or so Celcius at least on my machine, (max temp being 100 C). Additionally this will make the fans go kind of whacky. There are a few fixes (and you can implement multiple), one of which I chose to do and it resolved my issue. The first fix is you can undervolt your processor. This requires software called intel xtu. I didn't mess around with this option. The second option is re-pasting your processor, and installing thermal pads on your heat sinks to draw the heat from the processor and GPU to the bottom case to dissipate the heat correctly. This, in addition to the intel XTU are your options if you NEED 4 GHz. The last option, which worked perfect for me was to turn off TurboBoost in the BIOS (very easy). This permanently clocks your processor down to 2.2 Ghz - which for me, was way more than enough performance. I'm able to game at the exact same FPS as with turbo boost, as well as photo editing without any noticeable slowdown. All I've seen from doing this is better temps and no more crazy fans. Again, this isn't a dealbreaker for me and I don't think it should be for you. If it is, and you NEED 4GHz either be prepared to do some work to fix it, or you should consider a gaming machine that dissipates heat better.

The second issue is the WiFi card. The Killer 1535 card included in this machine has some issues. I am replacing it with an Intel 9260 (very inexpensive Wifi Card and easy to do) to deal with these issues. The issues with the card are random disconnects somewhat infrequently, but the 9260 is a cheap easy fix. Driver updates didn't seem to help.

I still love this laptop despite these issues.

ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW

After owning a Dell Latitude E5450 for the last few years, I decided it was time for an upgrade. I set out on a research hunt for a laptop that had high build quality, great performance (preferably with a dGPU), good battery, as compact as possible and not overly expensive. I also wanted a strong 4k panel. Those are some tough requirements to meet, but the Dell XPS 15 9570 exceeded my expectations in these areas.

I've owned a lot of laptops in my lifetime, everything from an Apple Powerbook 150 to a GPD Win, to fat gaming laptops. Out of all of the laptops I've ever owned, this is easily my favorite. Over the last few years I've been fairly disappointed in the direction of Apple and have found myself leaning more and more towards Dell, and as far as I can tell their quality has only gotten better.

BUILD QUALITY
The build quality of this machine is unbelievable for the price. Although styled differently, I feel like I am holding a machine on par with the quality of a MacBook Pro.

PERFORMANCE
The performance of this machine is great, especially for how thin and light it is. The i7 CPU has 6 cores. It's faster than many desktop processors even on the market right now. 16 GB of RAM should be enough for anything you'll run aside from some video processing type tasks. The GTX 1050Ti Max-Q is a fantastic card as well. It's about on par with a 960M in terms of performance (not quite as good as a true 1050ti). Although I don't use this for heavy gaming, I'm able to play Playerunknown's battlegrounds on 1080P with about 50-60 FPS on average. The NVME SSD is snappy. When doing photo editing tasks, the machine doesn't have a single issue.

THERMAL
The laptop stays pretty cool, even under fairly heavy loads. I haven't done any empirical tests, but during heavy gaming the keyboard gets a little warm as does the underbody. Nothing that doesn't happen on any other laptop with this kind of hardware. I did not notice any throttling of the i7 CPU (monitored with task manager) during gaming either. The fans will go on in these situations but this doesn't bother me at all; I'd rather have a cool laptop with fan noise than a hot one with none.

DISPLAY
The display on this is the best part of this whole package. I have the 4K screen and I highly recommend it. The colors are perfect on it, it pops and looks perfect, especially for creative tasks where color is important. I wouldn't recommend the 4k if you have extremely high battery demands or perhaps if you're a hardcore gamer; the 1080p screen would probably be better for you. The 4K screen will probably set you back an hour or two of battery time, and for gaming in FHD on it, it will look a bit weird downscaling to 1080P on a 4K monitor...but to me, the 4K is worth it for the colors and pure beauty.

KEYBOARD
The keyboard is flawless in my opinion. About as good as you can get for a laptop keyboard. The tactile response is perfect, the sound is clicky enough to be engaging but not loud enough to be annoying. Backlit keyboard is a nice touch too.

BATTERY LIFE
Battery life is fairly good for the specs that are in this, with a 97+Whr battery. With keyboard lights off, battery set to high battery life mode in Windows 10, and Dell Power Command set to Optimal, I get about 6 hours with moderate use (web browsing, Photoshop Lightroom CC). This is totally acceptable to me. With the 1080P screen you'd probably get 6-8 hours. With heavy use (such as gaming) don't expect more than 1 - 1.5 hours.

SERVICEABILITY
From what I can tell, this machine is fairly serviceable, especially by today's standards. The RAM and SSD are easily user replaceable, and I'd argue that the battery is as well.

Honestly, I can't think of anything bad to say about this laptop. Maybe that I wish the battery life was a little bit better, but this isn't Dell's fault and I can't knock the machine for it. The hardware in it is some high end power hungry stuff. They somehow stuffed nearly a 100 Whr battery in here which helps a lot but I'm not sure there was much else they could do.

Any other questions and I will try to answer them in comments. This here is a keeper.

title: For the pricepoint, it's a winner.
text:
As an IT Pro for the last 20 years and computer nerd since 1977, I know quality when I get my hands on a device.

I bought this for my mother who wanted a simple computer that was portable, affordable, and limited in frustration seeing that she's a computing neophyte like many people. Admittedly, I'm not all too familiar with Windows 10 S, but know enough about Windows to navigate any other version. From what I experienced, it's a functional OS environment for people who simply want to use the machine without knowing much about security and other IT mumbo-jumbo. In other words, I'm saying that it works as it should for an entry level machine that feels well made without the burden of bloatware and other junk most vendors load onto their devices. The Flex 11 comes straight up with Windows 10 S ready for use straight out of the box -- except for the few minutes you are going to have to spend to get the OS updated via Windows Update.

Unlike other machines that have that "cheap plastic" feel, this doesn't. The keyboard is responsive, the hinges have enough tightness with zero play, and it has all the ports you'd need to plug in any peripheral you would need. The only issue I have with the build is the lack of a "chamfer" on the edge of one of the panels to assist in opening the device when it's closed.

Don't expect this device to beat any speed records - it falls into that "Chromebook" class of 2 in 1 laptops that may outperform many others of its class but again, it's not supposed to be a speed demon with a litany of GPU benchmark records under its belt. It has all the power it needs to surf online, participate in all the social media tools, and entertain with decent multi-media play. The audio and video is functional - not the greatest and certainly not the worst.

What can I say about a machine that does more than what I expected for $266USD? It's a fantastic value for the performance, and it feels durable enough to invoke confidence that it can survive the wear and tear that a primary device will endure.

title: Arrived properly aligned. Got the job done.
text:
Choosing a low-to-medium priced laser collimator can be confusing -- so many makes and models and a price ranging from $20 to near $100 for what seem to be the same item (and, if fact, probably are!).

Some reviews report collimators arriving out of alignment, so the ability to realign the collimator if needed was the deal breaker. Happy to report the Astromania was perfectly collimated out of the box, but with the three little dig-out plugs should it need touching up (no allen key included). To check the collimation, I placed the collimator in the eyepiece focuser and rotated it. The location on the primary mirror of the laser dot did not change. However, I will probably set up V blocks and check at a greater distance.

The included 2" adapter provides a good fit with the collimator, with just enough clearance to get it in and out of the adapter. As expected, this contributes to a small but necessary amount of slop in the position of the laser dot. The solution is to seat the collimator firmly and squarely in the adapter or eyepiece focuser before tightening the screw. If using the adapter, do the same when mounting the adapter in the eyepiece holder. My unit came with a battery, even though it is stated as "not included." On my unit, there is a large step in brightness between positions 4 and 5, and not much difference between 6 and 7. The dot itself is well focused and round. The brightness knob is a bit stiff to turn, but might loosen up over time. Oh yes -- instructions have some spelling errors and erroneously state this collimator is "...for mirror (refractor) telescopes)."

To sum up, you can spend several times over for what appears to be the same item. It worked as expected. In actual use, none of the shortcomings prevented me from aligning my reflector.

title: Great Picture - Okay microphone
text:
Update:
A customer service rep reached out at the beginning of the year. They were running an end of year audit on reviews. This shows the company is serious about getting feedback and improving, which I can appreciate. They sent me two models (this one, the N930E, and another, which I won't discuss here).

The picture quality is still great and I love the ring light, which really can improve the picture quality. I tested the microphone and this one does NOT have the same problem as the previous two I tried (clicking sound when the lens focuses). I guess they just had a bad batch or addressed the problem.

I'm tempted to give 5 stars, because I don't think a microphone is of much importance with a webcam (pretty much every device you use it with will have it's own microphone and you can always buy standalone device, which you probably should anyway). I also appreciate the proactiveness of their customer service. I upgraded it from 3 stars to 4. I'm leaving one off simply because the microphone still leaves something to be desired. I'll let you decide if that's important to you or not.

Original Review:
When I first hooked up the camera it was in poor lighting. I was immediately impressed with the camera quality. The auto focus does a good job, though in general I tend to not be a fan of that feature on any camera. My wife did a live video that night and the first thing I noticed was how absolutely awful the microphone was. I ran various tests on multiple devices and in multiple locations. All the same results.

I got in touch with support and they informed me I needed to do an Amazon return since it was the first 30 days. I did this and I had the replacement 2 days later. After several more tests, the second camera has the same issue, as can be heard in my video. Every time the camera focuses, you can hear a clicking in the audio. There's also a constant "whining" or white noise throughout the audio. It's a shame, because the price point and picture quality is great, but I can say with complete confidence that this is by far the worst microphone I've ever used.

Bottom Line:
If you have a separate microphone, consider getting this. If you expect to use the camera microphone, look elsewhere. I will be returning the second one I got, because while I have a great external microphone, my wife doesn't, and I don't want to worry about moving a separate microphone back and forth.

title: Flimsy, noisy microphone
text:
Background: I purchased this product to upgrade from an LG HBS750 headset which I have used for several years and still functions appropriately, but I have found annoying on occasions due to the external earbud wires. I was looking for something with similar form and function to the 750 and my evaluation of this product will unavoidably be compared against it. I am greatly disappointed on this product as per the PROS/CONS below.

PROS:
- Battery life: excellent both for calling and listening to music
- Fit: comfortable fit and I often forget I am wearing it around my neck. It usually stays in place even if you recline or lay down. Earbuds are comfortable once you select correct size adapter and do a great job of blocking noise.
- Incoming sound quality: It has excellent sound quality for listening to music or phone conversations.
- Aesthetics: Sharp looking headset

CONS:
- Outgoing sound quality: People constantly and forcefully complain about background noise, whether this be rustling of papers while sitting at my desk, walking, any accidental brushing of headset against the collar of my shirt, etc. Please note that my habits and environment have not changed significantly since I started using this product vs. the 750 and this was not an issue in the past. It seems that great care was not taken to minimize pick up from background noise and sound transference along the components.
- Durability: The neck piece broke near one of the hinges after only one month of use (see pictures). It should be noted that, while this headset can be collapsed and packed away, I have not used this feature. It generally spends its days in the deployed position on my nightstand (charging as needed) and then worn throughout the day.
- Charging plug fit: The plastic plug used to block the charging port when not in use has a poor fit and will not stay in place no matter how carefully it is inserted. This never became a significant issue due to its early failure.
- Buttons are somewhat difficult to locate and access, particularly when wearing (even thin leather) gloves.

I would not recommend this product based on the durability and ambient noise pickup issue.

title: It is a great screen protector
text:

This kit comes with four pieces; a keyboard cover, a touch pad (mouse) protector, a privacy screen cover and a large microfiber cloth.

The privacy screen cover works almost as stated. It darkens the screen when looking from either side. If you are in a public place, no one sitting next to you will see your screen. I do think that on an airplane, given the closeness of the seats in coach/economy, the person next to you will be able to see about 40% of your screen.

The keyboard protector goes on easily and stays in place. It is extremely thin and hard to notice. It does bounce very slightly while typing but it provides good protection for the keys.One issue I have encountered with this is that it has been stuck to the privacy screen after opening the lid of the laptop. I have to place it back onto the keyboard.

Tip for installing, place the top in first and align it to the left and right edges. The just apply it from top to bottom and it goes on straight.

One more tip, save the plastic cover it came with. This will help protect the privacy screen when you are not using it.

title: Incredible value for price (1yr update)
text:
EDIT: After three months the phone is still so solid in all areas. Made a great purchase here.
EDIT 2: After one year, AccuBattery reports 90% battery capacity retention. Solid.

Original review: The Galaxy A50 is the first phone I've ever bought unlocked. I've had it for over a month now and I feel I can safely say that this really is an incredible phone for the price point.

Its battery is the best thing about it, and it's actually why I bought the phone. It always lasts the entire day with heavy usage AND GPS on, will probably last you two if you don't use it very often throughout the way. Full marks.
I'm on AT&T's network and there's been absolutely no reception issues in Texas. Can't say for anywhere else but I assume it's still good.
The speaker volume is very good and the phone even came pre-installed with a screen protector, which is awesome. (And a microSD card!)
I can't say much for its gaming performance. Not because it's bad, but rather, I hardly play games on my phone to properly give an opinion. Seemed solid with Minecraft though. (Update: It runs kinda poorly in Pokemon Masters, but all other games are no struggle.)
And although it may not serve much use in the US, its radio feature is actually very cool. I love that.
This may be a hot take, especially considering others' reviews of it, but the in-screen fingerprint reader is not half bad. It's definitely not as lenient as you would hope, but if you can learn to scan your finger in a consistent angle, it's acceptable.

The camera's the worst part about the phone, but I feel the default Samsung Camera app does it even more injustice. For video capture, stabilization is always on so you have a large feeling of delay when you capture video. Some aspect ratios aren't available, and video framerate options are nowhere to be seen. Additionally, while the camera supports the Camera2 API, those features are stripped from Pro mode. A workaround I now use is downloading Open Camera off the Play Store and enabling Camera2 features.

All that aside though, the camera still offers interesting and fun shots to take. It really should be fine for people who aren't power users. It's good enough.

Another minor inconvenience is that the phone lacks Smart Capture entirely, for whatever reason. I had to download Screen Master as a replacement ... which seems to do fine as is, so it's not a big deal.

One last thing is that I notice my touches stick when I type too fast, resulting in accidental swipe text input. I don't know if that's a global thing or if that's just some sort of unfortunate issue I have. This never happened with my S7. I just remedy it by typing slower.

Overall though? This is a really good phone. It's exceeded my expectations in several areas. :)

PS. Attached images are shots I've taken with the camera. Aside from resolution shrinking (for bandwidth's sake) and captions, these are unedited.

Onkyo receivers while rated one step higher than Yamaha from my research have issues with HDMI. I have an older 720P HDMI Plasma with pre HDMI 1.2 compliance and it had big issues with syncing over HDMI with my TV. There are a number of forums out there covering this issue with several of these receivers. My last Yamaha Receiver after 3 years of operation started having issues with switching HDMI inputs and the reason for this purchase. While I wish I did not have to make this purchase I was happy with its performance and local and online internet connectivity with Spotify, NAS, NET Radio, AirPlay, Bluetooth, Apple TV, Fire TV, and Blu-ray device I have. I have a 7.1 Polk speaker setup and sounds great. Easy to use controls and excellent iOS app for my iPhone with extensive amount of control functions. Great integration with Logitech Harmony Hub and Alexa. No THX in this unit but not sure I will miss that with a 5.1 setup. This receiver does support 7.2 and a second zone as well as Dolby Atmos if I want to go that route in future. Standby power option is a must if you stream music from phone and want the receiver to come on when you start playing a music selection. Onkyo phone app was not as extensive as the Yamaha app I use.

[Update 1/25/2020]:
Added 2 side speakers for 7.1 setup and still performs well. For entertaining the instant on and streaming music from Spotify and NAS is easy and soundstage is great even in a small apartment.

Overall I will give this projector a solid 3.5. It satisfies my current needs and performs exactly how I expected.

I purchased this projector to setup in my garage to watch football/basketball and the occasional movie for my kids. I will say that the crispness of the picture at night is good, small lettering is easy to read from 15 feet away. The color is good, and the keystone config is good enough. This Projector is pointing to the back wall in my garage (north/South), furthest from the garage doors and the ambient light (easy/west) that comes in from the sun around noon - 5pm is enough to wash the picture out completely during the day. As of 6:30pm on 10/11/2020 it's getting dark enough that you can easily view a game outside, while still managing to keep an eye on the kids (bonus +1).

On a side note, I'm also using a Roku to stream via the supplied HDMI and USB for power. The Roku does NOT control audio/power to the projector.

You just have to make sure there isn’t a single piece of fuzz/dust/hair on the screen and then it should be fine. Also, when installing, I would recommend doing it in a room where there isn’t a ceiling fan on or any other type of air blowing because fuzz/dust/hair is in the air. Also, don’t peel the plastic off the screen protector until you are 100% ready to install because like I said, “there is fuzz/dust/hair floating around in the air,” and if it gets on the sticky side of the screen protector and it’s a lot harder to get off than it is on the actual screen.

While the 25mm works great, 1 of 3 lenses working is ridiculous. The Barlow lens is cheap and pointless. While I don't expect an amazing telescope at this price point, it should be decent for a beginner. This one missed the mark and will be returned.

This is my 3rd Kindle. The first was maybe a 3rd Gen. then I had the 2nd Gen Paperwhite briefly. The upgrade program was irresistible from the Paperwhite to the Oasis. I went with the 32gb, no ad, WiFi Version.
I have always liked paper books, but I wanted a dedicated E - reader that would motivate me to read more. The increased screen size and the inclusion of Audible was what sold me. I wasn’t sure if I wanted to spend $300 on this, I could have spent another $80 and got a nice iPad. But I merely want to read more books and I believe I will do that. The user experience is very satisfying.

title: Great battery life, frustrating design
text:
UPDATE: I've bumped this up to four stars for the following reasons: 1. Anker's legendary customer service - as a long-time Anker customer, I knew this about them, but they once again proved that they are a costumer-centric company. This makes them stand out among the fly-by-night retailers of Apple knock-offs.

2. A few more weeks of use have allowed me to see the design as more idiosyncratic than frustrating. I still don't like some things (see original review below), but I've adapted. Now, I genuinely like these things.

3. Ongoing great call quality. I'm always impressed with how good I sound. This makes them worth a lot, compared to other truly wireless buds.

Two more quick notes: First, the picture I posted is NOT the correct way to wear them. As my review mentions, this is to demonstrate that you can wear them in either ear, with a fair degree of comfort. Second, I've had NO problem with audio-video syncing via earbud, whether using an iPhone or my Windows 10 laptop. Good for you, Anker.

Okay, here's the original:

I've used dozens of wireless earbuds over the years, but these are the first truly wireless set. For my budget, they were kinda pricy at $80, but a gift card from a friend, along with a Best Buy rebate program, brought the price down. I've used single ear micro ear buds, but they're a different animal from these. Here are my observations, after a couple weeks of use:

PROS
- **Excellent battery life**: I usually listen for a few hours every day, and have gone a full week without recharging the case. Granted, I often have only one earbud in, and the volume level is between 30-50%. For my needs though, the battery is more than enough.

- **Fantastic mic for phone calls **: After some minor shifting of the stem to point more directly toward my mouth, I sounded really good to everyone I called. This is a first for me, using Bluetooth buds. Again, I usually use only one side for casual calls and listening, and the mic quality is good. For even better quality, or in especially noisy environments, put both earbuds in.

- **Comfortable fit**: These are light and easy to find a good fit for your ears, with three different sets of rubber tips. With ear canals the size of Erie Canal, I used the largest size, and had no problems. They are also fairly discreet in the ears. Anyone can see you are wearing them, but it isn't ostentatious.

- **Solid connection**: These have _less cut-out_ than wired BT earbuds, especially when outside for a jog. Even walking along a wide-open field on a windy morning, I didn't experience any issues. Other devices will cut out when I go outside; these don't.

- **Gets really quiet without going silent**: While some earbuds get plenty loud, they don't get super quiet. If you are listening to these as you drift off to sleep, you can turn them way down, while still hearing them.

This list shows that Anker got a LOT right. And of course, there are some gimmes that I haven't mentioned: They stay in the ear, they come in two colors, they are water-resistant, the rubber tips fit securely on the plastic body, etc, etc. Many cheaper sets don't hit these marks, resulting in a frustrating experience. But this review isn't over. Here are some "meh" aspects of the Liberty Airs:

HO-HUM
- **Okay build quality**: The plastic seems durable, but it is a bit chintzy-looking with the glossy plastic. Though the magnetic lid usually stays shut in my pocket, if it drops, the lid flies open and the buds invariably fall out. It's not bad, but it could've been a bit better.

- **Middling volume level**: I didn't have a problem hearing these, even around loud tools, like chainsaws! But I've definitely had louder. It's not bad at all - but they don't crank as loud as some.

- **No USB-C**: It just seems like this would be a no-brainer in 2018-19. It's simple enough to use the regular USB port, but they're so finicky, and we all need to work to ensure that USB-C is the standard. Missed opportunity, Anker.

- **Not-super-intuitive audio prompts**: I like the chimes and beeps to let me know what's happening - they're pleasant enough, anyway. But it's not clear what's happening every time. It seems like they could've done a simple voice instead of the slightly-cryptic R2D2 lingo.

None of these are deal-breakers, and they shouldn't make you question the purchase. However, there are blank more things you should be aware of. These are potential deal-breakers:

FULL-FLEDGED CONS
- **Insufficient sound quality for price**: I really thought, with an MRSP of $80, these would have really decent sound. Don't get me wrong, it's not bad for casual listening. But I've heard better in wired Bluetooth earbuds. There is little depth to these earbuds. Everything sounds flat, with little aural texture. Perhaps I expected too much, but I was disappointed.

- **Pathetic on-earbud controls**: The touch controls are finicky at best. Even after a couple weeks' of use, it still takes two or more tries just to pause a podcast. While I didn't have much problem with accidental triggering, the over-engineered touch-sensitive zones are way too much form and cool factor, and not nearly enough function. Fail.

- **Inability to use both sides independently**: For me, this is the most frustrating failure. You can ONLY use the right earbud by itself. The left is a "slave", meaning that it doesn't pair with the phone, but the right unit. This means you can't switch back and forth between the two buds while the other charges; you can't switch ears when one gets fatigued; and you have to be careful to not lose the right one. Since my left ear is more dominant, I have figured out how to wear the right bud in that ear when desired (see pic in review). But I really wish they hadn't designed it this way.

- **Awful experience when switching between devices**: The most confounding problem is switching between devices. I have an iPhone 6s and a current-gen Windows laptop. But if I want to switch between the two devices, I have to unpair one from the buds, turn off the Bluetooth, and then search for the earbuds from the other device. Often, that doesn't work, and I need to turn off and turn back on the earbuds. There's really no excuse for this.

With this list of cons, someone might ask why I don't just return them. If all I needed these for was listening to music, I would. But they still are great for audiobooks and podcasts. Also, the strong performance in phone calls make them worth it to me. I'd grade them a lot better if they didn't cost $80.

If you want reliable quality, long battery life, and great mic performance, these are for you, even at nearly $100. If you value ease of use, switch between devices often, and want to really experience all the nuances of your music, consider something else.

title: Hidden Gem in the Portable Monitor World
text:
I've been on the search for a good portable monitor for about the last 1-2 years to use as both a portable larger screen for gaming (Android Phone or Switch) as well as a portable monitor for working while on the road or away from my typical desk setup. I use Microsoft Surface products which have pretty great monitors so the bar was already set pretty high, since the portable monitor sits right next to the Surface device in my setup.

I had seen a couple of reviews praising this monitor from Uperfect but had to see it for myself. In a few short words I was blown away. I'll list a few of the great features:
- the monitor is very bright, especially when using the supplied AC adapter or other high wattage supply. One great feature, when the power being supplied is weaker, the monitor sets a lower brightness to allow it to function regardless.
- the colors are rich and vibrant, even when compared to the Surface device or my vibrant phone screen.
- after having used a few portable monitors and other devices needing micro-HDMI, mini-HDMI etc. it was an amazing convenience to just plug a standard HDMI into this monitor. A great feature I didn't know I wanted.
- the monitor settings control uses a series of buttons, NOT joysticks or rotary wheels that break and are delicate as seen on other brands. I have high confidence that these buttons will last and not be damaged when transporting the monitor (as seen on other brands). This is a PORTABLE monitor after all.
- the 13.3 inch size is surprisingly small and portable yet large enough to be very useable. I should mention that the overall monitor is also very light, making it even more portable.
- other little features that make this monitor flexible and convenient for any use: micro-usb passthrough for using wired keyboard/mice, 2X USB-C (one for signal, one for power), mini-display port (Mac) and the headphone jack if your device doesn't already have one (typical these days), the body is metal giving more confidence in the overall durability.
- when propping the monitor up for use, I find it easy to use the pencil method or if I need more angle variability I use my Moko stand (small and easy to transport). Since the monitor is so light (no battery) any light duty stand will do.

The only downvote and it's very minor is that the case is pretty cheap and not very useable. I'm working with Uperfect to remedy this.

Because the picture and overall quality are so high, I'm really looking forward to an eventual update of this monitor with a higher refresh rate (120Hz), and touch input, but keeping the same size, if they decide to go down that route.

Highly recommended for your PC, Phone, Nintendo Switch (with dock of course), Raspberry Pi, SFFPC and uses I haven't realized yet. It's so refreshing to see a brand finally get this right!

title: Great for more than just photos, but a little slow
text:
I'm really glad I found this! My use for it may be a bit unconventional compared to others. I actually purchased this card reader for storing large files for an animation project, and needed a lot more space on my ipad to back up my work every day. I work with large PSD documents in procreate and use them back and forth with photoshop on my desktop. I was pleasantly surprised, the boneview is very useful and reliable so far.

Pros: you're not limited by the sizes of OTG flash drives, since those can get quite pricey and SD cards are more accessible and plentiful! Also the boneview app is relatively straightforward and easy to use compared to others, there aren't many bugs.

Cons: I should mention that there's a few trade-offs you should be wary of. It's a bit difficult to move files within the external card using the mobile app, you kind of have to cut and paste them back onto your device and then back onto the card. This might be a bit annoying if you accidentally put them in the wrong folder.

One big issue is that the writing speed is very slow (it only clocked about 5-6 MB/second when I was adding files to it on my computer). I'm not sure if that's just due to the limitations of using SD cards, or if it can be ameliorated in the future version. But as long as it works and is reliable, I don't have many complaints for the slowness, as I can leave it transferring files in the background while doing something else of course.

title: STAY THE HECK AWAY!!!!! Pins too long and we’re bent from the factory
text:
You know I had high hopes for this motherboard, In theory it’d be awesome if i could had used the board, we ordered the Gigabyte Aorus Z370 Gaming 7 Motherboard and Thermaltake tempered glass tower and several other parts for our daughter for Christmas to start a gaming tower build, and finally got the rest of the parts for it this weekend to build the computer so I mount the board and all that stuff and it’s ready for the cpu and I pop the protective cover off and go to seat the processor and it won’t lock down, several pins are sticking up way too high, they were too long and won’t let the processor seat, I’ve been doing computers professionally since 1994 and I’m pretty sure I know what I’m doing by now, I call gigabyte and they tell me I can have the board replaced if I pay an additional $100.00 because, and get this, “socket damage isn’t covered under the warranty” I said wait this is a defective product they said nope it’s not covered under warranty and I needed to go back to amazon where I bought it, well I paid $230.00 new in December and because we didn’t open it and install it until today it can’t be returned so now I have $1500.00 worth of computer build gaming parts that were bought to build around this motherboard and I can’t use any of it unless I buy another of the same board so I stand by my statement and say stay the H E double hockey sticks away from this manufacturer, this was a brand new board and it has pins that are too long and bent from the factory, yet that’s my fault that it’s a manufacturers defect and I have to eat $230.00 because amazon won’t return or replace it and neither will Gigabyte

You know it’s a sad state of affairs when a manufacturer won’t stand behind their product, they blame the customer and take their money and say go to that place downstairs where the developer punishes you for your sins, except this isn’t my sin, it’s gigabytes cheaply made product and they obviously could care less about their customers or their product and if you get a defective product they tell you oh my this doesn’t happen to our product, it’s your fault you did it even though you didn’t even touch the socket until you went to put on the processor, what a shoddy way to do business and a bad way to treat your customers... it’ll be my last gigabyte product of any kind and no one I know or talk to will ever use this product again because they value my expertise and experience, I mean I’ve been doing this for 25 years, every since the personal computer became popular in the early 1990’sso this isn’t new to me and I know my way around a motherboard

Stay away and go with a different manufacturer because I doubt this is the first case I’d this happening regardless of what Gigabyte support says

Bill

title: Better than original running time, fixed bricking problem
text:
Had a Samsung Galaxy S8+ phone that developed the infamous problem of bricking when the battery ran out. What happens is that the phone doesn't have enough power to turn on and ask for fast charging, and so it can't be charged back up or powered on at all. Reviving such S8's involves connecting it to a fixed 9v power supply to get it to unbrick and start charging, after which it will charge normally on the OEM charger—until the next time you run it to 0%. Over the next year, the phone got to the point where it was self discharging rapidly, even if turned off. So rapidly that the phone would slowly discharge even when fast charging on the Samsung wireless charger!
I purchased this battery in hopes of at least restoring usable battery life, if not fixing the bricking problem too. So far, it has exceeded expectations: the phone runs longer than ever before on a charge, and powers up after a few minutes of being connected to the OEM charger when run dead. Only one more test remains for this replacement battery, and that is longevity. If it wears out quickly, I'll update this review. Otherwise, assume that this battery is continuing to impress!

title: A quality earphone, with great sound at a fair price.
text:
These headphones are not only convenient but efficient as well. They provide comfort and great sound quality. You can tell the difference in sound quality compared to other brands and earphones alike. They are the perfect sound device for listening to music, stories, videos, news, etc. They provide quality noise cancellation as there is little to no background noise when using these. I also enjoy the minor, minute details built into these earphones, such as the noise cancellation command. If you wish to cancel out any noise, you can. However, if you wish to hear your surroundings, then that is also an option. The controls are simple and easy to adjust to. However, a couple of issues are that if you take out one earphone, it pauses you completely. It is not bad, and though it is definitely smart, I feel that it should be optional instead of forced. Additionally, for over $150, one would hope that they would be waterproof so that music and stories could be enjoyed while showering or perhaps while in the rain. Unfortunately, that is not the case, so bummer there.

Furthermore, the charging case is very convenient. Simply pop your earphones in to charge, and within a few minutes, they are charged and ready to go. The case has an extended battery life and is also magnetic, making for easy earphone storage and charging. These headphones are handy for listening to some good tunes while on the go, active, or killing time as they provide a quality sound with no distortions or breakups in sound. They are easy to pair, to turn on and off, and to operate. I'd say that overall, these are quality headphones. However, there is room for improvement, as stated in the critiques above. You get what you pay for. However, if you're looking for something more advanced, then there are certainly other options out there. Personally, I find them to be about right in price for the quality you get and they are still great, but they could be better.

title: Cable management is a breeze with this case
text:
First off, my last PC case was a mid-tower and that felt quite a bit cramped, especially with modern graphics cards getting larger and larger, and CPU air coolers being so damn huge that it takes up the rest of the space in your case. Oh and then there was the hard drives with their cables dangling in the way. Some people are really good at cable management and those people are cool and all, but I wound up with my last case looking a total wreck because I just didn't have any room for anything.

Well this case is a full tower so it's much more roomy. Hard drives are actually oriented sideways relative to the front of the case, so the cables aren't in the way and there's enough spots to route cables through that you don't even have to see them if you don't want to. My power supply has all the cables nicely pre-wrapped and it's modular so I can install them as I need them (or don't and save some more space) and combine that with being able to route the cables around the back of the motherboard and the whole thing has a MUCH cleaner look to it. You might almost be convinced I'm now one of those cool guys who can do really good cable management.

The glass side panel is tinted a bit, but if you have some fancy internal lights you can still easily see everything. I've got my CPU cooled with a huge Noctua DH-15 cooler and with everything running it barely makes any noise. The hard drive makes more noise than the fans do. I docked one star off the noise level because the hard drive DOES make a lot of noise. I think it vibrates the whole case or something. Maybe if it had some kind of dampening it wouldn't be so bad...but it's still a whole lot quieter than my old Lian Li case.

There's also plenty of ventilation holes in the top, front, back and bottom of the case. The top and bottom also has an external air filter held in place by magnets so you can help keep the insides of your case from getting dusty.

All in all though, this has been a great case as long as you don't mind the size. I used to prefer the mid towers but I think I enjoy having all this extra room. It has made installing everything much easier.

title: installed today, kind of
text:
Got this on my porch yesterday and put it on my truck today. For the price I was not sure what to expect. Comes with a little camera and mounting plate, a little LED screen, and a bunch of wire. I have a Tundra with a cap, so backing up and getting close to anything is hard to judge. Usually leave way too much space. I know I will be at a ski area tomorrow where they have packed my truck in before. Turning radius is not great, and even in a little car I don't think they leave enough room. So had been thinking about something like this for a while, and for the price figured I would give it a shot. I attached the camera to the license plate with the license plate screw, ran the wire up into the truck bed, through the cap clamps just to keep it out of the way, through the back window of the cap, through the back window of the truck (just closed the window on it) and across the back seat to the front. Plugged it into the lighter, flipped it on and it worked!

Few things I need to do. First is to figure out a better way to get the wire from the back of the truck up and into the cab. I would prefer not to drill, but may end up doing that (for this and other reasons). Used to be that they would put little rubber gaskets in the firewall, but don't see anything I can snake a wire through on this truck. Also don't like the wiring going through the window, and across the back seat. So a real install will be longer and will have to wait until temp gets warmer.

But I am impressed. I did notice my license plate sits set back, so my field of vision is limited, and it also means that I can see the back bumper step with the camera aimed down. Since it is at an angle that way, it means that I still have about a foot when I see something go out of view under my bumper. Day time picture is fine, and even at night had no problem backing up into my driveway and getting close to my garage door. Very much the same quality picture as our factory installed/ built in Honda one on our other car. My only fear/ concern is that I can see the camera getting a very dirty lens, and where it is could be bumped easily. Also worry about wires getting snagged and breaking. But overall a good product for a great price.

title: A simple fix for the one real product flaw - the mounting bracket - and an update
text:
This is an outstanding value and there is a simple solution to the flimsy bracket problem.

Find or purchase some ready-to-use lightweight "spackle" (wall hole filler/repair paste) or modelling clay that hardens and fill the spaces in the part of the bracket that mounts to the surface. Let it dry ("cure") until it's firm and it will keep the plastic from cracking or splitting if your screws are driven a bit too tightly.

Some other recommendations:
-Keep a magnifying glass handy when you're reading the "quick start" guide (the print is incredibly small).
-Be patient waiting to charge the battery the first time - it takes hours before that orange light goes out and the green one (fully charged indicator) comes on. We proceeded with the connection setup while it was still charging.
-Also be patient with the PC/Windows installation process; the network setting instructions are neither intuitive nor crystal clear and the only detailed manuals available on the Reolink web site do not match this particular product. (Couple this issue with the bracket problem and you'll understand why it's a 4 star not 5.)
-For your own privacy and security, make sure you change the password!!!
So far, so good.

Update - March, 2020 - the Windows client software has developed a significant bug and the beta test new version they sent me a link to doesn't connect to the camera. Basically, the capture function that used to work now creates non-readable 0K .jpg files. You can still get them from your Android tablet or your smartphone, but if you're counting on being able to capture images to your PC, you should wait until they resolve the issue.
