title: Unbelievable sound with a more, unbelievable price.
text:
I have been on the hunt for the RIGHT gaming headset for over a year. I have owned the Turtle Beach Stealth PX24, Hyper X Cloud Stinger, both the Playstation Gold and Platinum Wireless headsets. Then, I upgraded to the wire-happy, Astro A40 TR with mixamp. I felt the A40 was bit, overpriced, performance-wise. THEN, I went to the Turtle Beach Stealth 520, which is wireless and has several, surround sound presets, including the featured, SuperHuman Hearing. However, it seemed, like each time I would game with the Stealth 520 for a bit, my ears and eventually, head would start to sweat, due to the enclosed, faux-leather design of the ear cushions. Many times, I would snatch the headset off and play, without it. Then, I went to the Arctis Pro, which was superb in sound quality and build. However, I returned them because they caused me to have headaches after gaming sessions. Then, I was on the hunt for another headset. However, I decided to go a different route and get some stereo headphones for gaming, which led me to finding out about the HD688B by Superlux. I learned about these headphones via various reviewers on YouTube. In addition, they mentioned how superb the HD688B was for gaming, despite being stereo headphones by default. I was sold and decided to give them a try. For the price. Why not? Still, I was wondering, if I would get a good experience by gaming with stereo headphones or should I stay in the gaming headset lane?

DESIGN: Overall, the design of the HD688B is not my favorite. Very, basic design. The headphones is very, comfortable. The headband is made up of a wiry, hard, plastic, structure, which looks cheap, but is extremely, durable. Underneath, is a patented, auto-adjusting, headrest for stability and comfort. Plus, the headrest has a manual, sliding adjuster to compensate for an increase in head size, as well. The headphones are semi-open, which means all of the sound, may not leak out for others, nearby to hear. Also, all outside sounds, may not come in. Of course, sound performance, may vary, based upon, if the ear cushions are changed from the original ones. Of course, the original, faux leather cushions, which are included on the HD688B are terrible. I would suggest buying some aftermarket, ear cushions. Needless to say, I fell in love with the AirWeaved ear cushions, which were featured on my previously-owned, Arctis Pro. So, I purchased those on Amazon. Also, the headphones do not have any external buttons to work the headphones, like a volume button or an external mic, as it is not a gaming headset by default. PS4 users will have to change the volume by accessing Volume Control (Headphones) option on the PSN settings menu. Not much of a hassle in my opinion. Of course, if a DAC or sound card is purchased, which has a button, that could change. Also, a mod-mic will be needed to use a microphone for these headphones.

SOUND: The driver size is 50mm, double-dome, neodymium magnet, which is great. The frequency response is an above-average, 10-30KHz. Many headphones or headsets are at 20-20KHz. In addition, the impedance of 56 ohms with a maximum input power of 300 mW is impressive for protection from overload by various audio equipment. The sound from the HD688B, gives perhaps, the most authentic sound, which I have heard, while gaming. Every sound can be heard with ambience and clarity from all angles, crisp with no distortion. The highs/low balance of sounds are very good, as well. Bass is there in the HD668B, but not too, much. An increase amount of bass, drowns out pure sound in my opinion. Of course, I use the headset for gaming on my PS4. With the standard ear cushions, the sound was, just right. Not, too loud or too, low. However, with the change of the ear cushions, as mentioned, I saw a much-improved, difference. I would also, suggest to add a sound card or DAC. I have a [ [ ASIN: B01MXJ83G4 Neoteck 192kHz DAC Converter with Volume Control Aluminum Digital Optical Coaxial Toslink to Analog Stereo Left/Right RCA 3.5mm Jack Audio Adapter for PS3 XBox HD DVD PS4 Sky HD Plasma Blu-ray ] ]. The combination will surely, make the HD688D reach its full, optimal sound performance. With that said, there have been opinions, the HD688B is not loud for PS4. Well, get both of those modifications and that opinion will change, quick.

I tested the performance of HD688B with the original and the AirWeave ear cushions, while playing Call Of Duty Black Ops 4. The original ear cushions, made the sound from the HD688D a bit, average. Not, too loud, but not too, low. However, I saw a noticeable difference, between both, while playing. The design of the AirWeave cushions, enhanced the sound and the treble of the HD688B. I was in awe of how authentic the sounds were, as I was playing. The gunfire, explosions, dialogue and other random sounds on the map to the left and right of me, were heard, loud and clear. The HD688B picks up low sounds, like a vacuum. For example, on the Morocco map, outside of hearing the common sounds, during gameplay, I could hear the clinging and breakage of pottery, while being shot or kicked around. Never heard that on my last two headsets. Then, while playing on the Icebreaker map, hearing the deep, crunching sound, as my character, Battery was trampling through the snow and the cracking of the ice, sounded unbelievably, real. Once, on the map, Summit, Battery ran inside of an open-ended bay. Battery was making a quote, while outside and the quote ended, while going half-way inside of the bay. There was an echo of Battery's voice, while making a quote, inside of that open-ended bay. The authenticity of the echo was unbelievable and nearly, scary. Of course, FPS gamers like to know about being able to hear footsteps. Well, footsteps of teammates and enemies CAN be heard, clearly and in more abundance, as they come, much closer. Perhaps, stereo headphones, might be better than a gaming headset. Considering, these headphones are under $50, the HD688B performs better than many, gaming headsets or even, headphones that is twice or three times the cost. HOW could Superlux pull this off and sell these at such a low price? I am cannot complain.

MIC (OPTIONAL): Like I mentioned, a mod-mic will have to be purchased to utilize, while online gaming. The prices vary. I have not tried this, yet, as I do not have a mod-mic at this time. I do know, with one attached, it should perform, exceptionally, well.

VERDICT: Overall, the Superlux HD688B is a steal, considering the performance for the price. They, just might be the best ever, which is puzzling because it is the cheapest of the majority of the so-called, high-performing, gaming headsets and various stereo headphones. While the design, may not be the prettiest, the HD688B makes up for it with an unbelievable performance. Of course, as headphones by default, the sound is great. In addition, these headphones double for gaming and performance better than any gaming headset on the market. I would suggest going to pick these up. After use, stereo headphones, just may be the way to go, moving forward.

title: Excellent build quality, ok temps and build options
text:
This was the first time I used an NZXT product for one of my builds, and the fit and finish of this case was excellent. Great for anyone that wants a clean simple case while still being able to show off their fancy gamer build. Only mild complaints are with build restrictions and airflow.

The case is designed around a specific layout: rads want to be up front, cables have to use the classic NZXT shroud, etc. Not really a problem if you're ok with how they planned things out, but know it's not the most flexible layout.

Airflow is not amazing compared to other ITX cases with more perforations. However, the entire front intake area is covered by a dust filter, and realistically your temps will probably be only a couple degrees C higher than a case that has a lot more holes (and probably dust) in it.

- yes it fits a Noctua D15 with Chromax covers
- yes it fits an ATX PSU
- the NZXT cable shroud is removable for squeezing in a top fan
- if you have a bracket to stack 3.5in hard drives, you can fit at least 2 inside the lower shroud
- cable management is great as long as you follow their intended layout
- wish the glass panel was tinted, or that this came with a vented metal side panel option
- add your rear M.2 drive before installing the motherboard in this case. The mounting screw was blocked on the Strix B550-i

title: Great compact fill light
text:
There's a lot of positive things to say about this light. I think that it achieves its purpose very well and that it's a great bang for the buck. For $25 bucks you get a lightweight, rechargeable, hotshoe/tripod mounted light that easily has enough power for filling in dark spaces or casting light on close subjects.

Build quality: Overall, pretty great. The USB-C port was nice and tight, and the dials feel good. They have a good tactile click when you turn them on and off and the selection of color is easy with the smooth turning dials. The light face has a nice diffuser plastic covering it and even at the lowest light level, a camera would struggle to see the individual LEDs. One complaint I have about the fit and finish is that the hotshoe mounts on the sides of the device are pretty tight and it's hard to get something else seated all the way into the mounting points.

Light quality: The light from this portable device is pretty bright. The first and last picture show the light at its max and minimum light setting, and there is a pretty good range. Comparing to a normal bulb, I would say that this equivalent to about 30-40w. If you are using this as a vlogging light, you can turn it bright enough to make it uncomfortable to look at, but also adjust it down far enough that you could easily put this in your camera hotshoe and use it as a fill light for your face.

Overall impression and usefulness: I'd say that this light will permanently live in my camera bag as a fill for video or photo shoots. While flashes are nice and provide a ton of light, sometimes having something small and convenient like this can make all the difference. I'd get another one, and at only $25, it's a pretty good deal. The most convenient thing about this is that I can easily charge it from my power bank with the same cable I use for my phone, so it really cuts down on clutter in my bag.

A bit small for VRAM but you can stack two of them side by side to about cover it. These are definitely for VRMs.

One thing to note: these are miserable for sticking to the chips. The pre-attached thermal tape does not adhere well at all to a chip die surface. I ended up using the existing thermal tape that was on my VRAM already and just stuck these to that. So far it's been fine, but they still could come off easily. Fortunately the tape I had there was already sticky.

On the other hand, my card has a midplate that covers the VRMs and I just kind of stuck these on top of that for a bit more heat dispersion because.... well, I had them so why not? And it turns out they stick like glue against a metal surface. They locked down to the midplate like they were welded to it.

Overall these are okay. They definitely helped my temps a bit. But I'd recommend replacing the thin 2-sided thermal tape included with something actually useful.

title: Great Slider. I really enjoy it!
text:
[[VIDEOID:2d9553c9bf0c050d6032a6326fa51481]] The nylon case is sturdy and has plenty of padding. There's a small zip pouch inside the cover to hold your tools (a set of 5 allen wrenches included), a handle, and shoulder strap. Also included are interface cables for each major camera manufacturer, the control module, and battery.

Each of the four legs are individually adjustable, swiveling a full 360°, and locking into place with grooved teeth when the tightening wheel is secured. Each of the rubber-tipped feet can extend and extra inch or so via a screw, and secured with a locking washer.

The control module and stepper motor are one integrated unit, and is powered by a standard rechargeable Sony NP-f550/570 battery (charger included) that attaches to the unit. Mounting the control module is fairly easy - just slip the rubber belt onto the gear and pulleys, attach the unit to the tray via securing nut, then tension the belt via the tightening screws on the side frame sections. The motor is very quiet, but not entirely silent (refer to the uploaded video), so any noise will have to be edited out in post.

The slider tray glides very smoothly along the carbon fiber rods, with no play at all. There is a 3/8" mounting screw on the center spindle to mount your camera (via 3/8" to 1/2" adapter) or your favorite head. The bottom plate also has several 1/4" and 3/8" holes to mount the slider to a tripod. For more stability, each side piece also has 1/4" and 3/8" holes, so you can use 2 tripods. The motor appears to keep a steady speed, with no skipping or jerking. The "soft start" option adds easing to the start and end of each slide. Using the mobile app, you set the start(A) and end(B) points by wirelessly moving the tray to each position and accepting the values. The motor will not automatically stop when its reaches the end of the slider, so be careful manually setting the end points so you don't damage the drive belt or motor. The mobile app, used to control the unit, works consistently, but is not entirely intuitive. The help section is a bit difficult to understand.

The panning bar can be set so the camera mount will rotate to create panoramic, tracking or linear static paths. Two securing screws on each end of the panning bar keep it in place. Even secured, the panning bar can vibrate during operation, causing a metallic buzz (:06 of the video), caused by the slightest of gaps between the panning bar and the side frames. I fixed this by cutting a piece of backing paper that you get with adhesive labels, folding it in half so the slick side is on the outside, and sliding it between the panning bar and bottom of each side frame. There are guide marks on the side frame to help set the panning bar angle, but you have to eyeball the placement using the large red securing screws.

I really enjoy this slider. I got the 31" version and it feels very solid and sturdy. It does everything it promises very well, and I recommend it!

title: Good cards for general use, not high performance
text:
These cards are solid performers in UHS-1 mode, but not particularly stand-out. In UHS-2 mode their read speeds are very satisfying, but their write speeds don't really improve. I tested in multiple readers, including my SanDisk UHS-1 and UHS-2 readers (which never fail to produce the best speeds from most SD cards) and write speeds never improved in UHS-2 mode, relative to UHS-1. I use SD cards mostly in my cameras, but also in SBCs that I use for various projects, so SD card read/write speeds are very important to me, for device usability. If your camera has a UHS-1 card slot, these cards will do a good job, but there are cheaper cards that can do better. In my Canon T7i, I have tested more SD cards than you can shake ten sticks at, and the one the gets the most continuous frames before buffer-slow-down is actually this one: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07FCMKK5X/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_apa_i_QnYIFbWM8HSF3

I realize it's a Micro SD card, and those are usually not as fast as their full size counterparts, but that little guy nets me an extra frame before going into buffer lag, against any of the three runner-ups. I have plenty of other cards that can beat it for Read/Write Speeds benchmarks, but my camera likes it the best.

If your camera has a UHS-2 card slot, and you are on a budget, these Lexars will do an adequate job, and are a good value. But if you, like me, are trying to keep your camera shooting for as long as possible, before hitting the buffer wall, you're going to have to cough up the additional $$$ for the higher-end cards.

Hope this helps.

title: Disappointing
text:
I had high expectations for the Powerbeats Pro, and have ended up highly disappointed.

Fit
If there's one good thing I can say about the Powerbeats Pro, is that they don't fall off like AirPods, EarPods and most wireless and wired ear buds do. The Powerbeats Pro come with four pairs of ear tips in different sizes. Too bad none of them actually fit my ears. I wish Apple would just make their current AirPods with an ear hook to prevent them from falling off our ears. Anyway, the ear tips included with the Powerbeats resulted in either flat out pain or discomfort. After trying out all four pairs of ear tips, I ended up going back to the medium ones that come installed out of the box.

Sound
Sound quality in ear buds is directly related to their fit and how well that fit can create a seal. Needless to say that I cannot get good sound with the ear tips that don't cause me pain, and I can't get good sound quality for too long with the painful ear tips. The end result is ear buds that sound like the cheapest earphones you can buy, except that the Powerbeats are not cheap at all.

Battery life
If the Powerbeats Pro are supposed to have better battery life than the AirPods, I seriously don't want to imagine how awful the AirPods can be. The Powerbeats Pro can't even stand a whole day without needing to recharge, and that's regardless of whether you use them a lot throughout the day or barely at all. Yes, even in Standby these ear buds suck a lot of battery. Don't forget to take the oversized case with you, because you are definitely going to need it before you come back home..

Pairing
Don't be fooled by the super quick and simple iPhone pairing process the first time you use the ear buds. If their batteries reach near 0%, the ear buds lose their pairing and you have to re-pair them by long pressing the pairing button on the case.

I'm seriously debating whether or not to return these ear buds. They are not worth the money I paid for them. I'm already talking to people I know against buying them.

title: Recommended by this cable tech
text:
Speaking as a cable technician for one of the larger companies out there, this runs cooler (less heat produced, more efficient with electricity) and more stable (doesn't drop off nearly as easily due to low dBmV or low MER signal issues) than the rental Ubee, Technicolor, and Arris models my company "includes for free with your package". And yes, the AQM also works with the Cisco CMTS we use are our hubs currently, at least in my city that I work in. I bought one myself in December, it's been running a server without interruptions. Of course any line damage or RF leakage issues will still need repairs, but I've seen it more than once with weak signal on the coax (sometimes even negative dBmV levels from the tap), but yet this modem stays locked on without issues. That's impressive, and only one or two rental model modems we offer (which are exclusive to business class, not residential customers) gets close to that feat. Any one-star reviews you see here are likely going to be significant leakage issues inside or outside the home, almost never the modem itself with a well-made model like this MB8600.

If the manufacturer changes who is designing & making this (i.e.: no longer Motorola engineering), I will update this review. Until then, 5-stars and my non-official (can't speak on behalf of the company I work for of course) but personal experienced-based approval.

title: Very nice keyboard, but needs keyboard settings adjusted before use
text:
The Pros: Small footprint, quiet but solid keys, lightweight, number keys on Left side making it easier to position the keyboard closer to the mouse.

The Cons: the only con is that for some reason this keyboard uses the "sticky key" function by default (never had this happen on the last two USB keyboard I had on the same system). I didn't realize this was a possibility, and returned my first one as being defective. When my replacement started doing this after a week, I did some research. Apparently it is an "Accessibility Option" in Windows 10 where if you hold down the Control or Shift keys too long it turns on the Sticky key function...so the CTRL key never releases unless you do another specified 5 second hold. I had to go into the Keyboard settings and disable this annoyance. I took off a star as this really cost me some time working on Excel/Word and some Hospital software when selecting multiple items, and the CTRL key would stick and start selecting everything I touched and not release any selection.

The manufacturer should address this with an insert in the packaging addressing the user to disable this setting. It is not a normal occurrence for other keyboards, so there must be something with this particular keyboard that causes this to happen.

Now it works perfectly, but caused me weeks of issues.

#1)The keyboard uses only one AA battery. And the mouse uses only one AA battery. So to carry back-up batteries I only need another 2 AA. #2) The F1 through F12 keys are primary function instead of secondary...GREAT if you are using this for CAD modeling like I do.

#3) arrow keys that are not half the size/too small. I've used mini keyboards that have terrible small buttons...not worth the space savings if the end product is not functional

#4) individuals key travel is very similar to full size keyboards. I work on an HP desktop at a corporate job and it's very easy to switch back and forth between these keyboards.

#5) aesthetics...the keyboard doesn't look too crazy. Personally i could go without the red BUT it does get positive comments from other people.

#6) mouse works on all the surfaces I test mice on. table top, magazine and book covers and of course works flawlessly on a mouse pad. it's 1000dpi.

#7)auto sleep auto wake. no power switches.

#8) low voltage indicator. the LED labeled "lightning bolt" will flash when battery reaches 1.0v

#9) power consumption.
keyboard: 4ma working mode, after 3 seconds idle 0.2ma, after 8 minutes it goes to sleep and uses almost 0.
mouse:8.7mA working mode, after 1 minute idle 0.22mA, after 8 minutes almost 0.
If for some reason battery life is not fantastic i will come back and amend this point with more real experience. manual says batteries with 2580mAh will last 160 days when used for 2 hours per day.

Honestly. This thing is the jam. If you like the looks and you like my 9 points above you will not regret buying it.

title: Limited features. "Mesh" is not smart
text:
The good: Relatively simple setup. When placed close together, mesh works well.

The bad: The wireless range on the M3W (rectangular) wall units is noticeably weaker than the M4R towers. The units have to be relatively close together.

The Ugly: Missing about a hundred critical features. "Monthly reports" are absolutely useless (shows # of monthly users ONLY). Not intelligent about re-configuring the mesh if one AP reboots. Hogs wireless spectrum. All APs use the same wireless channel. The App is slow, spins constantly and unnecessarily, and it's pretty much useless after initial setup. QoS setting does nothing. New features are promised by support, but never show up. Good luck debugging problems whenever they crop up since not only is the App frustrating and slow to use, but it tells you nothing.

About our setup: we have 6 Decos working in a large, 7-bedroom house. I ended up hard-wiring 3 of the units since wireless mesh was inconsistent.

title: This is a great camera. Broad coverage area. Excellent night vision.
text:
UPDATE: I've decided to record to the SD card instead of the cloud. The main reason for my decision is our internet provider had an issue the other day and we were without internet for almost 8 hours (which meant our Wi-Fi was out too). Since I was recording to the SD card our security video was uninterrupted. If I would have been using the cloud we would have had an 8 hour gap of security video.

I'm very pleased with this camera. So much so that I've bought 3 of them now... I gave one as a gift... and I'll probably be purchasing 2 more for myself. I've also bought one of their indoor cameras.

The day and night vision are both excellent. I've included multiple pictures to show the different times of the day/night. We also have motion security lights... So when our lights activate it increases the night time visibility range of the camera. Without the security lights on, the night vision has enough range to illuminate a fair area... and the clarity is great.

The motion detection is good and you can set the level of detection you want in the app.

The recommended app is simple to use and gives you the option to save the video to an SD card or upload the motion detected videos to the cloud.

SD card vs Cloud: I'm still experimenting with which method is going to work best for my needs but so far I think I like recording to the SD card best. The differences between the two that I've noticed are: if you set it to cloud then the only video that is recorded is when motion has been detected (unless you purchase cloud storage). If you set it to SD card then video is recorded all the time, during the time frame you select. You can then look back at the full days video if needed. I've been using a 128gig SD card, recording 24 hours/day. With that it seems to store about 10 to 14 continuous days. The really nice feature is it has automatic loop recording... so you don't need to worry about the recording stopping when the SD card gets full.

The wi-fi works great and connects easily. I haven't had any problems with it losing signal. We've had a couple of power bumps and as long as our WiFi router boots back up properly the cameras reconnect without any issue.

Checking in on what the camera sees live is easy and works through the APP while you are connected to the same wi-fi or while you are away. This camera does not allow you to pan the view but it's capable of covering a very large area... with almost a fish eye view.

I have not experienced any negative issues. I recommend this camera to anyone who is looking for high quality security video in an affordable camera.

title: Good purchase. I’d give it 4.99 stars (why in the description)
text:
Read full description for explanations.
=>Pros:
-Powerful and fast (booting, game loadings, etc)
-Audio
-Screen

=>Cons:
-Edge of the laptop might bother your wrist skin while typing for too long
-Might get too hot for lap use (assuming it’s right on top of your pants)

A strong and powerful machine. So far I’ve played AC Odyssey/Origins/Syndicate, SW: Jedi Fallen Order, Destiny 2, Apex Legends, Fortnite, The Witcher 3, No Man’s Sky, Ryse Son of Rome and many other in the top graphic settings. Never had any issue. There’re many preset for fan and cpu/gpu power. The auto settings for the fan will make it really quiet (the outside metal might feel a bit hot, but totally standable... it means the heat is going out of the inside). Turbo mode will make it really cool, but with the price of the noise (you won’t notice with headphones. Audio is good. Booting time is awesome (even with my SSD full it won’t take even 10s to reach Windows 10 login screen). Screen is cristal clear (came with a 120% screen ratio configuration, changable in MSI config panel). Keyboard light brightness can be changed (4 levels, 0 to full), but color is always red. Touchpad is weird for me, but it isn’t bad. It’s really thing and light for it’s configurations. The power button is a bit hard to press, and in the first time I thought it was out of battery, but actually I didn’t press hard enough. Webcam will be automatically shutdown all time, unless you turn it on using Fn+keyboard button (which I don’t remember which one it is at the moment), I checked the Device Manager and it’s really like it’s not connected at all. The power input is at the left side, by the middle of the keyboard. Bluetooth works nicely with Xbox One Controller.
The reason I’d give 4.99: while typing, the edge next to you might slightly bother you skin (since I’m using it mostly for gaming with a controller and I use a wireless keyboard when I need to type, doesn’t affect me, and it gets a bit too hot for lap use sometimes while gaming.
Really good product, I’d totally recommend it.

Friendly reminder: it’s got around 500GB, so you might get around 8-10 of newest games installed, since they take around 40-60GB these days.

title: Avoid the Grandstream GWN7000
text:
Having deployed dozens and dozens of these GWN7000's, in a myriad of configurations and internet circuits, we can declare with expert opinion that these routers advertise far more capabilities than they actually deliver. The hardware itself is spectacular. The concepts behind what can be accomplished are spectacular. Unfortunately, it's all downhill from there.

Support is horrendous. You'll quickly find that you know way more than the folks answering (or criticizing) your questions. Grandstream simply does not value the networking support channel. Firmwares are few and very far between. Literally only 2 over the past 2 years, and those are primarily associated with the access point management aspect. In the ever changing router world where security is of the utmost, Grandstream is not "getting it".

These units on standard cable internet will never pass through the speeds expected. No matter the settings (QoS, bandwidth throttling, etc.), you seemingly will not ever be even close to the speeds you're paying for. Example: 100Mbs circuit from your cable provider will always, via ethernet wire directly into the GWN7000, be reported as 50-75% slower. Something in the unit is filtering high throughput traffic, and this is a major problem where there is high demand for video and audio. Many have been reporting the issue to Grandstream for years now, and it is something that is, unfortunately, ignored completely. Dedicated point to point circuits seem okay (ie: fiber), but cable circuits have, for us to date, never been accurate - circuits such as Comcast, Charter, Cox, etc. all over north America.

Site to site VPNs between GWN7000's will connect, but will not work, or pass traffic correctly. All protocols (OpenVPN, L2TP, PPTP, IPsec). As mentioned, don't even think you're going to get any level of expert support when you report the problems. You can even provide them direct access to the units, and they still won't or can't solve the problems.

The GWN wifi access points work great, but use them outside of the realm of these GWN7000 routers. Grandstream is NOT a router company. They don't get it. They don't take it seriously. They simply don't care. Avoid these and run your router out of something else. Recommend: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00LV8YZLK/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_U_bACMEbK5GVRPH

This review is not taken lightly. Lots of time and money have been spent on these GWN7000's. Several meetings with Grandstream representatives, along with countless emails and forum posts. Now we're faced with un-deploying them to keep our customers happy, and that in and of itself costing us thousands. Grandstream appears to be focused on the prettiness of the units and the underlying software, but the functionality does not match up. Lipstick on a pig. Avoid these.

text:

Their exact email, "Based on the information provided it seems that the fan assembly on the Intel® NUC is failing; therefore, the only option we have available to move forward will be to honor the unit’s warranty; however, based on the current availability for both the fan and the unit itself the only option we have available will be to either provide you with a refund for the whole unit or to provide you with the fan’s part #, a list of websites where you can look for it and of course the instructions to install it."

For reference this would be like purchasing a vehicle where the buyer provides the engine and tires. After 2 years the brake lights stop working and the dealer buys back the vehicle because they are too cheap to purchase the replacement parts and too ignorant to recognize their faults. Thanks Intel Management, nice work denigrating a once sterling reputation.

title: Killer Feature: Captures 240P component RGB signal.
text:
I'm using this as a capture device from a modded retro console (a Turbografx-16) which outputs 240p RGB over component cables. This is a very uncommon signal format for component, and VERY few capture devices will accept it for input. I consider this a 'killer feature' and was THE deciding factor when I purchased this unit. The specs don't advertise that it'll take 240p over component, but it does.

I have 2 gripes, neither of which are serious:
First, it stretches 4:3 input to 16:9 widescreen. If you're taking a 4:3 signal as input, you'll have to use some additional software to reformat it to 4:3 aspect ratio. I use OBS for streaming to twitch, which has a filter to do this, but the bundled software that comes with the capture device doesn't.

Second, the software this comes with is VERY limited. Kindof. It has a lot of "features" but its mostly stuff you won't use. You can't convert the signal to a different aspect ratio, you can't flip horizontally or convert to greyscale or anything like that. Maybe a new version of the software will add more, who knows.

This IS compatible with OBS, but was a little weird to setup the first time.

title: True to its price
text:
When it comes to video projectors, products range from $100 to several thousands. What we have today is the low end , but quite sharp, portable Pansonite Mini Projector.

First of all, this projector is designed to be small and portable. It’s lightweight and can easily fit in a backpack, measuring only 12 x 7.5 x 5 inches and weighting around 3 pounds.

Despite it’s small form factor, the Pansonite Mini Projector has a surprisingly bright and sharp picture quality. Equipped with a 5200 Lumens LED bulb, this projector can produce an up to 200 inches picture with a 3000:1 contrast ratio, supporting Full HD (1080p) video resolutions and all popular aspect ratios (4:3, 16:10, 16:9). Being able to project to a 200” size means that you can position the project quite far from the projection screen. In my tests I placed the projector about 12 feet away from the projection wall. I placed the projector on a small bookshelf, but you can also mount it on a tripod with the typical camera/tripod mount. No ceiling mount provided with this product.

Connectivity options are sufficient but not great. This is normal due to the small size of the projector. You get 1 HDMI port for high definition video. If you have older analog video devices, such as an older game console, you can use the AV port and the provided RCA-to-3.5mm adapter cable. Moreover, you get 2 USB ports for USB drives, and the projector supports pictures (JPEG, JPG, PNG and BMP) and most common audio/video files (such as AVI, MKV, MP4, MPG, MP3, WMA etc.). In the sound department, a common audio jack will allow you to connect your headphones or stereo speakers (you can connect RCA sound input with the provided RCA-to-3.5mm adapter cable). Last but not least, a VGA computer port is also available if that’s your thing.

Regarding configuration, the Pansonite Mini Projector can adjust the focus and keystone of the lens via rotational switches. Additionally, there are configuration and navigation buttons on the top of the projector. Alternatively, you can use the provided remote control for all basic functions of this product. What’s cool is that Pansonite put two IR sensors on the projector, both in the font and back, so that you can use the remote control from virtually any angle.

But what about its performance? Well, having the correct expectations and keeping in mind that this is a low end projector, I would say that the performance is surprisingly good. The picture quality in particular is quite better than expected. Bright picture, above average colors and very good sharpness even at 12 feet away. Not many projectors in this price range can perform that good. The sound is nothing to be impressed about, but delivers decently. You get options for Surround and True Surround, even though both those are emulated via the limited capabilities of the single 3.5mm audio output. Of course, you get extra options on the configuration menu to customize the individual parameters of both video and audio.

I also found the projector to be relatively quiet, even though you can definitely hear the cooling fan running non stop. Increasing the volume should solve that problem though.

Regarding the manufacturing quality, you shouldn’t expect much in this area. The plastic body feels cheap, and the buttons feel flimsy. But keeping in mind the price and segment of this projector, that is totally acceptable. The LED bulb has, according to Pansonite, 30,000 hours of life which would basically guarantee that you will never have to replace the bulb.

Overall this projector is addressed to people that are casual movie watchers or that are looking for their first projector to enter the arena of home movie theaters. It cannot be compared to the high end models by any means, but it performs better than expected. For what it is, I recommend the Pansonite Mini Projector.

For twin drivers these are amazing. I was expecting them to be a little bottom-heavy, or too crunchy. No. Bass is solid and articulate, highs have body not just sizzle. I am more than impressed, and I can be a grumpy old guy about "audio these days." I have put these buds through their paces with electronica, dance, R&B and jazz both old and new, classic rock, shred, examples from 50 years of pop. If the recording's right these will put a vocalist or Herbie Hancock's keys or Van Halen's guitar inside your head. Amke it easier to pick out the parts in a Dream Theater onslaught and rediscover that Beethoven's quartets were the work of a mad genius. All with the outside world a million miles away. Yeah, I'm using superlatives but for me, these are that good. Forget good for the money, just that good.

title: Decent earbuds with some caveats
text:
I purchased these earbuds since they checked many of the boxes for a pair of travel earbuds:
Sweat resistant for exercise
Active Noise Reduction/Cancellation
Strong battery life and rapid charging
Small case

Unfortunately while the specs were great the reality had too many compromises. The Active Noise Reduction is pretty weak compared to competitive earbuds. I give Amazon credit because they accurately advertised it as reduction instead cancellation but the lack of strong cancellation makes it less useful when traveling. Noise quality is decent but I am not an audiophile. I can tell that they are not as good as my Bose but they certainly sound more than good enough to me.

The earbuds only have two controls on the buds themselves which can be customized in the application but the typical person will want more than two (Play/Pause, Enable/Disable Noise Canceling, Assistant activation). The case is flat making it perfect for pockets and traveling. The use of Micro-USB to charge is also frustrating for a $100+ earbuds which means that someone who has converted to USB C will have to carry an extra cable.

Advanced customization requires the Echo Application which if you are all in on the Amazon Infrastructure shouldn't be a problem but if this is your only Amazon device it is a pain. It also keeps Bluetooth active even when they are in the case and shut-off which blocks my phone from pairing with other devices such as a car. They work without the application but customization is limited.

I wound up returning them after trying them for a day, they are decent earbuds but the issues with the Echo App keeping bluetooth active and Micro-USB port made them not worth the $100+.

title: The good and the bad...
text:
I used the PhotoStick 2.0 on my Windows 10 laptop. I suggest looking at the available options before you run your first scan. For example. you can customize things like what it scans, file types, etc. You can choose to remove duplicate photos and choose to keep or remove source folder names.
Note: The PhotoStick does not delete anything from your source drive.

Good:
(1) Great way to find all of your photos. It found over 13,000 photos, and once duplicates were removed, I was left with 8000+ photos. Really glad I didn't have to do that myself!!! (fyi... duplicates are found by looking at filenames, not images)
(2) Storage Capacity - My 8,000+ photos (and some videos) only took about 6% of the PhotoStick capacity. (18.7GB out of 117GB)
(3) The photos can be sorted by Name, Size, Location or Date.
(4) You can create folders on the stick to help organize the photos.
(5) You can Print, Save or Delete photos.

Bad:
(1) Organization: Folders created on the Stick cannot be renamed or sorted. They will be listed in order of creation. This makes organization limited and cumbersome. So I suggest you think about the folders you want and the create them in order (chronological, alphabetical, etc) before adding photos into the folders.. Also, you cannot create subfolders (folders within folders). This may not seem like a big deal, but when you're dealing with thousands of photos or videos, folders are critical to finding what you want.

NOTE: Photos sorted by date will be in order of last saved date. For example, if a photo was taken in 2017 and you moved or edited it in 2019, it will be listed with the 2019 photos.

A workaround to the folder limitations would be to use the PhotoStick "Save" option. You could use the stick to find/organize your photos, and then Save them to your hard drive or another thumb drive on your laptop. Note:
Photostick will save photos within a PhotoStick folder, but the photos will not be in a folder when you save them to another device. PhotoStick folders do not appear in File Explorer)

You can then use Windows File Explorer to create and organize your folders. If your goal was to put your current photos on a stick, you can then copy the folders/photos you organized in Explorer to a regular thumb drive.

I know this sounds like a lot of work, but PhotoStick really does most of the effort by finding all of the photos on your device. That's its greatest benefit in my opinion.

title: Excellent bargain with very powerful features.
text:
I was very pleased upon receiving, configuring and using the WansView wireless 1080P camera.
I liked the picture quality as well as the features available.
For a reasonable cost, there are certainly a lot of very powerful features included with this product.

Unboxing:
It arrived very fast even when I had selected "Standard Delivery".
It was packaged in a sturdy package and all parts were very securely packaged.
The box was wrapped in a waterproof plastic bag which is very good considering the weather we are having.

Everything that is needed was included in the package.
The package included the USB Power supply.
A very long Micro-USB cable to power the camera.
A CAT-5 Network cable.
A mounting bracked includin screws in case you want to wall mount the camera.
The instruction manual.

Installing the Android App and configuring the Camera:
I searched for "WansView" on the Android Play store and downloaded and installed the App.
The Instruction manual made the process of initial configuration of the Wifi Camera very easy.
Firstly you use your Smart Phone's Camera to scan the bar code on the bottom of the Wifi Camera.
Next you enter the password for your 2.4 GHz wifi connection.
Make sure that your phone is not using the 5 GHz Wifi connection during configuration of the Camera.
Now the phone will display a QRCode.
Point the Wifi Camera at the QR Code.
It took no time to read in the QR Code from the Wifi Camera.
Once the QR Code has been read, the WansView camera performs self configuration.
After the configuration was complete the Camera appeard to be "Online" in the Smart Phone App and you can then click on it and it shows the Camera View.

The App has many good features.
You can pan horizontally and vertically using buttons on the app.
You can flip the view horizontally and vertically also depending on how the camera is mounted.
You can set Alarms and events in the App. For example an alarm can be set to be triggered by Movement and another event can be triggered by sound.
This way you can configure the camera to only record video or images when there is movement or when there is a sound.
This can be very useful for saving space on the SD Card.

You can record Pictures captured by the camera as well as video.

title: The Onforu SK03 Is the Perfect Bike Companion
text: This is a wonderful product; very good quality, bright, clear sound, with plenty of undistorted volume.  It attaches snuggly and securely to my old 10-speed's handlebars and stays in place when encountering jarring bumps on the trail.  Also, there is no skipping of the audio when in micro SD card mode during rides.  The audio is crystal clear even at high volumes. The battery has plenty of life and the speaker is simple and easy to use.  I purchased the Onforu SK03 speaker to replace a name brand bluetooth speaker that I paid 3 times as much for 1 year ago.  What I like about the Onforu is the ability is play directly from a micro SD card.  This eliminates having to charge and manage a both a speaker and an MP3 player.  You can navigate forward or backward from song to song on the micro SD card by using the + and - volume buttons.  A longer press on the buttons increases or decreased the volume.  The Onforu has more volume than my old one so classical pieces with quiet passages will now be heard while riding.  The four buttons have double functions making the Onforu very convenient and versatile to use.  I would highly recommend reading through the supplied owners manual to understand how all the features work.  It can switch manually between SD, Bluetooth, and Aux using a short press on the power button to jog between them.  Or it will automatically connect to the correct mode upon power up, depending on what is hooked up at the time.  If an SD card is inserted it will power up to the SD mode.  If nothing is connected it defaults to Bluetooth mode.  If something is plugged into the Aux jack it powers up on that mode.  (The manual clearly states how this all works.)  This model has a 3.5mm aux jack and supplied cable so it can be used with older MP3 players that are not Bluetooth.  The speaker sounds as good as the old name brand speaker it replaced - only the Onforu has much more volume.  One of the things that impressed me as I was reading some of the negative feedback on this product was how willing the company was to correct problems.  Mine came without the set screw that tightens the bracket to the bike handlebars.  I contacted the supplier (Onforu) and they quickly resolved the issue by refunding some of the purchase price - more than enough to cover the cost of a new screw.  They responded to me within 24 hours and placed a refund through Amazon the very next day.  I'm very impressed.  I would have no reservations about purchasing another one of these amazing speakers.

title: Great ergonomics but it needs a rechargeable lithium battery
text:
Every person has their individual requirements for a pointing device. In my case, I have what is called "essential tremor", ie shaky hands. This gives me a lot of grief when I try to position a traditional mouse and then click it without moving. The trackball completely separates these two operations. Precise pointing with user-adjustable acceleration allows one to quickly traverse a 27" monitor to locate a point on the screen by rolling the huge trackball with any part of the hand. Once positioned you can take your hand off the ball and click the user-assigned buttons. Dragging can be assigned to one of the buttons so you do not need to keep holding down a button (with a shaky hand) while moving the pointer.

The ball just floats on sapphire bearings and its motion is measured with an optical device for smooth, jerk-free pointing. I have used a USB cable connected version of this mouse for many years and have been extremely satisfied with its operation. I decided to go with the wireless version to free up a USB port and minimize wire clutter.

The battery life is OK. I needed to replace the 2 AA batteries in two months without turning the unit off. I assume that it goes into a low-power mode either whenever it is not used over some time or the bluetooth connection is lost. But here is where I wish that Kensington would put some further effort in developing the wireless version. The TrackballWorks software does not provide any indication of the battery strength/level. I found out my batteries were dead in the middle of a project when the mouse just stopped working. I think they would have a better product with an internal rechargeable lithium battery that could be charged with a USB cable and modify the TrackballWorks software to provide a battery level and low-battery warning. If a low battery happens in the middle of a project, the mouse could be charged with the USB cable and the mouse could be temporarily used as a wired device so that work could continue.

title: Best Consumer Tablet - Photographer's Perspective.
text: This tablet is the best for consumers but not so great for creators. You will be able to read, watch and listen to any content you want without lag for a low price. I got this tablet for only $99 during Black Friday and is well worth the money. I use this table to read and watch content and I could not be happier. The battery lasts for 12hrs of continuous use but realistically this will last you a couple of days without a charge. The screen is very sharp and has great viewing angles. The touch screen is great and highly responsive. I don't use this tablet with speakers but from what I can tell they are nice and loud and will do a good job for anyone that is not an audiophile. My only complaint is the awkward button placement. The volume buttons for some reason are on top of the tablet as opposed to the sides which make it awkward to adjust the volume when using the tablet in landscape mode. This tablet will work best if all your content is purchased through amazon as it neatly has tabs for your music, books, newspapers and videos on your home screen so navigating to your content is a breeze. The google play store is not on the tablet by default so you will have to download it if you want to have access to a greater number of apps. The tablet has 2MP cameras which are great for video calls but horrendous for photography. There is a ton of noise and chromatic aberration when taking pictures even in broad daylight but you are not buying a $100 tablet to create with. However, if you are a photographer, this tablet can handle some light photo editing. You can get an SD card reader, import your photographs into the tablet and open them up with the lightroom app and make basic edits such as cropping, color adjustments and exposure adjustments without any issue. The materials that this tablet is made with seem to be of good quality. The screen is made from scratch-resistant glass and the back is made of some kind of metal alloy. Probably aluminum. For $99 you cannot beat the price for what this tablet can do.

title: Amazing Musical Sub
text:
If you are looking for an incredible musical sub, this is your sub. Very fast response and able to blend into my main speakers seamlessly with some tuning. I have two of these hooked up in mono for each main speaker and tuned to match.

Sorry to say this, but if you are looking for a Home Theater sub or if your musical tastes are more to the boomy music (Rap, Electronica) this is not your sub. It is very tight crisp and clean but does not give you that boom. This may sound odd but these subs are just too tight for that level of boom, you need a less precise larger sub to really fill that role.

Lastly, make sure you purchase this through Amazon. REL support is absolutely terrible, they do not answer the phone and it takes days to hear from them by email. I have REL a wireless sub transmitter that needs to be returned and I just gave up and wrote it off a lesson. If I had purchased through Amazon I would have just returned them. That's my biggest caution with REL, as a purchaser of two of these subs I am absolutely concerned about anything going wrong. For what they charge they should be answering the phone on the first ring. Contrast that with SVS where they answer the phone and immediatly address any concerns.

The other con is the High-Level connection is through a Neutrik connector. You get a 12m cable with the sub but if you need a shorter one bear in mind you are cutting a $500 cable if you buy it from REL. You can find one aftermarket for around $100-$150.

My recommedation, if you are looking for a sub to fill out a main speaker with Rock, Classical, Jazz or any non-boomy music get the REL. But, make sure you get it from Amazon so you can return it, you might even consider the extra warranty to guard agains REL. If you are looking for a great home theater sub or dont need quite so tight of a response look to SVS. They are a great value for the money and sound incredible for movies and boomy music.

title: Works well for me
text:
This review is for the 10GTek X550-T2 (PCIe 3.0) card, not the X540-T2 (PCIe 2.1), though I suspect that the same performance would be seen with the X540-T2.

This card works great for me!

I bought 3 of these NICs and a Netgear 10gbps switch (XS708T) as I was tired of my 4x1gbps (Intel Pro 1000 PT NICs) Windows 10 auto aggregated links dropping to 1gbps due to MS dropping support for the automatic aggregation that they accidentally added into Win10 a few years ago. MS pulled this very nice (accidental) support and I was back to 1gbps without doing full switch configured LACP aggregation. I got really tired of backing up 45TB on a 1gbps connection. So I threw $ at the problem and hope to be good until 40gbps, someday.

These NICs works well for me via single port (9.9gbps) or dual port with aggregation (> 10gbps).
I am running this on Windows 10 Pro and Workstation with the standard (Windows Update) drivers that were automatically installed.

Testing
I have tested with iPerf3 and even with single, a few or many threads, it is very hard to saturate the connection and show > 5gbps. So for me, iPerf3 just won't do.
I now test by performing long running SSD to SSD tests through a Netgear 10gbps router which shows me hitting 10gbps (and greater with dual ports and aggregation).

Real World Feel for my daily workflow
I have also tested my heavy Visual Studio work flow with my solutions and projects running on SSD on an older 7700k system and the connection seems very snappy, barely noticeable from my main local storage which is 3x Win10 stripped NVMe (Samsun 970 Evo Plus) 1TB drives, where I get 7GB/s sequential block performance and snappy small random block performance. I suspect that if I use this NIC on a mid-high-end NAS with 10gbit NIC that I will be satisfied with the perf of my workload (lots of small files). I will update this review if I am able to test that in the future.

Windows 10 auto link aggregation (just plug multiple single-machine Cat5/6 cables to your switch)
As of recently (this NIC or Intel Pro 1000 PT) I _DO_NOT_ see automatic aggregation with Windows 10 Pro, but I _DO_ see automatic Win 10 aggregation (this NIC or Intel Pro 1000 PT) after upgrading my Windows 10 Pro servers to Windows 10 Workstation (I don't use Windows Server). I see spill-over behavior where when the one port is saturated (10gbps) then the 2nd port starts taking on any addition load (I have only gone to about 13gbps) . The only reason I upgraded to "Workstation" is that I have plenty of OS keys from MSDN, so why not try it - it worked. Not sure if you would get the same same result - so don't assume.

I will keep using these NICs unless I see a reason to not to (which I would add to this review).

I attached a photo with a level so you can quantify what crooked means to me. The measurement is the same when I take the monitor off the monitor riser, so its not an issue of the riser sagging. It's not a huge issue, but it is the thing that kept me from a 5-star review.

If you are looking for a height adjustable 27'' monitor this is a nice, solid choice. I'll update this review if I have any performance reviews over time.

It took me 7 mins of sending de-auth packets before I got an alert. The only issue with that is, it doesnt take but maybe 5 seconds to capture a WPA-2 hand shake or PMKID and once captured you can bruteforce, dictionary attack, or pay to have it cracked on a website. Without getting into to much network jargon and details. If this had the ability to adjust the threshold as you see fit for your environment, it would be beneficial to be able to get an alert as soon as you start to receive those de-auth packets, so you can take the necessary action to protect your network by changing the password to your network and the admin password on the router if necessary.  Attackers can do some serious damage if they get your network password. They can use up all your bandwidth, sell your credentials on the darkweb, use your computer as a zombie, and much more. As homes become more advanced as smart homes. The need to protect your network is becoming more vital than it was in the past.

title: Works perfectly!  Consider this to unburden your wifi and improve your streaming...
text:
This adapter works perfectly and is extremely easy to install. It delivers smooth stable streaming to my busiest HDTV and taken a significant load off of my wifi - which has completely stabilized everything that remains on the wifi.

A bit of context - i recently "cut the cable" and went to wifi-only. I have 100mb internet service and a centrally located wifi unit in my home that for years has easily supported roughly 10 active devices at any given time. That may sound like a lot, but you take a couple smart phones, a couple laptops, smart thermostats, a couple Echo devices, and throw in a few smart plugs, e-readers, and so forth and you can get past 10 pretty fast. When i finally "cut the cable" i added two streaming TVs to that load, each TV at opposite ends of the house where the wifi signal was good but not great. Each TV worked fine individually, but if my wife and i were using both tv's at the same time, the picture quality would degrade and within minutes the wifi would collapse and kick everything off the network.

Fortunately, my home also has ethernet wiring with connections near the wifi as well as near our most heavily used tv. I was able to use the existing wiring and the Amazon Ethernet Adapter to connect the main tv directly to the LAN port on the router/modem and therefore remove all of that traffic from the wifi. The results have been a clear stable picture on the main tv, with no issues on any of the other devices (including the other TV) that continue to use the wifi - no matter how many are in use at the same time.

There are alot of questions/concerns raised here and in other forums as to whether this (and other) ethernet adapters are faster than wifi and you will find alot of videos showing comparative tests. My view is they are missing the point - an HDTV requires at most a 10-15mb of speed to support high quality streaming on one device and this ethernet adapter EASILY supports much more than that via your wired connection to your router/modem (unless your router is in a different zip code). The REAL benefit is that the connection is far more stable - particularly if you have a bit of distance between your wifi unit and your streaming device as i did, and if said wifi unit is pretty busy talking to other devices as mine was. Using the ethernet adapter to remove the traffic of one busy tv from my wifi has solved all of the issues - and for alot less money than adding additional gizmos to spread more wifi all over my house.

title: Search "nvidia rtx 3090 failure rate" - EVGA RTX cards have issues
text:
Update: March 11 2021 This was a Four Star review - No longer

I can not believe this card just died tonight. It died as I entered a room playing Bioshock Remastered on Steam. I had just launched the game so there wasn't even any crazy fight going on. The cards fans spun up and the signal to the monitor died. I put my hand over the case and the card was venting an unreal amount of heat. A complete brick.

I've never had issues with EVGA cards before but after doing a search for 3090 failure rates, it looks like EVGA has some serious issues.

Given the price we are paying because of GPU stock shortages, steer clear of any company that is having problems with their RTX cards. I understand that EVGA has awesome Customer Service and I really hope so, because this is a major setback.

________________________________________

For starters, the EVGA RTX 3090 FTW3 out of the box performance is very impressive. I'm getting consistent frame rates even in busy scenes. Not one notable hiccup on frame drops in four days I've played using it.
I upgraded from my RTX 2080 Super. The frame rates notably jumped with higher avg frame rates. This translates to smoother game play at max settings. Playing Borderlands 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, the increase was within 15 - 20+ @ 1440. I'll also note this card has a physical onboard Overclock switch that is set Normal. I have not tested this.

Its BIG and Heavy
There's no getting around this. Length and Width are considerable and I would really consider the case one plans on putting this into. ie: Your case should be running a cool ambient temperature and offer plenty of space for air flow. It's three lanes wide and those fans need little to no obstructions. See attached pics for reference comparisons to a RTX 2080 Super. Medium sized cases with plenty of components inside may present ambiet cooling challenges.

RTX: Real Time Ray Tracing and DLSS
Yes, RTX can have some really impressive effect when used but its still very expensive when enabled. It saps an avg 20 FPS in Cyberpunk 2077 and to be quite honest, the game already has some impressive visuals, for me, those extra frames are better used for actual fights. DLSS 2.0 is the real technology here worth writing about. It really does create some impressive scaling that yields impressive performance gains.

Power Hungry
I am running a two year old EVGA 1000 Watt PSU running an OC'd CPU, 32GB sys RAM, two HD's and one SSD and an optical drive. This card has three 8 Pin power connectors so it is power hungry. It is not advisable to use a power split cable (a cable with two 8 pin plugs).
Now, I have checked EVGA's official forums and the mods have verified that newer PSU's rated at 800 Watts or above are good to use two 8 Pin power cables instead of three. Having read reviews were people are encounter high temps, excessive fans, and frame rate issues, I went with three separate cables running into my PSU. I haven't encountered any problems.
I am running this on a Corsair water cooled system in a big case which runs very quietly and I've yet to hear the fans on the 3090 run up while playing any titles.
If you are running a much older PSU and/or its rated below 800 Watts, you might really consider upgrading it.

What Frame Rates can you expect?
Unless you are running top tier Intel or AMD CPU's your frames won't match those posted on Tech Review sites. My frame rate increases are relative to my existing hardware, particularly the CPU. It shows in the fact that I am using a mid range CPU from two years ago. An OC'd Intel i7-7700K. So I will not be hitting those numbers until I complete my system built around AMD's Ryzen 9 5900X.

Final Word
Unless you're a content creator, this card is a bit of overkill in the cost to performance gains. I use editing applications that benefit from architecture in the RTX 3090.
Due to its sheer size and power requirements, I really can't see this going into a mid sized cases especially if overclocking is a goal. Cooling could be a problem.
A card like this really is set back if its being paired with mid range components. I can see that with my build right now which is why im building a new rig around it.
For that reason, I would be hard pressed to recommend the 3090 just for gaming when the RTX 3080 is likely the best bet in cost and power usage. The net gains here are minimal in comparison.

title: Never going to disappoint, might not wow you, but a solid device for sure!
text:
What can I say. It’s a Garmin. It’s going to work. I would have bought one model down, but there was a $200 discount at the time of purchase direct from Garmin and also via Amazon, which made this the same exact price as the lessor model - so no brainer there.

I’ve been a long time Garmin customer. Recently I use CarPlay with my car, but for over a decade previously I also had Garmin car navigation devices, from StreetPilot, to Nuvi, etc. They’re rock solid.

This device has some trade offs. The touch screen isn’t the most responsive. The screen doesn’t scream “high brightness, great contrast”, but it’s visible in all but the most direct glare of sunlight, and has an incredible battery life - which is important for those long rides!

Functionality wise, it works well with other devices (pairing to speed, cadence, heart sensors, plus a front and rear Bontrager smart lighting system). The directions work well, as I tend to wander, and then when I feel my ‘gas tank’ getting low just tell it to navigate me home. I probably don’t flex it’s muscle with all of the various options, but just to get around, and to see how your heart, speed, distance, etc are going it’s fantastic.

Just not the best screen or touch sensors, which I suspect was a deliberate trade off to get something with a decent price and long battery life.

Kudos to Garmin for including about a billion mounting accessories. Two disc based mounts, plenty of those silicon bands in multiple sizes, plus a out front mount are all included. If you can’t mount this to your bike, you probably aren’t doing it right.

The monitor OSD suggests audio signal can be routed to the device over display port and I have the included display port cable run directly to my Asus ROG Strix 2080TI and the included USB3.0 cable run directly to one of my Asus ROG Maximus XI Hero motherboard's USB3.0 ports. The monitor shows up as an available audio playback device, but I cannot hear any sound when I switch to it. For whatever strange reason, I can hear test signals from Windows 10 so I am starting to wonder if the OS is the issue but I am still investigating. Docking one star for tech support here because I have not been able to find any documentation on how to make this work anywhere in the support section of ASUS's website for this product. The good news is that I also have a USB audio interface run to studio monitors so this feature is not super critical for me.

2. RGB Lighting Issues: I have had issues getting the RGB lighting on this monitor to work correctly. I have a personal PC connected to the device as described in issue #1. The only lighting on this monitor that I see working is the solid red LED on the top of the unit. The large RGB ROG Logo on the back of the unit and the small RGB ROG logo under the display stands do not light whether or not I've enabled the Aura Sync functionality in the monitor OSD. I also am not able to get Aura Sync to find this device when the functional is enabled on the monitor. The existing support documentation for the RGB lighting on ASUS monitors is pretty basic and not very helpful so I am docking a star for tech support. title: COMPLETE JUNK! The connectors are so sensitive it disconnects & reconnects constantly. Avoid!
text:
Complete junk. Just buy the Sabrent one and you'll be better off.

Like another review mentioned, the connectors on this cable are complete garbage. Even the slightest bit of movement on either end—even due to thermal expansion from the heat of a thumb drive, or just a fan on in the room—is enough to cause your device to disconnect and reconnect constantly.

And it's not a power issue, as the thumb drives draw less than 1/30 of the rated 900mA power of a USB 3.0 port, at 28mA each, under load.

The cable part itself is high quality and the molded ends of the cable are nice, but the connectors make it essentially useless. Nothing I enjoy more than corrupted data transfers due to poor connector design on an extension cable.

Avoid this and just buy the brand name ones. I replaced with a Sabrent and it's perfect.

Usually Amazon Basics are pretty good, but sometimes they need a couple revisions to get them right. This definitely feels like version 1.0 and desperately needs a version 2.0, because this version is junk.

text:
Ordered this as a replacement for an older Sony unit. The old Sony remote looks exactly like the new one and works fine with the new player - that was a nice bonus [two remotes - now I can lose one without crying LOL].

Two critiques: With the older player, I could press play or eject and the machine would turn itself on and perform the function. This player takes longer to wake up and requires you to use the power button, wait for it to wake up and then you can press play or eject - that's a little annoying. The second nit-picky comment - the front of this player is equipped with hard to push buttons across the top of a beveled front section of the player. Yep - it's pretty, but when you push the button hard enough to make it actually depress, the player has a tendency to kick up in the back and kiss the shelf in the front - not the best product design on the planet. Would've been better if the buttons had been on the front of the unit instead of on the top for that reason. I like the overall look - just button placement could've been a little more thought out.

These two things are not deal breakers, just a little annoying, and overall, this is a great player. I'm very happy.

title: Sturdy microphone that sounds decent but has a few issues
text:
The microphone itself is of decent quality; it seems that the main body is made of a plastic variant so it feels super light and slightly hollow. Definitely not the premium feel, but it feels like it could take a drop or two easily too. The stand is made of a nice metal with a heft to it, so I'm confident that this won't be tipping over on my desk anytime soon. However, the ball joint on the stand is pretty stiff and makes a crackling sound, almost as if there's a spring inside (there might be?). Probably not going to adjust it much to avoid the sound.

It comes with a detachable right angle micro-USB cable which was a nice touch, but it's placed on the bottom left of the microphone which makes it stick out a bit. A better placement in my opinion would have been in the back center, where it would have been blocked by the stand. Doesn't affect function in any way, but it would have been nice to have.

The quality of the microphone seems pretty average. I quickly plugged it into my laptop and tested it on a voice call; the other person said it sounded clear and didn't have much distortion. However, they did hear a bit of a whine in the background but even at max volume it was barely audible. Not sure if that was a manufacturing defect or something in the room, but keep that in mind.

The last thing I wanted to add is that I don't think there's a way to turn off the green/red led strip running around the body of the microphone. Green is for unmuted, red is for muted. The mute button is also mushy and doesn't have much of a tactile feel to it, but it's not the biggest deal.

Because of the interference and the mushy button with the LED light that can't be turned off, I've decided to go with 4/5 stars. It's more than usable, but these were just some small issues that didn't sit well with me.

title: Works out of the box w/ hassio 0.96 using ZHA & Z-Wave integrations. :)
text:
I'm using this on a rpi with the current release hassio (zwave and zigbee integrations). Worked right out of the box with no extra configs. This should be the case for others getting started with hassio.

If you have other usb devices in use take note... when I added a 3rd usb-serial device to my pi (arduino nano), I had to specify the usb paths "by-id" in my configuration.yaml to get all 3 usb devices working properly after a reboot (ie using /ttyUSB0, etc may fail after reboot). You have to ssh in to get the by-id paths for your hassio install. This is a minor inconvenience that has nothing to do with the husbzb-1 (it's due to root user limitations in hassio). With the correct usb ports defined in configuration.yaml, all 3 usb devices have worked perfectly for a while now.

title: Best Monitor I Have Ever Used
text: Of course, this picture just doesn't do it justice; but I had to post it.  I have owned many monitors since the mid-1980s, as well as using countless monitors at work. Calibrated at the factory by HP (I use the Neutral Color setting - Looks very natural), plenty of connectors, including the newer USB-C, and it'll be my monitor for many years to come.  The 27" screen is perfect for my needs, and many times I will work with 2 or even 3 windows open, which makes for an awesome working experience.  Everyone seems to get hyped up about 4K screens, which cost a lot more, and I guess they have a place, in some circumstances; but 1440p is plenty for most folks' needs.  Keep in mind that the higher the screen resolution, the smaller everything gets on a desktop - I have no issues with 27" & 1440p, but I know some folks who actually liked the "standard" 1080p better; it was more of a size thing for fonts, icons & such than any type of screen quality.

title: For under $20 it's pretty good
text:
I came into browsing these headphones knowing I should probably buy one at least $35 or so because that seems to be the lower limit of quality. I noticed there were a few that looked like clones of each other and decided to give this one a shot at $16 because it was more of an 'oh what the hell' purchase. I kinda knew it before buying it, but the part that covers the ears isn't very comfortable and it seems geared more toward the small ears of children. If this thing had the entire over the ear coverage like more expensive ones it would be a damn good deal but it presses against the ears flat instead of resting them inside a padded circumference. This from what I can tell allows them to use cheaper drivers and amps because instead of cranking higher clear decibels they can just ram the little speakers right up as close to your ears as possible instead of allowing them a small bit of breathing room.

I stretched the flexible metal out a little so it felt more comfortable around my big head. Now they feel pretty good, but still not as perfect a speaker-to-ear match as some of the competition. The sound quality is 'decent' with not too much noticeable distortion and the bass is about average. Comparing these to a pair of Cowin headphones my roommate owns I can say the $30 or so price difference gets you better cancellation, a little more comfort, and noticeably better sound quality.

If you're looking for a great headphone experience you probably need to spend about $40 bucks on a better model. If you just need something that works well, don't care too much about super high quality reproduction, and has bluetooth/aux/recharge ability then this is a damn good deal.

title: Wow!  What a great Black Friday gift to myself!
text:
I'm still in the 'infatuation' stage, but that makes it a perfect time to write a positive review. Backstory: I've got an Oculus Rift headset, and love the immersion of 3D and 360 images. I was actually shopping for a dash-cam when I came across a positive comment about the Mi Sphere. Usually $200 or even $200, the Black Friday price was below $100 and I pressed "Buy" (but have to admit it was with crossed fingers. Was there ANY chance that a spherical camera at this price would do .... anything???) It has exceeded every expectation of ease of use and performing as advertised and hoped. It arrived in a heavy-duty box; everything inside was undamaged; I had it charged in an hour and connected to my android phone wi-fi shortly after. Took photos and posted one on Facebook within an hour. Amazing! My thoughts at this point: If you're looking for a consumer-grade spherical camera, then for the money, this is a no-brainer. Yes, I'm still going to explore the higher-end features (exporting in RAW and tweaking the images; long time exposures; etc) but even if they don't do well, I still have a great camera for spherical images of upcoming trips to the Rockies and Andes. (Reminder: spherical VR images can't appear very crisp or sharp until at least 4K or higher; image data has to be shared over a HUGE area - much more than an ordinary photo - so the apparent 'resolution' of the pictures is low-to-average. But, this isn't the camera's fault; it's just the math of filling the inside of a complete sphere with just 23m pixels. Our eyes see much better than that.) So, don't get grumpy when any given part of your image isn't as sharp as your phone could have done. That isn't the magic of the Mi Sphere. Rather, it takes a picture of everything, and with very little fuss or bother it drops that image to your android phone (already stitched and ready for export to Facebook, or Oculus, or ... BTW, if you're new to this as I am, the 'already stitched' feature is HUGE. You don't have to buy software to convert your photo from double-fisheye to equirectangular projection. It comes out of the camera ready to view.)

OK, hope I have conveyed wide-eyed enthusiasm for this unexpectedly delightful little 360 spherical camera! Five stars!
