title: TL;DR: Not worth it, get something better.
text:
I'm a software engineer who writes embedded software for very very expensive and sensitive specialized hardware, so I know a thing or two about how these things work.

I ordered this to be a second power supply for my new Eluktronics MECH-15 G2Rx laptop (which is a great buy) and before I even plugged it into my machine, I gave the unit a quick look over and read the labeling on it. The title says 19.5v/9.23A, but the unit I got (which matches the picture) says 19v/9.5A. I will grant that these numbers are really close, and for most cases nobody will ever know, except that the regulator inside the laptop will have to get hotter to do its job. This additional heat will shorten its lifespan. So, for the otherwise uninformed user, you will get a blue light in the charger, and your laptop will still boot/charge and everything will look just fine, but you will end up needing a new laptop sooner than you would have otherwise needed one.

That alone didn't deter me, as I'll probably upgrade my machine before blowing out the internal regulator, so I pulled out the ole multimeter to see what voltage the charger that came with my laptop was putting out, and it was putting out a nice steady even 19.96V. Again, within a volt is just fine, but it was steady at 19.96V, which means the factory charger for my laptop had some really nice smoothing capacitors on the output, so my machine is likely getting really really clean power. Then I looked at this charger, and watched as the voltage bounced around between 19.2ish to 20.1ish Volts. This jumping around at no load means that under heavier load (like powering a laptop) it is going to jump around even more (as the capacitors discharge deeper). This was the deciding point where I arrived at the conclusion that the power supply was going to have to go back.

After spending over a thousand dollars on a laptop, it isn't worth it to cheap out on a second charger that will likely considerably shorten the life of my computer.

title: Network Speed Increased Dramatically
text:
Let me first start off by saying this: when school's started transitioning to online classes because of covid-19, I noticed a huge decrease in speeds in my network. With the increase in demand, it only made sense that the ISP will limit the speeds of their customers until they could ramp up server production. My bill reflected this dramatic change from 170 mbps to a 26 mbps.

But once I installed this, I noticed a huge increase in network speeds. There were no dead spots in my house anymore. Here are the steps to installing this product:

1) Simply turn off the 2.4/5 ghz Wi-Fi from your modem
2) Download the app provided in the instruction manual
3) Connect one TP-Link router to your modem through an Ethernet cord (I recommend getting a CAT 8)
4) Connect each router by scanning the QR code in each of them, and using the SAME name (SSID) on ALL.

Cheers!

text:
I previously owned Skull Candy Ink'd headphones, but the microphone broke. I've owned expensive Sennheiser open backed headphones that I love, so I thought I'd give these a try. First off, the construct is high quality. All of the tangible parts feel great and you know they took great care in designed them. Like other Sennheiser products, the treble and base are well balanced, The sound comes in softer than cheaper earbuds and the best way to describe cheap earbuds is they BLURT music instead of it being carefully constructed. These are great for recreational use: running, hiking, working out or routine housework. I saw a couple of reviews talk about noise cancellation. you DO NOT get noise cancellation with these. They give you plenty of tips to fit your ear as best as possible. If you have the right fit, its like wearing foam ear plugs and most of the ambient noise is blocked. Overall for the price, it is a really great product, and if you're like me, you'll use them for years.

title: Just works on my Dell T5500 w/PCI-e USB 3.1 but throttles speeds 15% compared to USB-C direct
text:
I'm using USB-3.1 on my Dell T5500 via an AbleConn USB3.1 adapter. It works great if you're looking for external storage faster than the built-in SATA2 like I am.

Even so, 1x USB-A and 1x USB-C is just not enough. In my hunt for USB-C hub in late 2019, I discovered they don't exist yet. Sure, multiport adapters with NIC, HDMI, DP, SD/MMC are out there, but try finding one with more than a single USB-C port on it.

The consensus seems to be they aren't available because the controller chips aren't out yet.

Forget all those pricey offbrand imports, AmazonBasics to the rescue. It just works.

The downside is the 15% speed limit through the hub compared to direct connection to the adapter card. I get the same speed limit when connecting directly to the card's USB-A port, so it seems AmazonBasics is not to blame.

I'll revise this review later, but for the moment I'll let you analyze the results for yourself. I ran CrystalDiskMark and UserBenchmark with my Samsung T5. In all cases, direct connection to the USB-C port recorded the fastest sequential speeds. Random reads and writes were closer, but in most cases, direct connection over USB-C was the winner.

If you need more USB 3.1 ports, AmazonBasics will get you there, but I'm still trying to find out why it's slower over USB-A than direct via USB-C.

This is not the kind of flare that can be cleaned up in post. I realize this may not matter to many, but if you need clean source images for more technical work, steer clear!

Even in normal shoot situations I don’t see why this lens is so wildly overrated. Contrast, color and sharpness are fine, but nothing to rave about. Yes, it is probably better than some lenses at this price point, but don’t let the Rokinon-sponsored photo vloggers (they seemed to have sent everyone with a YouTube channel a test sample) convince you that this is a replacement for a high quality lens!

title: Buy it, but be cautious!
text:
Ordered Ring Alarm System Enhanced kit on Sept 22nd to replace my ADT system to minimize and avoid high monthly costs. Whole Kit Delivered Sept 24th. Installed Sept 27th.

Installation was easy though it took me little bit longer since i removed all the old ADT sensors/System and installed ring system. Also, i screwed in my Sensors to be more secure instead of just using 3M tape.
From get go, Base station never had complete blue circle in front as expected with disarmed mode. Left it alone for 24 hours. Called Tech Support 24 hrs later, sent picture to them. Guy asked my to power boot the system. So took down AC power, had to remove and replace battery, guess what the whole LED circle went bad, meaning no light at all. Tech support told me to be in touch with RAS team. Called them, had to tell story to 1st person again and then got to Logan with RAS Team. Also, told them that base station never made any alarm or sound when doors open and no alarm when armed mode.

After spending 1.5 hours through Web chat/phone call; finally RAS team person mentioned that it is a bad piece and they will send a new one. They will be sending the base kit (Which sells for USD 199) though i only need base station, so i can keep rest of pieces as my compensation for all the hassle. Plus, they will give me 3 months of extended protection plus plan.

So, yes it is good, but disappointing part is, this is brand new system (I hope), have already spent 1.5 hrs dealing with customer support. On top of that, when new base station arrives, i will be installing new base station. And on top of that i will have to re-sync each and everyone of 7 contact sensors, 1 keypad, 1 range extender, Water alarm, 2 motion detectors, 1 panic alarm and 1 CO alarm. So i am probably looking at another 1-2 hrs of doing this. On top of that, i am expected to pack and mail back/deliver the faulty base station to UPS/USPS/Fedex store (Since otherwise, i may get charged for device), so probably another time spent there. Also, not even sure if i will get brand new replacement or refurbished though i paid for brand new item.

Now this comes on top of the issue i already had with Ring Doorbell Pro which went bad earlier this week and had to spend >1 hr with tech support and eventually, had to get a new one in mail, replace it with old, pack and mail it also.

Overall, i like ring systems, I do have Ring Doorbell pro (Which replaced 3 years old Original Ring doorbell), Ring Floodlight Cam, Ring Alarm system and also ordered Ring Spotlight Cam recently.

But these 2 recent experiences have been off putting and very disappointing.

title: One of the best 60W-level PD Charger
text:
Conclusion upfront: It's perfect in everything but for ultimate portability.

ZMi is a very famous brand in China when it comes to wall adapters. This 65w product is THE BESTSELLER on many Chinese online shopping websites, as one of my friends from China told me so.

Back to the adapter itself, it's nice that for $20 it comes with a C-C cable in the box, with up to 100W capability. It's not that small, as mentioned in the title, but it's by NO means big. Without GaN, this might be close to the minimum in terms of volume. It's just not that awesome compared to adapters like the Ravpower 61w GaN one.
Yes it feels heavier than my Apple 12w iPad adapter coming with my iPad, but not that much, far from making it annoying to carrying around.

But that's where the Cons end. Talking about charging itself, no doubt about it: compatible with iPhone, Galaxy Phones, my iPad Pro, and my Thinkpad X1 Carbon. So that's PHONE(18w/15w), TABLET(about 30w), LAPTOP( max at 65w, depending on your model). It should be able to enable 25w on Samsung Note 10+ and the new S20 series, but 45w is NOT very likely, as that would require a 10V/4A PPS PD protocol, which is not covered by most under-70 adapters.

The power is absolutely abundant, while it does NOT heat! I know for now it's very subjective to say so, as the weather is very YMMV, but talking about my own situation, at Seattle around the wintertime, inner T like 10C(50F), charging my laptop merely warmed it up! Nowhere close to being hot. This is very incredible, as I also have experience with the Ravpower 61W 1C(GaN)/1C1A(non-GaN) and the Baseus 65w 2C1A(GaN) adapters, all of which heat more obviously fueling my laptop ( the 2 GaN ones much more significantly).

My Lenovo requires a 65w input, as is the rated input from the OEM charger, so all chargers would work at maximum. The heat is so intense with the 2 GaN that it actually caused me to fear about further use. This one, while not so compact, allows enough space to distribute the heat so well that you can literally feel it.

If more to suggest about it, the 1C config is kinda limited and you would probably need more charger if you got a lot on the go. Also, since some part of the exterior is well polished like a piano's surface, it may show signs of wear and/or scratches easily. But these are just some minor issues that shouldn't discourage you from going for it.

To finalize, this is the 99% perfect 1C 60w-level PD adapter, if you feel the specs fit you, then just buy it.

title: Works good, 18650 could give you some issues if not paying attention.
text:
I primarily will use this for charging NiMH batteries but I have several 18650 in flashlights and some old ones I removed from laptop batteries. The pros are this will automatically select the type of battery and start charging it. It determines the aH to charge at but you can manually set it to charge one or all cells at the same rate by pressing the mode button. You can't see all of the 8 slots on the display at the same time. Instead it will display Each slot one at a time and you have to push the "slot" button to see each one. The display shows the ah and the voltage in the same place by waiting a second for the display to change. I'll post a couple pics of the display.

Other than needing to hold the mode button down to select ah charge rates and the slot display only shows one at a time its been good at NiMH. It does not charge D cells either. Li-ion I would be careful with.

The main con I have seen to this is other than no test or discharge function, if you have some 18650 that are super low voltage the charger will recognize them as NiMH and start trying to charge them. I simply do not like that it does this. I had to "jump start" them with a different charger (or use another fully charged 18650) to give them some voltage so that this "smart" charger will correctly charge them as Li-ion cells. I do not leave any 18650 cells on a charger over night or when I'm not home.

Overall its a good 8 bay charger for under $50, would I buy the same model again, probably not. But it has been working good for charging my AA and AAA cells which is why I chose this 8 cell charger over some of the more expensive or 4 bay chargers.

text:
I was pleasantly surprised when I first used this. The noise isolation is much better than I thought it would be given how small device is. It is like wearing earplugs but headphones.

I wear these around the office. What often happens is there our conversations in the joining cubicles that are a little bit too loud. If I put these on what's a bit of music or a nice podcast, then all of that conversation becomes unintelligible. In fact there have been times when a co-worker has walked right up to me, looked me in the eyes, and asked a direct question in a conversational voice. And I have not been able to make out what he said with these guys on.

In terms of sound quality, these are not the same as over the ears, or even the multiple driver headphones that are out there like the one from 1More. But these are very good. Combined with the fact that a lot of the ambient noise is blocked, you actually can hear the quieter sounds a lot better.

In all, in my opinion this has been a good purchase. After this I actually bought the Bluetooth cable kits from Shure themselves. If you're going to use this with a smartphone, I recommend doing one of those options.

title: High quality parts, poor sound
text:
The folks on head-fi rated these really well, but I am underwhelmed. The primary advantage is superior isolation. With the included foam tips, these could be used as great earplugs. The cable and housing are high quality. They are light and tiny and fit perfect. The Knowles driver is supposed to be great... Unfortunately, they just don’t sound good. It is like listening to a single mid-range driver while the woofer is blown and the tweeter is missing. A sine wave below 80Hz is accompanied by significant harmonic distortion, and above 9k is breathy. I am no bass head, nor do I play at loud volume. I am not just a balanced armature (BA) hater either (I swore by my Sensaphonics 2x-s dual BA customs for many years, till they broke).

Bottom line, unless isolation is your primary need, there are better options for less money.

title: Three outlets, but can't fit more than two plugs
text:
Anker is one of my "preferred" and "trusted" brands because they have proven that their products are really good quality, especially for the price.

Furthermore, a product can have "good qualities" without actually being a "good design."

The good qualities are that it's built really well. It feels like it's durable and it has a nice aesthetic. It also has guards to prevent stuff from falling into the slots.

With three outlets presented, it would be expected that all three can be used at the same time. Unfortunately this isn't the case if you have devices with larger plugs due to the layout/orientation of the outlets.

For whatever reason, Anker decided to orient the outlets in an unconventional way (compared to most power strips) which increased the chance of devices trying to occupy the same space when both are plugged in.

Included is an example picture. We can see the Anker USB charger encroaches into the next space which prevents that outlet from being used.

Seriously Anker? Two of your products don't play nice together...Hmm...

The USB charger has the prongs oriented properly so the brick would not interfere with whatever was below (when plugged into the wall).

Now you might wonder why I bought the strip when it's very clear that the orientation of the plugs is unconventional. Well it's really not something I thought about when buying a power strip. That's definitely on me though.

The next question you might have is why I'm using a separate USB charger when this power strip has three USB ports. Well the simple answer is that none are "fast charging" so they're only used for devices which don't require fast charging.

But yeah, I'm disappointed in Anker's design team on this.

text:
EDIT: I have reduced the review down to one star from two, because the seller tried to bribe me in order to remove this review. That is not a professional way to go about selling on Amazon, and it is a clear violation of seller policies. My product review is staying, and you can reference it below.

The pros of this product are that it is really sturdy and durable. I wanted to get a laptop stand without hinges or anything that could break or wear over time, so this will definitely do the trick. And it can hold a ton of weight, although that benefit seems gimmicky since the heavy laptops it can hold will not be well supported as they will topple off the back.

However, despite saying it can fit a 17" laptop, I often found my top-heavy 15" Surface Pro toppling backwards off the stand, time and time again. It was getting really frustrating, especially since my laptop is built for having the screen touched. It also means I couldn't open the laptop too wide, or it would topple backwards.

I managed to make it work when I went to Home Depot and made a kickstand out of a couple blocks of wood. And it's absolutely perfect when I have my laptop in tablet mode, since there is no top-heaviness. But it's frustrating that I had to do this in the first place. Their pictures even mostly show Macbooks, even though they say it can hold larger laptops (it can't, or at least not without something like what I put together). And based on the other laptop stands, it seems like that is the market they are targeting.

Just because Macs are popular does not mean you should ignore your PC counterparts!

The product build is solid and it fits the device well when I take the bottom protector shell off - which can be inconvenient at times.  When using on a flat surface, I like that the adaptor fits snug to the device to minimize wear and tear on the USB-C plugs. However, when I use the adapter on on a laptop stand or on my lap, the advantages of this adaptor disappear.  In fact, I'm always concerned when using it in mobile situations that the device itself may be placing unnecessary stress on the USB-C portal plugs.  Since I use my laptop in mobile settings primarily, this has been a constant concern with this adaptor.  Frankly, for mobile use, a dongle adaptor makes more sense. title: This is the review you came here for
text:
I bought 8 of these drives for my home FreeNAS server. My idea was for the price I could have 2 backup drives sitting in case something failed on me. Following the guide to give them a proper testing/burn in (google FreeNAS Hard Drive Burn-In Testing). I just put all 8 drives through that test for over 90 hours total and then went back to a SMART test to check the logs. I have testing data on 6 of the 8 drives and all of them passed the most important ones:

Reallocated_Sector_Ct
Current_Pending_Sector
Offline_Uncorrectable

All of these returns raw values of 0, which would be the expectation of a healthy drive. At this point I plan to fire up the storage array and start putting data on them. I expected them to be used drives. The power on hours of the drives I check varied from 32000 to 42000 hours.

title: I want to love this TV....but I can't. I can only like it.
text:
I bought the Samsung UN58RU7100FXZA to replace my nearly 15 year old Toshiba. It was the first flatscreen TV I purchased, and it had served it's purpose.

Let's review!

Setup on the TV was a breeze. Plugged in my Ethernet cable and we we ready to go within 3 minutes. Netflix, Hulu and Amazon Prime were loaded already, and Spotify was easily downloadable. I plugged a wireless USB keyboard into the back of the TV and it worked like a charm. Now I was ready to type in searches instead of using the remote. Whoo!

The TV easily recognized my computer and cable box. The remote even paired with my cable box, eliminating one remote on my coffee table. That's NICE! I also have a Samsung Note 9, so I can turn the TV on and off with my phone, as well as use it as a remote if I want to. Extra nice! I can also mirror my phone to the TV - Extra EXTRA nice. Wasn't expecting that.

I also love the fact that you can plug a USB stick into this thing with pre-loaded videos and it knows the file format. It's great if you're looking to play a movie file and you don't have a computer hooked up to the TV.

Netflix, Hulu and Amazon Prime all look FANTASTIC on this thing. No issues whatsoever....here's where the problems start, though.

I have an LG Soundbar, and the audio output is just SO soft coming from this TV. I have to keep it about 10 notches higher than on my old TV and the sound output doesn't sound as good as my old one. It's even worse when I've tested bluetooth...just not loud enough for me. It could be my soundbar, it's not amazing, but still. I've dicked around with all the settings and I still can't get it to sound as good. This TV doesn't have a 3.5mm jack, so I ended up buying an HDMI ARC Adapter and that thing saved my life. Highly recommended, although it takes up 1 of the 3 HDMI ports.

I watch a lot of hockey, and this TV has issues with the judder effect on hockey specifically. No other live sports seem to effect it. The TV picture will slow, and then it seems to sort of catch back up with itself. I've screwed around with every setting on the TV - picture mode, auto motion plus, and nothing fixes the effect. I have no idea why it's doing it, but my old 15 year old TV didn't have that issue.

Lastly, the display from my computer is pitiful. I've tried to watch things right off my computer and it's dark and terrible looking. Again, not sure why. Never had that problem with my old TV. It could be my video card. My old TV didn't recognize that it had a computer plugged into it, and this TV DOES, so I suspect its trying to display some sort of TV specialized video setting and it just looks like hot garbage. Luckily I don't really need to have my computer plugged into it, but I wish I would have realized that before I bought it.

Anyways, to sum up, if you're looking for a TV that's going to get you amazing picture on streaming services, get this one. You might have some audio issues if you're using an older sound bar, and you may have some issues with the judder effect like I do. If you want something top of the line, this isn't for you. This is a mid-range TV that's going to last you about 7 years before something even better comes along.

Let’s face it, sometimes you just don’t feel like crawling into the hot attic and drilling holes in your ceiling below. In my scenario I have spray foam insulation in my attic floor so my visibility of electrical wiring is nil and makes me hesitant to drill.

So I opted for choice B, purchasing the UniFi BeaconHD. This repeater works well, was easy to install and required only a little trial and error to select the best location.

You will get the best result if the beacon is located close enough to the AP wireless link that you have at least 90% signal strength. This will maximize your speed and stability. Overall, 30 minutes of time increased my sons Xbox network speed from 17 mbits/s to 285 with 100% signal strength in his room.

title: Unexpected Extraordinary Value
text:
I bought this PC as a perceived best option to replace a failed main workstation. I needed a replacement that would be compatible with a GNU/Linux operating system. HP has their own Linux Enterprise distribution, and being a business-oriented model only strengthened the assumption this would be perfect for my needs.

Specs on this are across the board better than the failed unit's. I knew I would be changing hardware, so I made sure that I could make these changes before buying.

The provided Hitachi 2 TB HDD was nearly 9 yrs old, with over 54,000 hours of run time on it, so I swapped it out for a brand new 2 WD 2 TB I had in inventory, adding a slightly-used 1 TB WD as a second drive. Although a noisy operating drive, SmartMonitor suggested that the Hitachi had a lot of life left in it. I'll use it my docks as a spare backup solution.

(Extra value #1)
The 120 GB SSD included in the PC wasn't needed, so I used it in my laptop. The improvement in performance was very noticeable.

(Extra value #2)
A Tendon W311M a/b/n class Wi-Fi dongle was provided in a static-protection pack. I had no need for this in the HP, but I did have a Gateway desktop that was going into the workshop and needed Wi-Fi capability. Now the Gateway can connect to my router via Wi-Fi.

Noted Shortcomings:
The laptop designed DVD drive is useless. It struggled to read my burned DVD-Rs. There is a bay provided that will open to the outside for a 5.25" DVD-RW. I plan on adding one from my inventory. Unfortunately, I will need to keep the DVD drive in the chassis, until I can order a blank cover.

HP doesn't provide enough mounting screws to fully populate the drive bays. I ended up with 7 instead of 8, now mounting two HDDs. I ordered a set of eight screws from Amazon (about $8 USD.)

I wish the motherboard has just one PCI slot. I was fortunate not to have an immediate need for one, but...

Linux users will need to download from their Tendon's website the source code for their v3.0 proprietary driver. This won't be a standard 'make, make install' installation. A binary is provided under the 'tools' directory to install driver to the system. There are no instructions provided on the website or in the source package. it took some searching and a 'cross my fingers and try this' approach to figure this out. Installation is dialog-free, without visuals. You'll know it's done when the HDD stops.

Lastly, I'm not fond of paying a 'M$ tax' on a PC I buy, but I'm used to it. In getting the full use of the drives I've destroyed a legit, complete OEM Windows 10 installation. It *only* bothers me that I paid for it.

The extra values, in my case, made the cost for this unit an extraordinary value. Time will tell how durable it will be. The 1 yr warranty is a big plus, and that the vendor will not void my warranty because of the above changes made. I highly recommend this PC for Linux users wanting a cheap system with lots of modern features. I can't comment on running the PC with the provided Windows 10 installation.

title: A Masterpiece
text:
This DAP is ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC!!!

I’ve been a dap user for a few years -- everything from an Ibasso DX50 to an Astell & Kern Kann and a Sony NW-WM1A. And my three current iems are Noble Kaiser 10, Campfire Atlas and Jerry Harvey (JH Audio) Roxanne II with the Moon Audio Black Dragon cable. I’ve only had the Dethonray for a few days, but I’ve already logged many, many hours listening to it (I just don’t want to put it down).

I was a bit surprised that the Campfire wasn’t a good match for the Dethonray. Its V-shaped signature had great bass (it’s basshead favorite) but the midrange and treble were decidedly on the thin side. The Noble worked very well indeed, but with the JH the skies opened up onto a crystal clear day. A slight layer of haze was lifted from the other iems and everything snapped into focus. Fully fleshed-out midrange, superb imaging and amazing detail without a hint of glare or sibilance. And the bass was powerful and actually better than the Campfire. Don’t get me wrong, the Astell & Kern and Sony are excellent players, but the Dethonray just does EVERYTHING better.

But what’s mentioned but not extensively commented on in the reviews is its phenomenal dynamics. Reviewers generally don’t pay much attention to dynamics, but It’s dynamics that makes music come ALIVE, and the Dethonray beats the other daps hands down. Snare drums SNAP, kick drums KICK, and microdynamics on strings and vocals are terrific.

I have over 1,500 CDs and exactly three hi-res albums, but fully expect that in the very near future a significant chunk of my bank account will wind up over at HDTracks.

And as good as this dap sounds with my Roxanne IIs, I suspect that the guy who wrote the review who has the Audeze LCD i4s is in seventh heaven.

Just one suggestion for Mr. Tse…

I used to equalize lots of music, but I haven’t really found much of a need for an equalizer on the Dethonray, but occasionally it would be nice to have. The half-octave equalizer on the NW-WM1A has very fine db adjustments and adjustable Q and is out-of-this world excellent. Would it be possible to build an equalizer into a firmware update?

And Mr. Tse,

Congratulations on making such an AMAZING dap, and THANK YOU! THANK YOU!! THANK YOU!!!

title: Did not meet expectations
text:
I got the Android app and updated to the latest device firmware 2.4.4.20190711. I set this up as a driveway camera 160 feet from a hardwired wrt54gl Wifi router (direct line of sight to the camera). It shows "50% wifi" and seems unable to stream HD smoothly although SD is smooth. I initially set it up upside down because that was convenient and turned on "rotate view" in the app. The problem is every time motion is detected, the first 1-2 seconds has the image upside down and then it switches to "rotate view" which means it does not catch what triggered the motion. I then switched it back to normal orientation and turned off "rotate view" and still the motion detection lag means all I ever see in the video is the distant object (if moving away from camera in view, see attached image) or NOTHING (if approaching camera and going behind camera). So the major flaw with this camera is that is cannot record 24/7 - if it could be constantly recording, then when motion is detected it could include several seconds PRIOR to motion detect. The object is long gone by the time video starts (we are talking 5-10 mph here).

Additional issues:
* Sometimes completely misses an event. As I was writing this review I had a lawn service pull up the driveway, then back out right past the camera. I have no 'Alarm' for this event. It only has alarms of ME going out there afterwards. Frustrating! Not sure if this had something to do with me streaming it Live when the truck pulled up.
* There is no ability to rewind/forward the video you are watching, only pause
* The app does not support horizontal orientation except when playing video, making it difficult to view the first few seconds of video because I have to rotate it out of portrait mode every time to get full screen video
* Can only view the list of captures one day at a time (one big list would be better)
* The cloud/SD videos do not match up consistently. It is missing portions of the capture sometimes and sometimes cloud is missing an event that SD has.
* The video quality seems poor. I was hoping it could capture license plates
* I get "lost connection" and "missing SD card" messages frequently

title: Great Kit, Minor Complaints
text:
Packaging Quality: 3/5
Tool Quality: 4.5/5
Tool Variety: 5/5
Case Quality: 2/5

Overall: The kit is great for what it was designed to do; which is to give you just about everything you'd need to get in and work on laptops, cellphones, and other electronic devices. The case is also designed to be convenient. It's very easy to get things out and to put them back in their designated slot. Unlike many tool kits, you're not going to open this up and find things ready to fall out or rolling around in different places if you put them away properly.

What could be improved: Ship in boxes, not paper/plastic envelopes; improve case craftsmanship; improve case quality control; improve storage of anti-static strap using some sort of hard shell; add an additional suction cup.

Packaging Quality: The packaging is pretty good. It consists of a hard front-loaded box and a slide-over cardboard label. There's nothing special about it, but it looks nice and provides adequate protection for the actual product. The reason I gave this a 3/5 is because the shipping method. I've received two of these, one came in an Amazon branded plastic envelope while the other came in a manila paper envelope from iFixIt. In both instances, the product's packaging was damaged during shipping. While the product itself remained seemingly undamaged, seeing the product's box with smash corners isn't the most reassuring thing.

Tool Quality: Most of the tools are absolutely great. The screwdriver and provided bits seem to be sturdy and well made. Likewise, the Tweezers, opening pics, and spudgers all feel great. The only complaint I have is that wire on the anti-static wrist strap feels like a cheap slippery plastic.

Tool Variety: This has just about everything, really. The only thing I wish they would have done is included two suction cups instead of one. My turning the elastic bands to the side and moving them over, they would have had room for both of them in the case too.

Case Quality: This is my biggest gripe about this toolkit. I don't know if I just have bad luck, but the first kit I got had a tear in the upper-left corner near the magnetic plate (under the 64 bit driver kit) and in the second kit the top appears stretched out of shape a bit with what appears to be the start of a tear in the top left. I believe this happens because they cut the material without adding any sort of trim and stitching around the cut. Likewise, there are various other areas where the case has bad stitching, loose hanging threads, and overlapping trim. For such a nice quality set, the case seems less than expected. However, it's still a great bargain considering all that you get for $60.

My only other complaint about the case is with the anti-static strap. Getting it back in its storage pocket in a manner that allows the case to close properly is annoying. I'd have liked to see a hard-shell to help keep the anti-static strap compact or a hard case for the entire kit.

title: Short & Long version "case" specific review
text:
Short Version:
As a BASIC case though noticeable heft and moderate protection from scraps, scratches etc this case is "acceptable" BECAUSE IT IS IN STOCK for delivery NOW. If you expect to enjoy the flap cover, etc you will likely be disappointed. Button pressing is useless with this case on though. This VERY likely will make you hate the Supveco case.

Long Version:
First and foremost, this case was selected because at the time of purchase (09/28/2020) NO cases for the just-launched Tab S7 Plus were readily available. The new Tab S7 and S7 Plus are high-end tablets built with premium-feeling materials. I personally HATE scratches/damage on my electronics. So I searched for
1. thin (aka not Otter style tank) case to protect the metal and glass back/edges
2. S Pen slots (front edge of tablet or rear) SEE CON/PROBLEM NOTE BELOW

I selected this case knowing I would ultimately modify it for the way I intended to use it. I will explain. I personally am not a fan nor do I really need the flap/cover. Though I will comment on it. The flap, just like that rest of the case is of decent gauge plastic. The flap is appropriately thin. The magnets HOWEVER are MUCH TOO weak to really maintain the triangular shape when using as stand/lift. As long as there isn't much jostling, the folded case "should" keep it's shape. But a rambunctious toddler or strong gust of wind will cause the flap to collapse. If you are looking to primarily use this case in this way, look for something else.

Next, the case is heavy. Its weight is noticeable. Here are the weights I recorded with my postal scale.
Tablet, naked no pen = 1lb 3.8oz
Case, empty = 11.6oz
Tablet in case with Pen = 1lb 15.6oz

The area on the back of the Tab S7 Plus where you attach the Pen magnetically IS A PROBLEM with this case. The plastic is NOT CUT OUT! Luckily there is a groove molded into the plastic but the case plastic on the rear is thick enough that the magnet attachment is NOT RELIABLE while using this Supveco case. I solved this with my exacto knife. This ALONE would NOT be a deal breaker for me personally. But...

Lastly, the worst part of this Supveco case is the button area. The buttons are now INCREDIBLY hard to press. You can't even feel by touch alone anymore. You have to look and press WITH determination. Power button is the worst/most unresponsive with this case on the tablet.

THE BUTTON PROBLEM MAKES THIS CASE A HARD PASS for long term use/comfort. Unless you cannot find basic protective case, understand you gain weight and REALLY unresponsive buttons. I am keeping it because I cut the Pen area out. I accept that as I needed something to protect my tablet until I can get a skin type case (aka super thin TPU style, just to protect against scratches etc.)

I paid for this case. It was NOT a gift or sponsored.

I am rating this ONLY TWO STARS because of the horrible button response and the weight.
The non-existent cutout is an easy fix.

title: Two thumbs up.
text:
I have a friend who purchased a different backup camera, a wired one. He had to run wires from the video screen on the dash, down underneath the carpeting, under the back seat, then drill a hole and continue the wires under the bed of his truck, to his hitch. Then make up a special connector to his trailer, then another set of wires over the top of his trailer, to the back of the rig, where he drilled holes to attach the camera. Since he was trying to make the setup look nice, the whole ordeal took him a couple of long days, and cost extra money for nice looking wire conduit. Whew.

My LeeKooLuu Wireless Backup Camera, on the other hand, required me to plug the screen into my 12V dash socket. Then I drilled holes in the back of my trailer, like my friend did, to mount the camera, and hooked up the camera to 12V in one of the trailer running lights. The whole job, trying to be careful, took me maybe 90 minutes. Turned on the vehicle power/lights, and, bingo, a hi-def picture was there on the screen. I had worried that the signal from the camera might not be strong enough to reach from my 23-ft trailer to the screen mounted low on the console, but so far, not a single dropout.

I'm pretty impressed with the overall quality of this equipment. Everything seems very solidly constructed and well-made. Like many Asian products the instructions were not written by a native English speaker, so there is a bit of 'interpretation' to do, especially with the programming instructions. But the programming is not complicated; watching the company's YouTube video for a few minutes was enough to get me familiar with the screen controls.

I'm guessing that the picture refresh rate is not as high as say, a TV, so the picture, when you're driving down the road, is slightly 'choppy', i.e., it's not quite as smooth as watching your home TV, as the traffic and scenery is going by quickly. But it's certainly adequate to determine what's going on behind you, and when actually using the camera to back into a space you don't notice any jumpiness at all.

I'm very satisfied with this backup camera. You might even say that I'm a happy camper. Literally. Would I buy it again? You bet.

title: Did not support three 27'' 11.75lb monitors
text:
- Instructions for grommet installation were terrible. Step 1 includes a picture of a nut on the top of each bolt, which doesn't exist. The listed supplies contained two nuts total, and they are both used for after threading the bolts. I get that companies often re-use pictures for different models, but it's added confusion when there's no way to fasten the bolt above the desk. The top tips of the bolts must be secured in a hollow shell (the base of the stand) before they are threaded through the desk, so they can freely spin, move, and pop up up to a full inch within the shell while trying to thread through the desk (see picture).

- The product cannot hold three 15 pound monitors. It can't even hold three 12 pound monitors. I hooked three 27'' monitors up (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07J4SXNQ5/). They stood fine when they were all overlapping directly above the base, but when spacing them out 27'' (so they fit side-by-side) the base immediately began cracking as soon as I tightened the 3rd monitor. I assume that to say "Maximum support weight 15.4 pounds" they stacked the monitors vertically directly above the base.

- The bottom tips of the bolts were stripped during installation, which made it a pain to uninstall. The stripping was my fault, but because the bolts can't be fastened within the shell, the bolt freely spins while trying to twist the nut off. Some awkward clamping could've made it possible, but after an hour of attempts I just bought a cheap hacksaw to get the bolts out.

All issues were with the base and grommet installation. The rest of the product seemed pretty solid. The arms were easy to tighten and position however I wanted - except the screw to stop the outer monitors from horizontally swiveling couldn't be hand turned - the hand-screw just pushes into the base no matter how it is positioned). The cable management looked very useful. The item weight obviously isn't "0.16 ounces" as it states on Amazon - it's closer to 30 pounds. Perhaps the high reviews are for the C-Clamp base, which seems to be advertised more, but my desk didn't have a 4-inch lip at the end. Wish they could've refunded the wasted time and the two holes I now have in my desk. Thankfully Amazon's returns were a breeze.

title: It's almost perfect
text:
So here's almost just what I wanted. It's almost perfect. It turns the ipad into a netbook. Hard case + keyboard = awesome. I love it. I highly recommend it. I will be showing it to my friends and guarantee I will absolutely drive future sales as I think this thing rocks. I do have some feature suggestions.

I could care less about the pencil holder thing. It's clearly modelled after the MS Surface tablet as the stylus loop is pretty much exactly what my surface tablet has for its stylus that I never use. Meh. Big meh. I'm tempted to cut it off. Wish like on the surface you could have the option of sticking it on either side. The Surface stylus loop is a sticker, put it where you want. It makes NO sense for the pencil holder to be on the bottom instead of the top in portrait/tablet mode. Kinda dumb. Even in clamshell mode it is on the left when most people are right handed. Little product design advice.

Next advice: This hinge is clearly modelled after the Lenovo Twist laptop, which I had. Now my daughter has. The hinge works the same way. This is super cool and I love it as it was one of my favorite laptops. Here's the hinge issue though. It can't fold all the way around to the other side. That would be super cool. Just needs a double cardan type hinge so it can fold on a second hinge and get the full flip under.

Next product feature request/suggestion: It needs a touchpad so it feels more like a laptop. A small one would be fine, certainly enough room for one. It should also suggest turning on the advanced keyboard navigation features in the instructions because that option makes this keyboard even way cooler. Okay, that was two.

Next feature request is to make this thing work more like the ASUS transformer, which it obviously also gets its design ideas from. The tablet/netbook design rocked. The transformer was a tablet with 8 hours of battery that clipped onto the keyboard dock... which had its own battery that could charge and prolong the life of the tablet for another 8 hours for a total of 16 hours of battery. Surely, you could come up with a wireless or wired charging design. This would fix another issue...

The keyboard is too light. If it had the battery bank in it, it would increase keyboard weight so the thing doesn't fall over backwards when you tilt the screen too far back.

Is USB-C too much to ask for? Seriously? Using micro-USB is so 10-20 years ago. Again, back to the battery bank idea, plugging in the keyboard to charge both keyboard battery bank and tablet is just a good design idea for the next gen product.

If there was even a thin covering of a neoprene like rubber in the case to help absorb shock from drops, that would rock.

And if the tablet could mount in either way left or right (for the lefties, not that I'm one of those weirdos :D) that would just be a solid design idea. I mean, what would it take, cut some more holes?

Whoever designed this made the coolest ipad keyboard case I have seen so far. I love it. All the above isn't criticism in the slightest. Just suggestions. If you're reading this as a customer, just buy it. You'll love it. Those floppy soft keyboard cases suck. Can't use them on your lap without a lapdesk. This case makes it a mini laptop running iOS (sadly). It's dope. Pull the trigger and get it, people.

Okay, suggestions out of the way. They keyboard, while a little small, is excellent to type on, and I am a larger dude with big clumsy fingers, yet I can touch-type on it great. It's quite good. The "Twist" mode stuff is exceptional, the hinge feels sturdy, the material is solid. It seems to have amazing battery life. It's almost exactly what I wanted. It fits the bill quite nicely. I got one for my son and after playing with it for an hour I knew I needed one for my ipad. I love it. Buy it.

title: Great Sound, Short Battery Life, Vulnerable To Breakage
text:
I purchased these headphones for use on the plane, in the office, and while I mow my yard. I was very happy with the sound quality. The case doubles as a charger, which was very convenient, especially for travel as it fits neatly in my backpack. The headphones paired easily with my phone or laptop. While mowing, I had to push them in every now and again (I live in Texas and it's always hot when I mow). But, having no wire to yank out when I shifted the mower or other yard tool was a major improvement. The noise cancellation, volume, and sound quality were exceptional. I especially enjoyed movie soundtracks as the bass was cavernous and the stereo field wide. Wireless calling was solid, as reported by people I was on calls with. Even walking through the airport, background noise was not an issue.

Battery life quickly became in issue on my first flight to San Fran (3.75 hours) during which the batteries died, roughly 2.5 hours in. I brought wired phones as backup, which defeated the point of the convenience of not being wired to my laptop when watching Netflix. I also like to listen to music in the terminal. So, you can see the issue. But, I just made sure to charge them up to get the longest life out of them I could.

I dropped the case one time on a hard floor, which is easy to do as it's a completely smooth, egg-ish shape, and now one side will not charge at all. I have yet to open it up to see if it's as simple as fixing a solder joint. But, it seems quite vulnerable to breakage if one drop is enough to make the phones unusable.

So, with the caveat of "don't drop it" and if you never need more than 2.5 hours of battery life between charges, the sound quality and ease of use are strong. Provisionally recommended.

title: You get 3 bags!
text:
The Bopai Slim Laptop Backpack with USB Charging system is a downsizing dream.

The exterior is a combination of neoprene like and thick canvas material with padding in all the rights spots on straps, back and front to protect your gear. Shhh *it’s even got a secret zipper on the back with a strap that hides the pocket!*

The zippers, straps and interior key ring have a high quality feel. The main pocket for your laptop is a soft suede like material, with a dark blue and red interior pocket system for accessories.

You also get a cool 40 inch soft-braided USB ‘one cable to rule them all’ tossed in to hook up all those toys and phones to a battery pack (not included) if you like. The interior cable for your pack is one foot long standard USB male connector.

The bag comes in right around 765 grams. And as noted all over this page, it's slim.

Downsizing your backpack is a must in 2020, I’ve tried a few bags over the past 6 months and I have loved going smaller. I used to carry around a datacenter but now I’m lean and light!

Transferring my ‘light config’ to the Bopai was easy... I’ve got:
HP EliteBook 840 G5 (9 inches wide). This pouch could go 9 ¾ maybe?
Small portfolio notebook for taking notes (put this in the side zipper exterior pouch)
USB-C power brick (charges laptop and phone)
Travel mouse (Logitech Anywhere MX)
USB IP Phone Headset
USB-C network adapter
2 pens, a sharpie, flashlight, polishing cloth, brush, clippers, floss, gum, biz cards.

I used to have a ton of dongles, docks, card readers, converters, chargers, cables, candy, remotes, Lego and all other kind of stuff that I ‘thought’ I needed, but the point is to travel light now, you see!

As I loaded the above into the Bopai, it was getting a little crowded in the main compartment when I realized I was under utilizing the outside main pocket which is a generous exterior with a top zipper that opens up and was perfect for the remainder of my junk.

It’s also got a water bottle side pouch!

The only thing I can say ‘doh!’ to on this so far is the handle. Great straps and I usually go with the single shoulder stroll, but at times I do just carry it by handle. I would have preferred a better handle up top, some padding or larger grip area. Can’t even dock a quarter star for that.

I’m making this my daily driver and will report back any surprises, but so far this one is an attractive full feature keeper!

Ps: You get a big plastic zip top bag it was shipped in and a large blue recycle like bag with draw string to store it in… Bonus! You can use these to store all the old junk that you don’t really need to carry around with you anymore when you downsize like me. You’re welcome.

title: Overpriced
text:
Starting with the pros, these have very good sound quality. While I didn't get them for listening to music, you totally can and they will sound like a good pair of wired headphones if BT source you're using supports high fidelity.

Unfortunately, that's where the good parts end.
The touch buttons, while a good idea at first, perform very poorly. There's a significant lag between touching them and experiencing the effect of the touch. I found myself double and triple activating the buttons because I thought it didn't register the touch the first time around. Pretty bad.
Then things get worse. Battery life is dismal. Li ion batteries don't like to be charged to 100% and kept that way. After desperately searching for an OFF switch on the headphones and then on the case, I resigned myself to just putting them down and waiting for them to power off. If only. They would randomly come back to life and more often than not, I find myself with low battery after less than 48h since last full charge and less than 30min of use time. Most of the time one side will be down to 20% while the other would be 70% or more charged. I also found the battery levels to drop from the reported "about 50%" to "low battery" within 15 minutes. Ridiculous. A bad attempt at copying the iFruit company.
Like most other BT devices, they suffer from the occasional stutter and magic disconnects. To add insult to injury however, I also discovered that if you pair them to more than 1 device, the device that comes back to life last, will steal the connection upon powering on. Yup.. if you're connected to your phone and laptop and and the laptop turns on, the connection automagically switches. At least in my case it did.
So overall not something you want to spend over $200 on. I didn't get them for the noise canceling feature and have consistently avoided doing so. I like the pass through sound mode, so you can hear the environment. At $100, perhaps more palatable.

title: Ring insists on operating ILLEGALLY in the City of St Louis
text:
This entire system is essentially useless to me at the moment because the Ring service operates ILLEGALLY in my city. I pay for the alarm monitoring service, but am unable to use it because I cannot convince Ring to acquire the required permit from the City of St Louis. My city’s regulations are clear and specific - for monitored alarms, the MONITORING COMPANY must obtain a permit for the service. Non-permitted alarms in STL are subject to a fine, and after one or more fines police and first-responders may not be dispatched at all (you read that right...look it up). Because of this, I have left my alarm monitoring disabled, despite having paid for the service. I made attempts to contact Ring about this and each time they told me that "permits are not required in your location." I insisted that this was not the case - assuming that maybe they made the classic mistake of thinking that the City of St Louis is located in St Louis County, where permits may or may not be required (it is not - it is its own independent city-county).
They eventually “escalated my issue” to the permits department and ended the phone conversation, saying it would take 4 or so days to get back to me. That was 3 months ago.

That's the main issue. Fixing that would certainly make the system at least a little more useful. But there are still other problems with the system:

- No ability for separate zones or buildings. I have a detached garage that I would like to arm without arming all of my house doors at the same time, but this isn’t possible with Ring.

- Lack of integration and customization between alarm system and cameras. My Video Doorbell 2 (also a garbage device) regularly misses visitors and delivery personnel at my front door, or only captures the last few seconds as they have already turned to leave - I was hoping I could solve the issue by placing a motion sensor from the alarm kit out front and linking it to the doorbell cam so that it would be triggered sooner and more reliably, but alas, this is another simple customization unavailable to Ring users.

- Needs an additional alarm mode. There really needs to be something in between “Home” and “Away.”
-- "Home" mode means sensors are set to trigger after a waiting period and motion sensors are disabled - this is good because it means I can still walk into or out of my house without setting off the alarm.
-- "Away" mode enables all sensors (door and motion) for immediate tripping of the alarm - also good.
-- "Sleep" mode or some other custom option should also be available, to allow outside (or “Main”) door sensors to still trip instantly, while disabling select motion sensors and inner door sensors so that I can get up and move about my house (in the morning or when I use the bathroom) without tripping my system.

I feel terribly insecure sleeping in “Home” mode because by the time the system alerts me to an intruder (30-90 seconds after the door sensor trips) it could be too late - but I likewise hate sleeping in “Away” mode because I risk tripping the whole system if I don’t remember to disable it before leaving my bedroom.

Additionally, I've had a raft of problems with the cameras in my system - failure to detect motion/people (despite picking up EVERY SINGLE CAR that drives down my street), repeated failures to connect to the cameras from my Echo Show and from the iOS, Windows, and Mac apps both from inside my home network and from outside, and cameras that show "Firmware up to date" in the preferences despite this not being the case. I had to unpair/remove a Stick Up Cam earlier today and re-pair it to the system in order for it to recognize that it needed a firmware update (the one that provides Snapshot Capture). After re-pairing the camera it immediately downloaded the update and made the feature available, despite moments earlier lying to me, saying that it was up-to-date. Every other device I own - phone, computer, TV, printer...even a frickin' coffee maker - TELLS ME WHAT VERSION OF FIRMWARE IT IS RUNNING. Why does Ring insist on obscuring this information from its users??

Speaking of Snapshot Capture - why is 14 minutes the closest interval for Stick Up Cams when the Doorbell cam can do snapshots every 3 minutes? They use exactly the same battery, and therefore should have similar battery life! It's these little incidences of disjointedness throughout the Ring ecosystem that have made it one of the most infuriating product sets I have ever dealt with.

I know I'm the fool here for thinking a cloud-based startup-y system (despite Amazon ownership) like Ring could really do all of the things I want my alarm system to do, but it's amazing how completely it fails on all fronts. It's super frustrating to have spent $1000+ on absolute junk parts with a junk service behind them, in any case.

title: Very mixed
text:
This is the only Razer product that I haven't been able to give 5 stars to, and I was jumping between 2 and 3 stars.

Pros:
- The orange keys are very quiet for mechanical keys. If you've never used mechanical before it's still going to be "loud" but compared to my old cherry blues and browns it's quite "office friendly".
- It's really easy to switch between devices

Cons:
- Battery life. Even at 25% brightness and generous sleep & dim times (dim at 2 minutes, sleep at 5 minutes of idle) it still MIGHT last 1 8-hour work day. For such a high-end product this is almost unacceptable life.
- Poor QA and/or shipping protection from Razer. My first one came with a sticky left-shift. It just did not come back up by itself. Razer asked to send it to them so they could see what broke and keep it from happening. I just wish I knew it'd take 2 weeks. Should have just exchanged with Amazon. The replacement that Razer did send, 10 keys were loose and had to be popped back on. No biggy since mechanicals are typically easy to take key-caps on and off with no damage but doesn't give you great confidence that it wasn't damaged in shipping.

TL;DR; Wouldn't buy again. battery life is non-existent and unusually poor QA from Razer.

title: Swiping to turn pages was an epic fail in my 10th gen PW, so glad to have page turn buttons again!!
text: My first Kindle was a Kindle keyboard purchased in 2011. I still love it, it still works, and I still use it at times. Then I've had two other models: the 2013 Paperwhite, which works well but I wanted more drive space, and a 10th generation Paperwhite purchased in 2018 to get the larger drive. Enjoyed the 2013 device, still have it and use it when traveling, but absolutely hated and despised the 10th generation device. The swipe function just never, never, ever worked properly.  I read fast, and turning almost every page took multiple swipes. My husband had the same experiences with essentially the same devices. So this year we decided to bite the bullet and get each other an Oasis as an early Christmas gift during Prime Day.  I've now been reading on mine for nearly three weeks. Overall, I love the device and I'm thrilled not to have to "swipe" anymore. However, as has been the trend with ereaders from Amazon, battery life continues to get worse and worse. I read a LOT now that Covid is a reality - I greatly prefer that to TV and I recently retired, and traveling is not really a good option these days.  I have to charge my Oasis every single night, and no, I'm not reading in the dark with the light turned up high to compensate. I have long term worries about the battery being used in the current devices; over the years the quality of the components in the various ereaders seem to have gone down with every successive generation. As noted, I consider my 10th generation Paperwhite an epic fail in functionality since swiping never functioned properly.  I do enjoy the ability to turn on the warm light on the Oasis at night to block the blue light if reading close to bedtime, but don't need to use that often. It is a well balanced device that is comfortable to hold, and the slightly larger screen is nice.  I hope the considerably higher cost of the Oasis will be mirrored by a long life span - otherwise, it will be time to look at other brands of ereaders. I have to assume that removing buttons from the Paperwhite devices was a marketing decision to drive readers to the considerably more expensive Oasis. I finally gave in, but that will be a one time surrender unless this device has a very long and very healthy lifespan.

title: Does the job but there are difficulties...
text: The claim is, this will install straight and without bubbles if on follows the directions.  The first is marginally true, the second appears not to be -- and this is not entirely the Maker's fault.  I've been sticking screen protectors in place back to at least the second gen Palm Pilot; I'm not a novice.  It's not an easy chore.  The supplied frame goes along way to solving the issue of straightness, but I found myself having to do the initial placement over on all three attempts.  The bubble problem is less tractable:. The problem is not dust n the screen, but dust that blows in and sticks to the adhesive side of the screen.  One speck equals one bubble, and the speck cannot be removed without leaving a mark on the adhesive.  In short this is a materials problem.  Sparin's claims about getting rid of bubbles are, therefore, disingenuous.  All this said, you don't see the bubbles when working, however unattractive things are when the screen is off.  And the extra layer of glass is a real protection, in my experience.  The price is modest enough.  So three stars off for excessive claims about straightness and bubbles and for a certain deceptiveness, but not a complete don't-buy.

title: Love it, but sometimes a bit much
text:
The only complaint I have is how long it took receive this and the subwoofer. Sound is amazing. Bought two "rear" speakers as well. Gorgeous sound. Well done. Can't complain about the time given the stresses on the supply chains during Covid-19.

** Update after a month or so of use

I still find the sound amazing, but with the full set-up, it sometimes gets shockingly loud. This is especially true for high action / Marvel type movies, but happens with lighter fare as well. The problem I have is some special effects sounds boom shockingly loud given the volume level needed to hear normal level dialogue. I've tried tweaking the bass way down on the subwoofer, tweaking the max level percent, and of course using the dialogue enhanced mode. These measures help a bit, but ultimately there are still times where it is simply jarring.

I can't take a star away for that, because when that is what you want, it delivers. And really, you buy a total system like this for those kinds of audio experiences. However, sometimes I just want to watch a regular show and not have to keep trying to balance between being able to hear dialogue while not being overwhelmed by booms or door slams, etc.

One thing that I think would help, and I believe this could be done through a firmware update, is to enable removing the subwoofer / rear channels without having to completely unpair them. Currently, removing these extra speakers requires a complete repairing later when you want them on again. That's kind of annoying. A temporary disabling of the extra channels would be much appreciated.

Also, I would definitely not recommend leaving the rear channels on while removing the subwoofer only. It throws to much bass at the rear channels in that configuration, and it sounds awful. So it's either remove three speakers, then later go through the full process of pairing the system again, or be prepared to volume dance when watching a show when you want less than a cinematic, booming experience.

title: Great gaming monitor MPG27CQ
text:
Right out of the box the excellent construction is very apparent.

THE STAND
The stand is no exception. It is well engineered and sturdy. It is so good I feel bad for not using it, because my setup uses a VESA mount. The stand is mainly constructed of Aluminum. It is connected to the back of the monitor using a quick release plate. Its adjustments are smooth and fluid. My only concern with it is the front legs are quite long. It could be an issue for some peoples setup. Thankfully the rear leg is fairly short so the whole unit can be slid back as far as possible. 4.9 stars on the stand. It truly is epic except for the length of those front legs.

THE MONITOR
Again the construction seems stellar. I must tell you I have only owned sub $300.00 monitors before. NEVER AGAIN. I am amazed at the build quality difference. The frame is sturdy and rigid. When picking the unit up there are no creaks or cackles from cheap lose plastic frames. This is a plastic case, but not a cheep one. There are no gaps around the frameless bezel anywhere. I did see a review where there was a gap in the bottom but not on mine, Its perfect as far as I can see. The RGB on the back of the unit while pointless in my opinion, looks pretty cool.

The OSD joystick on the back is an awesome feature. It is easy to use and even reprogrammable in the OSD. This way you can assign different frequently used selections to it instead of having to enter the OSD all the time. The OSD itself is quite nice to use. Its not clunky to use and seems to be well thought out. They took the chore out of trying to make adjustments. WELL DONE MSI WELL DONE!!

The screen is well.... a nice screen. It arrived with zero dead pixels. The 144hz at 1440p has been very nice in game. I have it coupled to a RTX 2080 and have it running in G-sync with no issues. This monitor does not appear on Nvidia's compatibility chart but it works just fine. I stepped down from a 4k display at 75hz and was a bit worried about it. But wow I am so glad that I did, what a difference 144hz makes.
Now comes my first complaint with this monitor. The colors out of the box kinda suck. In some stuff they appear overdriven, in others washed out. I have played with the settings and got it worked out fairly well. I have the ability to get it calibrated and will soon. But here is the thing..... I shouldn't have to. MSI, you need to address this in the future if you haven't already. ;)
The 1800R curve is not at all what I expected. Being my first curved monitor I expected a break in period to get used to it. But for me, not at all. Its just enough of a curve to almost not notice it. But, enough to make it easier to look around the screen. I really don't know how to explain it other than I really do like it.

VESA MOUNTING
Let me be clear, I am using a standard television swing arm mounted to the wall. Your experience may differ as I have never used an actual arm designed specifically for a PC monitor. Plain and simple, The VESA implementation on this unit is dam good. The mount locations came with the necessary screws pre installed. So there was no hunting for the correct screws. THANK YOU MSI, nice touch there. The VESA mount locations are hidden under where the stand quick release plate attaches. So you don't see them if you don't need them. Keeps it clean. When using the VESA mount option, you simply take out the four screws, and install four standoffs that are supplied in a baggie. These standoffs look exactly like motherboard standoffs. Because the mount locations are typically hidden under the monitor stand mount, these standoffs bring the VESA mounting locations out even with the back of the monitor. Nice and simple. This brings me to complaint number two. The screws have very small heads on them, so I had to supply washers so they wouldn't fall through my VESA bracket. While this is knit picky, The supplied screws could have had a wide head on them or washers with them. Either way, its no big deal but could be an inconvenience for someone.

CABLING
Included in the box is:
1 x HDMI 6'
1 x DP 6'
1 x 3.5mm to 3.5mm Stereo 6'
1 x Super speed USB type A to USB type B 6'
1 x Power supply and cable. Total length about 8'.

I was disappointed to find this unit came with a separate power supply. I wasn't aware of this when I purchased the unit. While it made my installation a little more inconvenient (had to source and order a longer cord), its not that big of a deal. We can't all win right? :P

DOCUMENTATION
Here is complaint number three. What documentation????? Oh scan a QR code on the back of a pamphlet to get to the digital download for the users manual, the software downloads for the OSD app, and Gamesense. SIGH...…. Kinda hard to download and install PC software on your smartphone.... Seriously? Seriously.... But alas just jump on MSI's website and its not bad to navigate to find the downloads.

Final thoughts.
I love this monitor. I am planning on grabbing another one when I can. It really is a nice monitor especially at this price point.

title: CAUTION!  Extremely poor instruction system!
text:
When you get this "Micro Converter" to work, it works!

But there are no instructions in the box, and they do NOT tell you that the firmware needs to be updated for the unit to work. Nor is it easy to find the "converter program" required for the update on Blackmagicdesign's website -- if you can FIND the website. If you DO find the website, then finding the actual updating program (that they do not tell you about) is as tough as finding the actual manual for the unit (which is hidden in the Customer Support section, which you find by clicking on a PICTURE of the converter section, which you find by tracking down the WEBSITE, which you find ONLY after you've trolled through Google for an hour or so.

Black Magic engineering documentation is a shambles.

Once you find the website (Very hard! Black Magic is a much abused name on the web.) Once you find how the system works (I had to write to them to ask -- and their answer was not much help. On the edge of snide.) Once you find the manual (non intuitive naming system -- the converter manual has ALL the converters in it -- and it goes by some weird name.) Once you find the "Updating program" and discover that the micro USB power slot is also where you plug in to update.... Once you have spent an ENTIRE DAY on this project, you MAY get it to work IF you know your Black Magic ATEM switcher well enough to realize that the SDI is some esoteric (and undefined) version of the SDI pantheon. (It puts out SDI -- but WHICH ONE? What resolution? It's actually 3G -- but it's called simply SDI with no documentation that tells what's actually going on! What frame rate? Progressive or interlace?? We had to switch the ATEM 4K switcher back and forth until magically the SDI input showed up! Then we had to reconfigure ALL THE CAMERAS IN THE STUDIO to match this wonderful little box's requirements. Not the other way around. When I left -- after a bitterly long day -- we STILL had not resolved the Hyperdeck issues caused by switching the entire system to match this little box. It records but we can't get it to play back through the system.

When all that is done, it works just fine. If you have the patience of Job, the persistence of a champion, and the ability to reset and reconfigure YOUR ENTIRE SYSTEM to match what this device can put out...

Well then go for it!

I suspect you'll rue the day you did. I sure do. I got there at six on Thursday morning and it's 2:15 AM on the following Friday. Guess what I did for 20 hours without a break?

title: Not an expert, but the film works!
text:
From what I’ve read, there are many factors that contribute to the success of an instant photo: the camera, the lighting, the temperature, the subject, how still you are when shopting, the film itself and how careful you are to keep it in the dark during its developing. That said, you will just have to try it out for yourself!

I’m new to the vintage instant camera scene, but I’ve already learned how easy it is to mess up a shot.

My only complaint is the price, but it’s not like there is any other option. Hopefully some day, they will be able to produce it more efficiently and thus cheaper. Until then... I’ll be very choosy about taking a snap.

Oh! And it might be helpful to note that my camera didn’t want to eject the film after the dark slide. To fix this, I found a resource online that suggested the following:

—Open the camera to reveal the film cartridge.

—Locate the thin, long strip of plastic (on the cartridge) right in front of where the film would come out. Just beneath this strip is a thin black Mylar sheet.

—Carefully bend back on that plastic bit to remove it. Might take a little rocking back and forth. It will snap right off.

—If the film is still not ejecting once you close up the camera and go to take another photo, you can open the camera again and fold back the little Mylar sheet to eliminate the resistance of the photo popping out. I used my nail to fold it (bend it back then fold it to keep it down and away from where the film pops out).

^I realize these pieces are there to keep the film dark and being contaminated with light, but this has caused me no problems thus far. I have done this with 3 of my vintage cameras and film. Do so at your own risk, of course!

Hope this helps. (:

title: Audiophile performance at bargain-bin price
text:
If you're an audio enthusiast that isn't wealthy, this is a must-audition. I am an audio dork but I'll keep the Stereophile-subscriber talk to a minimum - here goes...
Your DAC makes as much difference as your loudspeakers, amplifier/integrated, digital player, CD transport, cables, etc. People getting into entry-level audio (which, counterintuitively, means looking at brands most people aren't familiar with and prices they find silly), when beginning to broaden their horizons, need to ignore those who say "it's just taking the 1s and 0s and turning them back into soundwaves". Yes, that's true, but there are myriad resources online to explain crucial importance in the "how" behind DAConversion - delta-sigma vs multibit is a good place to start. You don't need to be an audio dork to get the benefit from this product. It may be one of the standout products that starts to "ruin" you for cheap, mass market audio most folks live with and find good enough. All of us audio guys and gals have a historical moment when we heard equipment that imparted a realization that there's a "next level" - first-gen PSB speakers and my first NAD 304 and 5425 were part of my epiphany.
Back to the point: your audio enjoyment, beyond your ear/brain limitations which are different for all of us, hinges on the weakest link in the chain. Unfortunately on-board DACs are frequently passable but not great. I LOVE my NAD 3020 MkII but the Schiit Modi MB absolutely, positively decimates it in terms of sound quality. Whether from my CD transport at 16/44 or from Tidal at 16/44-24/96 (and maybe 192? Not sure where Tidal is on that yet). For the novice: everything sounds "cleaner". For the audio people: the immediate and obvious differences in any type of recording (from the spare, few-instrument demo-track type recordings, to all genres of rock, to hip hop, to be-bop, and beyond) are a huge reduction in smearing and unintended sibilance vis a vis other DACs. Yes, as I listened to many genres, there were other improvements on my modest stereo setup - decay and imaging probably coming in 3rd and 4th.
It's not a magic box. I does do a far better job of transforming bits back to waves in the manner intended when the music was engineered.
The price is absurdly low. Great for then entry-level audio enthusiast, or those starting to want more than the 90% garbage sold for music playback. Even if you think you might be in the latter category, shell out the extra few bucks.
This product provides the best improvement in the DAC process that you can achieve at the price point with a few *possible* exceptions, e.g. the DragonFly v2, which has the downside of it's all in one packaging; and maybe Musical Fidelity or ProJect's low-end products if you can get them on sale or NOS.
For a stereo-based system I can't recommend this bargain enough, and I haven't even brought headphones into the equation yet, where I am sure there will be some other revelations specific to that type of reproduction vs. loudspeaker based. Absolutely excellent and not just at the price point. No MQA but, if you are MQA technology savvy, you probably aren't making any decisions based on my review here. That is a feature I'm not sold on and willing to wait a while to embrace (the unfolding part of it, anyway).
If non-portable, high-quality DAConversion is on your upgrade list, this absolutely demands an audition.
Associated equipment: NAD 3020MkII, Cambridge CXC, MacBook Air 2018 running Tidal, Vox, VLC, Wharfedale Diamond 225s on Plateau Slantbacks spiked to custom platforms, ELAC 3010 v2 sub on spikes coupled to custom feet, TrippLite Isobar 4, multiple PS Audio Noise Harvesters, AudioQuest signal and speaker cabling, lots of sorbothane, custom built audio rack with integrated isolation, significant quantities of acoustic room treatments.

title: Great For Games
text:
I got this monitor because I was playing Fortnite on a 60hz, 6 ms 4K IPS panel. The IPS panel is great for movies or art, but not great for games. I switched to this 240hz panel, and the difference is astonishing.

With my old monitor, I grinded Kovaaks FPS aim trainer for like a month and my high score was 7400 in ascended tracking v2. I was never able to beat that even after a couple more weeks of grinding.

Picked up this monitor, and my first time using Kovaaks with it I got 7300. Second time using it, I got 7700. Was happy that I beat my score and put Kovaak's down. Can't wait to see what high scores I can get with a couple of weeks of grinding on this monitor.

Also got a 10 kill dub in Fortnite. Pretty happy.

However, I'm using a dual monitor setup (this monitor on the left, old monitor on the right). This gives me an opportunity to do a side by side comparison. This monitor is a million times smoother than my old monitor, but my old monitor has vastly superior colors. The colors on this monitor are sort of strange. There are different preset color profiles you can try, but haven't found anything I really like. Maybe I'll find something if I set up a custom profile, who knows.

Colors aside, I'm glad that this has helped my game so much.

I dropped the stars down to 2 stars because this monitor has the worst stand I've ever seen in a monitor. There's a random leg in the back that stretches out like 4 inches from the back of the monitor. This means that you can't scoot the monitor very far back on your desk, it has to sit in the middle of your desk for the sake of that back leg. It wastes table space :|. Very serious design flaw.
