title: These filters fall off the camera
text:
Update:
FStop Labs, after reading my review below offered to send me another ND8 filter to replace the one that fell off my GoPro Hero 8. I received it today, and appreciate their good customer support. I revised my original rating from 1 star to 3 stars. I will continue to use these filters, and will update this review again in a month or so. I use my GoPro 8 at least 4-5 times every week, and it's always action on boats, mountain bikes, etc. It I never lose another one, I will eventually upgrade my review to 5 stars. The filters themselves are great, and they are certainly easy to take on and off the camera.

Original Review:
Seems like a great idea - design one set of filters, and then just make an adapter for each camera. The filters are oversize so they will fit cameras with bigger lenses. The adapter snaps onto the GoPro Hero 8, and is secure. The adapter is metal and the filters each have a magnetic border which allows them to snap into place onto the frame. I wondered how strong the magnets would be on an action cam where there could be a whole lotta shakin going on. Today was about my 3rd time to use one of the filters. Before taking off in the boat, my ND8 filter was on the camera. When the battery died and it was time to change it... no filter. Since the mount overhangs the boat, the filter is no doubt somewhere at the bottom of the lake.

I also use my GoPro for mountain biking on very rough trails. I didn't even try these filters in that situation because I was nervous about the magnetic hold. There is no rim around the lens adapter. Just a flat filter magnetically stuck to a flat adapter. But I thought the boat would be safe. Not so.

Unless you have your gopro mounted on a tripod I don't recommend these filters. They are not suitable for any action.

title: Great idea, not ready for prime time.
text:
This review is for the XR500.
I like how easy it is to set the GeoIP, but it doesn't always work.
The ping to the other systems is never shown, though the docs says it should be.
The interface is very slow and somewhat clunky.
The main reason I would not recommend is that it spontaneously reboots.
Netgear customer support says to downgrade the firmware, but you have to go so far back that you lose even more of the features you paid for.
The system log does not survive a reboot and there is no way to use syslogng (or something else that sends the logging data to another system so it is not lost on a reboot. You also cannot ssh into the system to monitor it to see why it is rebooting.
DumaOS customer support is much more helpful than Netgear, but they can only deal with the interface and GeoIP. The reboot problem is up to Netgear.
Until Netgear admits there is a problem and fixes the firmware I have to say buy a different router.
Connecting my computer to my Spectrum cable modem I get 110% of my 400Mbps connection. Using the XR500 speed test I would get 105% of 400Mbps. Connecting my computer to the XR500 I get 20% of 400Mbps. So something is definitely wrong with the XR500 and getting worse. I started using the Netgear X4S and I get 110% of my connection speed again and after a week I have. yet to get a reboot. Contrast to the XR500 which reboots daily and is getting worse. Maybe in a year of so they will fix the firmware, but until then I suggest you save your money and go with the X4S.

title: Fine if you do not want to use Dolby Digital
text:
When not using Dolby Digital, the sound bar is quite good. But who wouldn't want to use Dolby, right? And when you do, there is a horrible lag. I was worried it was just me, but looking into it a bit, it is obvious that this is a problem with the Klipsch soundbar in general. Klipsch uses a weak decoder for Dolby, resulting in a bad sound delay. In theory, you could overcome this by adjusting the delay on your source device, but even that doesn't work - the amount of delay varies with the source meaning you would have to adjust the delay every. time. The only alternative is to turn of Dolby altogether and use a PCM audio stream, which is inferior.
Now, don't get me wrong, this isn't a problem for everyone - if you have a small TV and bad eyes, this might be the perfect soundbar for you. But if you can see when actors mouths are moving, it's going to get really annoying that the voices aren't happening in sync with those lips.
Knowing what I know now, I would not have bought this model.

title: Beautiful picture, very happy thus far.
text:
-EDIT- About 6 months in, and this is still a fabulous monitor, I couldn't be happier. It does everything well that I wanted it to do, and then some. Highly recommended.

I like to read ebooks on my PC, so there are a few things that are important to me. 1) Picture quality. This monitor has a GREAT picture. 2) The monitor actually works. I had to send an AOC monitor back for refund prior to this one due to a permanent red line down the middle of the screen. So far so good with this one. 3) A "reader mode" to reduce blue light. Check. 4) High resolution. Check. 5) IPS display. Check. 6) I read comics too, so I need the monitor to rotate to "portrait" configuration. Check. 6) Height adjustable so I can put it on my monitor stand, and stand up when I want to. Check.

All in all I'm very happy so far, assuming it doesn't fail like the AOC I just sent back. One odd design decision, in my opinion, is the base. It's a really wide arc of plastic, almost as wide as the monitor itself. It's not a problem, so I'm not taking a star off, but I would have preferred a more utilitarian, traditional base. The base actually sticks off the edge of my monitor stand a little.

One added bonus is that you can turn off the stupid power LED on this one! Hurray! Man I got tired of my old monitor blinking at me all night.

The OSD is nice, and the multiple "split screen" modes are something I've wanted for a long time.

Oddly, the audio actually sounds better than the integrated sound from my motherboard. It's more clear, louder, etc.

Overall, A+ so far. I really can't say enough about the picture quality. Fan-tastic.

title: This bag is the shiz
text:
This bag ticks all the boxes for me. It looks good, it has zippered pouches, pouches easy to get at, it can be closed with a flap or zippered closed, and the flap has velcro that is coverable so you can open it quietly.

You all know how it is with camera bags. You'll get the greatest thing ever, but it's the wrong size. You'll find something the right size but it is missing a feature you want. Somehow you always want another bag. I've gotten a few in the last five years or so because of this and this one is higher quality than all of them.

I had a good bag from another company for years that was about this size. After 15 years the zippers failed and, frankly, it looked like a shiny nylon camera bag so I wanted to replace it. Five years back I bought a Domke bag, which is an absolute classic, and I love the look over shiny modern nylon. It's the classic 70s news reporter bag of there ever was one. But it is not protective and has no padding. The top doesn't zip closed so things can fall out -- I lost my favorite pen when my pen case fell out while on a plane -- and a velcro closed top for quick in and out is really the most convenient of modern conveniences.

I got an Amazon branded bag for cheap that closed more securely and held a laptop and it was fine for the price. But it isn't particularly good, just good for the price. I like it for travel with its computer case, and I like that its fabric rather than shiny, but it only OK overall. And it's too big for walking around locally, when I'm not carrying a computer with me and don't want to bring two spare lenses and a flashgun. I also have a couple of holsters, just big enough for the camera with the lens on it, which are wonderfully compact, but obviously limited.

Enter this badboy. It's big enough for my Z7 or 7100 wearing a lens, another lens, and acessories like a flash gun, or maybe a small prime. That's it for the camera compartment, but that's enough. There's also a hole for a tablet or whatever in the padded section, and this whole camera/tablet section can be zipped close for secure storage.

The back has a zipper closed pocket, good for storing a cellphone or something valuable when you're doing street photography where there might be pickpockets, a situation I've encountered before. The front has both zipper closed pockets and open pockets that are easily accessible. The open pocket is pretty secure as the top flap closes over it and can be velcroed down.

As mentioned above, the velcro holds the top flap securely but you can leave the camera compartment unzipped and pull it up quickly to grab the contents, or leave it zipped when you want it to be much more secure. The velcro has covers that you can put over it so you can leave it closed, but silently open it, which is great at a wedding or concert when you might want to reach into the bag and not make an obnoxious velcro ripping noise and watch the whole crowd turn around and stare at you just as the bride is about to recite her vows.

Construction is high quality. Everything looks sturdy and really well made. Even the shoulder strap is nice, and the padded part that goes over the shoulder ACTUALLY WORKS. Like, it's padded, comfortable, and stays on your shoulder where most other bags I've had might as well just be the strap, the shoulder pad is so useless.

And it looks good. To my personal aesthetic tastes.

So, I'm happy with this one. It'll see a lot of use. When the cheap Amazon bag wears out I might splurge on the bigger model for those times I need to fly somewhere for work and want to bring a laptop and my camera.

title: Tiny but wow! Better than my laptop speakers. Volume max is most surprising.
text:
You know how there are "retro" games of wooden boards/puzzles/appliances, but are in reality lacking quality once bought? This is the complete opposite! I have only used it for one hour so no clue about how long it lasts after max charge.

I bought this little speaker since my laptop has poor quality speakers. My old Bose speaker died some months ago and I did not want to buy something mediocre even after trying some demo from the local electronics stores. Lately it seems I have been bombarded with Youtubers and influencers promoting 'ok" and questionable brands speakers. I feared a bit that this cute retro one would fall into the same story of "people love it because it's ok and it's cute".

Upon opening the Amazon box I was surprised to find the actual package box was decent! The speaker was nested in the foam insert. A charger cable was attached as was a typical "nice-touch" storage pouch (although that defeats the purpose of using a speaker?).

Although it powered on after arrival, I plugged it into charge (micro usb from my own cable). After being bored of a Youtube binge and dinner I decided to test it out.

Volume Pro, Warning: I do want to say NOTE: the volume controller needs a delicate touch. From the tuner all the way down I only need to move it maybe 0.25 of an inch to play in my room at night as not to disturb others. If it was daytime and I was doing errands, washing dishes, it can be cranked up. While I would not use this for a "party" unless quite small--it can get close to as loud as the max of a "regular TV" in my opinion. That's quite amazing when you see it in person and know it's a mix of metal or wood with plastic backing!

Radio FM: It's exactly as I imagined in terms of use. The little dial turns to the FM function and the face lights up orange (and remains so). Then you turn the face tuner to change radio channels. The--signal reader--is on the top of the flat surface of the "radio box" so do not put your hand or block it or it will distort the radio sound to be "fuzzy". 5/5 in terms of wow and use and clarity. What I am not sure about is that the channels it picked up is way different than my car overall, so not sure why that is and before someone says was it AM?--based off most music stations I do not believe it was AM radio.

Bluetooth: Yes! The entire reason I bought this is to listen to my tunes clearly while doing cleaning. Left the volume dial as is and paired with my phone's Bluetooth in 3 minutes. Then I just played a song. Right now the radio is on a desk away from me, and I can just tap the side volume control from my Note 8 and lower/increase the volume from my bed! I know it sounds a bit --gee really? how's that exciting?-- Well it is for me after having the finicky Bose that died which by the way was superior in sound quality, but I'm not going to shell out money like that again. It did last a few years, but I'm no audiophile. This cute lil speaker is my new best friend while doing chores. Also while in Bluetooth the "face" will light up Blue there is no way of turning it off to my knowledge. Not a bad thing in my opinion.

Audio Quality: It's definitely good. It's not mediocre or "ok". It's actually decent/good/satisfying. Again, it's better than my laptop's speakers. It doesn't compare to my old Bose speaker or headphones, but it's not disappointing. In fact it's "that" good I will consider purchasing it as gifts!

Other positive bits to know: There are two little feet that you can peel the plastic off to provide some "grip". I like to slide the radio (though that's a bit risky) on my desk so I left the plastic on. Mine came with a little wrist strap cord? It should be removable. I like that it's kind of like a tail so I left it on for now. Maybe the wrist strap is for use outdoors to loop the radio "safe" over a pole? I don't advise it, but---it's possible maybe? I'm not sure why someone would hold the speaker in their hands and use the strap wrist that way.

Build/Color: It looks exactly like the picture. I purchased the "Cherry" color wood. I think it is really wood? It's really smooth and you cannot tell if it is molded wood pulp. The back Aux is easy to access and so is the charge port. I hope this device lasts longer than my Bose...anyway for the price it would be a fantastic Christmas gift or birthday gift.

Possible Cons:
1. I don't know the battery life after max charge is true to the "9 hours" claim
2. People need to know to charge their radio with a micro USB. I think that task doesn't register based off some negative reviews I read. There is no quick battery replacement only micro USB charge.
3. The front is identical to the pictures, but know that at least for the "cherry wood" I bought, the back is clean and smooth, but black plastic casing is exposed. The wood does NOT wrap around the entire body! If you buy this please know that in case you expected it to fully cover or if you don't want guests to see that for whatever reason.
4. The charge port light indicator is a bit dumb as it is located below the insertion point. Meaning you cannot see the indicator light status unless you lift up and look or somehow coming from a lower angle. Minor annoyance. I can live with it.

As an underwater photographer I need to free up my memory cards for each dive. With this unit I upload my picture files to my laptop, then to the SP drive. I bought the first one after my camera was stolen ( I work a lot in 3rd world countries) and I lost the last day of pictures which could never be replaced. I now use it as storage for my older laptop and use the new 2TB one for storage on my newer machine. These are military grade, a little larger than a pack of smokes, and have no moving parts to break. They are rugged and small to pack. Why would you risk someone hacking your files from the cloud when you have a better, safer alternative? 5 Stars all the way!!!

title: Great Line In device
text:
This product worked as expected and exceeded my expectations. While you can use it to record off of record players (or anything with a 3.5mm or RCA jack), I used it to listen to my Nintendo Switch's Game Audio (Super Smash Brothers Ultimate!) while having a Discord call open on my computer. It works without having to use the drivers on the CD and comes with useful accessories, such as the female to female 3.5 mm adapter and the coaxial to RCA Left/Right audio adapter

The audio may initially sound distorted or bass-boosted when you first plug it in, but all you have to do is go into the Sound Control Panel>Recording>Right-click on the device> Properties>Levels, and adjust the volume there until the distortion goes away (somewhere between 50-75). After setting that, the audio will be clean and clear with no humming or buzzing introduced by the adapter. To listen to the device while its playing audio, go into the Sound Control Panel>Recording>Right-click on the device> Properties>Listen and click Listen to this Device.

This is significantly better than Nintendo's offering, with the drawback that it won't work with phones, but if you use your computer to chat anyways this a worthy investment. It's also really useful if you find a record or cassette tape that has songs you would like to make digital.

Note: The software bundled with the drivers (Audacity) is a free program. If you are recording audio, I would recommend downloading the latest version off of the Audacity website (google it!). If this is the default recording device (denoted by a green check mark in the Sound Control Panel >Recording) then it could be possible to use the built-in voice recorder in windows 10, however it wouldn't offer as many settings as Audacity.

title: Can't wait for V2.0!
text:
UPDATE:

Firmware bug causes 4k60 footage to revert to 1080P... HALF MY GRANDD CANYON FOOTAGE WAS SWITCHED TO 1080P

READ THE DJI FORUMS... IT IS JUNK

I HATE THIS PRODUCT NOW

I bought this camera for a trip to the Grand Canyon. Two years ago, I used my Note 4 on a gimbal and got good results, but it was overly cumbersome to hit the trail with this large gear... so I used the combo less than I thought I would.

Fast forward to this years 30 mile hike, now I have an Osmo Pocket. I literally did NOT have enough time to play around with the OP, before the trip, so I had to rely on pc-less QA of my videos. I forced myself to use the OP in stand-alone mode without connecting my Note8. Luckily I had the latest firmware at the time that allowed PRO mode switching without tethering a phone. The results were mostly good! This camera is pretty easy to use. There is a walking bump like many show on social media... it is avoidable to an extent by "ninja walking" or using perhaps a selfie stick... hey, I'm on a 30 mile trek... I'm not ninja walking with a multi-day pack on!

Personally, tethering a phone to the USB-C (or lightning) connector is a bit of a pain for "run-and-gun" shooting. Might as well just use an Osmo and your cell phone. I chose stand-alone mode for most of the trip.

So, I set out to see the world through a postage-stamp sized screen, and at times, it disappointed, at others, it shined. I purchased a set of ND filters, fearing the colors would be all washed out during the day, but color issues only happened using in D-Cinelike in PRO mode. In fact, the cinelike colors are OK, not over-saturated, maybe a bit un-saturated to my taste.

The ND filters are a waste IMHO. One of mine fell off within 4 hours of testing. I simply didn't use another.

The PRO mode might be best used while tethering. You can set WB and exposure (including auto for both) as well as manual shutter speed, but there's something wrong with the colors if you don't set PRO mode up correctly, and in changing light, you have to re-adjust it (That is normal with any manual mode, BTW). The tiny screen is almost useless in this regard, so stick to standard mode if un-tethered. PRO mode really helped at night, allowing me to set ISO to 1600 (grainy, but watchable)

Standard mode gave me surprisingly good results in all day-lighting conditions, with or without ND filter attached. At night, it was kind of a miss, so switch to PRO mode for night time. I think the OP is supposed to detect night somehow, maybe this feature isn't ready yet.

I tried one Motionlapse. You need the phone tethered for set up only, you may disconnect and let the camera do it's thing, which is a good thing. I used a 2m USB-C M-F extension cable for this. I was able to "jack in" occasionally to check up on the status. There are many things lacking in motionlapse, like variable shutter, more precise timing controls, and maybe a "preview sweep" before you commit... I found out that in the app, there is a "save original frames" feature in Motionlapse "pro-mode", you can use something like Virtualdub on your PC to load the frames in for editing. Also, Pro mode frame recording gives you UHD-size, not the 1080P output of Motionlapse... Excellent option, DJI!

Hand-Held timelapse does not work, always use a tripod.

The panorama function is cool, just make sure to use the app to stitch before copying your SD to your workflow. It sounds like a pain, maybe it is, but I did not mind that extra step. The two panorama modes are fine. in no way is this a 360 degree camera, so, don't expect a spherical panorama on this. Use a 360 camera for that.

I wish this thing built in a joystick for pan and tilt. The screen kind of has a tilt control, it's awful, and consistently, I got "you cannot perform this function while recording" errors came up when attempting to tilt, ruining my shot entirely. For this... you guessed it... add a cumbersome and expensive add on. Now the pan/tilt add on might be nice... there is no way to tuck the OP into it's protective case with it on... WTF DJI? I won't buy that.

Focal distance is not as wide as a GoPro. I actually see it as a trade-off. Selfie mode seems a little tight, but is OK, while landscapes wish to be zoomed in a bit more! I like the choice here. I don't remember the equivalent distance in mm off-hand, but I see it as more of a 35-40mm full-frame. Definitely a little wider than a 50mm portait. A small optical zoom of maybe 3x would be absolutely stunning, but make the device larger, and that's OK with me! I suppose the F stop would be slower with zoom than the current bright F2.0 however...

WIFI/BT... need an attachment... WTF again DJI. I won't buy it.

I did buy a 3rd party USB-C tripod adapter that works great for motionlapse on tripod and handheld slo-mo on selfie sticks. It also has the ability to charge the OP with a battery bank if desired. If you use a tripod, you can connect the OP to your phone via extension cable for remote control. Pretty neat.

Video Qaulity: So, UHD at 100mbps sounds great, right? wrong. I compared the shots to my Panasonic ZS-100 (1" sensor compact camera with zoom). The Panny crushes the OP in image quality at same resolution and bitrate, no comparing the two. However, the OP crushes the Panny in rolling shutter artifacts and image stabilization. It seems like a trade-off. Honestly, my Note8 has better video quality then the OP, but again, my phone lacks mechanical stabilization, and that is a deal-breaker. OP wins!

Battery life: It's OK. I shot an entire day with it and only connected a battery bank for my motionlapse, just in case. Android has this reverse-charging thing with USB, so I blame the OS, and not DJI for the Android issue. I can't comment if Apple has this issue or not. It's no big deal to me, but I do see how it would irritate some. Again, I put blame on Android for the charging issue that drains the OP battery. Use Wifi, and it solves the problem, unless you need to transfer files. You cannot remove the battery. This is a product for 1 year and then hack it, I suppose.

Speaking of file transfer... I wish this thing incorporated a thumbnail cache. If you reconnect your phone with a hundred files on it, the app just sits there blank... no "loading" banner, nothing. You might think your connection is lost or something until magically, 4 minutes later, your media apears. If you lose connection for a split second (happens when directly tethered for me anyway) you have to re-cache the thumbnails. ARRGH what a PITA. File transfer is quick, at about 10 megabytes per second when tethered via USB-C.

Story Mode... OK, this could be a great feature if you could use a laptop. You can't. So... you better have a 512GB cell phone capacity to load a multi-day shoot into your phone to make a quick video for family and friends. There is a way to do a story mode as you capture, I'm confused either way, I just don't know what I am doing here. I don't think Story Mode is for me. I fell like my workflow should go into my i7 laptop with 1TB storage and let the laptop app do up a quick recap story for me, not shuffle files to my phone, where storage is more precious. I think shooting in story mode effectively takes the burden off your external device, but I see it infringing on manual video settings and other issues... I'll leave this one to the Story Mode pro's, I am just confused hahaha!

The button taps for centering (2) and selfie (3) are intuitive and clever. I love that feature.

I wish you could simply hold the record button to snap a photo, while tap to start/stop record. For now, you have to change modes, which while hiking, can be a little annoying, especially the tiny screen and big fingers, causing you to set the wrong mode.

SLO-MO: This feature really shines on the OP. My biggest gripe is the auto-focus really sucks for a shot ranging from close to far and vice-versa. You can't do a macro to wide pan for instance. In general terms, the slo-mo is neat, and i WISH it was in UHD! Why not? I bet the SOC could do it. Perhaps V2.0... Anyway, slow mo is fun and easy to do with great results in 1080P.

60FPS UHD: This is niiiice. I used 30fps for some footage and it looked choppy on my 60Hz PC monitor. A lot of video seems to look jittery to me, but the 60FPS stuff all looks smooth. You definitely see compression artifacts, however. A larger sensor and possibly higher bitrate would alleviate this to a degree.

V2.0: OK, my wish-list...
1. PTZ Joystick and not a virtual screen control (yes, 3x optical zoom would be awesome, like the Osmo+)
2. Larger screen and larger device (DJI could still make this pocket-able)
3. Built in WiFi/BT
4. Larger image sensor (not looking for 1", but something larger will help)
5. AI to soften the "walking bump" (If DJI included a 5k sensor, they could use portions to smooth the bumps, and still make it UHD)
6. UHD Slow-Mo and Time/Motionlapse
7. Built-in tripod screw mount!
8. Waterproof housing accessory (not available yet)
9. One switchable ND filter built-in? Yes please :)
10. GEOTAGGING - Yes Please!

Overall, I am pleased with this device. I say BRAVO to DJI for putting out a revolutionary product! I hope future firmware updates improve this little guy while DJI works on a bigger and better model. I will say that it is easily pocketable, and almost un-noticable to carry around a long day in a city. I really like it.

title: Best value for under $50 (when it's on sale)
text:
Title says all.

The other reviews will tell you most of what you really need to know, so I'll just add a few caveats, things the manual does not state:

(1) Advertised battery life is 15 hours, as long as you don't use lights or extra bass. In my practical day to day experience, in the way I use it, for occasions when I really want some volume, (meaning it's not my normal day to day BT speaker), I get 10 hours.

(2) Speaking of the extra bass, they really shouldn't have called it "extra" bass, and merely called it "bass." It's because, even if you set your source material's EQ curve or present to be bassy, there won't really be any out of this speaker with the "extra" bass button off. You'll need to have it on in order to have any bass.

(3) The sounds that sound like telephone busy signals, two each spaced out from time to time, are the low battery indicator, and in my estimation, they seem to start when battery life is at 1%. That is one of my pet peeves about many BT speakers, that they start whatever their battery life is low warning is, way too soon, circa 15% battery life left. And sometimes, said warning is intrusive, and interferes with whatever you're listening to. This device starts the warning at the correct interval, IMHO, at 1% left, and does not much interfere with what you're listening to.

(4) It's pretty big, with decent materials, especially along the right and left facing sides. It is actually heavier than it looks.

(5) I generally find the lighting schemes to be cheesy, but every once in awhile, with the right song, they can be entertaining.

(6) Overall sound quality is not the best, even among BT speakers I own, and I don't own any expensive ones. But that's to be expected for the price point. It does get plenty loud.

title: Significantly Faster Than Original
text:
Finally the speed we have all been waiting for! I have been a TicWatch owner for some time now. I have owned the TicWatch E and then moved up to the original TicWatch Pro. I have used the original pro for well over a year now and I am happy to say the New TicWatch Pro 3 is a breath of fresh air.

While the original wasn't bad, the new model solves many annoyances. The biggest issue was always speed and UI smoothness. The moment I started to configure my new watch the difference was dramatic to me. The interaction with the UI is very smooth and free of hiccups.

To be honest I resorted to rooting my original pro watch, flashing a custom rom, adding a few tweaks to help make it run a bit smoother. All while also having the animations turned off. Even comparing the new pro to my rooted original pro, the difference is still very apparent.

The appearance of the new TicWatch Pro 3 is overall similar to the original. It has a noticeable reduction in weight, it's slightly slimmer, but the biggest change is to the under side where you can see the crazy amount of new sensors compared to the original TicWatch Pro. I will just outright say it, this is not the smallest watch in the world. To me personally I like a larger watch and display size, but I can see it bothering some.

There are a few other areas of improvement, the mic is slightly better. The speaker is also a bit more cleaned up now. The UI now allows apps in the app drawer to be dragged and dropped and placed in what ever order you like. Speaking of apps, I have been testing the new sleep monitoring app. Overall I'm impressed at how well it actually monitors your movements at night. It definitely does a nice job giving you a picture of what you're doing while you sleep, I think it's very interesting. The new SPO2 app and its monitoring features are also very well done. I have yet to find any issues, everything is very seamless.

I do believe the apps are all more impressive and less clunky feeling because of the speeds the watch is capable of now. I used to worry about having too many things monitoring in the background, because I felt it would kill my battery or made the watch slowdown too much. That worry is gone now and the watch is able to run whatever task I toss at it without hesitation.

My overall take on this watch is this version feels very refined. It has everything it should to complete or even top other smart watches in the market. This new watch compared to its predecessor has enough significant improvements that I can say with confidence even if the price of the original TicWatch Pro drops dramatically this new one is worth the extra. It will most definitely give you a better overall Android smart watches experience and you will enjoy it, I have no doubt.

title: Buy this mount!
text:
I've installed three television mounts in the last few months in my house and I've learned a lot in that process. I installed a 50 inch Samsung television in my living room using a mount I got from Target, a Sanus mount. It was decent but incredibly expensive and the way the television mounted to the mount wasn't confidence inspiring. Recently I wanted to install another 50 inch Samsung in the bedroom and I looked to Amazon for a cheaper, better, and quickly arriving mount.

Enter the Mounting Dream. Now let's start by saying people don't usually get excited about television mounts and the name "Mounting Dream" is fairly cheesy - let's be honest. But yet, I'm a believer in the name now and am thrilled with this product.

The mount is very quality construction, doesn't feel cheap and not excessively heavy. The way it mounts the TV feels very secure and is confidence inspiring when hanging tons of money on the wall. The kit came with everything I needed. In fact, the bolts were too long and I prepared to go to Lowes to get appropriate screws when I noticed they included tons of different size spacers - problem solved and they worked perfectly! (The Sanus from Target did not have various spacers included). Additionally, it came with a level, HDMI cables, a template to stick on the wall and that really helped. No one likes buying a home project only to find they don't have a tool or piece needed to finish it and begrudgingly heading out to Lowes. Everything in this kit is thought through smartly to avoid just that.

I cannot recommend this product enough and what made me decide to purchase this was the insane amount of 5 star reviews and I'm happy to see why there were so many and add another 5 stars myself. Great quality, excellent price, and all the necessary tools needed to do the job (including a level and HDMI cables, come on!) Do yourself a favor and buy this mount!

title: I've tried many security camera systems. This is the one!!
text:
My criteria for security cameras is as follows:
1) Good quality picture
2) Triggers at good distances
3) Records videos locally (no monthly fee and privacy)
4) Low number of false triggers
5) A good phone app to control the cameras and view the videos.
6) A reasonable price

The Zeeporte camera checks all of the above boxes.

I'll start here by saying that I've tried Eufy 2C, Vava, and Blink X2C systems. They are all more expensive (and sometimes much more expensive) than the Zeeporte. But the Zeeporte is a superior system to all that I've tried so far.

The battery life of this camera is decent. I've used it heavily over the past 6+ days with many tests. I've recorded 209 motions and it is at 89%. Since I've used it heavily, I'll estimate 10% per week which means that it'll last 10 weeks (2.5 months) on a charge. In regards to size of the memory card that you'll need, I've used .22GB of the 120 GB card that I bought. At the current rate, it will record for 1.5 years before getting full - and then I'll just reset it. It is easy to transfer clips to your phone storage (online for my iphone).

When I did my testing, I set it to the motion detection sensitivity to the highest value (95). What really impresses me with this camera is the low number of false triggers.. Really, I get none. It records people and cars and that is it. And it does not seem to miss any events. The angle of the camera did affect the distance of the triggering so try different angles.

The only area of improvement that I can see is the mount. It is fine, but as I noted in my headline, I've tried several brands now including Eufy, Vava, and Blink. All of these brands had superior mounts, but the one that Zeeporte mount is fine. I had to make sure I tightened it well. One note - the other manufacturers that I listed require base stations and do not record on the camera itself. The Zeeporte does. This means if someone steals your camera, then they will get your videos. So, just don't put your camera within reach. A camera should not be mounted low and the instructions tell you to not do so. This is probably another reason that Zeeporte does not have a magnetic mount.. which would make it easy to steal. The mount that it has requires you to screw it off.

Oh.. I just remembered another great feature of the Zeeporte. After your day is finished, you can view the events for the day (and all prior days) in a mode that shows you a timeline and lets you quickly sweep to each event based on the time and watch it. This is really nice to have!

Overall, I do recommend it 100%

title: Not a good TV if you're sensitive to motion, also Ghosting issues
text:
Let's start with the positive aspects... The tv has surprisingly good contrast, colors and deep blacks, especially for the price no other tv can beat it. Also the input lag in game mode is excellent.

Now the not so positive aspects... The tv supports HDR but can't display it well, so it might as well not have it since it makes the image look worse. The image response time is awful with duplication, has ghosting with dark colors and movies in particular suffer with a lot of judder and the only way to fix it is with Motion Plus but it makes the video look weird (soap opera effect). Also the viewing angle are some of the worst I have ever seen on an LCD TV. If you aren't right in the middle the image looks washed out.

In conclusion the TV has good contrast and colors and low input lag but the motion handling is simply awful, thus making the tv bad for watching movies, bad for gaming, bad as a PC monitor... Honestly if I could I would return it since my 5 years old Samsung is way better than this. This tv is only good for sports, since colors there tend to always be bright, and for watching the news and that's it. The low input lag is wasted on this tv.

title: pleasant, balanced, layered
text:
I also have the 9500 model. As open backed models, they provide a nice large soundstage with good layering of the elements. What is the difference between them? Where the 9500 goes for utmost clarity by accentuating the treble, the 9600 is smoother and has more meatiness to the music. The mids are more forward on the 9600 providing a more balanced musical experience. The 9500's are perfectly fine when listening to sparse music with only a few instruments, such as jazz or folk. But I find the 9600's better suited for more complex and involved music such as prog rock or classical.
Update: I've had them now for four months with daily use. After a month or so, they really open up and become spacious. There is good texture in the mids, whereas the SHP 9500 and even the X2HR are a bit anemic there. Aside from music, they are great for movie watching. Of course, at this price they are not going to be as durable as a much more expensive set. And I've seen some people complain that they leak sound; that is the very nature of open back headphones. But I've come to appreciate these inexpensive, yet lovely sounding headphones.

title: Mixed...
text:
Edits at the bottom....

Decided that I wanted to upgrade my RT-AC5300 to AX and make use of both routers in a Mesh configuration.

The latest official release 384_5979 still has IPv6 issues (reported on various online groups as well) and Fusion VPN is not working (can activate the VPN but clients do not use the VPN when associated with it). I installed the latest Beta that I have seen 384_6156 and IPv6 appears fixed but still have issues with Fusion VPN. (Fully reset via the WPS button before testing). The issue with Fusion is my only complaint but its a major one at this time (since it's a key feature). I will state that the Beta firmware looks better visually that the latest official firmware due to the text being 'normal' sized on the left menu options (vs over-sized on the official release).

I did have issues peering the RT-AC5300 as a Mesh Node. It would get to 99% and then fail. I tried the reset button method to reset it, but it still would fail. But, after a full reset (using the WPS button as per ASUS hard reset instructions) it finished with no issues and has been working well.

It should also be noted that if you are running the Mesh in either Wireless or Wired mode, you will lose the 5G-2 channel. I have heard discussion that a firmware upgrade may allow 5G-2 use if connecting the Mesh as a wired link, but not confirmed or guaranteed. For my setup, using wireless as the Mesh connection works fine.

Also, currently Merlin Firmware has no official plans to support the GT-AX11000 router and you have to use OEM firmware for Mesh functionality (so I had to remove the Merlin from the RT-AC5300). Fingers crossed for a future Merlin release for both that supports Mesh.

Rating support as a two due to lack of response to my inquiry about the Fusion issue yet, a three for Value for the broken Fusion functionality, and four for wifi signal (it appears to be solid throughout my large home with significant wifi interference from neighbors that do not understand band management).

EDIT: After a lack of support from ASUS (other than creating a new case each time I responded to them with some new bit of information), I was able to fix my Fusion issue. Per the logs on the device via telnet (not the gui), I was able to identify remenents of my older configs when testing release versions. I followed ASUS's procedure to hard reset the device 3 times in a row and then rebuilt the config from scratch, testing each component. It works as expectd now (while in a MESH and with all the bells and wistles turned on. I'm not going to raise my rating though because this should have been addressed with working with support....not my piecing together posts from forums and usergroups on OpenVPN.

Edit 2: Days later, still having issues. VPN settings are only partially working. Some devices are using it, some are ignoring the settings and using default. So still buggy.

Edit 3: Still no response from their tech support team after a week.

Edit 4: After escalation via their CEO line, I was advised that the "Research and Development team were unable to find anything abnormal with the log and files provided in your submission." Yet, here are the error messages in the log provided:

Jun 19 22:34:39 vpnclient5[2430]: WARNING: Failed running command (--route-up): external program did not exit normally

Never received any contact except the statement that nothing could be found and still have the issue with only select hosts routing over the VPN regardless of the VPN settings under the Fusion VPN GUI. Adjusting to 1 star until Asus actually starts attempting to resolve the issue.

Edit 5: Finally got somewhere with Asus through persistence. Worked with the overseas programmers and tested several beta versions including some not ready for prime time (although I can confirm they are indeed working on a WPA3 version). We finally identified the issue with Fusion VPN (it would only support half of the statically bound hosts - 33 to be exact). They fixed the code and all hosts are now working as expected. I'm still having significant WiFi issues when using AiMesh. It will work for a few hours then throughput will slow to 10% of normal. It also looses the ability to reach devices (ping, print, etc) on the Mesh Node until the Mesh node is rebooted. However, if I turn off AiMesh and set the node (in my case the RT-AC5300) as a repeater, it works flawless and never looses connectivity nor speed.

I also identified an issue with reaching amazon.com during surfing related to DNS handling. At this time, I do not know if it was fully related to DNS or if it tied into AiMesh. But with my AX11000 set to use my provider's DNS (under WAN) and manually setting my remotes (under LAN DHCP) to my 3rd party DNS (1.1.1.1), it's working. HOWEVER: You can only set the primary DNS entry under the LAN setting. Secondary defaults to the router/gateway. Note:I am currently using 9.0.0.4.384_6332 beta firmware.

So, I will raise my rating back to a 3 for now. I would give it a 4 if AiMesh worked as advertised. I will not give a 5 until they fixed DNS/Mesh, added the secondary DNS server to LAN DHCP, and allowed you to sort static bindings by IP.

Edit 6: New firmware 3.0.0.4.384_6436 seems to have corrected the AiMesh issue. Still testing DNS but still only single DNS server under LAN DHCP. Stable for the last week so raising back up to a 4. Note: New bug identified with this version....If your host is mapped to the VPN, the bandwidth monitor shows both downstream and upstream traffic as upstream. If you aren't mapped to a VPN, it reports it normally. That said, it's minor.

title: Totally awesome home theater projector
text:
I'm a big home theater nut, and I've been through maybe four generations of home theater projectors. With every generation, the picture gets better and the price drops. Last year, I had the pleasure of testing the Epson 4010 and I was really impressed with the overall quality at that price point, so I was definitely eager to try out Epson's newer 5050 to see if it pushed the envelope even further. I'm happy to say that for the most part, the 5050 exceeded my expectations in nearly every way, and it's managed to earn a spot in my home theater, replacing my older JVC, Sony and even the wonderful Epson 4010. The 5050 is easily the best projector under $10,000 I have ever witnessed.

First, let me repeat something from my review of the 4010...

If you're used to Epson's compact business projectors, the 5050 might be a surprise in terms of sheer size - it's huge. Because of my experience with the 4010 (which is similarly huge), I wasn't surprised, but if you're expecting the size of a projector you might see in an office meeting room, you'll be surprised. You'll want to give a lot of thought to how you mount the projector, and obviously anything you use needs to be heavy-duty. The picture quality the 5050 is capable of deserves a rigid, rock-solid mount so as not to be muddying the picture with small vibrations. I use a motorized Da-Lite mount rated for 300 pounds - it was perfect for the 4010, and it's also a perfect fit for the 5050.

Other than mounting, the rest of the setup is pretty easy. If this is your first projector, you'll want to align it to your screen as perfectly as you can. Yes, there are keystone controls and so on, but truth is, you get the best picture quality from any projector when it's precisely in alignment with your screen.

Choice of a screen is an interesting decision too. Since I've had older projectors that aren't as bright as the 5050, I invested in a 120" Black Diamond screen a few projectors back...it has fairly high gain, wonderful contrast and helps reject ambient light in a brighter room. With my 1800 lumen JVC projector, this high-end screen was necessary, and while it looks amazing with the Epson 5050, I think the picture quality from the Epson is high enough that you could get by with just about any decent screen. Still, if you're looking for the absolute best picture quality, don't overlook the screen...the Epson 5050 has the goods to put an amazing picture on a top quality screen.

Once firmly mounted and paired with a high quality projection screen, the rest of the setup is simple. The lens can be adjusted from the remote (zoom as well as focus), and the relatively wide zoom range from the excellent Fujinon 16-element lens (22.5mm - 46.7mm...a 2.1x range) makes it easy to precisely fill your screen from any reasonable projection distance. There are plenty of inputs, and the HDMI is high-speed 18Gbps on the 5050, so you can use high-speed cables with video input having 4.2.2 or 4.4.4 chroma subsampling. If you have older HDMI cables, they might not handle the faster speeds...it's worth an upgrade if you're on ten-year old cables like I was - a high-speed HDMI cable made quite a difference since it's the key to 4K 60fps HDR video.

Fine-tuning the picture was fairly straightforward as well. I have a calibration meter, and in truth, the projector was a fairly good fit for my environment out of the box. The presets were pretty close to what I'd choose for myself, and with a few tweaks, I found it an easy projector to get the color, brightness and sharpness to be spot-on. This projector supports some of the newer HDR modes, including HDR10 and HLG, and although there aren't too many things to calibrate, it's definitely worth trying these modes as you're setting up the projector. On a technical note, I notice the 5050 is better than the 4010 at reproducing the full DC3 P3 color gamut...the 4010 was about 96% in green and blue, and about 92% in red. The 5010 hits 100% in RGB.

The 5050 also supports a number of 3D modes...I didn't try any of them as I'm not a big 3D fan.

With any projector, fan noise is always an issue in a quiet theater. I'm happy to say that, like the 4010, the 5050 has quite reasonable fan noise. It's audible if you stand within a few feet of the projector, but it's subdued enough that you barely can hear it from anything more than 5-6 feet away.

The 5050UBe model includes an innovative 4K wireless projection module that frankly seemed too good to be true, but it is a wonderful addition. With this little puppy, you just connect your HDMI sources to a single wireless module and there's no need at all to connect even a single cable to the projector itself. I was skeptical that it wouldn't introduce lag or reduce picture quality, but except in a few very minor circumstances, I can't see much difference between the image sent over the cable, and the image sent wirelessly. It's definitely convenient versus hard-wired cables to the projector.

Note that lag can be an issue depending where you connect the wireless module. Originally, I had it in the signal path just on the HDMI connection out of my AV receiver, and there was notable lag. By moving the wireless transmitter "up the food chain" so that it's output went on the input side of my AV equipment, the lag is much, much less.

The remote works well and has all the controls you need to operate the projector. I have a Logitech Harmony setup connected with Amazon Alexa, so I rarely use the Epson remote. I had this same setup on the 4010, and I'm happy to say that most of it worked unchanged with the 5050.

Of course, the real test of any projector is the image quality you see on the screen, and this is where the Epson really shines. With good quality 4K content, the images from the 5050 are about the best I've seen in my home theater, and I've owned and auditioned projectors that cost more than five times what this Epson does.

With a good Blu-ray test disc, the Epson displays razor-sharp and uniformly bright patterns from the center of the screen to the corners. Colors are vivid and saturated, black levels are excellent for a projector, and contrast is sharp and punchy. Compared to the older 4010, I'd say that there's a very notable improvement, partly because the image is brighter overall (2600 lumens versus 2400), and partly because the 5010 seems to produce better contrast and blacker blacks. The HDR mode and 18Gbps HDMI - which gives you 4K 60 fps HDR at 4.4.4 chroma subsampling - probably helps too.

Some reviewers debate whether 4K native is better than pixel-shifting solutions. Having seen both up close, I'd say a lot depends on size of the screen and viewing options. On my 120" screen, I'm not sure I'm able to see a difference...indeed, if I wanted a better projector, it would probably be to get a brighter image, not to get anything sharper by going native. In my office, we have a $60,000 Sony VPL-VW5000ES - that's a native 4K laser projector that puts 5000 lumens on a 250" screen. While I'd love to have those 5000 lumens, I'm not sure the additional sharpness of native 4K versus the pixel-shifting technology on the Epson 5050 makes a difference on the smaller screen in my theater.

I also had an opportunity to compare the Epson to some of the other similarly priced units from BenQ and others, and I believe in most any side-by-side comparison, the Epson is a clear winner at this price point. For me, not until you get to the $15K and up price level are there projectors I'd consider as hands-down winners over the Epson 5050, and that's saying a lot. As you move up the price curve, most of what you'll get is more brightness - important on giant screens or in areas with high ambient light levels, but it's not a major impact in a dark room with maybe a 100-120" screen. As with a lot of high-end products, there's always something better out there if you're willing to invest five times more money, but sooner or later, it gets to be a case of diminishing returns. To my eye, the Epson 5050 gives about 95% the performance you'll find in a $20K projector, and honestly, I'd rather spend this difference on better screens, light treatments, better audio and so forth.

Last year, I loved the 4010 and for the price, I still think it's a great product. This year, I'm finding the somewhat more expensive 5050 to be a worthwhile successor, and truly, if it's in your budget, I don't think you'll find a better option at anywhere near the price. This is one product I have no trouble at all giving my highest recommendation - it's definitely worth a try if you want a top-quality home theater projector without breaking the bank.

title: Life is short, fragile and precious. Toys are not made to be perfect, but played with. So have fun.
text:
I have been using the Edifier NB2 TWS earbuds for 5 days now, and here are my thoughts.

Overall review point is:

This is how you upgrade a product to the next level. You don’t tinker around the edges. Edifier has really stepped there game up with there NB2 TWS noise cancellation earbuds, both in form and function. But most importantly in quality and value for the dollar. What does that mean to a consumer like myself? It means that what is offered in form and function is of equal or higher value than much higher price equipment. That’s my definition of high quality and high value for your hard earned dollar.

So imagine with me, using the Edifier NB2 TWS for 5 days, back and forth to work and NOT knowing the price. If I was told they were $200.00 dollars US. I would say, I can see that. But knowing they are $99.00 US dollars ( with a 10% discount coupon as I write) the Edifier NB2 TWS noise canceling earbuds are almost to good to be true. My review is based on the quality and value of what you are getting for your $99.00 or $89.00 dollar purchase. It is not based on what is missing from the earbuds. It’s a fairly common practice these days to White glove a product, even the really good ones to death with phrases like “deal killer” if the item does not have one feature or another. Or we don’t like the Oder or sequence of how the Manufacture has implemented something. I am off my soapbox.

The Sound:

I loved how the original Edifier NB TWS were tuned. One reviewer said it best by describing the sound as "tube amp" sounding, warm, rich, detailed without any overly sharp edges. Plus the vocals on the original Edifier NB TWS were seductive. Was any of this accurate musically, of course not. But who cared with a sound so rich, deep and warm from a pair of TWS wireless earbuds. The new Edifier NB2 TWS are not tuned this way. I would say it’s sound is more like very Hi-End transistors verses tube equipment. Yes there is definitely warmth and richness, but there are faster more energetic swings of Highs & lows with slam at the end of notes that the original NB’s could not keep up with. The new NB2 sound more open and alive, but still with that Edifier magical warmth in the mids, bass and most importantly sub bass. There is a noticeable step up in sound clarity and volume level with the new NB2.

Active Noise Cancelation:

The ANC is definitely better on the new Edifier NB2’s than the original NB TWS. More noise is blocked out for sure, and you can feel it when it kicks in. Music will sound good with and without ANC activated, but I like the ANC on all the time. It just sounds better to me with it on. Commuting is great with ANC when you need to block out the chatter you don’t want to here. This is a quality ANC upgrade, not just some thrown in ANC to check a box.

Ambient Sound Mode:

Here again the Edifier NB2 gives you a noticeable quality and value upgrade over the original NB TWS. It’s the best one I’ve used so far, and it has a sliding bar for you to raise or lower the intensity of the ambient level. I was in a UBER recently and the driver was playing something I didn’t want to here, but I had to stay in contact with him to get to were I was going. So I had my music playing loud enough not to here his music and had the ambient setting so I could still hear and talk to him, it was great. And the slider really works well. And even on the lowest setting it is noticeable over having none on at all. A well thought out Quality upgrade.

Phone Call Quality:

The phone quality is better than my Apple AirPods. People sound like I’m in a old school phone operator booth. I have been told I sound crystal clear and full sounding as well. This Level of improvement over the original NB TWS I did not expect. But with a clean natural voice call with it's much improved mics and extra volume headroom, I can talk inside and outside with no issues. Another quality upgrade.

Optional Features etc... :

I like that if I pull a earbud out the music will stop. And when I put it back in the music will pick back up. Yes my Sennheiser Momentums TWS do this flawlessly without the Edifier's NB2 slight pause. I also like that I can disable this feature in the Edifier APP. I do like that there is an APP for firmware upgrades and changing some features and Edifier adding some features if they choose.

I love the styling of the new Edifier NB2 TWS over the original NB. They don’t look clunky like the originals. I think they are very stylish and low profile, which does matter to me. This product is Edifier not tinkering around the edges, but looking and surveying the landscape they are in. And listening to there customer base as well by continuing to provide both quality and value to the consumer. Big ups for the design upgrade to the Edifier NB2. There is also a touch sensitivity level in the APP for the touch control on the earbuds themselves. The sensitivity level can be adjusted to avoid accidental or unwanted action to take place.

Battery life is really good, since I use ANC all day with the volume almost all the way up. I get close to 5 hours, plus there is a quick charge feature on the earbuds. This long review should let you know I really really like the Edifier NB2 TWS earbuds for what they have and bring to the table plus the quality and value that comes in this little box. Perfect earbuds, of course not (what is). But what is missing I can and have easily navigated past. Enjoy more music, it helps to drown out all the noise.

title: Wired client speeds slow down over time - must reboot
text:
I've had this almost a month now, and it replaces a Netgear R8000P that died on me. I liked the Netgear, but it had significant issues after just over a year (failed wifi on 2.4ghz main wifi, VPN server never was stable, and finally required constant reboots to remain connected to internet which was its death to me) thus requiring replacement.

So far, what I like about the C5400x: 8 LAN ports, good wifi strength, stable VPN server.

What I don't like: WAN TO LAN speeds are reduced for an unknown reason after a day or so for WIRED clients.
I have gigabit fiber to the house, and work from home so the speeds are needed for my job for what I do. What I noticed thus far is that there is no way to turn off QOS on this device, and for whatever unknown reason, Wired LAN to WAN speeds will reduce to the 350Mbps range after a couple/few days thus requiring a reboot of the router to get back to ~850Mbps speeds at the PC again. I have my work PC set to priority always, and still see the reduction in speeds.

Also, the web management UI is a bit lacking - it was a bit less intuitive to use than what I had hoped for. You don't get a ton of control to turn various features on or off on this device.

We run several (~20) wifi devices and stream our TV using wifi to an Apple TV without issue. Which is what I would expect from a device of this price point.
We had a party not too long ago and opened up the guest wifi for ~20 guests to use and no issues were reported by anyone.

I'm on the fence on this device - its pretty good, but there hasn't been a firmware update for it since 2018-09-25 which has me concerned slightly. The reboots to get back the wired LAN speeds is my main concern. Yes, I can schedule daily reboots of the device, but I just don't feel that it should be needed for a device of this price point.

This is my first TP-Link product - I cant say that I'm "impressed", but I am fairly happy with the one exception about needing to schedule daily reboots. (Also, I'm not impressed with TP-Links community forum its difficult to see if others are having same or similar issues as you with how its organized)

title: Awesome PC travel replacement!
text:
The Samsung XE520QAB is not my first Chromebook household purchase (purchased one for my son who is in elementary school three years ago), and I'm a teacher who utilizes Chromebooks during classroom instruction often; thus, I'm not new to Chromebooks. I hope this review helps buyers who are new to Chromebooks or who were skeptical about replacing (or in my case partially replacing) their primary computer (in my case, a PC laptop) with a Chromebook.

The skinny (summary): This Chromebook is fantastic! It is fast, has excellent battery life, and can handle the majority of my daily work and personal computing tasks. Another great feature/function is that it communicates seamlessly with my Samsung Galaxy Note 10+. If you are looking for a mid-grade (most tech vloggers consider this a mid-level machine, but I don't know why because it has all of the bells and whistles of most top-level machines for a much lower price), then this is the machine for you. I would suggest you purchase a case and a micro SD card (I bought a 128 Gb card). However, the 64 Gb onboard storage combined with 100 Gb Google One drive cloud space (free for one year with purchase) should be more than enough space, I like having the peace of mind of having extra offline space available if necessary. I have watched movies and screencast with no problems from this Chromebook. If watching movies or listening to music directly on this device, I suggest using headphones or Bluetooth speakers since the audio from this device does not have a dynamic range. Playing games on this Chromebook in TABLET MODE is great! Games function exactly as they do on my Note 10+. Since I have a Note 10+ and have owned previous phones from the Samsung Galaxy Note line, writing with the stylus/S pen on this Chromebook is no different. I will warn it is very small/slim and will take some getting used to, but it writes extremely well on this device. If you pair this device with web-based apps and apps from the Google Play Store, you should be able to complete the majority of computing tasks you complete on PCs/Macs.

**The remainder of this review is just more personal insight into how this Chromebooks completes tasks compared to my current PC.**

This Chromebook will probably NOT FULLY replace your PC/Mac... just yet. I use Adobe products for photo/video editing. While there are Adobe apps you can purchase/download from the Google Play store, they do not have the full range of functions/capability of their full-version counterparts available on PCs/Macs. Chromebooks, while this one, in particular, has a powerful processor for its OS, do not have graphics/audio cards that support full range photo, audio, and video editing.

Now, if you don't require a computer for advanced functions such as media editing, then this Chromebook is definitely for you! As a teacher, I can complete all work-related tasks such as email, document editing (both Microsoft and Google). I primarily use Microsoft, since the majority of the faculty and staff in my district have not fully jumped on board the Google bandwagon. Both office suites allow offline usage after initial sign-in. I have experienced only minor formatting problems when using Microsoft office on my Chromebook, but its nothing that renders a document completely unreadable or warrants complaints from readers on the receiving end of the documents. If I could wish for one app that would complete my work cycle on a Chromebook, that would be an app to edit my Smart Notebook instructional files (if you're a teacher who uses smart whiteboards, this could pose a problem). Other than that, I can manage since I don't need to edit/create those types of files often.

Personally, I use my computer a lot for paper crafting, sewing (embroidery). I own a Cricut Maker, and a Cricut Explore Air 2, Brother Scan n Cut DX, and will purchase a Silhouette Cameo 4 shortly. I have only used this Chromebook while operating my Cricut Maker (you can assume the same functionality for a Cricut Explore Air 2 as both machines use the same app). I will update this post once I thoroughly test the Brother Scan n Cut DX and the Silhouette Cameo 4 (no promises for the Cameo as I don't think Silhouette has an android app for its machines; the Scan n Cut is a mostly stand-alone machine with a web-based app client, so it should work just fine assumingly). Using the Cricut Design Studio Android app from the Google Play store, I was able to complete projects. You can slightly see the vinyl cutouts I made to customize the front panel of this Chromebook in a picture above. I did run into an issue of connecting to my Cricut Maker. I prematurely tried to connect to the Maker using the Bluetooth settings menu of the Chromebook instead of initially connecting within the Design Studio app, which may have led to connection problems. The devices connected eventually, and I have not experienced any further issues with the Chromebook relating to my Cricut Maker.

title: Doesn't Work and Slow Customer Service
text:
I bought the 128GB Samsung FIT Plus USB 3.1 Flash Drive to use as a daily "offsite" backup. I start a script at bedtime and the script encrypts and then transfers about 80 GB to the drive. During the day I carry it around in my pocket, just in case. I have drives from four other manufacturers that have all worked perfectly, but this one has failed four times in a row, using two different USB 3.0 ports.

OK so stuff fails. But I expect Samsung to respond reasonably. So far it's been 9 days since I reported the problem and I was only now able to ship the drive back to Samsung (UPS Ground - their choice). Seems like their repair-return process is designed more for $2200 TV sets than for $22 flash drives. IT'S JUST A FLASH DRIVE.

I'll report here again. if this is ever resolved.

UPDATE Oct 12, 2019: After a month I have received a replacement 128GB Samsung FIT Plus USB 3.1 Flash Drive. This one fails in exactly the same manner as the original - as if Samsung tested it, thought it worked, and sent it back to me. Maybe they did. It fails on both of the computer's USB 3.0 ports, and on a 2.0 port as well. No other flash drive fails on any of those ports, including drives from four popular manufacturers.

The files that cause this drive to fail comprise a backup of about 80GB, which is written to one or another of the various manufacturers' 128GB drives every day, with several more at the first of the month. That's more than 30 80GB writes per month without a single failure, ever, EVER! This drive fails every time.

I'm done with Samsung.

text:

I work a tech job, and have space at home that wasn't well served by WiFi for my needs... These power line links work, and work really well. I tested several locations - this office that I'm writing this review from, upstairs and the other side of the house from the main router, and out in my detached garage. One worked, one didn't.

The summary is - if the link gives you a green light, you've got a good link. Running SpeedTest showed no internet speed degradation (checked also by streaming some video without hiccups). It may not be as fast as a strung cable, but a heck of a lot easier and more flexible.

title: Dope starter kit
text:
This is my first turntable; not two days after setting it up in my music room, I was already getting called a record snob by those few people I let into my house. I chalk that up to the Jopostar's charming wood-board DIYey presentation which, coupled with its cheap price, is the main reason I chose this as my first turntable.
Other positives: it comes with a spare needle, it is AUX and Bluetooth compatible, and it's quite easy to figure out how to use--without having to resort to reading the ever-accursed manual. It's also lightweight and easy to transport, though I wouldn't advise overdoing such.
Negatives (perceived thus far): the built-in speakers are fun for about two minutes, but they're not sufficient. You should try to hook this up to something else if you plan on enjoying the music that comes out of it. But hey, if you're buying a turntable in the year 2020, you probably have plenty of speakers lying around. Second, the tone arm isn't very strong, so albums with high bass frequencies are bound to skip (Thom Yorke's recent record, Anima, for instance, and other downtempo albums). Problem can be solved by taping a coin to the needle cartridge, though, but do so at your own risk.
Lastly, and this could very well just be my machine, most records will not stop spinning after a side is finished. They will only stop if the record's center sticker has a large enough circumference--which is to say, as the needle moves closer to the center, it needs to bump into the slightly elevated surface of the label or else it will keep sliding along the lead-out and, eventually, carve a new groove. So y'know, check up on the record when the side's done or else you'll blunt the needle sooner than you want.
Happy collectin'!

title: Good Hardware. Potential Issues with Linux
text:
For anyone looking for a well-performing laptop at budget price, this ASUS seems OK. It may not be the top of specs, but for $700, that's alright.

The keyboard has better travel space than I was expecting, and is pleasantly separated and easy to type on.
The webcam quality (under Windows or Linux) is not the best, and the audio pickups can seem static-y.

If dual-booting: the laptop ships with UEFI and is "locked" to Windows without a little bit of finagling with the BIOS.
Also, a recent Intel firmware update "broke" Grub on this model (secure boot is disabled to allow a windows VM, enabled this issue is not present, but then no windows VM) back in June. It remains to be seen when it will be fixed.

It's running Kubuntu 18.0 without any issues--full KDE for a non-technical user (not myself)--and they report no big issues with the hardware.

It has fared well under video editing while streaming and running other issues--but your performance may vary greatly depending on OS more than hardware.

The screen is great, with pretty good viewing angle and very small bezels. It packs a far larger display into a smaller space.

The "lip" on the back is a neat idea, but can be uncomfortable to rest on your knees (if working on couch/in bed) for long periods of time.

Overall, it is a great budget laptop, well worth it for school or around the house. It is not a gaming laptop, but can edit videos with what appears to be minimal hassle.

It isn't very portable--due to it's 15'' size, although it is surprisingly light.

Overall, it is a solid budget choice,

title: Is the Life Q30 the perfect budget headphones?
text:
Updated review: 12-9-20

5 STARS.

Ankers customer service is unparalleled. They reached out to me to discuss my problems with this headset, as reviewed below. They worked with me and have delivered a giant fix via a firmware update. Anker has officially patched my number one problem with the headset, and now the ANC works when wired, and works very well.

You can now enjoy those story heavy single player games and intense movie watching while wired, WITH Active Noise Cancellation, high volumes with a great custom sound profiles and tremendous bass response, NO LAG what so ever (as it's wired) and best of all, NO distortion what so ever. This is the huge problem that plagued the prior model, the Q20's, and now this is the nearly perfect headset, regardless of price. The microphone is still a problem for some people, but that should not be a main reason to buy this headset anyway.

To make this set even better, all it would need is a low latency codec implemented. Perhaps this could be addressed through a future patch as well? That would mean they could be used wirelessly, (with a bluetooth transmitter) for ANY gaming and movies without lag. As they are now, there is severe lag in those use cases, but that's the point of a wired connection currently.

The value of this set is now beyond even the big boys like Sony and Bose, who will charge you 200-300 dollars, for nearly the same performance found here with the Q30's. Unbelievable.

Make sure to download the Soundcore companion app and update your headset to the latest firmware!

Original review:

So I'm a fan of Anker's ambition. I really enjoyed their previous high end set, the Life Q20, even though that headset had some problems too. Mainly with the faulty wired connection and out of date bluetooth connectivity.

I bought the new Q30 in hopes the problems of the Q20 were resolved, to make this the perfect budget set of headphones! I've been listening to this set for a week and have come to the conclusion that this set IS in fact better, including sound quality, but still has some of the same problems and new minor ones for my set.

First of all, the main reason I bought these was for Ankers superior noise cancellation. The Q20's impressed me so much, that I'm on board for the foreseeable future. The main flaw in these, is that when wired via the 3.5 AUX cable (for the most minimum latency) Noise cancellation cuts ALL sound by at least 75%. The highest volume with ANC on, is FAR too low for any enjoyment. This set simply doesn't function correctly when wired. Anker has to understand that this is still such an important feature! The simple operating buttons do not work, such as volume up and down, the ANC limits volume over 25% and of course the mic does not work at all when wired. Now, hopefully there is a way to patch these headphones via firmware update to at LEAST have a proper, higher volume choice when wired WITH Noise cancellation activated. And I certainly hope they can avoid the ANC problems of the Q20, which was extreme distortion at high and low level sounds when 3.5 wired. A part of me thinks they haven't even tried to fix this, and just drastically lowered the default volume to avoid the distortion that plagued the Q20s? Other cheaper noise cancelling headphones accomplish noise cancellation with 3.5 wired perfectly! Even sets with a push button instead of a switch. Why can't Anker get this right?

There has to be a way to construct a headset to remain powered on, to operate all these functions, but also be wired for the most minimum latency for Video games and movies with proper ANC activation. Right? Otherwise, dialogue will be out of sync. Which brings me to the next problem...

These do not have any low latency codecs. Just the basic 5.0 Bluetooth connection, which is fantastic for music listeners as latency does not matter in that situation, but bad for stronger connectivity, high quality/4K video/movie watching and most importantly, gaming. Apt-X of any sort would make a world of difference in connecting to certain devices and make the value of this headset skyrocket. Now, this doesn't make or break the set, the connectivity is still really GOOD. So this isn't a huge problem for many people. But for gamers, this set is basically useless. You NEED low latency for video games, and unless Anker can patch the firmware of this set to provide proper ANC function while wired, they won't get the job done. Various sets from Mpow, Taotronics and other companies have this feature in the bag and are much better gaming headphones currently, because of their low latency and properly working ANC while 3.5 wired. Those sets just can't match the sound quality of the Soundcores. I'll get more into that later as I speak on some positives.

The design of the headset is great. The look, button layout and weight are all proficient. The buttons feel natural once you figure out where everything is. It's easy to get used to. Build quality on my unit is a mixed bag. So compared to the Q20's the ear cups are larger, a bit thinner and slightly less comfortable. My right side ear pad is improperly sewn/connected, so the pleather material is folding up over the cup plastic. It's a bit unattractive and may be making it slightly more uncomfortable. I've attached pictures. It's not a huge deal, but it looks like my cushion is permanently being pushed in. The overall construction is a bit creaky, the plastic finish isn't ideal, as it attracts fingerprints and skin oil. The passive noise isolation (the general hug of the earcups) is weaker than that of the Q20's. This heavily comes into play when 3.5 wired, since the noise cancellation is useless when wired.

The sound quality is fantastic. The sound quality beats the Q20's by a fair margin, and the customizable options through the app, are a welcome addition. The Q20 models only feature a "bass up" button function, which honestly just muddies the sound, and makes it a bit too boomy. The neutral sound of the Q20's was impressive for the price, but now a fine-tuned Q30 is so much better! Clarity, lows and highs are all better and less distorted than the Q20's at higher volumes. With the Q30s you can pump the bass up and literally make the ear cups rumble your brain (to the point that it made me dizzy!) and it is STILL a clearer sound profile than the Q20's "bass up" function! That really told me everything I needed to know about the purity of sound in this set. Pick a preset, and adjust the equalizer to your liking. My personal favorite is "classical" with some minor adjustments. You can have many "custom" profiles and swap between them on the fly to really determine the best sound profile for you. Simply wonderful.

The battery life, as everyone has noted, is fantastic. No qualms there at all. 60 hours... is ridiculous! In a good way!

Overall, due to the few problems I can't necessarily recommend this headset OVER the cheaper Q20's. But if you find yourself a coupon or deal, the Q30s are the superior choice. The sound quality, battery life have improved immensely, while the build quality stays about the same. The ANC is still a major problem when using a wired connection, so this isn't for gamers or movie nuts. For general use and music listening, it's hard to beat. If Anker can really put some care into updating the firmware for these, then I will re-evaluate my review and they MAY just become the best set of headphones on the market! For now, 3 stars, as I'm so disappointed the same problems form the Q20 persist. But 5 stars in sound quality, battery life and noise cancellation effectiveness while wireless.

In that same photo you can also see how shallow the depth of field gets wide open at f1.7! Not to mention the f1.7 aperture comes in handy in low light situations! This is a VERSATILE lens that I HIGHLY recommend! If you don’t have a camera and you’re looking to purchase one. I suggest skipping the kit lens and buy the body only. Let this be your first lens!!! Trust me you won’t regret it! You can’t get that bokeh (blurry back ground) with the kit lenses. The kit lenses aren’t fast enough (have low enough apertures).
