title: After having the Define R2 for years, this was a nice upgrade.
text:
Due to me rushing the purchase and the search results being backwards, I purchased the Define S2 instead of the Meshify S2 which was my intention. Not a huge deal since they are exactly the same case, but have different top and front panels. I got in contact with Fractal to see if I could just buy the Meshify front panel separately, but sadly they don't sell parts outside of warranties in the US since they're bigger in Europe.

My older air cooled PC is still running great in the Define S2 case and decided to stick with Fractal for my new build. I've had the new build up and going for almost 2 months and haven't had temp issues so far. Without overclocking, buying a newer GPU, and AIO, I saw no reason to buy better fans than what was provided. They're not the quietest, but do the job. Vape test showed great airflow. I have one Fractal intake at the bottom front slot, two Fractal intake in the front panel, and one 140mm Noctua exhaust in the rear. I had no issues with the fan header as some people have mentioned.

Fractal did a great job with the updates in the chassis and also providing more than enough pieces, parts, and space to assemble your setup with ease. Wire management is pretty spot on. My only complaint is where you hook up wires to the USB headers at the bottom. As pictured, the USB 3.0 IO wire is huge and stiffer than the TYPE C, which means a quality wire; however, trying to hook it up and curl it 180 degrees then down through the hole is not the best design. I had to give the wire a lot of slack so it doesn't bend the header on the motherboard. To me, a 90 degree plug that could come through the hole and plug right in without 6 inches of exposed wire would've been much better, but said connector exist and will be purchasing one separately. Hooking up the wires up the PSU was tough because of it having its own section in the case. I wish I hooked those up first before running them to everything, but my intention was to bring the slack to the PSU.

The hideaway slots for the hard drives are a nice touch, and so is the offset top mount for radiators for my future 360mm Radiator that is said to clear my RAM. The pop off side panels is a much better design than the Define R2's 10 tiny slot slide back panels, and the full size glass panel is a nice upgrade from the smaller plastic window on the S2.

Overall very impressed with Fractal Designs keeping their classic ascetics, but making improvements where needed. If you had to choose between this or the Meshify S2, I'd say get whichever one is cheaper, because of them being so similar. If you overclock and choose to get an air cooler instead of water cooled, the meshify might be a better option due to the improved air flow. Temps under load are: CPU 50C-60C with AMD wraith, 72C bottle necked GPU, 42C RAM, and 28C M.2/Sata SSD. Board and VRM stay vary cool due to downfiring cooler.

title: Great sound, very good noice cancellation
text:
The main reason I ordered these headphones was the active noise cancellation (ANC) feature that they advertise. I travel quite a bit and I really need this feature to drown out the engine noise. My all-time favorite has been (and continues to be) the Bose QuietComfort 20, which are significantly priced higher than these from iqua.

If you are not familiar with headphone ANC, be aware that they are set up to cancel out white noise, like a subway, an air conditioner, plane engines, etc. You will find that sounds coming from loud conversations and crying babies are also drowned out to some degree, but that’s not really their intention or where they shine.

As far as the ANC capability for these headphones, I would put the Bose at a 10 and these somewhere around a 7-8. They do indeed cancel out ambient noise, and noticeably so. You can clearly tell the difference when you switch that feature on, but not quite to the same level as the higher priced Bose.

One key point.....the earbud size that they came with, the ones that were already attached, were WAY too small for me, which is rare, the stock earbuds usually fit fine, so I replaced them with a larger size. At the risk of stating the obvious, this makes a huge difference not only in noise cancellation, but also in their sound quality. In short, make sure they fit your ears snugly.

And on that point, their sound quality is nothing short of outstanding. Deep, resonating bass, with crisp and clear mids and highs. My wife was blown away by their sound quality as well.

My exact rating on these would really be somewhere around a 4.8, thus my five-star rating. For the price for which they are offered matched to their performance, I think these are an excellent choice.

If things change as I use them more, I will update this review. I hope it helped you to some degree...thanks for reading!

title: Awesome way to consolidate your remotes.  Much better than universal remotes from stores.
text: This remote is power packed for this price point.  My current setup includes an Amazon Fire Cube, TCL Roku TV, Verizon Arris cable, and Edifier S350DB powered speakers.  The SofaBaton U1 works perfectly and I can do everything I need with a single remote.  The setup process is quite easy.  You download the SofaBaton app, pair your phone to the remote, and use the app to choose each of your devices from the SofaBaton database.  The database sets up default settings for each device on your remote but you can also edit the remote buttons to what makes sense to you.  In addition, you can map buttons from one device to another.  For instance, you can set the cable box volume buttons to control the volume on your speakers.  There is a small black and white screen that lists your devices and there is a thumbwheel to switch between devices.  The remote can control both IR and bluetooth devices but I think it is limited to a single bluetooth device.  I use the bluetooth for my Amazon Fire Cube.  One minor inconvenience is that you need to do the programming of the remote using a bluetooth connection to your phone so you should program your bluetooth device (e.g., Amazon Fire) last because once you pair with the Fire it will break the programming connection.  You can always go back later and pair it again with your phone if you want to change some programming.  But then you will need to pair it again with the Fire when you are done.  Not a big problem but the pairing with the Fire can be a little finnicky sometimes.  There is a macro feature but I haven't had to use it.  My Fire Cube turns on my TV and Edifier speakers.  Then I use the remote to control the Roku, Prime, and cable content.  The volume buttons are mapped to my speakers for the TV, cable, and Fire devices.  Pretty slick and much cheaper than my Logitech Harmony remotes. Customer support was also very responsive.  When I first tried to set up the remote, the app was getting hung up.  I sent a message to customer support and got a response within hours.  It turns out their database server had gone down.  They fixed the server immediately and the app worked perfectly after that.

title: Not an easy install or setup for most consumers, and unusable for many
text:
Before I begin I wish to apologize for the lengthy review, but there is a lot to unpack with the Blue by ADT video doorbell.

This is a difficult review to write because ADT is such a respected brand in the home security space. But if they are planning to compete in the video doorbell arena, they really need to step up and offer something better than the current leader (out of respect for ADT I will not mention their name in this review).

The first thing you need to know is this video doorbell requires electric power to operate. It is meant to connect to the electric wiring that a normal household doorbell uses. So if you are not handy or do not have electricity at your front door, you will need to hire an electrician. And even if you are handy, the chime they include with the doorbell does not come with a mounting bracket, and the power cable that connects the camera to the existing doorbell wiring also connects to the chime, and it is very short, VERY SHORT. With the provided cable the chime has to be mounted within just a few inches of the doorbell. AND YOU CAN'T MOUNT IT BECAUSE THERE IS NO BRACKET PROVIDED!!! So if your existing chime bracket is located elsewhere, you will either need to get an electrician to modify the cable provided by ADT or you will have to move the chime mount on the other side of the wall from the doorbell, not a desirable location for many people.

If you are a renter, or cannot have electricity wired to a suitable location for the Blue by ADT doorbell, then this is most certainly not the product for you. If you do not want to spend hundreds of dollars on an electrician (at a minimum), this is not the product for you. There is a small internal battery meant to keep the unit running during power outages, but according to ADT customer support it is not designed to power the doorbell for normal use. And they currently have no plans to offer a rechargeable battery. In addition, there is no mount to angle the doorbell like the competitor offers.

Also, the included directions are pretty useless. They would have been better off not to include any instructions at all. And the security screw that prevents the doorbell from being removed from the mount is tiny and is screwed in with the smallest allen wrench I have ever seen. Expect to lose that in a day or two meaning once mounted it probably will not be coming off again, unless you have a tiny allen wrench dealer on speed dial.

So if you are still on board because of the ADT name and you don't mind doing a little extra work to get it set up and installed then good for you. Let's turn to some of the quirks with the app. The first problem I encountered was with the app detecting my wifi connection. It meets the security level required and the wifi router is visible for connections, but the app would not find it. I had to manually enter the wifi information into the app to get it to connect. There are a few screens you have to get through that show how to install and connect your doorbell (not really, but I'm humoring the developers who really tried to be helpful here).

Once you get the wifi established, setting up the doorbell in the app was actually quite easy. The video is clear and seems to work well, and the audio communication is equally good, both to and from the doorbell. When you press the doorbell button the app immediately notifies you, twice. In fact I get every notification twice. The motion notifications are often significantly delayed, up to 7-8 minutes at times, so don't plan on being notified about package thieves or intruders until after they are long gone.

And the zone controls setting is a bit limited. You basically can create a rectangular area on the screen to include the parts of the doorbell coverage area you wish to use as the area of interest for motion. And unlike the primary competitor, you cannot set separate notification sounds for motion verses doorbell activation. There is only one rectangle you can draw on the screen.

I honestly did not even attempt the chime. I would have had to cut wires on the included power cable to make use of the small connector that plugs into the chime for power. I would imagine it is also setup via wifi and that the setup in the app is as simple as the doorbell, but to test that I would have had to rig up a makeshift power cable and I simply was just not up to that. And even if I did rig up a makeshift power cable, how would I mount the chime? There is not bracket!!

It seems to be a decent product, but it is just not for most people. The choice to use household electric power for the doorbell is a bit baffling and limiting for the products appeal. The included chime is just a disaster because it does not include everything you would need to mount it and getting power to it would also be an issue. And the app and notifications need some improvement.

I gave it two stars only because of the video and audio quality, but I would not recommend this unless you are set on an ADT product. There are much better offerings when considering a video doorbell.

title: Buy This Tablet!
text:
Very happy with this product. The tablet features a vibrant-red case and is kid-friendly. It is also great item for people, like myself, who are young-at-heart.

I ordered this item to give to my friend’s grand-daughter for Christmas - I’m one of those people who like to start shopping early. Also, I wanted to see if the product worked, and if it did as stated in the Amazon listing. Therefore, I checked out the features myself and also asked some kids at the library about their opinions on the tablet.

I did not hear any negative comments about the tablet. The children liked the red color and high-resolution screen. I, too, was impressed with how the product made navigation easy for both kids and adults. The tablet already has five pre-installed educational apps - added for immediate use.

While the battery life is not all that long (5 hours), that is okay. You don’t want a kid looking at the tablet all day. That is enough time for a child to use the tablet for school or a related activity. You really do not want kids to become too occupied with a computer. Therefore, the 5-hour use is a good thing.

I like the tablet’s screen and the fact that it has a pre-applied screen protector. The carrying pouch is a nice addition for the cost. I received the tablet, a charging cable, universal adapter, carrying pouch, and USB cable. Everything featured in the ad came to my door.

The weight of the tablet is light. Yet the product is rugged, as it is designed to bounce back by dropping or any random handling. Overall, I believe the item is sturdy and easy to use – for kids and technically illiterate adults. It is just the right size for children, and has all the features that make using a computer convenient and fun.

Not only does the electronic come housed in a red bumper case, it features 2GB RAM and an Android 8.1 Oreo design. You can use the product with WiFi, HDMI, Bluetooth, or USB. The cameras on the product are great additions, especially if you want to teach a kid the fine art of picture-taking.

Overall, I would give this product a 5-star rating. If you want to buy a fun tablet for Christmas for a child, I recommend spending your money on this kid-friendly and fun-to-use red tablet. This is a good “starter” electronic for young kids.

title: Decent mic for the price.
text:
Alright round two for this review, I wrote a nice review... then amazon didn’t process it. End of rant.

So, decent audio quality in my honest opinion is a very important thing to have... whether you are vlogging for YouTube, making films, or shooting weddings... people are more likely to tune out due to poor audio quality than poor video quality. That being said finding decent microphones can be pricy.

Well I discovered the Moukey MCM-1, and well for a little over 20 bucks, it’s a decent little mic. A lot of reviews I’ve seen or read have said the mic had some reverb, or sounded canned.. but I didn’t have any issues at all to be honest and was really impressed with what I found.

One thing that stuck out to me was the box it came in, it was built nicely. I know, I know... what does this have to do with the microphone, well it is just nice to know that this company takes the time to Package the product decently. The box was definitely tough and in a day and age where packages get tossed around like frisbees, I felt safe knowing the contents would be safe and not crushed. Opening the box I noticed that everything was packaged tightly in the box, giving it a little shake nothing really loved around... again a big sign of comfort.

The mic itself is made of a metal casing, it definitely feels decent in my hand (get your mind out of the gutter.) it didn’t feel cheap, in other words, with a price point as low as 20 dollars I was half expecting a plastic case. It comes with a shock mount which is made of plastic... and it’s very rigid. Now of all the items this mic comes with the shock mount feels cheap, I honestly thought I was going to snap it in half when putting the mic in there but it went right in( ... get your head out of the gutter)! The mic! It comes with two cords, both are 3.5mm one is trrs- meant for cell phones or tablets, the other is a trs which is meant for dslrs or computers. It also comes with two wind screens, a dead cat which is kind of limp... (... I’m not even...) but DOES work. It fits on there well, and does a decent job. Although in very high winds I noticed it does rub against the mic which can cause some unnecessary noise. But you shouldn’t be using it during a wind storm. The other is a pop filter which is was really nice and again felt like it was made of quality and held up against a lot of elements. It’s just nice that Moukey includes all these as most mic companies seem to nickel and dime you for accessories. Out the gate you really don’t need to really buy anything for this, which is nice, kudos to you Moukey.

Now I did compare this to the rode video micro which would be the equivalent. Now, it’s no rode... but it did hold its own and for a little under 20 dollars.. I’d say... put it in the cart.

I have this mounted on top of my panasonic G7. It’s definitely better than the on camera mic. So whether you are a film maker, or YouTube novice, or you just want something better than your on board mic, this is worth looking into, especially for the price. I use it as a scratch track when I film my movies (I usually record audio separately.) it picks up the surrounding audio better and helps me easily sync audio from a separate source to the camera.

As always this is my opinion, pick it up for yourself and give it a try.

title: You All Better Buy These Spectaboulistic Earbuds!
text:
I'm Quintagilously Sold!

Case is solid and with hefty weight made of high grade aluminum.

I had no issues with the latch. They open & close easily.

You must select the proper ear tips to get the best sound quality. Make sure you have the right seal placement.

Sound is amazing! Great bass, mids & highs. I turned on the Dolby Atmos equalizer setting in the Samsung Note 8 and was able to further customize the sound to my liking. Sound is also prime on the iPhone XS Max.

The range is very good as well. Tested it 50-feet away: no cut-off, no lags. Penetrates through walls well. My phone was in the living room; I was wearing them and listening to tunes down the basement.

Pairing was easy. Just make sure you follow the instructions -- which I neglected in the beginning -- and had issues playing sound simultaneously on both earbuds.

(1) Take them *both* out of the case. Red + Blue light will blink.

(2) Turn Bluetooth on phone. Pair only one (1) earbud [mifo_R *OR* mifo_L].

(3) After paired with phone, Turn *both earbuds* Off.

(4) Press *both* earbuds' Power Button *simultaneously* for *1 second* --> Light will blink --> and they'll pair with each other. Both sounds should now play on each earbud.

(5) The next time you use them, *First* turn the Bluetooth on your phone. *Second* take the earbuds out of the case. Both lights should be blinking. It'll pair automatically to your phone.

If tested many wireless earbuds, and this is by far the best of all of them. Forget all the $120-$250 brand name products out there.

These are light, comfortable after hours of use, and they do not fall out like others.

title: 100% Perfect, no complaints. Good deal.
text:
After hours of research I finally settled on these. I've had a few hundred dollar headphones/earbuds to cheap $10 ones. For the average listener, these are perfect. I'm very aggressive on my headphones. Constantly listening to music day and night. If I can get a pair to last past 6 months I'm happy. Last bargain sale headphones were Carlos Santana's for $25 (originally $60+ something). Used and abused, I'd buy them again in a heart beat. Reviews show these can be fragile and break easy. Honestly feel like any other plastic headphone. They do have a tight grip and if you have bigger ears like me after 8-10 plus hours your ears can ache... As you would expect them to with anything pressed against them for that long... Packaging was nice and clean, short charging cable, cheap feeling aux cord per normal... Great battery life, went from 80% initial turn on to 100 in no time. As I type this I've been listening to them for a solid 8 hours and still at 100%. So I'm happy. Now they're just showing off...

For a $100 pair of headphones you really can't complain about anything... The social listener that listens to music, videos, occasional movies, these will be everything you want and more. You don't have to spend $300 - 1,000+ for great headphones.

Warning.

These will ruin all other headphones for you if you are mainly shopping for music enjoyment. Bass is fun and ridiculous, so much that sometimes it's too much... My bass slider chills at 50 - 20%. It's perfect. You'll hear people talk about highs/lows, etc. blah blah blah, again, to the untrained ear you can't tell, and if you can these put such a dumb cheese grin on your face that you don't care. It is not enough to really complain about. And you can find that sweet bass spot in every genre. I like my music loud, these are controversial and a personal opinion in that area. To my wife they are extremely loud, too loud. Me, they could be louder, they aren't the loudest, but they do borderline that area where they are hella doable, but you wouldn't want them to be any quieter at full max. Bluetooth is fine, I am usually in pretty close proximity of my phone or it's on my person. I don't have a need or care to be able to walk 40ft away from it. Came with a nice soft carrying case. Not sure why people are complaining about it. It's nice to me. No, it won't stop a bullet but I don't need it to. That bell/bong sound when you tap on the earphone is nothing crazy and people are nitpicking. That is like throwing 22 inch rims on your car complaining about the bumps and pot holes in the road being rougher... Comes with the headphones territory... Is what it is... Just don't tap it if it annoys you. Or shake your head like a bulldog 24/7 and you're good. Although, when I shake my head I don't hear anything like other consumers are saying they do.

I would purchase the crusher wireless over its more expensive siblings. And if you are going to get the cheaper ones I would get the mesh 2's over the mesh 3's.. The two's sound better imo.

In short, these are great, fun, headphones that will put a smile on your face at the fraction of other headphones that possibly might not. They are plastic, be easy on them. Take them to the most narrow part of your head and open them up to your ears. Keep the flex as subtle as possible...

I fear I will not be getting what these headphones deliver from neighboring competition at this price range. So, I will definitely be buying them again when time comes.

title: Some Good, Some Bad, Some Meh.
text:
I've had this laptop for a week now, and while there is much to like, there is also a few things that make me wish I had bought a different machine.

PROS: Display is GORGEOUS, and the dedicated graphics handle my current favorite game--FFXIV--at ultra high settings. Boot time is non-existent due to the SSD. The keyboard is a real pleasure to use. It's QUIET and gives good feedback. It's also intelligently laid out. I love that there's a num-pad. Also, aesthetically, the lighting is a lot of fun. I don't usually buy gaming laptops for the bling, but hey ... I'll take bling when it comes my way. It has plenty of ports, and feels solid. I don't feel like it's going to fall apart on me.

CONS: The CPU runs HOT. And while this is to be expected when processing a high-graphics, high-input game, the fans are NOISY. The chassis grows hot in the upper margins above the top row of keys (I suspect this is where the CPU is housed), and if you want to keep it cooler, you have to crank the fans waaaay up. The GPU is fine. This pertains only to the CPU. This feeds into the next complaint: The audio for this machine truly sucks. The speakers are located on the bottom of the machine, so with the fan noise and the speaker location all the audio is either inaudible or very muddy. I had to lift the laptop up to make out what someone was saying in a Youtube vid--and the speakers were on high. This is purportedly a gaming laptop, and games have soundtracks that people want to hear. This just feels like they tried to cut corners. Lastly, I had to disable the camera driver. It would switch the camera on and off randomly and in quick succession whenever I'd start up a game.

So ... yeah. If you want it for high-end gaming, maybe find a different machine that won't bring you annoyances. If you are playing videos, or listening to music only, or using it for writing, etc, you'll be fine.

Five stars for the screen. Three stars for the gaming due to the sound issues, and lack of sluggish cooling for the CPU. I only use it plugged in, so I can't attest to the battery life ... hence four stars.

The picture is an example of how high the resolution is in a gaming environment. Sweet stuff.

title: It Runs...But Does It Work?
text:
I'm neither gamer nor road warrior, and my relatively stationary customized, non-OEM laptop sometimes runs warm, noticeably during sustained use or when recharging. (The laptop vendor said, "That comes with the chip," and I couldn't rightly argue.) This device looked interesting on paper and in pictures; I'd to date used an NZXT Cryo LX that appears no longer in production but is undeniably sturdy and demands a non-USB power supply.

You can indeed hold this device in your hand and pocket it. Simply slip the appropriately sized silicone shroud (a choice of four sizes) over the device intake and do your best to mate that with your laptop's primary exhaust vent, plug the device into a USB port for power, and turn it on. It lights up in blue and a four-digit number displays that appears adjustable with the twist of a knob. (On this run the number varies but stabilizes in the high 2200s/low 2300s; I infer that means RPM, and no real need to run that up yet.) Runs quiet enough. No software involved.

But...does it truly work? Time will tell, and on the question of power usage and durability as well. I'll update this as the need arises.

(UPDATE: It helps to keep the device intake level with your laptop exhaust vent, and Klim provides plenty "shivs" to support the device. I've also since determined that it demands a non-USB power supply. If I can find a suitable US5VDC-AC adapter and cord plug I'll report same.)

(SECOND UPDATE: And the winner appears the combination of a Dericam 5V 1000mA AC to DC Power Adapter with an [I]BERLS Universal 5V DC [5-foot] Power Cable, USB to DC, 5.5 x 2.1 mm [its default] plug. Still something of a juggling act, though, and I'll see what results of prolonged use.)

title: Great Tv, PS5, Series X Gaming Ready
text:
I already had a pretty good tv, a 2018 vizio v series 4k, but I wanted a tv that was next gen gaming ready, and this fit the bill.

Its crazy to me that's there's no information or advertising of this TV having HDMI 2.1 ports, not on here, or LG website, but it has 2. If you don't know what the HDMI 2.1 ports are, they are needed to play games at 4k at 120Frames Per Second. I did a lot of research before buying this TV, and to my knowledge, this is the cheapest TV that has 2.1 Ports(most tvs average at $1k).

I play games on Ps4 currently, until next gen comes out, and the gameplay is great. I have 0 input lag, and games that support HDR look great.
I played around, and watched some video on what settings to apply and turn off to make the TV as lag free as possible, if you want my settings
Picture Mode-Game
AMD FreeSync Premium-High
Instant Game Response-On
HDMI Ultra Deep Color-On
LED Local Dimming-OFF
Smooth Gradation-OFF
Tru Motion-OFF

I can't comment on the sound quality of the tv speakers, as I use a sound bar.

Now to the picture, I think its fantastic. Like I mentioned, I already had a pretty solid Tv to begin with, and this is noticeably better in picture quality. The picture is very crisp, and clean. Colors are super vibrant and look authentic.
Only issue I have is when setting up my picture setting, when I click "apply to all inputs" it simply doesn't work for some reason.

My other favorite things besides the picture are the remote, and Alexa/Google.

The remote is just magical. Its like a magic wand, you just point at the screen and the arrow follows. No need to scroll to pick what show you want, just point and click.
The remote also has built in Alexa and Google Assistant. Just hold down the prime video button for Alexa, or the mic button for google, and you can ask it anything a normal Assistant would do, as well as find shows/movies to watch.
With Alexa, you get notifications on the TV as you would on your echo dot and such, like when a package has arrived or shipped.

Overall I think its a great Tv.
It has a ton of great options. It has a bunch of built in Apps, like Netflix, Hulu, Disney, Prime Video, Peacock, Apple TV, and whatever apps it doesn't have, just download them on your phone and you can stream it to the Tv.
Theres also a catalog of Free Live TV for anyone considering cord cutting.

FYI, my Local bestbuy had this exact model on display at my store, so I was able to check it out before purchasing.
-Note, I ended up buying the TV through Bestbuy so I can't comment on any delivery concerns. They offer price match guarantee and bring it out to the car via curbside pickup so id highly recommend it.

title: The most sturdy of DVD cases! =) BUT, they have some significant flaws. =(
text:
Firstly, I have to give the maker of these cases credit for making these the sturdiest and most solid-feeling DVD cases I've come across since the heyday of the DVD format, way back in the late 90s and early 2000s.

The relative bargain pricing of these cases (10 cases loaded with swing trays for 3 discs each, all for 11 dollars), is also a great point. I wish I could give more stars for this product, but unfortunately the following bothersome flaws altogether take it down to around 3 stars for me:

1) Some of the edges of the black plastic here are molded/cut rather roughly, but this point alone is not a big deal, and it's understandable given the pricing of these cases.

2) The disc hubs hold all 3 discs securely during storage, BUT when inserting or removing a disc on the front/first hub (located on the swing tray), the action can sometimes put enough pressure on the third disc (located against the back wall, underneath the swing tray) to dislodge it in the process. The type of design for the 3rd hub is just not ideal for this kind of multi-disc case, given how easily it releases its disc.

3) There is -- for me -- a rather strong plastic chemical-type smell from these cases that seems peculiar to some generic DVD cases. Perhaps I have a sensitive nose, but I couldn't stand handling them for too long, so I didn't want to put them in with my existing DVD collection. I know many other DVD collectors/users probably wouldn't mind or wouldn't even notice the smell, but for me it was unfortunately a dealbreaker, so I had to return these. =(

If the manufacturer remedied the last 2 flaws especially, these cases would be a great product all around. But as it is, I had to find a solution for 3-disc cases elsewhere.

title: Once you buy your first Holsem you'll buy more and nothing else!
text:
I have been buying Holsem surge protectors for the past year.

My first purchase was this very 12 outlet surge protector. I bought it based on overwhelmingly positive Amazon reviews.

From the moment I unboxed it and plugged it in, I was hooked! This is a quality-made surge protector like no other for the price point. It's as if Apple made this product -- that's how perfect it is.

The first thing you will notice is how "loaded" this device is with AC outlets and USB charging ports. As you know already, you can plug up to 12 devices into this unit. The only downside with so many outlets is that they are packed rather close together. This means if you plug in a block type plug, it will take up more than one outlet space. It looks like Holsem has tried to alleviate this problem somewhat by configuring connections on the sides and the middle. If you are lucky, you might be able to get normal and box plugs to coexist together.

In addition to the 12 plug outlets, there are three USB charging connections. Two IQ ports have a charging speed of 5V/3.1A and the third has a charging speed of 5V/1.0A. IC technology automatically detects the device you are plugging into it and then provides the fastest charging.

And what would a surge protector be without overload protection? In the event of such an overload, the safety switch will trip off automatically thus protecting your plugged in devices and ultimately, your home. The adapter is also flame retardant and features a 6-foot cord which gives you plenty of room to place this device exactly where you need it.

As I noted previously, for me it was love at first sight. This is really a surge protector to behold. Once you use this in your home, you won't want to go with any other brand. I have bought two additional slightly smaller 8 outlet surge protectors that Holsem also supports. As of the writing of this review, the smaller strip was remarkably slightly more expensive than this one. So, if that's the case for you it's a no-brainer to go for the larger protector.

On the back of this surge protector are keyholes that you can mount this to a wall or baseboard.

Extremely happy with this brand. As I stated earlier, I won't buy anything else. I believe you'll be just as happy with this purchase.

title: Excellent wired mesh network. Omada controller software is a must for roaming
text:
TP-Link's EAP mesh access points have been a revelation. Before this, I had been using two separate wireless routers (one as a dumb access point) to cover a 2-story house. It worked ok sitting in one spot, but the roaming experience was bad. Now with two EAP225 APs, devices roam seamlessly with no delay switching between APs or bands.

Wired back haul is the best option for multiple access points (APs) in a network. This reduces wireless traffic between APs and to the main router. While tri-band wireless mesh helps by dedicating a wireless channel for back haul, it still suffers from wireless interference. If you choose a wired back haul, PoE is a convenient option because both data and power are delivered on a single cable. No need to look for a power outlet to plug a wall wart into. The EAP225 is exactly what I was looking for: PoE and wired mesh.

The Omada controller software unlocks the full capability of the EAP mesh APs. The EAP can operate without the Omada controller, but it won't support fast roaming and band steering. The easiest way to install the Omada Controller software on Linux is with the mbentley/omada-controller Docker container. These are the options to run the controller:
1) TP-Link's dedicated Omada box for around $90.
2) Omada software on a Linux box (hardware can be as simple as Raspberry Pi or a full blown PC).
3) Omada software on a Windows box (not recommended due to Windows heavy resource requirements and instability).

Remember that the Omada software must be running at all times to support seamless roaming. The EAPs will operate without it, but roaming handoffs will be much slower.

The administrative web page for the Omada controller is elegant and easy to use. You can configure the EAP radios, SSIDs, view the clients, how much bandwidth is used, and all sorts of handy dandy stuff. It's truly an enterprise grade system for the home office. I recommend it for small & medium sized businesses as well.

title: Reviewing the TASCAM TH-02 vs Sony's MDRZX110
text:
Both head phones I rated 5 stars because, for the price, they are both excellent. I am writing a review just to help someone like me in the future figure out what is the best option for what they want to accomplish. First off, I am an audiophile musician that has much more expensive headphones. I just wanted a pair to use that I was not worried about losing or damaging. I bought both sets and will keep both sets because they are both great, they just have different uses.
Sony MDRZX110: If you just want to listen to music, get this set hands down. It is more comfortable and had better bass response. You might get a little better bass with the overpriced Beats headphones, but I was pleasantly surprised when I tested my headphones and they are orders of magnitude cheaper. They are not top notch as far as durability and do not provide a balanced audio response. Also, I don't know if it is in the description but the 1/8" plug is at a 90' angle. This would have made them worthless for what I bought them for because it would have not fit. That being said, I will keep these to listen on my computer and for the price they can not be beat.

TASCAM TH-20: If you are looking for studio headphones or headphones to practice your instrument quietly, get these hands down. They provide a more balanced tonal quality needed for studio mixing or playing instruments. They are more durable than the Sony's by a good margin. They are not as comfortable, but for my average sized head, they are good enough. They are over the ear and have closed backs making them better for noise isolation. They didn't quite provide the balanced response against my top of the line audio headphones, but they were not bad and are quite a value for $20. Also, one other thing to note; the Sony's have wires to both ears, these only have one to the left ear, if that is important to you.

title: Nice camera but burns lots of data
text:
The camera actually performs quite well, high resolution and easily integrated into the Ring app.

Where I had an issue with them was data consumption, and support. I bought my 3 Indoor Cams in early December 2019, and during the month my data usage with my ISP (Comcast) jumped from 490GB in November, to 1.2TB in December. I have a 1TB cap on my internet usage, and took a financial hit on my last bill. Since I work from home I had very small motion zones set up, but since I knew the only new items on my network were the Ring Cams, I had a major issue.

The first time I called Ring support, i asked them for help and was told there was nothing they could do for me. That was in early January. Over the last couple of weeks, i roughly blew through another 500GB of data. I called Ring support again, and this time I asked to be escalated to a second level engineer. When I explained the problem this time, he suggested that I delete my motion zones and see if that stopped the excessive data consumption. It actually seemed to work this time, as I’ve only consumed about 20GB of data in the last couple of days (vs. about 45GB/day in December).

I’ll keep monitoring my usage, but as long as I stay under my data cap, I’m satisfied. But there is no way to control data consumption, except by eliminating the motion zones. That turns the cameras into nothing more than on-demand tools, and defeats the purpose of the built in intelligence of the cameras.

Maybe this incident (and the experience of others) will compel Ring to allow users more control over data usage. If they do that, then I’d be more inclined to rate the cameras higher. But until then, beware of how motion zones influence data usage.

title: Perfect isolation from the utility company
text: I have had issues with my cable company and electric company using separate grounds outside the house. We have lost a lot of electronics over the years due to lightning and the improper utility grounding. Using a fiber optic break between the power and the cable eliminates the possibility of a lightning surge travelling from the cable company, arcing through the electronics back to the utility ground. I have been using these fiber optic converters for about ten years now and have had no more surge damage. Note that even a surge aerator outlet will not protect you if you power company and cable or phone company are not solidly grounded to the same grounding stake outside your home.

title: Perfect integration with Samsung TV
text:
I wanted to add a sound bar to a new Samsung 55" 8 series TV because the sound of the TV was lacking. I have the TV sitting in a large TV console wall cabinet and it is pretty much enclosed within it's own cubicle. With the rear facing speakers on the TV this setup made for very poor sound quality. This was made worse by the fact that I have hearing impairment and wear hearing aids.

This sound bar is pretty much of an entry level unit priced at a little over $200 so I really didn't expect too much when I ordered it. One of my biggest concerns when deciding on which sound bar to get was how it would integrate with the TV. I did not want to have to deal with a separate remote for the volume. I also wanted one that would turn on and off automatically with the TV. Because the TV has HDMI ARC capabilities, I wanted a sound bar that works with that technology. Based on the specs, the Samsung HW-N450 seemed to fit the bill perfectly.

When I took delivery of the unit and unboxed it I was initially impressed with it's build quality - it just looked nice and solid !! In spite of it's great appearance I began the installation with great trepidation. I first powered up the sound bar and the woofer and within seconds, they found each other - SUCCESS ! I then connected the HDMI ARC cable to the proper ports on the sound bar and TV and lo & behold, I had sound. The TV speakers shut down and the sound began on the sound bar & woofer. The most surprising part was that the Samsung TV remote worked with the sound bar and the DirecTV remote worked as well. I realized that once you have the volume of the woofer where you want it, you can stick the sound bar remote in a drawer and never need to use it. I literally had the sound bar operational within a half hour of unpacking it. Prior to adding the sound bar, I had the sound setting on the TV to around 40 which was loud but somewhat muddled. After setting up the sound bar the setting is now around 30 and a much cleaner, crisper sound with a definite bass boost.

I spent several hours doing a custom installation of the sound bar above the TV using the wall mounting hardware that came with it. I have the sound bar hung from the top of the TV cabinet cubicle and is completely free of the TV itself. This installation allows me to move the TV itself without have to move the sound bar. The only caveat I would mention is if you are planning on installing the sound bar on top of the TV using one of the "universal sound bar mounts" it will not work without major modifications because the only mounting screw holes are on the bottom of the sound bar.

If you are looking to improve the rear facing sound on your TV to acceptable levels then this is the item for you. If you are looking for theater like sound system you should look elsewhere and expect to spend a lot more.

I purchased this computer from Microsoft since they are presently applying a $200 discount, hence no Amazon "confirmed purchaser" rating. I am an Amazon member.

Battery usage looking good but I can't rate it yet hence no stars.

Cons,

Previously reported fan noise, none.
Previously reported excessive heat, none.
Previously reported touch pad looseness, none.
Previously reported case squeaks, none.
The awkwardly placed selfie camera, not going to use it in any case.

This computer is so well made that I can only think that Huawei management saw some of the critical comments on their early models and made a massive QC efforts.

I will report on any longer term problems but I am now impressed, very impressed.

title: Desktop Usage Review - Updated
text:
The black version of this got bad reviews. Hoped for the better with this white version with the reviews here. But it's like what the black version reviews say.

The plastic material is a nice white and sturdy feel. The color ring is pretty cool, cycles to different colors every 5 seconds it seems like with smooth transitions. Plugs do plug into it easily, maybe too easily. And they all work, powering up anything that needs juice. The USB plug seems to work well. It charged up my Note9 at 70% to 100% when I came back in 30 minutes, could've charged it sooner. Used to original Note9 cord, plugged right into the units USB socket, and didn't use the Note9 adapter.

The travel socket does fit very loosely. Like the black version, if you turn it upside down, with bare minimal shake, the travel plug falls out by itself. Unit is very light, hard to believe there's any surge protection, in terms of any joules. The flat plug is about 7/8 inch thick. My Belkin power strip plug is flatter, but doesn't have the cool LED light ring. Things plug is kinda loosely. On the other hand, the USB plugs in firmly. Too bad the plugs aren't as firm.

Because then, this would be a great unit. I plan to use mine on the desktop, to plug in the monitor and PC, and cell phone. For this purpose, since it works, the cool LED light ring, it's good enough, for the cool factor, number of plugs and USB available. Who knows how long it will last. But so far, it'll work. If the normal plugs held more firmly, this thing would be great.

3 week update. Going to have to return this. The plugs just walk out by themselves. There's no grip to hold it in. It just sits on top of the desk, and when the AC kicks on, the plug falls out. I know it's a bit of an exaggeration, but meaning, it doesn't hold well, and dangerous metal plug is exposed. Gave it 2 stars for the cool LED ring. But really, this unit needs to be taken off the shelf, only to return after it's been corrected, just like they do when salmonella is found in foods. I really wanted this to work, but it's just bad. And even the cool LED ring... I have one blocky plug that only fits on top. But the LED light switch is so touch sensitive, the blocky plug keeps changing the cycle, so I have to keep fidgeting it back to the auto color changing mode. Much to fix this unit has.

title: Awesome Product!!!
text:
This is 99% the perfect solution. Im coming from a custom UNRAID setup, that i left for various reasons, wont get into detail.

Here are the pros of this unit:
1. SIMPLE To Use and setup!
2. Setup your own cloud to sync folders/photos (i canceled iCloud 2TB monthly service)
3. The CPU you might think its slow, but it keeps up with my 8Core UNRAI Setup in regards to what i need it to do. (PLEX, Dockers, CloudServices etc).
4. It is 100x more reliable with time-machine backup from apple devices, UNRAID would work for 1-2 weeks, then id have to re-mount, re-tinker to get it to work again.
5. Speeds for transfering data to and from are the same, and is dependant on my 1GBE setup. I spend weeks trying to get 10GBE working with UNRAID i gave up on it. So for extra fast storage i run an Akitio Tunderbolt3 Raid Station which is amazing!!.
6. Finder works amazing with this synology, files are listed 100x faster than it would with UNRAID.
7. You get what you pay for, your not paying for the hardware here, your paying for the software people!!! You get a complete ecosystem of apps for all the major platforms.

Cons:
1. the nvme m.2 cache can only be attached to your disk volume. And DSM(The OS) decides what goes on cache. Its not predictable or guranteed stuff you always access will allways be read from SSD. MY Plex Artwork the 1st time i launch the webrowser for the day pulls the artwork from disk to cache, then the rest of the day artwork loads instantly, then the next day the first time i launch plex web portal again it has to pull artwork from disk to cache. (By the way this isnt a complete bottleneck, its still acceptable from a use perspective, its just not instant like i had it on UNRAID where artwork/database lived on SSD.

I talked to tech support and they took my request to allow users to create a volume on cache pool so i can run my PLEX(App/Database/Artwork/Dockers/Etc) 100% from SSD.

Overall i give this product 100% for the fact that it just works, and works GOOOOOD!!!

title: Best portable / travel telescope I have found.
text:
I bought this scope so I could take it in the car on family vacations and actually do astronomy. My other equipment is too bulky to fit in our car. Other portable small scopes are flimsy and just not up to the task and have proven to be both a waste of valuable money and car space. Fortunately this scope works as advertised and has allowed me to continue my hobby while on vacations...

While on vacation at our beach rental I was able to track planets with the telescope comfortably to 100x on the mount provided. Saw the red spot on Jupiter, the flash of the Cassini division on Saturn's rings. I think the 90mm may be better on the stock mount since it may weigh slightly less than the 102mm. I also used a different finder, than the red-dot finder, which may add a bit more weight to the optical tube assembly and put more demand on the stock mount.

At home, I use this scope on my CG-4 mount when not traveling. On the CG-4 I can take the scope up to it's maximum magnification (200x) but I seem to find 133x being the best balance of magnification and amount detail on Jupiter/Saturn to date. I also use a different finder than the one provided.

I enjoy the wide aperture this scope provides, it provides enough aperture to be my grab and go scope at home. This scope can also use 2" diameter eyepieces which provides a whole different capability than being limited to 1.25 inches. It's 600m focal length means that my 2" diameter 17mm Nagler eyepiece achieves 35X, but has an 82 degree wide field of view so it takes in lots of sky. I'm currently researching a 4.5mm 1.25 eyepiece so I can get to 133x without use of a barlow. I may also get a 4mm to see if the sweet spot is really 133x or 150x.

This scope and my CG-4 mount are now my quick grab and go scope. The smaller stock mount allows me to take it traveling and few travel scope mounts track as well as this design.

This is the best value travel scope I have found.

title: A great tablet for the price.
text:
I bought this table because I wanted a big size screen and an easy to set up and use tablet. This tablet fulfilled my expectations. The screen is bright and apps are installed with no hassle whatsoever. It is a great tablet for the price. Internal memory is enough to have many apps installed in it and it can be expanded with an SSD card. It runs at a good speed for all the applications that I have installed in it.
There is only one flaw that I encountered when I first set it up: the SSD card has to be in a specific format. I had purchased a Samsung Evo card which format is EXFAT, but this tablet is not compatible with that format; the default format for it is FAT32. When you place the SSD card in the memory slots it informs about this incompatibility and then asks if you want to format to make it compatible. Well, I agreed and that was a big mistake. That step corrupted the card and it could not be used in the tablet or any other device. That's when I contacted Customer Service and was wonderfully surprised. When they ask you not to returned the tablet but contact them first that they will make you happy, they are not kidding. They would really do their best to make you happy. What a pleasant experience I had. The lady that took care of my problem was outstanding. She handled the whole process in a very professional manner, was very responsive and never ever left me hanging. The most incredible thing is that she even got me a refund for the SSD card that has been corrupted. That is what I call "keeping the Customer happy, no matter what it takes". I would buy from this company again when the need arises and highly recommend this tablet to anyone looking to buy something similar. Way to go Hoozo! Keep the good work!

title: True CAT 7?
text:
I have the 50ft roll of this flat cabling running through a couple of rooms to a HDBASET adapter.

The HDBASET adapter feeds a projector with HDBASET in port. I have noticed intermittent connectivity issues with the wiring that are often resolved with some slight wire wiggling. I have a feeling that this cable is not truly up to the CAT7 spec and would be interested in seeing their certification if so.

I am only feeding 1080P which is about 3GBit/S and nowhere near the theoretical 100Gbit/S max transmit rate of CAT7 at my length. I have a feeling that this uses conductors closer to the 30AWG size range as the cable is very flexible, but in the same token is also very easy to break. You will not be able to shorten this cable and terminate your own RJ45 connector because of how thin the internal wiring is.

For an average consumer, this stuff probably works fine but I would be interested to see if anyone has attempted to run 100Gbit/s or 10Gbit/s through this ethernet cable.

text:
I bought these mainly for the noise cancellation, but the feature is pretty useless.

Tried on a plane and around other white noise, like a fan. At low volume, there is no difference. At high volume, it seems to just slightly increase the volume of your music.

All these off-brand headphones have tons of fake reviews. This one looked somewhat legit, but guessing I got duped.

I was replacing an old pair of Sony earbuds that died and are no longer made. Those had real active noise cancellation. Even at zero volume, when ANC is enabled, the plane engine noise would simply disappear. They also had a monitor button that would let you hear/talk to people around you while ANC was still enabled. It was magical and worked by listening to the noise around you and injecting an inverted sound wave to actively cancel it out. I’m guessing most of the cheap headsets out now are just trying to fake it.

title: Multi-port USB-C hubs are hard to find. Glad I found this one.
text:
Being the geek that I am, I couldn't believe my eyes, when I saw a device with FOUR USB-C outputs. I've been looking for one of these, for a while. Not to be confused with a docking station, this is strictly a hub. Three USB-A and Four USB-C is about the best I have seen. Being the latest adopted generation of USB, this is a god-send for someone with as many peripheral devices as I own and utilize, daily. It's a bit costly, but the return on investment (for me) well justifies the investment. I would own one (immediately) even had it not been a Vine item.
All ports tested well, but I only have one device that could even come close to testing the limits of this device (a second-gen NVMe to USB-C enclosure). Windows tools for this are not nearly equal to the task of testing overhead, throughput, power consumption, etc. I'll have to wait until I have free access to a Linux box to truly put this through its paces. I'm not familiar with this brand, and they seem to be relatively new (or I'm woefully out of touch with the industry). So far, this little device is screaming along and being a powered hub means it will not tax a notebook like unpowered devices. I would not bother with a device of this type that did not have an independent power supply.
Until I perform a more thorough set of tests, I can only give this four stars. Short term performance (even wih a heavy usage) cannot justify that much. My notebook port is revision 3.1, so the full capacity of the 3.2 revision cannot be fully tested. Longevity of performance is also just as important as performative quality. If something works great for a month, then dies, what's the point? For now, I'm extremely happy in the flexibility this hub provides.
No drivers were required, and recognition was instantaneous. At least I know that the backward compatibility with 3.1 is there (at least with my Dell). I do have to caveat my commend on its cost, however... While this isn't "bleeding edge," it is near the cutting edge. With USB 4 revision due to come out, soon (USB-IF is boasting 40GB/s) Adoption of this standard I have not yet discovered which VERSION of 3.2 this device is (there are three, listed below), ad it is not in the documentation.
SuperSpeed 5 GB/s
Superspeed 10 GB/s
SuperSpeed 20 GB/s
The above three are not easy to figure out, and your cable matters, also. While the protocol is rather confusing (even to those of us that geek out over things like this), it is further compounded by the fact that cables are not clearly identified with revision/version/capacity. Just because a cable has the right shape connector, and it works, doesn't mean you're getting the most out of your device... The fact that backward compatibility is virtually seamless to the user can often lead to disappointment, when the expectation does not align with reality. When one considers the GENERATION of the cable/device, the light at the end of the tunnel of understanding begins to dim. This is part of the reason adoption has been met with some resistance. This is one of the tech advancements that is moving faster than the general consumption public's ability to identify and understand the benefits (both perceived and real). For the time being, the vast majority of the public is happy just to know that there is no wrong way to plug in a USB-C cable, and this charges mobile devices MUCH faster (and cosumes power faster) than any previous revision and form factor. Whether USB-C or USB-A, know that there is sufficient bandwidth in most connectors to convert and carry audio/video signals for HDMI/DVI/DP outputs and below.
Fellow geeks can drop me a comment/question, if they're interested in the details discovered. I will see what I can find out.

It did improve speed but without using a wired connection for the satellite unit, speeds have gone from averaging 20Mbps to 40Mbps in our office.

This is a notable improvement but still a bit disappointing. My connection is 400Mbps and near the main router speeds often exceed this rate.

I plan to try the “extended” wired connection in the office but wish I didn’t have to drop money into another product to get the expected performance.

One plus is that the app made setup very simple. It is easy to send credentials to new devices and there are great features for monitoring network activity. You can set device specific hourly limits and easily prioritize signal to devices for streaming or gaming.

I did have a little trouble integrating our google home products. It took several attempts at “rebooting” the spy pucks to get them to log onto the new network. Eventually they worked but if you might avoid hassle by using Alexa based devices that are explicitly supported.

title: Buyer Beware: this device doesn't work on Surface Pro without being plugged into another hub. :-(
text:
I plugged this into my 1st gen Surface Pro, and it didn't work, couldn't even get USB power out of the ports, but if I plugged it into another (**unpowered**) USB hub and then into the Surface Pro everything worked fine. -- It really puzzles me that this was required because it basically makes it useless for portable devices (which you would think would be the primary use case of this device), but it suits my needs just fine. (I'm building a Batocera box out of an old Surface Pro, I can cram as much hardware in there as I want...)

Other thoughts: I've done some USB development in a past life, and the only time adding an unpowered hub between the device and the computer helped was when I was using REALLY cheap (non-USB compliant) parts and faking the USB protocol (essentially the hub acts as a signal filter and can be more forgiving than a strictly compliant device)... -- It makes me wonder just how cheaply this device was manufactured... -- At the end of the day though, it serves my purposes, and it does work (with the above caveats), so I'll give it a 3*. -- If I had been wanting to purchase this as a single hub for using my device more portably then I would have gave it 1* and returned it.
Other-other thoughts: It comes with a driver CD (what is this, 1998??) -- obviously that's unhelpful for my usecase (e.g. Batocera is Linux) -- but I have the same exact problems in Linux as I do in Windows (or even booting from USB) -- it works 100% just fine IF it's plugged into another hub first (even an unpowered one); if it's not, it won't even power anything plugged into it. -- If you experience a different result, your device might have a built-in USB hub. -- But if your device only has a single USB port, then there's a chance this device might not work for you.

EDIT 02/21/2020
I really liked the Fire stick for a while until the last few months I've noticed unresponsiveness from the UI, glitchiness, and general slowness. I currently have it plugged into an AC outlet to ensure it gets a constant stream of power. There are instances where the UI becomes unresponsive to the point where I have to reboot the device. When I scroll through the main Amazon Video UI, I experience all sorts of glitchiness and slowness. Sometimes it doesn't allow me to navigate through the titles and sometimes it's previewing the wrong title that I have selected. Trying to use Alexa is unresponsive and slow. I suppose that there is not enough computing power in these little sticks. I will probably look into getting the Fire TV Cube or a Roku device since they will have better processors.

I finally configured it with my TV and my Yamaha soundbar. I was very surprised that it can control my soundbar too since it is plugged into the TV via an optical cable. Many thanks to the software developers and engineers on this! This configuration is found in settings, which walks you through every step and allows you to select from a very long list of soundbar manufacturers.
The power button on the remote turns on my TV and since I have my soundbar powered by an energy saving surge protector, it turns on the soundbar only when the TV turns on. Saves on electric bills!
I enjoy the user interface that the developers have created. The only thing that I haven't really used much is Alexa voice control. It seems to work well, but I generally don't use it. Will have to test further. I don't like that I can't search in YouTube using voice recognition. I think that they should add this feature. It would save me the hassle of typing out words letter by letter. The signal strength is great - I don't have to point the remote directly at the TV to get a response.

Overall an amazing product. Would highly recommend. Google Chromecast is unfortunately inferior to the Fire Stick at this point.

title: Problematic USB-C
text:
I purchased the 22R Pro just before Christmas. In between the sales.

On the plus side, it's a nice monitor. Well built, and solid feeling. The pen works as well as the ones on the Wacom tablets I've used.

But.

One of the big selling points for the 22R-pro vs one of the lesser screens was that it would work on USB-C and power. No other cables.

This has never worked for me. I'm connecting to an Alienware 17R3 running Win 10 pro 64. First off, if the USB-C cable is connected to the USB-C port on my computer, the boot process hangs. I have to unplug the cable to get the machine to boot. If I let the boot process complete, and then plug in the USB-C cable, I get video. But the pen does not work.

If I connect the monitor's USB-C port to a USB3 port on my computer ( using the provided adapter ), and connect an HDMI cable for video, then it all works. I really didn't want the extra cable, but it's a workaround.

With a USB-C to USB-C connection, the pen has NEVER worked. I have tried different cables, and a different computer. Same results.

This is very disappointing, especially since I paid a premium for this monitor.

I have had an email in to XP-Pen's customer service for some time. They replied on another issue, but not this one. Probably the New Year holiday, but no message stating that.

I hope at some point there will be a firmware update or similar that will fix the USB-C issues. If that's important to you, perhaps you should hold off if considering a purchase.

title: Great product, but has a few issues that need to be addressed.
text:
Bought this May 2019. My biggest 3 factors were picture quality, NAS local storage compatibility, and price. It was between this and the Arlo (Arlo does not allow local NAS storage). I reached out to customer service and they were kind enough to offer me a discount code that I had just missed, which made the decision really easy.

Pros
- Excellent picture quality
- Excellent audio
- Easy to set up
- No subscription
- NAS compatible (huge plus for me)
- Battery is holding up pretty good for the amount of recordings (~60 per day between the cameras)

Cons
- Most recordings start with a lens flare for the first half second. Not a big issue, but a bit annoying
- No motion zones. I know this is an expected feature, but thought I would mention it. My cameras face the road, so I get quite a few more alerts than necessary.
- Abyssmal base station range (this is the biggest issue imo). I was hoping to set up the base station centralized so I could monitor the front and back. If I keep the cameras inside this might work. Once the camera moves outside, the base station immediately loses signal. It seems to have a hard time penetrating brick, even if only a dozen feet away. I managed to move the base to accommodate the range, but this was a huge disappointment, that should be addressed.
- Grass seems to be a dead zone that the camera doesn't pick up. My cameras have a bit of grass and driveway/road in frame. Grass often gets ignored when there's motion, while pavement gets picked up quite well.

Overall I'm quite happy with my purchase as it meets my needs fine, but it has a few issues that need to be addressed.

Edit 6/24/19:
- Motion zones are in beta and available for testing. I am still tweaking the settings, so I won't comment fully on this yet, but what I've noticed so far.

I intended to use this to decrease road recordings to save battery. The motion zones still record outside of specified zones, you just don't get notifications for it. An option to only record in motion zones would be ideal for my situation, as my cameras batteries are still being drained from excessive recordings.

- I also hoped the motion zones would solve my issue with the cameras not picking up in the grass very well. With notifications only being pushed from activity within the motion zone, I increased the sensitivity, but had to turn it back down as I was getting false notifications every couple of minutes.

I appreciate the feature, it just isn't quite what I was hoping for. I'll tinker with it some more to see about providing a more thorough update.

title: Must be used in pairs.  Despite the listing it is not a “splitter.”
text: In simple terms, an Ethernet cable has 8 wires in it.  But, only 4 of the wires are normally used, so another 4 wires are available in the same cable to carry a second data signal.  Using these devices in pairs lets you use a single cable to carry 2 signals.  In my situation I have a barn about 250 feet away from my house, too far away for a wireless signal to make it from my home wireless router. But I do have a buried cat5e cable that was placed during construction.  I want both a reliable cable TV signal via Ethernet, plus a reliable computer connection.  So, the home end BaseT plugs into 2 separate Ethernet ports on my cable modem, then into the single cable running underground. In the barn, the second BaseT takes the two individual signals and separates them to my television cable box and to my computer.  Essentially, the final result is as if I had dug another 250 foot trench and buried a second cat5e cable.  But with the pair of BaseT units I was able to use the single buried cable for carrying 2 separate data signals.  Again, the BaseT device is not a true splitter.  They must be used in pairs.  If you try to use them as splitters, with one input  into the single wire end, one of the twin wires receives the signal, and the other wire is dead.  The reason for one star reviews is that those buyers did not understand what they were ordering.

I ordered this for a co-worker who has a major problem with dry eyes. It's been an almost debilitating condition for her and made more difficult by the fact that her job requires her to spend much of her time at the computer. We had tried several remedies to no avail, so we thought we're try this. She is amazed at the difference it makes. The pictures show the difference in ambient temperature between the screens with and without the filter. Without, the temperature is 80 degrees and climbing. With, it is 73 degrees and steady. She is so pleased with it she is ordering another filter for her other monitor and one for home.

This is allowing her to continue doing the job she loves, and I am very happy to have found a solution that works for her.

title: Some great ideas, but unfortunately not practical for me
text:
TL;DR: Bought this bag as an everyday work/school/travel bag. Storage is great, including ability to expand. Did comfortably fit my 16" laptop. Unfortunately

I bought this bag to use as my everyday work/school bag, as well as to use as a personal item while travelling. I had the bag for about a week before returning it, so I cannot speak to the durability but the quality of materials and construction seemed good. Also, the storage is great on this thing. Plenty of pockets and options for storage, each one well made and seemingly well thought out. The zipper across the bottom to expand the storage is really great. I used this when I had my clunky laptop in the bag, and then shrank it back down when I just had papers and folders.

In fact, 90% of this bag was a 5 star bag for me, but the design and implementation of the flap was so poor that it made the bag just about unusable for me--to the point of returning the bag.

My issue is that the flap is surprisingly difficult and cumbersome to open and close. I like to be able to open/close my shoulder bag while it is still hanging on my shoulder. This was almost impossible for me because of the buckle placement and design. The buckles are tucked up underneath the front flap, I guess so that they're not visible, but that makes them pretty hard to reach. You can see in one of the pictures I'm reaching the buckle from above, which requires the sturdy flap to be bent way up. Even if you get the thing unbuckled, good luck getting it buckled again. The female end of the buckle has a couple small ridges (pictured), presumably to guide the buckle in. But the buckle also has this groove in the bottom (pictured), and if you don't line the buckle up perfectly straight, the groove goes over the ridges, preventing you from buckling once it's 75% of the way in. One of the pictures shows this issue--the buckle is almost completely buckled, but won't continue past where it is shown. I will have to remove it completely and re-insert it. When I'm doing this from above (as the bag is hanging from my shoulder) I sometimes have to do it multiple times to get it lined up perfectly. Instead of guiding the buckle in, these ridges pull it off course.

So my next idea was to only buckle the bag if I knew it would need to stay buckled for a while (like while travelling) and if I'm going to be in and out of it, leave it unbuckled. The problem then is that the top handle becomes unusable, and picking it up by the top handle while the flap is unbuckled causes it to sway heavily to one side and hang open (pictured). I understand the handle is on the flap, but even moving the handle off-center would have helped with this issue.

I don't know how much of an issue this would be to other people. Like I said, most of the bag was a five-star bag for me except for the one-star flap. I averaged that out to a three-star rating. If I had to use this bag, I would. There are benefits that help to offset the drawbacks. But in a world where I can choose my bag, I choose a different bag.

Pros:
- Great storage options and capacity
- Seemingly well-constructed
- Flexible options (different storage pockets, expandable main storage compartment, etc.)

Cons:
- Flap design makes it very cumbersome to open and close, and handle placement makes it impractical to leave open

title: Perfect signal in all rooms and smart connect rocks
text: I ordered this product for 2 reasons, signal strength and smart connect. The firmware on my old R6220 Netgear router updated and made it where I had to have a separate username and password for both the 2.4 ghz an the 5 ghz bands that my high speed connection puts out. It initially was not required but to have one username and password to push the speed thru and my devices would use the bandwidth they needed. With this I am getting full strength in my bedroom whereas I did not before. With ONE username and ONE password! I can now enjoy full strength service anywhere in the house. My cable company offers 1 gig speeds so I’m also going to get a 10 gig modem to run higher speeds up to 3.5 gigs which is all this router will push through. Might not need anything stronger than 1 gig but I certainly want to use the router and new modems potential. I believe the tri band and the 6 antennas pushing the single out hard, allows me to get the most usage of my connection. If I had known about this sooner, oh boy would I have gotten it. Was kind of forced to because of the annoying separate usernames and passwords, and weak signal strength of my old Netgear router. Netgear is by far the best and easiest to use and set up. I’m happy to use their products. Best one I’ve ever had so far.

title: Good for it’s price.
text: First Impressions: So far I am really loving this tablet. For the price point, it delivers everything that you are looking for as it gets the job done with pretty good accuracy. Other tablets around a similar price point can't really compare to this one IMO if I didn't know better I would have said that this tablet belonged somewhere around the $150 range. The glove, on the other hand, I feel like its too tight it kinda feels like my fingers are suffocating in a way that's the only real criticism I can say about them. Other than that they are perfect with the standard minimalist design as well as the font of which the logo is in compliments this very well. But onto the packaging itself, the outlier gives off a very professional minimalistic vibe and looks much better than others out there IMO. The box feels sleek and gives off that new tablet smell that I just can't go without. The only thing I would say about the packaging is about how the USB-C cord was packed inside I felt like it was slightly difficult/less enjoyable to unbox that aspect of the product. But honestly, this can all be overlooked because of how well the tablet itself performed. If anything the tablet alone would have been worth the entire price if not more. It has really great accuracy and decent registration distance as in you don't have to physically touch the tablet with the pen in order to move the cursor. In conclusion, I would defiantly recommend this tablet it is a high performance but affordable option that is well worth the price and deserving of a 5* rating. The only thing I can really call a con is it’s pressure sensitivity. Other than that if you want a decent easy to use drawing tablet this is the way to go.

When we finished grilling, the speakers were brought back into the dinning room and filled that room with rich clear crisp music, the bass could be heavier, but it is not that it's not present! For less than 100 dollars you cant go wrong with these beautiful speakers which come packaged in these very nice zippered carrying cases, that allow you to take them anywhere you go, to the beach, in the car, camping etc.
The battery life on these is just incredible as well, I charged them up before everyone got here, and they played from 5pm til almost midnight, today I booted them back up and they are still going strong! I highly recommend these blue tooth stereo speakers, at this price, they are a great value and beat anything on the market!

text:
This is so far the best sounding music player I have listened to. It is slightly more analytical than Hifimans r2r2000 and a lot more open and precise than the top end sony players. Extremely responsive and intuitive user interface! Very good battery life; in the typical mobile use with IEM phones (wich implies the amplifier set to low gain) the battery easily lasts 7-8 hours. On high gain mode the battery life suffers but that is only needed for very power hungry large headphones, so not really a mobile use case. For reference my standard home use large headphones Sennheiser HD-800 work just fine with medium gain amp settings. The only case for high gain so far is with fairly inefficient planar magnetics. The high gain modes drives them just fine!

On the often critisied large size. This is a big unit compared to a standard smartphone, but it is still smaller than a traditional walkman, so perfectly usuable for travelling, not so much for in pocket use while running or doing sports, but then who really uses a super high end player during sports.

title: This 1080P Video Camera represents and good value for the money.
text:
[[VIDEOID:3c6fb4fd32e2599a19b4530a7cf22fc6]] You get quite a bit for the price. It takes decent 1080P video and has pretty nice auto white-balance and auto exposure. Exposure compensation is, of course, a bit slow compared to a higher end camera but it shoots a nice picture as long as the lighting stays fairly consistent. I found color to be pretty accurate as well.

The stereo boom microphone attachment was surprisingly good with gain and low-cut features. Personally, I did not see a big advantage to the stabilizer handle although the lens hood was useful. That it has HDMI out and 3.5mm audio in is a big plus at the price point as it makes this camera viable for webcasting and vlogging. The remote is very handy in this case.

There is not much zoom bandwidth and the zoom is all digital - to be expected at this price point. Overall, not a bad bang for the buck.
