Fast Forward 7 hours later of uninstall re install reboot reading tech support forums , I finally got it to work once, then turned off the machine and back on and it went to a black screen again.... Not fun, so I decided to uninstall the Razer Software mind you the software even though they say keeps the drivers up to date, and provides you the latest firmware, there is none available and only updates the software so unless they package deliver firmware inside the synapse software for it, I do not even see a button for firmware update nor does it even list what firmware is installed on the device. HOWEVER removing the device + uninstalling the razer software and rebooting and letting windows find the device and install it then IGNROING the razer software makes the device actually work, somewhat, it still has issues from time to time getting a signal so I have to uninstall it reboot re install and it will work again.

Now here is the thing, audio was easy to get in as you just have to add the proper audio input source like you do with your mic, easy peasy, when it does work THIS Device is pretty good, color reproduction is decent , audio is fine so forth. Getting it to work is a whole other beast in itself.

Issues I have with the device, there is no drivers, I know that sounds funny but hear me out, the device uses the same MS usb / cam drivers that every other device has used since 2006 (driver tested it with razer synapse installed and not installed.) , it is identically the same Microsoft driver dated 6/21/2006 , actually on further inspection I attached a photo it uses the same driver that my usb 2.0 webcam that is embedded into my laptop. When I say Identical its down to the same driver revision . Normally this would not be a problem however the device is highly unusable in its current state, and honestly I do not see razer updating it anytime soon.. Which is sad because when it works it works well , if you can ever get it to work at all.

title: Wow! Better than expected!
text:
Just got this installed and was surprised at 1. How easy it was to install and 2. How good it sounds..

As many have said- there are no instructions- but the labeled wiring diagram picture is spot on. I bought a harness for my truck (FJ Cruiser) at Advance then connected the wires. Boom! I had sound.

The backup camera is a different story. I was unsure how to wire it and really over-thought it because for some reason it didn't make sense to me.

All you need to know are these steps:
1. Find the wire to your reverse light and strip a portion of it.
2. Splice the red wire from the camera power plug to the little red wire on the yellow RCA plug, then splice them to the bare wire on your reverse light wire.
3. Connect the black wire from the camera plug to a ground then plug the camera in.
4. Connect the other end of the yellow RCA plug to the "camin" jack. On the back of the stereo and splice the other little red wire to the pink wire on the back of the stereo.
5. Start your car and wait for the stereo to boot up. Put it in reverse and the camera till turn on.

This should make more sense when it is all in front of you.

Other items to note:
-This unit does have a sub-out port and other RCA ports.
-it also has a second video in port to install a second camera or dvd player or whatever.

Operation-
Buttons are clearly marked and intuitive. Super easy to figure everything out.

If your phone us NOT connected you can use the radio and Bluetooth. The Bluetooth does display the song artist and song and has ff and rw buttons.

If you connect your android phone via USB cord it acts as a screen mirror. Whatever is on your phone screen will be displayed on your stereo screen.

I tested it with Spotify, Waze, and Netflix and all worked great with the sound coming through the car speakers. I had music playing on Spotify while viewing the gps on Waze.

The only downside is that if you turn your phone screen off the unit also goes black. But on the up side it does charge the phone while plugged in so we'll call it a draw.

The sound quality is better than the stereo that was in it. Plenty loud and the manual eq allows you to tune it.

Completely satisfied with this- especially for the price. I needed something quick and wasn't expecting much. Very impressed... But I have only had in installed for a few hours.

title: (Updated: Scratched After Falling 2 Feet) Sturdy Phone Case, but Button Covers are Too Firm
text:
(Updated to 1 star):
My phone slid off my couch with this case on. It dropped 2 feet, at most, onto an end table. The case got scratched. This is a $40 case that is slippery, difficult to use because of the firm button covers, and it can't even resist scratches from falling 2 feet onto an end table. I'm returning it. Apple should be ashamed that a case this bad costs $40. I would love to know what they used for their "thousands of hours of testing" when it can't even be protected from one of the most common types of falls - sliding off a piece of furniture.

Mostly what you'd expect from a phone case. Fits the iPhone 11 Pro securely. The material is not overly slippery, so I'm not worried about it sliding off my couch or out of my pockets while sitting down (e.g., while driving). From what I can tell the material would be very difficult to scratch, though I've only tried running my fingernails through it. Anything more than that I'd be afraid to try since the case is so expensive.

Works with my wireless charger, and no issues getting the wired charger plugged in either.

I wish the button covers weren't so firm. You have to put noticeable effort into pressing the volume up/down and power button - even significant effort depending on the angle you're trying to press the button. For example, if my phone is laying down on my couch armrest, and I reach over with my left hand to turn the volume up/down, it is very difficult to press the buttons in. I've never had this issue with a phone case before. I'm a 24 year old man with about average strength. Anyone who has weak fingers, grip, or arthritis would likely have a very hard time with the buttons. If the buttons ease up over time, I'll update my review to be higher. For now I'm deducting 2 stars because it is really inconvenient.

$40 is pricey as well, but you get the peace of mind from having the official case from the manufacturer of the phone. The description says it was put through thousands of hours of testing, so I would hope that it holds up well over time.

title: Cooling cooling cooling!!!
text:
I rarely leave reviews, but this one needs to happen.

Although you get 4 cooling fans inside this case, do not let that fool you. I have absolutely 100% brand new everything into this, and the case is the only mistake I made in the build.

Here's why: The front cover leaves very little room between the fans, the case, and the front cover, leaving very little area for air intake (or exhaust if configuration is changed). The main culprit is the tinted plexiglass face. The clearance between the fans and the cover are approximately 3/16 inch.

The other main issue is the tempered glass removable cover. Luckily it is removable, or I would not be able to use this case at all. I have also changed the airflow of the 6 cooling fans. This also required that I remove the tinted plexiglass front and the tempered glass side cover while computer is on, AND turn ALL the fans on to 100%.

I have considered purchasing a cooling system other than the cooling fan that came with the Ryzen 5 3600X CPU, but have since decided to purchase a different case altogether AND purchase a cooling unit for the CPU as well.

Overall, this case is quite attractive for looks and price, BUT the case is NOT a good pick, even IF you are willing to modify. It's not worth the time, effort, and money to modify, when a much better case can be utilized with little to no modifications for the same basic cost.

title: Works ... but needed some finessing
text:
I'll preface this review by saying there are probably more permutations of PC components than stars in the universe... so my experience may be different than yours. But I'm leaving this review in hopes that someone searching for my same issue finds this and is helped.

Installing the card was easy. I put it in a PCI-16x slot. (PCI slots are backwards compatible.) The only problem is that the card was in AHCI mode by default. (It says "Passthrough AHCI") I was not adding a new drive. I was replacing my boot drive, which was in IDE mode. Windows does not like switching. So I received the dreaded "inaccessible boot device" flavor of the blue screen of death.

I searched my BIOS to see if I could change this ATA miniport card to IDE mode. Alas, I don't think you can, or at least I couldn't with my motherboard. So after much Googling, I stumbled upon a Microsoft tech support article titled ""INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE" error message after you install a third-party ATA-miniport driver or change the SATA mode of the boot drive on Windows 8-based computer," which had steps to resolve the issue.

Short version: Before moving your IDE boot drive to this device, you need to force windows to boot into safe mode the next time it starts. (After issuing the command, but before restarting, move your boot drive to this device.) Then when you next boot, safe mode causes Windows to rebuild the storage controllers, and thus support the AHCI boot drive that used to be IDE. Even though I have Windows 10, I followed the steps for Windows 8 and I'm happy to report that I'm typing this review with a faster boot drive happily in my system.

4 stars, because it was easy enough to install the physical card, but came with zero documentation (which I expected because... hey, $25). Taking away one star because I had to troubleshoot on my own.

title: Poison and antidote
text:
I have written books on privacy and am a lifelong techie.

I owned a ring doorbell and thought to add a couple other cameras to cover other areas. I set them up and they work.

But...

An orange ad pops up on the bottom of the IOS app cajoling you to buy an upgraded “protection” plan in the next 30 days. This plan stores the videos for a little while. I didn’t want that, for privacy reasons (easy to hack ring cameras and these were interior) and saw no reason to pay for something I didn’t want just to get rid of an ad.

Being patient with tech, I waited the month. But you guessed it, the ad is still there telling me it’s not too late.

I searched everywhere for how to disable it. It’s annoying. No luck.

I chatted with ring support where the rep cheerfully typed that the only way to get rid of their ad is to buy their plan.

Sell the poison then the antidote.

Crazy. I wish I had never bought it. Arrogant and snarky customer support policies does not bode well for the future of Ring

You’ve been warned.

***

Oh, to add on to the customer service part. I was contacted by a Ring person who offered to "educate" me. Because a big honking ad will no longer be annoying after I see the light, I guess. She stated that they aren't going to remove the ad.

So why does this piss me off? This is a hardware device that I (and maybe you) bought. It's not a software service that's subsidized. Them running a nag ad at you is uncalled for and should, worst case, be able to opt out from. This is a disturbing trend lately. Look at LG smart TVs. They are actually doing 3rd party popup ads--on the tv! Not Netflix, not Roku or Apple TV, but on the hardware which you bought and are captive to.

The problem with Ring is that there is, as far as I know, no way to see the video feed without using their app. To use the product, you must see their ad. Right now, it's nagging about a plan I don't need. But once we're all desensitized to the idea, who knows what comes next?

text: BE WARNED BEFORE YOU BUY THIS! PLEASE READ! I checked the wiring using a meter and it is in fact wired to the 5V pins on the USB port, there is no data connections. SO in short if you were planning on using a USB cord and a power bank to power this as you build your projects you CAN NOT, unless you make a custom cord with a USB Type A male on each end! For the price I'm not going to return it and just power it thru the barrel plug connector on this board, at least they got that part right!

title: Software update required
text: I played 4 rounds using this watch, on three different courses.  The courses were identified and the yardage was similar to that identified on the devices used by others, usually differing by three yards (+/-), which will not negatively impact most of us duffers.  The sad part:  The watch did not want to switch between military (24 hour) and civilian (12 hour) display.  Scorekeeping was awkward, in one outing it logged two rounds (one was played) scored were recorded between the two rounds.  On the upside, customer support was responsive (via email) and after a couple of weeks, presumably to allow time for coding changes, provided a software update with instructions for downloading to the watch - with the caveat that this may cause all scores to be erased. title: EXTREME DISAPPOINTMENT!
text:
FINAL UPDATE: Read the 1 star reviews first! Mine is gone, and just in time Amazon has dropped the price of this system by $100. They must be getting a lot of them returned, Too bad there are so many unbelievable reviews skewing the average.

UPDATE3; Going back. Too many things wrong with design and operation. Why?

Battery life sucks. And without optional power cord, cameras have to be removed to charge battery. Forget about mounting high out of reach. Stealing them would be easy (even if they won’t work for the thief)

Picture quality poor. My 10 year old phone takes better pictures.

Long lag time. If you get an alert, whoever tripped it is long gone.

Continuous monitoring, which only works for an additional $20 month fee, burns batteries.

Identifying things is poor. It’ll pick up a squirrel, but it didn’t catch my car pulling up driveway 20 feet away. When it does detect something, several seconds pass before it starts recording.

Range gets worse the further camera gets from base.

And, the final straw, from what I hear, local storage stops working without subscription. $3 month PER CAMERA.

Don’t judge this system by 5 star reviews. Like so many things on Amazon, a lot of one line 5 star reviews are fake or planted. Judge your purchases by the believability of the 1 and 2 star reviews.

UPDATE2; Removing another star. After seeing an ad for Ultra 2 camera (unrelated to Pro 2. You need to address your numbering system), I just wanted to know if the battery was the same as Pro 3 uses, so opened chat on their website. Instead of getting an answer I was met with “What is you first name?”. Fine. But then “What is your last name?”. Then “What is your email?”. Just to get a simple question answered.

This goes with exaggerated claims that battery life is up to 6 months. Try a week! Maybe if the camera is turned off in a drawer it’ll last more than a month. If it lasts a week in 70 degree weather, how long will it lasts when temps hit freezing?

Add to that, quality deteriorates rapidly as distance from hub increases. Camera located < 20 feet from hub delivers pathetic images.

I have a week before 30 day return to Amazon window expires. It may go back.

UPDATE: Removing one star. Battery life is horrendous. I can just see myself removing these things in the winter every few days just to charge the freakin’ batteries. Forget about mounting higher than you can reach easily, making them easy to steal in a few seconds.

Had for about a week, with some pleasant surprises and several disappointments. Starting at the beginning... there are two mounts provided. A magnetic one and a screw in one. They recommend not mounting the magnetic one over 6.5’. Why? Probably because it is not a strong connection, but might survive a six foot drop. The screw in one uses a standard tripod thread, but provides no way to turn the mount to screw it in. You pretty much have to turn the camera to put it on. So, why such a fuss about the mounts? Because unless you buy an expensive charging cable (proprietary connection), you have to remove the camera every time to charge it. “Oh!” You say. Just pop the camera out of the shell. You can’t. The shell has that proprietary connection. There’s no way around it without buying an external charger, a spare shell (~$30) or a cable. Unless you don’t mind spending more money, it will prove annoying at best.

The app is not well conceived for changing settings or accessing recordings. This morning, workers had a jackhammer going across the street. No problem. Just turn off the microphone. Except that didn’t work. You have to turn off smart notifications for audio. There’s no easy way to just mute the camera for a set time. And, so far, it seems, turning off smart notifications isn’t working either. Sensitivity should be adjustable.

Next complaint, subscriptions. If you’re trying to figure out if you should buy an Arlo 2, 3, or Ultra, most is in the subscription. With a 2, you get 7 days of free rolling cloud storage. The 3 will give you higher quality, and distinguishes between types of alerts, but you pay for it. PER CAMERA. $4 a month for each camera, or $10 for up to 5 cameras. No option to get the scaled back free storage on an Arlo 3. (Although you can buy an Arlo 2 camera and use it with the Arlo 3 hub).

Let’s talk about that higher quality image. When the sun goes down, the Arlo 3 provides nice images, but only if it’s mounted ideally. One camera was out in the open, and provided me with a clear b&w image at night. The other was mounted in an alcove, and the camera was tricked into thinking it was brighter than it was, because of the reflective surfaces right next to it. So, instead of a nice monochrome image, all I got was an unviewable pixilated color image with no shadow detail (the entire image other than reflections). You can’t choose image quality settings. The preview shows what you’d want, but when you look at the live camera, it’s useless.

Compared to my 5 year old Uniden, the Arlo is a huge step forward. But then so are most devices using digital imaging. One nice feature is a USB port to plug in a flash drive. You can’t view the files remotely, but it does give you copies of all events recorded by the cameras. (Nice if you don’t want to pay for cloud storage on all your cameras).

Some experimentation may solve some of the mounting issues. Although the design shortcomings are just stupid, easily correctable things, that seem to mostly be there to get you to spend more money on optional stuff. They advertise “Works with Alexa”, but I’d bet spending $70-$230 on an Echo Show would prove to be a nightmare with poor results. If you want continuous streaming that can be reviewed later, that’ll cost you, too. Another $20 a month. Something that could be easily provided with local storage if they wanted.

Like so many things, this is really nice product, and I’m glad I bought it. But it could be so much better if the company put less weight on profit, and more on functionality.

title: Easy to install and working fine
text:
What good is a review without some context? So, I've been building my own computers for 20 years. This power supply was purchased for a new build. It's nothing really power hungry, ASRock phantom 4 B550 Pro, AMD Ryzen 5 3600, only using a nvme drive and 16 gigs of ram. So I'm not really putting it through the paces. Currently using a GPU with no power cord needed, but will definitely be adding something beefier very soon. There's plenty left of the 650w for a video card, though. I will update the review if I run into any issues.

Power supplies are not really easy to review without proper testing equipment, but here's my experience with this one. It fit right into my case (PS on the bottom if that matters to anyone), it powers everything I need it to, which isn't saying much right now. It is very quiet. In my experience, heavier power supplies seem to be better quality. This has a pretty good weight to it considering the amount of the casing that is open for ventilation. Time will tell about durability and stability, but I have not seen anything to indicate there might be a problem.

The one thing I really don't like is that the cables are a ribbon style instead of round. I'm pretty OCD about cable management, and the flat cables don't like to stay where you put them. Also, I'm using a mid tower and they are long enough to reach everything, but not quite long enough to route and zip tie them around the edges of the motherboard when using the connectors closest to the PS, Not a big deal. If you are building with a mini tower and/or not using a full ATX motherboard, you won't experience this at all.

title: The greatest upgrade you can make for an old computer

These are $20 a pop. This is the greatest performance to price upgrade you can make for your old computer.

Although I have been using laptops with SSD's since 2012, I have never exactly purchased one as an upgrade since they came always stock. However, prices have become so low for NAND memory that it is economically feasible to just throw these into all my obsolete computers to give them new life. I popped these in several very old Core 2 Duo laptops that my parents still use and now they run Windows 7 with ease even if they are only running at SATA II speeds. Anyways, 4k random read/write speeds are the most important for OS execution, so the sequential read/write speeds don't have to be the fastest.

You will need to purchase a SATA to USB cable as they do not provide one.

I also recommend that you use Aomei Backupper to clone all your partitions. EaseUS does not work very well with Kingston drives for some reason.

title: Still loving it after 2 years!
text:
I needed a good backpack for everyday use as well as for travel. This bag meets all my needs.

First, I noticed the material is thick and strong like denim. I have not tested it's water resistance but it certainly seems like it would repel rainwater for a short period of time.

Second, I love how many pockets there are inside. When traveling, you want all your stuff handy when you need it. With this bag, I can have my charger, my medications, my tissues, my passport, and whatever else I may need in a convenient, separated, and easy to get to pocket.

Third, this backpack holds a lot. I got the smaller size, which fits nicely in the airplane storage under the seat with room for my feet as well. Despite the smaller size, I can fit a tablet, a change of clothes, cell phone, backup battery, passport, medications, some toiletries, a Kindle, and everything else I needed for 24 hours of travel. So I was very impressed!

Lastly, the cushioned back liner makes it comfortable to carry even when it's full of stuff. I also want to note that the "security pocket" in the back liner is a great idea. However you will not want to store more than a little bit of cash and maybe a passport. Anything thicker than that and it begins to interfere with comfort while carrying.

There are only one criticism I can think of. The shoulder straps do not adjust easily while you are carrying the backpack. This is probably a result of using a thick cotton material for the straps instead of cheap nylon. So the friction makes it harder to adjust. However, I think I prefer the look and feel of the cotton over the nylon and over time it should become easier to adjust.

+++++UPDATE: MAY 2021+++++
Changed from a 4 to a 5 star because this bag really held up over the past 2 years and shows almost no wear. Also the straps adjust easily now, which was something I complained about above. I am not sure when that happened but it didn't take too long. Probably should have updated this review sooner. However, I am still super impressed with this backpack! Definitely worth thirty something bucks for sure.

title: Fantastic Product - 10x faster than Wifi6!
text:
Our bandwidth increased from 70mb/s to 700mb/s with Moca, using the existing coax cable system in our house.
10x faster than the latest Wifi 6, no matter how far are you from the router.
The good news is that you can use it with a cable modem on the same coax cable.
Here is how:
1. connect all moca adapter on the 'moca' coax port to the wall.
2. the moca adapter with the cable router should be connected through the in/out port with the cable modem.
3. then the cable model should be connected with a lan cable with from the router's ethernet port to the moca's ethernet port.
4. then the rest of the moca adapters should be just connected with the 'moca' coax port and then use an ethernet to connect to local computers. amazing! :)

title: Works at rated speed with a B450 motherboard
text:
I am gradually upgrading my gaming PC, and these memory modules are part of that multi step process. It was difficult for me to choose this as this was not specifically listed in the supported memory of my motherboard. But as an enthusiast builder, I gave it a try, and it works.

My setup is:
- Ryzen 9 3900X
- 32GB (2X 16GB) G.Skill Trident Z Neo Series 3600MHz C 16-19-19-39
- MSI B450I Gaming Plus AC
- MSI Geforce RTX 2080 Ventus OC
- No overclock, cpu and memory running at rated speeds with XMP enabled

I went from a Vengeance LPX 3200Hz memory module to this GSkill 3600Hz as Ryzen CPUs love faster memories. At first I tried different memory settings, speed, timings, all of them causing crashes. What eventually worked for me is just run in default settings with XMP Profile 1 enabled, and it detected the timings perfectly running at the rated speed of 3600MHz. I will not bore you with benchmarks and technical details, there are lots of those information out there. But I have a real life usage example that is evidence of a jump in memory speed. I usually have 2 windows of Chrome browser that has 20 tabs each opened for work. When I load all of these tabs at the same time on 2 windows, it is very snappy than before. We know how Chrome browser is a memory hog, but these memory modules can handle loading 40 tabs (2 windows) in a snap.

So far, I am very impressed with these memory modules. Installation and configuration was almost auto in the BIOS, and it just works fine. I am planning on getting a B550 or X570 motherboard later on to get a little more headroom for overcloking. And, yeah, the RGB light is pretty.

title: Essential for international travel
text:
I reviewed an earlier version of this product but now it's even better: the previous one had a fuse that, if blown via an overload, had to be replaced. That's been replaced with a protective cut-off that doesn't involve fuse replacement. That's rather a nice improvement.

Otherwise things remain the same. One side of this cube shaped device is a socket that accepts virtually any plug: European continental, US, British, and most Asian. The other side is a series of plugs, extended and retracted via a series of sliders on another side of the cube. The plugs cover the same (large) list of countries. They lock in place and are released with a button. It all works very well.

So that lets you use this as a plug adapter, but there's more. On the last side of the cube there are four USB ports used for charging. You can use them all at once. They put out up to 2.4 amps, and are controlled via a sensing chip. Maximum total current is 3.4 amps. Charging times vary with your device and number of devices connected, but the convenience here is just enormous. ONE device acts as a plug adapter and charger for most of the world.

This is not inexpensive but it is well worth it. It comes with a nice little cloth zipper case and should serve the international traveler very well. Five stars for sure.

Each receiver comes with a battery within the pack that your have to insert, but the remote controller does NOT come with batteries. I deducted a star because of this. You need two AAA batteries. As you can see from my photo the receivers aren’t huge, but a nice size.

I also love that the kit comes with stickers and labels you can apply to the remote controller in order to know which button goes with each receiver. I highly recommend this product and will be purchasing extras as gifts.

title: This beauty gets hot !!
text:
Very fast, very quite, everything as advertised, no complaints other than.....this thing get hot ! I bought a five fan cooler for it to sit on, the PC is for my wife who ( yea, I know, its way overkill for her use, but I am disabled and may eventually become bed ridden so I got her one that was very much overkill for her mild usage just in case ) basically just uses it for FB each evening an plays very easy games requiring virtually no internet or enough CPU / GPU usage to even break a sweat.....yet, it runs 20C+ hotter than my big desktop in every stage, sometimes more.

As an example, it idles at 40C, all 6 cores, sometimes up a bit more, never less than 39C, and this is in a house I keep very cool, the house is never above 18.3C ambient air, so all the PC'S have a good head start in this place. To make sure that this PC will hold up if I do have to use it myself one day to play games, I decided I need to download a modern game that would at least tax the cpu/gpu and see what the temps do. Ran the same game ( free demo of newest Tomb Raider, has DX12, maxed detail to run the temps up a bit, and ran them on both computers.

On this desktop, which I understood would of course run cooler than most any laptop that I built, I never got past 70C on any of the 4 cores ( 3770K ocked to 4500GB ) and it has the same 8Gb Nvidia 1070 that the new laptop has in it, so seems like as fair as it was gonna get. I had trouble playing that game very well as I am a FPS guy and not a 3rd person player, but in the fairly short time I played, over 40 minutes it was averaging 90 to 93 C on the 6 cores, and I never even made it to any fight scenes, intense game parts, etc.....sooooo....although that was not a critical temp yet, I am not happy with temps that high so quickly, especially on a laptop being assisted by a five fan precooler sitting under it at all time and always on high.

On the other hand, not a single other negative to list, and BTW, while playing that game taxing the system best I could, with everything maxed out, played like a solid gold watch, and was very quiet.

Easily would have been a 5 star, kept the last one out cause i am still not sure about how it is gonna handle the heat. Otherwise, all thumbs up !!

text: Had this antenna for just over a year and it was working just fine.  Had to disconnect it for a move and the coaxial connector on the antenna came off with the coax cable when we tried to remove it.  It is a poorly designed bulk head connector where it can spin with the coax cable when trying to tighten it or loosen it.  The outcome was that the antenna's connector came off with the cable rendering the antenna useless. I am an RF engineer and I understand how to make these types of connections more robust, a simple reversal of the barrel connector where the fixed hex head portion is on the outside where a 5/16" wrench could be used to hold it would have prevented the issue.  I contacted Winegard support on this and they agreed this was a problem but said that it was passed the 1 year warranty and would not cover it.  No offer for a discount on a replacement or antenna or anything.  I am extremely disappointed with this company and would not recommend any of their products based on this experience.

title: Not a good value. The listing has misinformation. See below for a review of the laptop.
text:
The first thing I want to say is this laptop is not a good value; the asking price is too high for what the product has to offer. This doesn't mean it's a bad laptop, rather, for the money, there are better options out there. The listing also has misinformation in it, notably it mentions an "HD touch screen" but this laptop does not have a touch screen. It also says it comes with Windows 10 Home, which is technically true, but it comes with S mode enabled. S mode does offer a value if this is going to be handed to a child who could be prone to getting viruses because this mode restricts executables (Apps) from running other than the Windows store. The good news is you can disable this, but it requires logging in with a microsoft account to do so. You also cannot revert back to S mode. To make this change, open Settings and go to Activation, then click the Go to the store option.

Given that this laptop is a budget laptop, and is probably aimed at non-tech savvy users who just want a machine to do work or school on (with optional light gaming), the review won't be too technical and I'll try to explain things in a manner that anyone can understand without spitting out a bunch of numbers or tech terms.

DISPLAY: Starting with the display itself, it's not very good. The viewing angles are bad, meaning when you look at it off angle as opposed to directly on, the picture starts to wash out and becomes more difficult to see. The resolution of the display is also only a baffling 1366x768, which falls short of the 1080p standard most displays are designed around. This means some websites will not scale properly on the display, as well as the picture not being as crisp as as 1080p screen would offer. The good news is the bezels, or the edging around the screen itself, is thin which looks nice and shows more of the screen.

KEYBOARD: The keyboard is just okay to type on. You shouldn't have any problems writing school essays or work reports on this: the key travel (the distance the keys push down before they register the input--which helps people who type "feel" when the input is activated to facilitate typing) is fair but if you want to write a novel I suggest another laptop with a more mechanical feel. Also, notably, there is no backlight (when the keys light up so you can see the keyboard in the dark) which is a big disappointment.

PORTS: The available ports are: (Right side = SD storage, aux port for wired headphones) // (Left side = HDMI out (so you can connect the laptop to another monitor or TV that has HDMI in which will then display your laptop screen on that monitor or TV), one USB 3.0 , and two USB 2.0. The difference between 3.0 and 2.0 is the transfer speeds. If you stick in a flash drive, make sure you use the 3.0 slot. You can tell which one is 3.0 by looking at the image I put in this review.

CPU: The processor included in this laptop is a bit worse than the latest comparable Intel option, the i3 10th gen mobile, but it's also less expensive. This again goes into why I think this laptop doesn't have a great value, because to me it's worth $300 at most, but they're asking for over $400 for it. When you look at laptops in the $380 range, you're getting an intel i3 10th gen with a 1080p screen, and in some cases, more RAM and memory. However, that doesn't mean it's a bad processor. It's quite good for what it is, actually. If the most you want to get out of this is to watch 1080p videos (even though the resolution of this laptop doesn't go up to 1080p), the processor is more than capable of handling that.

MEMORY: There is 4GB of RAM soldered to the motherboard, which is really the bare minimum a windows 10 laptop should have. Given that it's soldered, you aren't able to swap it out with something else, but the good news is there is an open slot on the motherboard to add your own RAM. If you want to go this route, which I suggest you do, here's what you want to buy: you can go up to 8GB (for a total of 12--though I recommend just an additional 4GB stick for normal usage) of DDR4-2400Mhz 1.2v. If you're looking at a listing of "laptop RAM" make sure it falls within those specifications. Getting to the memory banks is easy, even if you aren't tech savvy I'll easily explain how to do it safely: 1) turn the laptop completely off. 2) use a small screwdriver to remove all the screw underneath the laptop (be sure not to lose them). 3) near the hinges, lift your fingers up and slowly and carefully pry the back of the case off. I was very careful and still broke some tabs because it's very cheaply made, but don't worry if you do--the tabs don't do a whole lot anyway. 4) once the back is off, add the RAM into the slot, and put the case back on and put the screws back in. Lastly, just make sure the case is sealed all around the edges by pinching them until it clicks back into place.

STORAGE: The 128GB SSD included is in NVME form, which just means if you want to replace the storage (can't add onto it since there's only one slot for stoage), you can do so with a bigger NVME drive. To replace this, look at the above steps for replacing the RAM and also follow the software transfer guide incluided in the NVME package for moving the operating system and your files over to the new drive.

TOUCHPAD: The touchpad is pretty good. It's fairly responsive and responds well to multi gesture touches, such as using two fingers to scroll up and down on webpages.

WEBCAM: The webcam is horrendous. It will suffice at the bare minimum but the resolution is 480p at 30fps. If you don't know what that means, just understand it's well below average. Thankfully, there's a privacy shutter which blocks the webcam so certain malicious ads and attackers can't open your camera to see you while you are using the laptop.

WEIGHT: The laptop itself is also too heavy for what it is. It's almost 5lbs. Other companies are able to shave almost a pound off of a similarly-sized laptop.

CHASIS: The chasis of the laptop is made out of plastic through-and-through. It flexes incredibly easy, meaning if you press down on it with a bit of force, the plastic will bend. The panel is also easy to flex, but this is to be expected on a laptop in this price point.

GAMING: This laptop is capable of doing light gaming. I didn't go too in depth with testing, but I did install minecraft and low visual settings, the game was running at a consistent 55fps for the most part, the lowest being a short dip of 18fps when it was loading a lot of things at once. There's only one heat pipe on the motherboard, so it's not really designed around cooling. The laptop will get pretty warm if you start to use it for heavy tasks, such as light gaming.

BATTERY LIFE: The battery is decent. It could have been bigger, especially since there's plenty of real estate in the laptop to allow it, but it was is a cost-cutting decision. However, during my testing, when I ran this laptop at 80% brightness and using "Better performance" in Windows 10 for the power output, I was able to get around 6 hours of YouTube watching from 100% until it forced itself in sleep mode to prevent it from shutting down completely.

SPEAKERS: The speakers are surprisingly decent. You won't be forced to use headphones with this. Other laptops that I've reviewed that are more expensive than this one had worse speakers, so this is a plus.

If you do decide to get this laptop, here are some things you should know:
+Setup is easy out of the box, but don't connect it to the internet until you get to the desktop otherwise it will force you to create a microsoft account. If you want to do that, go for it, but I'd avoid it. However, if you want to disable S mode, you'll need one anyway so weigh your options here.

+It doesn't have bloatware at all, meaning you don't need to comb through the laptop to remove a bunch of unnecessary crap. In fact, the installed applications were one drive, some lenovo app, and office 365. I uninstalled 365 because I don't need it, but keep it if you do, I think they give you a free trial.

+When you get to the desktop, click the start menu and type Update, click "Check for updates". Click "Advanced Options" and enable the first option which says to Receive updates for other MS products when you update windows". Click the back arrow then click Check for updates and keep installing updates until there aren't any left to install.

In conclusion, the asking price of this laptop is too high for what you're getting in return. There are other options that are cheaper or comparable that will get you more memory, a better CPU, and a better screen, but looking at this laptop in a vacuum, it's not bad for what it is.

title: Decent Webcam For Price
text:
Use case
----------
I was looking for a webcam that is adjustable and would sit on my monitor, so I can keep my laptop docked in a vertical stand when I'm in my work meetings.

Pros
-----
- Sits on the top of monitor
- Webcam is on a ball head mount (you can move the camera up, down, and side-to-side)
- Easy installation (just plug in the USB and it works)

Cons
------
- Not the best camera quality
- Video has a slight lag/delay
- Did not come with a privacy cover

Notes
-------
- The privacy cover is a detached piece that you're supposed to manually attach onto the webcam

This webcam does its job, and for its price, you can't expect too much. It was a bit of a downgrade in terms of camera quality from the built-in camera for my laptop because of the delay and the slightly grainy footage, but this isn't really a deal-breaker since I was looking for the convenience of keeping my laptop docked during meetings. However, privacy and convenience are important to me, so the fact that the privacy shutter wasn't included was a deal-breaker for me. I have to always unplug the webcam whenever it's not in use. I could have probably just contacted the seller or Amazon to get that part shipped to me, but it just didn’t seem worth the trouble. If you're just looking for a webcam and don't care too much about the quality or lag, then this product is probably for you. In the end, I would recommend spending a little bit more money and buying a better quality webcam.

title: Questionable Construction and Ill Fit for Ronin S
text:
This is my just out of the box, one day of use review. First, this thing is light. It weighs very little, and compared to the weight of the Ronin S and Sony A7iii, it adds very little heft. In fact, I'd say that the whole setup feels a bit lighter because the weight is now spread between both arms. Getting the handle setup is relatively straight forward, and there are some instructions included in the box. When I tried to get my Ronin setup for the first time, I was a bit stymied. It seemed that the Ronin didn't fit at all, as the clamps on the handle open to an oblong shape and installing the also oblong Ronin battery grip meant that the whole thing was turned 90 degrees. After some fretting, I realized that the clamps on the handled did indeed open enough to fit the Ronin. I'm not sold on the gripping ability of the clamps because they only make contact on the small sides (i.e. the front and back) of the battery grip.

The second issue is the construction of this product. The plastic that the handle is built from is very light, but also feels very cheap. If the Ronin is perpendicular to the ground, the whole thing feels pretty stable. However, when the Ronin is pointed in any other orientation, the handle creaks and flexes. If the flexing stays at this same level through long-term use, I see no issues. If it starts to break down over time, there is a real concern that it could come apart and risk dropping the Ronin and camera. The creaking is a whole other issue. While it does not creak very loudly, the sound is still present and might be audible if you're recording sound.

I'm going to get through a couple of projects with this handle and add to my review as my impression changes. I think its flaws might prove fatal, and I think it's important to consider potential issues when you're relying on this thing to hold your possibly several thousand dollar setup.

title: WARNING - DO NOT BUY FROM THIS COMPANY
text: Let me start off by saying that I understand it is a risk to by anything that has been refurbished.  With that said, I expected much more from this company.  Based on my awful experience and terrible customer service, I would recommend finding somewhere else to buy whatever it is you are looking for.  I purchased these headphones in late on March 30th.  I had some issued with connectivity and sound out of one of the earbuds.  I found that if I did a hard reset, I could usually get them back to working and thought nothing of it.  However, just after the July 4th weekend, I went to get the earbuds out of the charging case and noticed that one of the earbuds snapped off while sitting in the charging case and was discovered when removing it from the charging case. I  After examining it and doing a lot of research online, this should never happen!  In fact, I found a website discussing people trying to "undue" these headphones to learn about the technology and they were unable to get the earbud apart...when trying to! would not be reaching out if I thought it was normal wear and tear that caused this.  At this point I have to assume that this is what the "refurbished" part of the earbuds was.  Given the connectivity issues all along and the way it just came apart, there is no other explanation other than they did a terrible job a fixing this earbud but were willing to sell them for $145 hoping they would hold up.  In this case, they did hold up just long enough as I was one week outside of the warranty window of 90 days.  I thought that the company might be understanding given that is is an obvious refurbishment gone wrong and these should have never been put back on the market.  I received a very short response basically telling me that the 90 days is up so there is nothing they will do.  I wrote back restating my reasoning and letting them know I would send these back for a replacement pair - I was not just looking for my money back.  To this email I  received an even shorter response saying the same thing.  I guess in the end you do get what you pay for, just expected a lot more from the company.  When it comes to buying from this company, I hope this review saves some people from making the same mistake that I did.

title: Nice. Great cord.  Quality seems great. Multi-voltage.  Not Apple Certified MFi, no USB-C
text:
I got this because I needed 3 plugs behind my bedroom dresser and did not want cords or adapters pushing my end table from the wall. This works well with a plug where the wire comes off to the side. I placed this on the floor behind my end table.
I do not use the built in USB charger because it is not Apple Certified. That does not mean that it will harm my phone. It just means that Apple has not tested it. It also means that the manufacturer does not have to pay Apple a royalty. But some chargers have been know to harm phones and shorten battery life, so I am not willing to take a chance.
So I plug my Apple chargers into the outlets, along with the table lamp and I am happy. If you are looking for USB charging, this has USB-A. Newer phones use USB-C which provides a higher current. This is not included.
I am impressed with the look and feel. It gives me the impression of quality and the all-white makes it feel like an Apple product. The power cord and plug feels like it is high quality, yet is flexible so that it is easy to place the unit.
Its voltage range includes Europe, so with a country specific power plug adapter, you could still use the USB charger. The power outlets would be the higher voltage, so be sure to only plug in chargers that can handle the higher voltage. I do this sort of thing all the time when traveling to Europe so I can plug in our 4 universal power chargers for our two phones and two tablets.
I would buy it again. I would pay more for MFi and USB-C higher power charging. A nice product.

title: BUY ANKER. Do Not Look Elsewhere. Don't Waste Your Money.
text:
Let me just come out and say it. I use to be that cheap guy that never cared about my cords. If it worked, it worked. And then when it broke, which it always did, I would turn around and buy more cheap cords and continue making the same mistake.

Then one day I decided to give Anker a shot. And now I haven't looked back. Look, cords are wear and tear items. We use them every day, they come with us wherever we go, they get beat up, pets chew them, etc. If you buy a set of tires and they go the distance they're suppose to, are you mad when you have to replace them? Sure, you don't want to spend the money, but it's necessary. This is the exact same thing.

Sure, you can go and spend half the price on 2-3 times as many cords and then when they start acting up in three weeks or one of them just doesn't work, you'll be buying more and more and more. Or you could just spend the extra $5 right now and not have to worry about it.

The cords are sturdy, they start charging as soon as you plug in and there's no flipping around the cable because one side will charge and the other won't. Hell, I'd say these work better than the Apple cords that come with your products.

On top of just being an overall solid product, the team behind them are great. Anker has one of the best customer service teams I've had the pleasure of dealing with. AND! Most if not all of their cords come with an 18-month warranty. Of course, this doesn't cover EVERYTHING. But it gives you the peace of mind that if your cord does unfortunately crap out, they've got your back and will make sure you're taken care of.

I can't recommend them enough and don't make the mistake I did by buying other cables. Skip the BS and buy Anker.

title: Excellent Stand and cheaper than many triple mounts for those who need extra height
text:
I was looking for a triple monitor mount that would lift the monitors a good ways up, as I have a lot of radio equipment on my desk. For years, I've been balancing the monitors on the equipment using shims and blocks of wood to keep them somewhat on the same horizontal level. Recently I decided to look for a triple monitor mount so that I could clean up the desk a bit and give myself more room.

After looking at the mounts that are out there, I found that most triple mounts include a center support post that is only about 18" in height. With the monitors installed in such a setup, I would only get 6 or 8 inches of clearance below them, which wouldn't leave enough room for my radio equipment. I searched for triple mounts with longer center posts, but the few that I found were well over $100. That's when I happened across this quad-mount stand. It has two posts that screw together to give a length of about 32". Though it's designed for four monitors, it works perfectly to give my triple monitor setup a lot of extra 'lift' off the desk.

Only time will tell how this stand holds up, but for the price I'm very impressed with it so far. The construction seems to be of good quality and it includes both clamp and grommet installation pieces to attach it the various styles of desks and tables. With the great range of height adjustment, this stand can give you lots of room back on your desk and would also give enough lift to set up a standing work station if that's something you are looking to do.

As a final note, while I didn't see many complaints about side monitor 'droop' with this stand, I found that it can happen if all the various joints going out to the arms aren't tightened fully. After installation, I noticed that the side monitors sat about an inch lower than the center monitor, even though the center monitor was right up against the side monitor mounting bracket. I solved this by simply tightening all of the joints in the side arms. Once I did that, the side monitors were lifted quite dramatically and even ended up being a tiny bit higher than the center monitor. So, if you find your side monitors sagging, try tightening those joints up and it should solve your problem.

This camera does eat through batteries quickly, but because the camera itself is smaller, the batteries are also smaller and don't last as long. As for call quality, in regular environments, it will catch your voice as well as anything going on behind it quite well. But If there was wind noise or a droning nose like a vacuum cleaner in the background, forget it. People won't be able to hear you. For voice calls, my Plantronics Edge or 5200 works great. It will even remove the vacuum noise in the background. It's a mono-headset which is nice when you want to listen/watch things inconspicuously.

So my recommendation, get a Plantronics for voice calls. Use the Legato around the neck headphones for music. If someone has a good option, for both music and calls, let me know!

I've had 4 LG around the neck headphones, Galaxy Buds, Airpods 1 & 2, bose OE bluetooth, Legato, countless Plantronics, motorola and other generic headsets. Been using bluetooth headsets in the early stage with those flip out Motorola headsets. At that time, people thought I was crazy when I was talking and walking with no wire attached to my phone.

title: Great little sub!
text: I bought this OSD Audio Nero Dual X8 to add to a secondary, 2 channel audio system that's in a front room of my house and it really did the trick.  I have multiple audio systems, several 12" subs, tube amps, etc. so didn't expect adding an 8" sub in the front room was going to be earth shaking - but that wasn't my goal either.  The system is a "Zone 2" to my larger audio system and is only a two-channel system to watch occasional TV and play music throughout the house via Zone 2 from the main system.  I have a decent amp and two bookshelf speakers in this front room and really wanted to just "bump" the LFE signal a bit for TV and low-level music when I'm at my dining table and to fill the house with more even sound.  I have multiple 12" subs in my main audio room, so I knew I wasn't going to get chest thumping low end from an 8" sub - but this little Nero really filled the gap well where I needed it!  I hooked it up, adjusted the crossover, set my AVR/AMP accordingly - AND used an SPL meter to dial all three speakers in (including the Nero) and frankly it sounds really nice.  I play music at fairly low levels in this front room but when I step into my office (an adjacent room) I can still sense the bass frequencies well.  I do wish this little bugger had an actual LFE input and crossover by-pass (which I could have sworn it had when I looked at it on Amazon the first time) but all in all it works well when set up properly and for the price point I suppose it is what it is.  The over-all build quality is good, and it has an exceptionally small footprint which may be attractive to you if you have a small living space.  I wouldn't necessarily recommend it for a 5.1+surround system and for movie watching (always go bigger if you can) but if you listen at low levels in a small room then maybe it'd work well for you there.

title: These Sleeved  PSU Cables Work Well
text: There are a few reviewers for these cables that apparently could not get them to work. I have a Corsair AX1600i PSU. These cables work great for Type 4 PSU's. Perhaps those reviewers didn't notice that when a cable should be split for their particular PSU, MOBO, or GPU, it could be. They are snapped together, so you have to look closely. Also, I have a giant case, a Cooler Master Cosmos C700P. I didn't use the cables included with the PSU. I only used the cables from the Corsair Pro Kit. Everything I needed was included, and all of them were easily long enough, and worked like a champ. They even allowed convoluted routing due to cable management constraints. These are not extensions. They are cables, and are all you need. Of course, they don't work with every PSU Corsair has. But, they do have a support page, and a number listed above, which will identify the compatible models. The only con I would mention is, I wish they had more than one comb per cable - three at least. I got the red set. They are a bit pricey, but you get what you pay for.

title: A lot of capability for the money
text: I have had one of these for about 3 days now. I have a radio technician background. My receiver is the same brand and specs but I bought it from another store. Mine did not come with a manual and from what I understand none of them do. I was able to get some manuals online from the Malahit group on Facebook and other sites. The original receiver was developed in Russia and the Russian manual converted to English is the best. This receiver comes with the Russian software, which is better than the limited Chinese software supplied with some versions. When you power up the receiver, it will list the Ham Radio call letters and names of the original Russian development team. The hardware is of course Chinese. Without the manual, you may think that many of the features do not work or you cannot figure out how it works. Most of your questions can be answered on Facebook and some Ham Radio forums. Some people talk about downloading upgrades to the installed operating system version, I am not convinced that is a good Idea. All features seem to work with the right settings and upgrading the operating system can be very tricky and technical. Do a lot of reading before trying it. There is risk involved. This radio comes unlocked so that you can tune from 50kHz to 2000Mhz. It works fine with AM, USB, LSB, Narrow band FM, Wideband FM and CW (with the ability to decode morse code.) With CW settings are important for it to be able to decode it. The filters work well. Agc Automatic gain control works well. The NR button works well in removing background noise, makes a big difference. It has about fifty memory slots for storing your favorite stations. I have been researching and reading for about 3 days and am just now becoming comfortable with how it operates. I worked 20 years in radio maintenance in the USAF, so it may take you longer. The only thing I will say negative at this point is that the volume and frequency encoder controls are small and could be better, of course the radio is small so they have to be. On the bottom of the receiver is a small black recessed button. This will will turn off the screen with a quick tap. A long press will shut the power off. A quick tap will turn the power back on. took me a while to figure it out. It is supposed to be able to connect to the computer through the usb. I have not yet accomplished this, I need to find the right driver so that my computer recognizes it. Once that is done, you can control it with different SDR software packages like SDR Sharp. Good luck and have patients. One last thing, you will not receive much short wave with the small telescoping antenna. Look for some cable adapters with an sma connector on one end and whatever other type connector on the other such as a PL-259. A 20 or 30 foot piece of wire works well for short wave. If you use something like this, go to settings and set antenna impedance to Hi Z. Hope this helps some. I will try to check back periodically in case there are questions.

title: Faster than my network on a Mac Mini M1
text:
I bought this to connect to a new Mac Mini M1 as a networked drive. With a 10 gig dummy file (made using Windows fsuitil), it took 2 minutes to copy from Windows to the Mac-attached drive and 93 seconds to copy back. Basically, it was maxing out the speed of the 1 gigabit switch they're both hardwired on.

Copying the same file to and from the Mac's SSD was approx 3x faster (44 second write, 32 second read). That's a bit over 300 megabytes per second sustained read locally and 113 megabytes a second across the network. That's plenty fast enough to stream 8k video over the network (if I had a screen in my house capable of 8k). I think a faster network switch is going to be my next purchase, though.

Only had it a week, so I can't testify to longevity, but it's really quiet when not in use and a little thunky when in heavy use.

title: Plug and play, very good quality.
text:
I didn't even look for directions. Everything was just plug and play. There are two wires needed: 1) the HDMI that plugs into whatever monitor or projector you're using (which is NOT included), and 2) a micro-USB cable for power (which IS included) just like you probably use for your non-Apple phone.

I didn't bother with the USB viewing as my equipment has HDMI, so I can't comment on that. I'm not sure I'm going to have ready access to power within ten feet or so where I'm doing my presentation, so I plugged it into a USB battery charger and left it on for a couple of hours. I started with three bars and ended with three bars. I doubt I'll need a plug, but an adaptor is easy enough to find anywhere. It seems to sip power, but I can't find specs.

About the quality. The frame and structure are very nicely built. The base is heavy and stable. I'll end up using clamps on the table top pressing on the heavy metal base just in case, but it shouldn't be necessary in ordinary circumstances.

The focus works. I'm using big notebooks where one side might be higher than the other, and will slide the notebook back and forth on the tabletop depending on which side I'm viewing. The focus does get confused sometimes and goes blurry. But one touch of the autofocus button and within 2 seconds, you're back in business. It's not graceful, but it does work.

The zoom. I'm not a fan of digital zoom. It basically dilutes your 8k image to a lower resolution as you zoom. But optical zoom machines are much more expensive. Having said that, I have two observations: 1) on full zoom, I didn't see any image degradation. That tells me that 8k is plenty to play with and leaves plenty of room for quality erosion before my eyes could even notice. I think that's the irony of modern high resolution images. My eyes can't really tell the difference after 1k. And not many monitors are even higher resolution than 1k. So on full zoom, you should still be at 1-to-1 in resolution. But I'm not a videophile, so someone may know better. Still no one can tell my what my eyes saw or didn't see. And 2) if you don't want to use the digital zoom, just pull the camera head closer to the image, and don't use it at all. So I guess it kind of does have optical zoom after all.

The filters. I don't get them. But you don't have to use them. I won't. It can invert the image from black print on white paper to white print on black paper (maybe to keep the room dark?), turn the background paper yellow (easier on the eyes?), and a few other options I didn't really understand.

The light. It's weak, but I won't be illuminating images in the dark, so I don't care. The exposure adjustments should more than make up for weak ambient lighting.

You can choose between 50hz and 60hz. Not sure why or what that does. It was set to 60hz out of the box, so I left it there. I didn't try to change it. No comment there.

The image: I plugged it into my 1080p tv using HDMI. It looked fine. The black letters seemed to have a slight bright white outline which I though made it look a little washed out. So I brightened the exposure and that seemed to correct it. Maybe other more expensive units don't do that, but I can't imagine you can get as much and as good as this for anywhere around that price.

title: This Audio Extractor works exactly as advertised - 5-Stars!
text:
It's a 5-Star Choice for delivering composite Audio output from your HDMI source (BluRay or Satellite DVR/Roku Streaming Device), while still passing HDMI signal to your AVR Receiver/4K TV, However...

Beware that many 4K sources deliver DTS MAster Audio or a Digital-Only Audio Bitstream versus PCM. A bitstream audio signal will send a standard Dolby Digital or DTS 5.1 (or higher, such as DTS Master Audio) surround sound signal to your receiver for further decoding, the PCM option will only send a two-channel signal.

Therefore, you will need to select PCM Audio Out option at the HDMI Source (Roku/BluRay player) in order to have a signal that this Audio extractor can process. Otherwise, you will simply hear Digital Noise (hiss) through your Analog Audio RCA jacks. This means that you will be choosing to down-rez your Audio Signal from the source to Dolby Pro-Logic versus Dolby Digital+ (anything beyond 5.1 Surround Sound), in order to split it off via the Analog Audio Jacks.

Arlo also proudly advertises their activity zones and shows you can make 8 anchor points to any shape. This is not true!!! This was a big selling point for me but you actually only get 5 rectangles. I found out that arlo took out that feature from reading forums though they still market it and advertise it. I think had I had the 8 anchor point activity zone I could have dialed it in even more and the break in might have gotten caught on tape (provided that was the case and it wasn't just random period of the system not being connected as it likes to do). Either way it is blatant false advertising, the rectangles are very crude and don't provide enough detail to tout that as a usable feature.

BOTTOM LINE: I BOUGHT THIS CAMERA SYSTEM TO RECORD CRIMINAL ACTIVITY AND ARLO FAILED TO DELIVER WHEN I NEEDED THEM TO.

title: Somewhat Misleading Product Information Regarding USB Charging Cable
text:
Like most people reviewing this item, I like it. The sound quality is really quite nice...especially if you use nice headphones such as Audio-Technica's ATH-M20x.

BUT, I give it three stars on what is, in my opinion, misleading product information.

For those of us who use, for example, iPhones and use the USB charging cable to plug into the wall socket and into the iPhone, we are, indeed, charging the battery of the iPhone. I had to write to the company to get a clarification on functionality, as there is nothing in their literature that explains what their "USB charging cable" actually does, and even then it took them four days to answer the question and even when the question was expedited up the support chain of command, which is to say that the original support person could not answer the question.

The USB charging cable does NOT in any way re-charge any internal battery. In fact, it doesn't even charge up a re-chargeable battery that you might have placed into the CD player, hoping to recharge it.

What it does is simply act as a way to run the CD player without batteries, i.e., it should be considered a power cable in USB form, and, of course when using it in this manner is not portable at all. The company does not provide that part that plugs into the wall socket, so if you want to use it, you will have to purchase that at a store separately.

But, if you were hoping that the "USB charging cable" actually charges the CD, you will be disappointed.

title: Comparing the WH1000xm4 to the Bose 700
text:
Owned the WH1000xm4 for a week. Thought the sound was great for a noise cancelling headphone, however if you don’t care for noise cancelling you can get better sounding bluetooth headphones for an even lower price, from Hifiman, Grado to name a few. I bought the Bose 700 a few days later. Sound quality is close between the two. The Bose sounded warm and neutral while Sony sounded a little lean and neutral. With the Bose you are sitting a little closer to the performer because voices sound closer to you, with Sony you are sitting a few rows back with a little wider soundstage. I would say Sony has a little better bass impact compared to the Bose. For a noise cancelling headphone at this price range I would give both a 9/10 in sound quality. However, compared to my $1700 Sennheiser HD800S, both would get a 5.5/10 if the HD800S was a 10. These are not audiophile headphones but sound good enough for non-critical listening.

Both are very comfortable, Sony is cushier, while Bose has a little firmer foam around the ears. Because the Sony is cushy with more surface area contact, your ears can feel warmer, good if you live in a cold area I guess. With this one I prefer the Bose.

Sony has more functionality with its phone app. However, Sony’s AI algorithm DSEE which is supposed to enhance compressed audio cause some loss in audio fidelity. Overall better with it off, at least with my ears. Music untouched and played as close to neutral as possible is best. Sony has a built in Noise Canceling Optimizer which made no audible difference to my ears. These are probably unfinished functionality pushed by the marketing department. I’m not sure. Before I bought this headphone, I was reading a review from Soundguys website where they tested battery life. Anyway, these got just below 20 hrs, not 30. So on par with other brands.

I would have kept the Sony, was happy with it. However, it wasn’t compatible with my Samsung TV(2019 model). Searched online and a few people have the same issue. Noticeable audio lag, and loss of sync between audio and video. With a firmware update from Sony, this will probably be fixed in the future, but I didn’t want to take a chance, especially considering the price of the headphone. So anyway, bought the Bose 700, now zero issues with my tv. Sound quality is identical, build quality and choice of materials is just as good. Final Rating. Sound Quality 9, Build quality 9, Noise Cancellation 9, Comfort 8.5.

This camera does quite a lot, especially when you consider the price point. The benefit of that for my car would be that I could have constant power to the camera in case i wanted to film while the engine wasn’t running. My car shuts off power to the charger when I turn the car off, but I drive electric. Most cars continue to power the charger or cigarette lighter when the car is turned off, but I digress.

The camera comes with a micro SD card that has far more memory than you’d likely need. It’s very easy to remove the card and stick it in a computer or phone to upload video or photos. This could be especially useful when handling an insurance claim or possibly fighting a traffic ticket in court. The camera can swivel 360, so if you wanted to car vlog (my kid is constantly asking to do this), you could do that too.

Seriously considering getting a second one for the rear window. Also plan on taking this on our next European vacation to record driving in Paris. All in all, very pleased.

title: Poorly designed, cheaply made
text:
For such a simple product I'm amazed with how much went wrong in making these.

First, the screw holes in the raceway are inconsistently drilled. Between any two given pieces the holes varied by up to a half inch, and I had one raceway that was even drilled twice. All of the holes were not deburred and had sharp edges and extra material that can cut you or damage the cables running through them.

Going into these badly positioned holes are the included flat-head screws, which seem to be made of the world's cheapest metal and stamped out by a toddler. The heads on the screws were not concentric with the stems, meaning that the screws wobble all over the place when you try to screw them in. This makes getting a level raceway much more difficult. The metal these screws are made of is very soft, and more than one stripped just by using a handheld screwdriver driving into a drywall anchor.

These included screws also have a flat-head design but the manufacturer didn't bother to countersink the holes in the raceway. This means that the angled (read: sharp) screw heads stick up a good 1/8" into the raceway and are perfect for snagging cables and making your life miserable.

You know what else is good for snagging cables? The edges of the raceway. There's no built-in method for aligning the raceway segments so cables will easily snag on the edges when being pulled through unless you perfectly align them by hand - you know, in spite of the non-concentric screws trying to push them out of the way while they're being tightened.

Of course I'm missing a step: going between the raceway segments are straight connector pieces, designed to cover the seam. These connectors attach by using flanges that hook into the raceway covers. But these flanges aren't centered on the connector and the provided raceway covers are exactly the same length as the channels which attach to the walls. This means that if you want to use a connector to cover up a seam in the raceway, you need to cut 3/4" off of every raceway cover where a connector is used. For a complete 'kit' using all 4 connector pieces, that means 8 cuts you need to measure and saw by hand that should have been done at the factory.

To add insult to injury, the box containing the raceway arrived beat up and torn, while the raceway pieces themselves were covered in dirt and specks of what looked like machine lubricant.

+1 star because at the end of the day, once you're suffered through cleaning up the poorly drilled holes, fishing the wires across the sharp and uncovered bolt heads, cutting the covers to fit properly, and hammering the connectors to sit flush - it does its job of hiding the cables on the wall.

Buyer beware.

text: I got it on crutchfield but wanted to leave a good review about my experience. First the touchscreen is way better than my last JVC, which is surprising. The install was easy after wiring my harness. I've never connected a backup cam before, so I'll share some things that may help. First, and most helpful: The cam wire on back of your stereo, it doesn't need to go to any power behind the dash just use an 18-20 AWG wire to connect from that tucked in trim all the way back (straight shot) to the hot wire that leads to your reverse white light by splicing into that - there will only be 2 wires, the hot and the ground. The line they provide starting from dash you'll connect the red pigtail to your 12v red line between stereo then the video yellow connector to your stereo. Then running the other end of long cable to back tucked in trim same path. Your power cable will connect to power on your camera, and mount the black wire to body, in my case I found a nut I loosened and tightened underneath (I did all this in area behind the license plate). In my car Nissan Sentra there was already a small plastic piece by the license plate light like a plug, I pulled that out and drilled a 3/4 hole into it leading wires through that and weatherproofing the area around the wire entry with butle. The wires to get from upper trunk to body, I followed the path of the license plate wiring which lead into lower trunk. I just used Velcro strips to tie it along the rubber type conduit and cut X shaped hole into the rubber seal to get to lower area adding 100 silicon caulk to reseal it around wire entry -- that was pretty much it, works great and I can turn on cam even when not in reverse. Another tip is you can wire your parking brake wire to your body behind dash to ground (trick) it which will allow a DVD or Vid to be played with out having E brake on or even moving. title: Great head unit - especially for Android Auto
text:
Camry 2016 OEM radio wasn't all that great, and I found myself looking for something that provided more functionality, as well as better sound for my music. This Dasaita PX6 head unit does just that.

Installation was fairly simple. It is basically just plug and play with the existing OEM wires. It comes with an external microphone if you want to set that up as well - but there is one built into the unit that works well. I watched this video on YouTube which helped: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yv-outtqoxU&t=1088s

The unit takes about 30-45 seconds to start up. Once it's ready, it moves fast and no lag that I've noticed. It has a built in app called Zlink for Android Auto and Apple Carplay. Android Auto does take a moment to load, but it's not a big deal - it provides so much more functionality than a standard radio you find in most cars. The user interface of the head unit itself is good. It's straight forward and easy to navigate - I just prefer Android Auto. But those who use this head unit without carplay or auto will be happy.

The sound is so much better after installing the unit. Just make sure to enable some of the amplifier app settings (app is built in). I had no idea my little Camry speakers could sound that good. Was one of the main reasons I looked into replacing the OEM radio - glad I did.

Pros:
- Looks really nice
- Bluetooth connection to phone is dependable
- Sound is drastically improved
- Easy to install

Cons:
- Unit does take a moment to start, esp if you're using Android Auto or CarPlay
- Installing Apps on the Play Store is a bit of hit or miss, sometimes the app just crashes to the home screen. Might take a couple tries to successfully install some apps.

text:
I wasn't expecting this level of quality.

I love my SkullCandy Hesh 2 headphones. They're my favorite headphones I've ever owned. They're over the ear, loud, and comfortable. However, the vinyl was deteriorating. I had to replace them.

I originally placed an order for another set of headphones, from a third party seller. They were $60 and offered a $15 off coupon discount and an additional promo code, knocking the headphones down to $15. However, the third party seller didn't want to honor the new price. I was a little bit upset. Why release promo codes and coupons, and then not honor them? Those headphones are still in stock, by the way.

I was looking for an alternative. Something similar to my beloved SkullCandy Hesh 2 headphones, basically.

These headphones popped up, underneath a section on the Home Page, of items similar to those I've recently viewed. I've never even heard of Amazon Basics. But for $20, I figured trying them out wouldn't hurt. If I didn't like them, I could always return them.

My expectations were low, but these headphones are incredible. The audio quality is amazing (Crystal clear and loud.), they're comfortable, they're over the ear style, and they arrived in 1 business day. For $20, they're a great purchase.

Keep in mind : I've never used top of the line DJ style headphones (Beats, for example.), but I'm sure these aren't comparable to those. But if you just want to listen to music on your phone or laptop, these Amazon Basics headphones are perfect. And all I wanted was to listen to music on my phone.

I'm very pleased with this purchase.
