title: Perfect for what I want it for, but received a used one first time.
text:
This mini-laptop is perfect for what I wanted it for, which is writing when space is very limited or on the go. Unfortunately, the first one I ordered and received was used and was already registered to another person which you can see in the photo. When I contacted amazon, they told me it couldn't be exchanged or returned to the amazon depot even though I'm only about 6 miles away from the million square feet distribution center here in Orlando. This was on Saturday. I was told it HAD to be returned via UPS on Monday, then they would process it and then I'd get a refund in 3-5 business days AFTER they received it! Even though I'm 6 miles away from where they sent it and would resend another one. So this process takes a week to get my refund from the time I received the first one. I could have saved a few days if I had just reordered another one but since I had already received a used one and they couldn't refund for days after they got it back, I was a bit hesitant to do that since my initial impression was not good. What if they held up the refund? Lost the return? Claimed I registered it, etc etc etc.

So, I finally get my refund a week later. I go to order another one because it really is the best one out there to meet my needs according to the research I'd done...and the price went up $10!! So amazon's mistake of sending me a used one, then making me wait to send it back, then making me wait for a refund before I can order another one, actually cost me $10 to go through all that mess!! NOT the best way to operate a business or treat customers when it was YOUR error for sending a used machine!

Regarding the mini-laptop itself: it's pretty amazing, even if it is overpriced. If space is more important than cost, then you'll be happy with this little guy. The screen resolution is amazing and easily outshines any other product in this category or even tablets. It's actually quite remarkable. With the new CPU that's in it, it's very fast. I added a 400GB Sandisk Extreme micro SD card so it took advantage of all the speed it offers and now has a ton of storage that is as fast as the built in one.

The screen is touch screen and there is no lag when using it or loading programs or videos. The only slight negative is that the hinge at the bottom of the screen is fixed making touching icons at the bottom of the screen a tad bit more difficult than it needs to be. With a flexible hinge, that wouldn't occur so hopefully they'll address that in the next version. I think they made it that way this time so that it rotates the bottom of the laptop off the table a bit to help cool it but it doesn't really help so they'd be better off putting bigger bumpers on the bottom to increase airflow. With it plugged in, even with the fan active and blowing, it gets REALLY hot on the right edge of the case where your hand sits when you type. If you raise the back or put more space between the bottom, like larger rubber bumpers, it actually remained cool and didn't make typing any harder, so something to consider doing if you get one. This doesn't occur if you are not pushing the graphics to their limits. When set for maximum battery life, it doesn't even get warm.

When downloading and installing programs or games on it, it felt the exact same as my fully decked out Alienware laptop. The performance is that good. Astonishing actually. Office 365 loads and runs exactly like my main laptop does. THAT I didn't expect or even think possible for a mini. Graphics on this are great for videos or work stuff and okay for main stream games. I don't plan on using it for that so it doesn't matter to me but you CAN game on it with lower settings. If you run phone games like candy crush or anything simple like that, this machine does it so easy you feel dumb even testing it. But you know you're gonna so prepare for it to laugh at you.

The only weird thing that happens is that you forget it's a FULL-FLEDGED laptop running windows 10. Because of it's size, I went to install apps like netflix, amazon prime video and hulu for offline viewing ilke on my android phone. I mean, the screen begs you to run movies and tv shows on it. The problem? They aren't in the windows store. Well Hulu is but they don't have offline viewing yet so who cares about them doing a halfway job. So you have this amazing machine, with an amazing screen...that can't store and run videos offline directly from those apps. ;/ I sure hope they add their apps to the windows store in the future to take full advantage of this machine in offline mode while on planes, trains or out of network areas.

Overall, simply an amazing piece of hardware. If you need/want a small-factor FULL windows 10 capable mini-laptop with a decent keyboard for writing or quick notes to yourself, it's going to be hard to beat this. It's expensive but the ability to hook up a usb-c hub and connect it to a screen at a meeting with the FULL power of a full sized machine running butter smooth whatever you throw at it...just cannot be over-stated.

It's a 4-star review for a 5-star mini-laptop because not offering exchanges, which mandates a refund and reorder, and then having to pay an extra $10 for the exact same machine a week later isn't consumer friendly. If you don't care about your customer's experience, then you don't care about your 5-star rating...and if you don't care, why should I? It's a petty thing probably but my only way to express my unhappiness of ME having to pay extra for YOUR mistake AND wait an extra week.

title: KZ ZS10 Pro vs KZ AS-10
text:
Just got a set of ZS-10 Pros in the mail today and have had the AS-10's since Thanksgiving last year. Maybe I'm looking for a different type of sound than most, but the detail, clarity and the control of the AS-10 are leaps and bounds better than the ZS-10 Pro. The ZS-10 Pros are much more V shaped than the AS-10's and while not sibilant, the treble is mildly harsh (a bit in your face). The bass definitely hits harder with the ZS-10 Pro over the AS-10 but its "sloppy", for lack of a better word, relative to the AS-10. The sub-bass in the ZS-10 Pro tends to rumble and muddy up the overall sound. The AS-10 isn't a bass monster, but it doesn't lack bass. It's there, but it is very controlled. It doesn't have any of the sub-bass rumble that the ZS-10 pro has, so some may say it lacks bass. It's more mid bass focused and the ZS-10 Pro is sub bass focused. Another thing I'm noticing is that the ZS-10 Pro's have a lot more distortion and crackling that occur in them than the AS-10's. This could be due to the additional boost they have in their bass and treble, as the AS-10's don't have this issue. So you can turn up the volume more on the AS-10's than you can on the ZS-10 Pros while having a cleaner sound.

The AS-10's are more "forward" than the ZS-10 Pro's making the vocals nice and clear. The ZS-10 Pro's have a bit more scoop in the mids putting those vocals a bit further back in the mix. Some may think this adds soundstage to the mix, and yeah it may be welcome in a more instrumental song, but those vocals start to get a bit lost in the mix in the ZS-10 Pros. Combined with the boosted sub-bass rumble, songs sound "muddier" with the ZS-10 Pros. Despite their boosted treble, I feel the details get lost in the ZS-10 Pro.

I like the size and fit better on the ZS-10 Pro's than the AS-10's but I think I like the AS-10 cable better than the ZS-10 Pro. Yeah, I said that. I think I like the mold-able wire better than the pre-bent loop over the ear. My ZS-10's for some reason have the molded wires bent incorrectly having the wire come over the ear instead on behind the ear. If I swap the left and right wiring to the opposite ear phones, then it all lays correctly, but the sound is backwards (for lack of a better word).

In the end, the ZS-10 Pros aren't bad. They are actually really "fun" for a set of $45 earbuds, but I feel the AS-10's are worth the additional $20 over the ZS-10 Pros. If you like a tight, controlled sound with lots of detail and no specific frequency screaming at you, the AS-10's are the way to go. If you like a more "fun" earbud with a boosted bass and treble, and detail isn't your priority, the ZS-10 Pros are the way to go. I'm going to keep both and use one set at home and another at work. Overall they aren't that expensive and both have their positives to them.﻿

title: Totally exceeded my expectations
text:
This little Aiworth recorder is amazing. My 10 year old Olympus unit started acting up and this device does many things better than that one did. I use this to record parts of private or small group lessons. I can record the instructor and/or quiet notes to myself without disrupting others. Most recordings are less than 15 minutes long and I archive them to a PC every 2 weeks or so. The PC connection works flawlessly. I can rename the recordings and copy some of them back onto this device in a different folder for review on the go. The very nice display shows the file name, so I can easily find the ones I want to review. It records .wav or .mp3. The wav files sound noticeably better, so I use that format for recording. It plays back MP3, WAV, FLAC, APE, OGG, and WMA. I usually use noise reduction mode, which forces a mono recording, which suits me fine. It even accepts a micro SD card, though with 16GB storage (on my model) I may never need to try using it.

Operation: my Olympus was simpler, mostly because it did fewer things. Unfortunately, this one takes a few seconds to wake up, where the Olympus was instant. I start and stop recording often during these lessons, so this would not bother most other users. The tiny red LED on the record button flashes when recording, steady when paused. The screen is backlit well. The button layout is easy to manage without having to look at it every time. It's a little slippery but I just put a small strip of gaffer tape on the back and that helps.

This is a very well designed device with almost every feature working just the way you expect it to. Many similar devices have features that don't work well at all, like no way to pause during recording. But this recorder does everything I want, as well as I need it to, and is an astonishing value. I highly recommend t.

title: Fantastic sound for the price.
text:
Paradigm has been around for decades and is a very underrated company. Their speakers, even their entry level line, produces sound that is above and beyond what others in this price range and configuration offer.

My dad used to have a pair of Monitor 7 floor standing speakers and their sound was superb. After owning a 5.1 setup consisting of NHT SuperOnes, a SuperCenter, and a Klipsch KSW-12 subwoofer that served admirably for over 20 years, I decided to purchase these Monitor SE Atoms and a Monitor SE 2000C expecting an upgrade in sound and I was not disappointed!

There are some things to be mindful of, though. First, these speakers are ported versus enclosed. This means that they have a higher sensitivity rating, which allows them to pair easier with a wider gamut of amplifiers/receivers, regardless of budget. However, by being ported, these Paradigms are more sensitive to placement. If you place them too close to reflective surfaces, such as walls, glass window panes, etc., they will sound boomy and muffled. It all depends on what your room configuration allows. Second, even though they have a 5.25" woofer cone, they are huge. My NHT's had a 6.5" woofer and were smaller in almost every dimension due to their enclosed nature. Third, these speakers are rated to produce sound down to around 60Hz, so one might be tempted to rush and purchase a subwoofer. Of course, for Low Frequency Effects during movies and if you want to produce proper sound down to the 20Hz range, a subwoofer will be a must. However, when properly placed, the bass in these speakers is tight and present so you might be perfectly happy with just these speakers. Last, these speakers are neutral sounding and revealing, producing the sound exactly as it receives it from the source. If you prefer listening to compressed audio files or to stream music, you will hear the loss that compressing music produces versus lossless audio.

All in all, these speakers will sound great without any equalization and fantastic with the required slight adjustments based on your room. These speakers in white look stunning and their build and construction is top notch. Highly recommended.

title: very happy with cinegrey 5d
text:
I purchased the cinegrey 5d.. Exusting reviews tell the story fairly well. I can confirm there were creases in the material due to the way it was rolled for shipping. This product must be stretched. I used a fixed screen frame and stretched the material 1-2 inches and it removed all creases. If you are using a motorized screen, I doubt the cables on the side are enough tension to pull the creases out. I would use this screen for fixed applications only where you can pull the material a good amount.

Overall the material did wonders for my picture - specifically contrast. I came from a 1.1 gain, white, PVC screen. This material is much darker, so Blacks look MUCH better. The material also has a reflective property - the effect is similar to what happens to road signs when you drive with your car's bright lights. So though the screen is much darker, the light areas are actually about 10% brighter than my old screen. The combination of deeper blacks and more POP to the bright areas is a vast improvement for me.

As far as ambient light rejecting goes, I am not sure there is much really happening here. my ambient lights are less noticeable because the screen is dark grey, not white. or to put it differently, because the contrast is so much better with this screen, ambient light has less of an impact to the overall picture.

Negatives:

My biggest issue is that the material can also show some striations of brightness in high contrast scenes that pan left or right across the screen. I believe the reflective coating is not quite uniformly applied in the manufacturing process. The effect is only noticeable if you are looking for it, but it may bother some people.

Not so much a negative, but I did have to retune my color due to the grey screen vs white.

title: Will not power on
text:
Long story short: press power-on switch and the Republic of Gamers logo flashes pinkish every two seconds. There is also a red LED adjacent to the EATZ12V connectors that flashes once every 20 seconds. It’s really gorgeous but that is all this mobo does! I have a Zalman 850W PSU (which I swapped out from an older machine that functions flawlessly) whose shorted 15/16 pins start the PSU purring. I checked all of the voltages on the 24- and 8-pin connectors and they are within anticipated specs.

As a final test, I disconnected everything from the board except the power supply and power-on cable. No joy. Both ASUS mobo’s I have been using have lit LED when the computers are shut down (power on/reset) so I anticipated that this board would have similar LEDs - and maybe it does but, alas, nothing but the flashing logo and the occasional red LED.

If the logo stayed on vs flashing, this mobo could, at least, serve as a night light. Then, too, at $300, that’s a bit extravagant. Yes, a joke, but if I didn’t laugh I’d be crying. I attempted an ASUS help chat but the fellow I chatted with was not sure this X570-E mobo was compatible with the Ryzen 5 3600 CPU. Now I know I’m in trouble. He then wanted to know all about my GFX card and other peripherals. Finally he wanted me to upload an image of the sticker bearing the serial number so he could verify the BIOS version/compatibility etc. but I’m thinking, kind sir, the BIOS is sleeping because the unit will not power on. At this point, I politely thanked the (expert) rep and advised him I would keep digging.

Customer service (chat) is not up to par and QC is surely not something to brag about IF all of these negative reviews are legit. After the chat, I sent an email to ASUS; the response is pending and I will keep you posted.

UPDATE . . . .

Received email response from Lane (ASUS) who adeptly pointed me in the right direction, alerting me to the correct meaning of the mobo LED flashes. Thank you, Lane. I appreciate your rapid and knowledgeable response.

Ed

title: Easy to Setup, Well-Made Outdoor Security Camera
text:
[[VIDEOID:edc427332a939e0d8b08ac4899f0ec8c]] This is a great security camera that works! It's very easy to set up and get going. The app (I use Android), works well and is easy to navigate. I think the hardest part of the setup is actually finding a place to mount it. It is wireless, however, it does need to be powered by an external power source - it's not that big of a deal to me, just something to be aware of. It comes with a lot of mounting accessories in the box and they all feel very well made.

The wifi range will vary depending on walls and interference, however, I was able to mount it about 50ft from my wireless router going through 2 walls and still had decent signal.

The camera itself is a bigger camera, however, it feels very nice and premium in terms of build quality. This is an outdoor camera and it can handle the elements.

The overall picture/video quality is decent - I have attached a photo and video sample from the camera. It's not as crisp as I would have liked it to be, but again, it's decent and clear enough. The night vision works and is acceptable in my opinion. I would say it's good to about 20ft or so.

To my surprise the camera does have some built in storage - it has 32gb available. I found that out through the app and you can set it to over-write old files as it becomes full or just notify you if you don't want it to delete it anything.

For what this is, it works and it works well. If you need a nice outdoor security camera that is well made, this one has my recommendation!

title: These are seriously solid buds, longest life ever!
text:
I am a exclusive user of Bluetooth accessories, and have tons of headsets, always on the quest for the perfect companion. I have had these for a few months now and will say that they are the best earbuds I've ever owned.

1- Runtime, they go for an amazing 14 hours plus re-charge in their case. You can use a single bud in either ear while the other charges so could use them continuously if needed.

2- Flexibility, amazing. You can set them up so that the right and left buds are paired to your phone. Done this way you can take either one out of the case, pop into your ear and it will connect on its own to the phone. should you want stereo, just pull out the other and it's instantly connected as well. The first bud you put in your ear is the "Primary", it is used to answer calls. I often use only one so as to hear sounds around me, and two when I want to concentrate on the content.

3- Connectivity, stellar, I am normally a Plantronics fan but they don't run as long and do have somewhat frequent dropouts. These Creative Outliers almost never have disconnect issues. At most I might hear a very brief blip but far better than any others I've used. I often wear one or both buds for a whole day of walking, working all over the place and these beat everything.

4- Fit, they will fit you or they won't, they do have two pairs of a small and larger size silicone ear tips. I use the small ones. They fit me very well and are comfortable for hours at a time. My daughter tried them and we could not get a comfortable fit for her, so if they fit you, great.

5- Noise cancelling, good, they are basically ear plugs so a lot of ambient noise is blocked. I listen to mine usually and volume level 1 with no issues hearing the content.

My only wish would be for a smaller, more rounded case for pocket storage. On the charge side, while USB-C is up and coming and is probably a better design, I personally would prefer micro USB for the charge connector instead as this is used by about 98% of all accessories around.

I'm now a huge fan of Creative, they really produced a winner here.

title: It's the best laptop for the price if you do photo/video editing or gaming/power demanding work.
text:
Edit: If you are using ethernet cable for gaming and it's not working properly, go in "Killer Control Center" then go in settings and turn off "Advanced Stream Detect".

Amazing laptop for the price, really good desgin (thermals aswell) and quite compact compared to last year's model. There is back light bleed but only noticeable when displaying something completely dark/black (for example when laptop is booting up.) and some back light bleed is in all models of helios 300 so don't worry about it. Also black light bleed is not noticeable at all during normal use or whilst gaming. However, if you see more than expected back light bleed, do contact amazon tech help and sort it out. Battery life is actually better than expected for this power hungry gaming laptop with such a small battery. I highly recommend getting a 2.5" or m.2 nvme ssd. There is one empty slot for 2.5" hdd/ssd and one empty m.2 slot (with another m.2 slot having 256gb ssd pre-installed). I'd suggest 1tb m.2 nvme ssd which goes for around $100 on amazon. Keybaord is really good, though it comes with just blue backlight & no rgb, that rgb model for same price is only available in Australia. You can get rgb model on amazon but you will have to pay more and you will get 512gb m.2 ssd instead of 256gb which is installed in this one. Trackpad is also better than expected since you usually have low expectations from trackpad in a gaming laptop, where you would plug external mouse for gaming anyway. USB-C port does not support thunderbolt 3 or video output, it's just for connecting external USB-C devices, or dongles if you want more ports. Display is really good, 144hz refresh rate ~ 3ms response time makes it one of the best displays in laptop of this price point & bezels are way smaller compared to last year's model. It also feels and looks much lighter than last year's model thanks to compact degsin and actual weight decrease of about 250g from last year's model. Do enable turbo mode (by pressing the turbo button) if you do anything demanding as it will increase the fan speed, so no thermal throttling, it would increase cpu power limit and overclock gpu to extreme. You will get better performance for both gpu & cpu and even ram this way. In my opinion it's the best laptop for the price (I paid $1200 but you can get it for $999 on prime day) if you do photo/video editing or gaming/high performance demanding work.

title: Works as a kickstand like a surface pro at shallow angles and with care.
text:
Surface book 2; 15", i7, gtx-1060.

I think the maker of this product messaged me directly on an online forum to show me this. They looked too flimsy and small for what i needed but owning a $2.5k computer, i had the $40 to piss away, so i bought them.

What i wanted: a surface pro/surface go style kickstand for the tablet portion of the book 2, so i can use as a laptop when i need power and i can stand it up places like the kitchen counter, dining room table, lap, and others as needed. BUT the kickstand needed to be able to always be on the tablet portion, whether traveling, on my desk as a full on laptop or really any other time WITHOUT sacrificing cooling at all or almost at all. That product may exist for the 13" model, but not the 15" model. All the kickstands i could find were either not connected at all (so just a stand that wouldn't come with the tablet if i picked up the tablet) or were full on cases that covered the back metal almost completely.

This is not the product that made that dream a reality, but short of microsoft adding a kickstand to the next model i dont think it ever will exist. But this does come pretty damn close, and in my book close enough to satisfy my need.

Can it hold the 15" model up without the base present? yes! i can even use the touchscreen gingerly without tipping it. BUT only at a 5 to 25 degree angle from vertical. lean back to 30 degrees (by adjusting the height of the stands), and touching it will make the tablet fall. lean to 35 degrees, and it's gonna tip by itself. You'd think it's hard to know where that's at, maybe mark it on the screen or something? NO! actually one of it's "drawbacks" kind of becomes a feature at this point. these things will not let the pen attach magnetically to the tablet on either side, but this is only a problem if you set them high enough to where it would lean the tablet to 30 degrees. So maxing out the height of the stands while the pen is attached gives you a built in landmark to adjust to the best angle. I have thee Pro 4's pen (first pen version that had a working eraser side rather than a purple button), i dont know if they make longer or shorter magnetic pens, but if they do this might not hold true for those pens. I'm not an artist, so i can't speak to the usefulness of these for drawing.

Quality wise they feel like real metal, they're not magnetic so it's not iron/steel. have not had the glue fail just yet. Don't dissasemble them and avoid closing the book 2 with the stand side, which should be easy since i cannot fathom why anyone would close the book with the screen exposed, so if you set them with the arm side of the kickstand on the back side you shoultnt have to move them.

This will definitely be easier if you have a friend to hold the multimeter probes to the output side of this board as it can be a bit tricky to try and adjust the voltage while holding the probes to the board. Alternately if you have a cooler multimeter kit, just use the gator clamps that came with it. Either way, once you get it to your desired voltage just solder up some wires of appropriate thickness, put this in some kind of small project box (3D printer opportunity here) then move on with life. This was definitely a great investment for the price over some of the other adapters I've seen, required minimal work and was a fun little project. Oh and don't forget to double check power requirements for the device you want to power and also fuse things because safety and stuff.

title: Warm, silky, smooth, precise, clean power
text: It's about time Denon reintroduced a true high fidelity line of components in the USA. This amplifier is well above the hum hum avrs I'm accustomed to seeing in brick and mortar stores. The pma800ne integrated displays Denon's prowess and pedigree for developing true high performance components for music only lovers. To me, this amp is like being right in the control room of a studio with the engineer. Any audio manufacturer of repute will say their passion is to faithfully render the artist intent as accurately as possible. That's all you can ask. The pma800ne integrated does this well. If you're seeking a natural sounding high power amp that has good imaging, dynamics, accuracy, good bass lines, smooth treble, fine detail, quick transients--if you favor 2 channel simplicity for a music only set-up, then I wholly recommend this amp. BIG TIP:#1 You may initially find yourself fighting and struggling to engage the direct and the analog button with hopes of higher quality sound, but it's unnecessary, as this amp is already quiet and, in my qualified opinion after many months with this amp, the sound without the direct and analog buttons engaged, is far, far more natural and less noisy. It's tempting to believe those buttons will get you that Nirvana where everything in life falls to the wayside. If you want THAT feeling, don't use them. Your music will get you feeling all warm and fuzzy inside w/o them! With that said, if you get your groove on with that stable, clean, pristine circuit engaged, always be mindful that mine, nor anothers' sense of hearing, matters, and the way I hear will help you naught. Some listeners like speakers towed in, some push their speakers flat against the wall behind them, some use bass and treble controls turned to produce a 'v ' eq. In the end it's your perception alone that qualifies you.

I needed a tool kit to open my phone and tighten my taptic engine. I initially bought this kit because I watched a youtube video demonstrating the repair I needed with the tools in this set. However, after I received this kit, I watched other videos and saw that others were using a metal crowbar to help wedge the screen open. I tried to open my phone without the metal crowbar, and just using the plastic tabs provided in this kit, but they were not strong enough to wedge open the phone. I tried for ~1 hour to wedge the plastic tab between my screen and the frame, but got nowhere. I even broke the keyring from the suction cup, rendering it useless.

I'm giving this product two stars because:

1) It was not a complete set to EASILY open my phone. I bought a different kit and I was able to open my phone AND tighten the taptic engine in half an hour.
2) The suction cup separated from the keyring.
3) The other tools I used, screwdriver and magnet, worked well so it's not a complete waste if you can pry open your phone screen without something more sturdy to create a big enough gap between the screen and the frame.

title: Do NOT allow a full load on this supply.
text:
I use this power supply to power my ham shack. Battery array and all. I have a storm and the power was off for a half day. When the power was restored, this power supply was Driving 50 amps in recharging the batteries etc. It seemed to be working.... an hour later I smelled burning electronics.. But everything was still working... 2 days later the supply failed. I opened it up, and discovered the INPUT surge suppression (Thermistors) were a white powder.
They paralleled 2 thermistors (Without spacing) for the current, BUT they did not anticipate the extra load. (MAX DC output and MIN input (AC) means MAX input current current. Bigger thermistors would have solved the problem.

title: Really excellent performance in my very large old house.
text:
I used this set to replace a hodge-podge of homegrown Ethernet + converted old routers as access points. The old system, despite using as many points as I was, still left dead spots in the house, which makes sense, as it's really old, made of solid wood, and seems to have a lot of slats inside the walls instead of just studs & sheetrock.

The plus of this specific mesh is that it uses the AC grid in the house for part of its communication. I was EXTREMELY skeptical of this-- I've used other products that rely on this technology and while it's a brilliant idea on paper, it's very hit-or-miss in practice.

In my case, I set it up per the app (if you're wondering, you CAN log-in and control/configure the system via HTTP, also), and then placed the points in decent locations around the house (1 downstairs, in the location of the old Spectrum router, 2 upstairs, 1 toward the front of the house, 1 toward the back).

I then metered every room in the house, looking at both signal (2.4 + 5), and then data throughput (speedtest). I was stunned to see that I was achieving close to wall-speeds (speed I'm getting from my provider: 400d/20u) in almost every room in the house, and the one room (at the very back) with the speed dip was still around 100/20.

My downrating on the app is that it's highly simplified, and doesn't offer any useful diagnostic information about the performance of each node, nor the AC portion of the network. So, I just had to assume that's how some of the nodes were talking, because the performance I saw seems unlikely otherwise. Even logging in through the web interface offers about the same level of sophistication-- you can get a few more details, upgrade firmware, etc., but it tells me about 50% of what the Spectrum router does, and about 10% of a ddwrt router.

But, for what I actually wanted-- easy wifi coverage in the entire house, with low maintenance headaches, I seem to have found it.

title: Sexy, Beautiful, and an Overclockers paradise...if you have the money!
text:
I purchased the MSI MEG Z390 Godlike for a personal computer build. I built my system, using the Godlike as my base component. My CPU of choice was the i9-9900k. I included an MSI 2080 RTX Gaming Trio Video Card, and 32 GB of Corsair Vengeance Pro RGB Memory. The cooler I used was a Corsair 150i RGB AIO. I was not disappointed.

The motherboard is black and grey, with silver highlights. It is a large E-ATX board (make sure you have a roomy case). It is presented nicely in the box, without the normal static bag protecting it. This allows for a window to view the motherboard, unobstructed. It is a sight to behold.

The Godlike earns it’s name. It is a beast when overclocking. It has 18 phase VRM and the voltage is stable as a rock. There are two CPU power 8 -pin connectors, and a 6-pin PCIe Power Connector (for overclocking Video Cards). included in the BIOS is management for voltage droop, as well as a myriad of other overclocking related functions. I am currently running my system at a 5.1 GHz overclock, using the Gaming Boost function on the Godlike. The Gaming Boost overclock is controlled via a dial on the mother board, BIOS, or MSI's Dragon Center Software (from within windows). I choose the easy route by using the Dragon Center Software. I was not disappointed. My system is stable as a rock at 5.1 GHz, with manageable heat dispersion (35c idle, 62c Gaming). I am sure I could run a higher overclock using Gaming Boost, as the included auto settings on the Gaming Boost overclock software are outstanding.

The Godlike has multiple LEDs on board telling the owner of the state of the motherboard, and other components, without the need to be in the BIOS or windows. This is very handy for diagnosing errors and other issues. These LEDs are a "Godsend" for hardcore overclockers and allow on the board monitoring while using Liquid Nitrogen or other extreme methods of overclocking. In fact, the board has multiple fan headers, and even a "Pump" header. It even has a liquid flow indicator header. Very handy, indeed.

The three (3) on board M.2 slots allow for a plethora of storage options. Besides the M.2 slots on the board itself, is a PCIe Card with two more M.2 slots. There are six (6) SATA ports, and a U2 connector as well. Note: Using the various M.2 slots will affect the SATA ports and the U2 Connector that are available to use. Using a NVMe is recommended over a SATA M.2, as this configuration will leave the most SATA ports open for use (as well as being much faster for accessing and read/write).

The Godlike has 4 PCIe slots and a Mini slot. It will run Crossfire or NVIDIA SLI and comes with an SLI Bridge in the box. Make sure you use the best slots for your cards, as instructed in the Motherboard manual.

The Godlike has an on-board Infinity RGP Mirror, a "MEG" RGB Tagline, a MSI "Lucky" Dragon RGB, and an amazing OLED Screen with Error/Temperature two number LED above OLED. The screen, and other RGB elements, can be controlled via the Dragon Center Software. The OLED Screen is called the "Dashboard". It can be used to display voltages, temps, and other hardware information. The "Dashboard" screen has a rather cute set of built in function indicators when using said functions; Gaming Boost, Fan and Temperature info, Sleep/Wake/Power On, and Errors. The screen is rather handy when monitoring the motherboard and system. It is also just plain fun. I love watching "Lucky" the Dragon battling Ninjas as a method of letting me know my system is running smoothly. It is just too cool.

If you love RGB lighting, the Godlike will not disappoint. Included with the on board RGB lighting and OLED Dashboard, are headers for plugging in ASUS Aura or Corsair Rainbow lighting accessories. I currently have my "Rainbow" accessories plugged into the board... and it is beautiful to behold. I love that I can control my RGB system lighting from the Dragon Center Software. The software is currently being improved, as it does have some issues. The RGB lighting sometimes has a mind of its own and requires some manipulation for Dragon Center to get the lighting to work properly. The software can also forget setting and revert to a neutral state. My research into these issues has led to my understanding that MSI is working to fix these problems. The 80% of the time the RGB Dragon Center lighting works is a sight to behold. I am sure MSI will sort out the issues, as they are responsive to their customers, as evident by the interactions MSI has on their Forums.

An accessory included with the board, is a Capture Card. I plugged it into the 4th PCIe slot, and it runs like a charm. It does not require driver updates and uses XSplit or OBS to control it. It works wonderfully, and the HDMI Port in the backs accepts ANY outbound Signal for broadcasting. This includes other Computers, Video Cameras, Phones, and Game Consoles. A very nice addition.

I love this board. It is an amazing piece of tech... but it is expensive! This is a premium enthusiast board, and it is not for beginners. If you want the latest and greatest hardware, get this wonderful board. It is amazing, fun, and if you want a challenge (overclockers listen up) it affords one. I cannot recommend this board any more highly, if you have the time and money.

PROS:
Great Overclocker
Two 8-pin CPU Power Connectors, and a 6-pin Power Connector to feed additional power for overclocking video cards
Many Storage Options
Dashboard Screen with Error/Temperature LED above
Multiple Fan Heads, a Pump Header, and Liquid Flow Indicator Header
LEDs displaying system status
Cool RGB Effects (Dragon, Meg, and Infinity Mirror)
Can control many current RGB options (Corsair Rainbow and ASUS Aura)
Beautiful

CONS:
Expensive!
Not for Beginners
Some issues with the Dragon Center Software

Rating: 95/100

title: Excellent quality feel, with consistent speeds, and backwards compatibility.
text:
This CAT8 cable left me really impressed so far. First to note a few things:

CAT8 is a standard that supports up to 40gbps of throughput. This is roughly 5GB/s (or 5,000 MB/s). The more common internet service one could expect to find is 1gbps (which is not slow, but nothing close to CAT8 speeds).
In order to achieve speed of 40gbps (or anything higher than what you may have) everything you are connecting to must also support the intended speeds. This means your router/modem, computer, and switch (if you have them) must all support 40gbps (or 1gbps for 1gbps speeds, 10gbps for 10gbps speeds, etc.)

This also means you must have an ISP service on a 40gbps plan (or 1gbps, 10gbps, etc.) If you know you purchased the correct hardware (everything is compatible with 40gbps) but you are being limited to 1gbps (this is CAT5e speeds) then it could be that you don’t have the correct plan with your ISP. Alternatively, if you know you have the 40gbps plan with your ISP, but your computer is only running at 1gbps, then something within your devices is not compatible (or not properly configured).

Lastly, this is being sold as STP or shielded twisted pair cabling. This means that there is an inner layer (like foil or mesh) that helps reduce EMI (electromagnetic interference). This would make for a more “durable” or “robust” feel of a cable compared to UTP, or unshielded twisted pair. I personally like using STP in walls or in attics, it is meant to be used in industrial settings, but UTP can work just as well (especially with home and basic office use).

So, this is a CAT8 STP flat cable that feels and looks like a good quality cable. It is definitely thicker and the stiffness is reassuring (STP cabling should feel this way). Compared to other cables (with a flat design) that I have tried, this is by far the best one I have tried.

Now, I only have a 1gbps (or 125 MB /s) connection in my home, so there is no way for me to test the full CAT8 speeds of this cable. However, when I tested the transfer speeds from my network storage, speeds were consistent at an average 108MB/s (ran the test thrice). I do have a NVR (Network Video Recorder) that uses a portion of my bandwidth, so this cable is capping at full 1gbps speeds. title: Problem free containers
text: I've seen some complaints about how this container is a rip-off of another brand, but these containers have been around for literally decades, made by different companies from the same design template. What I like about these is that latches are more solid than they usually are on some brands. Harder to open is actually a good thing. Because as these go through some wear and tear, having more flimsy latches is going to be a downside. I've had some that after a while the latch just doesn't want to close anymore because the plastic wasn't made thick enough in that area. The only thing I've never liked about these is the permanent label. It's not easy to remove. You can of course just put another label on top, but it's not every pretty when you do that. Especially if you are constantly relabeling. Also, while padded, these cases will only provide minimal protection for your standard platter drives if dropped. There is just too much that can go wrong with those drives is mishandled. They'll survive probably a two to three-foot drop onto a hard surface inside this case, but that is about it - and there is no guarantee. A little better than if you had your drive in an external enclosure. That being said, I have dropped drives off of book shelves six feet high in these kinds of cases (don't ask me why they were up there), and still had them work because they fell onto the edge rather than flat.

Original review:
I had to wrestle with this device for 40 minutes, despite a few years of experience with Windows 10. What the instructions don't tell you is that you first need to download the Microsoft Wireless Display Adapter App from the Microsoft Store and install it. The next hurdle is to call the Action Center. Per the instructions it should be as easy as Notifications --> Connect --> Select the Adapter, except, I never got a notification, and I could not find the so-called Action Center. Some instructions on the web will tell you to use WINDOWS+C, except, on my system it's WINDOWS+K. This brings up a screen that cannot be accessed by any of the settings controls (bizarre!), which finally lets you connected to the adapter. To me it's a mystery why Microsoft would use an obscure key combination to access this menu. BTW, the Microsoft documentation (including the help text that shows up on the TV screen) is for tablet PCs, where you can swipe to get to the connect menu (another mystery why Microsoft forgets that there are millions of regular PCs out there). After finally connecting, things started working, and now the controls behave like screen copy or duplication just like when you connect an LCD projector.
Overall rating 1 star due to absolute garbage documentation. One should not be required to scan ten websites to finally be able to connect this little piece of hardware.

title: It was easy!
text:
I paid more because I wanted a high quality mount for my nice new TV. This delivered.

Most of the work can be done by one person. The only part that requires two is when you attach the TV to the mount and set the tilt for the first time. Those 10 min would be impossible by yourself. The joint feels loose and the lever that you are supposed to be able to use to tighten it and loosen the joint to control tilt doesn't really work (it sort of functions like the quick release on your bike seat or wheels with a leaver) so you need someone to support the TV while you tighten it for the first time. Once set however, I have never had to touch it again.

I had two reasons for getting the articulated mount.
1) Sometimes we eat in the media room at a table. It is great to be able to put the TV (85") from the wall and tilt it away from the couch and to the TV.
2) I was flipping my room around from watching TV on the North wall to the South wall. This meant many weekends crawling through the attic feeding wires through walls with wires coming from various locations. One weekend it was speakers, next coax and Ethernet, next power bridge. It was soooooo easy just pulling the TV away from the wall so that I could perform the work, cut holes in the wall behind the TV and media cabinet and then just push it back. I was quoted $650 to do this work but the mount made it possible to do it all myself. I guess I could have done all the wiring before the TV was mounted but the TV was on sale for labor day and we enjoyed the TV for 4 weeks while I did all the work to make the set up better and better and better each week until done.
THANKS!

title: Braided, good strain relief, slim, stiff and pose-able
text:
HDMI cables either work or they don't. Since HDMI is digital, the bits either arrive or they don't. If they don't you either get no image, or an image that periodically drops out either because of image signal loss or HDCP instability. A good HDMI cable is not going to deliver better image or audio quality than a bad one. The differentiating factors are really just compatibility (different HDMI versions have different capabilities, and not all cables support all capabilities), and physical attributes. Using better quality material can allow cables to carry signals over longer distances, but the image quality is not going to be degraded by doing long runs with low quality conductors. At 2M/6FT even low quality materials are usually sufficient for high-bandwidth applications.

The main differentiators between HDMI cables, assuming you get one that's good enough to work for your application (i.e. Blu-ray player, PC-to-TV, Game console, etc...), are the physical attributes - quality of casing, strain relief, kink/tangle resistance, bulk etc...

These cables come with right-angle adapters which is a really nice bonus.

The cable itself is thinner than most of the braided 4k HDMI cables I've purchased recently which suggests smaller gauge wire, and/or lack of shielding, but these aren't terribly important factors - wire and shielding which meets minimum specs will perform the same as wire and shielding which exceeds them. So the thinner cord is nothing but a plus in my book because it means less bulk for carrying around with a laptop.

I can't legitimately validate the claim these cables make to support 8K because I don't own an 8K TV because I don't own an 8K source. I can validate that they work great with 4K sources and displays.

Perhaps my favorite attribute of these cables is that the cable is actually stiff and pose-able like a pipe-cleaner. I have one particular TV where the orientation of the wall mount and the HDMI sockets gives almost no room for my hands to maneuver to plug in new cables. It's always a knuckle-scraping time-consuming ordeal. But with these, I was able to bend the cable like into the right shape and position and push it into the socket from several inches behind the plug itself.

In summary, if an HDMI cable works at all, it works the same as a more expensive one with more impressive sounding attributes. Exotic high-end materials are only really useful for very long HDMI cables, and they just make them work, not improve the picture/sound quality. These cables are slim and work fine with 4K. I can't verify 8K because I don't have any 8K things. These cables hold their shape like a pipe-cleaner making them easier to install in tight spaces.

These are priced pretty reasonably for the quality of the outer material. There are cheaper 4k cables with similar attributes, but not that much cheaper, and assuming these will work for 8K, you might be able to keep them around for a while.

Pros:
- Support 4K HDR 10 @60 hz with no trouble
- Slim cord
- Poseable like a pipe-cleaner

Cons:
- none, really

title: Protective, Stylish and Comfortable - A Good MacBook Pro Case
text:
For all my mobile devices -- iPad and iPhones -- I always purchased a very strong protective case and screen protector either prior to or at the time of purchasing the device. I am of the mindset that if I am purchasing an expensive device, its good to give it at least some protection from the elements. But when I purchased my brand new Mac Book Pro, I felt that there might be some benefit from purchasing a cover. There are many cases available on Amazon. The reasons I purchased this particular one were as follows:
- As seen in the attached photo, the painting on the case is beautiful. Based on some reviews, I was worried that it might be a bit pixelated. But that is not true with this case at all. The picture is crisp and in excellent quality. The material on the outside of the case is a hard plastic with good structural integrity, but also soft to touch. There is no rough texture from manufacturing.
- The top and bottom covers are independent, allowing full range of motion of the monitor joint. Both components are also very easy to place. They are appropriately sized and snap on at the top and bottom sides.
- The bottom has multiple ventilation slots to allow the Mac Book Pro to remain cool despite moderate activity. The bottom also is raised due to rubber feet at each corner, this protects the cover from scratches at the base, but also allows it to remain raised enough to allow the vents to be effective.

Another feature of this particular package that I enjoy is the keyboard cover. One major concern I had about buying the 2019 Mac Book Pro was the butterfly keyboard. I had read that if particles of food or dust were to get into the keyboard, it could lead to stickiness of the keyboard. The included keyboard cover will significantly help to prevent all that. It lays perfectly over the keys. Let me reassure you - the keyboard cover is sized PERFECTLY. Each key, each gap -- end to end -- is perfectly sized. The keyboard cover lays and stays in place perfectly. It is very comfortable to type on. It feels rubbery, but that also feels good because it reacts easily to the key press. The "lettering" on the keyboard cover falls perfectly over the "lettering" over the actual keyboard -- so it does not look like an imperfect overlay. Please do keep in mind however that the keyboard backlight WILL NOT WORK simply because the keyboard cover is opaque and does not allow light to shine through.

Overall, I definitely recommend this protective cover and keyboard cover combo. This particular graphic is beautiful and brings a whole lot of color and personality to my laptop. No regrets!

title: I LIKE THIS UNIT – EXCEPT FOR ONE INCONVIENT GLITCH
text:
At first glance, this is a very nice unit. The physical attributes are excellent. The seller’s customer service was top rate. Here is the main issue I found:

Anytime you unplug the USB charging cord (to go on battery backup) OR when you plug the charging cord back in, the power from the battery base to the dot is momentarily interrupted. This causes the echo dot to do a “loss of power” reboot. After the reboot, the echo dot seems to function normally (In both the cordless and charging modes).

I contacted the seller (UGREEN) and they responded VERY promptly. After informing them I troubleshot using different USB cables and chargers, they promptly sent me a replacement. Unfortunately, the replacement unit did the exact same thing. Whenever the battery base senses a power change on the input/charging micro port, the power output from the base to the echo is interrupted. This causes the echo dot to do a reboot. This is definitely a “convenience” problem. Since both my cable modem and router are on battery backup, I can at least use the echo dot for a while if we should lose power (assuming a power loss at our house doesn’t mean the cable internet. connection also goes down). My review would have been 5 stars but for this one inconvenient glitch. I really like the set up as far as how the dot attaches to the base and the short little cable from the base to the dot. Customer support was fast responding and tried very hard to be helpful. Unfortunately, I feel there is an inconvenient flaw in the design or perhaps a manufacturing problem. However, the units are usable, despite this inconvenience.

title: Bright, but poor contrast and focus
text:
I think how you feel about this projector will depend largely on what you use it for.

As a 4K video projector, and for the price, it is a reasonably good deal. I picked my 3200 up on sale at BestBuy. You will find the contrast unsatisfactory for dark scenes unless you have a blacked-out, light controlled room. Of course, good contrast always requires a blacked out room, but even so, the blacks on this are dark gray. For example, when playing Assassin's Creed Origins, I cannot see my way around a crypt without having all other lights in the room off. HDR is not very noticeable, but is adjustable. You will notice the auto-iris kick in a moment after scene changes some times (this is Epson's attempt to make up for the lower contrast levels of this projector). I can live with this, happily, if the projector is only used for video.

The projector is incredibly bright. No issues there. The crappy contrast may go unnoticed in a room without light control. In my basement, with no windows, I find it very bright in ECO mode, even nearly 1000 hours in.

The lens shift feature blew my mind, and hugely simplifies installation without having to mess with keystone correction, which leaves the trapezoidal gray/black light around your picture.

The worst part of this projector is focus. With video you may not notice, but since I've been working from home for the last few months of COVID, I use this as a 142" monitor for programming, several hours a day every day. It is _impossible_ to get even focus across the screen with text. You can have one area sharp and another area dreadfully blurry, or you can have the entire thing slightly out of focus and rub your eyes all day long. Lest you think it may be caused by imperfections in my screen, or not having the projector perfectly centered...I can put a piece of paper in the out-of-focus area and walk back towards the projector 4-5 feet before that text is in focus. So, it isn't due to flatness of the screen.

Tech support: Epson tech support has been good. When I finally bought and mounted a screen to verify it wasn't due to my uneven wall, they happily replaced my projector with a refurbished one via 2-day fedex, prepaid both ways. Unfortunately, the refurb was even worse for focus issues and had light scratches on the lens, so they overnighting a brand new one. The focus issue persists, so it seems to be common for this line -- or my setup is inexplicably wrong somehow. Epson does not have a way to trade-in/upgrade to something better, so I'll probably have to try to sell it on my own and take a loss.

So, overall - acceptable for the price for movie night. Not acceptable for computer work. If you can afford to spend a little more for something closer to true 4K, with better focus and contrast, I'd recommend doing so.

**Update** I have been ceiling mounting this projector to keep it out of the way of people and reduce shadows from the same. The lens shift that was so delightful, seems to be a contributor to the focus issue. Switching to keystone correction instead of lens shift helps the focus, but it is still an issue. Also, keystone correction throws off the aspect ratio so the image no longer fits the screen - it's either too wide, or I have to leave small dark strips at the top and bottom of the image. Finally, I unmounted the projector, put it in tabletop mode, and stacked boxes under it so the image is perfectly centered with no keystone and no lens shift. The center is stunning, but the side is STILL out of focus. I've included a couple pictures from the panel alignment mode to show the focus difference from center to top-right (tabletop mode) when the projector is perfectly centered on a flat, professional screen.

title: Did it's Job, Basic Protection & Great Value
text:
First Off, i take care of my toys, just because i bought a case protector for my MacBook Pro doesn't mean i started tossing it around like a football. That said, this cover lasted 3 years !!

One of the rubber feet came off right away. I took some super glue to it and it was never a problem again. It snaps in place and the fit was "almost" perfect. However it scratched my aluminum case at some point, don't know when.

Eventually it dried and cracked around high use areas. The lip on the top cover cracked right where you lift open your screen. The left tab on the bottom cover cracked all the way underneath, right where you set you palm/wrist for typing.

I think i only ever took the cover off once to clean my laptop. You can see how dirt, dust, and grim can sneak thru. But that is expected with years worth of use.

One night, my laptop slipped in between my bed and my wall and the cover ate up all the fresh paint meant for my laptop. It scuffed it up a little but it did what it was suppose to do. Protect my MacBook.

Overall i rate this 4 stars. A little super glue would have prevented the rubber feet from coming off in the first place. How it scratched my aluminum case i don't know but the tabs can be felt on your wrist when typing. I think i got use to the feeling over the years. That said i just bought another one for my new MacBook Pro and i would be totally satisfied if i got the same exact performance with the new cover. Nothing Less Thou

I ordered 4 of these and HALF of them were 2 of the same direction (that I did not need, and that apparently are the uncommon direction). So, I had to return those and order again to get the parts that I need for two builds.

Anyway, the piece seems sturdy enough. It has a bit of black foam tape over the mini-PCB that links the power connectors on either side of the device. title: Not functioning as a mesh network - TPLink knows about issue but has not fixed it to date
text:
The (frustrating) problem with these units is that they all try to connect to the "main" node, rather than forming a mesh based on the relative signal strengths between the units. And, there is no way in the app to configure how the units interconnect. I have unit "A" (main) in one building, and units B and C in an adjacent building. B connects to A (which is correct) but C also connects to A, resulting in a very low signal strength and low bandwidth for C. One time I somehow got B to connect to C as it should, and the bandwidth was fantastic at C.

Many are having this issue, and TPLink has known about it for over a year per forum posts. They told their customers to "please wait patiently" and keep checking the app in case a solution is provided, but none so far. "All they need to do" is to let us choose an affinity between the units in the app. I will update this review if they finally fix it.

title: Quieter than the Microsoft 600 and the Logitech k120
text:
I was on a quest to find a quiet keyboard, so my keyboarding isn’t heard over the phone. I originally had the Logitech K120, and I also purchased the Microsoft wired 600 keyboard. This Kensington keyboard was the quietest of the three. I did a test over the phone with an Apple headset, and the person on the other line helped me to rate which keyboard was quietest over the phone. The Kensington was the quietest over the phone, with only the space bar being heard when I typed carefully. The Microsoft keyboard was second, and the Logitech being a few years old was the loudest. The Microsoft had a deeper, more consistent sound, while the Kensington had higher pitched mechanical sounds at times. Loudness seem to depend on your technique. If you clicked fast and lift your finger up off the key, the keyboard will make more noise. If you click and keep your finger there to absorb the rebound vibration, it’s much quieter.

From the standpoint of comfort, the logitech was the best, and the Microsoft keyboard was second. The Kensington keyboard is very flat like a laptop so it wasn’t as comfortable. If you’re used to laptop keyboard, you’ll probably think it’s OK. For me I didn’t like the action so much since I was so used to the Logitech keyboard.

All the special buttons of the Kensington worked on windows 10 without any special drivers. If you’re looking for a quiet or near silent wired keyboard under $25, this it’s probably your best bet.

title: A unique & well-made device that's a must for anyone with a Thunderbolt-enabled tablet
text:
I wasn't expecting this to look so small! This is just as big as it needs to be to provide all the ports it offers. And it offers a lot: SD & Micro-SD slots, two USB ports, another USB-C, Ethernet (1000 Mbps), HDMI & VGA - AND supports high-speed data transfer (10Gbps) and PD power supply throughput to the tablet at highest speed & volume (100 watts 20V/5A). This thing is a beast - a very small beast!
It has another feature I value: it is the only hub of its type that doesn't have an attached short cable to connect to the tablet - you supply the connecting cable. That's an added expense, and USB-C Thunderbolt 3 cables (full throughput - not cheap partially but not fully compliant cables) are still expensive. Why would I want that?
Thunderbolt 3 cables need to be as short as you can live with. Even short cables are pushing the technical capabilities of the standard: longer than one foot (30 cm) and you cut throughput & power delivery dramatically. Even the best 1 m cable delivers less than half the power & data delivery. The attached cables on competing hubs are all in the 3-4 in range: plenty short enough & fine for a laptop but too short for my tablet.
If you have a Lenovo X1 tablet or it's biggest competitor the Microsoft Surface, the USB ports are all on the side of the monitor, the actual tablet, and not on the keyboard, which is a slim detachable peripheral. I'm guessing the Dell tablet is similarly configured. This means a 3" hub-attached cable can't quite reach the port to connect: keep in mind that Thunderbolt 3 cables are pretty stiff, too, and don't bend easily. And your patch cable, if it can reach far enough up to connect, is hanging off the side of the monitor, not lying at table surface-height. This leaves connected cables waving at right angles where they are in the way, it puts the tablet at risk of being dragged off the table by the cord, and it puts the connection port in the tablet at risk of being bent & broken by a pulled cable. Not good.
I've paired CableCreation's multi-port adapter with their right-angle 90 degree adapters so their short 12" Thunderbolt 3 cable hangs down tight beside the screen. Where it's safe and out of the way. The cable is very stiff but long enough to curve around behind the tablet, so it's out of the way too.
I love the tablet, but it only offers two Thunderbolt ports for connectivity. We still live in a multi-port world & that means dongle hell. The multi-port adapter is a one-stop solution that connects to pretty much anything. And supports charging or running off A/C in the background.
Quality of construction is great: this thing is milled out of a single piece of aluminum. Ports are all solid. If feels light but strong. It's small enough to take with the tablet. I carry the tablet in a leather zippered portfolio that provides a pad of paper and still has room for the adapter, it's cable and the digital pen that came with the tablet. And a magazine or two.
I'm happy to recommend anything made by CableCreation: I think you'll be pleased with design & quality. I now have this hub, several connection adapters and several cables. All appear to be the best-made peripheral devices I've purchased ever. I've purchased a lot of IT gear in the past 40 years; these are only peripherals and cables, but I always appreciate finding something really well-made. This stuff is.
Delivery was prompt and reliable as I've come to expect from Amazon.

title: Long, Sturdy, Flexible.. What More Could You Ask for In A.. Charging Cable?
text:
Dirty jokes aside from the title, I've been looking for dependable charging cables for my Apple products. The reason? We got a rabbit and they love to nibble through cables (instinctively, they apparently look like tree roots). My original apple cable (RIP) was chewed to pieces. It was also a bit short anyways to where our new bed layout is compared to the outlets (we had just moved). Therefore, it was prime time to go shopping for a solid alternative. I came across this product, which not only provided extra cables for other places in my house / as spares, but seemed strong enough to deter against those evil rabbit teeth.

Durability:
The most important test - WILL IT WARD OFF AGAINST RABBIT ATTACKS? So far, yes! Hallelujah! See pics for the amount of fray the rabbit was able to make onto the cord (it didn't take much to coax her to give it a few nibbles). Overall, fantastic - only a few Nylon strands frayed, which means the cable itself is protected. Well done, well done.

Length:
Ten feet. That's a literal giant. Most people probably won't need cables this length, but I assume this is where part of the premium comes into play. It's great for what I need - I have a large headboard where the outlet is covered by, so my cables need to loop around and eventually settle on my side table. This provides adequate flexibility on how I can position my Apple products and makes it that much more convenient!

Price:
At $14 for 3, these come out to roughly under $5 per cable. This is in the medium to higher end range of cables, but the price is justified when comparing to all the benefits that come with this. There's definitely good quality materials used in this, and I doubt I'll run into issues with frayed heads. I'll update this review if I run into any issues in the future.

text: Since I work from home I need the maximum UPS run time for my home network so I opted for this UPS.  I installed the UPS in my home rack with 2 switches, a DOCSIS cable modem, a firewall, and a 2-bay Synology NAS plugged into it which totaled 133 watts max according to the LCD (the load later settled down to 125 watts).  I connected the USB cable to my Synology since it supports UPS monitoring and configured it to shutdown after 1 minute of battery.  After letting the UPS run for 24 hours to ensure it had a good charge I tested the battery run time by disconnecting power.  The battery capacity plummeted quickly and after only 4 minutes the LCD showed the batteries were at 0% and after 14 minutes it turned off.  My Synology NAS did not gracefully shut down and started throwing repeated alerts that it had lost communication with the UPS when I disconnected power.  The NAS had gracefully shutdown when connected to my old APC desktop UPS so I know that feature should have worked.  I contacted support who instructed me to try the UPS' battery test feature which passed, however he offered to replace the batteries anyway which is a mark in Tripp-lite's favor.  It was then that I decided to look at how to replace the batteries which required me to unrack the UPS and unscrew the side panel.  This made me realize the UPS is not designed to have its batteries replaced while running so I have no more use for it.

title: Audiophile quality:
text:
Spectacular sound quality. I am using two of these as mono-block amps, just using one channel per amp. It is a trick I learned a while ago that bumps quality to the next level. I am using expensive studio monitor speakers with a pro level D/A converter. I have used several good amplifiers in this system, but these little Class D amps are the best I have tried yet. One thing to note: the title of the Amazon listing is "280 watt" It is actually 2 x 80 watts at 4 ohms. This works fine for me, because they play louder than I can listen if I crank it up that loud, and they have muscular, clean, transparent bass. In fact the entire audio spectrum is astonishingly clear. Be aware, your other components will need to be excellent to get the best out of these little amps!

EDIT: Clarification
Because these amps can not be bridged into mono, I use only one channel of each amp. For example, connect the left RCA to the left input and connect the left speaker terminals to the left speaker. Then do the same for the right channel. This does not increase the rated power, but it does do a couple of good things.
- It lets you mount the amplifier closer to the speaker if you wish, using shorter speaker wires.
- It provides better channel separation so that fluctuations on one channel do not steal available power from the other channel. This keeps the power supply from sagging and essentially increases headroom.

I would try one amp first and use it normally to see if you like the sound quality. These amplifiers are intended for near-field or mid-field speakers in fairly close listening situations. If you have inefficient speakers and you want to fill a large room with sound, these are not the amps you're looking for.

In my small studio I sit six feet away from my monitors, they are 4 ohm, I am using XLR inputs, and I do not like to play really loud, so these little amps work for me.

Something to note, the XLR outputs on my DAC put out higher signal level than RCA outputs. This is typical of most true XLR outputs, more so on mine, which go a bit higher when set for that on the DAC. This might impact how loud you can play these depending on your DAC using RCA.

If your speakers are very efficient, say 90 db and above, you could do some serious loud with these. Mine are rated at 84 db, so they will not fill a big room with loud sound, close listening at satisfyingly punchy levels in a smaller room. ( using XLR outputs from my DAC).

So, try one first, see if you like it, add another if you want to experiment with audiophile obsessiveness.
I hope this helps.

title: Constantly shuts off when connected to a USB hub
text:
I bought the Razer Nommo Chroma speakers last year and am finally writing a review of them. I really like these speakers as they both look and sound great (considering there is no subwoofer). That said, they simply cannot be connected to a USB hub, which is really frustrating for my set up. Whenever I have them connected through a hub, they shut themselves off within seconds. Connected directly to a USB port on the USB controller itself (on an eGPU enclosure), they work great and have no issues whatsoever. I've tried multiple hubs, both powered and unpowered with no change in behavior.

This is a problem for me as I only have four USB ports available in my eGPU set up. Having other Razer Chroma devices, my USB ports get eaten up really fast--and not being able to have a device hanging off a hub is a big deal. I already cannot have my mouse or keyboard on the hub, otherwise I experience occasional hangs and delays. I have gone through and updated all my USB controller drivers and still have not had any luck.

I'm not sure what it is about these speakers that cause them to completely shut down while connected to a hub, but that's definitely the case for me. If they worked while connected to a hub (or if I were ignorant to this problem), I would have given them five stars.

title: Impressed with performance connected to Xbox Series X
text:
For a couple of weeks I was looking for something I could use for my new Xbox Series X in my home office for premium sound that would be more compact than the Logitech 5.1 setup I was using. Considering that the Series X did away with the Optical out component, I needed something that would work as a HDMI pass through that would output 4k video as well as decent sound. Dolby Atmos would be a plus, but not totally necessary. I did purchase an HDMI passthrough that had optical out, but it just didn't work well. Kept getting video artifacts or just bad performance.

I've only had the sound bar set up for a couple hours, but I tested the sound using an episode of the Mandalorian in 4k with Atmos... Wow, it was great! The Dolby Atmos worked perfectly and the display was just as crisp as if I had the Xbox connected directly. I setup my Xbox One remote to control volume and for the Xbox and the sound bar to turn on and off together without any problems. Audio is very clear. Music and dialog are free of hiss or muddy sound.

Next, I played Die Hard 2 (already watched Die Hard :) ) the 3d surround was perfect. Felt just like a decent surround sound system. The Logitech was better, but also took up 10x the space as this little guy. Haven't tried any games yet, but I don't expect the performance to be different.

The reason I gave this 4 stars is that I did have one momentary audio glitch that a power on/off fixed. Haven't had it repeat, but if it does I will update.

This isn't the cheapest solution, but is a very good one. If you are looking for something in a small'ish room for your PC or Xbox/PlayStation I would heartily recommend.

title: Worked great for a year. Then it stopped. Fixed it. Finally died after almost 3 years.
text:
When I first got this TV I left glowing reviews. I really loved it. I left it unedited so that you can see how happy I was, and then how quicly disappointed I become. Update below.

UPDATE:
13 months later, it stopped working. First I started noticing little glitches. It would hang and never recover. I'd have to restart it to get it going again. Then one day it didn't recover and system restore was the suggested option. I did that. Worked fine for 2 days, then it said it had an update. Did the update and it never turned on again. The LED is lit, but it will not turn on. TONS of articles and videos about this issue with this TV, I did all the suggestions. Still won't turn on.

Contacted Hisense support. 13 months, so "sorry you're past the 12 months hardware warranty.".
However, the support agent said they could "request" a manual update. Meaning they'd send me a link to download an executable file that's supposed to fix the issue.

Of course, the download for this fix to a KNOW ISSUE isn't posted on their website, so customers can access it easily. After giving them a copy of my purchase receipt, and the TV's serial number, now they want my home address. For a software download. I ask why they need my address for a download link, double-talk ensues. I give it to them. Now I have to wait 24-48 hours for the link. What? I just jumped through every hoop, and you can't just give it to me?
Worst costumer care ever. If this is a KNOWN ISSUE, why do you have to jump through so many hoops for the software fix? Why isn't this a download on the support page of your website like EVERY OTHER electronics manufacturer does?

Suffice it to say I'm not as happy as I was when I purchased it, and now Hisense's handling of this issue and overcomplicated hoop jumping just to get a possible fix adds a level of frustration and ridiculousness that makes me never want to trust this company again. If a year is all you expect out of a TV, then get this model.

UPDATE #2
Finally, 5 days and 3 phone calls later....I got the email with the firmware. It didn't work. Contacted support again and supposedly someone is going to contact me to schedule a service call. TV has been out for a week now.

Update #3
It's about 3 weeks later. Hisense did finally schedule a service tech to come out. He replaced the board, and the TV started up and worked again. It's been about 7 days, and it's still working. Still not sure if it was the update or the board just went out on its own. Tech says it could be either.

Bottom line Hisense did fix it. It wasn't easy, or timely, and the customer support wasn't good..too much run around..but at least I have a TV again. Not sure if I'll trust another update. May just stick a streaming stick in it and stop using its smart features and disconnect it from the internet altogether.

Considering all that has happened, I raised it to 2 stars. Quality control and customer support needs to be better.

Final update- It finally died today. Just kept turning itself off, then will just go black 3 seconds after restart. 6 months ago a huge area of the screen turned brown. It won't factory reset, it won't recognize it won't uninstall any apps, remove my profile...it won't do anything except go in circles claiming a storage issue, but it won't let me uninstall anything.

Hisense support said they'd send me the firmware, but as I mentioned above it's not on their website, they have to send you a link..and lucky me, apparently their systems have been down more than 10 days now.

It's going out with the trash tomorrow. I gave it a shot. Never again.
