Liked: It works. Have a laptop that I had hooked up to an old Toshiba Dynadock that kept losing connection to a monitor when the computer went to "sleep" mode(?) after a period of being away from the computer. Found this EUASOO docking station and read the mixed but mostly positive reviews. Figured I'd give this a chance as my goal was to be able to get 3 displays (2-32 inch monitors and the laptop screen itself) and eventually add another monitor. Plus the price was right vs. others that I thought was comparable. Didn't setup right away as I had a deadline and being a non-tech person, didn't want to mess up my system. Now that I have the time, I am back to running the same setup. Didn't take long as I just changed out connections. I did make sure I connected everything first before powering up as I've been told that could be an issue which I don't see why but I didn't want to take chance with the monitors and keyboard/mouse. Did connect my Fujitsu scanner and had issues connecting. I did have issues connecting before so I'm not counting it against this docking station but just mention this as it is easy to blame the "new" guy in this setup.
Disliked: Got an email AFTER I made the purchase that I needed to check to see if I had the "Thunderbolt" drive(?) to see if my computer is compatible. Whatever as it was too now since I waited but IT WORKS so not an issue at this point but be warned.
Instructions are not intuitive. Why plug into HOST 2 and not 1?
I still need to plug my laptop power supply when I'm in HOST 2. Was under the impression that by connecting to the docking station, that would power my laptop via the connection with the USB-C cable. The Dell docking station does that but that is not a deal breaker but just a warning for those that may think the the way I thought. Would have been nice to have one less outlet being used.
Touching the USB-C cable caused a "recheck" of the system. Just a warning. Mine is out of the way so shouldn't be an issue going forward.
Initially all screen were mirroring each other. Just went into the computer Display settings. Initially the computer only detected two screens; so, couldn't go to the 3rd monitor. Tried to detect and identify. After a few minutes, the computer was able to show 3 screens. Rearranged the screens in the settings to match the physical layout. Initially that didn't work but again after a few minutes even even that, the I was able to move the pointer from left to right and back seamlessly like before. Basically short story long, just give it a few minutes. Was frustrating for a non-tech person but in hindsight, just needed patience as I kept remembering that it didn't take this long before but could very well be remembering wrong too.
In the end, if I can get this to work, almost anyone should be able to do so with some patience. Not sure if I will be able to add that 4th monitor as it seems like It would only work if I hooked up another computer but will update if and when the time comes. Now the next project to hook up computer speakers that I just purchased. Plugged into the docking station and voila. Simply works!
DIsclaimer: was offered a GC for a review. That did not affect the review other than it prompted me to give a review which I don't always do. I did however give more warnings since I'm going to do a review I figured, it should be something that helps. I always find if frustrating reading reviews as you see some that love it and some that hate it in a lot of products.

title: Hit and Mostly Miss
text: At first thinking this would seem to be a power solution for an Amazon Fire TV device.  Particularly when the normal power supply and cable provided with the unit does not have a nearby or available power outlet.  You should know that there is a considerable amount of USB power out variations from one TV to the next.  Additionally some TVs remove power to the USB port when the TV is powered off.  This means that your Amazon or any internet TV box also is powered down each time resulting in a delay before the device is available for streaming.  You will also see (on your TV screen) the statement that the device is not supported by Amazon Fire TV.  Trying these cords with the 4K Amazon Firesticks on a Sony big screen caused me a number of problems.  Periodic reboots of the device for no reason, longer than normal delays in startup, and other operational issues caused me to remove this cord and return to the direct power connector.  In my opinion, stick with the direct power unit that came with the device and save yourself some money.  Too inconsistent and variable for use.

One thing I didn't see mentioned in description or other reviews, is that it has a small blue LED on the top of the plug-in to show data transfer or that it's working. You have to look at it from above, as it's too small to see it otherwise, but it's a nice feature. If you work on your own PC's, or would like to be able to use an old internal SATA drive as an external hard drive for back up, or (if large enough...) as a really big thumb drive. You can get fairly large 2.5" laptop hard drives that fit the palm of your hand, heck, you can even get enclosures for them, and that is a way to get a huge portable external hard drive for your laptop bag. Once I've got these two jobs done, that's what I plan next. Get a low cost 1TB drive for my laptop bag, since my work laptop only has 250 GB SSD, and it's filling up fast. title: Most infuriating tablet I've owned to date
text:
[[VIDEOID:11c94cdbc88354e038a6b0b1cb65932e]] I bought this tablet officially almost a year ago to replace my dying Wacom Capture. I'd been looking into tablets with screens for quite some time and after reading about this one I made my decision and purchased it.
The setup was a pain, even for my Windows computer. Following the instructions and with the help of several online videos, I managed to troubleshoot enough to get it working!
For the next month or so this tablet was my very best friend. I loved it! Colours weren't awful, the resolution met my basic needs and I was having a blast.
One morning I turn it on, however, and the screen and everything on it is bright green. No amount of correction could get it to match my monitor. Tablet was in Pristine condition otherwise, mind you, as I'd been taking care of it in the best way I was able and despite all of my research online I was driven to ask for assistance here. The response was fairly quick and through a correspondence of a few weeks I was able to send in my tablet for a new one as evidently it was a technical issue on their end.
This new tablet works fine in terms of Not Turning Everything Bright Green but the cable on it is driving me to the edges of insanity. It doesn't go in all the way as one would expect and pops out at the slightest bump. The screen flickers like Halloween lights and overall I'm tempted to throw it out the window. You can't hold it at certain angles, the cable has to be twisted a Certain Way and don't even think about adjusting yourself as you draw or that cable is making a leap for it. I have never been more frustrated by a piece of technology.
One day I fear I'll lose my patience entirely and end up snapping it in two. Far too much trouble and it wasn't all that cheap.

title: Amazing unit : A Few Comments
text:
The Helix 7 arrived very quickly, 3 days, even though the projection was about two weeks. So far, the unit came in perfect condition and exactly the way I wanted it. I have not had it out on the water yet but will update if anything changes. READ THE DESCRIPTION YOU ARE BUYING VERY CAREFULLY TO GET WHAT YOU WANT or learn the return policy. This seller has a very detailed and strict return policy that could cost you money just to return the item.
Some issues with the installation, my fault not Humminbird, if you do not follow the instructions: 1. Make sure you have enough cable to move head. The keeper on the power cord will not go through the drilled hole and you will have to redo power connection. This is my second Helix 7 install and I still had to redo the power cord. 2. The unit does not come with a trolling motor adapter. Humminbird used to have special combos that came with a trolling motor transducer instead of the high speed one. They may still, but I did not take the time to look. If you have an old trolling motor adapter, mine is 20 yrs old, the new transducer will not fit. The new one is 1/4 inch too wide. I split mine in half to finish the connection and will probably buy a new one in the near future. 3. This unit does not come with a head cover. 4. The Navionics card is a micro SD card in a mini SD card adapter. I was a little upset until I figured that out since the Helix 7 head will only accept the micro SD card.

If you have never used one of these type units...be very careful if you are going out in very low light conditions. The brightness will blind you if you do not turn it down. Overall the unit itself is amazing. The only drawback is you will have to spend some time learning the operation. The unit will do many things but only if you know how to get there. I am still amazed the detail in the cartography. All the way down to small creeks. Now, if they could only design one to tell which fish will bite.

title: If non-responsive, disconnect battery...
text:
This laptop has been in use at our house for exactly 60 days, in a stationary location, under fairly light google classroom, google docs, and youtube/netflix workloads. We immediately upgraded to 16GB ram, and installed Autodesk Inventor on it, which also ran superbly the couple of times it has been used so far.

Yesterday, it was non-responsive, with no power lights, and no sign of life whatsoever. I put a meter on the powersupply which read 19.5 volts (close enough to spec) but laptop was still non-responsive. I had the 4GB DIMM out and was getting ready to swap it back in and return it under Amazon's extended COVID return window, and the 13 year old to my chagrin said "don't you think we should disconnect the battery to make sure it has reset?" Now in my defense, it has been a long time since I've encountered a system that a long hold of the power button wasn't an effective power disconnect, and in skepticism I pulled the powerplug on the battery for her. That seems to have fixed it.

But now, for this review, I'm pretty skeptical about what kind of lifespan I'm going to get out of a laptop that needs a battery disconnect after 60 days in order to boot. What in the world could explain this? Preparing to update the BIOS as a precaution, but I don't see this issue listed in any bios release notes.

title: Swarovski SLC VS Zeiss Conquest HD VS NIKON HG
text:
Below is my review of the Monarch HG 8x42 and how it stacks up to close competition and less/more expensive competition.

I am coming from a Monarch 5 8x42 (newer ED version) I have used for a few years

Hopefully this helps people make a decision.

My pick ended up being the MONARCH HG 8x42, reasons are outlined below.

So I have tried 4 commonly compared BIONS back to back:

- Monarch HG 8x42 (HG) ~$1,000 new
- Conquest HD 8x42 (HD) ~1,000 new
- Swarovski SLC 8x42 (SLC) ~$1,500 new
- Monarch 5 8x42 (M5) (newer ED version) ~$300 new

They are all different and excel in different areas compared to each other.

Here are the comparisons of the above 4

Sharpness:
SLC>HD=HG>>M5 (HD might be better? I can't find it, SLC I can)

Edge to edge sharpness
HD>SLC=HG>>>M5 (HD "technically" wins, but b/c FOV of HG is so large, more stuff is actually sharp)

Brightness:
SLC>HD=HG>>M5

Least CA
SLC>HD>HG>>M5 (HD very VERY slightly Less CA than HG, SLC CA almost non existent)

Weight (Least to most)
HG>SLC>HD (on stats HD=SLC, in use SLC noticeably lighter than HD)

Color accuracy (Not sure, but to me):
HG>HD=SLC>M5 (HD a little grey prob due to less contrast), (SLC kind of yellow tint?maybe?)

Contrast
SLC=HG>HD>M5 (SLC may have slight edge to HG, I can't tell)

Focus depth
SLC>HG=M5>>HD (HD too thin, gets annoying and always "focus hunting")

Exit pupil (least Black outs during use)
SLC(5.3mm)=HG(5.3mm)=M5(5.3mm)>>HD (5.25mm) During use alot more black out with HD

Focus knob (smoothness/light)
HD>HG>SLC=M5

Diopter adjustment (personal preference between HG and SLC, I prefer HG)
HG=SLC (both locking)>>HD (not locking)

Focus/ over drive past infinity
HD=HG=M5>>SLC (SLC is like -4 or so, HD and HG are at least -6.5)

Close focus
HD-6.5'=HG-6.6'>M5-8.2'>>SLC-10.5'

Eye cup adjustment
SLC>HG>M5>>HD (HD works, just really stiff)

Manufacture
HG Japan, HD Germany, SLC Austria, M5 glass made in Japan finished in China

Build Quality
SLC>>HG>HD>M5 (SLC really feels like quality here, esp. eye cup function)

Construction
HG (Magnesium) = SLC (Magnesium) >> HD (Aluminum) > M5 poly carb/fiberglass/plastic?

Protection / Durability
HD>>SLC>HG>M5 (HD is built like a tank and Heavy, if you rap on it it is solid like a brick. If you rap on SLC you can her something vibrating, SLC does have alot of padding, HG sounds a little hollow and has least padding) Not issue for me, I am very gentle with my binos and I don't hunt.

Ease / pleasure to use
SLC=HG>>M5>HD (focus wheel, weight and FOV: HG>SLC. HD makes you "work" for the view. HD is not as forgiving esp. b/c of focus depth. you really have to get "jiggy" with the focus wheel, have your eyes perfectly centered, the narrow FOV you have to move, weight also makes it more cumbersome)

IMO the optics in the HD might be ever so slightly (I mean very slightly) better than the HG, but the HG's ergonomic and ease of use make it more pleasurable to use than the HD. The HGs are more forgiving. The weight, FOV, and focus depth adds to the ergonomics. In spite of very slightly more CA on the HG vs the HD I find myself reaching for the HG vs the HD. In addition, using the HG leaves me not fatigued, and I look forward to it using next time. Where as, after using the HD I feel fatigued and recalling limitations (like constant focusing and weight) as opposed to recalling what I was looking at. I find the ergonomic of the HD negatively distracting and I find them to get in the way of viewing. And I find the ergonomics of the HG to allow me focus on what I am looking at and forget about the binoculars. I had the same feeling with the SLC (actually even more so than the HG).

At the given prices I think the Nikon HG wins hands down. At cost non-issue the SLC is clearly the best as it should be at ~1.5x the cost. I don't think the SLC's price gives you 1.5x more bino than the HG. M5 is still AMAZING value for price and fantastic binos.

The HG is definitely a considerable upgrade from my Monarch 5 8x42 in every regard.

All of the above are my personal preferences and opinions. In addition, the top 3 (SLC, HG, HD) it is kind of splitting hairs and any of these binos are excellent instruments. I could have been happy with any, but it is nice to have options. In the comparisons above I really needed to look and test them side by side to find the differences.

I hope the above helps future buyers.

title: Wide Rich Sound in Budget Buds
text:
I'm not sure what the qualifications are to become an audiophile, but I'm not one. I'm just a guy that likes music and needs a pair of earbuds to listen discretely at work. I need deep bass, clear sound, reliable connection and decent battery life.

The Truengine SE delivered on all fronts. The big sell on these buds is the dual driver design. The sound quality is superb but not for the reasons I expected. The sound is very rich and well balanced. I expected booming bass and maybe some vocals, but instead, I hear the full spectrum of sound on every track. That's not to say the sound is not powerful, but I would describe it as a mile wide not a mile deep. This made for a very enjoyable experience. I know I'm enjoying a new pair of headphones when I go back through my favorite tracks just to see how they sound.

The Truengine SE fit very well for my ears. I was afraid that they would be heavy given their aggressive design style, but they are not. They sit well in my ear and seal nicely with the provided tips. I've had them in while talking or chewing and they stay nice and put.

My only gripe for these earbuds is the aesthetic design. As stated above, they are a bit on the aggressive side so if you need something that looks discrete, this might be an issue. While they have a nice matte black finish, they are thick at the base and stick out of your ears like plastic bolts. That being said, if you place a premium on sound quality, it's worth the trade off.

Overall, I really like the Truengine SE and highly recommend them as a budget set of buds with a mid-range sound profile.

title: Is it worth the expense?
text:
I am doing many pictures of paintings and art objects in museums. For that you need to take pictures at rather wide angles, at low light (no flash allowed), get high resolution and no distortion of any kind. Up to now, I was using two prime lenses of good quality, one Sigma 16 mm and one Sony 1.8/35. The sigma lens shows quite large distortion, but it is well corrected by the camera.The problem is that I needed to change the lens from time to time, with the risk to drop them or damage the sensor of the camera. The use of a quality zoom lens 16-55 was very appealing. I got this new Sony lens and I have tested it in many different conditions. The quality of the image is fantastic even in poor lighting, you see it from the first shot with very crisp images. When you zoom the image on the computer monitor you could see all the details at high resolution. Even after cropping by a large factor, you could print quite nice pictures.
At 16mm, there is some distortion. mainly volume distortion. A planar painting will appear partly folded. For a lens of this price, Sony should have issued an update of the camera firmware so the correction could be made directly by the camera. I could make the correction with a proper software, but ...I hope Sony will release such an update ASAP.
If the price had been significantly less and a firmware available, this lens will really deserve 5 *. Personally, I don't regret this investment because of the quality of the product and the fact I need to take only one lens with me>

title: Excellent photos and video for a budding pro
text:
[[VIDEOID:6cf40e2975da9e0beaf4f8f094b98e3]] I was a photographer and videographer in the U.S. Marine Corps and U.S. Army for two decades. While I have used Nikon gear in the past, I had not owned any until this Z5 ended up in my possession. I like it more than I expected to. First of all, if you own a lot of Canon lenses (as I do) there is an amazing way to save your investment should you decide to switch over to Nikon bodies and don't want to spend thousands of dollars on new kit right away. I cannot link to it, but simply type this into your Amazon search: Fringer EF-NZ Canon to Nikon Lens Adapter Auto Focus Adapter Ring Compatible with Canon EF Lens to Nikon Z Mount Z5 Z6 Z7 Z50 Cameras Adapters.

The adapter is amazing (you may need to update the firmware.

I am including two photos with this review that were taken using a Canon and a Canon mount Sigma lens on this Z5 body. Incredible! With appropriate adapters I am able to use my six EOS EF mount lenses on my Nikon Z5 as well as on my new Canon R5, giving me a plethora of options.

The battery life on the Z5 is excellent - I have not run out of juice yet in the field. So far that means I have been able to shoot more than 500 images and still have battery left over. You can see video from the camera although I cannot show you the actual quality here on Amazon due to the way the site compresses videos. The 4K is fine for most videography situations and the auto focus is good although Canon's dual-pixel auto focus still has a slight edge when it comes to focus.

One thing I noted and immediately came to love about the Z5 is that it has dual storage cards. This can save your bacon if you are in the field and a card goes bad. If people are paying you for the photos and video you are getting out of this camera that feature is a must in my opinion. Interestingly, you can remove a card on the fly and the camera will keep working using the other card.

The kit lens is not bad at all for what it is. You will eventually want better glass, but 24-50 is a good place to start for well lit situations.

Some of the things I think are important for this kit configuration:

24MP full-frame CMOS sensor
4.5 fps continuous shooting with AF (not for sporting events, too slow)
5-axis in-body image stabilization
3.69M-dot OLED viewfinder
Dual UHS-II SD cards (extremely valuable)
4K/30p video capture (with 1.7x crop), 1080/60p video capture (no crop)
Headphone and microphone ports
Dust and moisture sealed (have used in rain with no issues)

The Z5 does not have a back side illuminated sensor like its more expensive siblings the Z6 and Z7. If you plan on doing a lot of low-light shooting, spend more money for a camera body that has BSI (they collect more light and thereby reduce noise).

If you mostly plan to photograph sports events at dusk, this is not your kit. If you want the primary use to be capturing fast-moving 4K video, this is not your kit. For most everything else I can think of this kit will be adequate to pretty great. You can do a lot with it!

title: Awkward to use
text:
Perhaps it's because I've become so accustomed to a trackball that has left and right buttons on each side of the ball, but this Kensington Orbit Trackball is extremely awkward to use and doesn't have a good ergonomic feel. The main problem is that the left/right buttons are on the side. When I press the left button, I naturally compensate with pressure on the right to keep the device in place. When I do this, I end up clicking both left and right buttons at the same time. As well, when I pick up or move the device out of the way, I end up clicking both left/right buttons.
When I remove my hand from around the device and just use my fingers to roll the ball, the device turns in the direction I spin the ball. However, this only occurs when I use the device on a smooth surface (i.e., granite countertop, stainless steel table).
I didn't have as much a problem with the scroll pads (on either side of the ball) like others did. I have to make an effort not to rest my fingers alongside the ball, which causes the screen/text to scroll.
My preference would be to have the button on top of the device, on either side of the ball. Build-wise, this is a nice device, but for me me that's the only good point.

Pros:
- Good build/materials

Cons:
- Ergonomically awkward

title: Difficult setup and get full resolution on Macbook Pro
text:
Overall this is a nice monitor, it is a great size to replace 2 4K monitors. It is a little shorter than my 2 previous 28" monitors side by side and maybe a bit wider. The ability to have multiple screens in 2/3 and 1/3 sizes helps a ton in laying out and using all that space.

Initially through USB C it will not support the full resolution (5120 x 1440), which made me almost return it. After doing some digging I decided to try display port via this cable from Amazon: "Cable Matters USB C to DisplayPort Cable (USB-C to DisplayPort Cable, USB C to DP Cable) Supporting 8K". That didn't initially solve it, then I installed "RDM" application that allows you to select more display sizes than OSX offered, selecting 5120x1440 and a reboot resolves it. Helpful that the on screen display shows what resolution is being pushed, the other similar applications were changing the resolution but upsizing from the 3840x1024 resolution so it was impossible to use.

Overall I am disappointed that OSX does not support this display natively, so I have to have my charging cable AND the display port cable plugged in, not the end of the world, but it was one of the reasons I switched.

The display itself works well, I am using it for work. Email, coding, etc. and it the text is clear although slightly distorted due to the curve I assume. Not enough to not live with it. One odd thing is the backlight is a little inconsistent, again probably due to the curve of the monitor. For the price I would hope it would be flawless, but after 2 mins of using it I don't notice it anymore.

Overall I would buy again now that I know how to make it work, the real estate it provides makes having 3-5 open windows on the same screen much easier and as I said above much more usable than 2 monitors.

Hopefully the review will help others to get around the OSX issues.

title: It works, but the TB3 specification is kinda a mess
text:
I bought this to be used for my eGPU (which is a Razer Core X in tandem with my Razer Blade Stealth i7-8550u) just in case I needed a much longer TB3 cable, and it works for that use case. I don't have the know-how in doing performance benchmarks in finding a performance loss if you'll use a much longer cable like this one than the included cable in the Razer Core X (I'm saying this because it's commonly asked). But after testing it out on games I didn't really notice any major performance loss. But I'll say that using the included shorter cable feels more responsive overall, but I think it's just me. The cable quality is good, the cable is sturdy enough to handle a daily in and out bag throw, but I'll strongly advise to still take care of this, why? Because this is too expensive for a cable.

Now regarding the TB3 specification, again in the case of using it for an eGPU it does work but if you're looking at this and (NOT JUST) using it for TB3 devices but a "one USB-C cable to rule them all", this is not it. This is relevant because USB-C should simplify the cable & ports specification problem we're having, but with the TB3 specification this isn't helping. This cable is what they specify as an active TB3 cable which means you can only use this at its actual TB3 specs when IT'S connected ON both ends to a TB3 enabled device. This means if you want to use this as a native DP (Display Port) cable for your monitor, this cable will not work. Another thing is if you try to use this as a normal USB cable, it will only WORK AT THE SPEED of A USB 2 (480 Mbit/s) NOT the speed of USB 3.0 (5 Gbps) or 3.1 (10 Gbps). But obviously if you don't plan on using this cable for those cases, then this should do you fine. And lastly, the thing that I don't like the most is the price, these things are just too expensive. So just make the most out of this if you decided to go the TB3 ecosystem.

Side note: The TB4 specifications is on the works as of writing, so if you don't really need this but just wanna try out TB3, I would advise to wait until the end of this year or until next year for the TB4 to make its appearance. The TB4 specs seem to address the problems of TB3 standards and also that may hopefully drop the prices of TB3 accessories and cables.

title: Great, but limited.
text:
I really really wanted to love this monitor, it had the hello webcam and built-in speakers along with HDR and FreeSync. Unfortunately, I game very rarely, so those last two were not a big deal for me. I had just recently bought a Dell U4919DW, after which saw that this monitor was now selling for $850, quite a bargain compared to the $1200 I spent on the dell. Used this monitor for a few days, and after frantically googling solutions, looking for any reason to keep it, finally gave up and returned them.

1. Compared to the Dell, the KVM is limited to 2 computers, and one has to be the USB-C. I have 3 computers I rotate around, my work laptop, my home PC and a Mac. The Dell easily rotates among all 3 and it is able to do so because the Dell comes with 2 USB upstream ports whereas the Phillips only comes with one (there was something in the manual about the third USB, being able to be used as a upstream port, but could not figure out how). The Dell also comes with 5 USB A outputs (2 of them easily accessible), whereas the Phillips only comes with 3.

2. Phillips' SmartControl is useless. Dell's DDM is bad, but SmartControl is worse. You can change brightness and contrast with both, that's about it. At least with Dell's you can use it to configure the KVM, use it to switch inputs and create a custom desktop layout. You can't do that with the Phillips' app.

3. Could not get the PBP mode to display full screen, even after setting the resolution to the correct layout. That might just be me, but it was frustrating nonetheless.

4. Cable management is non-existent in the Phillips, leaving all the cables dangling as if its the 19th century.

5. There is a weird bug in PBP. I had turned off and disconnected the monitor, decided to give the monitor one more try, and reconnected just one PC using DisplayPort, the monitor remained stuck in the PBP mode will not display the output. Clicking on the Menu button only brings up the language change options, nothing else. Maybe if I had reconnected the other PC, things might have returned to normal, but, I didn't bother. This is the main reason I gave up and returned it.

title: Best softbox I ever had
text:
[[VIDEOID:9a86aebdc3b3397b3932739e6417f467]] The Mivitar is a Bowen mount softbox. It measures 35.4inches wide and 24 inches deep, a pretty large and deep softbox.

What is in the box?
It comes in a nice carrying bag.
It is sturdy and padded with two handles. In the carrying bag, You will find the softbox itself, two external diffusers, one is the traditional softbox diffuser, and the 2nd one is more a clear frosted diffuser with a grid pattern. It is also not as soft as the standard white diffuser. The description says that the white diffuser is for photography, and the frosted diffuser is for video.
Also, in the carrying case, there is a grid,
Now. It does not come with an inner diffuser, but there is a place to install one.
The structure core is an umbrella style for quick setup, but it is not the conventional umbrella softbox style. It does not have the intrusive rode in the middle.
Also, there is no assembly at all. The softbox cover is attached to the core so that it will not slip down when opening and closing the softbox.
Build quality looks to be very good.
The measurements on this softbox are well planned for the most part. Everything fits perfectly.
The softbox does stretch at the back part to the point that you can see the light through the seams, but it is pretty loose in the front of the softbox.
Now, the only place the softbox is tight snugly is the flaps with the velcros at the softbox's back. With that said, the flaps are doing a great job covering all the roads entirely.
Material wise. The softbox itself is a type of plastic, it looks and feels strong, but only time will tell. I personally never had a softbox that ripped.
The core itself also feels sturdy, especially the top part of the rode and the locking mechanism.
To lock the softbox roads, you need to carve up the road until you hear a click.
Now you supposedly need to do it one by one.
But I found a much quicker way to put it together.
So if you first lock the four roads from the opposite sides, then all you need to do is push down on the Bowen mount, and you will get all the roads to lock at once.
Much quicker and, in my opinion, less stress on the roads and the locking mechanism.
To lose the roads, you need to pull up the road a bit to ease the locking mechanism and then push back the lash.
I tested both diffusers and found that the frosted diffuser almost used half of the white diffuser light intensity. Both diffusers are softening the light equally, in my opinion.
Now, I am not sure why one is better for video than the other. The only thing is with the frosted diffuser; you would get away with using small lights like the Godox SL60 easily.
Also, with the frosted diffuser, the background will be darker compared to the white diffuser.
Again, you can use either one with excellent results. Just with the frosted one, you wouldn't have to crank up the intensity as much.
For me, this is the best softbox I ever had. I highly recommend it.

title: These must be paired in stereo!
text:
There will be plenty of reviews for the Studio in stand alone, single speaker use. It does sound excellent that way. But if you pair two Studios and throw in the Echo Sub, that is an extraordinary composition! That is the way to do the Echo Studio! That is how I'll review it here.

I decided I must pair two Studios since I had two Echo Plus's stereo paired with an Echo Sub and it sounded pretty darn good. So I had to try the Studio paired in stereo, and since I had the Sub, I threw that in too. What else am I going to do with it? The Sub added a lot to the two Plus's. I wondered would you even notice it with the two Studios? I'm here to say that you definitely notice it. You notice it's not there, I can tell you.

The sound of this whole system (two Echo Studios and the Echo Sub) is quite exceptional. I would have to say it's thrilling! Yes, it costs $530 but that is bound to come down and did I tell you that it sounds incredible? It commands a respect, it really does. There is such a depth to this. The bass is deliberate and authoritative. Very punchy. It has exceptional dynamic range (at high volumes this can be startling) and the stereo image is just stunning. An enormous stage. Those 6 midrange speakers sound sweet indeed. Be sure to turn everything up in the equalizer in Audio Settings of the device in the Alexa App. This thing likes loud! It can easily handle max volume for extensive listening.

You crank this up to ten and it literally takes over the room. If you can listen at that volume for awhile with this system (you must live without neighbors) you will be found with a huge smile on your face.

All of Amazon's music library is now available in lossless CD quality streaming or better, which shines on this. The new celebrated 3D formats also sound excellent, though I thought there'd be more to them (Abbey Road sounded great but I didn't think it was transformed). But anything you play on this will sound exceptional. I really can't believe Amazon has taken it this far from the original Echo. Bravo! I notice that the Apple Homepod is now down to $200 at Best Buy. Would two of them paired sound better than this setup? I truly doubt it. They'd need a subwoofer and none, as far as I know, are available for it.

A few things. The circling Alexa lights are now on top of the speaker. You can no longer really see them from the side, which is unfortunate. I love those lights! And two, the Studio comes with this "spatial" setting set. I recommend turning it off. In the Alexa app, go to the device and then Audio Settings and below the equalizer is that on off button for the spatial effect. I don't find it adds anything even though it really changes the acoustics. But if you want to hear music as it was recorded, leave this off.

Oh, and I have to say that Amazon still does not make it super easy to set this all up. You have to start with a new or deregistered speaker. Set up each separately and then pair them. But it's anything but obvious or close to foolproof. Come on, Amazon!

And I feel I must tell you that you can't connect to the Studio by Bluetooth when stereo paired. It will only play through one Studio, the first one you set up. To use the Studios in stereo pair with the Echo Sub, you can only stream. And you can only stream if you pay.

Finally, then, these things are big. Really quite large. And seemingly only available now in black, though there's a gray one in Amazon's web site ads. This is not a speaker that sits demurely upon a table. It's almost as big as the Echo Sub, if that helps visualize it. But you will definitely be challenged as to its home, because that is where this will stay, like forever. Especially if you go for the whole magilla. But I urge you to at least try it (the whole magilla!). But be prepared, I guarantee you won't send them back!

UPDATE: After a software update, the Spatial effect is now the preferred way, so leave it on. Turning it off now makes the music too flat. I think it may even turn off one of the mid range speakers. But something's missing!

ADDENDUM:

After two years, these still shine as brightly as ever. But the thing that must be emphasized is that this system of two Echo Studios and the Echo Sub is designed to take full advantage of Amazon Music’s HD streaming service, since these can work together only with streamed audio. Using that enables you to get at least CD quality audio recorded in lossless FLAC files (what Amazon calls HD, 16-bit/44.1kHz) for everything in the catalog, and Ultra HD (up to 24-bit/192kHz) available on an ever-growing list of recordings. In addition, it is also capable of playing Amazon’s (admittedly still in limited quantity) so called 3D Audio recordings (Amazon Music supports Dolby Atmos and Sony 360 Reality Audio spatial audio formats). If you don’t get the Amazon Music HD package ($12.99 monthly with Prime / $14.99 without), then you will be missing out on what these speakers are designed to deliver. Amazon’s Ultra HD music must be heard on a system that supports it to be appreciated. It truly is something else in audio quality, significantly better sounding than any CD or LP. And Amazon Music’s catalog is growing by leaps and bounds every month. It is currently quite vast, even its Classical Music selection which has exploded in the two years since the Echo Studio was introduced.

Using the Amazon Echo Link ($140), you could get this same quality streaming audio (or even better depending on your amp and speakers) for an existing Hi-Fi setup (at least I think you can- there seems to be some confusion about whether it supports the full 24-bit/192kHz Ultra HD), although you could not get 3D Audio with the Link. You could also use the Echo Link to attach any other sub-woofer to your Echo Studio pair but that would also require an additional amplifier thrown in. However, if you don’t have that Hi-Fi system already, these (2 paired Echo Studios and the Echo Sub) are the way to go to take full advantage of Amazon Music HD at a very favorable price. Just compare their cost to that of a good Hi-Fi system consisting of amplifier, pre-amp, two speakers and a sub-woofer as well as the Echo Link you’d need. The Echo speakers here are a definite bargain for getting excellent audio with minimal wires or fuss!

title: An decent deal
text:
I wanted to replace an old after market pioneer car stereo. I needed a detachable front cd player unit and wanted to upgrade to something with bluetooth. I also wanted to spend around 50 bucks or less if possible. After looking around, I decided on this BOSS 750BRGB stereo.
. This stereo shopped for $53 n change on amazon with free Prime delivery, the same stereo is priced for 71.99 on the BOSS AUDIO web page and 59.99 on walmart. com.
. The stereo arrived overnight, brand new in box. It included the unit, instructions, hardware, wire harness, and remote control.
. The installation was very easy, AND IM AN IDIOT!
. Right out the gate i noticed improved sound over my old pioneer stereo!
. Also, right out the gate I noticed the longer loading time for cd's to play, and I don't think the unit provides song/artist/album info text on the LCD screen. I'll have to look into it. I suppose I'll get used to this.
. After a week with the stereo I am satisfied with the bluetooth capabilities. The unit pairs with my android phone right away and it transitions smoothly when I turn off the engine to pump gas or something. Pretty impressive.
. The unit offers preloaded equalizer settings, loudness option, and lets you customize treble, bass, and speaker volumes.
. The stereo offers choices of color lighting (Single color at a time). The unit is very BRIGHT, and I don't see an option to dim the unit.
. I have not tested the remote control nor the call capabilities.

Overall I am satisfied with this unit. The sound is good, and the bluetooth capability has been solid. I kinda miss being able to look up the album/track/artist info on the lcd screen. The cd player is a little slow to respond and loud as it does its thing, it reminds me of the cd players from the 90's. I hope it has longevity.

text:
After having these for over a month now, I can say they are really not worth $130. These work okay as long as you have decent service. 4g is spotty and 3g not at all. So with the new 5g might be great. The sound goes in to some sort of test mode from time to time. It kinda cuts out in both buds, then in one then the other. Even tapping and holding has to be done carefully or it won't work. The biggest draw back for me though is how it operates the music on my phone. Alexa will turn the volume up and down but she won't chance the songs. Not even to the next or previous song. You have to do that by tapping or grab your phone. Which I can get from a $40 set of buds.

The good things are the passthrough is nice and you can have alexa turn it on and off. So when things get noisy I can just have her turn it off so I can keep doing what I am doing and still hear the music. The sound quality is great. They do all the normal Alexa stuff like tell you the weather or time, etc. They do fit very well with the different size ear pieces so you don't have to buy anything extra. I have not experienced any problems with the charging like some other have stated.

So all in all they are of good quality and sound but not $130 worth. I would say $60 at best. The only thing these bring to the table is the passthrough and the Alexa. To me it's not really worth the $90 differance i can get from the cheaper $40 ones.

text: A bit pricey these days for it's size, but there is one feature of this SSD vs others that was of particular interest is that it has Power Loss Protection. PLP (on a basic level) basically means if something happens between the time the disk receives the data from the OS and it's actually committed to flash, it stays in a capacitor-backed DRAM; which under most circumstances won't matter to most people...but in a data center this how data stays consistent through a failure; or, if you're using a ZFS File system and want to use an SSD as a ZIL...if that makes sense to you, then this disk's slightly more expensive cost would make sense for you!

title: Are you actually using the 5G band with this adapter?  (** Updated **)
text:
The driver for this adapter (apparently Realtek) for some reason disallows setting the preferred band, i.e. 2.4 or 5Ghz. While the driver automatically installs, as default configured, it seems to prefer the 2.4 Ghz band. I had to configure a Windows adapter profile, and play with the driver configuration to disallow all protocols other than 802.11ac to get the laptop with this adapter to even connect to the 5G band. After a couple of hours of such tinkering, this adapter connected to the 5Ghz band .... for three days. Now, it will only connect on the 2.4 Ghz band.

I have my NETGEAR router configured with "smartconnect", i.e. it presents one SSID for all available bands, and allows the network to choose which band to connect on. I may switch off smartconnect and segment the network into multiple bands (i.e. separate SSID broadcasts for 2.4 and 5 Ghz), and try connecting on a dedicated 5 Ghz band before returning this adapter. However, I'm working in parallel between two laptops, one with this adapter installed, and one with a native 2.4/5 Ghz adapter installed, but with same Windows versions. I can only attribute the differences in the driver and behavior to the adapters and drivers installed to support them. This adapter has been a bear to configure for a 5 Ghz band connection.

Bottom line: This adapter seems to work well if 2.4 Ghz is what you're looking for. However, you won't get 1200 Mbps connectivity in that band. As a 5 Ghz band adapter, this is pretty much a fail. I'll update this review if I see improvements with further testing.

Update: In response to the vendor's comment below, computer installed is an HP laptop with Windows 10 OS, properly patched and updated, with an SSD drive, ample disk space, and etc. The router in use is a Netgear "Nighthawk" X6 R7900 dual band router. There are other devices that successfully connect to the router on the 5Ghz band, through three stories and different locations and distances. The router works fine. The PC where this NIC adapter is installed, works fine.

I turned off Netgear's "smart connect", thus splitting the network bands into one 2.4 Ghz, and two 5Ghz SSID's. Then I attempted to directly connect to the 5Ghz SSIDs. Neither would connect. I disabled the 2.4 Ghz band, and then the NIC attempted to "automatically connect" between the two (5Ghz) bands, rolling between them until after a half dozen unsuccessful passes, it timed out with a "cannot connect". I attempted multiple tests, turned off the embedded 2.4 Ghz wireless NIC to ensure no conflicts, uninstalled the Realtek driver for the ChainPlus adapter that Windows automatically installed, and then installed the driver provided with the enclosed DVD disk, uninstalled and allowed Windows to automatically install the driver once again (appears to be the same version as on the DVD), and etc.. I probably spent 3 to 5 hours playing with this adapter and the driver configuration, but the ChainPlus NIC can't hold a 5 Ghz connection. I tested with the laptop 15 feet away from the router, and as I've said, other PC's, printers, and devices have no problem connecting to this router in either 2.4 or 5.0 Ghz bands, through 3 stories and up to 100' from the router.

Further tests eventually resulted in BSOD's. It's been at least 10 or 15 years since I've seen an attached device destabilize Windows to the point of a BSOD. I threw in the towel at this point, uninstalled the Realtek driver, and this wireless NIC is going back to Amazon.

I'm a 35 year technology professional, Unix, Linux, Windows, programmer, developer, Database Administrator, and etc.. The NIC I have is defective, will not connect to a 5Ghz band, and destabilizes Windows while connected to the PC. I suspect some sort of incompatibility between the Realtek driver and the device. When it comes to devices and Windows PC, the drivers are everything to ensuring compatibility.

title: Robust, Well-Designed Surge Protector with 6-Ft Cord Can Power 8 Devices at Once!
text:
For years, my living room has had a dirty old power strip with loose ports, making it easy for plugs to slip out. Lately, I’ve gotten tired of constantly looking at it and having to reinsert plugs, particularly as I’ve been staying home all the time due to the novel coronavirus restrictions. I’ve been spending way more hours in the living room for meetings, screenings, live streams, meditation, yoga, dance, etc.

In the past few months, I’ve upgraded to a new HP Chromebook and a new Samsung Galaxy S8 phone. As the lockdown continued, I ordered several speakers and headphones/earbuds. I reckoned I should get a surge protector to protect my investment.

Unlike my flimsy, dirty old power strip, my new, black Bototek surge protector is stylishly designed with round curves. It appears to be robust and well-built. Its six-foot power cord comes in handy when I need to stretch the length, i.e., for a vacuum cleaner.

I chose this model because it has four USB-A and four AC power outlets. One AC outlet is set apart with extra room to allow for a big plug. At times, it’d be nice to have more power outlets, but I knew what I was getting into.

The only other thing I wish was different is that the USB-A ports don’t support fast charging, say for my Samsung Galaxy S8. That’s okay: I get around that by using my wireless charger’s fast charging or my charging station’s PD port.

The power strip can power/charge 8 devices at once! For example...
USB-A 1: Samsung Galaxy S8
USB-A 2: Bugani boombox speakers
USB-A 3: Earbuds
USB-A 4: iPhone
AC 1: Wireless charger, which has a big plug that fits into the wide-spaced outlet
AC 2: Toshiba Chromebook
AC 3: Lamp
AC 4: Bototek charging station (black, matching the surge protector)

Because the charging station has four ports and the wireless charger can hold two devices, my configuration can technically charge 14 devices!

Actually, it’s potentially even 17 with the five available USB ports on the Toshiba Chromebook, the Bugani boombox, and the HP Chromebook plugged into the charging station. But let’s not get carried away now...

text:
Wow what an amazing speaker. Literally if you want to shut down all the speakers in a big open space then this is the speaker for you. The speaker isn’t perfect as obviously nothing is perfect in this world but it does have a lot of pros and obviously it has its cons but overall its an amazing speaker. So lets talk the good and the bad of the speaker.

Now the good. The good of this speaker is that it sounds amazing. The clearness of the sound and the loudness that it can go i never heard a portable speaker sound this crisp at high volumes. I owned and heard many of these speakers that be at the parks or beaches and mostly of them are PA speakers which literally have no treble or base which makes the music sound awful. If you want quality sound then this is the speaker for you. The build is top notch you can feel the quality and the weight the speaker has (literally its 30 pounds) it really makes it feel like its top quality. The weight doesn’t bother me but if you are a person who can’t carry heavy things this ain’t the speaker for you. What also makes this speaker unique is that the battery is swappable which is a major plus. I tried many portable speakers and none of them last for more than 6 hours a full volume. They might advertise it can last 50 or more hours but they are being super generous and most of the time the speakers last 5 to 6 hours. Atleast with this speaker you can swap the battery and can last literally a whole day playing at full volumes if you own multiple batteries.

Now the bad. Like i saw previously these companies be advertising that the speakers be lasting 50 or so hours which is completely bull. In the description soundboks says that at full volume the speaker last 8 hours which is a lie. At most i have gotten 6 hours at full volume and that in indoors mode. In outdoor the battery last 3.5 hours at full volume. I own multiple batteries and none of them last 8 hours at full volume. The only bad of this speakers is the battery because for the price you would assume this speaker would last longer than a 100 dollar speaker which it doesn’t.

Overall i do love the speaker as i get a lot of people trying to tell me where i got it but the price is just insane for what I received. I was expecting a 40 hour speaker which is the reason why i got the speaker but i wat i got was a very loud good sounding speaker that actually needs like 3 batteries to last a whole day.

title: A long cable that will guarantee 4k-8k compatibility with anything you can throw at it!
text:
My review applies, specifically, to the 16ft, 8k cable. For shorter cable runs, you'll likely be fine with a standard 4k 18Gbps cable. (Assuming you aren't worried about 8k in the future)

This (16ft, 8k) is the cable to get if you want to be absolutely certain that it will work with every 4k-8k HDMI feature and standard at a longer length. I needed a 15ft or longer 4K cable to use with my monster gaming PC. Every other 4k cable I tried at longer lengths had some kind of short coming. The ones that could manage 4k@60hz would not also do 4:4:4 chroma and full dynamic range. Any time I tried to enable all of those features at the same time on other, cheaper long length 4k cables, the picture would flicker and sometimes cut out. Only the shorter 4k cable runs would manage to do it all at the same time. You could argue that 4:4:4 and full dynamic range isn't necessary and doesn't make a big difference. But if you're spending a ton of money on your displays, computer or other A/V equipment, I think you'd be aiming for the best picture quality. That said, this 8k cable will do it all. With a monstrous 48Gbps data rate, there is no signal this cable can't handle. If you need a shorter cable run, you'll be just fine going with a shorter 18Gbps 4k cable. But if you need something longer, this 8k cable is worth every penny.

I've been running my PC games 4k@60fps with 4:4:4 and full dynamic range from a 1080ti and haven't seen any video anomalies in the few days I've been playing. I can also say that every other resolution and ultra-high framerates have been working flawlessly as well. Not to mention, it'll also do 8k in the future, if that ever becomes a widespread feature.

This cable is extremely hefty and sturdy as it's rated for in-wall installation, so keep that in mind if you plan to use it outside of the wall like I am. It's flexible enough but you won't be making any super-tight, sharp turns with it very easily. But that's a good thing. This cable looks and feels like you could drive a bulldozer over it and not make a dent in it.

Highly recommended and quite worth the money, unlike the flimsy, cheap feeling of so many other HDMI cables. If you need a fully capable 4k cable for a longer length run, this one is the best I've seen! Price is also very fair considering the length, build quality and technical specifications.

Highly recommended!

This is, by far, the best gaming headset I've ever owned.

Fit

It connected to my Xbox One immediately with no problems. It's surprisingly light and comfortable, making it easy to wear for hours. The headphone cushions are comfortable and seem to breathe really well (unlike other headsets I've had that tend to get hot because the synthetic leather traps heat).

Sound

Even better, there are two volume controls: one for the game audio and one for the chat (in case your squad has zero radio discipline and you need to sneak around in a game, you can turn them down to hear enemy footsteps).

Microphone

The microphone is unobtrusive - it folds into the headset, so it won't get snagged on things while sitting out. The mic audibly alerts you when it's switched between live and muted. title: So far so good... But beware of advertised features.
text:
I purchased this as a replacement for another product that fried my brand new drives after 24 hours. So far so good. I have a few complains, though. First, the main reason I got this was because it says on the box: Individual Power Switches per hard drive. I was expecting a power button per drive so I could turn off and on each one as needed, for example during swaps. This is not the case. The individual power switch is actually one of those DIP switches on the back that you have to move with a tiny screwdriver. It is more of a 'disable bay 1-4' function rather than power on off. I don't see why I would want to disable a bay at all.

Second, the hot swap capabilities are poor. I am using a mac, and when you eject a drive on the OS it does it correctly. However, when you pull that drive out, the device disconnects ALL drives giving you the error of improper removal of the other 3 devices plugged in. So, in order to remove a single drive, you need to eject ALL four drives to protect your data. Thats a bummer, but in fairness is something I have seen in most external multidrive enclosures.

Third, the power button is a soft-button, which means that in a power failure the device won't turn back on again. You need to re-start it. Again, I chose this over the more popular brand here because that brand has this dreadful feature as well.

So overall: I paid $30 more because I was expecting more. In return, I got a device that seems to be feature identical to the Mediasonic one -- except that is uglier, but maybe sturdier. Time will tell.

title: NVIDIA SHIELD TV USERS BEWARE...
text:
TL;DR: This drive is 'teh s uck' / see bottom for alternative.

I purchased the 128 GB drive to use in conjunction with my Nvidia Shield TV (16 GB). I chose this specific drive because it was one of the few drives that Nvidia recommends you use. Nvidia warns that using other drives may result in slower performance so you know there's some backroom handshaking going on between Nvidia and Sandisk. I connected the drive and set it to be used as internal storage. All seemed well, for one week, then the drive failed.. ..completely.. ..as in "He's dead, Jim!".. ..as in "This is an ex-thumb-drive".

Points to make:
1. The USB connector on this drive gets intensely hot when its plugged in.
2. After the drive failed, I removed it from the Shield TV and tried to repair it using my PC. The drive is unreadable from Explorer, so I used "Diskpart.exe" (from a command prompt) to 'clean/create MBR/new primary' the drive and I noticed it took longer to complete than it should have.
3. When I then tried to format it within Windows, it froze indefinitely.

1+2+3 = Either the drive was faulty straight from the factory or using it as directed by Nvidia damaged it. Either way, I now own, well, ..nothing.

Caveat emptor, people!

Side note: The slide mechanism this drive employs to expose the connector is poorly designed as it doesn't sufficiently lock when extended. As a result, you need to keep your finger/thumb on the slide when plugging it in or it will retract into the sleeve during insertion.

Suggestion: If you are looking for a better solution to expand storage for your Nvidia Shield TV, I recommend using the "VectoTech Rapid 128GB External SSD USB 3.0 Portable Solid State Drive" (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01JKMZ70G/). That is what I'm currently using and there hasn't been any issues. It may cost a bit more, but it is a dedicated SSD and because it connects with a cable, there's less chance of heat damage to the drive.

title: Great Gaming Laptop under $2K
text:
I had been wanting a new gaming laptop for a few months. When my ASUS G50VT-X5 died after 10 years of faithful service, it was time. After a couple of months of use, I can say I am extremely happy with my purchase.

This may be due to my liking "older" games (I do play the 2016 DOOM) and not really delving into today's AAA titles but, I have some FPS info that may be helpful.

Pros:

Great graphics performance from the RTX 2070. Playing most games at over 60 FPS on their highest preset (exceptions are the Total War games I have. Empire will run between 30 and 70 depending on the size of the battle. Rome II was usually over 30 in battle and capped around 50 on "extreme" preset with AA turned off.)
DOOM 2016 avg 80 FPS
World of Warships 75 FPS
Minecraft Java max settings (graphics = fancy, clouds = fancy, particles = All, etc.) and max render distance (32 chunks) ~60 FPS

The 144Hz 1080p display is pretty amazing despite not being able to max out graphics and play at 144 FPS. Text is clearer than ever and the AORUS Control Center has a "Blue Light Killer" setting which has practically eliminated any previous eye strain I has using an older laptop.

The M.2 SSD boots this laptop faster than I have ever seen a PC boot. The initial Windows setup takes a few minutes to get going when you power up the machine for the first time. After that, restarts and cold boots are near instantaneous.

The 512GB SSD leaves plenty of room for Windows to operate speedily and for other launcher games like World of Tanks and War Thunder.

The 2TB 7200 RPM platter HDD gives you enough storage for a good sized Steam library. I have close to 200 Steam and GOG games installed and have only filled the HDD half way. Load times are still bearable on games like DOOM 2016 and Total War: Rome II.

The AORUS Control Center makes updating chipset drivers and flashing the BIOS completely painless.

Dual fans with 2 intakes and 2 exhausts keep the laptop at a stable temperature. I have attached a SpeedFan screenshot of the temperatures under load while gaming.

Not Chromebook light but, lighter than expected for the power and storage capacity it has.

Power cable is long. I didn't measure exactly but, approximately 10-12ft. That and it only requires one power brick, I was looking at other models that had two and was not looking forward to that possibility.

Cons:

For the price, I would have liked to have received Windows 10 Professional instead of Home.

*Obligatory "Battery Life" complaint* the battery does drain pretty quickly even in power saver mode, expect 2 hours of life in that mode.

Other thoughts:

When you first setup the laptop, go the AORUS Control Center. Use the Smart Update feature under the Smart Utilities tab to update the BIOS and the control center itself. The control center update supposedly helps with the fan noise under load. The BIOS update should fix the only issue I had with the laptop, When I would wake the laptop up from sleep, the fans would not spin up when I started a game and I would get terrible framerates. I would have to restart to resume normal performance. I have not had this issue since I updated the BIOS. The BIOS update was completely automated after being started by the user, on reboot it flashed the BIOS without any further input from the user and proceeded to boot normally after.

Fans are only obnoxiously loud in "Max Fan" mode which you have to select manually. They are no louder than my desktop when set to "auto" and under load.

Exterior does like fingerprints.

I would highly recommend this AORUS 15-X9-RT4BD to anyone that needs a g-solid mobile gaming platform.

title: Good For What They Are - Ergonomically Well Designed
text:
These are fine for what they do well, but don't expect too much from these either.

Pros:

1) Louder and clearer than the built-in speakers to the monitor.
2) Attractive
3) Good, clear midrange to top end at low to medium sound levels.
4) Well designed and located, and easy to use volume control

Cons:

1) The big one is that at volume levels louder than medium, the sound gets congested and distorts. Perhaps as the drivers break-in, this aspect might get better (and drivers' suspensions do break-in and get more flexible).
2) Even though there is sort of a bass port on the bottom, fuggedaboutit da bass. Perhaps if you were to put these right against the wall for bass reinforcement, you might get a hair more response, but these essentially have none. These speakers are not for listening to music at satisfying sound levels. These will be fine for watching YouTube videos, watching interviews, etc, things that will be helped with having speakers with greater clarity in the midrange and top end.

But anyone who is looking for a pair of speakers that is going to sound very good and will be satisfying when listening to music, there will be far better options than these.

So in summing up, they lack any real bass response. In some ways, that's better than huge, sloppy, gloppy bass. But they're not even giving you anything of substance. They're not even pretending to provide it. It's just not there. But they're not tinny sounding speakers, either. They're very good for the human voice and for general purpose. I got them for my 91 year old father-in-law who needed speakers that are capable of higher volume and clarity. These are quite good for that purpose. They're attractive, too.

Regarding the USB connection, it's the USB that is providing power. More powerful speakers would need to be plugged into a power outlet on a power strip or to the wall. These, requiring a more modest amount of power, can get powered via the computer's USB. Sound gets plugged into the speaker port, as pretty much most speakers will.

text:
I was on a search for true wireless ear buds that were waterproof and could handle being used in the shower. After trying a couple different brands and realizing their faults, which I'll explain shortly, I found these bad boys which cover all the bases for using in the shower.
First off, one of the issues with my first purchase was that the controls were very limited. No volume control or forward/backward capabilities for music, ect.

I tested this in cold water and the same thing occurred so I came to the conclusion that I needed to find IPX8 TWS ear buds that had both physical buttons for control so I wouldn't have to worry about the water making the ear buds go crazy, and a wide variety of abilities like controlling volume, play/pause, forward/backward, ect.
Low and behold, these guys. They are not just IPX8, but IP68 so they have been tested to be both completely dust proof and waterproof over 1m underwater. They have great battery life, wireless range due to the bluetooth 5.0 technology, charging time because of the USB-C tech, and obviously, full audio controls/physical buttons so I can have complete control over my music and can take a shower with them on and not have to worry about water causing any unwanted commands.

GREAT BUDS, WOULD BUY AGAIN.

title: Easy-Peasy install
text:
Had ZERO difficulties getting it up and running and then connecting my devices to it. Didn't have to change any passwords, wasn't hard to do. Not sure why people are experiencing difficulties. I'm a 70-yr-old woman, and it installed easily by myself. I didn't do anything special.

Note: After getting it up and running (just plug it in, turn it on, and then press the Wifi button or whatever it is), you will want to scan for alternative wifi sources when you try to use your existing devices, and choose the one that has a suffix of "_EXT". Then click to connect, and Presto, I was connected. ** I should add that I had to press the scan button on the Netgear router I've always had. Regardless, you do that everytime you want to add any device, so this is normal. Just regard the extender as another device on the router, but you don't have to add a password to connect the extender to the router.

The speed was just a trifle slower than the main router source, but then I can't ever connect at the far end of my house to the main router, so it's irrelevant that connecting directly to the router provides faster service. There's no service at all at the far end of the house unless I connect through this extender.

Works beautifully! Now I can watch Netflix and Roku stuff in my far-away bedroom. What a delight!

title: This IS the droid you’re looking for!
text:
Let’s be honest, a portable/foldable Bluetooth keyboard is not a piece of gear that everyone needs in their day to day life but the fact that you are here checking out this product and reading these reviews tells me that you are likely one of those people!

So, who needs a device like this? I think the easiest way to explain that is just to tell you why I purchased one, and it is very simply for typing on my iOS devices. When I travel I seldom bring a proper laptop unless it is 100% necessary, so that leaves me with my iPad Pro which I love to travel with. Let’s face it, 99% of the trip I am utilizing my device as a consumption device and it’s only during the actual meetings that I am using the device for creation/presentation purposes. It is because of this that I no longer utilize one of the bulky keyboard case options that I have tried in the past, aka Logitech, Brydge, or Apple’s Smart Keyboard... I just don’t need the keyboard on all the time... might as well use the laptop if that’s the case...

So for me I use a slim, yet protective case made by Zugu which keeps my iPad protected and allows me to prop it up to watch movies on my long flights because at that moment I am in 100% consumption mode. Then, if I need to draft some pre-meeting notes on the fight, or finalize a report once I get to my destination, I pull out this awesome foldable keyboard by iClever and *BAM* I am now typing away as effectively as I am on any laptop.

“But what about the iOS keyboard?” Yes IOS has an on-screen keyboard... but apart from some brief notes, I HATE the tactile-less experience of typing on a glass screen. Maybe I am old fashioned but there is just something about the feel of the key press that just gives me a better all-around typing experience and that absolutely translates to a better end product for me.

So what do I like about this keyboard... Well first of all let’s be clear that iClever has two versions of this keyboard for sale and this is the larger of the two, model number IC-BK05, (IC-BK03 being the smaller). What isn’t there to like?! For me the build quality is top notch. Compact fold is a great feature but if the device is cheaply made then it doesn’t really matter how compact it is if it’s just going to fall apart on you. In my experience typing on this keyboard I have had no indications that this device will fall apart unless it’s due to my own miss-treatment. So build quality and compactness were paramount for me but one thing I did not consider, but I now throughly appreciate, is a solid Bluetooth connection. This thing connects lightning fast on the initial set up and after that it remains paired with the device until you put the keyboard to sleep, which, cleverly enough, is done just by folding the device up... and to turn it on - you guessed it, unfold it! The Bluetooth connection is rock solid and I have yet to drop the signal when utilizing it within a reasonable distance. What is reasonable you might ask... it’s a keyboard folks... most of us will be using this within 6 inches of the device it’s pair to but I also tried pairing this to my home entertainment system and for me it works from the couch, which is about 10’ from the receiver, and that’s without any drop in signal... Haven’t tried it any further because I realistically would never use it any further than that.

The tactile feel of the keys is every bit as good as the keyboard on my MacBook Pro, pre-butterfly keys, and I opted for the “larger” version of this device and I am very pleased with my decision. It is every bit as portable as the smaller version yet my hands experience less fatigue because the keyboard is the same size as a laptop keyboard.

The backlit keys are really useful and the option to chose between three color, blue, green, and red is a nice extra! While I think the blue looks the coolest, I tend to keep it on the green as it is the brightest of the three colors and I find it the most usable in the conditions were I use the backlit keys.

Finally we come to battery life, and yea, it’s pretty darn good! The manufacture claims 10 day battery life if used 8 hours a day and that’s really amazing. First of all you would never type on this for 8 solid hours a day for 10 days straight but those are pretty solid numbers. They claim that this equates to 90 days of normal use and that works for me! Standby time comes in at a comically good 218 days and, on yea, it charges in 2-3 hours! I have not actually timed how long the batter lasts but if it is even close to what they claim then we will be just fine. I will obviously update this review if I find the battery claims to be significantly off.

All in all I am VERY pleased with this purchase and I offer my FULL recommendations to those who are considering a device such as this. This will be my new “go-to” configuration until further notice!

title: Good economical 2nd monitor, shipped fast!
text:
I have owned other HP monitors and while this one is on the lower end of the quality and feature spectrum, it
is perfectly fine as a 2nd monitor. I am using it next to an older HP w2408h which is also a 24" monitor but has a different aspect ratio so I just had to to tweak my display settings in Windows 10 so things didn't change size dramatically when I move something from one screen to the other. Usually if you are going to use two screens, you get 2 of the same model. However, I was abruptly tossed into working at home so I didn't want to spend the money for two new monitors especially when my older HP was working fine and looks a bit better.

As far as features go, this is a basic HP model. It's got adjustments for brightness/contrast, color and few other things, but no physical adjustments for height, only tilt. I stuck a hardcover novel under it to raise to the height of my existing monitor. Color-wise, it appears a little washed out compared to my older HP monitor. Even after adjusting the saturation all the way for RGB, my older monitor still beats it. This new monitor does provide crisper text and graphics so that is a plus (my older HP is 8 years old)

It did come with a VGA cable which I swapped out for a DVI cable because my other monitor was already using the VGA input.

The seller shipped this very quickly and I am grateful for that because trying to work with a single monitor when you are used to having 2 at the office is a killer for graphic design work.

title: Security Concerns!
text:
I rarely write reviews, but I wanted to share information that I wish I’d had before I made this purchase. Maybe I can save someone the aggravation and wasted time.

I bought this TP-Link AC1200 Gigabit Smart Wi-Fi router to replace a still functional, but aging, Netgear unit. My main goal was to upgrade to stronger, more modern encryption for enhanced security.

With the TP-Link router plugged-in, I opened a browser window and pasted-in the URL of the startup site. My browser refused to open it, flagging it as non-secure and high-risk. After several more attempts with the same result, I tried another browser.

The second browser flagged the site the same way, but it did eventually load the page. When the home page opened, it was, in fact, a non-secure website. This was even more concerning because my browser has an extension that creates a secure https connection with non-secure sites whenever possible (and what kind of credible company builds wi-fi routers but doesn’t have a secure website?).

I was able to establish a wi-fi connection with the TP-Link router but my Bitdefender anti-virus software flagged it as a non-secure connection. Needless to say, I had extreme misgivings about registering the device and creating an administrator password over a non-secure site and connection.

I eventually did both, and closed the window. Then I remembered that I had intended to set up visitor wi-fi access. When I attempted to load the website again, my browser refused, flagging the site as high-risk. The only way I could get back in was to press the Reset button on the router. This erased everything, and I had to start from scratch, then set up visitor wi-fi on the way out.

Out of curiosity, I tried to get back in via both browsers but with no success. Then I remembered that TP-Link offers a free app to control the router. I downloaded the app, but I couldn’t get the router to accept the password. I tried multiple times but was never able to connect.

I used the router for several days, and each time I turned-on my computer, my Bitdefender software flagged the wi-fi signal as non-secure.

The final straw came when I tried to print a document and discovered that my printer no longer worked. My printer offers four or five different ways to establish a wi-fi connection with a router. I tried all the applicable methods with no success.

Needless to say, I unplugged and boxed the TP-Link router and returned it to Amazon. They were good enough to take it back, as usual, and I expect a full refund in time.

By the way, I plugged-in my old Netgear router again, got a secure connection right away, and all my devices automatically reconnected, including my printer.

title: Amazing Service...Warp Speed Claim Payment!!!
text:
I bought the 4 year coverage 2 years ago for a 3 piece luggage set I needed. I was hesitant as most any other time I've bought long-term product protection, turned out I never needed it. But, I went ahead and got it.

Fast forward to two months ago. While not heavy use or overweight, I hit a huge opening in the sidewalk while wheeling the suitcase and, sadly, shredded and broke one of the wheels. I got the insurance info when I got home, went online and filed the claim, ready to go with pictures and everything.

The online claim filing was easy...asked a lot of important questions and when done, clicked submit. I quickly received a Claim number, etc email and was told it could take up to 72 hours to process and for any additional follow up.

title: Exceptionally good quality with some nice attention to detail
text:
[[VIDEOID:df5edc803e1a0a69c16394287afc2d53]] I have softboxes from about 5 different brands, and this is my new favorite for a few reasons.

1. Setup is easier than others. The rods pop into place with very little effort, but the box is still plenty strong once they are all in place. Some softbox rods are super rigid and hurt to put together. Not this one.

2. The diffusion is really great. The internal baffle has a double thick center piece so you won't have any hotspots. Some softboxes do not have this, and cheap ones don't include an internal baffle at all sometimes.

3. It comes with a grid. A lot of softboxes don't include this

4. The velcro flaps on the back of the softbox ACTUALLY FIT. I have so many softboxes where the flaps are a tiny bit too small and leaves gaps on the back so light spills out. These fit very nicely without having to use a lot of force.

5. It's very lightweight. This is by far the lightest 36" softbox I own. Super easy to put on and take off without feeling like it's going to snag or fall and break a light.

6. It comes with a great case. I'm a sucker for cases, and this one is nicely made and branded for easy recognition.

It has many sides, so the shape of the front face is very round, which is great for catchlights.

I would not hesitate to buy this again or recommend it to anyone. Very happy with this purchase.
