title: Major design flaw- drains battery while in charger
text:
[[VIDEOID:643941e6d721df978307d44025e7e221]] Edit: I returned the first one and my second pair is having the same problem. This is clearly a major design flaw in which: 1) they don't seat in the charger properly and 2) they may still be running when in the charger.

As this is my second pair I'm paying close attention to the battery. Yesterday evening I listened to Audible for 30 minutes (on full charge) with just the right earbud when I went to the store quickly just for stamps, leaving the left bud home in the case. When I got home, I put the right bud back in the case, closed it, and left it for the night. In the morning, I opened the case to listen to a podcast. I popped in the right earbud and got the battery drained be-doop-doooo sound. Looking at the iPhone widget, sure enough, the right one DRAINED FULLY WHILE SITTING IN THE CHARGER overnight and the left one drained about 2/3 of the way despite not even having been used. (see photo- right one dead and no "lightning bolt" indicating charging)

Maybe I'm spending more time than is warranted to troubleshoot, but my best guess is that it's running while in the charger. Also I note that unlike my AirPods, sometimes it says on my apple watch "phone call" when running audio apps- these things, despite being apple devices, may bot be programmed right. Looks like sometimes they may treat apps as phone calls and not hang up properly when I'm done using them? Could explain the dead batteries. Either way, I'll be returning these. I just want headphones that work,

Original pair review:
These are great headphones, when they work. My issue is battery drain and ineffective charging. I use these for running, 45 minutes to an hour tops, and give them a wipe and promptly return to the charging case. Usually well within the advertised battery life. Sometimes I listen to audible on my couch with just the right ear bud in, and again, return it to the case after no more than an hour of two of use.

Yet oddly, I typically find the left earbud battery fully drained. Is it running when I’m only using one ear bud? And not even that earbud!

More problematic however is the charging adapter. I have to set them in the case just right and poke them about until I hear the click of the magnetic pins- otherwise they look like they are charging but really are just sitting in the case. Lately I’ve taken to using my iPhone widgets to monitor both earbuds’ status when placing in the case, taking extra care to make sure the lightning bolt shows up indicating charging.

Another problem is that when you close the lid, it pushes the ear buds. Now I’ve noticed that the act of closing the charger lid moves the left earbud off the charging connection while the right one continues.

This is a shame because otherwise I like the headphones. They have good sound, block ambient noise, and fit nicely. Just the charging case is garbage. Do yourself a favor and either avoid these until they get a better case, or just be extra careful to monitor charging status and location so they don’t get bumped and disconnected from the charger.

I really wanted to like this monitor, but after some time of using it (bought early 2019) I just can’t recommend it.

The body is made of metal which is a good marketing tactic to make you think it’s built solid, but when you hold the monitor you can tell it’s flimsy and isn’t as stable as you would think. After a week I lost one of the small screws that was in the back. It shouldn’t have fallen out in the first place.

The ports are misaligned with the edges so it’s difficult to plug in the power cable or other cables without jimmying it in.

That being said, it constantly flashes when in operation and no cables are loose. I’ve adjusted my computer video settings and it still flashes.

I do like the stand which is adjustable and fairly solid. This is the only nice thing that came with the monitor.

I’ve really tried to like this monitor and support smaller/newer businesses but this is just not a good monitor. It’s not worth over $100 imo.

EDIT:
As of now, in 2021 this monitor has started to die. The screen is fading and the edges are whiting out. This monitor hasn’t moved from its spot during the pandemic and has been used every day, so this WILL NOT LAST. Get a monitor from a proper and reputable company.

title: Jack of All Trade, Master of None
text:
Overall I enjoy this monitor and am happy with my purchase. I use this monitor for three main purposes, my Xbox One S gaming monitor, my vertically oriented monitor for productivity purposes, and since my office is also in my bedroom, as a movie screen at night. This monitor is serviceable for all three tasks, however it is not exceptional at any of them.

The HDR effect is underwhelming, even with extensive calibration. When displaying HDR sources, the screen appears to have a faint white film over the image. In my opinion, the color back is actually deeper when not in HDR mode. As others have mentioned I think this is due to peak brightness being low cause it's a a computer monitor, not a television. However, it works as an almost too small television stand in from about 15 feet away.

I have my XBOX One S plugged in via HDMI, and the display works in 4k, and switches between HDR and non-HDR sources correctly (with a short moment of blackout, which is standard in my experiences). When I compare the HDR calibration screens on my XBOX between this an and my low to mid-range 4k HDR TV, the TV has a much more dramatic HDR effect. Technically this monitor supports HDR, but it's an underwhelming effect, if you can notice it at all.

However, I've had issues with HDR when using my computer that had a noticeable effect, but not in a good way. I have my 2020 MBP plugged in via display port and I don't have HDR enabled on my MAC. But the monitor has a tendency to treat the signal like an HDR input, resulting in a hideously over-saturated image. In order to resolve it, I have to toggle the HDR setting in my OS on and off several times and then seemingly at random the monitor figures it out. Slightly annoying, but manageable, and all firmware and drivers are updated.

Overall, I'm not dissatisfied with this monitor, but I'm not blown away either. I still give it 4 stars because of the features it offers with consideration for the price point. But gamers looking for a monitor at this price range should considering sacrificing 4k and HDR for a monitor with a higher frame rate. I don't think the display is accurate enough to be used for intense graphic design, especially if you're wanting to work with HDR format videos. You're not going to be blowing away by the deep black colors or the details within the brightness that HDR is supposed to bring. But if you want a versatile display that can do all of those tasks at a serviceable level, this monitor could be for you.

title: For those confused about the addressing, please read below!!
text:
First off, it's a great little OLED and has worked perfectly for me! I've noticed a lot of reviews are saying the addresses are incorrect/misleading, which, in my opinion, is just due to a lack of understanding for the I2C Protocol.

I2C uses 7-bit addressing (values 0x00-0x7F), but in order to find the proper address, you take the address shown (0x78 or 0x7A), convert it to binary (01111000 or 01111010), remove the least-significant bit (the one on the far right, giving 0111100 or 0111101), and convert it back to hex (0x3C or 0x3D).

If you're using an arduino then most libraries will handle this conversion for you since 0x3C tends to be a default address, so you shouldn't have to worry too much.

title: Great for those with hearing problems.
text: Sony WS1 Immersive Wearable Speaker is an amazing concept! I've had a hearing loss since childhood. It's not bad enough to warrant a hearing aid, but it does interfere with my day to day life at times. I have a partial tone loss, meaning I miss certain levels of sound. I have a few reality type TV shows that I enjoy watching from time to time. Those shows, I've noticed, I have to either turn my TV up to very high level, which is unfair to others in the household, or as I usually do, I just miss parts of what is being said, or key background sounds. Until NOW. First of all, these are surprisingly comfortable to wear. They rest comfortably around my neck, or you can place them nearby on a side table. They have a raised volume control, that allows me to easily raise or lower the volume as needed. They also have a very cool vibration feature that immerses me into the action. They are fun to wear while gaming too. I can feel the vibration, but it's not overwhelming or annoying, it just adds to the excitement. I was impressed as I unboxed these stylish speakers. The first thing I did was to charge them on the included charging base as the detailed instructions mentioned. Next, I read the instructions and connected the receiver. I discovered that the TV in my living room could not connect to them unless I disabled the built-in TV speakers, which would make other people unable to watch TV along with me. At first, I was disappointed. Then I realized that I like to watch most of those shows in bed at night any way, and decided to try that TV and it worked immediately! And it worked GREAT! For me, it was like really hearing TV sounds for the first time! I could hear everything I had been missing, and others got to hear all along. I felt jubilant.. That's the only word that comes close to expressing the emotion that I felt. The Sony WS1 Immersive Wearable Speaker does not interfere at all with my hubby's listening pleasure. Since it doesn't cover my ears, I didn't lose the ability to also hear normal sounds and talking around me and carry on normal conversations with my surroundings. As I previously mentioned, the speaker itself is lightweight at approx. 11.82 oz. It's an easy and convenient wireless connection to your (compatible) TV. Also, you can connect two devices simultaneously. It comes with hard wires to also directly connect to my laptop and tablet, and... Wait, there's more.. It connects to my cellphone!! Now I can finally hear those social media videos!

I have limited space by my TV, and placing my wired subwoofer under the TV looked ridiculous. I have tons of space behind my couch and in the corner of my room, but my walls are pretty bare, so running a cable would've also looked ridiculous.

With the price of $100 though, I figured I'd try the cheaper option on Amazon first, which was another brand named Nyrius, and the receivers/transmitters had large square antennas. When I tried that one, it almost had me second guessing the wireless option, since it worked so poorly. There was static and constant popping.

So I returned that one and bought this BIC wireless setup, and I was blown away by the difference. This setup works flawlessly with no static at all, the sub sounds just like it was wired in, no noise at all. So I guess lesson learned, the extra money spent for this setup was worth it, since it works flawlessly, as advertised.

As a side note, my wireless router (which has 2.4 and 5Ghz bands) is right next to the TV, and doesn't hinder the BIC transmitter at all.

title: Some things you should know about recording vinyl records
text: Overall, this is a pretty nice self contained unit. I;m not much of an audiophile so it sounds just fine for me. I bought it primarily to transfer my records to my hard drive and the cloud. I'm also a novice at this task. The USB drive will continue recording until you stop it. This means that the only way that you can separate songs (you could, I guess, do that later with software), is to start and stop the recording between each song. I'm not going to do that so I record a record side as one song. Now comes the fun part. My computer is set to load songs to iTunes but I want songs to end up on Google Play. The turntable records the files as MP3. Now, I could be doing something totally wrong but, my iTunes takes an MP3 and it is heavily garbled. Oddly, it sounds fine in Google with Google Music Manager automatically copies it from iTunes to Google. In order to do that I also had to figure out a way to provide some attributes to the file (album title, artist, etc.). This is way out of my background but I found a free program called Audacity that allowed me to do that. However, I still have the MP3 issue in iTunes. Seems iTunes likes MP4 (AAC) and Google is fine with that format. I had to get a free add-on for Audacity to save in that format. Go to Audacity, open the MP3 file from your USB drive, give it a name , export (save as) a MP3 and then choose the MP4 (AAC), and add the file attributes, open and load to iTunes, copy to Google, and you are golden. Took me two days to figure this out so hope it helps someone:)

title: Perfect soundbar for LG TV, no auto shut-off and clear dialogue
text: I bought this soundbar and the equivalent Samsung so I could compare them in person before making a decision.  I wanted a soundbar that would work best with my LG TV and would improve my ability to hear dialogue in movies and auto control volume level at night so I wasn't constantly riding the volume button. But most importantly, I wanted a sound bar that would not turn itself off if I left it paused for a long time.  Apparently that is a very hard feature to find.  Using HDMI ARC, I was able to pause a Disney + movie for over 45 minutes and it never shut off. I just pressed play and it kept on going.  The Samsung, like every other soundbar I've ever seen, shuts off after 20 minutes or so, forcing you to have to find the soundbar remote to turn it back on.  Another good feature of the LG, is that I can adjust the volume of the center channel separately, since most dialogue is kept on the center channel.  This is one of the biggest benefits of getting a 3.1 soundbar over the internal TV speakers.  TVs and even 2.1 sound bars often have to down mix the 5.1 channels and in the process the dialog gets muddy.  Combined with the high dynamic range of Dolby Digital codecs, this is why movies can be so hard to hear especially when you're trying to listen in a quiet setting without waking up the kids.  Get this soundbar, it solves all of those problems.  Of course, I can only speak for folks with newer LG TVs with HDMI ARC port.  It's possible that there's something special happening to allow the two LG products to talk to each other that keeps them from shutting off.  I've read that the Samsung has better audio quality, but I can't imagine your average person would tell the difference.  Personally, I found the sound of the LG to be brighter which actually helps with intelligibility.  The Samsung did seem to have a slightly larger subwoofer driver in it, but I'm not trying to shake the house down.  Convenience is king, go with the LG.

title: Great PC For The Price
text:
My 8 year old or so Dell XPS 8700 was starting to give me a lot of headaches, and I knew the time was coming. The hardware didn't like Windows 10 updates anymore, could hardly make a backup of my 2 TB drive without crashing. Me and PC's go way back.. to Leading Edge (remember them?) and before that, the Sinclair around 1980/81 which wasn't really a PC. Built two PC's from scratch, and also owned several Dells in my life, too. Top quality for commercial product. But never owned an HP. For a while there, HP produced a low quality product.

Shopping around for an All-in-One, I looked at Dell, HP, and a few others. And for the price and the fact that it came with a DVD burner built in where others required external USB drive, I took a chance. And I'm happy I did. Only had this up and running for under 2 weeks, but I am definitely happy with the purchase.

The Good:

Well, I configured this 24" with a 2TB HDD and a 256 GB SSD, and 16 MB of RAM putting the price around $1,130.00 Well worth the few extra bucks. I was tempted to get the 512 GB SSD, but stuck with the 256 GB. Good enough, since I keep most files and programs on the HDD and really just boot Windoze from the SSD for fast starts. And they are fast.

The touchscreen is nice and very responsive. But, I rarely use it. Old school, I guess, and really the iPad and iPhone need touchscreen more than a desktop. Sits very nice on my office desk at home, and at first I thought the white color of the keyboard and mouse would bother me. But they don't.

And, HP has definitely improved it's quality from years ago. Not bad. Not quite up to a Dell, but close. I do like their online support, which is in some cases better than Dell. That was one thing I was worried about, but I am no more!

The Not So Good:

I read some reviews from folks that talk about a "hum", which is obviously one of the cooling fans. It's there. Mine is very minor and only when things are quiet do I notice it. I think the annoying thing about it is the "in and out" sound it makes.. like "HMMM hmm HMMM hmm, etc. But again, it's really not that noticeable.

Another disappointment is that I could only buy it in the i5 8440T CPU, and would have preferred the i7. Reason being that I do some heavy duty engineering that is iterative or solving large matrices, and speed is important. But, again, it's still faster than my Dell XPS 8700 with an i7 processor, so all good there.

The biggest disappointment was with the built-in speakers. Not good. And, when Windows did an update, it actually kicked the max volume way down. I spent hours updating drivers, F'ing around with a zillion setting, etc., etc. Nothing worked. But even when the sound was louder, the built-in speakers sound like crap. So, I took my external speakers with an AC power supply, and plugged them into the headphones jack. Wow! Beautiful sound is back. I don't use headphones on a PC, so losing that jack input for headphone use is meaningless to me.

The keyboard and mouse are a little cheap. But, they work. I had gotten used to a mechanical, backlit keyboard that I bought for the Dell some time ago, but I can always go back to it. To be honest, I like the faux mechanical keyboards and the touch and key action on the HP supplied keyboard is nice. The mouse, optical, is built real cheap but works fine. Can always go back to the Logitech I was using with my Dell. Mouse and keyboard are wireless.

Finally, the last disappointment is with HP's placement of the USB, HDMI, ports on the back of the unit. And, only 4 USB ports total. There is a mini-USB port next to the Power On button on the bottom of the screen, but who uses that? I would sooner had another 3.0 or even 2.0 standard USB.

That's it! I know that I didn't write a lot about the positives. I tend to point out the bad things. But don't let that bother you. Like I said, for the $$ it's hard to beat this All-in-One and HP has definitely got themselves a winner with this Pavillions. :-)

title: Great modern motherboard!
text:
This is a fine example of how to do a mid level motherboard right. It's got all the gaming basics down cold, from a clean layout to the nice addition of lighting tweaks both for peripherals and the motherboard itself, to even including a really neat trick up it's sleeve in the BIOS. Read on:

This was very easy to work with, and my simple budget gaming rig I put together for my little cousin went together without a single issue. I added an AMD Athlon 200GE, which I overclocked to 3.9GHz thanks to MSI's inclusion of a multiplier in it's BIOS that allows this otherwise locked chip to get as high as 3.9GHz without crashing, nice. That's another 15-20% of free power thanks to this motherboard! Good one, MSI!

As for bells and whistle's...well there aren't too many, but that's not totally unexpected for the price. The graphics slot is reinforced with metal for the heavier video cards out there, the onboard audio is well done and sounds great, the addition of 4 ram slots allows for future upgrade-ability...it's just a well rounded motherboard for the money spent.

The Mystic onboard RGB controller is a nice touch allowing for a few different colors to light up your case with a simple but limited software interface to get it going. Overall, this motherboard feels sturdy and well thought out, making it an easy job to get up and going fast. The inclusion of BIOS that allows overclocking an otherwise non overclockable processor just makes this a killer deal. Recommended!

text:
The PoE Hat is pretty nice. It's small and solid state, unlike some of the competitors. It slides right on the Pi very easily. But there's one HUGE problem. It requires active cooling (a fan) and most cases that are any good (FLIRC and Argon One for example) don't have room for any HATs. So if you get this PoE Hat, make sure that you have a case that not only has a fan, but ALSO has room for the Hat. Every fan case I could find clashed with the HAT and wouldn't work together.

If anyone has a great and professional looking case that works, please say so in the comments. I don't want a see through case or any such madness.

title: Good value for under $100
text:
Anker has always been my go to brand for affordable and well made cables, headphones, battery banks and speakers. I own multiple speakers and headphones from Anker and have always been impressed with the sound quality. Anker was kind enough to send me a pair to try out and I have some mixed feelings.

To be fair, I'm not a huge fan of completely wireless headphones. One of the main reasons is the fear of losing one of the headphones if it happened to slip out while on a hike or run. These fit pretty well, but don't think they fit as snug as my pair of Soundcore Spirit X's that I use almost everyday. Those you have the added benefit of longer battery life in between charges, the adjustable behind the head strap, an over the ear clip to ensure your headphones stay put, a higher IPX rating and, in my opinion, better sound quality. Often felt like I got a much fuller sound with the Spirit X's.

Pairing these headphones to my phone also required me to look at the manual as, at least for me, they didn't immediately show up on my phone as being able to pair. The process to pair was a little unintuitive and confusing but once they are paired, you're good to go. They connected to my phone everytime I took them out of the charger case. The only disappointing feature is if you wanted to use only one earpiece for phone calls or whatever else, you must use the right earpiece. If you try to use the left one, the headphones do not connect. A minor nitpick but good to know.

SoundCore seems to be just missing the mark for me. The price is in a good spot, the headphones are convenient and small. You can slip the charging case into your pocket and not even realize it's there. You have ultimate freedom in terms of portability and clutter. However, for me, my listening habits required a longer battery life and my preference was towards a more full sound.

That's not to say these are a bad set of headphones, they are a good quality for $65 and for the most part seem like a good value. It more comes down to a matter of preference. If you want something that is completely wireless, has a decent sound, has the latest Bluetooth technology and is under $100, these aren't a bad buy. Just for me, there are other offerings, even from Sound core, that although aren't completely wireless, are a better buy for under $50. I'll be trying these out more to see if my mind is changed, but for now think my daily driver will still be my Spirit X's

title: A Real Android Tablet and More - Finally !
text: I'm not sure why Amazon isn't selling this device.  It's been available at Best Buy from the outset and now at Walmart. Other vendors as well.  For $299 for the 128 GB version, this Chromebook/Tablet  is an amazing deal and will be of great value to you if you understand the product and your use-case fits.  First of all, for a $20 or so difference, please don't go for the 64 GB version. The 64G version makes no sense (no SD card slot) with such a small price difference. For the 128 GB version, for $299, you get the tablet and the kickstand and the keyboard.  That is an amazing deal.  The tablet has an ARM processor but that is not something to be looked down upon.  Go ahead and install some Android apps which seem to play well with ARM.  Sure, there are occasional glitches in sizing and other issues if you install Apps from the Playstore, but mostly the experience is very satisfying. With only 4 GB's of RAM, the Duet works well if you don't extend it beyond it's limits.  Don't expect to keep dozens of Apps running at once but for the most typical use case this little guy will do just fine and even surprise you as to how well it performs. The real positives for this device  are the bright and beautiful screen and the premium build quality.  Nothing feels cheap about the product.  Everything looks really good.  With regard to the keyboard, there are reviews that say that the keyboard is "OK." Sure, it's OK for the device but what do you expect for a keyboard and  a 10 inch screen? Once you get used to the keyboard you  will find typing is very pleasurable with good key travel. That said, given its size you're just not going to get a full typing experience but if you need a keyboard to shoot-off a quick email or be productive  you got the keyboard and it's included in the price. Amazing.  Don't think you'll be able to use the Duet as your main computer but if you think of it as a stellar tablet with Chromebook functionality (which is getting better and better) your are going to be very happy with the purchase.  Bravo to Lenovo for disrupting the Android tablet market and giving Apple and  ios some competition - finally !

What is not to like...it is cheap, works as it should, and it is the best value when it comes to low-priced software defined radios. In my shack I have older multi mode transceivers, pre-SDR. Currently I use 2 RTL's protected by a MFJ 1708b TR switch. I use SDR Console software to give me a decent view of the band I'm operating on as well as received signals I may be interested in contacting. It is NOT a substitute for sophisticated transceivers such as a FlexRadio or an Apache, but this configuration works fine for me. In fact, this setup has spoiled me so much, I am not in any hurry to upgrade to a modern SDR transceiver.
A SDR is only as good as the software you use. Luckily there are many choices such as SDR Console (my favorite), HDSDR, SDR Sharp, and SDR Uno. I'm starting to like Uno but it has more features than I need but it is interesting.

While lifting up the speaker manually holding the mount, the 360-degree joint held still but the swivel arm kept turning downward (under the weight despite using a pass-through socket wrench and allen wrench to tighten the hell out of the nut) and the elbow joint held by the bolt/wing nut was bowing out in a very scary way so that the teeth not long interdigitated and looked like it was going to snap off.

text:
Update: Still unable to get any response from CyberPower "support". In the meantime, in addition to not kicking in when the power goes off as described below, the UPS now also fails to connect to my PC sometimes when it reboots. I.e., the UPS is getting worse. Bad products can happen sometimes, but bad support is not acceptable.

---

We had a late winter storm in Chicago two weeks ago, and power went off repeatedly. I purchased this UPS in February, and the UPS failed each and every time to keep my system running. At load I am only using about 20-25% of capacity, and the UPS software promises 20+ minutes of run time – this turned out to not even be 20 seconds.

This is my 3rd UPS, I’ve had two from APC before, and only heard about CyperPower recently and decided to give it a try. Having had previous UPS systems, I know what to expect from them and how they perform if they work properly.

I contacted CyberPower and documented the problem extensively. I went back and forth with support for a few e-mails. At some point they stopped communicating and haven’t responded to repeated attempts to contact them. Clearly the product is not working, and neither seems to be the support.

At this point the UPS functions as an overpriced extension cord, I certainly can’t depend on it, nor would I recommend this brand, or purchase another one.

Very disappointed that I put my trust in this company and its product.

title: Decent product at a reasonable price
text:
These are great for making controls for Do-It-Yourself handheld devices. The Teensy's Arduino libraries are demonstrated in examples spread out across the internet, and in the Arduino IDE's examples, but it's super easy to get a controller for Emulation Station on a SBC like Raspberry Pi. The examples illustrated on Teensy's website are also well documented and easy to follow, but do not entirely document concisely all the useful libraries available, such as "bounce.h."

I'm surprised that these aren't marketed more, as I don't often hear the DIY community praising Teensy MCU's, but they're really excellent for making controllers, since they have ability to be used as a USB device. 48mhz may not seem fast, but it's much faster than an Arduino Uno, and can get the job done while being energy efficient. I hear more about the Zionist/Jewish control over America and their pushing of communism, than I do about the cool controllers you can make with Teensy's brand of MCU's. I've bought 2 LC's and a 3.7, but I'll definitely be back for more should the need arise.

title: Unsuitable for daily use
text:
I care a lot about over-the-ear noise-cancelling headphones. I've owned many models from Bose over the last 20 years, as well as the Sony XM2 and XM3. I am disturbed by the Bose media blitz / social influencing campaign that is somehow netting largely positive reviews of the Bose 700s. They are *much* better than the Sony WH1000XM3s for phone call audio. Their noise cancelling abilities are similar enough. In every other way, they are SIGNIFICANTLY worse, to the point where I *only* use them for phone calls.

As you would expect from Bose, the software support is terrible. But it's worse than that: Bose has designed these so as to rely on a "primary" bluetooth device (your phone, most likely). So the software implementation affects usability greatly. One of the worst aspects is that the headphones will start to randomly "click" with static sometimes if the primary device, thinking it can power down its bluetooth antenna (since you're listening on another device), becomes intermittently connected. This leads to me power cycling the headphones ridiculously often. One of my major uses for noise-cancelling headphones is in ELIMINATING distractions, but these headphones provide their own distractions frequently. I hate them.

The other place where Bose is terrible is battery life and quick charging. Again, this presents another major source of distraction. Whereas my MX3 charge seems to last forever, I find myself often turning on the 700s to the annoying voice notice of a low battery warning.

[Edit: I changed my review to one star after a few months with the headphones, and observing that firmware and app updates do not fix the major problems. Bose is like Intel. They were entrenched as the only market leader for such a long time that they stopped innovating. When other companies started to produce premium quality noise-cancelling headphones, Bose had to suddenly catch up, but to do that after neglecting R&D for such a long time, they had to cut corners. One of the major corners they cut with these headphones is to offload as much as possible to a secondary processor--your device. While methods like buffering and variable-rate compression can smooth-over *audio* problems that arise from interference and connection fidelity, that level of latency poses major problems when it comes to control and maintenance of connections. Suddenly Bose has to work with at least three different operating systems, and they are very, very bad at software. Today I heard--on a loop--"Connected to Pixel 4 XL. Connected to Pixel 4 XL. Connected to Pixel 4 XL. Connected to Pixel 4 XL..." when I simply moved to an adjacent room. Maybe they're fine for a plane, where the setting is very stable. Everyone's flying these days, right?]

[Edit #2: Bose introduced a "turn off headphones if no motion for X minutes" feature. Except it doesn't work. The motion sensor is not sensitive enough to detect even moderate head movement. So if you use them at a desk or on, I don't know... an airplane, then the feature is useless.]

title: This Fixed my raspberry pi 3 low voltage warning...
text:
The raspberry pi 3 supposedly needs a 5v 2.5 amp power supply. No matter what I plugged it into, it would give low voltage warnings. I even tried plugging it into my Tablet's 5.2v 3A plug and it still gave the error on occasion. When I used my usb tester on them, it was always under 5 volts so they wouldn't put out good current and voltage unless it was used on their own device.

I got the 5v 60 watt power supply and set it to 5.1 volts and I'm getting no errors. I tested the output voltage as I was expecting and it was still outputting 5.1 volts. I am currently powering a Raspberry pi 3B, an SKR 3D printer board (to keep the board in sleep and accepting a power on command when it's not on 24 volts, a MOSFET to control and dim the printer head lights via M355 command, and a power control relay to turn on and off the 120 volt going to the 24 volt power supply with M80 and M81 commands respectively. it's a bit overkill, but does the job well.

title: Worth the money
text:
[[VIDEOID:a886bb3da7e0e0665e46155a8bc8dbe3]] Update 4/16/21: it’s been almost a year since I’ve purchased these. I finally took the time to look up how to control the music with my earbuds. I normally just use my phone though. Anyways, my initial complaint about dropping music seems to transcend these. I recently was using a pair of Beats and they dropped the music in the same way these did. So maybe I just interrupt Bluetooth connection when my phone is in my pocket. Either way, I’m happy with these. They have been very good at keeping the other employees I work with at bay and saving me from needless social interaction.

I was fairly skeptical at first, but given the price point of these wireless earbuds, I decided to take a chance. Needless to say, I wasn’t disappointed. The case itself has a very sleek and simple design, with indicator lights by the charging bay to show the battery life of the case. The earbuds rest nicely in the case to charge, and there is no movement when shaken moderately. The three size choices for the earbuds are nice, although I didn’t need to change them as they fit perfectly. Obviously, the fit is snug and secure. I bought these to work out in and simulated such with my movements for testing purposes. Once again, no movement. The sound is awesome. Even without any noise coming through the speakers I could hear very little of the world around me. I didn’t have to turn them up very loud either for them to be impressive. Connecting them is impossibly simple, and they reconnect automatically every time you pull them out of the case, provided they are on and the Bluetooth on your other device is turned on as well. The battery life I have yet to test, but given how outstanding they have been already, I’m sure I won’t be disappointed. All in all, I’m very satisfied to decided to buy these.

Update: It’s been almost a month since I purchased these and even though I don’t use them very often I have yet to need to charge the case. I pretty much use them when I need to count inventory at work. I have noticed a few things that seem a little glitchy but I’m not sure if that’s truly the case or not. First, when out doing yard work one day they kept disconnecting as if they were far from my phone even when my phone was in my back pocket. I noticed it happened whenever I bent over so I’m really confused as to the cause. No biggie. I removed my phone from my back pocket and set it on my deck and didn’t have any issues after that. Today I’ve been wearing them around work and several times they’ve just randomly disconnected, including the automated voice letting me know they disconnected and repaired with my phone. Again, I have no idea what is causing this but it’s only slightly inconvenient for me I suppose. I’ve noticed also that the button on the earbuds themselves seems to have a problem working as it doesn’t always play when I press it. But it always pauses. Again. Only a minor inconvenience for me. Still at the price point I can’t complain.

title: Best in class security built into a tank!
text: I started my 2FA journey with Authy. Authy is just like the Google Authenticator, but not tied to one device. It worked well until they stopped supporting Chrome. No problem, I have the desktop app too. Or, I did... They stopped supporting Linux too. With Google constantly changing how their browser works and breaking extensions I decided to switch to Firefox. And with Authy breaking everything else, it was time to change. I tried MYKI but had difficulty syncing. Their Linux desktop app also began giving me problems. I've heard nothing but praise for Yubikey, so I took the plunge. It turns out, while not all sites support it directly, they have an app just like Authy and Google as well. Virtually any site that supports 2FA will work with the Yubio Authenticator. Yubico uses open source for its authenticator app, I like that! They have a Linux Desktop app, a requirement for me. But what really sets Yubico Authenticator apart from the competition is the Yubikey. It's a hardware lock for the authenticator app. Sure, all authenticators have a password lock. But if someone gets or guesses your password, they're in. With Yubico you must have the key and you must touch it to receive the TOTP code. Each touch of the key generates a seemingly random 32 character key. It adds a couple of additional layers of security. And that's only one protocol. For sites that officially support Yubikeys, you get an extra layer of protection.  Yubico supports just about every currently known protocol. As an added bonus, Yubico says that in the 11 years they've been in business, they have never had a security breach with sites where the customer has utilized their products. That says a lot! Speaking of the hardware itself, this model is pretty indestructible. You could run over it with your car. Run it through the wash with the laundry. It can take it.

title: Close, but no cigars
text:
This is my 6th ASUS in the last 10 years so I guess that tells you that I am a fan.

When it comes to form factor and hardware configuration, I think ASUS Zenbooks provides the best value for money hands down.

That said, this model is ALMOST great, but falls slightly short. These are the reasons why:

1. Trackpad does not work smoothly and freezes from time to time. Not enough to affect usage, but enough to be somewhat annoying. 2 and 3 finger gestures also not as reliable (works 85% of the time) as previous models I have owned. I use a BT mouse so it does not affect me as much personally, but still...

2. Battery life is not as good as advertised. I would say around 6-8 hours of non-heavy use (browser, MS Office plus 1-2 more programs running at the same time).

3. Fan seems to keep spinning on and off for no apparent reason, without changing/opening additional programs. Not audible during the day but at night when I am working on the bed, this can be quite annoying.

4. In previous models, the LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN keys double as HOME/END/PG UP/PG DOWN keys with the FN key. These worked great when using keystrokes for browsing/navigation (like moving between tabs, going to top of the page) and when using Office products (like moving between Excel tabs, or going to the end of sentences/paragraphs in Word etc.). In this model, the same HOME/END/PG UP/PG DOWN keys are now moved to F9-F12. This makes no sense. I now have to move my fingers all the way to the top of the keyboard to reach them, which slows me down and defeats the purpose of using keystrokes to increase productivity. As a heavy user of spreadsheets and text editors, this really irked me.

ASUS - WHY CHANGE A GOOD THING??? Especially when the LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN keys ares not paired with any additional useful functions??? This is beyond stupid!

I believe most of the issues I mentioned can be fixed with a BIOS update. So ASUS, if you are reading this, PLEASE PUBLISH AN UPDATED BIOS AND FIX THESE PROBLEMS!!!

And if the BIOS update can bring the FN+ HOME/END/PG UP/PG DOWN back down to where they used to be (LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN ), that would be much appreciated.

title: A good sounding headphone becomes victim to over-hype.
text: I have owned 3 pairs of Audio Technica WS1100's and the reason is because they sound incredible for their price, and also because the headphone jack keeps shorting out. I have been looking for something comparable in sound quality, but with better build quality, and I thought these would be it. I have read numerous reviews about how the M-100 would "change how I listen to music forever" and "the headphones are built like a tank" neither of which are true. They certainly sound good, however comparing them to my WS1100's which are about half the price, these just don't sound as good. There is more bass, however it is muddy compared to the WS1100 and they are much darker. The sound stage is good with a nice separation, however the mids seem to get lost behind the inaccurate bass notes. ( so much for the dual drivers ) or whatever Z-Moda is calling them. As for the build quality, I didn't feel that they are cheaply made, but they certainly didn't feel "heavy and solid" or "built like a tank" as many reviews have claimed. In my opinion, these are a good portable headphone that would be more accurately priced at 100 to 120 dollars as opposed to the whopping 250 that these cost. If you are in the market for a good sounding bass enhanced headphone, go with the Audio Technica WS1100 for half the price. In my opinion, they beat these all day. And that is probably why people shouldn't over hype things. As for the comfort level, well that is another point of contention. These are definitely on-ear phones. Why market them as over ears? I suspect that the reason is because V-Moda is trying to make these headphones a do it all solution, and it doesn't work. resting the pads on my ears as opposed to trying to stuff them inside the small opening felt more comfortable. So to wrap things up, knowing what I know now that I have had these in hand, is that they are a nice compact, portable headphone that would compete well in the 100 ish price range, but since they have been over hyped and over priced, I just can't recommend them.

title: 5 stars but with a couple of observations.
text:
These are great sounding headphones, but they are not perfect. There are two things I think are worth mentioning about these:

1. You get both on-ear and over-ear pads on the box. By default, they have the on-ear ones. They are fixated by magnets so it's easy to swap between them. Now, the on-ear ones come by default and sound really bad. Absurd amount of bass. You can listen to mids and highs too, but the bass is always present, taking power over everything else. I believe these would be perfect for bass-heads. for me it's too much and I don't like it. However, when you change to over-ear, bass is way (a lot) more moderate. Not flat at all, but it is not omnipresent, making you enjoy your music. I love that they give you tons of detail, so you can listen to every instrument and voice. they are still a bit on the bass-heavy side, but it is not exaggerated and you can enjoy everything in your recordings.

2. Some reviews on the internet claim two things that are related: the magnets are weak for the bigger, over-ear pads and that over-ear pads sound bad. This is only partially true and I guess it comes from something that happened to me when I first tried the over-ear pads. See, the headphones have to small pin thingies and the pads have two small holes where those fit. The on ear pads are smaller and the magnets hold them firmly. Just place them close to the headphone and they will snap, making the pins fit the holes. With the over-ear pads, the magnets are not that strong so you may place them and have the pins not fitting in the holes. I didn't realize this and when I listened to the over-ear all the bass was lost, and they where terribly harsh to listen. Also, the pads fell off easily when manipulating the headphones. I was very dissappointed until I noticed the pins. I pushed gently on the pads to make both pins fit both holes, and then they are firmly held, no accidental falling off, and they come to sound as described on point 1. Take this into consideration when you swap to over-ear.

Finally, even when I give them 5 stars, I'd like to remark some cons:

I think they should have been engineered in a such a way that the sound didn't change so much when changing pads, or have the description state that the sound signature changes A LOT when swapping pads. It's just not a matter of isolation, they really are two different headphones if you compare both pads. Also for the magnet detail with the over-ear pads, IMHO they should just snap in place like the smaller pads do. And finally because all things considered, I think they are a bit expensive for their sound, even taking into consideration their build quality (which is very good). I'd probably give them 4.5 stars but Amazon just lets me give an integer amount of stars, so all in all, I give the 5.

title: For use with flat iron in Bali, Indonesia
text:
I am from the US and needed an adapter/converter to use on my trip to Bali, Indonesia and China. I purchased a dual voltage Conair 1600 watt compact hairdryer and it worked perfectly in the adapter slot of this product (when purchasing a dual voltage hair dryer make sure you turn the dial on the dryer to the higher voltage before you plug it in if you are in a country with 220-250 voltage!). I also purchased the Revlon Ultra Straight ceramic 1" flat iron. This is a basic flat iron with a high and low setting. I purchased this specifically because it DOES NOT have an auto shut off as my understanding after reading the instructions for this adapter/converter was that auto shut off products were NOT compatible with it. Because the flat iron is NOT dual voltage, I plugged this into the converter plug slot (this was my entire reason for purchasing this product as I needed the converter to convert this 120 volt product to the higher voltage in Bali, which is 240 as the flat iron is NOT dual voltage)....worked beautifully without any problem my entire trip!

I used this product in Bali using the plug adapter with the 2 round metal plug prongs and in China using the adapter part that corresponds to that country (make sure you research this ahead of time to know what type of electrical plugs are used in the country you are visiting!). I did not use the hair dryer or flat iron in China as those items were in my checked baggage and I was on layover in China so I cant speak for how those items would work in that country as I didn't use them there.

My best advice is to read the product instructions and info on Amazon thoroughly and carefully before you purchase! It tells you exactly what brands are compatible and what types of products you can and cannot use with this. Once you understand this, then you will know what you can use with it. I used these specific guidelines to drive my purchase of the hair dryer and flat iron I bought.

title: Great Device for Overseeing Your Property
text:
I purchased the Ring doorbell the end of July. The doorbell was easy to install on the outside of the house. A few screws, a few wires, and all set. I had a bit of difficulty setting it up the first time, but then my wifi gets interference when the a/c kicks in. I tried a second time without a/c interference and it was an easy process. I was able to connect it to my Alexa app easily too.

I set up notifications to go to my phone and Alexa for both doorbell and motion. This was also easily accomplished. However, my doorbell is higher than the recommended height (probably closer to 5 ft) and I was getting a lot of motion alerts. I was able to change settings for motion but still got lots of alerts, so I disabled the motion alerts. I have since ordered the "wedge" to see if that helps and will update my review to reflect that. (Update - After having purchased and installed the wedge kit, my motion alerts have decreased dramatically. Even though I've now expanded the range, the alerts are only a few each day (mailman, arrival of guests) and not every car that drives by as before. Therefore, I would recommend getting the wedge kit for those having stairs or close to a road.)

What I like about the system is that I am able to "see" my front door LIVE at any time. I like being able to know who has come and gone during the day. It was fun being out with friends and knowing a package I was expecting had been delivered that day. I am considering possibly getting something for the back of my house as well. I also like the alerts that come from the neighborhood link on the app. This allows me to hear about happenings as local or a far away as I feel the need.

The doorbell came with 30 days of free "Ring Protect Plan". Right now, it is fun to have a history of every visit to my front property, but there is a lot of recordings of the mailman that I don't think I need to pay the monthly fee to see. I have not made a decision as to whether I will continue with that part of the service. As the month moves along, I'll decide which way I lean.

Overall, I am pleased with the device. It does what it is intended to do. It alerts me to doorbell rings and motion on my front property.

title: I didn't use my other Kindle, I love this one.
text:
I didn't like the original kindles quite as much as having a book in hand, but these I like more.

Bigger is better - The size is big enough where I feel like I'm actually getting into the book before I have to turn the page, which is something I like.

Buttons - I like turning the page with the buttons, and having the option of disabling the screen so I can hold it while I read.

One handed - The battery pack is along the right side of the device giving your hand purchase and feeling comfortable to hold with one hand. This does get covered up with a case.

Lights - More lights does making it easier to read in low light.

Fonts - More fonts and sizes, I played around with different types on a few pages and found a combination that is just really pleasing for my eyes.

Look ups- You can lookup characters by name you don't remember and read previous passages about them without losing your place, in addition to the dictionary function.

On the downsides

Weigh me down - It is heavier, you will notice the difference if you're changing. I don't mind it but my mother has mentioned not liking it.

Tactile - It's slippery smooth. I like a secure grip, so I bought a leather case that was decently expensive.

Honestly, I wasn't much of a reader before I got this, and I find myself reading 3-4 times a week now up from pretty much nothing.

title: Great TV for the bedroom
text:
I bought this TV as an upgrade for a circa 2009 Samsung 32 inch LCD TV (720p) that still works fine and will be put in a guest bedroom. There have been advancements over the past decade. This TV has a brighter picture with noticeably better contrast, and has an easier to use OSD. It's "smart" features are welcome as I no longer need to have a gaming console connected to it to use online services like Prime Video or Netflix.

The only downsides is that the motion rate (it has a 60hz panel yet virtually all manufacturers for some reason greatly inflate the refresh number "rating") can lead to a less-than-cinematic experience. Fortunately you can easily turn it off. And because this TV has a 4k panel, and most content is 720p/1080i and then upscaled by the TV, you will get some artifacts, some of which are noticeable if you're relatively close to the screen.

Overall, it's a fine TV for the money. In addition to their cell phones, and SSD's, Samsung makes a good TV. For me it came down to this model or the higher end OLED model. In the end I went with the standard LED TV as I didn't feel the extra money was warranted on a secondary TV.

On a side note, this TV will connect to 5Ghz wireless signal. When I did the initial setup via my cell phone the TV automatically jumped onto the same wifi network as my phone, which was the 5Ghz network.

EDIT: It's now late May, 2021. The TV is about two years old and now exhibits severe ghosting when left on for more than 2 hours or thereabouts.(probably a heat issue) It does operate normally up until that point. It did some troubleshooting and the problem is definitely with the TV, not any of the sources (cable box, game console, etc.) The TV has the latest firmware, and has been factory reset twice, additionally I blew out the vents with compressed air. This is probably going to just get worse, so I'll be replacing this TV in a few weeks. The replacement will not be a Samsung.

I did reach out to Samsung and they just recommended the same troubleshooting steps I had already done. Since the TV is not under warranty. I would have to pay for the service call, diagnosis and repair, which would run into the hundreds, which on a TV that was ~$400 to begin with doesn't make much sense. This was a disappointment, but not a surprise. I get that this wasn't a high end TV, but I don't think that it's an unreasonable expectation for a TV to last for more than two years. As such, I'm revising my original rating to two stars.

I purchased this product to digitize old reel to reel tapes and LPs.

By the way: Audacity has detailed, easy to follow instructions on how to transfer vinyl and tape to digital and burn to CD. You can learn a lot about analog and digital just by reading the Audacity Manual.

title: A Bit Of A Disaster
text:
I wanted a 9H glass screen protector for my Garmin GPSMAP 66. This fits the bill. Price ($9.90 per 2-pack Amazon price at the time of this review) isn't unreasonable.

But they just don't adhere to the Garmin. I assume it's because the surface of the Garmin screens are of a type of plastic where this technique just doesn't work.

A shame, really, as the cut of the glass is absolutely perfect and it fits the Garmin's screen quite well. So as far as the product goes, well, not really good at all.

But there are works-around. One would be to use some sort of two-faced tape on the edges, but that is both overly-complicated and more than a bit messy (and permanent).

I got the glass to stay in place (we'll see if it works out long-term) by buying/using one of TUSITA's silicon covers (Amazon ASIN for the black edition: B07MV59FBH). The price of the cover ($10.90 Amazon price at the time of this review) is a bit rich (it's probably worth half that), but it does work to keep the screen protector (with its minimal adhesion) in place.

Whether the cover works long-term or not the review is for the screen protector standing on its own. Keeping that in mind...

2 stars.

title: Just an Expansion Card in a Static Bag. The Rest is Up to You!
text:
[[VIDEOID:fbee75690d8d90ec3f226d8955d25ecc]] Firewire and .avi's are long dead but the tapes live on. In drawers, closets, storage, etc. I wanted to transfer, upscale, and convert all of my old miniDV tapes to .mp4 without spending too much or borrowing a Mac. When I found this card for cheap I knew there was gonna be a little work involved.
First off, the card ships with no literature. At all. The necessity for the legacy Firewire driver for Windows 10 isn't mentioned anywhere in the description, just that it's compatible up to Windows 7. It's a cinch to find and get installed correctly once you know. See attached video for the complete process, install to .mp4, in 2 min.
The card has performed well for me, with no noticeable loss of quality in the .avi files that WinDV exports.
Premiere and some of the other high end editors can still capture and use .avi's, but I use Resolve these days and this is the only thing that I haven't been able to do with it.
Overall this card has saved me from loss of image quality from using the a\v out on the camera. Although Firewire only transfers the data in 1:1 time, it doesn't use any compression on the player or capture side. I didn't have to buy or install any huge applications, and the end results are well worth the effort of dealing with an obsolete and forgotten interface. Kinda cool that I'm set up to use my old Canon GL1 again for it's awesome lens, too.

title: Built Solid ASRock! Amazing choice for your Ryzen build!
text:
I was exceedingly pleased with the quality of this motherboard. It has more than met my expectations.

First of all, since this is the SLI/AMD Crossfire board, I will address that, since that was one of the reasons I chose this board, as I do use a multi-GPU setup. The two x16 slots are reinforced with steel which really helps secure the cards from drooping which is a really nice touch that they don't really touch on in the sales pitch. Moreover, I was really pleased with the results while using AMD Crossfire as it seems the performance scales better than it did on my old Gigabyte board.

The second reason I chose this board was more memory compatibility with my Teamgroup 3200Mhz CL14 RAM, and I was excited to see that the board posted into XMP 3200 Profile with no issues at all, and is now comfortably overclocked to 3466 MHz with CL 14 Timings. I was also able to overclock my Ryzen 5 2600 to 4.0 GHz with comfortable voltages with relative ease.

The only concern I had during setup was the first time I loaded the UEFI, it appeared frozen. However, after a simple Clear CMOS operation, the UEFI became responsive. So if you do buy this motherboard, I recommend you Clear the CMOS during setup. My only other minor concern was the M.2 heatsink was not fully secured on the motherboard, which scared me when I opened the package because I thought I had a broken heatsink, but it seems they did this intentionally for the end user to be able to find the M.2 Slot.

All in all, this board is a big improvement over my old FX-Series Gigabyte board, and I am exceptionally pleased!

title: Great choice!
text:
I've had these for about two weeks now. I use them for working out primarily, and also to help protect my ears while mowing/using the chainsaw. First, the sound quality. I like these very much. I read in other reviews that audiophiles may not like these. I don't know what an "audiophile" is, unless it's someone who thinks they are the authority of how something should sound. I've been around music my whole life. These headphones do really, really well with the sound. Whether it's Parliment, George Strait, or Queen, the music sounds like it's supposed to sound. As for noise cancelling, I've used better, but I'm not expecting total noise cancellation, just enough to not interfere with the music. These fit the bill fine. Lastly, they stay in my ears no matter what I'm doing. My workouts are an hour of high intensity interval training...I'm moving around a lot, and have never had them fall out. After my last workout I decided to grab a basketball and hit the court. I didn't play in a game, but I did practice some aggressive moves, drop steps, step backs, stop and pop, and only once did one fall out. In retrospect, I should have recognized that it was coming loose before I made the move I made. I popped it back in and finished my workout without any other issues.

All things considered, I'd have happily paid what I paid for the BeatsX that these replaced. Easily their equal in sound, and the true wireless nature of the Soundpeats make them an easy choice. Nothing but good to say about them.

title: 3MP, AC wifi, ONVIF, Saves to local NAS
text:
If you've done enough research on doorbell cameras by now you'll know that this is just the same OEM camera as many others, just with different branding. The others floating on Amazon, like EZVIZ, have the same specs, same design but may have some differences in the app and accessories used. I went with Hikvision because of their track record with higher end security cameras. Yes it's a Chinese company and yes they got hit with Trump's ban. The company has not had any data breaches (yet) and there is no reason to believe they have malicious intent (more on this below).

My checklist for a doorbell camera included >1080p resolution, no cloud saving behind a paywall (looking at you Nest), ONVIF compatibility, local saving to a NAS or NVR and AC wifi. This camera checked everything. Installation was easy, instructions were clear. Kept using my 16V Nutone mechanical chime (with a C905 transformer). I have a Synology NAS with surveillance station and it works without issue using the generic ONVIF profile. If you have trouble with Live View, switch the camera settings to "streaming" instead of RTSP.

The Hikvision app (apk file) needs to be side-loaded on Android right now due to Trump's ban. Note that you do have to create an account with Hikvision but from my research you have to create an account for any doorbell app from this OEM. Initial setup requires that you use the Hikvision app which I had no problems with. You should be able to use a 3rd party app from the Play store once this is done. All video and picture files that the camera takes are stored on the SD card. If you setup a NAS or NVR then it will be stored on those as well. I like having recordings in multiple places.

Resolution is good, no real complaints there. Keep in mind Amazon is compressing my attached photos. My only gripe is the frames-per-second. Live-viewing over my local network is great, 20+ fps at all times. Recordings on the other hand are only 10-15 fps and I do not see a way to change this. Right now I have it setup to record on motion detection to save space. My NAS allows for 24/7 recording but the camera itself does not from what I can tell. Codecs used are H264 for video and AAC LC for audio. I have a wifi access point about 17 feet from the camera going through a standard insulated, outside door and a glass/metal storm door. Reception hovers around -60dBm over AC. No problems with detection range yet, no false positives.

The camera does beep when people get close (and has been recording before the beep) to get their attention. You can turn this off in the app. Camera firmware is updated from the app. The app itself is pretty good, I currently see no reason to use one of the 3rd party apps but this is subjective. The two-way audio is good, if not a bit loud on the camera's end. I do not see a way to turn down the speaker volume in the app.

Overall I'm very pleased with this doorbell camera considering the ~$115 price. It's a one-time cost with nothing going to the cloud unless you configure that yourself with a NAS or NVR.

title: Ugly logo and some annoyances, but solid picture quality
text:
When I was shopping for a little photo frame, I was looking for three things: I did want the frames to be 4:3 rather than widescreen, I wanted decent picture quality, and I did NOT want the frame to have a visible logo. After all, when was the last time YOU put a photo of your family out on display with prominent company branding around it?

This frame succeeds at the first two, but completely flunks the third, which I wish I had noticed other reviewers commenting on. The MRQ brand logo is large and prominent in the bottom right corner, which is very disappointing, because NOT having that prominent branding was one of the reasons I chose this frame in the first place. I will find a way to cover it, but it's frustrating to have to, as no solution to this will look as good on display as it would if it simply didn't have the logo in the first place.

That said, the frame itself is functionally decent for the money. I can stand it next to our other frame (a larger nix frame, entirely without any such ugly branding) and the picture quality looks pretty good. However, it does have its share of annoyances.

Some of the transitions from picture to picture are clunky, slow, and ugly. They don't work properly on this little frame, and I wonder why they haven't been removed. But even more annoying is the enclosed remote, which only partially works. On the frame, the back/forward buttons skip through pictures -- but the corresponding buttons on the remote, marked with the same symbols, don't seem to do anything. Those would have been the buttons I'd use the most, so it's possibly the most major frustration I have.

Despite the annoyances, however, the strengths of this photo frame do outweigh its annoyances. It's a bargain for the money, but it's frustratingly close to having been a much better product than it ultimately is.

title: Using as boot drive for rPi4
text:
Really a nice drive, the metal case helps dissipate heat, but it barley get warm to the touch. It has 2 small blue led's that blink with activity (very small). I've tested against SanDisk Pro 500MB disk and this tested faster in every test. It not quite as fast as Samsung 500Mb or 1Tb drives, but within 5-10% on writes and 5% on reads. And it's much smaller and seems to be more durable. Tested on HP x360 with USB-C and USB-A connections; USB-C is faster but not by a huge about, especially random activity. in bursts USB-C is always faster.

But I primarily bought to try the new rPi USB boot for rPi4, after updating eeprom boot to version dated 2020-06-15; and it worked with no issues, now my rPi has no micro SDcard - VERY happy with it. Wanted smallest possibly drive, and this fits the bill, will buy 2 more and convert more rPi's to this faster more reliable drive. For the price (250mb & 500mb) this is the best priced/performance you can buy (the 1Tb could be a little less expensive).

title: Suited purpose- and then some.
text:
Windows 10 installation results:

As an OTR truck driver, finding a useful WiFi signal, even at a truck stop with paid "premium" extended WiFi access, is never a guarantee. Unless you're footing the bill for a Satellite ($600 just for the mobile SatTV antenna), plus monthly, etc. - we live by WiFi access for downtime entertainment.

During my last few overnight stops, I specifically scanned with my phone (a good WiFi gauge) for the "low" spots in the lot. After settling in, my laptop with built-in WiFi could barely see a connection, if it appeared at all with another truck rolling in front of me. Tire Shop buildings are always a good block to a signal. I knew my Roku box was going to be a complete failure on the WiFi front. (NOTE: This is *NOT* compatible with a Roku Box!!!)

I connected up my phone Hot Spot to the laptop then plugged in the new external WiFi setup. (I used the phone HotSpot so I could get the latest drivers without installing the entire included CD utility). The entire process took less than 1 minute. New drivers installed, phone hotspot disconnected.

Results: My subpar built-in laptop WiFi connection in this situation is now replaced with a completely usable WiFi connection. I was SURPRISED and it works quite well.

Pro: It works!

Con: short USB3.0 cable could be a bit longer!

title: Item Number is Misleading
text:
Update: Creative Car Audio was very helpful in ensuring I did get the product that I needed. There was a minor hiccup in shipping, but they were very accommodating with excellent communication; I would receive responses to my messages within an hour or two. I still highly recommend adding a note to the listing that the item number in the title does NOT refer to the subwoofer inside the enclosure and that the impedance in the title refers to the total impedance of the enclosure NOT the impedance of the voice coils on the subwoofer. If this were clear in the listing, it would have saved me about a week and a half of back and forth shipping to finally get the right product.

Original Review: The listing title states product number 46TL7T124. The Kicker website shows this to be a 12" L7 subwoofer with dual 4-ohm voice coils. Where this gets confusing is that it is IMPOSSIBLE for a 46TL7T124 subwoofer to be wired for 4-ohm impedance. Because the listing is not clear about whether the 4-ohm impedance describes the rating of the voice coils on the subwoofer (which is what part number 46TL7T124 would refer to) or the rating of the loaded enclosure, I placed my order based on the part number of the listing. I REQUIRED a 46TL7T124 subwoofer because my selected amp was chosen based on its 2-ohm output, which can be achieved with dual 4-ohm voice coils. Apparently, I should have done the exact opposite. Upon receiving the item, measuring the impedance across the terminals on the enclosure showed 4-ohms, which means what I was nervous about is true. The subwoofer inside this enclosure is NOT a 46TL7T124 it IS a 46TL7T122 which is the 2-ohm voice coil model. Why the "item number" of the subwoofer changes from 46TL7T122 to 46TL7T124 when you place it in a box is beyond me. The information that the 4-ohm value on the listing refers to the loaded enclosure and NOT the subwoofer itself should really be made clear in the listing and it is not.

title: Received a Defective (or deceptively manufactured) cable, not functioning as USB 3.0.  Fully tested
text:
UPDATE - Second cable (Replacement for defective cable): I just received a second JOTO cable and it failed to function as a USB 3.0... Shipped from North Texas Amazon Distribution center, I would assume all units coming out of this region are most likely defective.

NO NOT ORDER THIS CABLE FOR OCULUS LINK (Or for any products that absolutely require a 3.0 connection).

If you order this cable just know that you stand a high risk of receiving a defective rushed product. If you have no means of testing this product through benchmarking I would advise you choose a product that has a better track record. Two defective units in a row is really bad! I hope the manufacturer reads this review and ups their QC process.

Review from first cable received:
Purchased for use with Oculus Link (Oculus Quest VR headset). The oculus software detected a USB 2.0 connection so I decided to run some test to see what I was working with and to rule out port or driver issues. The cable works only as a USB 2.0. Looking inside it has the correct number of pins but it’s apparently defective and only the full set of 2.0 pins are working/detected. I bench marked with a 3.0 external drive which received 160 MB/s using the supplied cable with the hard drive. With this JOTO cable I get 40 MB/s which is the max a 2.0 is rated. Sadly most people won’t be able to test these cables so all of their data transfer speeds will be much slower than advertised. I used Crystal Disk Mark to run my benchmark test. I have requested a replacement in hopes that this is just a rare defect. I have given it one star but if the replacement works I will update this review.

The Velcro strap and plastic rings are a pain in the ... They're a pain.

The Good:

text:
If you can get this on sale for one hundo thirty-ish, just go for it!

The build quality and knobs are excellent. 8/10. They really make you feel like you're using a quality product.

The sound quality. 8/10. Its ~3" woofers get way down to about ~40Hz, which is crazy, but dont expect subwoofer levels of bass. While the bass and treble are tune-able, the bass is cut off at sub frequencies to prevent distortion. It's fine, but some low notes disappear and then come back super loud. That's nitpicking, and the only way to avoid this type of speaker for bookshelf or towers.

Overall 10/10. Its shortcomings are only due to the size of the product, but that's the whole appeal. I think it's a fantastic product.

title: I Wouldn't Recommend for 25"+ Monitors, It WILL Sag
text:
[[VIDEOID:a84c308ecf9a438835fc159d478f803e]] I think lighter & smaller monitors (i.e. < 25" and < 15 lbs) should be fine and you won't be upset with this mount. Check out the photo & video I uploaded showing how the arms are sagging. I have a 25" Dell (U2515H) monitor on the left arm and a 27" Acer (VG271U) monitor on the right arm. Both have very, very significant sag.

Everything else about this mount is great like how the arms swivel in every direction and how you can tighten or loosen how easily each joint swivels. Also, mounting and removing the monitors is easy and feels very safe.

However, the product states that it can hold up to 27" monitors weighing 22lbs on each arm, but even just the arm holding my 25" Dell U2515H monitor (which, according to the amazon page, weighs approx. 15 lbs) is sagging.

Another drawback of this mount is that monitor height is not adjustable. If you want to adjust the height, without risking damage to your monitors, you will need to remove the monitors and unscrew the bolt holding that joint in place and move the arms up and down.

title: Surprisingly bright, crisp focus, and good sound
text:
Used this for a presentation in a conference room; while I wouldn't recommend it for an overly bright room, it does very well in medium lighting (and even better in darkness, of course). Sound quality was much better than my laptop's speakers, and provided decent volume. The picture is actually much better than I expected it to be, based on the price - and my operating system reports it as a full 1920x1080p (but also capable of other modes, like 1600x1200p). Decent selection of connectors. Connector labels are difficult to see in dim light; when on a desk or table, HDMI1 is on the right and HDMI2 is on the left, which may not be immediately intuitive.

While it does have manual vertical keystone adjustment, it has limited range, and requires a fairly flat angle (15⁰ or less) to display without distortion. If the angle is larger than that, not only will the rectangle of the projection be distorted, but you won't be able to get the entire screen in clear focus at once.

The fan is a little loud - not deafening, but definitely audible.

title: Acer always come through.
text:
I've used Acer since about 1997 or so, only had about 3 desktops of theirs in that time, which is saying a lot. If there were any problems it wasn't anything major at all. Also bought a laptop from back in 2010 that still works today, the power button just needs replaced, and also a 2008 small Acer Aspire that finally burnt out this year. So yes they do last. My 10 year old Desktop I just gave my parents also works VERY well, even though they don't use it much. My 5 year old HP still runs pretty good (even though I've never been an HP fan) but is getting some age on it. And has Windows 8 on it, so they won't be supporting it much longer. And it has some slight issues. So i figured it was time for an upgrade, and this is the only brand i fully trust.

I know gaming laptops don't have the longest lifespan, but i have a Dell Desktop that is just fine with an older I5 and a good graphics card in it. So i didn't really by this for gaming, even though i may do a small amount on it. It's just a good backup, upgrade with great specs and will do anything i need it to do. The keyboard has very good travel and is great to type on, much like this small Acer Chromebook I have, which is also a little beast. The red keys only light up when touched, instead of on 24/7. Also Acer is one of the few companies that still put a button to turn off the trackpad when you don't feel like using it. Especially when typing reviews. The GTX 1650 can handle any modern game you through at it, although I haven't tested out much, just a few to see how it runs. And the cooling system Acer uses is really nice, showing you the actual fans on the screen, temp, speeds etc. It gets meh, kind of loud but nothing overbearing like a lot of laptops of this size.

The 128gb SSD is also a nice feature and makes windows 10 run a LOT faster. But the real no brainer was the 1TB HDD it also has in it. So there's your real storage. Instead of using an external drive to try and game on, etc. Which isn't a great idea anyway. So overall the build quality is nice, it looks great, is very fast, and I also got it on sale for only $679, at BB, which i hate. But oh well. That's better than close to a grand. The only draw back is the screen, it's not very colorful, but very bright. So the color gamut could be better. Battery life is also mediocre, but i rarely use it on battery, so no biggie. But that's a minor issue. I hope this Acer lasts as long as my others. And since i take good care of my electronics, i don't that being an issue.

title: Nice little dac amp, just the right mix of warm and detailed.
text: I went through a number of DAC amps when picking this one. The Fiio BTR5 (super muddy and distant sounding despite the good reviews, electronics are nice in it, but the sound was duuull), the Monolith USB DAC (super extended high-end -- which I loved, but pretty much no low end, super forward. That DAC turned everything into a horn speaker sort of experience -- forward and lively.) I almost kept the Monolith because I like analytical detail in my sounds and I really enjoyed the liveliness, but I went with the Zerda, because even though it's warmer it rendered a fuller range better, mostly flat, while still being detailed. I generally find 'warm musical' DACS to be muffled so I don't get why people like them, I also don't understand the concept of fatiguing harshness -- I listen to music, it's rarely just background even if I'm doing another task at the same time. For the price this sounds excellent, I'd have to go much more expensive to get hyper detail + full range so this wins and I'm quite happy with the Zerda.
