title: Predator continues to dominate
text:
This monitor is five years old and still continues to be a relevant, top tier gaming monitor. Acer has continually released updated versions of this model, the one I received was manufactured in Q4 2019.

PROS:
- IPS display. Can be viewed from any angle comfortably.
- 144hz refresh rate. This is the *best* option for gaming. (144hz = 144 frames per second). If you are coming from a traditional 60hz monitor, you will instantly know the difference.
- G-SYNC compatible. To get the most out of this monitor, you will need a fairly modern GPU. I currently have a GeForce RTX 2070 Super, which is more than enough to push out 144 frames.
**If you have an AMD GPU, consider a FreeSync monitor, they are generally cheaper than G-SYNC monitors**
- 4 USB 3.0 ports. Not only does this help with cable management, one of the ports is a dedicated fast charging port for mobile devices.
- Comes with all necessary cables, including DisplayPort 1.2 cable (required to achieve 144hz). The cables are only 1.5M in length, so the monitor must be in close range of the PC.
- 5mm bezel on top and sides. Very sleek yet sturdy.
- Factory default picture settings not far off from optimal. Specifically the gamma was almost spot on out of the box, which can be a headache when it requires manual adjustment.
- Bright and vibrant. Personally, I don't exceed 25% brightness in any situation, but I know some prefer very bright screens.
- Gaming performance. Nothing else to be said, it does what it was made for extremely well.

CONS:
- Poor UI/On-Screen Display. The monitor only has 6 unlabeled buttons that change functions when entering a different menu. Confusing at first, but easier once you memorize what button does what.
- Speakers. Smartphones have better speakers than this monitor. Consider external speakers or a headset, using the built in speakers as a last resort.
- No HDR support. Meh, not really bothered by this.
- Hard to clean. While the monitor base and frame are rock solid, the screen is very delicate. Using anything other than a soft, dry cloth to clean the screen will void your warranty.
- Very short cables out of box, though an easy fix if it's an issue.
- Not intended for photo/video manipulation. Don't get me wrong, it's not 'bad' at colors, but it certainly is not what a photo editor would use for work.

Even in 2020, this monitor exceeds my expectations for everything I have used it for. I ultimately chose this instead of a 4K monitor since 4K monitors are usually only 100-120hz. If you thought you needed 4K for gaming, even in 2020, you don't. Seriously, go with 144hz.

title: Worked well at Burning Man 2019
text:
I was able to reliably text my camp mates at the 2019 Burning Man event. There were many other GoTenna users out there and messages were reliably sent across the city with 2-5 "hops."

Pros:
- Reliable texting
- Optionally auto-share your location when requested. I just noticed that this is a PAID feature! Major drawback. This should be a free feature!
- Downloaded the 2019 city map before arriving and the map seemed accurate
- I like how it's easy to see in the app if your GoTenna is disconnected or how much battery it has

Cons:
- Geo-location was not very accurate. Using my Bluetooth-attached phone, the location should have been accurate to a few meters. Instead it was several hundred meters off
- Battery life is not good. I had to be conscious about charging a few times/day, carry a charger and wire with me
- Uses micro-USB, making it slow to charge and incompatible with modern devices that use USB Type-C.
- Device setup was a pain. I had to uninstall the app and re-pair the GoTenna several times at home before it worked. Documentation and software ease-of-use are lacking
- The Emergency feature sends your location and "This is an emergency, please help me!" to everyone on the mesh network. People seemed to be sending emergency broadcasts accidentally which really worried a lot of people. I spent considerable time one day looking for the person in need of help, only to find out the next day that they accidentally sent the emergency messages. Also, with location not being accurate, I couldn't easily find them. Emergency broadcast should cause the transmitter to beep loudly (or something) so that sender knows they are sending the messages.
- The Shout feature allows you to send a text to everyone on a nearby GoTenna. This quickly became a spammy mess at Burning Man. You can turn off Shout, so this is more of a hassle than a problem with the product
- As mentioned above, auto-location sharing is a PAID feature. This should really be a free feature, GoTenna!

Conclusion:
Despite the drawbacks, I plan to purchase more of these for Burning Man next year. I've used Ham radios in the past to communicate with camp mates, but this is really way easier. BM is the perfect combination of off-grid, and highly populated, to make GoTenna a solid communication solution. GoTenna, please improve the battery and geo-location!

title: Stunning Amp!
text:
My route to the Nova300 was a circuitous one. I came across Peachtree after inheriting my Dad's vintage 1976 JBL L-100 speakers (pictured), and was intrigued by all of the positive reviews. I wanted to purchase an amp that would bring out the best in the speakers, but at the outset had no notion of spending more than $2000 for it. On the contrary, I initially purchased the Peachtree SKY-125 for about $1000, but swapped it for the Nova150 when the SKY-125 developed a problem with the wireless module (Peachtree were excellent about helping with that, and gave me a generous credit). About a year later, Peachtree announced a trade-in option to upgrade to the Nova300, and (to my husband's dismay) I leapt at the opportunity.

I loved the Nova 150, but sometime during my path from it to the Nova300 discovered that I am a bit of an audiophile. The 150 had an amazing clarity -- by far the best amp I'd ever heard -- but the 300, paired with those venerable L100s, takes it to another level. Whether cranked to high decibels or playing at softer levels, the amp produces a life-like sound that is awe-inspiring in its breadth and level of detail, and completely free of the kind of harshness that mars some other amps I've heard. There were textures in familiar recordings -- mostly classical and jazz, whether on vinyl or streaming from the web -- that I'd never heard before. At 300 watts per channel, the Nova300 is stupendously powerful, but the power never feels gratuitous, but acts like an anchor grounding a breathtaking musical experience. The unit is also amazing to look at.

In all, a stunning amp.

This is a nice product and had been very happy, until I hit (lightly) one of my pathlights with the lawn mower and it it snapped off the stake. There is a small circular plastic ring attached to the bottom of the shaft, which attaches to the stake you put in the ground. This ring is attached to the bottom of the shaft with three small screws, and the small plastic areas where the screws go through were snapped off. I was going to glue the ring back on, but then I thought that this was a really good design: the engineers anticipated things bumping into the pathlight and designed this part to be sacrificial, to protect the rest of the unit.

However, I was told my someone from Ring that there were no replacement parts, and left a 1-star review because of that.

Within a day or two, someone from Ring contacted me. He said that the ring that broke was indeed designed to be replaceable, they just don't have any to sell at the moment and offered to send me a whole new pathlight. As promised, it arrived in a few days with a prepaid UPS label to return the broken one.

This is how customer service ought to work. I considered giving 4 stars only because replacement rings aren't available, but the excellent customer service I received really deserves 5 stars. Thank you Daniel.

All in all I'm very happy with the solar pathlights, they work as expected and actually alerted us to someone suspiciously checking our cars in the middle of the night, and activated the camera on our linked ring doorbell.

title: Very disappointing
text:
I bought this because it seemed to be an "improved" version of the awesome PR12 (of which I have two). The PR12 has excellent reception and surprisingly clear and powerful sound for such a tiny radio. The only downside is that the same buttons control tuning and volume (depending on how long the button is pressed), and this can result in accidentally changing the station when one meant to adjust the volume.

Some comparisons with the PR12, then:
1. They are nearly identical in size.
2. Both can play music from a micro-SD card.
3. The TR103 offers shortwave (the PR12 does not) but that wasn't really a selling point for me, as I have dedicated radios for that purpose. I scanned using the radio's short antenna and was only able to pull in a few stations - not surprising as I live in a major urban area. I didn't bother to try by clipping a longer antenna to the radio's built-in one.
3. The PR12 has marginally better sound. This may be because the PR12's speaker is not behind any plastic other than the speaker grille, while the TR103's seems to be partially covered in addition to the grille. We're not talking about a huge difference in tone, mind you, but it's worth noting.
4. I scanned both radios on AM and FM and they found around the same number of FM stations, but with AM, the TR103 found twice as many. That would be terrific if these stations were actually clear enough to hear, but most of them (particularly at the top of the dial) weren't.
4. Perhaps my TR103 has a defect, but I found that AM reception was MUCH clearer on the PR12. The only way for me to improve reception on the TR103 was to hold the antenna. I guess I could clip something to it, but that defeats the purpose of this pocket-sized radio.

So, to sum up: I'm quite disappointed. Retekess makes some stellar, inexpensive radios. Besides the PR12, there's the V115 which has fantastic sound for its size and price, and really great reception. (Again, I find the user interface less than ideal, but I still use it often.) I was hoping the TR103 would give me all the great things about the PR12 with less frustrating control buttons, but the performance is not nearly as good - that, or Retekess has some quality-control issues.

UPDATE:
Well, the folks at Retevis Direct who sell these radios are really on the ball. They must have read my review and I received a refund without even having asked for one. I wasn't asked to return the radio, either. I didn't get any email message, just notification from Amazon that a refund had been made. As a result, I'm upgrading my rating from two to three stars. And I'll certainly feel confident buying from Retevis Direct again.

title: This Has Won Me Over, Despite My Best Intentions
text:
I made up my mind before receiving this item it would only rate three, possibly four stars The main reason for this is I have owned some pretty great Portable Bluetooth Speakers, e.g. the BeoPlay which is a fantastical device I rated four stars (it has superior sound reproduction but weak battery and awkward albeit beautiful architecture making it easy to tip); and the 5 star-rated V-Moda which I loved for two years until the bass speaker blew out after near daily use playing at full blast (I recommended it to someone who bought one and loves it also). I also loved a Riva device until replacing it for the above-two mentioned.
Another reason for my decision is I expected the Stockwell II to use the Marshall name as a crutch for inferior sound reproduction and cheezy production values.
I really did try to hate this thing right out of the box even though it actually looks pretty cool out of the box. Creating a design that is not just referential but an actual miniature of an old school Marshall amp could have been a disaster if it had been cheap and tacky, but really the build on this is to such a high standard of quality that, unless you just absolutely hate the concept of a mini-me version of a Marshall amp, you are probably going to really like the way this thing looks and feels.
As to the bluetooth pairing process this is actually superior to every other bluetooth speaker I've owned. It is as simple as pressing a button on the control top and everything is taken care of with, so far, no false starts. Best of all, it does not, or at least it hasn't mine yet, pull your signal away from your phone when you are in the middle of a conversation as the V-Moda does much to one's irritation.
This is also the first bluetooth speaker I've had with separate treble and bass controls. They work adequately well to control such tones, but it must be said that sound reproduction while acceptable is not top notch. The bass response actually is very sweet, with a honey tone yet it can also punch out vigorously without getting muddy or distorted. Unfortunately, the treble register is a bit tinny or busy soudning at times. The literature touts a novel speaker array, featuring so-called "Blumlein Stereo Sound construction" and for this I have a bone to pick with Stockwell because, curious to know what this touted Blumlien construction is I looked it up online and from what I can determine it is actually a recording technique in which the microphones are set up in such a way (as the tweeters are in this device) as to capture a stereo sound. I saw nothing linking it to speaker positioning or to sound reproduction. Stockwell should include a bit of topical technical information on this construction if it really has an effect upon the sound output. I'm kind of thinking it is a bit of make-believe.
With that said, really sharp looks; high quality construction and finish; adequate sound reproduction; would easily have merited this a qualified 4 star review if it weren't for the battery issue.
This Battery is Awesome! Unlike my other devices which I would have to go back and forth between plugged in and unplugged after a relatively short time unplugged, I have yet to outlast the battery on this speaker. The longest I have been able to listen nonstop at just below full blast (8.5,9) is 3 hours with the speaker still going strong and showing no sings of weakness. With such a robust battery life one expects for this to weigh a ton but the device is not especially heavy. In fact, its weight just adds to its feeling of substantiality and helps its ground stability (one of the issues many of these devices have is the compromise between elegance and stability causing them to either be easy to knock over or be extremely heavy in weight).
While I am very much open to owning a different device which has all the good style elements, and the quality fit and finish this one has but with superior sound reproduction, this little 'amp' will more than do until I find one: Five Stars!

title: Viewing Angle Too Narrow for a Desktop Computer Monitor
text:
The Samsung UE570 has a viewing angle that is too narrow and unsuitable as a desktop computer monitor. When sitting in front of the monitor to use if, the different regions of the display have noticeably different color tones and gray-scale intensity. When I move my head form side to side or up and down, it becomes apparent that these differences across the display are due to the fact that I am seeing different parts of the display at different angles, while just trying to use it at an appropriate distance for computing. All displays look different when seen at different angles. However, even in a marginal quality computer monitor these differences should be small enough that when we are just sitting in front of the monitor to use it, the entire display will look uniform. The Samsung UE570 hugely fails in this basic requirement for a desktop computer monitor. It also has other issues such as the colors are muddy, white is greenish or grayish at the best setting, and the button for adjusting the display settings is very awkward to use.
Shame on Samsung for marketing this display as a desktop computer monitor. Shame on Amazon for flagging it as an “Amazon Choice.”
Side note, the stand that comes with the UE570 allows no adjustments whatsoever: no height adjustment, and no vertical tilt adjustment. I had to set it on a stack of books to even try it out. Reminds me of our first PC monitors decades ago!

title: Great System - Misleading Marketing on Battery Life
text:
OK - I'll start off by saying so far I really like the Blink System. Amazon was running a deal on a 5 Camera system for $284 - which is a GREAT value. Motion Sensors seem to be much better than my old Arlo's, and where the Arlo would sometimes be so slow to start recording and the video would miss all the Action, the Bilink system usually gets pretty much everything. Video Quality on the 1080p setting is excellent as well, and the sound seems to have improved with recent updates. Overall a much better value and performer than my previous Arlo system, at 1/3 the price of a modern Arlo system.

Pros:
- No monthly subscription fee required for the cloud storage
- Really good video & features for the price
- Extremely easy to setup and install
- App is pretty intuitive and easy to use to adjust settings as you go.
- Can turn off the blue LED light that lets people know they are being recorded - although would have been nice to know this feature prior to me getting all the camera's mounted in their weather proof housings (I bought those separately).
- Decent night vision & nighttime video. Getting lots of footage of deer coming through the yard in the middle of the night.
- Uses Lithium AA batteries, which are fairly common and inexpensive compared to the CR123A's my previous Arlo uses/eats.

Cons :
- The advertised 2 year battery life is EXTREMELY misleading as this camera is also advertised as 1080p, but it appears those two "features": are mutually exclusive. The two years is based on a 360p video quality (among other settings you'll likely change and be warned it will shorten battery life) - which I'm sorry is mostly useless if you actually want to identify anyone from the footage.
- Battery Status only reports "OK" not batter percentage, so no idea how quickly my batteries are being discharged at the higher settings.
- There is supposed to be a feature where you can designate certain area's of the screen that won't trigger a recording when motion is detected. This is not working for me, and the camera covering the front yard triggers nearly everytime a car drives by or when my neighbors come & go. This will again drain battery life and use of the cloud storage on useless footage
- There is as yet no option to increase cloud storage if you want to keep video's longer, or are generating a lot of videos.

Overall a great value. Knocked one star off for the very misleading battery life, and once I know how long I'm really getting may come back and knock another off if they last anything less than 6 months at what I consider the more reasonable settings for anyone to use who is investing in a camera system.

title: **Updated to four stars for Customer Service** NOT 6200 Lumens, and Customer Support Does Not Answer
text:
**Original Two Star Review**: I'm not sure what I was expecting in a $250 4k projector, but I certainly thought it would be bright, since it's advertised at 6200 lumens. The picture quality is noticeably better than the Epson EX3240 I was replacing (the Epson is advertised at 3200 lumens and SVGA quality), but the YABER projector is definitely dimmer in comparison. The manual keystone is problematic too. If you focus on the image in the center, any keystoning causes text and images at the top and bottom to become blurry. I've had to put my projector on top of a box, on top of a table, to raise it up enough so that I do not have to keystone, and now it's in my way if I sit head-on on my couch.

The remote control feels cheap, but the thing I really don't like about it is that you have to pry apart the entire back to insert two AAA batteries. I know at some point the thing is going to break in half, or the tabs that hold it together will break off. A sliding or clip-in battery door is a much better design that what this remote has.

I ordered the YABER projector because many reviewers said it was a good value and that the company had excellent customer service. An insert within the projector box urged me to email them first so that they could resolve any issues before I left a negative review. I've emailed them twice in the past week and I have not received a reply.

I'm certainly willing to accept the fact that I might be doing something wrong, with regards to throw distance, projector settings, my home theater lighting setup or whatever, but I'll never know if they don't get back to me. My return window ends on March 15, so I am most likely going to keep shopping for a better projector and return this one before the window runs out. My advice is to spend a little extra money and look elsewhere.

**Update April 1, 2020**
A couple of weeks after I had returned the projector, I was contacted by Yaber customer service. The woman explained that in the COVID-19 madness, they had dropped the ball on my service request, which makes me feel like a total jerk.
She apologized for the inconvenience, offered to replace the projector at no cost, and shipped the updated Y31 model to me. She explained that because they use a different technology than other manufacturers, their lumen calculation is different. That should not be the case because the lumen is an SI derived unit and is a straightforward calculation.
Still, I have to give them credit for their attempt to make things right, so I will update to four stars. If they change their description wording to indicate that these projectors are nowhere near 6200 lumens, I will change to five stars.

title: Noise cancelling is weak
text:
As a biochem/med student - I had longed for these noise-canceling headphones for years but could never foster up the courage to shell out hundreds of dollars for them. Since quarantine - my boyfriend and I have been doing school from home in our small apartment - and I finally decided to get the headphones so I could block out the noise and focus.

I put in a TON of research before settling on these ones - and ultimately picked the Bose because they were more comfortable and I knew I'd be wearing them for several hours each day. Once I got them - I was pretty underwhelmed with their noise-canceling AND their sound quality. With the highest noise-canceling setting on - I can still hear cars passing by on the street if the windows are open, I can hear the bathroom fan from another room, I can hear my boyfriend typing, talking, and eating a bag of chips, everything. I can hear everything. While I will say that the noise is "dampened" a little, it's nothing like what I remember experiencing when I had tried my friend's bose QC headphones in the past.

I had read online several times that "these headphones are better for low-frequencies like rumbling and less for the range of the human voice" so I know not to expect too much - but I really can hear everything with them on. It's *little* better if I play music through them, but the music has to be loud - and at that point, they're really no different from the apple earbuds that came with my phone.

I also read that something is up with the software update with bose and many people have complained about a significant reduction in noise canceling. Those complaints are mostly about the 4.5.2 software, and I currently have the previous 4.3.6 software - so I'm a little shocked that it could even get worse.

If I play white noise through them at high volume AND wear earplugs at the same time - that's when they actually block out some noise - but these aren't worth $300 if I have to do all that. Ultimately I am returning them. I'm so bummed that these didn't work for me. I don't have superior hearing or anything - I'm just a normal person who needed some quiet - and these headphones couldn't do it.

title: Easy setup - 15 mins total
text:
I just ordered a pair of those to add Surround Sound to my Yamaha RX-V685. I already had MusicCast app on my phone (after having installed it for the receiver 6 months ago).
I followed the instructions on the small one page provided: Turn the speaker on, add a new device on the app, press the connect button for 5 secs, it asked me to switch my wifi to the Musiccast one, connected the speaker, confirmed the Wifi network to connect to, done.
Repeat that for the second one. I now have the Receiver, back left and back right devices in.
I tried to set the surround sound using the app but it was not detecting a compatible device...
Simple fix: I overlooked "Update firmware" info on all these devices including my receiver. Click on update, let it complete, repeat for back left and back right speaker, update completed.
Go back to surround sound setup and everything is available. Select the two speakers and off you go.
Tried a movie, and it worked perfect!!
These speakers sound very good by themselves. As a surround sound add-on, they sound great!
After years of 3.1 due to no wires behind my couch, I finally have my 5.1 setup up and running!!

Update 07/30/19:
I upgraded my Wifi at home, changed my SSID and password. The steps to update the settings in these speakers are as follow:
Go to your Musicast app on your phone, release the speakers from the surround sound setup.
Update the Wireless info on your receiver first (if wireless)
Then redo the steps above for each back speakers (turn on, press connect 5 secs, connect to the speaker wifi, choose the new Wifi SSID, password) and done.
Go back to your app and re-add your back speakers to your surround setup and you're done

text:
This was really easy to setup as I was replacing an existing system. You can add 1 extra internal hard drive and 1 external eSATA hard drive. With 8 cameras and a 3GB hard drive added, I get 15 days of recordings. I am going to add another hard drive to get 22 days of recordings. It's easy to look at video on the phone app and look at recordings. Username and password setup and no port forwarding to deal with. I have 4 of the cameras on a POE switch connected to a secondary Google WiFi point and the System picks up the camera over the network and records video.

I have seen complaints about the motion sensors. You can change the sensitivity of the cameras on the phone app and also setup email alerts. You can also block off areas you don't want alerts from such as trees and things that will move in the wind to give you false alerts. The emails will allow you to tune the sensitivity until the point when you only get alerts when necessary. You can turn on alerts for single cameras and change the sensitivity and motion zones on a per camera basis also. You can also schedule when you would like alerts so you only get them at night or during certain times.

Setting up email alerts is easy. Just sent up a new gmail account and enter you email and password in the app. You will get a notification from google and need to change the security settings on your gmail account.

So far in typing this review, I have made two mistakes which have been auto corrected, not bad! The kickstand in the back is great and can be adjusted to your liking for viewing pleasure. It also has a pencil holder which is great (I really wish it had a pencil cap holder as well).
I like the overall feel of the entire encasement while closed - it feels like my iPad is protected. The back has a texture to it which I also like.

I will update this review as I utilize more often. I do use quite often for work, so I am looking forward to providing you with more things to go off of. As of right now, worth $89 that I just paid (from apple $129) - absolutely. Love it so far. Like typing on it, and will be using often.

Update: So, I have had this keyboard for 4 weeks now, and I have mixed feelings. It definitely is amazing to type on, I love the blacklit keys, makes it super simple to work at whatever hours with the lights off, and it is not noisy. I only took it to work one time :/

Reason why:
In my bag, the keyboard kept popping off, and swaying to the side making my iPad turn on and drain the battery. It seems that the keyboard is too heavy for the magnetic strip that fit to the smart connector. It is also very clunky... it’s definitely not slim, and adds a decent amount of weight to the iPad over a few hours of carrying it (at first it didn’t bother me).
Now, while I am home, it is my keyboard of choice to type with and to snap on to the iPad just because it is so comfortable. I love it! But I did buy it so that I didn’t have to travel with much for work; but it’s just too much weight and bulk to do this. Whenever I am outside working, I bring my Apple Smart Keyboard, because it remains slim, and comfortable to carry with me. I wish this keyboard was made a tad bit thinner, and I also wish the smart connector strip was a bit more durable.

I also try to show in the photos the gaps that exist and how easily it can be thrown off the smart connector.

title: Vey time consuming and near could get to to work well...gave up and sent back
text:
I really wanted this to work.....I am by no means an expert on these things but I am well versed enough to be able to set this up and I have set up a number of networks in the past. We have a long, multi level home from 1930 and have always had some trouble getting a good strong signal in all areas to make all 5 of us happy and work cameras and things outside. I had three airport base stations hooked up in different areas with thee separate networks. Worked okay but still have bad spots and you have to switch networks which can be a pain. I decided to do hours of reading reviews and try to find the best mesh network that may help with our type of home. Seemed the this Linksys had good reviews with customers and magazines so I decided to go for it. I took my other network down and hooked these three up around the house, working through the app. It is a fairly slick app, but each step is very slow. Took me hours to get it all up and running in the right spots. Once it was up I did speed checks all over and could never get a signal above 9! Very frustrating...
So I took it all down and reset it and tried again...and again... with some different settings and things...but still never a reading of speed above 9!!! Was not enough to reach far areas of my house. Even if this worked, I could see that I would have to by 3 more to really cover my home, at a total cost of close to $1000.
So.. I decided to spend my evening calling the help line to see if they could help me figure what was going wrong. After 25 minutes on hold, I decided to give up and send it all back... Even with the low speeds it seemed to work well at times then, freeze up at other times. I would walk by a box and the red light would be on for no reason...then go blue.
I hate this system!
Could all be my fault in the the way I was hooking something up, I'll admit that. But, I have enough time sunk into this thing. I decided to reboot my old system and move boxes around a bit and alter some settings and once up and running it was getting awesome speed readings all over the house. I'm running mostly apple products with comcast internet.

title: Every helicopter (insert parent, property owner, etc., here) needs one, or three.
text:
This is like James Bond, CIA, FBI and creepy stalker rolled into one. Talk about your standard run of the mill covert action...use with caution.

Here's why I bought this (hey, now don't judge). Crazy teenage boy who, with his inate need to push buttons and boundaries, says one thing and does another...using a car he doesn't own (I do)...yep, life is full of lessons and there are many to both teach and learn coming from both sides.

Anyway, I did some extensive research of how to best monitor this knucklehead's whereabouts and nothing proved all encompassing. What I found was between his (ha, not really his) smartphone (GPS tracking feature, as long as he didn't "accidentally" disable it) and this GPS device, I had covered 9/10 areas of concern. In other words, the likelihood he'd leave both the vehicle and smartphone at the same time, was less than 10%.

I chose this particular device for a number of reasons, including:

Cost - not the cheapest, but also definitely not the most expensive (by a long shot)

Flexibility - not hard-wired makes it easy to add to and remove from the equation (and use it for other needs, should the need arise)...and the battery life on this thing is ridiculous (once I figured out the sleep mode option, this can go on for multiple weeks before needing a recharge...the magnet makes for a nice touch of mounting/location options

Features - option to track via SMS, Android App, web site, Google Maps, etc., makes it one of the better devices

The only real con(s) I could give this thing aren't truly deal breakers, but more like "good to knows" before entering the game:

SIM card...yep, it needs one and one with data and/or (if you care to use the listen in feature) voice. While I'm an IT weenie in real life, the whole realm of cellular, carriers and wireless services is/was rather confusing, but I settled on the pay-as-you-go SpeedTalk Wireless SIM/plan...no lock in, contracts, etc., and you can pause/start as desired.

Configuration...this was a bit of extra effort as the initial programming was tedious-ish old school (code speak), but not difficult or impossible. While the instruction guide could be better, read and re-read it a few times before beginning the process. And be sure to follow the SpeedTalk directions properly, else you'll struggle.

Android App and web site...neither one are "polished", but each work as desired (once you get used to the process)...it's more like a learning curve, but definitely not something impossible for even those with limited tech backgrounds. I like it to moving from Apple-to-Android or Windows-to-Apple.

All in all, this device has served its purpose...for teaching an invicible, smarty pants child that life is full of teaching moments and learning experiences as well as always being mindful of who might be watching. Sometimes all it takes is a hard dose of reality and devices such as this, although could also be used for all the wrong reasons, helps to keep the family together. Trust is a wonderful thing, yes, but with peer pressure coming from all angles, this doohickey helps to drive (no pun intended) home the mantra to "being a good person and a productive member of society isn't easy, but it is necessary, and we can't go it alone".

title: Great, Versatile Light. Highly Recommended
text:
This is a very versatile light. In addition to standard LED panel features that you tend to get, with variable brightness and color temperature, this is also an RGB LED, which means you can create virtually any color light by just tweaking the settings!

Before we get into the light's features and how well this light works, I wanted to quickly mention the form factor. The light panel itself is 2 3/4" x 4 7/8" x 5/8" (7cm x 12.4cm x 1.5cm). On the side opposite the controls is a wonderful, fully articulating mounting bracket. This bracket adds another 3/4” (2cm) to the width of the whole package, but it’s great because right out of the box you can slap this light on any tripod and position it at any angle.

So this light is nice and small. Smaller than my iPhone 7+, making it easily pocketable.

The controls are nice and easy.

On top you have a dedicated power switch, which I like a lot. On similar style lights, you have a set switch, which doubles as a power switch, which isn't bad, but I really like the dedicated sliding power switch on this light. Also on top is the USB-C charging port. Which is awesome. I have long hated all variations of the USB mini and micro ports. Good riddance to those ports.

If you're looking at the back of the light, on the left is the bracket, and on the right you have the set switch for changing modes. The light has three modes.

Standard mode, where you can control the overall brightness, and the color temperature

In this mode you control the color temperature with the FN wheel, and set the brightness with the dim wheel.

In RGB mode, the color is set in degrees from 0º-360º, starting with red at 0º and moving through orange, yellow green, blue, purple, violet, and ending with magenta at 360º

There’s a handy chart on the back showing you the degree setting for particular colors, but even without that it’s easy enough to figure it out as the color of the light actively changes as you change the setting.

By default, when you enter into RGB mode, your in color selection mode, and to change the color you use the FN wheel.

If you want to change the saturation of the color you’ve chosen, you can press the FN wheel, which also acts as a button, to switch the setting from color to saturation, and then use the FN wheel to set the saturation level. Press the FN wheel again to switch back to changing the color.

And just as in standard mode, you can use the dim switch to change how bright the light is.

The last mode is Scene mode, where you can choose from various lighting scene emulations like police lights, strobing colors, etc..., and again, regardless of the mode chosen, you control how bright the light is with the dim wheel.

All in all, this is a great light. My only complaint is that the dim wheel is not very smooth. It’s very easy to spin the wheel and make big changes to the brightness, but making very small changes requires a little fiddling.

All in all great light

title: Perfect for self-driving cars
text:
I am using these mounts to hold an EON Gold Dev Kit from Comma.ai on my windshield. The EON Gold runs OpenPilot and makes my car drive itself like a Tesla. When Comma selected the windshield mount, they aimed to use GoPro windshield mounts. What they didn't know was that they chose a design with a tiny flaw in the cutting -- a design flaw that these mounts from AFAITH match perfectly. Rumor has it that AFAITH makes these mounts in two different factories. Only one of the factories appears to have corrected the design flaw.

Having corrected the issue means that you have a 50/50 chance of receiving an error batch or a corrected batch. You're going to receive mounts that work with the EON Gold from Comma.ai (but don't work with GoPro cameras), or you're going to receive a batch that works perfectly with GoPro cameras but does not work with the EON Gold Dev Kits. I lucked out and got an error batch that works perfectly with my EON Gold.

AFAITH, if you're reading this, PLEASE DO NOT FIX THIS ERROR. Your mounts with the design flaws are the only ones that work perfectly with the EON Gold Dev Kit, and the EON must be perfectly stable on the windshield to confidently steer the car. If you insist on shipping the corrected design, I'll urge you to maintain the flawed design, as your mounts unknowingly play such a critical role in the self-driving car space.

Crazy, right?

title: Great and Super fun with vintage feel
text:

There are three lights on the bottom left: battery, printing, and SD card. If the battery is white, it's fine to use, if printing is white, it's printing, and if SD card is red there's no micro SD (white means there is). The pictures it takes are super cute and very fun, but don't buy this if you're expecting iPhone or other camera quality pictures. They're different than polaroid prints, but are very similar quality to cameras from the early 2000s/2010s or so. You can see everything but it's not going to be super vivid and the color will be a little off. Also, try to take pictures in light, but as you can see in the last photo, the camera won't always adjust to super bright light like another camera would.
I bought this as the used (like new description) and it was in perfect condition. The box had a slight mark but had never been opened. This product comes with 10 sheets of paper, but if you're looking to buy more, amazon has HP Zink 2x3 sticky back paper that is cheaper than the Kodak brand of the same exact thing, and works just as well. Really no difference, just a few dollars more.
Last thing: in the instruction manual it comes with, the black and white vs color switch instructions seem to be slightly wrong. If you can see the three colorful dots, your photo will come out in color. If the dots are grey and black, it'll be black and white. The manual seemed to reverse this, so I figured I'd mention it. :)

title: Fun, useful, versatile surveillance camera
text:
Overall the camera is good quality and customer support is excellent as usual.
I have used a few different cameras from ieGeek and I am pleased with them all.
Just be aware of the features of any camera so you know what to expect. The descriptions about the product are useful. The main different features between the battery and plug-in type cameras
are the portability, motion detection, recording period, camera settings customization, and user interface.

Construction is great, small and simple. The picture quality is excellent.
The magnetic mount is extremely versatile, putting it on a metal book end allows you to move it easily around the house. Another advantage of this mount is that it's extremely easy remove the camera to recharge the batteries.
Microphone and speaker performance is like a typical cellphone in speakerphone mode.

Camera is very light sensitive such that if you turned off night vision, then even at dusk the color image is impressive. The night vision range is about 100ft outdoors. The camera accomplishes this with bright IR LEDs.
There is an undesired effect of these bright LEDs, that if the person or object is within about 20ft, then night vision will show that object as white. The two outdoor images were taken around dusk, too dark to walk around without a flashlight. The tree is about 25ft. away and the shed 100ft. away. Amazing that the daytime mode shows a bright colorful image with such low light. The grass within 10ft. is all white in night time mode. A solution would be to block one or more of the LEDs with tape and possibly use an external LED source that you can control the brightness. For future enhancement I would like control to dim or turn off the IR LEDs while still in night time mode.

If water drops in front of the camera such as from a roof eave, then in night time mode the motion detector may trigger if at high level. Switching to low level motion detection helps not to detect these drops. The camera got a little wet and it still functioned as expected.

When motion is detected the camera wakes up and needs to adjust exposure, the image may initially be all white for a moment. There is about a 1 second delay until exposure adjusts and video is accurate.

My experience with WiFi range is about 80ft inside going through floor, walls and around corners. Outside the range was over 100ft.

Installing the camera with CloudEdge is straight forward and the manual explains steps well. You must format the SD card before all settings for recording are shown in the application. I have not used the online storage, only the SD card.

I have ventured away from the WiFi router and the camera also works as a trail camera. The camera must be connected to internet so that you can view images/video on phone using CloudEdge App.

title: Best Note to date
text:
First off, let me say this is the 5th Note I have owned (2,4,8 and 9 previously). I was horrified at the price ($1200), but the pre-order freebies took a little of the sting away.
I can honestly say that besides the camera, there was little to no difference between the Note 8 and Note 9, and not REALLY worth the upgrade given the price.....The Note 10 on the other hand is a different story...it's worth upgrading from ANY previous note.
I've had the phone 4 days so far, and amazed at how quickly it charges with the included 25W charger. After setting it up, transferring files and playing with it for a few hours, I was able to go from 56% to 100% in 23 mins with the fast charger. Battery life is better than my Note 9... I use my phone a lot, but am not on it all day, and haven't seen it dip below 70% so far (except for initial setup which is battery intensive).
General speed of the phone is much snappier than my Note 9. All I can say is that it feels more "fluid" than any other phone I've owned to date. Gallery is lightning fast generating thumbnails and playing videos/viewing pictures....even from the SD card. Sound seems to be louder than with the Note 9.
Camera takes AWESOME video and stills. Many new camera features I have not explored yet.
Size of the Note 10+ is noticeably larger than the 9. Which is great, for me at least.
I have not tried out the fingerprint sensor yet, and when I do, will probably still stick with the facial recognition unlock...it's just so fast and effortless, I can't see adding the extra step of pressing a certain spot of the screen.
S-Pen works great, and the "air write" mode is fantastic. Again, many new features I have not explored yet.
CONS:
PRICE. VERY expensive. I'm not sure how long the promotion will last, but Samsung will give you $600 for a Note 9 trade in, which should be jumped on....getting THIS phone at $600 off with a trade in is a bargain.
No old style headphone jack...which is not a con for me, as I have never used headphones with my phone, and if I ever did...I'm sure the included USB-C headphones would work just fine for me. No replaceable battery...a feature not seen with Notes since the Note 4....I wish they would bring it back. You have to pay extra for the even faster 45W charger. Including a 25W charger vs the 45W charger is just a tease... but on the bright side, I read where charging your phone THAT fast greatly reduces the life of the battery.

All in all, this phone feels like a major upgrade, where previous models felt like a minor upgrade. This is a QUALITY phone top to bottom. If you are looking to upgrade, all I can say is "pull the trigger". DON'T get wrapped up in opinions on the net about how you should "wait for this phone" or "wait for that one".... I mean there will ALWAYS be newer, better features on EVERY newer model.... so if you are constantly waiting 6 months or a year for the newest "better phone"....you're never gonna have a new phone. LOL As a loyal Note user, this has to be the happiest I've been with a new model in quite awhile.

title: An OK Experience That Is Not Worth the High Price
text:
Edit 3: Janurary 2023 - The headphones have stopped worked. Would recommend staying away if you care to have a set that has longevity.

Edit 2: January 2021 the price shows these at $270. At this price, I would say this would be a consideration for purchasing. There are still "meh" qualities and I'd encourage comparison to other headsets, but $270 is a significantly better price point than the $450 I bought them for. Any price for these above ~$300, I'd strongly encourage you to spend your money on a better headset. $270 makes these more of a contender.

Edit: I've now had this headset for 6 months. I see the price has dropped to $360. I echo my review below and would strongly encourage you consider a different headset. Firmware updates have improved things but they have been very infrequent. The desktop app on the other hand has received a lot of updates, though that brings no improvement to the headset. I would still say these are still meh and not worth the price. I did get the Sony's and use those as my main set when working, if that matters to anyone.

Original Review:
First things first, these are not worth $450 (which is what I purchased them at when bought). They don't feel premium, but rather cheap plastic. I'm particularly nervous about the longevity of the boom mic. There's some nice features, like the auto pause of music, ability to pause/mute when taking the headphones off, and the busy light. But if you're spending $450 just for those features, I'd think you'd need to consider what you really feel is important in a headset.

I bought these solely for work since I generally spend 6+ hours a day on calls. The call quality is a bit above average, but does not cause anyone to say "wow, you sound so good!". It's better than other mics, but not by any significant margin.

Sound-wise they are decent. They are not as good as Sony or Bose, but they do an OK job. The Sound+ app equalizer is helpful to find the right balance. But I wouldn't recommend buying these for any sort of audiophile listening experience. ANC is OK. You can still hear some noises at certain frequencies but it's not bad ANC.

Comfort, these do fairly decent. I like how they cup over the ear. They take a little (i.e. 2-3 days) to get used to the pressure, but then are fairly comfortable to wear for longer periods. Not awesome as the Bose QuietComfort by any means, but they get the job done.

So, they do OK on call quality, OK on sound for music and listening, and OK on comfort. Bottom line is that I would not recommend these for $450. If they were around the $300, then I may say it might be worth it. At this price point, I would expect at a minimum a premium call experience and they just don't deliver as much as their marketing department would lead you to believe which is sad. I'd strongly consider the Sony WH-1000XM4 over these, even though the Sony's don't have a boom mic. They offer as good a call experience, a significantly better audio listening experience, and are $100 cheaper.

If another tile user passes your Tile, you'll be alerted where the Tile was located. That's handy and it helped one of my kids when they couldn't remember where they placed an item that had the tile. Took a few days but eventually the tile showed up on the app and they went to retrieve it.

title: This thing works, it replaced a ultra hi-gain UHF only & I had to remove one ampifier.
text:
We have used "Stellar Labs" antennas at work & they do their job.
When it came time to replace my personal antenna at home (due to not having VHF-High band) I tried this one.
Why I chose this one?
A) it has decibel (dB) ratings. only a few brands actually list this (Channel Master, Wineguard, etc.)
B) compact size (the one it replaced was 9' long)
C) wide field of view
D) UHF & VHF-Hi bands (old one was UHF only)

Warning!!! this antenna gets a lot of frequencies, & I was getting VHF-hi signal quality issues from Cell towers. easy fix was an "LTE filter" before my amp, it cleared 97% of the issues.
I also added an inline FM Trap before the amp also, this was cheap insurance for other issues.

Warning!!! Be careful with over modulation. (too much power)
I work with TV stuff more than I should for work & we have a Blounder Tounge meter for signal quality & I wish I had it at home... my dual amp setup was blowing the digital signal out on the top end, & I ended up removing one amp & dialing the other to 75%. I used the built in signal strength meter on our TVs.

title: Excellent value for the money!
text:
First off, Amazon sells this laptop for $649 and my understanding is that for the moment this is an Amazon exclusive offering - if you see it for more than that from a third party, they're buying it from Amazon and jacking up the price by $100 or more. Just wait for Amazon to get it back in stock.

Now, let's talk about the hardware: it truly boggles my mind what Acer is able to offer for $649. An *eight* core CPU with a surprisingly strong integrated GPU? 8 GB RAM? A 512 GB nVME SSD? Good battery life? A solid keyboard? Incredible value. Sure, the overall build quality isn't amazing, but it's $650! I'd heard the screen wasn't very good, but I was pleasantly surprised when I saw it in person. It doesn't get super bright, but for most people the screen is just fine.

The only negative experience I've had so far with this laptop is that when I was running Windows Update on it, one of the updates hung the entire machine - I had to press and hold the power button to force a complete reset. On a brand new machine with no third party apps installed yet, that's completely ridiculous. Acer and Microsoft need to do better than that. I haven't seen it happen again, but it also hasn't been heavily used yet. I hope that wasn't a sign of instability to come.

Overall, Acer has done an impressive thing here: create a laptop powerful enough for gaming and content creation, light enough to carry anywhere, with enough battery life to last for many hours. And all for $650? Amazing.

Every time I walked by, I would touch it to see how how it was, and the heat buildup was minimal. I eventually opted to power the Android TV box another way, but I would feel comfortable installing this inside the wall of an RV, or under a dash, or even burying it under carpet in the trunk.

Because I only used it for 72 hours straight, I can't give a long term review of it, but in the short I used it, it did what it was supposed to do. It is a very small converter that is about the size of a book of matches, so you can hide it easily. If I need to use a converter like this again, I wouldn't hesitate to buy this one again.

title: Netgear has declined in quality and consumer trust
text:

The router will absolutely NOT work unless you register with them (submitting your personal information, home address, name, phone number, etc) when logging into the router via PC or smartphone (with the Netgear Nighthawk App). Until you do this, the wifi signal it broadcasts has no internet connectivity. This goes contrary to pretty much EVER router out there, which is basically plug and play out of the box, with the provided wifi network name and default wifi password. title: The sturdiest magnetic stand case (that I've tested) for rhythm gamers
text:
I had been hunting for a landscape-oriented iPad Pro 2018 case that allows multitudes of angle adjustments and is sturdy enough to not wobble while under intense action (i.e. tapping quick and hard enough to produce a considerably loud sound).

As laying screen flat will cause damages to the neck and spine in a long run (you have to stay in the position where you bend your neck down and potentially bend your back for a long time per gaming session), I have been testing multiple solutions, including:
- Repurposing adjustable notebook stands
- Placing an object with enough inertia (i.e. being heavy) on one end and an anti-slip pad on the other end to create slope
- Using cases with stands
and find that having a proper case is the best solution for both ergonomics and portability (obviously).

Examples of the cases that I have test are:
- Cases with hinge designed that allows >150 degrees of adjustment but are not sturdy enough to withstand constant forces acted upon them
- Cases with a certain amount of angle adjustments created by folding
- Cases with a magnetic kickstand, basically where this product is categorized
The first two categories are not good enough so I will not describe their pros and cons here.

So what about the last category? There are several brands that offer cases with this design aspect, but with difference in the kickstand design. I am glad to say that after using this case for a week, the design for this case proves to be the sturdiest of the bunch, with the largest flap and the longest contact edge providing the level of sturdiness I have been looking for.

For the other aspects of the case:
- The buttons are really tactile and responsive
- The slot for Apple Pencil is not too tight or too loose; a great fit for the object
- The case finish has a nice touch to it although it kinds of attract dust
- Its weight adds the iPad enough heft that kind of prevents you to accidentally let the device slip out of your hands, although you have to get used to the weight initially
- Reduces WiFi signal reception to a certain extent compared to being bared; you have to be quite far from the access point to notice the signal drop/loss though
- It is easier to install/remove the case than quite a number of the cases I tested, as I have no accidental screen capture when installing/removing this case at all
- Cheaper than the majority of the cases with this design aspect

Most of the time I use the iPad in landscape mode, so not having an option for portrait stand is not a huge deal for me.

Solid 5 stars. Will buy a smaller version if it exists for my iPad mini.

title: Very good Antenna Chimney mount
text:
You'll need: 7/16 wrench, small hammer, screw driver, band cutter, instructions (not included-seems silly)
1. Go to the Skywalker website and get the instructions for the SKY6027
2. Make up "1/2 of each bracket" before you go on the roof i.e. put the metal bands on each of two of the triangle eye screws and mount one eye screw to each bracket (only 3 or 4 threads). Do as much as you can on the ground.
3. IT TAKES TWO PEOPLE. one person to hold the bracket in place and the other person to wrap the band around the chimney, run the band through the "band clamp" as shown in the directions and bang it down with the hammer. Tighten the triangle screws evenly (you'll need the screw driver to hold the triangle part from spinning). I don't think this is possible with one person.
4. Tighten the nuts on the triangle screws until tight, but go easy, I cracked one of the corner bricks. Cut off any excess band.
5. Add the mast to the bracket and you're done.

I had one of these mounts for over 20 years and it worked very well until the band snapped. I'm sure this new one will last as long.
Good Luck!

title: Ignore the “Not 10TB” posts.
text:
I have around 20 of these drives and have had 0 issues (all have been removed from the USB enclosures and distributed among my home servers to create a clustered file system). I normally don’t review products, but after seeing all of the “not 10TBs” I felt like someone needed to clarify the difference between TB, and TiB. These drives are 10TB, and most OSs will report them as such. Windows (and some other OSs) report drives in TiB.

One gigabyte is 1000^3 bytes. One gibibyte or GiB is 2^30 bytes.

Because of this, and some OSs choice to display values incorrectly (like windows does), the drive will show as a bit over 9TB when it’s in fact 10TB, and a bit over 9TiB. This will be true with 100% of drives (adjusted based on their capacity of course). It’s not the hard drive manufactures trying to be misleading, it’s the developers of poor sting systems choosing to use the wrong label throughout their systems.

Another thing I’ve seen pointed out is that it requires a wall power adapter, and people seem to think that’s a negative. USB does not provide enough power (at least most USB ports used today) to power a 12v ~1.5amp (18watt) drive because USB has typically been limited to 5v and 500ma (2.5 watts). Obviously you can’t power a device requiring around 18w with only 2.5 watts (if you figure out a way to do so, you should become very wealthy very quickly).

As for the product, as I mentioned, I’ve had 0 issues with the 20 or so drives I have running. I don’t expect that to be the case forever. It’s a matter of time before I have one/some die. It’s the nature of hard drives. Some may last a decade or more, some may last a day or two. With this drive, or any other, you need to have backups (or additional backups) of important files. Every drive on the market is susceptible to failure. This drive is no exception. This drive is often a great value when it’s on sale. If it’s a good price, you should feel comfortable buying it, just educate yourself s but before feeling like you got cheated somehow.

title: Not a bad attempt, but suffers from some serious flaws.
text:
Update 04/06/19: After a 5 mile run today I have chosen to return these. I have used them several times over the past week. When they work they are nice, they work fine if I use them at work or around the house, but if I'm running or hiking they de-sync from each other and stutter CONSTANTLY. They are completely unusable and infuriating. They have been updated by Samsung, but still the connection problems persist. Hopefully Samsung can fix these problems in the future, but until then I'm not happy about paying top shelf prices for a beta test. I'm going back to my $20 Chinese earbuds that actually WORK.

I received my Galaxy Buds last Friday the 29th. I was excited to receive them as I use earbuds often when working out or just walking around and the $20 set of Chinese earbuds I had been using worked reasonably well but I wanted to splurge a little on some really nice truly wireless earbuds.

Initial thoughts:

Aesthetically they are very nice, they don't hang out of your ears, really it just looks like you are wearing earplugs or something. They fit comfortably in the ears, they come with a variety of rubber parts of various sizes so you can really dial in the fit. Most importantly they sort of "lock in" to your ears. That is a feature that I cannot live without. There's nothing I hate more than earbuds falling out when you are just getting into a run.

I used them around the house over the weekend. Buds in, phone sitting on my desk or sometimes in my pocket and they worked fine. The sound is decent. I'm no audiophile but I've used good earbuds and bad ones and these definitely fall into the good category. The app is great, the charging case is convenient and easy to use, and the ambient sound "enhancement" works surprisingly well.

Now for the downside:

I took the Buds out for a little hike today, nothing serious. Phone in my pocket. At first they worked fine, but as the hike went on they started cutting out intermittently. Sometimes one, sometimes the other, sometimes they were out of sync with each other. I tried disconnecting them, turning bluetooth on and off, even messing with audio settings. I tried holding the phone, putting it in a different pocket, no matter what I tried it would only help the problem for a few seconds at most. By the time I was nearing the end of the trail the earbuds were almost unusable cutting out and stuttering constantly.

I had a similar problem with a pair of the Chinese bluetooth earbuds and I had to return them for a replacement, but now the current pair I have work flawlessly. I'll try the Galaxy Buds again and update my review, but if this continues and the connectivity is really worse than a $20 pair of earbuds I can't recommend these to anyone.

title: The power switch is badly located
text:

The previous version had a recessed power switch on the side which was easy to use and not susceptible to inadvertent deactivation. The bottom switch deactivates my Kindle with annoying regularity. I hold it in my right hand, the switch is almost under my little finger. The switch location results in turning it off while I am reading, or having to stop reading and clicking on a popup to cancel the power off. The fact that the previous version was engineered to avoid this problem indicated that the current version is a victim of poor design and/management.

While there are aspects of this version I like, the annoying interruptions in my reading overpowers them. I will not buy another Kindle with this retrograde switch placement, even if I have to use an Android tablet to read my books, instead of the Kindle, which in most respects I prefer.

"Incorrect AC adapter is attached. This AC adapter cannot provide enough power for normal operation of your computer. You may be able to charge your battery with the AC adapter if your computer is in sleep or shut-down states."

The laptop will charge in sleep and shut-down as indicated by the green power connection indicator near the laptop's charger port. That light is not illuminated when the laptop is powered on an awake.

title: Too many limitations.  Sticking with my tablet.
text:
Okay so all i really wanted was a smaller version of my Fire tablet with a built-in decent speaker.

I have three Fires, the oldest, an HDX 7" (with better screen than any newer model) had to be retired at 5 years old. I've been using the new HD8 (in constant airplane mode) as a nightstand alarm clock with the My Alarm Clock app, which allows me to use downloaded music as well as some decent prerecorded alarm sounds in an infinite number of configurations. I have about a dozen different alarms stored for different times with different music choices and sounds that I can use anytime at will.

All i wanted with this Echo Show was a smaller version of that without losing much of the functionality of my Fire tablet.

Total fail.

Amazon wants total continuous access to watch and listen to you. The options to disable the camera and microphones come with unattractive bright red warnings, two of which light up on the frame and screen, as if privacy was an anomaly. No, the active mic and camera should have the red alerts to remind you : "Hey, this is NOT private!!"

I can't download any music. The "customizable" clock faces aren't so much. Very limited choices for alarms and screen looks, and no matter how hard you try to disable them, Amazon keeps sending random messages on your screen.

I don't need to access smarthome functions and don't like Alexa. This thing assumes thats really ALL you want to do.

The music program offers no onscreen menu or choices to access your music. Bluetooth lets you play music from your phone, but my Fire play the same music without needing the phone and it can store music offline so you're not using up any WiFi data or allowing "Alexa" to watch or eavesdrop.

If these devices allowed us access to use the built-in microphone and camera for personal security - to monitor our space when not home, etc. - while keeping the airplane option to disable net connection -THAT could be useful. But instead these devices are only interested in using them to monitor us. No thanks.

It's small. It's cute. I can't call it a bargain even at the Prime Day price (Tax and Device disposal fee will extend that from $50 to over 60) because it is really not useful to me.

I'm returning it and sticking with using a tablet because (though it's bigger than I'd like) it serves my purpose. This does not.

title: Tuner is Faulty and/or Weak. Don't Waste Your Money.
text: I am 5 -7 miles Southwest from all of the stations I care about. I have a 50 mile antenna that I can receive those main 3 letter networks and about 35 additional channels when plugged directly into my TV. When I plug the antenna into the AirTV, I lose over 20 of those stations and Fox, ABC, NBC, and CBS become, a lot of the time, unwatchable. There are considerable loss of signal errors, and pixelation. The entire reason I purchased this device was to DVR those channels (football season). However, I can't do that reliably. I have repositioned the antenna (even though my TV picks up the stations just fine), trying to give this box the benefit of the doubt. What finally did it for me today was contacting tech support. After I explained to them all that I had done, the only suggestion that they could make was to get a stronger antenna. The guy in tech support told me that their boxes do not have any signal amplification in them and that was the problem. I do not wish to go spend more money on this defective box. I have already purchased the box, plus bought a specific (tested compatible) brand of USB HDD to DVR the OTA channels. Now, they want me to go purchase something else? I have great signal strength with my low-mid tier JVC LCD TV. Why wouldn't a box that is purpose built to receive OTA channels have a decent receiver? Why does my refurbished, several years old LCD low cost LCD TV have a better receiver than this box? My TV cost about 3x the price of the box, does all kinds of things, and has a 50 inch screen and you're telling me that they also built in a better HD receiver? This box has 1 job and it fails.

title: It works, but routing video cables is a hassle
text:
Alright, I'm a bit grumpy that my monitor didn't come with VESA screw holes. On top of a $30 budget monitor arm, I also have to purchase a $30-ish VESA adapter.

The Adapter Bracket works (it's not fantastic, but it's works) and it's pretty easy to install. The problem is that oval hole in the middle of the bracket is where your video cables are supposed to go (HDMI or DVI). The hold is too close to the monitor and/or the hole is too small. With enough wiggling, you can eventually plug in a video cable and you can eventually get the cable to run through the small hole. The problem is that now, your video cable is making a stressful bend in order to get through the oval hole.

If the plate was a little further back or if the hole was big enough to line up with the video ports, it would be easier to plug in an HDMI or DVI cable and the cable wouldn't be bent at a weird angle.

Buying a vertical 270 degree HDMI adapter would be a good idea. A 90 degree vertical adapter will NOT work because that will make your HDMI cable point "down" right into the bottom of the Adapter Bracket. Any right angle adapter that turns horizontally will probably work to avoid the Adapter Bracket.

title: FAA compliant....Great size and capacity for USB-C PD, but owners manual is lacking
text:
Update: I've been using this to power my laptop ((Dell Latitude 5591) which charges fine from it even though it says that it's a slow charger. It takes up a little more space than the actual charger, but nearly triples my runtime (68 Wh) without having to worry about whether there's a plug nearby. Another key thing to point out is that while you can use the USB-C Port to supply power to a device, you cannot charge the power bank via USB-C, only the supplied wall wart.

At 99 Wh, it's compliant with FAA regulations so you can take it onto any flight. That said, they have a bunch of mAh and other specs on the bottom, so it would probably be good if they actually listed the Wh on the case in case some overzealous gate agent gets their shorts in a bind.

I've been looking f or a really compact AC source to power several USB-C devices including a laptop, portable monitor and our Samsung phones. A lot of the power banks have a blocky shape which doesn't fit well with stuff in my messengers bag. The AC port is a bonus, though there are some issues I'll explain, as it also lets me use the power bank for some small items like a nixie clock and a portable LED floodlight. While there are inexpensive LED floodlights, this allowed me a free upgrade for a light I already had.

WIth ~100 Wh of total energy, the power bank is built around a stack of LiPo cells. It's got a really bright display with a lot of info - how much power you are using, how much time is left at that power consumption, as well as a % of charge left in the the pack.

The pack turns on automatically when you plug in a USB device, which is handy. It also turns on automatically with the USB-C PD outlet. Where it's not automatic is when you use it with AC items. When you plug in a AC item nothing happens. When you push the AC button, the display comes on then goes off. It turns out that you need to push the AC button and hold if for for about 3 seconds, then the green light comes on and you have AC power. Similarly to turn it off, if you press the AC button the display comes on momentarily only - you have to press and hold the AC button to get the AC to power down. That's more of a owners manual complaint than a product complaint. As a suggestion, the buttons could be a bit beefier, but otherwise this power pack is perfect for what I wanted.
