title: ChromeCAST Casting is a nightmare.
text:
I bought this with intentions of replacing the need for my long and winding HDMI cable, which I feed from my desktop computer to my television on the other side of the room. Essentially, I pull up various streaming services on the computer and then watch them on the TV, but in order to pause, rewind, or change videos, I have to get up and sit at the computer for a bit. It's a pain in the butt, however it's worked for me flawlessly for well over a year now. I had hoped to be able to cast TV, music, and videos from other devices (phone, laptop, tablet) to the Google Chromecast and save myself a few steps back and forth.
Unfortunately, my only truly compatible device is my Android phone which, due to storage space issues I use for nothing, so the control features built into this product are useless to me, and I don't have any other Google Home products so being able to call out voice controls isn't something I can benefit from either. When screen-mirroring and casting from my other devices (which was my primary goal anyway), the connection is absolute garbage. The video itself comes through in oddly poor quality, the audio is choppy and robotic, and the stream often lags despite having excellent high-speed internet in my home. I'm returning this thing, and will try an Amazon firestick instead. At least it comes with a real remote.

title: Works Great With Or Without External Power
text:
Up front the only reason this isn't a 5 star device is that I think the price is a little high for what it is. It's otherwise a very solid device.

If you're just using it as a hub for USB thumb drives/pen drives, and peripherals then you don't need the additional power adapter - this makes it great for travel because your laptop's 3.0 USB ports should be enough to power it.

The included adapter is a whopping 20 watts (that's seriously good) which means that if you have it also plugged into mains power you can also use it to easily charge your phone or power-hungry tablet as well. Alternatively you could use it without a Laptop/PC at all and just charge all your devices from wall power.

I don't like the fact that the USB3 cable is not modular - it's a fixed cable and it's maybe 2ft in length so if you're trying to use this with a desktop, your placement options may be very limited.

The surface seems to resist scratches and finger prints, and the entire bottom is covered in rubber padding material (which is much nicer than just putting 4 nubs on the underside).

It has a decent weight to it so it doesn't slide around too much when plugging and unplugging devices, though I would personally have liked it to be a tad bit heavier.

All in all it's a good hub with just a couple of flaws.

Pros:
- Works fine without external power
- Provided power supply provides enough current for power-hungry devices (i.e. Nintendo Switch)
- Nice finish
- Tons of ports

Cons
- A bit pricey for a hub - especially without an SD card slot or modular USB cable.
- Fixed USB cable (it's short and can't be swapped for a longer one)

title: Great performance
text:
EVGA ftw3 version runs super quiet. Can barely hear it run. At highest settings @ 6880 x 1440 resolution, it never runs hotter than 65c. As to whether 2080ti is worth it in general:

Increase in FPS performance- Too many people judge the 2080ti's merit on raw FPS numbers, saying its only x amount of percent greater in performance than the 1080ti. so its not worth it. But what they completely miss is that its not just about the raw numbers. Its about how those numbers translate into the EXPERIENCE of adding/using that component. The performance of the 2080ti is so much smoother, more effortless and frustration free, than the previous generation, that it was worth it for me to make the change.

Alernative Sli option- I tried 1080ti sli for about a month, it didnt affect the quality of my experience in a meaningful way. The presentation is still jittery and stuttering , making for a distracting experience. Support for SLI is inconsistent and it demands more power and space, creates alot more heat and noise. You can clearly see the poor quality of performance in side by side comparisons on youtube. Judge for yourself. Again, its not all about the FPS. A perfect analogy would be to cars- most high end races cars have respectable 0-60 mph speeds, but the experience and qualty of performance arent the same.

Price argument: Just because its expensive and someone cant afford it doesnt mean its a 1 star product. Check the quality, time and effort the reviewer put into the review and judge for yourself. It takes money, time and expensive R&D to make products such as these. Im not going to argue that its not expensive. It is. But consider that it beats two 1080ti SLI in quality of performance, then you realize it isnt. If you are salty that you cant afford it, try skipping some meals and dropping some vices and prioritize things differently. Seems everyone wants free things these days. I wonder if they would work without compensation.

Conclusion: Sure its expensive, but if you can afford it and you want quality performance, not just eye popping FPS numbers, which can be meaningless, get the 2080ti. Some just cant see the difference and thats fine. But for those who can afford it and have more discerning eyes, the upgrade is a must. My only complaint? It cant make poorly coded, inefficient games like Kingdom Come run better at the highest settings on a 6880 x 1440 setup. (Runs nearly every other game at the highest setting flawlessly at these high resolutions) Might have to wait for the next generation for that. Because of that and the "high" price it doesn't get a top recommendation but a very high recommendation.

title: Nice product
text:
This is my first drawing tablet so I can't compare it with others. I did do quite a bit of research prior to my purchase, so here are my thoughts. I haven't had any issues with it. I was able to familiarize myself with the device and draw/browse the web within five minutes of installing the driver.

I initially wanted a display tablet but decided against it. Display tablets require 3 cords instead of 1. And they are considerably more expensive. A lot of people complain about the disconnect with screenless tablets, but your cursor is tracked when the stylus is held above the tablet, so it is very easy to keep track of where you are. If you can use a mouse, you can use this.

I'm not a good artist, but my line art and writing quality when using this tablet is pretty comparable to pen and paper. Much better than trying to draw with a mouse.

Pressure sensitivity of the stylus is good. I feel like after watching a bunch of review videos, control and range of line thickness is more dependent on the software you use. Higher pressure count might allow more flexibility when configuring it to your taste in the driver.

The driver seems fine. I think the only thing missing is calibration and testing for stylus tilt. Speaking of tilt, I bought this tablet since it supports that feature, mostly out of curiosity. It works (tested in Expresii). It's a new enough tech I think a lot of software doesn't use it. So like pressure sensitivity, the software you use will be the weak link here. Tilt in general feels the least natural of features and will likely require some practice to master.

title: Logitech's Most Popular Wireless Mouse - Best Productivity - Even Gaming!
text:
I've been using Logitech mice ever since the company started pretty much. After all those crappy non-gaming mice that Microsoft were putting out back in the 90's, somebody had to step up! But if your old school like me, then you remember Logitech's logo back in the day. Turns out the company rebranded themselves to "Logi", following fears, that their company was considered a dinosaur by young folk. The re-branding's intention, is to make themselves seem hip as ever.

How many remember the Logitech MX1000 wireless laser gaming mouse? Over 15-years ago Logitech came out with that mouse, captured my heart forever. Used it for 7-years until the lithium battery died for good. Then I bought my first "G" mouse, the G700, back when the mice still were remanescent of the MX1000, just with added features and performance. Then the mice went total futuristic and overkill, when the G502 and G9 series came out lol.

The Logitech MX Master 3 Advanced, is literally one of the best mice out there. It still amazes me to this day, just how many features that they can pack, into a small space. The weight feels about the same as the old MX1000 and G700, so if you've used those mice before, then you will be used to it. The Master series has actually been around for several years now, and this is the 3rd generation mouse.

Because of the weight, this mouse does not glide over my cloth Hcman mouse pad, as easily as my Razer Deathadder Elite wired gaming mouse. However, the mouse pad was designed to allow a mouse tracking sensor, to have 100% precision in every micro-inch of movement. Wireless mice will glide easier over a plastic based mouse pad, however, the mouse will probably be less precise if you use one. So stick with a micro-fiber cloth mouse pad if you can.

This is a 7-button mouse, and as expected, there are many functions. Left Click, Middle Click, Right Click, Vertical Scroll, Forward Click, Backward Click, Productivity Button, Horizontal Scroll. Scroll Mode button adjusts the scroll wheel mode, clicky or smooth. On the bottom of the mouse is the ON/OFF switch, as well as the Bluetooth mode selector, and of course, the DARK FIELD sensor, that can track on literally everything, including your ham sandwich.

I bought this, so I would have a quality wireless mouse, for my tablet computer. Because it can be programmed for more then just 1-device at a time, I can also use this with my notebook computer. Its important to note however, Logitech software only works on Windows or MAC, there is no software support for Android. This mouse works perfectly with an Android tablet however, using Android standard drivers and functionality, built into the OS.

As soon as I turned the mouse on, the #1 mode began flashing. I searched for Bluetooth devices on my tablet, and immediately the mouse was discovered, and paired quickly. Reception is excellent, the cursor moved almost as smoothly as my wired Razer Dethadder Elite gaming mouse. If your somebody who does photoshop, or Adobe Premiere for production and editing work, you will love this mouse, plenty of sensitivity to get the job done.

Browsing the internet performance is very good as well. Other then the standard vertical scroll wheel that all modern mice have these days, I found myself also enjoying, the horizontal scroll wheel, which allowed me to scroll the pages left/right. This makes browsing the internet on a tablet much easier, and quicker. If you've been using your touch screen before, this mouse is going to be quite the upgrade for you!

Gaming performance is very good for a mouse that isn't technically rated to be meant for gaming. Unless your a competitive gamer, trying to reach the top ranks in COD, Battlefied, Fortnite, PubG, you don't need no 144 hertz G9! These MX Master 3 mice have more precision then the MX1000 had, its plenty for gaming IMO, and I did not have any problems.

I also do photoshop and video editing, but not professionally, and I find this mouse very easy to use. The ergonomics of this mouse are top notch, best I've seen! I find this mouse very comfortable to use. The mouse clicks are fairly strong, which provides tactile feedback. And the forward and back buttons, are thankfully not mushy like previous models, also very tactile. If you don't like loud mice, you might want to stay away, tactile feedback, means there is gonna be click noise.

Logitech seems to only have this mouse in either Graphite, or Mid-Grey. It would be nice if they came out with an pure Black version, as well as a Blue, and premium Red version. But like I said, they are catering to production artists more with this mouse then gamers. Still, Logitech should offer more custom options, it would get them more sales IMO.

If you don't want your mouse to look like a space ship however, and your not a super competitive gamer, you can avoid the G502 and the G9, and just go with the MX Master 3. In my opinion, its a fully featured mouse, with excellent precise control from the Dark Field sensor, excellent customisability of buttons through the driver software, and excellent ergonomics. Very well made mouse, and I am going to have to give it a solid 5 out of 5 stars!

title: Perfect card for a home-built FreeNAS storage server
text: High-performance, no-frills 8-port SAS controller. LSI boards are the gold standard for FreeNAS - well supported and reasonably affordable. This one only supports "IT" mode (no RAID), so I didn't have to mess around with re-flashing it to the best image for ZFS.  I swapped it into the PCIe slot on my motherboard, connected the two SAS-to-SATA breakout cables to the card (sold separately), and connected my new drive array. FreeNAS booted up and immediately recognized the controller and all 8 attached drives (they map as /dev/sd<num>, i.e. generic SCSI drives). Performance so far has been great. I run my ZFS pool with encryption at rest (via GELI), so I think the I/O bottleneck right now is the AES-NI performance of my Core i3 CPU. That said, I can sustain over 100MB/s write throughput without issue, and that's more than good enough for my needs.

title: For Dell Latitude E5470 Must Have Updated Bios
text:
I bought this for a ram upgrade to a refurbished Dell Latitude E5470. Crucial's website guaranteed compatibility and linked to Amazon for purchase. Initially, the Dell would not boot or post after installation and diagnostic flashing light pattern indicated "invalid ram". Turns out the Dell refurb facility had not updated the bios to the most recent version available; it came with version 1.18.6. After updating the bios to the most recent version(1.21.6), everything worked as it should. 17 hours and 4 complete passes with memtest showed no errors.
Moral of the story - if you're having issues with what should be compatible ram, check for bios updates. Also, don't trust a refurbed Dell to have an up to date bios.

title: Love so far... Update 11/28

The Mesh died on me today. No matter what I do, the wi-fi will not work. I bought this in April 2020, so I got 7 months out of it. Looking at some of the reviews it appears several have crashed around 6 months. I guess the old adage of "you get what you pay for" applies here, even though my last wireless router was a TP-Link that I paid 70$ for and got 5 years out of it.
I liked it while it was working but to not even get a year out of this device is unacceptable!

Disclaimer: I am an IT professional of 25+ years.
I have a 4000 sq. ft home, and for the first time in 15 years I have total coverage in every room including my two attached garages! Setup was very easy for me. You must install an app for your phone, and setup is done through there. Personally, I don't like that, but that is the IT security guy in me.
I ended up putting the main router cube in the center of the house downstairs. I put another in the downstairs garage about 35 feet from the main one. The other one I put upstairs in the master bedroom since that is where the main TV is and where laptops are used the most. WHAM! Complete coverage. I have coverage in every part of my yard which is about 1/3 of an acre lot.
Now what I don’t like.
• I don't like the limited features far as there isn't any advanced firewall features that are with most home routers. You are trusting this company that the network is secure out of the box. That said, I put mine behind a router to add an extra layer of security. For the IT challenged it isn’t hard to do, and any of your handy self-appointed IT family members can help you. 😊
• It is a 100 percent made in and sold by some Chinese company I have never heard of. They sell other miscellaneous items. I bought it because it was cheaper than all the other mesh type networks being offered. If it fails, I will replace it.
So, that’s it. In a nutshell it does what it is supposed to do. Its been in use for a couple of weeks without any disruptions in service of any kind. I hope that continues.
Feel free to ask any questions you may have.
Stay safe!

title: Beware Onboard Software
text:
I lost 100 hours of work and important project files because of this device. How?

The pSSD (what the device will call itself when you first plug it in to a computer) comes with a data vault that offers some privacy protection, which is great when having to pass the hardware around a company or group. HOWEVER, if you sync the folder to a desktop folder for automation on backing up files within the existing software that comes with the pSSD OR the "upgrade" 3rd party software that is available then you risk a massive chance of losing all your files during a sync.

Why and how?

For whatever reason, the automation backup system PURGES all your files within the sync folder on your desktop before backing them up on the pSSD, so if you cancel the sync or the sync crashes, which is often because the device burns itself out within minutes, you will lose everything in that folder besides the folder names themselves because it first and foremost purges the original files while doing the backup.

I cannot stress this enough. If you are going to use this device then DO NOT use the software on the device itself. Reformat the pSSD, purge it or do whatever you need to so you don't have to deal with their attached software.

That said, aside from the volume of the beeps, the product is good and well made.

Pros:
It’s pretty much top-of-the-line bone conducting headphones.
Battery life is fine
It’s very lightweight. After awhile you forget you’re wearing them. They don’t squeeze your head or anything.

Cons:
Aforementioned very loud beeps
Proprietary charger connector
Only pairs with one Bluetooth device at a time.

If you’ve never used these sorts of headphones before, be aware that you don’t get deep bass, the sound quality compared to good earbuds is worse, but that is unavoidable. No bone conducting headphones will do deep bass.

You can use earplugs (provided) which will actually make them sound better. It’s a trade off of course, because you probably want these headphones because you need environmental noises to come through.

title: Excellent for light use, not much more.
text:
TL;DR: At the price this tablet goes for, it's an awesome option for simple tasks like reading, streaming video, light gaming, and other general use apps - or for someone buying a first tablet for themselves or a loved one. However, it struggles where higher-end tablets do not, so it's not for those who are looking for an everyday or heavy-use tablet.

The Pros? It has video quality to match tablets twice it's price. It also comes with a screen protector pre-installed, which I think is extremely thoughtful of the company. The tablet has no trouble at all keeping up with basic use, even once several apps are running at once. Battery life is also not much of a concern; I don't use it every day, but I've yet to complain that it's dying too quickly.

The Cons? The touch sensitivity is not as accurate as it should be, which leads to problems with precise input. It also seems to be running a version of Android that isn't made for it; the drop menu is wildly undersized, and I - a young adult with decent vision - had to enlarge *everything* in the Accessibility settings to get things comfortable. The speakers have decent quality, but not very strong.

My most noted flaw: Wireless capabilities are not good. Updates take a little too long to update, YouTube takes a little too long to buffer, Skype calls are frequently out of sync and lose resolution, and cloud gaming with apps like Stadia work for a few minutes...then, don't. My phone can do these tasks easily on the same network, which suggests the tablet's internet capabilities are just subpar.

Still, at this price, this is not meant to be a world-beater tablet. It's an excellent light-use or beginner tablet at an unbeatable price. For frequent or intensive tablet users, though, it may not suit your needs.

One other note is that because this is USB 2.0 it can only achieve the full frame rate with compressed H.264 video. If you want uncompressed video at 30+ FPS, you’ll need a USB 3.0 camera, which will be significantly more expensive. If your video has a weird greenish tint or a low frame rate, it’s because because you’re using a different codec.

The main cross-platform application for changing camera settings (among other things) is Streamlabs OBS. If you’re just looking to use this with Zoom, you can find something more lightweight on the Mac App Store (search “uvc”) or wherever Windows users find such things. On Linux you can use guvcview for basic settings. There are also some extremely basic PTZ controls built into the menu system, but they may not be the most convenient for you.

title: Terrible Design -- Only use with skinny wire
text:
Let's eliminate one possible confusion up front: the intent of the product is to put spade terminations on speaker wire. This has nothing to do with banana plugs -- you can't insert banana plugs into the back of them.

Look at the pictures in the Amazon listing. Look at the one that shows the three separate parts of a connector. In the middle you see a gold-colored cylinder with two sets of threads on it. What the picture (inexcusably) doesn't show is that there are two set-screws on the cylinder. That would be okay except for one problem: if you unscrew the set screws enough to get more than an 18AWG stranded wire in, the outer, silver-colored cylinder will not fit over the set-screws.

This leaves us with two options:
1. Use a skinny wire
2. Don't use the silver-colored outer cylinder

If you go with option 2, you can't attach an additional spade using the "female spade plug connection."

There is a third option: don't buy this product.

Nakamichi is one of the earlier and more respected Japanese audio brands. Nak didn't make these; they were made in China. It appears that they were originally branded "Wakaka." Nak is really Wak, I guess.

title: At this price, can't beat it.
text:
[[VIDEOID:2b91ec8d218cc44cc0349490c89f2741]] I have been a user of both Nikon and Canon over the past 3-4 years and made the switch to sony in August of 2017. The a7iii is by far the best camera I have used on these three platforms. I previously owned and still use the Sony a6300 which was great for a budget camera but had tons of issues for someone who shoots professionally. I primarily shoot weddings and sports but also do commercial level work on the side. The photos I have provided are my first test of the a7iii in a somewhat warm climate doing both photo and video.

Improved Features:
1. IN CAMERA PROXIES... no one talks about this on youtube!!
2. dual card recording ability, dual writing ability
3. HLG color space, no overheating
4. Bright and Beautiful monitor, focus peaking, customizable buttons, uncompressed RAW photo capability, a large buffer depending on card size, and great autofocus with eye AF and face tracking... plus better "color science." Color science means absolutely nothing unless you are delivering a final image or video straight out of the camera, its all subjective and if you want Accurate colors Sony is the way to go. I could rant for pages about "color science."
5. Headphone Jack... Monitoring external audio is absolutely important if you are running wireless mics. I will use this to monitor my wedding ceremony Audio.

Things that could be improved:
1. The EVF is not calibrated color wise to match the display screen on the back of the camera... not a huge deal for video but it can get annoying for photo. Know your settings well enough to get you close in photos, and the RAW capabilities in Lightroom will give you some leeway.
2. No face tracking while using an external recorder AND recording in Camera. If you record solely on the external recorder you can still retain face tracking which is not a huge deal, there is an option in the settings but it turns the external screen black.
3. only 1 UHS-II slot. I would love to see two of them.
4. no 10-bit color depth... this is probably coming on the a7siii which I understand, but it would be incredible to get a firmware update on the a7iii, a7riii, and a9 to allow 10-bit color, making SLOG and HLG way easier to expose for and work with in post. Also, it allows creators to keep their a7iii and purchase an a7siii to match perfectly with it.
5. The shutter button is a little spongy... not a huge complaint here because I am being rather critical

The a7iii has improved almost all of the issues thus far I have experienced with Sony APS-C Cameras. In my example photos and videos, I used the 70-200 f/2.8 GM (incredible lens). The a7iii lasted 4.5 hours of continuous video and photo shooting to two different SD cards with a completely bright viewfinder and screen with 20% battery to spare... something I could only dream of on the 6300. This is absolutely a professional camera and is reasonably priced for the features it has.

if you are looking for a prosumer camera with pro features... you can't go wrong with the a7iii. It definitely is not a cinema camera but will absolutely serve me well until I need to upgrade in the future for both photo and video.

title: 4.5 Star. Great versatile tripod.
text:
Before getting this tripod I used a Mefoto Roadtrip Tripod for 5 years. Which I really enjoy, and trust using. These are my thoughts on the tripod after using it for a 2-3 weeks now. I mostly do landscape and cityscape photography professionally.
This is a very versatile tripod, with a good price.
Pros:
Gets very tall.
Gets very low with included short column.
The column pivots which can be very useful for macro and product photography.
Ballhead is good. No shifting when locking it down.
The finish is good.
The leg locks/latches are spring loaded which nicer than than push pull ones.
It is sturdy tripod
The legs lock without issue.
For the size of tripod it is not heavy.
comes with carry bag and accessories.
Cons but not deal breakers:
The center column is not locked in place. When you tighten down the center column lock you can still turn the column. It takes a bit of force, so it's not like the wind will turn the center column when tightened down. Just something to be aware of.
The column nut can get a little sticky sometimes. I am hoping that will go away in the time.
It would be awesome if the center column nut was more like the one on the roadtrip tripod.
I wish there was a softer, gripping material on the ballhead lock.
I plan on leaving the short column on most of the time so I will be putting a drop of breakable lock tight on the bolt that holds the ballhead to the center column.
When the short column is placed on the tripod. The locking plate gets pinched between the legs, not allowing the legs to fully close, so I replaced the locking plate with a smaller one.
Other than those minor issues, the tripod is great.

title: Way beyond my expectations.
text:
I'm a big Bose fan, but when I was looking for a speaker that I could use on my Kayak, I didn't want to pay the Bose price because let's face it, Bose is pricey and sound quality isn't my main concern on my Kayak. So I took a shot on this Tribit Stormbox Micro. I'd been seeing the Tribit stuff for a while and was intrigued. When I bought the Stormbox Micro, it was on sale for less than half of the Bose micro speaker.

When I pulled it out of the box, I was surprised that it looked and felt a higher quality than I expected. I synced it with my phone easily without looking at the directions. When I started playing music with it, I was immediately surprised by the sound. I was sitting next to the unit and could feel the bass coming out of the bottom of the speaker. I was floored by the fullness of the sound. I have a bose soundlink in my office that I have loved for a while, this Stormbox offered a surprisingly similar tone with comparable bass even at half the size. When I cranked it up, the sound was far louder than I expected and it was still articulate without distorting.

I took it on the Kayak and kept it at a very low volume so that I was not blasting my music for other kayakers and fishermen to hear. I could clearly hear the speaker with great sound while the volume was at 10-20% on my phone, it was still very articulate even at a low volume. When I returned home from about 4 hours of fishing, the battery was still well over 80% full.

I am very excited about the great product at this price. I'd be surprised if the Bose or UE micro speakers sound this great, and I personally know that the most portable JBL speaker sounds terribly weak compared to the Stormbox. I'd recommend 100%.

*Also, just a note. You will notice a big Bass difference depending on what kind of surface this speaker is sitting on. If I put this unit on my desk, the bass is huge and bold. Strapped on to my backpack the bass sound is warmer, but still very full.

title: Worth the Upgrade from Fenix 3!
text:
this is my third garmin watch as i have graduated from one to the next with latest being the fenix 3. the differences between the two is big enough for me to sink in $600 for this watch. for me, the most important functionalities are battery life on gps, music, and wrist based hr monitoring....but it offers so much more!!! i really like the design of this watch. it is a lot lighter than the fenix and slimmer. fenix was not a watch that i could wear to sleep but this forerunner makes it easy for me. there are so many added features since the fenix 3 that i feel like a kid in a candy store. although not needed, i added my credit card to the watch...so if you want to go on a shopping spree, all you have to do is lift my watch!😂 syncing my airpods 2 was a breeze. have i mentioned that this watch is awesome! the built in heart rate monitor surpasses my expectations. although the wrist type monitors are not as accurate as a chest strap, i am willing to give up that accuracy for something that puts me in the general neighborhood of how my ticker is doing. it certainly does that! as far as the battery life claim of 36hours....i have not had a chance to test that yet but will have a chance toward the end of this year. generally, i can get pretty close to the number that garmin publishes but i do have to turn off almost everything to achieve that number. although i could have continue to charge the watch on the run believe it or not, my mind was too foggy in survival mode of a 100 mile run to want to worry about that. i really like the layout of the user interface on this watch. if you are coming from a garmin watch, it is similar and the learning curve is not too steep. i was able to navigate it within a few hours for the most part. i know someone stated in a review they didn't like the buttons....i love the buttons! they are responsive and get me from me place to another quickly. it is true that not as much pressure is required to do that but that is my preference. the display is very very good. it is crisp and bright. oh....the watch face is very nice. one of the things that i didn't like about the fenix was that i could never get the second hand to move like an analog watch. this one does. as far as fit, it feels so light on my wrist that i noticed it for the first day but now is just there. overall, i love the added functionalities of thhhis watch and will come back to provide a more in depth review once i have a chance to swim, bike and run with it. first impression is that this is a solid well bought out watch with everything i need! highly recommend!

8/10/2019
i have had this watch now for about two weeks. it is awesome. here are some things that i have done with it that i haven't done previously:
- sync my apple airpods and a generic earbuds to the watch. both worked although the apple airpods worked more flawlessly.
- loaded spotify and my music onto the watch. very easy to do.
- the built in hr monitor is awesome! i don't even wear my strap anymore....it gives me a rash so glad to be rid of it!
- i love all the health readings! it is awesome!
- i love the strength app. it actually counts your sets and reps. still has a little bit of work to do but pretty cool.
- i got all my external devices like hr strap, foot pod and power meter connected to the watch
- it uses about 15% per day of battery although i have everything turned on. once i am in race mode i will turn everything off to save on battery
- i bought a couple of extra cables. they charged the watch pretty well.
- i love the voice alerts while running. it gives pace distance and lactate readings
- the watch analog face is pretty good. i especially like the red second hand.. it does eat a little more battery.
- gps is quick to sync!
- the apps and widgets are awesome. well thought out.

that's all i have for now as i am training for 100 miler and hasn't had a chance to swim or bike. i am pretty sure i won't be disappointed there either. will update once i log some distance for those activities.

title: Easy Install
text:
This battery seems to be working perfectly, but I'm reserving giving stars on the Battery Life section until more time has passed. So far, so good for the battery itself. If you want to read on, I've included some general tips.

I was not happy when I realized long ago that I did not have an easily-removable battery in my HP Pavilion. This was even more frustrating when, after only two years, the battery was completely useless. I was glad to find a replacement. This kit comes with minimal tools to get the job done. I suggest anybody who sets out to replace an internal battery like this get a good tool kit with things to pry your case open without damaging things.

If you don't have prior experience, it's best to look for instructional videos for your machine. Rule #1 is to always ground yourself when you're working on your machine. Another important thing is, there are often hidden screws. I found mine under the rubber "feet", which I had to re-affix.

Another interesting thing I noticed is that the hard drive ribbon/connector runs underneath my battery, to help hold it in place. When I removed my battery, the ribbon popped up, and I had to re-attach the hard drive to the board. So... watch out for the "3D of things" when you start taking things apart so you assemble things properly.

One more important thing... Before you screw the case back on, ensure your work is complete. Carefully check to see that your machine boots up properly. Once you shut back down properly, you can put the casing back on.

title: The best banana plug I've used so far.
text:
Anyone having used banana plugs for speaker connections know the convenience it brings to the table while maintaining a secure connection and protecting the bare wire, it also makes it easy to move or upgrade speakers/receivers/amps without much hassle. I've used monoprice closed screw type banana plugs from the get go, while they offer good connection using it with a 12 awg speaker cable (I've used 12awg monoprice speaker cables for my entire installation including a 300ft run of Amazon basic 12awg speaker cable too) could be a little tedious especially if the speaker wire strands get in between the threadings of the banana plug, which they inevitably do get in between unless your made the perfect cut.

The FosPower banana plugs were a pleasure to use. They made installation a breeze.. strip the wires to length insert them into the plugs, secure them with the two screws, which I tightened fairly tight without issues, insert the color coded covers and your done.

These banana plugs are extra tight to get into the binding posts of the speakers and receiver and I don't see that as a negative point but as a positive one as they give you the confidence of a very good and secure connection.

title: GE vs Noopel vs Sabre window alarms
text:
Summary: Noopel & GE recommend, Sabre DON’T recommend.

I live in a mixed urban neighborhood and my new apartment has more windows such I shopped for additional alarms to augment the Sabre & GE brands I already had buying first more Sabres, then because the Sabre units performed badly I purchased several Noopel units.

I’ll start with Sabre Wireless Home Security Alarm as I have the most of these. I purchased them on the basis of Amazon reviews at two intervals a year apart such I have experience with them. I found them WEAK & VARIABLE. Even on the stronger units the alert isn’t enough to wake me if sleeping, many units have such a weak alarm that I might not hear it in another room with the TV on.

Sabre’s weakness prompted me to return to Amazon for an alternative and I bought Noopel Magnetic Entry Sensor as a replacement. BIG difference, these you can hear at a level likely to chase an intruder off and alert the neighbors to turn on their lights. I liked these enough that I repurchased more as Sabre replacements.

GE Personal Security Alarm – Earlier I had purchased a pack of GE’s from Amazon and have over a year’s experience with them and would recommend. They still have a loud shriek and would serve their purpose to scare an intruder and wake you to the danger.

ON/Off placement. The 3 brands differ in where they locate the on/off switch with Noopel and GE placing theirs on the outside for easy access. Sabre locates their switch on the INSIDE such you must take the battery cover off to access the switch – both awkward and easy to lose your batteries. The Noopel & GE placement is superior in my judgment.

Overall I’m disappointed in the Sabre’s I bought. In fairness I tried new batteries and purchased more than one set a full year apart – no volume, no deterrent. Noopel is new and I can’t comment on longevity, but out of the package – they WORK. GE I have long experience and they have both better design & better performance than Sabre.

title: Gaming Laptop is No Longer a Gimmick
text:
I used to be the person who thinks a gaming laptop is unpractical and waste of money. It's bulky, heavy, and it will probably run out of battery 2hr after being unplugged from the outlet. Therefore, I have always done my PC gaming on desktop only.

However, since late 2018 when lots of thin & light gaming laptop with GTX1070/1080 MAX-Q started to show up in the market, I started to see lots of rave reviews on this new category of laptops which look, feel, and weigh like a ordinary laptop but with graphical power of a desktop.

After spending a few months reading reviews and waiting for the new products to launch, I finally pulled the trigger on the MSI GS65 Stealth-007 with RTX2060. I have been using this laptop for about a week now, and I have to say it has shattered all my impressions on laptops.

I have been playing the "Shadow of the Tomb Raider" on this laptop, and the game runs buttery smooth. It is simply an engineer marvel where a 4lb laptop can run AAA game with ease. The heat dissipation on this laptop is great even it is only 1.8mm in thickness. It has more heat pipes and upgraded fan design compared to the 2018 model. I went a step further and undervolt the CPU, and this laptop experience no thermal throttling issue during my gaming sessions.

The 144Hz screen is gorgeous to look at when the bezel is almost non-existent. When playing games at 1080p, the frame rate can easily top 90fps on this machine, and that 144Hz screen will make you appreciate how smooth the on screen motion is.

I will mostly used this at home connected to an outlet, but this thing can easily last 6 hours (web surfing, steaming video) on battery when unplugged. It uses Nvida Optimus Technology to automatically switch over to integrated graphics to conserve battery power. Since this is only weighs a bit more than 4lb, I probably will take this to places while on the go.

I am literally selling off my desktop components on eBay right now. This has become my desktop replacement, and it will serve me well for at least the next 5 years.

title: These are NOT 2800mAh batteries as claimed
text:
For the last 7 years I bought Eneloop batteries but the ones I bought in 2012 finally seemed like they were at end of life as it seemed they weren't lasting as long as they once did. So after looking at a bunch of different batteries I decided on these as an acceptable choice given the claim of 2800mAh.

Well these batteries are NOT 2800mAh as claimed. I purchased a charger which shows you the input of the batteries as well as the voltage and I have never been able to get more than 2200mAh into any of these batteries. They top out at around 1.47 volts like every other rechargeable I have. (The Duracell ones I have recharge to about 2600mAh.) To make sure I am depleting them I even place the batteries into a flashlight and use them until the light stops working. Generally that is around 1.16 volts. I do this after they go dead in my other devices, like an xBox controller.

So yes, you get a bunch of batteries for not a lot of cash, but they aren't as good as claimed. My 2012 Eneloop batteries are still putting out 2000mAh and the Duracell batteries at 2600 as said before. If you want good rechargeable performance, but the good Duracell batteries, and if you want long lifespan, buy the Eneloop batteries. Skip these.

title: Yellow banding/Discoloration
text:
[[VIDEOID:92b8748d4aa7da6351d6460478a1ee63]] Let me start by saying the display is beautiful and has so much potential.

Unfortunately, I ended up with two defective displays in a row.

The first display, had a strong yellow oval discoloration in the center and less pronounced yellow banding elsewhere on the display. See the video, I'm circling the area in red. It may be difficult to see in the video, but it was extremely visible in the person, making doing color accurate work impossible.

The second display arrived with one of the buttons on the top of the display stuck in the downward position making it impossible to adjust the color calibration settings.

The second display also had the yellow discoloration/banding, much less pronounced than the first one, but still present.

I've read on other sites that this discoloration can be an issue with other models of Huion displays after a few months, which is worrisome.

I really wanted this pen display to work out, so much so that I bought two hoping that I was just unlucky with the first one.

A couple other minor things; I do wish they could squeeze 2560x1440 into such a large display as the pixels are a bit visible at 1920x1080. Not overwhelmingly so, but would also be nice to have a bit more interface real estate for menus as well.

It's nice the pen has tilt support, but it would also be great if they could also implement brush rotation option similar to Wacom's Art Pen, but that's nitpicking.

I already have the Wacom Cintiq 16 and I was hoping this would be a replacement because the contrast/color and overall screen quality on the Wacom 16 is lacking, to be expected on an entry level Cintiq.

Hopefully Huion can iron out some of these issues in future updates at which point they will officially be a Wacom killer.

title: Thick braiding, spam for reviews, can’t confirm longevity.
text: It’s been less than a month but iVanky staff have already contacted me twice pestering me for a a review and for that, I left out one star. If you check my history, I generally review everything I purchase but usually give it a few months of use before I make a genuine review. I got the gray/black version because it was more neutral and fit my space better, however if I could have I would’ve chosen the red/black braiding. The braiding itself is very thick which to a novice, would indicate that the cable/copper is of high quality, however this is exactly the reason I’m concerned that may not be the case. Generally when manufacturers do stuff like that, it’s to hide something else, such as in this case, potentially cheap copper or the bare minimum AWG wire size for DP. That being said, I’ve been using the cable to power my Dell 24 inch, QHD (2k), 165hz/1ms, G-Sync monitor and so far I’ve had no issues, at least none that point towards the cable itself. There have been blurring issues but I believe that to be a scaling issue between windows 10, QHD, and 24 inch panel size, and not the display port cable. All in all, for $10 I would probably purchase again assuming this cable lasts, but I cannot condone the spam mail for reviews. Let it be known that if you purchase from iVanky, they will spam you for reviews on your purchase.

My only (minor) complaint is that they offer a 14H format, which should give you something like
00000013579acf
even if only some digits of the ID are read. The unit I received does have a configuration box on the bottom (in Chinese characters) which is not 8H and is checked. It does not, however, return in 14H format but in 8H format. To use the above example:

title: Al's is great, but Realize what this is
text:
The seller of this kit, Al's Variety in my case, performed perfectly; everything promised was in the package, which was shipped quickly. All items were as described. Note that this is effectively an "open box" item - the lens which is in the kit is removed, to be sold separately I presume. But the camera body and everything else was new as promised. The Nikon warranty certificate was included.

Nikon, however, does not receive such high marks. I studied some online (non-Amazon) reviews and decided this camera should be ok. I wrongly concluded that it was not a "beginner's" DSLR, but as others have noted here, that is what it is. My research was inadequate or incomplete: what I did not realize: 1) Many of the online reviews are just fawning 3rd party product promotions - none that I found mentioned that: 2) This model is the bottom of the in-production Nikon DSLR line from what I can tell 3) If there is any metal in the body beyond the lens mount, it is imperceptible - the whole thing appears to be plastic - hence the very light weight 4) The dinky printed manual is only a few pages and covers not much more than how to attach a lens and reach the settings menu 5) My main beef, and the reason I returned this - the "improved" button layout on the back is terrible IMO, making the efficient 2-thumbs operation of the earlier models impossible, and 6) More beef - the buttons are <i>smaller</i> than those on the D40 I wanted to replace, making them difficult to operate reliably, especially the navigation rocker and the OK button. For 4 X the price of an ASUS phone that takes pretty decent pictures I expected a better product from Nikon.

title: A unique high-end configuration with a fantastic screen; This is A LOT of laptop for the money
text:
OK, let's start with this: as of 5/10/20, this laptop is configured in such a way that isn't even offered on HP's own website. First, on HP's website, you can't get this 4K AMOLED Super Black display with the nVidia RTX 2060; you have to spend $350 more for the RTX 2070 to get this screen. Second, to get the maxed out 32GB's of DDR4 RAM, you have to spend $200.00 as an upgrade. Third, add another $200 to get the full 1TB NVMe M2 SSD drive. Last, this laptop comes with Windows 10 Pro, which isn't even available on HP's Omen configuration tool. Add it all up and you're spending over $2200 from HP direct. So, yes, this is a very unique laptop configuration at a very, VERY good price!

But what kind of performance and quality are you getting here? In short, quite a lot of both! On the performance side, the 9th Generation Intel Core i7 9750H is a huge improvement over the previous i7 CPUs because this CPU now sports 6 cores/12 threads, which makes running the content creation/editing software this laptop was meant for extremely satisfying. Applications like Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop really scale well to having all these cores and I can truly feel that am getting desktop-levels of performance here. From a graphics standpoint, the nVidia RTX 2060 offers everything you could need from a media creation/editing perspective, while giving very good gaming performance. I play mostly RTS games like Diablo, Civilization, Tropico, etc. and those games all auto-configure at "High" or better settings with the RTX 2060. I did dabble with Metro Exodus to check on the 2060's Ray Tracing and first-shooter performance and found that it does suffer a lot at 4K resolutions...much better to play at 1080 with Medium to High settings. However, this is in-line with the RTX 2060's desktop performance. No complaints...

The real star of this laptop is the screen. It's a gorgeous 4K AMOLED panel that really stands out, not just for all those super, high-resolution pixels, but for the incredibly vibrant colors and drop-dead absolute blacks. There is zero light bleed like you would get from a laptop LED panel, not matter how good it is. Color accuracy is decent, more accurate on the RGB scale versus the Adobe color scale. As a photography enthusiast, I do miss having a completely accurate Adobe scale panel, but the rest of this screen's specs are just too good to ignore...it's a fantastic display and worth every penny at this price point.

The rest of the Omen 15's components are really very good: the keyboard is a fully lit, four-zone affair, with good, solid key feel and travel. Storage is a speedy and generous 1TB NVMe drive, which leaves an open 2.5 HD "slot" for future expansion. The trackpad is good as well, but I use a trackball mouse most of the time. On board adware is kept to a minimum (thankfully) and the included HP applications are (mostly) very helpful and useful, especially the Omen Command Center app which allows you to monitor, configure and control many of the laptop's settings and setup usage profiles. Build quality is tops...I'm a HUGE fan of HP's Envy and Specter high-end laptops and this Omen is every bit as good. It's not a lightweight option (it's really hard to find a piece of plastic on this thing), but you don't get any flex out of it, either. It's very solid...

Negatives? There are a few. If you want a laptop strictly/mainly for gaming, I'd probably go with a RTX 2070 to make Ray Tracing and High/Ultra settings more viable. Also, 4K screens aren't the best gaming options right now as well...1080 HD screens are much more suitable for right now. Also, this screen tops out at 60 Hertz, where 144/240 Hz screens give you a better gaming experience. The battery life is not great, however, it is in-line with having the 4K/RTX 2060 combo., not to mention that the 9th gen i7 now sports 6 cores. That's a lot of power draw...

So, all-in-all? A real powerhouse of a laptop for the media professional that doesn't want to give up too when it's game time. But what really strikes me here is the value: configured as-is from Amazon, you are getting a laptop at a price that HP doesn't offer...period. For all specs this thing has, it really is a great buy!

title: Simple AND it works! Poorly documented wired backhaul works great!
text:
My previous WiFi setup was a collection of MikroTik access points. I spent hours learning just to get them up to work at all and I was never really satisfied with their performance. One of those AP failed and I had had enough. I wanted something simpler to setup that would actually work. I had setup one of the AmpliFi HD systems for someone else previously and liked it, but the form factor of the mesh points and lack of wired backhaul capability made it not very good for my needs.

Enter the Amplifi Instant. The secret to this product line is NEVER to buy the kit with the router and mesh point. For roughly the same price, you can buy two routers instead and get very useful wired backhaul capability along with other configuration flexibility and a display. The bundled mesh points are hard coded to the router and you cannot repurpose them or use them with a different router. With two routers, you can build a system that works like a more professional Unifi setup and that does not have this limitation.

I have FiOS and use their router since it is basically required for the TV and other features to work unless you want to get into some complicated workarounds. I have the WiFi on the FiOS router turned off and one of the LAN ports goes to a switch that has all my network equipment plugged into it.

I configured the Amplifi system by starting with one router with its WAN port connected to my switch. With the app, I was easily able to setup this first router and put it into bridge mode since I only wanted it to act as an access point. Then, I powered up the second router which was automatically detected and I used the app to change it to act as a mesh point. I flipped the setting for wired backhaul and moved it to a far away part of my house where I have ethernet run back to the switch and connected that to its WAN port. It came up in wired backhaul mode and happily connected through my switch. There is very poor wireless signal due to a lot of masonry walls beteween the location where the router and router turned mesh point are located so this works quite well. I also was able to use the LAN port on the router turned mesh point to connect a Roku device and that worked without any config.

The wired backhaul and ability to loop through and connect a LAN device at the same time are two key features which are poorly documented but work great.

The wifi signal from this setup has been worlds better than what I had with the mikrotik devices. Even at low signal strength (1-2 bars on connected devices) the signal is stable instead of randomly disconnecting. It even works outside for my WiFI surveillance camera and the PC in my detached garage. I'm very happy with it so far and it has been very stable. Plus, the setup could not have been any easier. It really does what it says and more.

title: No Ability To Change Trackpad Scroll Direction - Trackpad A Disappointment
text:
The two finger scroll direction on Mac is stuck in the natural direction regardless of what your actual computer settings are.

My MacBook Pro trackpad is set to the opposite scroll pattern but despite this setting this Arteck keyboard’s trackpad only two finger scrolls in the natural direction.

For someone who HATES this scroll direction and has never used it on any trackpad this is totally unsettling and obnoxious, and makes using this thing’s trackpad a real headache.

It would have been really good to know this before buying. Anyone who cares about this should be warned.

Also the buttons for the trackpad are a bit cheap and unreliable/difficult to control.

Otherwise the keyboard part itself is nice and well made, heavy metal, but unfortunately the built in trackpad is almost the whole reason I bought this so it’s pretty much a deal breaker for me. If the company were to reach out and tell me how to fix the scroll issue - if it’s possible - then it’d be a much better review but as I’ve tried everything I don’t think it is.

Just wanted to let ppl know.

title: Decent OTA DVR.
text:
Long time TiVo user. Only had this running one night so far.
1st, the power cord is extremely short. Other devices in the same location reach fine. This hangs like a clothes line.
The picture is a tiny bit soft compared to the TiVo.
The audio is lower. Say you were use to a certain number level, you must go up from there quite a bit.
If you have some channels that come in only certain times of the day, you need to rescan. This may cause you to lose other channels. It needs a "scan for new channels", so you can add to the list instead of a full scan.
Automatic commercial skip seems to work.
You do have to wait until it states it's ready for the automatic skip.
Will need more time to evaluate.

** Update:
Automatic commercial skip is a bit buggy. It is a beta though.

Guide data was missing for 2 channels and wrong on one. Customer service seems responsive. The 2 channels have been fixed, but the 3rd is not updated. Customer service requested to log into my device. Some sort of reset required.

Update: Found the guide data issue is on their provider's end (Gracenote). Going directly to Gracenote showed the same inaccurate information. Unfortunately I'm locked to an arrogant customer service representative who refuses to forward the lineup issue as what was done for the previous channel guide info. Telling me straight up he will not help me unless I reset my Tablo to allow them login and see that my lineup is incorrect. I have sent them screenshots of both my guide and the guide at Gracenote for proof. So like most companies, expect to waste time doing pointless troubleshooting to appease those who don't know what they're doing to eventually have it forwarded to a ticket system.

**Update Nov2019**
Guide data has been good. Commercial skip is still buggy, but love it when it works. Sold most of my TiVo hardware at this point.

title: Battery issues
text:
This is only a partial review. Some have complained about the radio eating batteries, so I believe that is true. Eaton said they should last 75 hours at a moderate volume level. I believe that also. The difference seems to be earphones vs. speaker. If you adjust the speaker to a moderate level and plug in the earphones, the earphones are painfully loud. My conclusion: at moderate earphone level the batteries should last a long time, while at moderate speaker level (the speaker is 1¾ inches in diameter) battery drain is much higher.
As for the user complaining that the dial light stays on, thereby draining the batteries continuously, this should not occur; however, this also happened to me one time, so this can happen (the light should stay on no longer than 30 seconds). My solution: I "reset" the computer by taking out and putting back in one of the batteries. That solved the problem and it hasn't recurred again so far, but if it does I'll reset it again.
For those who think a lock button isn't as safe as a lock switch, please note that the lock button needs to be long pressed to unlock, plus if you keep the "leather" case on when it's in your luggage or your pocket, it makes it pretty impossible to press the lock button at all.
Personally, I don't like the lack of memory settings, but as I only listen to a couple of FM stations it is at worst a minor annoyance. Those stations are strong enough that I don't need to use the whip antenna at all, or occasionally less than an inch of it.

title: Great carry-around camera, but location / phone software is horrid!
text:
Before we get into the review; I'll first provide you with a tip you'll probably overlook in the manual if you don't study every page. For maximum longevity, Fuji recommends keeping the batteries charged to a 50% level when in storage, NOT fully charged.

Now, to set my review's perspective properly, I'll say that my primary camera is a Sony A9, and Canon 5D3 before becoming frustrated with the Canon ecosystem. I'd often carry the A9 with 35mm non-GM lens, but it's certainly not the lightest camera around and I'd been longing for something a bit easier to take in more casual or outdoor settings, especially ski trips.

I debated this camera, the Sony RX1R II, and Leica Q. Obviously those latter two are dramatically more expensive, but cost was not really a consideration. I ultimately decided on the Fuji. The Sony is small, but you're basically paying for a great sensor in a piece of garbage that is six years out of date, has no battery life, and has never had a firmware update. The Leica checked all the boxes but had been out long enough I was worried a new version was on the horizon; two months after buying the Fuji the Q2 comes out, so guess I was right. I also didn't want to buy the Leica before seeing what the upcoming Zeiss Zx1 brings to market.

Where this camera shines is having all the typical features, knobs, buttons, of a real camera, records in raw, can do bracketed shots (but won't merge them in camera), and has great picture quality for the price. The battery life is surprisingly good, even in the cold. My Sony A9 actually ground to a halt in sub-20F temps (shutter release began reacting with 1/2 second delay) while the Fuji kept going fine.

The area where I'd call this camera average is the auto focus speed, particularly subject/eye tracking. If you're used to a Sony A7/A9 mirrorless, this is nowhere near that kind of speed, so just prepare yourself accordingly.

Where this camera really pisses me off is the lack of GPS receiver for location, and the massively disappointing phone app in general. The missing GPS receiver would not bother me so much if their method of 'solving' that problem was not absolute garbage, but that's what it is. The way you get location to this camera is supposedly to install their phone app and enable location linking from your phone. On my iPhone, with background app refresh enabled, I'm lucky for the Fuji to successfully link and get a location perhaps a whopping 5% of the time, and that's being generous. I end up just hoping I get enough locations that I can use Lightroom to assign the rest after the fact; it's a time consuming exercise in frustration every time I start post processing on my pictures. Now the app in general is pretty horrible, even for simple tasks like transferring pictures. If you shoot raw, you can't transfer them LOL; so there's that. If you really want a raw picture out of the camera, you have to use the menu system to convert it to jpeg, then the app will allow you the privilege of transferring it, and that conversion is not a quick and easy process with all the clicking it requires.

So anyway, fun camera, good pictures for the price, the software is horrible, you should just assume location data will never be recorded.

title: Inferior Optics
text:
My initial impressions of this pair of binoculars was positive. Materials seem good, the eye cups spin up and down easily and do not slip, both objective and eyepiece covers are included, the case is decent, rubber armoring appears to be a good quality, focus adjustment is smooth, diopter adjustment is ok, etc. They can be tripod mounted.

The optics, however, were dismal from the first view. The field of view was nearly filled - seriously, about 50% - with a colored haze. Fogged? Nope. Width adjustment? Nope. Flip-down objective covers in the field of view? Nope, and I actually took them off. Eyecups up? Yes. Something on the lenses? Nope. Coatings problem? Doesn't look like it.

The problem? Simple leakage and flare ... and on a heavily overcast day. Fully shielding the eyepieces with my hands eliminated a lot of the haze, but by no means all. Looking in the direction presenting the least issues, I still have about 20% of the view obscured. On top of that, in the glimpses I could get out to the edges, only about 50% of the view is reasonably sharp, getting progressively worse toward the fringes. Unfortunately, "sharp" isn't terribly sharp, either. It's actually not bad close-in, but less so further out, and there appears to be some collimation misalignment.

All-in-all, a pretty bad set. It may be just one bad example off the line, as the other reviews are good. But I have to judge based on what I have, and it isn't good.

I have owned perhaps 15 different sets of binoculars and other optics I currently own Zeiss Victory, Leica BA, Bushnell, Burris, Leupold, Swift and a couple of no-name binoculars sets for kids to use. I've had everything from cheap Tascos to surplus military. I'm picky with optics, but by no means a snob, and I will only keep this set as a loaner or kid set.

To be fair to Vanguard, I've looked through other models in their line, though I never bought a set. Most were at least comparable to others in their price range, but I would pass on this set.

title: FANTASTIC PRODUCT!!! PROBLEMATIC APP. ALMOST COMPLETELY USELESS TECH SUPPORT.
text:
My wife and her siblings got this as a Christmas gift for their mom (my mother-in-law). I’m the techie in the family, so I set it up in our house a few days before Christmas, and my wife and I fell in love with it!!! We have our first grandchild now and our daughter puts all of his baby photos in a Google Photos album that she shares with us. In the Nixplay app on my iPad, I simply added that shared album as a playlist and all of our grandson’s precious photos immediately began displaying on the frame in Full HD. What’s really great is that every time our daughter adds new photos that shared album (several daily, I assure you), they automatically appear on the frame. I swear we spent more time watching the frame during the few days we had it than we did watching TV. It’s now on my in-law’s TV stand and they told love it. I’ve send added shared albums from my wife’s siblings and even created and added a shared from their own Google Photos account and showed them how easy it is to add new photos to the frame anytime.

My only complaints are as follows: First—and this a BIG one—is that I called Nixplay Tech Support a couple of times, which seemed to be staffed by people with thick foreign accents and poor English (maybe a call center in the Phillipins?) In other words, they were so difficult for me to understand that I just had to figure it out on my own (i.e., worthless). However, to their credit, they were VERY friendly and genuinely tried to help, but the language barrier was just too great (for me).

Second, the Nixplay app, as well as the web interface, are not intuitive. There are a plethora of options, but the interface design needs a lot of work! I have A.S., B.S., & M.S. degrees in I.T. and I still struggled with it, so I pity the typical user who gets lost and then can’t rely on their tech support for assistance.

Nonetheless, the frame itself is just a magnificent product that will bring you a lifetime of joyful memories...if/when you can get it set up, that is. Good luck!

title: Really surprised and impressed
text: I like to listen to music when I'm working, and to audio books when I'm walking.  Both require headphones so as to not bother the people around me, or simply to be able to hear and enjoy the subject matter.  So I've always worn either wired headphones or wireless headphones/earphones. Both, however, tend to do a very good job of blocking out the sound around me, no matter what that sound is; some of them are so effective at this that I don't even know if someone is trying to speak to me until I see them. Now with my wife also working from home as well, that won't work.  So I did some shopping and reading of reviews.  For a first try at using bone conduction headphones I decided on these because reviews were decent and the price was too - I didn't want to spend big bucks only to find out I hate it. They arrived early this morning; a day earlier than anticipated.  I immediately charged then to full capacity and then paired them with my phone.  I've now been wearing them for 4 hours and I honestly cannot tell I have them on - that's how light and comfortable they are.  I've used them to listen to audio books while walking the dog, music, and 2 conference calls.  I am seriously impressed with the quality of the sound I'm hearing.  Music is rich and full.  Spoken word, either via the audio books or in a conference call, are as clear and crisp as if I were standing in the room with the speaker.  I keep my phone in a holster on my belt, and I had zero (0) interference or loss of signal or interference while walking around outside. And my ears are free and open so I can simultaneously hear everything around me.  But even with the neighbor cutting their grass, I'm able to hear and appreciate the audio book I'm listening to.  I can't speak to battery life yet, since I've only had them 4 hours now.  I'll update this review later on.  But so far, I'm loving this!!

title: Great Sound Production as a 2.1 Home Stereo Receiver/AMP, But it is Complicated to Use
text:
Only just received this Denon DRA-800H Receiver yesterday , using primarily as a Stereo Music Receiver for my Basement Music Setup. The overall sound is terrific, great clarity playing Vinyl LPs , CDs, and even old Cassettes. But first observation : Man, its a bit complicated to setup - lots of functions and controls. I used to think as myself as pretty good with electronics and such, but at 68 years old, lately I've fallen off that wagon a little. For instance, I thought I could just plug in a Flashdrive which has recorded music , hit play and here we go ! Nope, you have to configure and make selections using the Remote control. I still can't get to play the Flashdrive..... Granted I have my Denon Receiver connected to cheap Boytone Multi- Player (includes Phono, CD, Cassette , USB [player and recorder], so the source player can be upgraded for sure (doing just that now). But I can plug the Flashdrive into the Boytone, select USB, and in few seconds after reading it, it plays..... EASY .... The Denon is far too complicated so far. The same for just accessing the FM radio.......whew !!! It should be a simple matter to attach the a tenna (I did), select FM and sele t a station and play it......no not that easy. Maybe after I go through the Manual (which is on line only - another PIA in today's world of "paperlessness" - the Car Makers do it too), I may grow to understand the many features and also use them. Unfortuantel;y, I am a Manual Reader - I like doing that and understanding my product fully. I'll try to update my review after a few weeks of playing. By the way, I have the Deomn connected to two sets of Bookshelf Speakers and a Sub Woofer : a Pair of Fluance Signature Series speakers , a air of Elac Debut 6.2 speakers and a Momoprice 60 Watt SW. Although the speakers have different "sounds" , they seem to balance very nicely delivering great sound , and the SW is perfect for the space too. I play MY Music to accompany my "retirement Hobby - Playing Drums . Returned to that after 50 year layoff.... Really enjoying that - and I will more after the retirement is Officially completed in the upcoming months...:):)

Update to original review in 8/2020. After using the Receiver for some months now, I still keep the rating at 4 Stars. Performance is 5 stars, delivering a clear , precise and powerful sound from my Elac Speakers, but particularly since I have not connected to a TV, the setup and features are still confusing to me, it takes lots of patience to get through it. It took several calls to a Denon rep to go through some of the features to be setup. Maybe it's me, but I am unable to simply plug in a flashdrive into the USB front port, and have it plug and play. It should be noted that I am using this Receiver solely as a 2.1 stereo unit , and hope to expand its use in the futre to connect to TV, etc. But note ,it is not a full Surround Sound Receiver.

Update of Review 8/2022. 2 years of ownership. The Denon plays very well. I learned from AV Forums that I was "overloading" it by connecting 2 pairs (channel A &B) of Elac Bookshelf speakers that are rated 4-8 Ohms, BUT are nominal at 6 Ohms. The 2 , 6 Ohm speakers create a 3 Ohm impedance on the Receiver. At 60 Volume levels (max is 95), the Denon runs pretty Hot. If i connect 8 Ohm nominal speakers, resulting in a 4 Ohm total impedance draw, it runs cooler. However, the 2 pairs of Elacs sound fantastic played simultaneously!! I just learned of a "trick" on the AV Forum of how to change (manipulate) the selection of the Ohms settings. That seems to help a little by selecting a 6 Ohms settings in the software. To date, I still have NOT used all the features of this well behaved and great sounding Receiever. The availablility of Zone 2 (adding another Amp) is great feature. I have the Zone 2 connected to a IOTA SA3 /PA3 stack that are connected to 2 other differnet pairs of bookshelf speakers, playing in the same room. When both systems are playing together - WOW - sounds like a concert hall.

title: I have been waiting for a monitor like this for a long time.
text: I am thrilled with the quality and detail of the screen! The extra screen real estate is amazing and allows for much easier use of Photoshop and I can open windows side by side for easy reference between apps or I can keep my playlist open will still working in my primary app. Using video editing software and being able to drag and drop my media directly from a folder into the project has streamlined my work space. The experience while watching movies isn't as beneficial as the enhancements for software as it doesn't fill the entire screen but it doesn't distract me and the image quality is sharp and precise while the colors are clean and accurate with no color banding issues. If you are a gamer, this thing will blow your socks off. The extra screen real estate really gives a cinematic feel to gaming that has to be experienced to truly understand. After playing on this monitor and going back to a 16:9 monitor makes it almost claustrophobic in feel, almost like I was missing something. Again, the colors and detail were sharp and precise. You may need to upgrade your video card to support full resolution gaming with good frame rate at high detail but you wont want to sell yourself short by cutting back on the settings so you can see the true benefits of the display. Did I mention that this thing is huge? The box was so big that my daughter though I bought a TV and it dominates my desk space and steals the show from everything else in the area. I ran some diagnostic software called monitor test to push this beast through its paces. It passed the light bleed test without any issues. There was no noticeable light bleed which I was worried about with such a large display but the lighting was consistent throughout the display. Solid colors looked even and balanced but during the gradation test it did have some banding but it is much better than on other monitors I have tested. The moire test was spot on even at the finest setting. the patterns were all clear and didn't blur or bleed into each other.During the convergence testing there was no color bleed or ghosting and there was a sharp contrast between light and dark. Text was very clear and sharp even at 6 point Arial font and was easy to read. Overall, I am very pleased with this monitor. I have been looking for a monitor of this caliber at a reasonable price point. I would recommend this especially to art and video creators.

title: Started out bad, then improved once I reached the BT setting?
text:
Had some initial problems where the audio was really weak and I had to recharge the battery as it arrived at 0.0 volts, but like some DSP units, sometimes you have to "reset" the entry point before they start to perform, I started out at AM, (weak audio) then FM, (same) then NOAA and the audio improved a little, then the BT setting, afterwards I went back, the audio improved for all bands?

Once I got back stronger audio, then I could see about the performance of the individual bands, AM had surprising selectivity, ( a simple yet effective means to determine the effectiveness of this particular band using DSP-centric circuitry) FM and NOAA played better once I had adequate audio power, apparently going into BT mode reset the audio "baseline" for the entire unit, I have not tried the micro SD slot yet, but now with the audio power returning to a usable level, I imagine it will work better than my initial assumptions when I had the volume up all the way and could barely hear anything on any band.

I can't expect to downgrade a radio due to the "expected" shortcomings of some DSP based radios, but I will give this a deduction for arriving with a dead battery, that much is certainly "preventable" by the manufacturer.

One must have a certain amount of skepticism when dealing with the current market of DSP based radios as some have worked out most of the "kinks" while others appear to not care if the lowest consumer expectations rarely are met by any means of reliable production methods regardless of the entry point of those variable customer "expectations".

Time will tell if the foam will expand or break down like some others. This is why they send you extras and that's okay! Don't blame the playa.

You can see in the pics that I use a single ear bud with my memory foam tips (have tried a couple) and the foam tip actually helps keep it in place in my ear. Next to these tips is a 'medium' that I use often, which is larger than this sets 'large'.

I love the option to replace buds and glad Tennmak is coming in at an affordable price. Tips can expand to keep buds secure, block some level of noise (and these do) and enhance your audio experience. DVR/Camera Setup:

I have a background in IT and camera setups so I was able to figure it out but for someone who doesn't have that much background in this, you might want to call reolink and have them walk you through on how to make changes and also teach you what some of the words/acronyms mean but you get what you pay for right? Cheap usually ends up being bad, pricey ends up being good in some cases lol this case, very good.

IMPORTANT:
when you set the password at the beginning of the DVR setup, you will need to remember that password. When installing the app on your phone/computer, you need to use that same password upon initial setup.

I'll be updating my review in a month or so to let you know how the device is going :)
