title: The culmination of Beats' Vision - From Various Perspectives!
text:
These are by far the best Beats yet! Beats have been classified with several key values in the audio devices category: High-bass, hard-hitting, high-quality sound, great for workouts, stylish (both for their subtlety and their loud, "look-at-me" color palettes).

These PowerBeats Pro buds feel like the culmination of lots of R&D, and as the culmination of the brand - available in a subtle, stylish black matte finish, they are professional and low-profile. In their Ivory, Moss or Navy schemes, they are still subtle but have that stylish flair typical of Beats industrial design.

The fit is spectacular. I have ears that work with lots of earbuds, but my wife does not - She's been forced to stick to over-ear and on-ear headband design headphones for most of her life - AirPods dont work and most earhook headsets are just incomfortable for her. My former PowerBeats headphones were OK but even in my very flexible ear didn't have the best "stay put" feel. My wife refused to wear them, citing painful pushing of the inserted bud into the walls of her ear canal. Conversely, we now fight over the PowerBeats Pro - She's going to have to get her own pair! They are not only more comfortable for those with picky ears, but they sit much lower in profile, allowing for more subtle use... The first time I saw myself wearing my 2nd generation powerbeats I was a bit embarrassed. With the PowerBeats Pro, they appear flush with my head shape and sleek in appearance.

The audio quality is excellent. I'm a purveyor of true wireless headsets. I've been fortunate enough to own most of the current A-list of true wireless, including the Bose Soundsport Free, Jabra Elite 65t, Apple AirPods (1st generation) and these PowerBeats Pro. The PowerBeats are the ones that only leave my pocket or "go bag" to charge a few times a week at night when I'm not using them... The sound quality is excellent, with strong bass that doesn't muddy up the highs and mids of more sophisticated tracks, and yet hits with enough range that it feels immersive rather than just deep. In some ways, the PowerBeats Pro have replaced my Studio Wireless cans as well for at-the-desk listening due to just how good they sound, and how much more comfortable it is listening without covering my ears completely.

Add to that the modernization of the industrial design - Support for Lightning charging (Studio and Solo have no excuse left to not support this) and the nice, albeit large, carrying/charging case, and these are going to be a HUGE hit for a long time. I dont even know where they'd go from here. They leave me wanting nothing, and just completely enjoying my music.

title: Radio Auto-Set feature does not work in the United States
text:
Be aware that this is meant to be used in Japan. The radio signal it uses to auto-set must not be available in the US - well at least not in S. California. The instruction manual is only in Japanese. I wasn't able to easily find a translated manual online.

Nothing is actually wrong with the clock, it has a very understated & crisp design. You *can* manually set it. But no where in the item description does it mention what to expect in other countries.

There is an M.set button you hold down for 3 seconds, then press it again to run the clock forward until you reach the current time, then press Rec. to set it. One thing to note: every so often it tries to find the radio signal again - all hands with go to 12 for about ~10 minutes. Once that fails it will go back to the time you set.

title: No Peaks

Note that the Tripp Lite CAT6 RJ45 Keystone jacks (N238-025-WH) DO NOT have the peaked separators so you will have to buy a different brand if you purchase the CNE43705.  Tripp Lite just does not get it.

title: Couldn't get the usb to work...
text:
After unpacking the microscope I read the instructions and then plugged it into it's power supply. All was well and the image of a coin looked super (I wanted it for coin collecting). I didn't have a memory card and so I couldn't try saving an image to one. If that worked I could have transferred the image if I had a card reader on my computer. I didn't. I then connected the unit to my laptop usb port and started trying to get it to display. I went to the suggested site for the software I needed. The site took me to a Dropbox location insisted I create a Dropbox account. I didn't want to for just one download. After finally deciding to give in I filled out all of their form and then, at the bottom found out I could skip it. I did so and downloaded. Windows defender then warned me of a suspected virus. I deleted the file and tried downloading the AMCAP app as suggested in a review. This software gave me an error and would not recognize the Microscope as an imaging device. I tried a different version, same result. I then downloaded the drivers for the Windows camera and the camera recognize microscope device but the image flickered rapidly and wouldn't stop.

I might have kept on trying but I was also frustrated by the dashboard and remote controls that would not let me escape from menu items without turning off the microscope from the dashboard. I couldn't turn it off from the remote. After spending a lot of frustrating hours I gave up and sent the thing back. I've ordered a different unit that claims to be "plug and play." I'll see and write another review about it.

As I scanned for a replacement I saw that many suppliers neither provided plug and play devices or provided the software to operate their equipment. I know including a CD costs 40 cents or so. Adding plug and play to a unit probably costs more in terms of creation time. However, I would gladly pay a few dollars more to have something that was ready to work.

I love Amazon for their policy of taking back bad choices and also for their rapid delivery, I'll have the replacement microscope tomorrow! Maybe I should mention I'm old and my brain turns to mush easily, oh well!

Update: I've purchased and received the Opti-Tekscope Digital USB Microscope Camera. It worked immediately and was plug and play as advertised. I'm now going to write a review for that experience.

title: Fine little soundbar for a PC
text:
When my speaker arrived, I had these impressions:
- easy setup, plugged into my PC's speaker jack and the adjacent USB, and clicked it on
- the lights on the ends glow, and each end cycles on its own through the color ranges. You can't stop on a favorite color, but I find it soothing to look down and see the colors
- The cloth speaker grill is a high-quality touch.

The speaker is sixteen inches in length and provides fair stereo separation. It can put out a more-than-adequate volume, and the sound is quite clear, with no buzzing or a tinny sound. That being said, it doesn't have much bass at all, but I knew to expect that, and am pleased with the physical separation between the right and left speakers. The YouTube "Left and Right Stereo Sound Test" I ran showed that with this wide speaker, you can get good stereo separation.

It does take up a little space on my desk, but I think it's a worthwhile use of the area, and I have enjoyed using this speaker.

title: Ryzen Compatible
text:
I have used this ram in an ASRock B350 board paired with both a Ryzen 1200, followed by a Ryzen 1600. Both processors were clocked to 3.8Ghz on all cores at 1.28v.

Using the XMP profile, it went right to the specified speed of 2666 and correct timings. However, these sticks overclock extremely well. I could either loosen the timings and get them to run at 2933, or leave them at 2666 and tighten the timings significantly. The later produced much better results. Ryzen really responds to memory speed. By simply tightening the timings, I added almost 200 points to Cinebench R20 and typically 5 to 8 frames on most games like Apex Legends and The Division 2.

I used "Memory Calculator for Ryzen" program to determine the most stable timings without raising the voltage above 1.35v. The timings can be lowered drastically, sometimes by several points.

I would definitely recommend Patriot memory. They are clearly using decent modules, sold at a lower price as they try to gain market share.

title: Awesome device! Love it
text:
I've been a Surface fan for several years. I have the Surface Pro 3, and tried the Surface Laptop. At this point in time, one of the more power intense devices isn't necessary for me. I actually returned the Surface Laptop because I didn't feel I used it enough.

The Go hits the sweet spot for me because the size is perfect. I primarily use the device from the couch, so the smaller size is a lot nicer. It's very comfortable to hold and so lightweight! If you don't need this to function as a workhorse computer then it is perfectly adequate. I have a business laptop, so never do work from my personal computers. So for me, this is really all the computer I need. I'm not a gamer or editor, so I basically just browse web forums, watch youtube or Netflix, and other basic tasks. I have Word, Excel, etc installed too which is super nice. I think for people in my use case, the Go has plenty of power.

The Go's speed is pretty good. At times it seems really fast, and at other times I do notice it is a little slower than more powerful devices. I mostly notice the slower speed when opening new apps or screens. I played a simple game from the Microsoft Store (one of those cooking themed games) and was surprised at how speedy the Go functioned. It really didn't lag at all while I played it. Videos also look crisp and clean on the Go. The only time I noticed the Go acting buggy was with the touch pad keyboard. There were occasions when the keyboard would not open when it was supposed to. The on screen keyboard is sufficient for web browsing, but I would much prefer an actual keyboard for doing a lot of typing. In this regard, I do think you should pick up a secondary keyboard for the Go. I would honestly just recommend the Microsoft keyboard made for the Go, since it was made for this device. It will connect to it perfectly and makes it really easy to travel with. However, if you are only going to use the Go from a desk and not travel with it much, you could probably just choose a cheaper keyboard. It is a shame Microsoft doesn't just include the keyboard with the purchase.

Overall I'm really happy with the Go. For me it was a better fit than the Surface Laptop (also a good device but more power than I needed, and the size was preferable on the Go). The main cons are the keyboard not being included in the price tag and the general price of the Go (I bought the 8gb version). If the keyboard was just included in the package it would make the overall price easier to swallow. For basic tasks or as a secondary unit this is a great computer. It has the great build quality of a Surface device but in a more compact device.

text:

The subwoofer makes the floor shake and rattles the windows at only 3/4 of the way up! I love this system to watch movies and am rediscovering my music collection all over again.
Here's what I like:
--Sound quality
--Power (loudness)
--Elegant design and attractive looks
--Price (unbeatable for the THX certification)
--Two input ports with detachable cables
Here's what I don't like:
--No decoding; they seem to have discontinued the model with an optical input, which would have been perfect for my stand-alone Blu-ray player that sits on my desk with my computer.
HERE'S THE SOLUTION TO THE DECODING PROBLEM:
Search Amazon for the "Monoprice digital to stereo converter". It's just over twenty bucks and requires a power input (it includes the necessary power cable for your wall), but it will take either digital coax or digital optical cable (neither is included) and convert it to stereo RCA. Then you need a separate (also not included) RCA-to-stereo-minijack cable that will plug-in to this Logitech speaker unit. Now I have back the missing optical decoding solution and this speaker system serves both my computer and my Blu-ray player. Neat!

title: Great managed switch for those without extensive network training
text:
We have a somewhat complex network comprised of four of this series of switch (1x48 port, 1x24 port, 1x24 port + PoE, 1x8 port).

These are pretty robust switches and quite easy to configure. We have 9 VLANs and the switches are connected to each via 3 port LAGs.

I went in with zero experience with VLANs or LAGs and after a bit of reading was able to configure it all myself. We don't have these mixed with other vendors (or even a different series from Netgear) so I can't talk to that.

What I've found is that the default settings on these switches are pretty much right where most users need to be. Example: these support STP, RSTP, and MSTP. By default they're all set to RSTP and it just works.

Our racks which used to be comprised of a hodgepodge of different dumb switches all intertwined all route through single managed switches now. If I need to connect a piece of equipment to a device on the other side of the building I just I assign a port on each side to the requisite VLAN and plug it in. Need it to be isolated from all other networks? Make a new VLAN. Need more throughput between switches? Run another cable and add another port to the LAG. Simple stuff.

title: Excellent Product - The USB-C Hub Apple or Google Would Rebrand and Sell for $129
text:
I have been using the Falwedi USB-C Hub (7-in-1 version) for several days now, with my Google PixelBook and My Acer CB515-1HT Chromebook. It functions perfectly for pass-through charging of both devices, when using an appropriate power supply, which helps to free up a port while adding the convenience of 3 additional USB ports, a card reader, and an HDMI output. On both of my Chromebooks, the higher end and the lower end models, this allows for the placement of an additional hub on the other USB-C port, adding additional ports and functionality to my devices. This hub functions as intended, without a hiccup, and is an impressive piece of hardware both in the ease of use and the exceptionally classy design.

The device is smaller than I had anticipated, about half the size of a standard 2.5" SSD, or nearly a third of the size of a small portable external hard drive. This USB-C hub is portable. The all metal chassis adds durability to the list of qualities of this stand-out USB-C hub. The metal finish is brushed smooth, with rounded corners, it lacks sharp edges, the USB-C plug connects with a heavy gauge non-sticky rubbery plastic. The USB-C plug end, fits snugly, and as expected from a much higher priced item, into my devices USB-C ports, it leaves no room for wiggle, yet is easy to smoothly eject. This goes the same for the USB ports, HDMI port, and both card slots, they are engineered without a single margin of sizing error. The USB-C plug could have been manufactured to a longer length, but this would have added additional cost to the device, and it is long enough to safely sit beside the device on a desk, or to wrap around and rest the hub on top of the laptop while charging, when not in use. The cord is an adequate length for the intended purpose of the hub.

This USB-C hub works as advertised, all ports function to the highest degree of expectations, the USB 3.0 ports are fast, the HDMI is visually stunning, the the device appears to be quite durable, and made from quality materials with a superb level of engineering design. If you are looking for a USB-C hub and require the addition of HDMI and a card reader with the added bonus of pass-through power delivery for charging and perfect USB 3.0 ports, look no further than this product.

title: TR-002 - Good Quality enclosure
text:
I bought the TR-002 enclosure to use for RAID 1.
Likes:
- USB3.1 Gen 2 10Gbps interface (TR-002 model). Note: TR-004 model uses **USB 3.0** interface.
- QNAP External RAID Manager is great. User interface is intuitive and easy to use for RAID management:
- creating/rebuilding RAID array (I did test RAID 1 rebuilding. It worked great)
- checking RAID status
- reading S.M.A.R.T data from each individual drive
- updating enclosure firmware. The latest firmware version is 1.0.4 (as of 01/19/2020)
- Good sequential read/write 229/227 Mega BYTES/second from Seagate BarraCuda 3.5" 7200 rpm SATA drives.
- Reliable. I have been using the enclosure in RADI 1 configuration for 3 months without any problem.
- Automatic standby when PC is shutdown/hibernated. System status LED flashes ever 2 seconds in standby mode.
- Quiet cooling fan. Temperatures of 2 7200rpm drives reported by S.M.A.R.T were 40C (ambient temp was 26C)
- Supports 2.5" and 3.5" drives.
- Drive mounted on a drive tray with drive label face up so it's easy to visually checked drive spec.

Dislikes (minor):
- Drive status LED is flashing green for both read and write accesses. It would be better to use different colors like flashing yellow for READ, flashing RED write, and solid green for idle.
- Though fan is quite, fan speed is not variable based on drive temp.

Comparatively speaking, these are low-priced cables with a (cosmetically anyway) high build quality. That they immediately cleared the LG OLED error messages is all I needed to know. Ordered another for my OPPO BDP 103 BluRay DVD player (which cleared intermittent BluRay HDCP errors), and another as a backup in case I ever get a DAC with HDMI, or an Ultra HD BluRay player (if Redbox ever carries UHD BluRay in my locality).

Order a few of these BEFORE you buy your UHD 4K TV. You will be glad to have them on hand when you unbox your killer TV!!

title: Great Addition To The Echo Family
text:
When Amazon released all their new Echo products I though a wall clock, really? But after reading and seeing some videos I thought maybe it would be useful. I purchased one for our kitchen, as we set the most timers there.

Setting up the clock is super easy. I simply got it hung on the wall (screw was included) and asked my Echo to find it. Within a few seconds it connected and showed visually it was in the process of setting up and installing an update. Shortly after this the hands started slowly moving to reflect the correct time and we were ready to go.

There are only two things this clock does that are really a benefit:
- Sets the time itself, even when the time changes
- Visually shows timers

Of these two features visually showing timers was the main reason we bought it. Within a second or two of telling the Echo to set a timer the clock lights up to show a timer is set and how much time is left. It even can show multiple timers set. This has come in handy when cooking food or setting timers to show our kids how much time is left for something to happen.

I think the only complaint I have is the finish of the clock. It looks a little cheap and there is no glass covering the hands, so someone could try to change the time on it. I'm guessing they left the glass off as the led lights would reflect on it.

Overall this is a cool device and we use it every day. One concern that I have it how long the 4 AA batteries are going to last. My plan if it eats batteries quickly is to use rechargeable batteries, but being 3 weeks in have had no issues with this.

title: Protects the screen, is anti-glare, and feels like paper. You have to have this.
text:
I have removed and not really liked every single screen protector I have ever owned, period. Until now. This screen protector is also supposed to make the iPad feel more like writing on paper rather than writing in smooth glass. Writing on smooth glass took getting used to. You have to learn to compensate for the fact that the pencil is smooth plastic and the glass is smooth glass. The pen glides with no resistance at all. That being said I did get used to it over time and did well with this. But... would it be better to have a screen which feels more like paper? Always willing to try new things, but skeptical at the same time I ordered “paper like”.

Do watch the video for installing PAPER LIKE. You’ll want to get this right. I watched the video, and followed it to the letter. The end result is a nice even application with no bubbles on an absolutely clean and dust free surface. I think charged up my pencil, opened up GoodNotes 5 and started writing. NICE. Two things, it does feel more like paper and the screen becomes anti-glare as well. It is just better. For the first time I am happy with a screen protector. Mostly because this isn’t just a protector. It’s a more paper like feeling and I do write with the pencil for hours every single day.

Right now I m studying Russian and I find the virtual keyboard and writing with the pencil to be the two perfect for tools for language learning. Two reasons why this is the case. With the virtual keyboard, you get the characters of the language you’re learning. So you can type in that language. But to really learn another language you will want to write in that language and practice words over and over again so you remember the word, the sounds of the letters, and the spelling. As I write it, I say it. I was going through paper notebooks within days. Amazon has a record of me buying two sizes of notepad all the time. And I bought other types of binders as well. And i bought fountain pens and lots of ink because I found it easier to write with fountain pens for hours a day vs ball point regular pens. I really went through a lot trying to find ways to be able to write for hours per day without getting my hand and arm tired. The iPad Pro 12.9” is where this all took me and now the PAPER LIKE screen protector is my latest aid in this endeavor.

This is day one and I already ordered the 7.9” for same day delivery because I’m so impressed with the 12.9” for my iPad Pro. If you write all day with the Apple Pencil, you need this. You really do need this. Protects the screen. Gives you an anti glare surface, and it feels like paper.

title: Unstable performance, extremely slow in real use! at last test with USB3.2 reached only 36Mb/s
text:
Edited review!

(Note: Its possible that the specific unit is defective but in light of many other customers reviews it seem to have quite a bit of faulty devices with same behavior.)

Conclusion & Bottom line:
=====================
After few weeks of experience The Rocket nano 1TB looks like something who every one wish, with exciting design, and promising specifications. But unfortunately the ongoing use and experience is utterly disappointing.
The device is characterized by instability with frequent hangs behavior, along with a very low performance that is actually lower than even a generic flash device.
Pro: Small & cool dosing, lightweight, supplied with 2 matching cables (though too short and not flexible enough)
Cons: Un-stable, Extremely slow, very poor performance, tends to hang continuously. reach in test rate of 36Mb/s instead of 1000Gb/s, while in real usage its even worst drop down to 1500k/s.

Tests were performed in 3 sessions, and review is edited to update and providing the results.
Well, since my first review, I collected more info & experience with this Rocket usage, and things just went worst. :(
My first review was written (about two weeks ago) after having many attempts to find out what is the *real* performance speed.
I used many PC's with various HW. I was able to archive at best results only 1/4 of its specification, means around 250mb/s, This was with H81 chipset which runs USB 3.0 (not 3.1).
But I wasn't able to get such performance on newer HW which runs the lasted USB 3.2 10gb/s.
in these cases it always hang or achieve poor performance even slower then generic flash drive.
I tried several times to perform tests on the brand new PC (running Win10 64Bit) with lasted USB 3.2 10Gb/s port (Intel build in) in most of them the disk just stack and wasn't even able to complete the tests. so it was impossible to perform the tests & competition. - no screenshot were saved for that session.

At the second test session, the machine used for testing was only USB 3.0 NEC chipset, where after several attempts only few terminated, but at all the rest, the Rocket failed to perform a complete test.
See screenshot & the tests details below.
Also tried to use it in real use, copying 250GB of MP3 files while attached to an USB 3.1 port (5Gb/s), took more then 6 hours, which most the time the transfer rate was under 1500 kb/s - extremely slow compared to any other flash or mechanical HD.
In practice, in real use, the device is malfunctioning, often hangs up, and its performance drops drastically after more than 2 minutes of use.
This was frustrating and nerve-wracking experience.
As a PC technician with access to hundreds of different types of computers, I have not been able to prove a reasonable use of this device.
Even compared to a standard flash device its capabilities are terrible.
It is possible that the only unit I received is defected, so it is important to get feedback from other users.

Screenshots attached related to the second test session (first group) are for 3 different storage, which were taken in competition on USB 3.0 port powered by NEC (not the 3.2 which failed in all attempts).
1. Rocket nano 1TB (succeed only once ! )
2. Corsair Flash Voyager GTX 256GB USB 3.1 Premium
3. Silicon Power jewel j80 usb 3.1 32GB
all screenshots includes description of the relevant storage and the relevant test results.

A third tests session was taken on 30.01.20.
This time I tried again a new Lenovo PC. this are the specifications.
CPU -Intel I5- 8th generation, 12GB DDR4, Plextor PH6 System SSD (runs Win10 Pro 64 bit), NVIDIA 1650,
This PC nativelly support USB3.2 10Gb/s by Intel chipset.
I used 3 different USB devices as above replacing the SP J80 by the system SSD -Plextor PH6. runs 3 software for the benchmarks.
ATTO , AS-SSD, & Crystal Disk-Mark.

The results are shown in the new screenshots (Group two).
The rocket failed to perform any tests with ATTO & AS-SSD, only 'Crystal-disk' succeed it once (after many failures) but with a rate of 36Mb/s~ only. slower then the Silicon-Power J80.

=========
My earlier review: Tested the "Rocket" and was unable to be even close to half of the declared speed.
I repeated test on 4 different machines which had various HW combination, the highest speed I was able to reach stuck on 250mb/s. Both read & write operations. only 1/4 of the declared.
So I can not confirm if its only my specific one that is defective or is just the real speed of this Disk. very disappointing.

title: Nice, Inexpensive, but inconsistent fit cross platforms
text:
I received my Altura 8mm Fisheye lens for my Nikons and found that the learning curve for use was about 5 minutes. The easy to understand videos for the lens had me shooting and enjoying the lens quickly.

I found the lens to be a bit loose on my Nikon D3300. When mounted, it did not lock into place and, turning the bezels of the lens to the left tended to loosen the lens. It moved while mounted, (rattled) but once held steady was ok. It was easy, however to simply support the camera by holding the lens in place while using the on-lens bezels, so that it did not loosen up between shots.

I tried this same lens on my Nikon D3500, and the looseness disappeared, and the lens locked into place like a lens should! Apparently, the mounting hole on the D3000 is a bit larger than that on the D3500. So, with a little care it is usable on both cameras, but you'll want to watch for loosening if used on a Nikon D3000.

This is a MANUAL lens. No auto focus, no monitoring, so you have to set your camera to "M" and adjust your lens by hand. Set your ISO on the camera and your shutter speed too, take a couple of test shots and go for it!

The reasonable price of this lens outweighs any minor inconvenience that the looseness on the D3300 presents. It comes with a n interesting zip-open lens case that is BIG, so you'll need to make room in your camera bag. All in all, it's a keeper and I'll be using it often.

Edit! BONUS! The skies were blue and the sun was bright and in the photo. The lens presented with a natural, sharp sun flare that's a great accent point!

title: Easy Install...In The End
text:
This review is written the day after installing the case, thus I'm unable at this juncture to comment on durability, as well as long term usability. That said I first placed the Samsung Buds case within the silicone case without peeling the double sided tape. I did this to gauge the fit which as it turns out can be very good. It was clear that the adhering the top of the silicone case first would be key to achieving a good final result.

Thus leaving the bottom Silicone case in place on the Samsung case, I pulled back the top peeling off the paper on the adhesive and then placed the top back over the Samsung case. Reversing the process I did the bottom. In fact it took a second try for the bottom, where the Silicone case's adhesive released without any problem so I could reposition the bottom.

The net result is the edges of the top/bottom line up when the case is closed leaving only a minimal gap. If a larger gap is present, it's likely the silicone case needs to be repositioned. Test fitting first is key to getting this right without a lot of hassle. Additionally, the LED and charging opening were centered. I am concerned that the charging flap won't stay in place. It's a candidate for removal with a knife at some point.

With respect to opening the case, clearly it is difficult to fully open the Samsung case such that it latches open. That said I found that if one is careful the Silicone material moves enough that the Samsung case can be latched open.

title: Don’t buy if you have a big dog
text:
The product is easy to sync and install, although given the fact that the adhesive strips are built in to the back of the plastic, if you want to change the location you’d have a hard time getting it to stick. Not to mention ripping holes in your walls. Haven’t tried it but there are no tabs to pull or any release mechanism like command strips have. Does a good job detecting motion - the range and sensitivity seem like they capture everything in our large family/kitchen/dining room area.

My main beef with this product though is there is no way to set exclusion zones or pick a setting that will ignore a large dog. I set it on the lowest sensitivity and it still caught our 75lb golden every time. If there was setting that ignored motion signatures up to 100lb, or if I could set it to ignore the area 2-3’ above the floor then the sensor would be a lot more flexible. What are the chances that someone less than 100lb will break in and crawl through your living room?

Next step may be to mount it higher, but I’m afraid of moving it and there are no other recommendations I can find other than 7.5’ for pets. Honestly i will probably just set it to stay off all the time, and then turn it on if we leave the house for an extended time and our dog isn’t there. But that is kind of cumbersome as you need to adjust that in the detailed settings of the device every time.

Overall I’m kind of annoyed with this sensor, but it came as part of a bulk package and I’m pretty happy with ring as a whole so far so I don’t plan on returning it.

title: Pogo Pin sticks doesnt make contact
text:
I really liked the look of this battery base.
It was easy to contect following the instructions and even though I was a bit put off how long it would take to recharge.
My purpose was to use it portibly in the evening hours and then let it charge while the family sleeps.
It has been charging for 12+ hours and is still NOT fully charged.
So I thought well I will just remove my device from the base and see what is going on.
It was evident 1 of the 3 pogo pins was down and did not spring back and looks a lil bent....
My bad that I didn't inspect before placing on the base.
Had I damaged this then all of them would be bent. I followed exactly and carefully how to install and removed it as carefully.
I am returning for a replaciment and then I will go from there....should I recieve another defective device = refund.
Just wish that Amazon would make the battery bases for their devices.

~~~~~"UPDATE"~~~~~
Okay Folks so I thought I would update my review.
Why? I returned the deivce and was given a new one.
This replacement does have one contact that is shorter than the other 2 - BUT it is NOT on the bent side.
Also the recharge on this replacement is much faster even though it is still on the slow side.
With that said after a week I have more insight on this device.
It is lacking in may aspects and the main aspsect is this.
If you leave your Echo and this device connected when you are playing your music or listening to a book even when plugged into your main power the battery will drain at least half way.
My reconmendation is if you are not using this as a portable to take your music with you then disconnect the echo and the battery pack; if you know that you are going to be using the portable part of this plug back in and let charge for at least an hour if it has not completely drained.

When using this outside I have noticed some charge holding issues.
They as follows:
Humidity and any moisture are NOT your friends with the Echo and the this Battery base....
Yes I live in a Humid State and the Summers are horrible; the Humidty will degrade your devices quickly and drain them rapidly.
Sun and Hot temperatures make using Echo and this Battery base a problem and again I will state will degrade both.
I am very picky about my elctronics in the hot summer heat and humdity and that said I know that both will damage eletronic devices and void out most warrentees.
Keep both in the shade and way from moisture issues.
With a replacement and a week I am upgrading my 2 star review up to 3.
The reason I am not giving this a 4 or 5 Star rating is simple; this battery base needs to be upgraded with contection and durability.
The price is what makes this attractable and highly recommend for those with 1 Device and want to carry it into the garage, work shop, craft room or even outside in optimal weather conditions.
It is really sad that Amazon has NOT come up with their own version and I have tod them as much.

title: Defective & Damaged PC
text:
August 28,2020, we had a brief power outage. This Unit did not go to battery power on lines connected to battery powered (black). Maybe it did shut down my PC . It's hard to tell since the PC would have shut down anyway. Whatever the CyberPower BRG 1500 did do in the shutdown process damaged my Falcon Northwest rendering it unbootable. I had a Dell Optiplex in the next room (same power supply circuit). It was connected with a $25.00 surge protector. After the power was restored the Dell Optiplex started up just fine but the Falcon Mach V wouldn't reboot. The CyberPower failed to go to battery and somehow damaged the PC. So much for expensive surge protection. There was no way to know that the unit would do this until it happened, so I am just slightly outside their return window. The LCD showed full battery charge, etc. I can't see why you would test one of these units unless you hit the circuit breaker to create a mock power outage just to see if actually worked. Hopefully, CyberPower will just take it back. Otherwise, given the wording of their warranty, it looks like a small claims matter.
Additional information: This company makes returns and warranty service very, very difficult. For most folks the hassle probably isn't worth it unless there were costly equipment damages. I would advise not purchasing any products from this company. Down time, hassles over warranty and associated delay, likely short lifespan due to poor quality, etc. Note that you will pay shipping on warranty service return even when it quite new and is a clearly defective product. The prices are only attractive if you disregard the both quality, lifespan and additional
costs in both money and your time associated Their prices are good but you will be shopping at the junkyard.

title: Seems to have done the trick for a very common issue not explained by the cable company
text:
I had been experiencing dropped downstream connection multiple times per hour regardless of weather. I am an extremely OCD electrician and have been practiced in RG-6 for 15 years, so I doubted termination quality inside the home. I checked outside as well and found no water intrusion or install errors. The run is very simple. No TV service.
Just the big splitter on the pole, the drop to the home, an entrance block for grounding, a MoCA filter (used to keep out neighboring DVR systems which use the coax as a type of home network), and the run to the modem with nothing in between. Then it occurred to me that perhaps the run is so direct that my setup is missing some of the attenuation found in splitters used in a more typical residence that also has TV. I took a look at the cable page on my modem's setup and saw a few of the channels showing uncorrectable errors. After installing the attenuator, signal-to-noise has gone up slightly and errors are down to almost zero. I have not seen any drops in the upstream connection since installing it. Also, this model seems to be somewhat low-pass in design, so as to reduce the hotness of higher megahertz downstream channels while not affecting the strength of lower megahertz upstream transmission.

title: As Long As the Receiver Is Very Close To The Keyboard, You Can Work AND Game On This!
text:
I've been using this keyboard a couple of weeks now and I will update this review if anything changes. Okay so it's already well known from other reviews that this keyboard is absolutely marvelous for those who do lots of typing and work. The Flow software is also awesome and works very well for switching between a computers. I figured I could add further valuable input about this keyboard from the perspective of someone who does work on it as well as a lot of gaming.

I purchased this keyboard from Dell as a combo with the Master 3 mouse and paid ~$135 for them after a promotional discount. So, I'm reviewing this keyboard after essentially having paid ~68 for it, which is the most I've ever paid for a keyboard at this point. My other keyboards I've used are the Microsoft Comfort Curve 2000 (one of the best keyboards of all time in my opinion) and a Razer Ornata Chroma. I have used a Corsair mechanical for a short period, but mechanical keyboards just aren't my thing TBH.

My use case: I do a lot of typing on this keyboard for emails and school assignments and also gaming. I am no average gamer, though. I have played near the tippy top level of competition in games such as Half Life 2 Deathmatch and Quake 3 CPMA, which are FPS's that often require many keys being pressed precisely and at the same time. I have NOT played RTS's or MOBA's. The typing experience on this keyboard is one of the best I've ever had. To start, it genuinely FEELS GOOD to type on this keyboard. Like, it feels so good that sometimes I have a desire to type on it for the sole reason of it feeling so good to type on. I'm being totally serious about that. There is no uncertainty in the key presses, the actuation point is very clear and they always register.

My gaming experience thus far: *IMPORTANT NOTE* At first, I had the receiver plugged into the back of my PC which is ~4 feet away from the keyboard and behind a monitor. I had intermittent connection loss during that time in games. So, I tried moving the receiver to the USB hub that is built into my gaming monitor, which makes it only ~1 foot away, and since then I have had ZERO connection issues. Gaming experience: I have had absolutely zero missed keypresses or unintentional keypresses on this keyboard. All of my movement in Quake felt great, I'm still able to rocket jump around in CPMA at maximum speed. If you enjoy gaming on membrane keyboards, this keyboard can absolutely game so long as you place the receiver very close to it. (You could use a USB extension cable or USB hub for this, as well.)

So, what do I NOT like about this keyboard? Not a whole lot. For one, I see that Logitech sells this keyboard WITH the palm rest in Europe, but NOT the USA. We have to buy the palm rest separately! Secondly, the options you have with this keyboard in the software are quite limited currently. For example, I can ONLY customize the top function keys' functions in the Options software. I wish I could customize all of the keys on the keyboard to whatever function I like. I'm hoping this is something they will improve significantly on with this keyboard over time. Finally, I also wish that the keyboard had some very well engineered adjustable feet for changing the angle at which it is propped up. It has no feet, but fortunately the angle they fixed the keyboard at is very good so it's not that big of a problem. All of these gripes are minor, in my opinion, and I would still buy this keyboard if I could do it all over again.

I took 2 stars off of the Ergonomics category solely because Logitech did not include their very cheap wrist rest with the keyboard itself and made it a separate purchase in the US. This keyboard is still exceptionally ergonomic even without the wrist wrest, which I still have not purchased.

Overall conclusion: Do I think this keyboard is worth $100? Well, $100 is a hard sell for any keyboard in my opinion. With that said, I would pay $100 for this keyboard knowing what I know now about it. I think it's a great "do it all" keyboard as long as the receiver is very close to it. With the multiple device features on the mouse and keyboard, I am able to use this mouse and keyboard in my music space as well as my gaming space and just move the mouse/keyboard between the spaces depending on which one I'm using. If the Flow software also appeals to you and you have a use for it, it's well worth it.

Side note: In case anyone read through this whole review and also wondered how the MX Master 3 is for gaming: It is a good mouse for CASUAL gaming. I say this because if you are wanting to play any competitive FPS's with the Master 3, its lack of DPI switching and weight customization makes it an inferior choice to other mice in my opinion, such as the G502 (I kept my G502 for when I want to play competitive FPS's.) If Logitech released a gaming version of the Master 3 with weight customization and a DPI shift sniper button on the side like the G502, I'd buy it in a heartbeat. With all of that said, I'm currently doing playthroughs in Doom (2016) as well as Prey (2017) and the Master 3 is a perfect mouse for those games. It's been very enjoyable to play those games with the Master 3.

title: Would that I could give this zero stars--does not work.
text:
I chose this over a lower-priced ASUS board because the clean look of this board--not just the white aesthetic, but the fact that the I/O shield makes it feel sturdy and fit better in a case. The board is laid out well, though the RAM slots are (like many mobos) awfully close to the CPU, so your airflow/cooling options are limited as a result. If you have a big air cooler, you probably won't be putting 4 sticks of RAM in this. Just sayin'

But I don't want to bury the lede. I wanted to like this board. I wanted it to work to specs, but I bought one and it didn't work. Tried all sorts of troubleshooting. Spent literally months fiddling (took a while because I was doing it in my spare time), searching online (ASUS product support pages are awful) and troubleshooting.

My issues:
The QLED lights that are supposed to tell you if there's a problem with the RAM or CPU? Never lit.
No speaker beep going to POST.
No video output from the integrated HDMI/DisplayPort. No video output from dedicated GPU in slot 1 (HDMI or DisplayPort) or slot 2.
Stripped the build down, disconnected all the storage and took out everything but 1 stick of RAM. Still nothing.
Took the battery out, held the power button down, let the thing sit for an hour to clear the BIOS. Still nothing.
The 750-watt Corsair PSU works fine with other motherboards, so power is not the issue.
The issue is that I've spent months trying to get this board to work, hours upon hours of troubleshooting. I'm not an expert builder, but I'm not bad. But I cannot get this one to even beep and go to POST.

I spent so much time following the troubleshooting, sure that it couldn't be this mid-range board from a good manufacturer--must be something I was doing, right?--that I am no longer in Amazon's return window.

So I've requested an RMA with ASUS, but their oh-so-hopeful RMA page said I didn't enter a serial number (I did), and twice now when I've clicked "submit" I've been promised an email confirmation for my RMA and have yet to receive one. So I'm pretty steamed.

There are a lot of reviews of this board of people having the exact same problem as me--no video output, no POST, no beep, no QLEDs lit to indicate a problem--but most of them have a happy ending with people resetting the CMOS, or plugging a different output into their GPU, or flashing the BIOS (which I can't do, duh, because I have never gotten TO the BIOS). I think it's pretty poor product design when you have so many people who have to jump through so many hoops just to get the product to be usable.

I'm kind of locked in because I'm beyond the return window on a nonfunctional mobo, but I'm hoping ASUS makes this right. I'll edit this review if/when they get me a functioning motherboard. Ideally, one where I don't have to work for hours and hours just to get to POST.

title: Switching between apps/devices is not seamless, but I like them for online teaching!
text:
Preface: I am teaching virtually from home, and I am on Zoom/Google Meet calls for 6 out of 8 hours every work day. I have a MacBook Air and a Pixel 3a. I listen to Spotify on my phone as well as through the app on my computer. I show YouTube videos during class as well and watch Netflix or Hulu while lesson planning. I also have a puppy that is very vocal (barkity bark bark), and I live in an apartment complex with normal-to-thin walls (hello, neighbors' dogs). Recently, my lovely pup, Sir Barks-a-lot (not his real name), ate my headphones, so I decided to buy these because they're massive and the likelihood of me losing these is minimal.

Pros:
- Very comfortable and lighter than I thought they'd be.
- Easy to store, but big enough that I can't lose them.
- Sounds good for a someone who just wants to hear stuff (read as: not super judgmental about sounds)
- Battery life is dope (Charged it on Monday, and it is currently Wednesday, and I used them for 8 hours yesterday and most of today)
- Sound range is fantastic. I can listen to my computer from the other side of my apartment (1700 sq ft. - I have roommates and live in Michigan. I'm not rich).
- ANC and Hear-Through are neat features! Again, I'm not fancy, so I don't know if they're GREAT for ANC, but I think it's pretty cool that you can switch between modes! I CAN hear my doggo through them with ANC, but I cannot hear anything from any other room in the apt or my neighbors' apts.
- Connected almost immediately to my phone (again, Pixel 3a), and some set up was required for my computer (MacBook Air)
- When connected to Zoom on my computer, works very well!
- When connected to Google Meet on my computer, works very well!
- When connected to Spotify on my computer, works very well!
- When connected to Spotify on my phone, works very well!
- When calling on my phone, audio and mic sounded great!
- I asked my students if I looked cool yet, and they didn't say no... but then again, they didn't say anything because they were all muted with their cameras off. So I'm taking that as a win.

Cons (some of this might be user error):
- Switching between apps/devices is not seamless. Examples:
---- While I was on a Zoom and students were in breakout rooms, I received a call on my phone. When I tried to answer, the microphone and audio on both devices stopped working. I took the call with speaker phone, but when I went back to my Zoom, I couldn't hear my students, and they couldn't hear me. I turned off Bluetooth on both devices and taught the rest of class without headphones.
---- While I was on a Google Meet, the Google Meet window was sending and receiving from my headphones, but when I opened Youtube in another tab, the audio was coming from my computer and not going to my headphones. When I hung up the Google Meet, I thought it would autocorrect, but I had to go into my System Preferences and change output to these headphones.
---- When my computer is open and a Zoom meeting is happening, Spotify does not work on my phone. It will work from my computer, but I cannot control it from my phone.
---- When I am listening to something in a Chrome tab (let's say, hypothetically, Bones on Hulu), and I go into a Zoom meeting, the audio changes (I don't know what happens, but the hypothetical show sounds fuzzier).
---- I was on a Zoom, hung up, watched a few Youtube videos, went to the bathroom, and then hopped on another Zoom call, and the person on the other end said that there was loud buzzing and static that sounded like I was trying to blow out his eardrum.
---- When switching audio from my computer to my phone, the volume went to max for Spotify, and when I turned it down, it would automatically go to max volume. I had to restart all devices because it was blowing out my eardrums.
- My students tell me I sound fuzzy.
- Setting up audio and microphone from my computer was a little cumbersome and required some trial and error.

NOTE ONE: There was a software update that seemed to fix SOME (not all) of the issues!

Overall, I really like these headphones. They can be frustrating sometimes, but overall, I am glad I got them. I can wrestle my dog while listening to my computer without fear of dragging my computer to the ground. They're big enough that I can find them, and my dog won't eat them... hopefully.

WARNING (& UPDATE): if you have long hair, be careful! My hair got caught in the joint of the headphones and got pulled out :( I still like them though. Hair grows back.

title: Competent NAS for SOHO use.
text:
So after spending a couple of months with the QNAP NAS I think I am fairly comfortable offering a review . First, it's somewhat confusing to setup for the first time as a novice. The difficulty will be deciding on how you want to set up your hard drives, whether you want a RAID setup or use your drives as Single storage volumes or JBOD (using multiple disks as one volume). You need to be familiar with what Static/Thick/Thin volume types are in order to setup the drives. Once you get past this part of the setup, everything else runs smooth.

While there are many apps (mostly free) that you can download and use from the QNAP store, some get the job done, others are just terrible all together.

One of the biggest benefits of this NAS is being able to run docker containers. Container Station works but is lacking. Updating containers doesn't work at times since it changes the name of the container tags to something like (..data-1). Also, should your NAS go down in a power outage, your containers will not automatically restart since QNAP requires a system file check once booted back up after a power loss. If your away fom your NAS when this happens, you will have to remote in and perform the file check and then start the dockers containers manually. I ended up installing Portainer as a docker container through CLI and everything runs much better outside the Container Station limits. Watchtower also works, updating the containers and keeping the proper tags afterwards.

For torrenting, Download Station is pretty basic and has a lot of limitations. I installed Deluge as a container and have had no problems. I use Transdrone on my android mobile phone to add torrents remotely and have access to all the torrents.

QVPN works like it should, but I would like to set it up as a VPN client and have specific apps and containers use that while others not. Right now, it's all or nothing.

The 2GB memory model is VERY limited in what you can have running in the background. I run a few apps and containers and 2GB was not enough, so I updated the memory to 16GB. While the system claims it does NOT support anything over 8GB, it works fine with 2x the Crucial DRAM - 8GB DDR3 PC3-12800 Unbuffered NON-ECC 1.35V 1024Meg x 64 CT102464BF160B. Photo added to show that it does work. if you are considering this NAS and plan on using it to run containers or VM's, either get the 4GB or 8GB model, or get the 2GB and upgrade the memory yourself for less. I consider the 4GB as the minimum for a NAS in this price range and in order to take advantage of all it's strong points.

If you can't find any official apps on the QNAP store, you can always search for an app in the Un-Official QNAP club. Just be aware that these apps are user supported and may have separate dependencies that you will also need to download. Your other option is looking up docker containers and using Portainer to install them.

I also recommend you disable SSH access to the NAS. I found my NAS logging many attacks coming in from outside my network on port 22. I changed the port number and I only enable it when I need access to it, which I then turn off when I'm done. I've had no issues since.

title: Incredibly high comfort and build quality
text:
I'm not a terribly experienced person when it comes to IEM's, but I do own Shure SE215, KZ ZSNs, Tin Hifi T3's and Ikko OH10's to compare to. I'll mostly compare Shozy to OH10's as they're in the same price range.

Build quality, packaging:
Both Ikko's and Shozy feel like a very high-quality product when you first unpack them. However, over time Ikko's quality degraded and their lacquered surface started peeling off. Shozy seems incredibly high quality with nothing really to break/degrade. They also have exchangeable sound tubes that can be at least useful for cleaning as you can easily unscrew them. Ikko eartips have detached multiple times when when brushing against clothing/backpack for me, never happened with Shozy. There's wide enough selection of eartips included in Shozy packaging where I can find eartips bigger than needed, smaller than needed and multiple eartips of just the right size for me. I have kinda small ears and almost always use the smallest available tips from other earphones, but Shozy even have smaller tips than what I need.

Look & feel, comfort:
Shozy cable is amazing. The eartips themselves are weightless and fit amazingly well. I can run for a whole hour straight without re-fitting my earphones. Cable is pre-formed and sits very snuggly around my ears. I can wear them all day in my ears or dangling on my neck no problem. This is absolutely not the case with Ikko's as those are very(like, extremely) heavy, swingy and their earhooks constantly fall off my ears somehow because the hooks are just too big and go wide over my ears instead of around. Overall level of comfort with these Shozy's is so high that it kinda overwhelms all other aspects honestly. Why don't all manufacturers just follow the same exact design? It just works and it's just perfect. Shure headphones try to follow a similar design but they're nowhere near as comfortable as these Shozy.

Cable, connectors:
The only minor complain I have about the cable is the long jack that acts as a long lever and applies unnecessary pressure to my phone/laptop headphone jack socket. Literally everything else about this cable is great: it somehow does not tangle at all (Ikko OH10's are always tangled in comparison due to some black magic that escapes any reasoning), connectors are secure and earhooks fit me great. Why can't every manufacturer just use a cable exactly like this one and just change its appearence if needed?

Sound isolation:
I never owned BA-only headphones before and this is kinda new to me. Shozy's are completely sealed (there's no path for air to enter or escape the earphone) and because of that sound isolation is incredible. Even too much for my liking because I literally can't hear anything from the outside even if I want to. Also when sound stops (like, song ends for example) it creates this feeling of deafness when you literally hear nothing and it's kind of scary, same to how earplugs work. But I bet it's a good thing for most people.

Sound quality:
There's a very distinct difference between Ikko OH10's and Shozy's: Ikko has very punchy and maybe more natural sound than Shozy's. For some reason first time I listened to Shozy's I had a very clear image of them somehow sounding like when you rub a rubber balloon. It's a very strange comparison, but they do have something similar to that squeaky rubbing sound in their sound signature. It's not terrible, but I do honestly prefer the sound of Ikko's.

Verdict:
I have compared these Shozy's to its closest competitor in the same price range that I own: Ikko OH10's. Shozy's have far superior level of comfort to wear, subjectively better build quality and better thought out user experience. Sound isolation is scary good, cable is great, they feel great to handle. Sound quality, however, is a little strange compared to Ikko (that sound really good), but over time I kinda got used to it and now I stopped noticing any strangeness. That being said, if I had to choose, I'd definitely choose these Shozy over Ikko OH10's.

title: One of the best additions to my home theater - bar none.
text:
SUMMARY
The BST-1 is not a necessity for a home theater, but boy does it add something to the overall theater experience. I don't think I will ever go back to watching movies w/o them turned on. I think "Bass Shaker" although techincally is what it does, to me seems to have a negative tone to it. Properly setup think of it as a subwoofer extension. They seem to be built well, and have lots of heat sinks to get rid of the heat when driven hard.

CONFIGURATION:
As great as these are, they need to be installed and setup properly. The BST-1 needs to be anchored very securely to a flat wood surface for maximum performance and to eliminate rattles. Much like the configuration of all of the speakers in your home theater it is important that everything is balanced properly. If you look at these as an extension to your subwoofer like your subwoofer is an extension using bass management to your center / L/R/Surround / heights etc. The BST-1 is rated at 10-80 hz, but will make sounds at higher frequency's so it is important to have the signal crossed over (the install guide says 80hz), I have mine at 80hz w/ the sub crossover and it seems fine. So when very low frequency's occur in movie sound tracks your sub is doing what it can, but these add that extra low freq (even below human hearing). Its the really low frequencies is where these really shine to "extend" the overall low frequency impact that your home theater has. I also find that I can run the subwoofer (and the overall theater) at a lower output and with the BST-1. The experience is more enjoyable and better at the lower sound levels plus the BST-1. There are other "bass shakers" out there but they are more expensive and I would have a hard time to imagine that they would be that much better.

INSTALL DETAILS (For those who want to know)
I am using (3) in a sectional with a wood frame (see pics). The sectional sits on a concreate floor. These are 4 ohms each I have (2) wired in series for total 8 ohm load to one of the amp channels and (1) wired to the other amp channel. I then paned the amp output to the speakers in series to balance out the power and level. I am using a 100w per channel amp dedicated to these (an old 2 channel receiver) so I can shut them off (and adjust the volume) / balance if needed. The input to the amp is the sub output of the home theater receiver (that handles my other speakers) sub crossed over at 120 hz. spilt to the L/R channels of the dedicated amp.
For video games, we up the level, for movies we turn it down so it just "hits" when it adds to the movie and does not distract normally. I found that I needed to tighten some of the parts on the sectional to avoid vibrations at the very lowest frequencies.

Update 2-23-22 - Still going strong after about 2 years of use at least 1 / week. Updated crossover for the Sub and BST-1 from 120hz down to 80 hz. My Front/Surround/Ceiling all crossed over at 80 hz now. I think they (The BST-1) work better crossed over at 80 vs 120hz. Still a great investment in my opinion.

GOOD DEMO's for the BST-1
Jumanji - Welcome the jungle - (any scene where the games drums are playing)
Solo - A Star Wars Story - The scene with the explosion of the train of coaxium
Avatar
Any movie with low bass

title: MAC address masking
text:
This Extender masks all MAC addresses that connect to it. This means when a new client connects to the Extender, the REAL MAC gets added to the router so it can connect there, and the FAKE MAC gets added to the Extender so it can connect there. This actually makes it worthless to me as the DHCP server assigns static leases based on MAC the address. My router/firewall currently has about 50 known (allowed) WiFi devices. That's an obnoxious amount of duplication. Even if I'm not using the Access Control filtering on the Extender, it still masks the MAC to the DHCP server. If the MAC masking was turned off when the Access Control is, then I'd give this 5 stars.

Furthermore, after upgrading the firmware, all the FAKE MAC addresses got re-enumerated, which nullified all the previous allowances it entered in my Router/DHCP Server/Firewall so I had to start from scratch again.

From the Extender's manual...

"Q5.I have enabled wireless MAC filter, wireless access control, or access control list (ACL) on my router. What should I do before configuring the extender?

When a device connects through the extender to your router, the MAC address of the device shown on the router is translated to another MAC address. If your router’s MAC filter, wireless access control, or ACL is enabled, the devices connected to the extender cannot get an IP address from the extender and cannot access the Internet.

To solve this problem, please follow the steps below:

1.Log in to your router and disable the MAC filter, wireless access control or ACL.
Note: For more information about how to disable your router’s MAC filter, wireless access control or ACL, please refer to your router’s user guide.
2.Power on your extender, and run the Quick Setup to configure your extender.
3.Connect all of your devices to the extended network.
4.On your router, add all the Online Devices’ MAC addresses to your router’s MAC filter table.
5.Enable the router’s MAC filter, wireless access control, or ACL to complete the configuration. "

title: Addressable RGB Goodness
text:
This review is for the recently released DEEPCOOL GAMMAXX GT A-RGB.

I purchased this because it has the latest addressable RGB technology which uses a 5V 3 wire connection. My Asrock motherboard has the matching 3 pin addressable RGB connector. The CPU cooler and fan have separate 3 wire connectors which can be joined then connected to the motherboard. The motherboard software then controls the lighting pattern. The lighting looks great.

Note that the lighting continues even after the computer is shut down, unless you turn it off in the software or the motherboard BIOS.

The cooler fan is 120mm with a standard 4 wire PWM connector, and is much quieter than my stock AMD Wraith Stealth cooler. I haven't run any tests but I'm sure this cools much better as well.

The instructions are pictorial only and could probably be a little clearer, but if you know how to build a PC you should be able to figure them out. Keep in mind this cooler is quite tall. If you have a standard layout case, it should fit, but measure to be sure.

title: A must-have accessory for anyone who travels
text:
I wasn't sure was in the box that Amazon delivered... I didn't think I'd ordered anything that small. But as they say, good things come in small packages.

This ships tightly coiled in the box and I was dreading having to "train" the wire to relax and not bungee back like a phone cord, but it only took a couple of stretches and massages before it stayed mostly straight on it's own. It still has a bit of curl to help keep it neatly wrapped in my laptop bag. I recommend a velcro tie to keep it neat when you're traveling

The rotating plug is a lifesaver when traveling since outlets aren't always easy to reach, especially when you still need to keep the desk lamp or alarm clock plugged in by your bed.

The on/off switch is flat to the surface of the box when off and latches below the surface when on, so there's virtually no risk of bumping it and turning the power off accidentally and it's easy to see if the power is on or off.

Having 3 usb ports means I don't have to switch between my phone, my earbuds and my watch at night while my laptop charges on the outlet, and that's 3 less things to forget at checkout.

I was also surprised how light it is - I've carried all sorts of power strips in my laptop bag and this is one of the lightest that has a USB adapter built in. This cord has earned a home in my laptop bag and I'll fight any airport security that tries to take it! :)

title: Missed the mark, would not buy again
text:
I have had this thing for several weeks now. I have a 70 mile round trip commute and I have taken it on several multi-day road trips.

I am a pretty big advocate for Pioneer products and have owned many of them in the past - head units, speakers, etc... They normally perform well and are very intuitive. This one, not so much.

(skip this paragraph if you don't care about installation info)
I installed it myself in a 2010 CRV. Pretty straightforward and easy. For any vehicle installation, you will need a dash kit, a wiring harness, antenna adapter (if required), and simple tools. I also got a parking brake bypass. YouTube has videos showing you how to take apart the dash for most vehicles. If you plan on adding an amp, you will have to find another way to trigger the remote in the event you are installing it in a vehicle that has an antenna amp *or* if you are using a parking brake bypass because BOTH require use of the single remote wire. I soldered everything together and used heat shrink tube to cover the wires. I ran the USB out of the upper glove box and installed the microphone through one of the small filler panels by the steering wheel.

First, the appearance. The unit itself looks fine. Nothing crazy. A little more glossy that I would like though. The screen looks great....until the sun shines on it...or until it starts getting smudged up...which is immediately. I picked this particular model over others because it had the bigger screen. The dimmer works and is adjustable. You can select a color scheme that matches your vehicle's interior/dash lighting, which is nice. You can also arrange icons, how you want them to appear on certain screen, in the settings.

Second, the audio. It did in fact make my factory speakers sound better, but there are two catches. The first catch is the sounds quality. If you listen closely, you can hear what faintly sounds like a CD skipping very quickly. It is like the stereo is only playing 99% of the sound and taking a break for the last 1%. It is very obvious in parts of music where there is a lot going on - many instruments playing, lots of noise/sound singing, etc. Once you notice this happening, you will never be able to ignore it from that point forward. It just sounds like the audio is not "pure." Like it is only partially there. I suspect this has something to do with the D/A converter or some software issue.

The other audio catch is when you get a phone call. When you use your phone the audio changes in order to make the voices more pronounced - nice. I like it. The problem is, when you are done with your call, it doesn't change back to how it was. Now your music sounds weird. You have to unplug/disconnect your phone and reconnect for it go back to normal.

Third, the graphic user interface (GUI). Bottom line up front - the menus and overall operation are very frustrating. You will press one button and it will take you to a screen. Press it again and it either does nothing or goes to different screen, rarely back to the screen you wanted. Try the other button. Nope.

But wait, I swear it took me back to the screen I wanted a minute ago? The operation of this menu system changes depending on what you are doing. Using Carplay? Menus will now be different again. Super annoying. No consistency. Never had a stereo that acts like this one. As well, when you don't have your phone plugged in or connected through BT, it does nothing. Just says "stop" or nothing at all on the screen. It does not default to the radio. It just sits there in silence. You have to touch this strange drop down icon that shows you all the main functions....which is very different from every other GUI feature on the stereo. Makes no sense why they did this considering it is so different than everything else in the GUI.

Another quirk, it follows what you are doing on your phone. Want to read a text? Click on the text icon on your phone and the stereo screen follows. Why? Not like I can read the text on the stereo anyways. Why not stay on the music screen? Does the same thing when you do other things on your phone as well. What if you are trying to navigate somewhere? Too bad. Your screen is changing. Super annoying. But in a twist of irony, the stereo WILL NOT do this when you want it to, like with youtube. It is like Pioneer intentionally wanted to let people know they could make it happen, but chose not to just to mess with you.

But the worst....WORST part is how it works with Google and Apple maps. Sometimes you can move the map with your fingers, sometimes not. No rhyme or reason to it - vehicle in motion or not. Get a call? Navigation is no longer on your screen. Doesn't matter how many buttons you push. You have to touch the app icon now instead and there it is, still navigating. Disconnect your phone for a second? Too bad, your route is over. You have to set it up again, unlike when just using it on your phone.

Strangely, there are two different "now playing" screens for your music too. One is organized and familiar with song name, artist, album name, clear and crisp disc art. The other is a full screen display with giant previous/play/pause/next icons along with the disc art faded into the background. Why? I am not even sure how to get to this screen. Sometimes I stumble onto it by accident I guess.

These probably sound like nitpicks to some people, but in daily use this stuff gets really annoying.

Edit 1. I found a third now playing screen that is different than the others. I guess the first two were just not enough. Also, I used the drop down to select the radio instead of connecting my phone when I got in the CRV today. Drove to Lowe's. Came back out, started the CRV, now it was on a completely different radio screen that I did not select. This is probably the most annoying stereo I have ever dealt with.

Edit 2. After over 6 months of ownership, I dislike it more than ever. Some more quirks... If you open FB while connected, it stops playing whatever source you were listening to...except when it doesn't. There seem to be no rhyme or reason to it. Maybe I watched a video on FB and it thinks I still am? No. I tested it.

And I can't believe it took me months to realize this... THERE IS NO RADIO SCAN BUTTON/FUNCTION. They have this "Best Station Memory" thing that is supposed to find the six strongest stations in your area and put them as presets. However, this is not scan. There is also some "TuneScan" thing that is useless as well because it only works with Sirius/XM. No radio scan function? Are you freaking serious right now, Pioneer?

Pioneer, fire the menu designers, fix the D/A converter and this might be salvageable. Until then, I can’t recommend this stereo to anyone. Stop using engineers and employees as beta testers. Use normal people.

title: Great Budget Headphone Amp
text:
Headphone amps are great for driving and bringing out the full sound of your headphones, especially if they're open back and have a high impedance. However, the good headphone amps that actually improve the sound and aren't just a volume control usually cost a bit of money. That is until this surprising device hit the market. Prior to this headphone amp, the best and most affordable amp that improved sound was from the Fiio series of amps. And as you can see, this amp is designed a lot like those amps that are quite popular. However, this amp is made by Lvy and while it might not be as good as the Fiio series, it does its job of improving your headphones.

I have a Sennheiser HD 599 headphones, and they are pretty good with no amp attached. It has a mid range impedance of 50 so it isn't hard to drive using normal devices like smart phones, computers, televisions, etc. However, this amp improved the sound by making the bass, treble, and mid-range sound cleaner, and it really brought out the soundstage. So much so, that using these headphones beyond listening to music is an event as it seems to simulate a spacial sound field making the actions on screen feel like 3D surround sound, and I don't mean the fake version that sound like you're listening in a tunnel.

The amp has a volume control and a high and low gain switch, which is used determine how much you want the amp to drive the headphones. I have it on low gain, as I found high gain drives it too much and can be overpowering. But again, my headphones don't need much driving, so high gain might be good for someone who owns a 300 impedance headphone like the HD 600. The headphone also comes with a USB charger you can connect to your PC and any device that has a enough power to charge it. Note: In some devices, connecting the USB charger cable can cause noise if you're still using the amp at the same time. When the light turns blue, the amp is ready to go and it last for many hours before needing another charge. The only downside in the headphone cable that comes with it. It is very flimsy and looks easy to break. I guess cost had to be cut somewhere. Luckily, its a standard 3.5mm connection cable, not some custom made industry cable you need to pay a lot of money to replace. Meaning, you can easily replace it with a better one.

Bottle line: This is a great amp for the price. I'm sure there are more expensive amps that might do a better job driving headphones and making them sound more realistic and live, but this amp does the job. You will notice an immediate difference in your music as it will sound a lot better, especially if you own a pair of open back, audiophile based headphones.

title: I copied 4-55 GB of files on to the flash drive to test its (write) speed...
text:
I did five tests to see how long it would take to copy files onto one of these flash drives.

I copied over 4.7 GB, 9.5 GB, 20.1 GB, 40.3 GB and 55.8 GB. Read my review below to see how fast it copied files over during each test...

Test 1) I copied 4.76 GB of videos onto the flash drive from my computer. The computer prompt displayed it would take approx. 10 minutes to complete. I also set my timer to comfirm accuracy about how long it would REALLY take to complete the transfer. Once it was done, my timer displayed it only took 9:31 (9 min. 31 sec.) to complete. So it was a teeny bit faster than the computer approximated. During this test I wasn't doing much in the background--I opened up a few files for a few minutes and that was it--while the transfer was taking place.

Test 2) I copied over 9.57 GB of videos onto the flash drive. The computer display showed it would take approx. 27 minutes to complete. I once again set my timer to confirm the amount of time it would take to complete the transfer. Once the transfer finished, my timer displayed it took 19:27 to complete. So that was around 7 minutes faster than the computer approximated. I wasn't doing much in the background--I opened up a few files and that was it--while the transfer was taking place.

Test 3) I copied over 20.1 GB of videos onto the flash drive. The computer showed an estimated time of 30 minutes for it to complete. I set my timer again. During this test I WAS working in the background. I was opening files and uploading files to my server regularly. My timer displayed it took 38:15 for the transfer to complete. Eight minutes over the computer's estimation.

Test 4) I copied over 40.3 GB of videos onto the flash drive. The computer displayed it would take about 1 hour to complete. My timer was set once again, for confirmation. During this test, I WAS working in the background UNTIL 44% OF THE WAY THROUGH the transfer, then I stopped working on my computer completely. During the time I was working on my computer, I was opening files and publishing to my server. My timer clocked the time it took to complete the transfer at 1:13:08 (1 hr. 13 min. 08 sec.). Thirteen minutes over the computer's estimation.

Test 5) I copied over 55.8 GB of videos onto the flash drive. Estimated time the computer showed it would take to complete the transfer was 1 hour and 10 minutes. My timer was once again set. It took about 1 hr. 39 min. for the transfer based on my timer. This is about 29 minutes over the computer's estimation. I may be off by a minute or two because just as I clicked the timer button to stop, my timer reset on me. I have no idea how this happened, but luckily noted the time on my timer at 1 hr. 38 min. just before the transfer was about to be complete. I barely did anything in the background. Opened a few files in Google Docs on my computer and that was about it.

Here's a quick summary of how long it took to copy over each file size:

1) 4.76 GB (9 min.)
2) 9.57 GB (19 min.)
3) 20.1 GB (38 min.)
4) 40.3 GB (1 hr. 13 min.)
5) 55.8 GB (1 hr. 39 min.)

One thing worth noting, in case this makes a slight difference is, I erased the previous files on the flash drive before I did each new transfer. So, I started with an empty flash drive each time. I don't really think having files on the flash drive when you copy new ones over is going to make (much of) a difference, but just in case it does (since I don't know about these things) I thought it was worth mentioning.

On average, the write speed was between 7-10 mb/s. Keep in mind, the time it takes might fluctuate a little bit from user to user, but this will give you a pretty solid idea of how quickly the flash drive(s) operate.

The results above only reflect the testing of one of the flash drives I received. I haven't tested the other to see if results are consistent.

So the flash drive is pretty fast and meets my needs. I expected to pay a lot more for flash drives with really fast read and write speeds and went with this option instead after reading other positive reviews. I'm very happy that I did. It delivered above and beyond what I expected.

I hope this review helps you make a good purchase decision, regarding whether these flash drives will meet your needs or not.
