title: a119 v3 seems unreliable when hardwired
text:
I bought an A119 V3 2560 x 1600P Dash Camera with GPS Logger and CPL 2019 Edition on October 11, 2019. Until a month ago, I've been using it plugged into a cigarette lighter USB power adapter and it has worked fine. Last month I bought a second camera (the VIOFO A119 V3 2560 x 1600P Quad HD+ Dash Camera with GPS Logger and CPL 2020 Edition) to go in the rear window and wired them both up with the HK3ACC hardwire kits. I have been using a 256GB Samsung EVO Plus in the original and bought another for the second camera. Things worked OK including parking mode for the first week, then I started hitting the problems around 10/15/2020. WEIRD HOW THE CAMERA JUST WENT OUT OF WARRANTY, EH?

1. If the cameras turn off due to low battery detection on the hardwire kit, I have to physically unplug both of them to get them to resume normal recording. Otherwise, they get stuck in some wierd half-parking-mode thing and don't record properly.

2. The first camera that's a year old appears to have finally succumbed to the annual Wuhan Digital Flu and randomly locks up on me, requiring a power cycle to recover to working. The display screen also now shows random noise artifacts while it's on. Also, the unit will sometimes boot and fail to start recording, and though it shows the camera view in the display the buttons do nothing. It also sometimes just starts randomly beeping at me and I have to press the REC button to make it stop beeping and press it again to start recording again though this beeping thing is extremely rare).

3. The new camera is better behaved at switching to/from parking mode. It also frequently just decides to start beeping at me, whereupon I have to press REC twice to stop the pain and start it recording again. Not feasible in traffic for the rear window. I've not seen the new camera lock up solid on me like the other one.

I've run the full h2testw 1.4 destructive write/verify tests and I get solid 80MB/sec speeds and no errors on them. I have a couple of 64GB Endurance Pro cards coming tomorrow so we'll see if that changes anything.

So, basically, if you just want a plain-jane dashcam with no parking mode and are willing to go do some research and trial-and-error testing of SDCards, this camera probably works fine for about a year. Don't expect a lot out of it, though. Picture quality is pretty good but the options for that aren't the easiest to figure out considering the anemic user manual.

Based on the apparent unreliability of these and how much more painful to use they are than my old Mobius ActionCam that I used for years before "upgrading," I would not recommend these. Either stick with a cheap model you can replace frequently when they die or spend the extra money for a good quality Thinkware or something else. I was so happy with that thing the first year. Damn shame.

[edit] 12/1/2020 - Nope, the Samsung Pro Endurance 64GB SDCard made no difference; camera will no longer boot properly 90% of the time. It's dead.

title: Great idea, poor execution
text:
I swim frequently - usually 3-4 times a week, each lasting about an hour or so. I've been through essentially all major waterproof mp3 players in the market. I really wanted to like the Delphin and I've actually been looking forward to it. I've been a long-time user of the waterproof shuffle also from the same company and I've been a big fan of their products (and their customer service).

Sadly, Delphin has changed my mind about this company. This is not a good device.

Here are the problems that I have with the new Delphin:
1. Bluetooth connectivity with their bluetooth headphones is very bad. The headphones connection keeps getting cut out continuously. Disconnecting and reconnecting does not fix it. Forgetting it and adding as a new device does not fix it. I think the headphones is just a very bad product and it feels very bulky and cheap and rubbery.
2. Battery life is very poor. At full charge I only managed to get an hour and half before completely dying. It seems to be eating up about 8-9% for each 3-4 minute song. It does charge pretty fast though.
3. Delphin does not connect to my PC or my macbook. On my PC, it keeps chiming in saying that a new USB device has been detected but it disconnects a second later and chimes back out. I've been trying to wirelessly download onto Delphin but the touch screen is very very tiny so it is very very frustrating. This also means that you can't charge the device via your USB drive and must be charged by directly plugging it into the wall (not included).
4. Delphin is very bulky and has difficulty staying clipped on. The unit is significantly bigger and heavier compared to the shuffle and it should because its got wireless/bluetooth technology with touch screen while the shuffle was first released back in 2010. But because it is bigger and heavier, it does not stay clipped onto your goggle straps. This is especially challenging if you're using Swedish goggles. As soon as you start your sprint set, the Delphin flips off and floats away. Forget about clipping it onto your suit because that's way too far for fragile bluetooth connection to stay on.
5. Control is very cumbersome. There are hard buttons at the top that control volume and forward/back track. One button does both volume up and next track depending on how you press the button. It NEVER does what you want it to. When trying to increase the volume, it skips to next track. When you try to skip to next track, it increases the volume. Forget about using touch screen instead because the device is clipped to the back of your skull (plus your hands are wet so touch screen is very hard to use, especially on a small screen).
6. Price point is very high for what it is. Compared to other devices that have similar functionality, it is very expensive. It is the only one of its kind so I guess price is whatever they call it.

Also, be aware that this is not returnable via Amazon. Many of us Prime members are used to being able to make returns with ease with packaging and labels provided. This is not the case with Delphin as Amazon does not take returns on these. So make sure you're ok with above before you buy it!

I've contacted the customer service to remedy these issues - bluetooth and USB connection issues. Hopefully these issues are worked out and my experience with Delphin improves.

title: Only download ONE language at a time.
text:
The T8S Voice Translator is an excellent AI translation device. I received it as a gift and I am so pleased that it works so well. The voice translations and the photo translations are virtually instantaneous.
Some things I discovered while setting up and using the translator:
1 Make sure you charge the device right out of the box. A 5V 1A output-charging cube works.
2 Set up your Hotspot from your phone—you can rename the hotspot to something you like. A number password is easier to enter on the device because if you use an alphabetical or alphanumerical password it is harder to enter. The Alpha keys are setup as abc, def, ghi, per number key, also the space key is hard to find. Turn on your Hotspot on your phone.
3 Turn on the translator and swipe right to left to left to get to the page two.
4 Tap on “Internet connection,” make sure the upper right-hand slider is to the right (the On Position).
5 Select the name of your Hotspot and enter your password.
6 Swipe left to right to get back to the main page
7 Tap on “Speech translation” and select the language at the top to open a menu to select the language you want as your HOME language. It will be in Red Text. Then tap on the language at the bottom to select the language you want your HOME language translated TO, it will be in Blue Text.
8 Press the lower left “Swish” button and HOLD IT DOWN, “Start Talking” will appear, THEN you speak into the speaker. Let go, and the translation will appear and be broadcast aloud. Press the lower right “Swish” button and HOLD IT DOWN, “Start Talking” will appear, THEN the other person speaks to the device. Let go, and the translation will appear and be broadcast aloud in your HOME language. If you tap on the speaker icon it will repeat the translation.
9 The circle button between the minus and the plus symbols will take you back to the main page.
10 To setup the “Offline translation” tap on the Blue Chinese (Traditional) language and that will bring up a menu to select a language to download. Make sure your translation device and your phone are plugged into their chargers because it takes some time to download a language.
11 To the right of each language there is a download symbol to tap on.
12 THIS IS IMPORTANT: only download ONE language at a time. You must wait until it has completely downloaded to be able to select it as an Offline language. Each language is somewhere between 300mb to 500mb. Total storage is about 2.1GB. Do not do anything else with the device while it is downloading a language. Each language must be stored as a continuous file in memory. I suggest that you download only the three or four languages that you know you may need offline.
13 If you had attempted to download several languages, all at once, none of them will work and you may have to go to settings and tap on “Clear usage record” to clear memory before you download a language.
14 Now everything should work!

title: Great case for use as a laptop or tablet.
text:
Edit: January 2022
Case is still going strong. Keyboard still works great and stays charged for days. Some fading on the color on some areas handled a lot in the case but not very much or noticeable.

I purchased this case during the Cyber Monday sale as I was needing a case with a keyboard. I am loving the rose gold color and the backlit keys are definitely a bonus as someone who works nights in a very low lit room. The backlit lights come in 12 different color variations and 3 different light intensities. I have it at the brightest option and have had no issues with the lighting. I also appreciate how the lights do not stay on when the keyboard is not in use, as this assists with battery life. The battery life works great. I work 12 to 14 hour shifts and have not once needed to charge the keyboard during a shift. The keyboard is a great size. I have put a picture with a pen for reference. For me, the touchpad would move when I was typing so I now turn off the touchpad (hold down fn and T) when I am not using it. In addition to rubber gripping on the bottom corners to prevent sliding, there are rubber stoppers on the right and left side of the key board for further protection of the screen, preventing the top half from slamming into the bottom keyboard when closing. There is also an opening where the iPad charging port is, so you can charge your iPad with the case on. The apple pen fits well in the holder. The top can be a little wobbly but for the price I paid I can make do. I purchased this particular case over others with a keyboard for the rotating screen, and it has not disappointed. The only reason i am giving this 4 stars instead of 5, is because I noticed twice now that my iPad was slightly out on the top right side corner, despite proper installation. I may have just received a faulty case, and need to get in touch with the seller for this issue. All in all I am very happy with my purchase and would recommend this case for someone who would like to use their iPad as both a laptop and tablet.

title: Good purchase and uses all Canon Lenses (some with adapters) EF, EF-S, EOS-M and FD lenses!
text:
Added EOS-M6 to my photo equipment set, which includes M1, M2 & M3 bodies and 22 lenses with EF, EF-S, EOSM and FD mounts. Canon fails to tell you that all the old, wonderful FD lenses work perfectly (in manual Mode) on the EOS-M camera bodies. For years my FD lenses (designed for A1, FTb, F1 bodies) were stranded when Canon moved to the ES mounts and changed the dimensions of the focal plane. With the Fotodiox adapter FD-EOSM, all FD lenses work perfectly on this body including the FD macro lenses 50 f 3.5, 100 f 4, and 200 f 4. Macro lenses do not need autofocus, so save yourself lots of money and pick up some good used FD lenses and extension tubes. FD autobellows (with the Fotodiox adapter) works fine with this camera for extended macro work.

Recommend that you only use the Canon Mount adapter for EF-EOS M for EFand EF-S lens use. Buy used - like new for a little over $100.

The M6 camera is an update to the M3 with a few minor changes. It came in the original box matching the serial number and appears in all aspects as new. Price was great at $399.

For video work, consider the EOS-M50. I like the compact EOSM bodies for aerial photography and ease of carry. Over 40 years experience with Canon cameras, and still enjoying their products.

title: Just Ok, not ready for prime time.
text:
Not ready for prime time. There are a lot of pluses for the Echo Buds over the Air Pods but unfortunately there are also a couple of deal killers. The fit is very good and they stay put much better than the Air Pods. The sound is as good if not slightly better than the Air Pods after a bit of tweaking with the EQ in the Alexa app and Alexa seems to work great.

The biggest issues I have are the occasional drop outs and popping sound. I have only experienced this two times so far, both times on a plane and could have been caused by something in the environment??? There were obviously a lot of people on Bluetooth near me, not sure if that is a thing or not but since I only noticed it twice and in the same location both times, could be.

Pairing is not as easy as Air Pods or other bluetooth devices I've used but that's not a deal killer, it's still pretty simple.

The BIG issue I have is the charging case!!! If you do not set the buds in perfectly they do not charge. And I'm pretty sure that even if you do set them in perfectly they can jostle in the case to where they do not charge. Three times in just two weeks I've pulled them out to use them and one or both of the buds have been dead even though the case was fully charged. It is nice that I could put them back in the case for 15 minutes and that got me through two movies on a plane.

Bottom line, I like them and will keep them but will probably use my Air Pods most of the time.

title: I've always purchased Verbatim, and this model does not write at 4-6x!
text:
I've always purchased/used Verbatim CD/DVD/BD media for data security, but this model, BD-R 50GB 6x media, plainly sucks. (2019.06.28 Verbatim finally sent 2x's 10 packs replacement media for the failed media I tried burning at 4-6x's. I've bumped back up to 4 stars.)

The error I'm likely encountering is likely a known 4-6x write speed defect with this media, likely encountered during switching to the second layer or after writing 25GB of data. (See #5 below.)

1) This is not 6x media from my experience. I've only recently attained a good write on two pieces of this media at 1x speed using an LG WH16NS60.

2) I resorted to buying a new LG WH16NS60 drive after burning ~20-25 bad media at 6x's, in both Linux & Windows 10. (Windows 10 apparently defaults to 6x writing.) My slightly older LG WH14NS40 was probably operating just fine, and I just needed to rule-out dust on the lens.

3) Wrote an Email to Verbatim technical support using their web form. Well oddly, I never received a CC (carbon copy) of the digital support request for this issue via Email. Calling their technical support, I had difficultly explaining the problem due to the inadequate English language speaking skills of the Verbatim employee. It is now midday Wednesday and still no replay after sending the Email Friday evening or midday Saturday. (Since I have no CC via Email like most other companys do, cannot recall the exact time/day, etc.)

4) I'm extremely tempted to buy the cheaper 50GB media to avert wasting time and money. I cannot imagine risking money upon the expensive M-disc technology.

5) There error provided by growisofs, as Windows provides little to no error information, is "WRITE@LBA=b87780h failed with SK=5h/ASC=21h/ACQ=04h]: Invalid argument" which apparently occurs at after writing ~25GB of data, and likely during switching to the second layer. The writing speed and switching to the second layer are likely related to this error code.

Bottom line, likely best to continue buying/using <25GB media, unless you want to fiddle constantly with write settings going beyond typical users' skill levels.

(Just checked my Spam/XXX mailbox, absolutely no replies from Verbatim.)

2019.06.28: Restored review as iterated within first paragraph. Received 2x10 pack media this same make/model for the failed media I tried writing at the specified 4-6x write speeds. I'm now having good success at 2x's and sometimes 4x's write speed.

title: Need a few ports? This is works
text:
So I purchased an iMac 2019 model with usb c ports. I know this isn't marketed for that but more for laptops. For what I was looking for, this was perfect though. I wanted to have few ports accessible on the front of the iMac without having to go behind it. I'm a part time photographer so I needed a SD card slot and I have a Wacom tablet so the usb 2 port is perfect for that. I can unplug it when I'm not using it and again not have to go back behind my computer to plug it in.

The good thing about this is the port are all on one side and it is way less expensive than most other options here on amazon. It would be nice to have an addition USB 3 port but not a deal breaker for me. I was expecting it to feel cheap and come in a brown paper bag or something because of it's price but I was surprised at how nice the packaging was that it came in. Also, the silicon mold around the hub is really nice too.

The one negative thing I noticed was that when plugging it in to my iMac, I noticed I had to force it a little bit. Could be my iMac though.

Overall, it is a great product. If you are planning on using it for a laptop, it is perfect. If you just need a few ports accessible from the front of your iMac. This is a good option. (FYI, I purchased a right angle usb-c adapter which helped a little bit but not necessary)

Update- you may have seen another review mention that this company was giving out rebates if you leave a review. Well I did try to receive my rebate but never heard back from the company. I was honest in my original review. Although since I’ve been using the adapter for over 3 months now, I’ve found one major issue. Several of my images on my SD cards have been corrupted. I’ve never had this happen before. It’s happened to several cards too. As a photographer, I can’t trust the SD card slot on this unit. That’s why I’m dropping the review down to 3 stars.

Hope you find the adapter your looking for. If you grab this one, I hope you have better luck than I did.

title: Great Case! Highly recommended!
text:
[[VIDEOID:1fd7168f4b888a1d69ff5034afc546fe]] I LOVE THIS CASE! I have received numerous compliments and requests to help others build their computer with this case since I bought it. The metal and tempered glass seem to be high-quality and give the computer some extra weight.
- This case came with the 6 RGB fans installed and pre-wired for quicker install.
- The case comes with several extra screws for your hardware.
- The PSU has its own cavity as do the HDD(s) - you can install up to 3.
- The backside of the case provides a nice space to run wires and zip tie them together.
- There are plenty of openings to allow wires through and connect components without all the wiring exposed.

A few recommendations when setting up your computer:
- The instructions for installing the HDD do advise you will need HDD 3.5 trays, but you really do not. You can rest your HDD on a lip on one side and will need to add screws through the other side from the front of the case (behind the fans). This worked best for me as I could NOT find ANYONE who was selling these trays.
- Page 11 of the instructions tell you to "Connect the 3-pin ARGB wire to the MOB - THIS IS OPTIONAL.
You should ONLY connect to your MOB if you intend to control the RGB lights from your computer. By connecting this wire to the MOB, the fans will run but the RGB lights will not turn on and the RGB button will not function. Plus, if you're not careful, you can cause damage to your MOB. By not plugging this wire into your MOB, you will be able to control the RGB lights and settings using the RGB button the case.
- The PCI slots are solid plastic. I would recommend purchasing metal vented slots, although this seems minor, these solid slots were suffocating my GPU, which has 2 additional fans pre-installed. These fans pushed the hot air down towards the bottom, but it seemed as through it did not have an opening to escape. After removing the plastic PCI slots, it seemed to provided additional airflow out of the vent and cooled the interior further. PCI replacements measure about 12.1cm (4.76in) in length which fit the best, but you can get away with 12cm (4.75in), they're slightly loose but still do the job.
- The connection for the 3.0 USB seems to be a tad loose, so i had to zip-tie both connections to the case to hold them in place.

Overall, I highly recommend this case so long as you heed my advise above.
I have provided the amazon link to several friends to purchase one of these cases as well.

title: Get used to the sync with your phone before going onto the lake
text:
Pretty easy to set up once you figure out the phone WIFI and the Lowrance system. I highly recommend playing around with it in a tub of water before going out into a lake. I spent a couple of hours figuring out a sequence of how to reset my phone WIFI and then connecting to the fish finder (when it was actively transmitting) to sync them together. The method that I found worked best with my LG phone (even though it didn't repeat every time) was to log into the phone app, turn off my land phone WIFI, plug in the charger cord momentarily into the fish finder, remove the cord, put the fish finder into water in the sink , turn on my phone WIFI and connect to the fish finder. This sequence usually worked. When it didn't, then I tried it again and it usually synched. The fun was when I was on the lake and there was no internet where I launched. You MUST have your app past the log in screen while you still have a land wifi signal in order to get to the sonar screens If your app is past the log in screen it doesn't matter if there was an land WIFI signal as the fish finder transmits its unique WIFI signal.
I gave it 4 stars because using the phone app log in and getting it to sync should be much cleaner and easy to use. Why do you even need a log in to use the fish finder?
Update review 8 Dec 2020 after 6 outings on a lake: I was able to use it only 2 of the 6 outings because the 4 trips I couldn't use it was because I was still trying to log in using different methods after leaving home. I was definitely unable to log in to get to the sonar screen without a land wifi signal. Apparently you MUST have your phone app past the log in screen to use the sonar - so don't log out of the app. My work around solution was to keep the app open when I left home. My phone kept the app settings (past the log in screen) when I did a phone restart. I don't know what will happen if you drain your phone battery though. We may be out of luck. I emailed the Fishhunter -Portable Fish finder/Sonar Lowrance (Navico GoFree) app tech support 12 days ago and no response so far.

title: Why does Garmin insist on Annoying and Distracting Customers ?
text:
There is a curve up ahead. There are lots and lots of them - and you will know it because the screen will keep telling you. This would be extremely useful in cars that do not have windshields, The rest of us can just look ahead to know that - guess what, all roads are not straight, Need parking downtown? No? Well, too bad because the display will fill with a Can We Find Parking screen, and it will not go away unless you hit the touch screen - and it will come back with each recalculation ensuring you need to take your eyes off the road to address it.

Do you enjoy hearing "Please drive to the highlighted route" each and every time you begin a journey. Garmin engineers must since you can't turn this off just like you can not turn off the curve warnings or parking warnings.

Want to pull down a side street, perhaps to buy gas on your way - better address the Garmin otherwise "When possible, please make a U-turn" will be repeated about every 5 seconds.

Oh, and if you are driving that winding country road, the one with all the curves and curve warnings and you want to take a look at alternative routes, don't bother. Garmin treats every map like a central city - it will suppress road views as you zoom out. So in isolated areas it will only show the road you are driving, all others will be eliminated to reduce screen clutter.

Even after decades of refinement, this is what you get, Wow.

title: Works very well with OC200 controller. Less well in standalone mode
text:
My router was unable to handle the size of my house and number of clients that were connecting via WiFi (it kept overloading and shutting down the radio). I thought about getting a mesh system but since I have Ethernet in several rooms I decided to get three of these TP-Link access points and run a system in my home that is similar to what would be used in a commercial environment: a set of access points. I disabled my router and installed three of these in strategic locations in my house. You can easily configure each by connecting to them via their internal web interface and they have lots of great options (portals, etc.) that I mostly didn't use. I set them each up with the same SSID, password, and wifi settings but on different channels. I tested and the internet was very fast. Nice.

Then the complaints started coming in from my family. Devices that they moved from room to room, like phones and tablets, would say they were connected but be unable to download anything. I think they weren't roaming from one access point to another. I tried changing settings (decreasing radio power, for example) for quite a while but my family was getting really annoyed. I was ready to return these.

As a last ditch effort, I purchased the TP-Link OC200 controller. Basically it allows you to configure all these devices from one web interface and also monitors clients and bandwidth. That's not much value added in itself but it also said it enables "fast roaming." I installed and set everything up. Bam. Perfect internet, all the time, everywhere. You can walk all around and have no problems whatsoever. I'm not actually sure whether the technology is 802.11r or v or h, but I can tell you that once I installed the OC200, all my problems went away.

In short I'm 100% satisfied with these access points. They work superbly in all respects as I have them configured. However, I cannot recommend them in standalone mode. They require a controller like the OC200. Don't return them if you have a bad experience with standalone mode operation (and are willing to buy a device to control them).

title: No Regets.
text:
I have to confess, this was a complete impulse purchase. I already have an eight year old 27" inch ASUS PB Series PB278Q Monitor that was considered somewhat of prosumer PLS monitor suited for those focused on video and photo editing. In that regard, purchasing a Samsung VA panel could be considered a step down from a PLS. Logically, if I was going to purchase a widescreen monitor and I wanted to retain the picture quality I have become used to, the sensible choice would have been one of LG's IPS monitors. However, I clicked on the "add to cart" for this Samsung...whether it was the price, the QLED marketing hype or the mixture of features that made me pull the trigger I don't quite know.

I had a few reservations when I purchased it. 1) the fact it was a VA panel. 2) A string of reviews mentioning dead pixels, 3) The severe curve of the monitor....would it be impossible to get used to.

1) Yes, a degree of colour shift is seen, but 99.9% of the time it's not noticeable when sitting in front of the monitor. However, I did come across on instance it was quite noticeable. There is one video game I play where there is a window positioned in the upper left hand corner. It's green with large bevels having a slightly different shade of green. For some reason there is a noticeable inversion of colour between the window and the bevel as you move your head a few degrees. Not a big deal....unless you are using the monitor for serious graphics or photo editing.

2) No dead pixels. Overall manufacturing seems quite good (for $650, I certainly hope so!)

3) I was quite worried about the curve since I have never used a curved monitor. I can see both the pros and cons of curved monitors. Well, after a week's use it's starting to feel quite natural. Never underestimate the human animal to adapt given a sufficient amount of time.

Other thoughts.....

Make sure you desk is deep enough. The thrusting forward of the stand plus the curved back makes the actual depth of the monitor quite large.

Built-in speakers aren't too bad. Perfectly adequate for voice and Skype calls, music, not so much.

The matte finish on the screen is quite modest. Although it does a great job eliminating reflections from the ambient surroundings any light source behind you like a window or lamp will be a brilliant blob on your screen. You will need to position your monitor and arrange lighting as if it were a glossy.

Gaming with the widescreen and freesync has been an noticeable improvement over the 16:9 and just v-sync.

Works flawlessly on Linux Mint.

Conclusion

A great monitor for those who use their computer for a mixture of general office work, emails, web browsing, and gaming. It's suitable for those of us who play around with Photo/video editing and other graphics applications. For those who do Graphics design or video editing professionally, or those who do it for a hobby, but take it very seriously, this might not be the monitor (or any VA panel) for you.

title: Not too bad, but could use some contouring changes to make it overall a little better IMO.
text:
Not much to really go into depth with on this Amazonbasics Gaming Mouse. The software offers movement speed adjust-ability, the RGB can be change from the logo and the scroll wheel. The DPI button color can be changed, but only changes when switching DPI modes. The DPI, polling rate, double click speed (and two other windows offered adjustments windows pointer speed and scroll speed) can be changed per the user in the software suite. And macro's can be setup for the mouse on a per key basis.

The lighting abilities don't match that of the Amazonbasics Gaming Keyboard. The mouse actually can pulse a single color, or if put on RGB will slowly switch between colors. The speed at which the color pulses/blinks can be changed via the software suite to where as the pairing Keyboard cannot.

The mouse has some weight to it, but the weight resides mainly in the back/palm held area leaving the front of the mouse weightless and light.

The braided cable is a nice touch and makes it feel a little less cheap. Unfortunately, the scroll wheel does the exact opposite, but given the RGB I guess it's necessary?

If the overall contour of the mouse could be made closer to that of the Gigabyte M6980X, and the weight moved to the center of the mouse, I feel this would make the mouse a more gamer/market competitive mouse that more people might buy into.

title: Decent Sound With Total Dealbreakers
text:
I’ve never felt more burned by a Wirecutter review. Yes, the sound is decent. Yes, it has ANC, which is nice in noisy environments (or even to cut the white noise din of quiet but constant sounds).

Here’s what it doesn’t have:

- A charging system that makes sense. The 1More headphones look like they’re USB-C (after all, the plug is USB-C shaped), but they’re actually powered by USB-A with a USB-C end on them. What does that actually mean? It means you can’t charge them with your USB-C laptop charger. You can only charge them with an esoteric cable that was outdated the moment they produced them. Hope you don’t lose the tiny cable they include, otherwise you’ll have a lot of trouble charging this thing.

- A microphone that works on laptops. The 1More headphones have a microphone that is fully incompatible with MacBooks. If you want this as a dual purpose music and meetings headset, look elsewhere.

Neither of these things are documented on 1More’s website or in their user manual. We only found out after purchase through contacting support and reading comments on reviews. Avoid, avoid, avoid.

title: My favorite visual observation filter
text: I live South of Atlanta, GA in the suburbs.  I am a 90% visual observer with Explore Scientific 2" eyepieces on either my Celestron CPC-100 Deluxe HD or my son's Orion Skyquest XT10 Dobsonian.  I've tried lots of filters to cut light pollution (city skyglow and street light pollution).  I've tried the Celestron UHC LPR (which is my 2nd favorite but it has a purple hue) as well as the Orion Oxygen III, Orion Ultrablock (LPR), and this Moon & Skyglow Neodymium.  The O-III is a very specific narrowband filter for looking at certain nebulae...other objects will disappear...so it is not good for general visual use with all objects.  The Ultrablock is good for planetary and emission nebula...but it gives a green hue to everything.  This Neodymium moon/skyglow filter cuts down on city glow and streetlight pollution without adding too much weird coloration.  Contrast increases.  It has a very slight purple/blue hue to it, but stars are still white (instead of green / blue / purple with other filters).

My only criticism is that the bottom of the Chromebook gets somewhat warm while charging, and VERY warm whenever I'm watching videos. There are no fans on this thing to cool it, so if your intention is to set this on your lap and watch videos you'll want one of those laptop cooling pads to set it on or it will get uncomfortable.

title: Excellent Neutral Cable for an Amazing Price
text:
I got this cable (1.5M) to run between my SOtM tx-USBultra USB signal reclocker and conditioner and a Mytek Brooklyn DAC+. It replaced a 0.3M WireWorld Ultraviolet.
The first impression was that there is a minuscule improvement in details, better defined soundstage and more flesh to the voices and instruments. The trade off was a slightly rolled off bass. This I can live with as I have three subwoofers in this setup with a combined power of 4,100W.
The improvement was obviously due to Cardas improved geometry and materials which are optimized for constant transfer impedance rather than a full wave characteristic impedance. For the low price, this is an outstanding deal. Now I am looking for a longer Cardas Clear to run between the Media Server and the USB conditioner (using a WireWorld Chroma 2.0). It is interesting that even though both WireWorld and Cardas claim that their USB cables perform equally well at any length (the only two companies, the rest dont suggest or make any cables longer than 1.5M) the Cardas is actually proven to deliver on that claim. Another interesting fact is that the WireWorld Chroma and Ultraviolet - the two older cables I am upgrading - run a separate wire and insulation for the USB power , but that didn't help at all, they still sounded inferior to the Cardas. But those cables are 4-5 times cheaper too.
Regarding the other reviewer noticing their excessive brightness. I didnt experience that at all. Cardas is all about imaging, stage and details. They are not bright at all. But all of this is setup dependent and ear dependent. May be his gear was already excessively bright or may be he is used to warm sound. That is why you can buy a cable and return it if you don't like it.
As far as I am concerned, I am willing to shell out the $350 for the 5m run I need. Try it you wont be sorry.

title: Insecure And Hackable
text:
Update Dec 2022. : I am horrified at the lack of security for these cameras. This was a 3 star which given the seriousness of the defects, it should be a zero star. Do not buy this product.

Original Review

I have had these on for a month on vigilant mode, and these cameras work, but they could be better.

The setup and pairing in the app is surprisingly easy and straightforward. Although I could not attach to a virtual router, the connection pairing to a real router was also smooth through the app. Charging the cameras continuously takes about six hours per camera, but function without charging.

If you put these cameras even in a low traffic area and set for decent capture, the lack of person recognition turns on the camera every time, and instead of the year advertised, try four days. Also, a standard microUSB cord cannot charge these cameras, the connection is extra long, and basically only the eufy included micro USB is the only microUSB cord that fits in this device. This precludes you having the cameras always connected to a microUSB power source which I consider to be a major design flaw.

I think these are still the best cameras without a subscription, but there are both physical design issues and definitely software matters to improve. While this is not an obvious beta, I feel the amount of intervention and false positives cancel out the lack of subscription benefits considering the amount of manual intervention and card cleaning you have to do.

With the battery dying in these cameras from constant use, I estimate this product has a two year, possibly three year lifespan.

title: A budget bassheads dream!
text:
So i bought this subwoofer on a budget. I didnt expect much from it only because of the low cost. I have a custom built ported box tuned to 37hz. I paired this with my pioneer GM-D8701 monoblock amplifier. There was alot of confusion in the description for this subwoofer on amazons listing. But let me tell you what you actually recieve.

When ordered you will get the sub with the following basic specs:
Dual 4 ohm voice coils
2.5 inch voice coils
125 oz magnet
500watt rms rated 1000watts peak.
This subwoofer on a budget absolutely bangs hard on 500 watts. Im running it in the 2 ohm configuration and it has slammed hard before it has even broken in. There is no smell during this breakin period and i think i found the perfect match for my setup. Im only two days into using this sub and it definitely has surpassed what i thought it would be capable of in the box that i built for a completely different sub. The bass hits lows flawlessly until about 36hz. And drum bass? Thumps hard. This sub by itself without another sub is shaking my truck pretty nicely and has decent tonal quality. Not great but decent. But the performance of how it hits for me outweighs the lack of perfect tonal quality. This is a beast of a subwoofer for the money and really is a huge bargin. Mad props to American bass for putting this out for the little guys on a budget.

Update:
Has been a week since installing this sub and tried babying it through the breakin period. But i couldnt control myself and started cranking this thing to the max. This sub hasnt failed me yet! A true solid hard hitting, low rumbling, growling bass that just wont quit. Solid purchase for budget minded people. This is an spl sub hands down. And while i am maxing out at 570 watts....this sub just sucks it up and slams it out. Truely impressed with this beast of a sub!
Update 3/3/20:
Sub is fully broken in. Bass is ridiculous. Sound quality is still average however....it is crazy deep, crazy loud, and shows no signs of stopping. As this will be my last update. I will part with these final words. Worth the investment to anyone!

title: It's a good monitor, first one had a DOA Display Port though.
text:
The first one right out of the box had a bad Display Port (it only has one). The HDMI port worked perfectly fine BUT as we know you can't take full advantage of this monitor without using the Display Port due to the resolution and refresh rate. I even spent a ton of time troubleshooting it, if you google the issue a bunch of people reported similar issues on other LG monitors (none were reported for this one so it's not model specific). There were some fixes like letting the power completely drain overnight but this didn't work for me and I had to begrudgingly return it and wait for another. The cool thing was Amazon didn't allow for an exchange so I had to do a full return and repurchase - but when I did the monitor went on sale so I saved even more money so it all worked out in the end.

I had just bought the 850 version of this monitor before I found out this is a clone to it for a few hundred dollars cheaper. I had both side by side and they are identical. Reviews stated that the back of the monitor was different between the two versions and there were reports of different OSD interfaces, as of November 2020 this is no longer the case, the only way you can tell the difference is looking at the sticker that has the model number listed. Oh and the cardboard boxes had slightly different sized text on them and obviously the 850 has a nice cardboard box for the accessories and extra HDMI cables if we really want to get technical...

Zero issues with back-lighting. Had to adjust colors a bit so not sure if the 850 has better calibration or if just a fluke. Gsync works great (compatible with Gsync, does not have the chip built in however).

Very high quality monitor and surprisingly light but I guess that's how modern screens are. This was significantly lighter than the 27inch it replaced so the articulating monitor arm moves like a dream now.

Very happy with the screen, only giving it 4 stars because of the first one being DOA and seemingly something that wouldn't have cropped after it left the factory...

title: Almost useless
text:
I know what you're looking for, because I was, and still am at this point - a device that will turn one USB-C port into many USB-C ports, probably because you've invested in some USB-C connected devices and don't have enough ports on your computer, and it's probably a Mac.

This hub looks nice, and feels nice, and wants to work sometimes, but ultimately (after a few weeks of trying) doesn't work. First it will not work with anything self-powered (like an external USB hard drive that is powered from the port). Second, it will not work with media (e.g. an external monitor or webcam). The best it's done is to connect an iPhone/iPad, and even then the power cuts out after a while and the connectivity doesn't last for more than a single session.

I wish this worked better, and I would say so and even recommend it to others who are strangely in the same boat (no one really makes a USB-C to multiple USB-C device, that I can find), but I got rid of the box and packing materials or I'd be returning this - big mistake.

title: Kindle Family Lacks Any Real Innovation
text:
For the past few years, Amazon has seemed content to follow the e-reader pack rather than lead it and provide true innovation in its Kindle lineup. This version of the Oasis is no exception. While this latest Oasis adds the option for warm (amber) light, which is a plus for me since I tend to read a night, Kobo and Nook have had this feature for years. Amazon touted that its Oasis and now Paperwhite are “waterproof.” Big deal. Kobo did that in 2014. A 7” screen on the Oasis version 2 in 2017! Again, Kobo did that in 2013. The ability to change the boldness of fonts and provide some customization was provided by Kobo back in 2011. The Kobo Forma, an 8-inch radically different e-reader, shows what REAL innovation is. Go take a look at it.

Let’s talk pricing. $249 (with Special Offers) $269 without them. The top of the line Nook is $199. And only Amazon makes you PAY to have an e-reader without advertisement. Let’s be honest, that’s what “special offers” are, ads.

The Kindle ecosystem is second to none, unmatched by Kobo or even Barnes and Noble. That’s what keeps me with Kindle. It would be nice, however, if their e-reader line-up matched their industry leading eco-system. The big change between the Oasis version 2 and version 3 is warm light. Hardly innovation. Is it worth the upgrade? You need to make that decision. The screen is truly beautiful and evenly lit, the automatic light adjustment (including amber-warm light) is customizable and works perfectly, the software is excellent, and page turns are lightning fast.

But wait, the Kindle Paperwhite is now available in Twilight Blue! Now that’s some innovation, LOL!

title: It worked!
text:
I have an 11 year old iMac model 12,1. The thicker kind that you can easily open the screen to access the inside, unlike the newer “we will make you buy a new one” model that can’t be upgraded easily yourself. It still worked well. The hard drive gave out after nine years. Expected. If I took it somewhere to get fixed it would have been around 3-400 bucks and not easily done during a pandemic. So I chanced it and purchased this kit. The many positive reviews were all spot on.

The end result is it works and comes with everything you need, except tweezers. The video tutorial is on YouTube. Some insight. Find some good tweezers. The kit doesn’t come with them and you will need them to put the hex screws back in as the magnets make that tricky. Also, the take your time and have another person around in case you need another pair of hands. You likely will. My man fingers were too fat to easily pull some of the cables out. Also, the first cable you need to pull out is very tricky and easily breaks. Wiggle it side to side and it will give way eventually. The hardest part of this process was reinstalling the OS multiple times. High Sierra is the best you get in this machine due to the old chip set. I first reinstalled Snow Leopard and then had to install Sierra, and then eventually High Sierra. That was a lengthy but not difficult process. Good luck! I’m up and running again and saved myself several hundred clams. :)

title: Not the NAS you're looking for
text:
You want the QNAP TS-431KX. Let me explain.

We use multiple QNAP rack mount NAS at work, and we needed a device for offsite air-gap backup. First, we tried the TS-131K 1-bay NAS. Had to return it after discovering that you cannot use a generic USB enclosure to expand the storage; you must use a QNAP-model expansion device.

Next, we tried the TS-431K 4-bay NAS. Had to return it after discovering that it runs slow due to insufficient RAM. Furthermore, the RAM is hard-wired and cannot be upgraded.

However, the TS-431KX is what you want: it comes with 2GB of RAM, upgradeable to 8GB.

title: Best of Android, but still room for improvement
text:
I've owned this watch for 7 months now, and so I hope my feedback would provide an accurate and detailed description of my concerns and fascinations with this watch. Before jumping in, I have the black 44mm Active 2 (wifi) watch paired with a Samsung Galaxy s10e.
To get straight to the point, this watch does its job well...and that's it.
It doesn't strive to jump through excessive hoops to overwhelm you with extensive features that will mark it different from the rest of the competition. It is a good watch with clear and abundant watch faces, it lasts for a while, it'll get you notifications, and minor app support. I'm not an expert reviewer, but I'll try to touch on these points since they are - as I feel - the highlight of the watch.

PROS
1. It's a good watch. Since the battery management on this watch is fairly good, you can set it up to have a "Screen-always on" feature enabled. What this does is that when you are not "flicking your wrist" to get the screen on, the screen remains a dim (but fairly visible) colorless version of your watch face. In this mode, some designs would even disappear from the watch face to only show the time, and when you adjust your wrist to turn on the screen (gesture), the whole watch face will come back. I think this is nice since I wouldn't have to keep enacting the gesture just to see my watch; at that point, I feel it defeated the efficacy of its main purpose as a watch.
2. The Galaxy watch store (which I believe is just Samsung's galaxy store) has a ton of options for watch faces. Some are tacky, but if you look through, you can find some of which may fit your style. Some watch faces could also be customized to place tidbit of information on the face, information such as step count, weather, heart rate, etc.
3. Battery Life. The battery is some of the best in the market I would say. It may not last as long as a Fitbit versa, but considering what it does, it does it well. With an Always-on Screen, the battery lasts easily 2 days. Without it, maybe 2-3 days. There is a power-saving mode that may limits features and can give it an extra day, but the ultra power saving mode apparently lets you use it as a clock only for 41 days. I haven't tested that, but I think it's a feature worth noting.
5. Notifications. Nothing out of the ordinary here. You get notifications, and you can reply to some of them (I am not sure how well this works on iOS). There are quick reply options and then there is that Bixby voice thing. Eh. It;s ok. Not always accurate, but if you need it, it can get the job done. You can also limit what app notifications show up on your watch!

CONS
1. Minor app support. I don't think this is Samsung's fault entirely. I just don't see a lot of apps on their store that seems...well...good. They are tacky, pointless, or terribly designed. I am not saying that the app is what makes the watch great, but if you are buying a premium watch with money, I sort of expect at least an app store that could provide some users more functionality if they so desire.
2. Oximeter? There was a rumor of the watch having this capability. It hasn't been unlocked in my entirety of owning this. I guess Samsung doesn't want to release it?
3. Heart Rate sensor. Fitness on this app is otherwise great! I am just a tad bit skeptical of the accuracy of the heart rate sensor. I would use it more as a guide rather than an actual metric. When you check your heart manually, I tend to get it slightly different. Hopefully, an update would fix this.

title: Not perfect, but still the best pen display out there.
text:
UPDATED REVIEW-
I have updated this review. I have become more critical of the fans now that my house is quieter in winter, and the backlighting issues are actually a little worse then I realized. Overall it's still awesome and am glad I got it though*

WACOM THIS WACOM THAT-
I am a long time wacom user, starting with the intuos 4 medium back in 2010 then in 2012 I upgraded to the 22hd. At the end of june 2020 I upgraded to this 24 pro.

For over 7 years I heavily used the 22hd and logged a massive amount of drawing hours on it. If it were a car it would probably read over 300k miles by now. It was the darn near center of my life. Gaming, drawing, painting, study, reading, tv, shopping, watching cat videos on youtube, I did everything on it. Despite a few problems I was very happy with it and I had no plans to upgrade anytime soon. But then suddenly a dirty usb plug led me to falsely believe my 22hd was dying. So I did my research... said my prayers... and ordered a 24 pro.

STUNNING 4k screen-
Even though I don't have 10bit color mode enabled yet, the color difference from 22hd was still immediately noticeable along with the larger screen and 4k. I had never seen a 4k screen before, and it absolutely blew me away when windows booted up the first time with my fun colorful desktop picture now brimming with a new vibrance and clarity I have never known. I figured getting a 4K cintiq would have to be an upgrade but I was not prepared to just how massive this upgrade would be. Working on large pieces of art like this is really nice. The color is a little more accurate on the 24 pro too. No more weird greenish yellows for me.

GAMING-
Games in 4k are absolutely mind blowing (well most games anyways) it is almost as visually shocking as the first time I tried VR, I kinda feel like I am almost really there. It's beautiful eye melting clarity and I just love it. While my 1060gtx works great at 4k for drawing and doing work in windows, it is not strong enough to get more then a dozen fps or less in games unless I put everything but resolution to low (which oddly looks kinda cool in some games). If you can somehow find a 3060 rtx or better, you are going to have a great time with this display.

HZ-
This screen is 60hz which is standard for most 4k displays. Even so I would love to see a 120hz or higher 4k cintiq someday, especially considering how expensive these cintiqs are. 4K gaming beyond 60fps is now a reality thanks to powerful new video cards coming out.

LARGE MARGE-
As impressive as the 4k resolution is, honestly the 2 more inches might be the single most useful thing about this coming from a 22hd, at least for drawing and doing work. I can't say enough how much I love the extra space for the multitudes of open windows\apps I often have open. I don't feel cramped anymore. You might think it better just to have 2 screens, but I prefer just 1 because everything is still "right there" for me, especially since you generally pull the cintiq close to you when working on it (a big screen in your face means you really have to turn your neck to see a 2nd screen off to the side).
The 24 pro seems to be the perfect size. I am not sure I would want larger as it becomes more of a struggle to reach up with the pen to the far sides of the screen.

DEAD\STUCK PIXELS\DUST-
Sadly I have 4 dead\stuck pixels (or are they dust?). A fair number of reviews seem to have the same problem, consider yourself lucky if yours is flawless. I decided to not make a fuss about it because at 4k these pixels are soo tiny I can only see them if I pull the screen close to my face and try hard to see them, and there is a strong chance a replacement would also has dead pixels anyways.

If you are wondering, I did try pixel fixing videos but it didn't work.

BACKLIGHT BLEED\GLARE-
If the screen is very dark I can see some light bleed on the bottom middle of the screen. Not nearly as bad as some people seem to have it. For me the worst part is the 4 corners that have a GLOW\glare if I am watching a really dark tv show or playing a really dark game. I didn't notice this much at first, but now that I've had more time to evaluate, it's definitely there and can be a little rough on the eyes, and I now consider this to be the singular worst thing about the 24 pro, but it isn't bad enough for me to call it a major problem, though some people get 24\32 pros with severe levels of this.

FAN NOISE-
The 2 noisy fans seem to be the number 1 complaint about the cintiq 24 pro.

At 100% brightness (which is too bright when working long hard hours) they are definitely noticeable. Kinda like pc case fans (cheap ones) and on pretty much all the time. Thanks to how cool they keep the drawing surface I don't mind it when drawing or painting as I generally don't work in complete silence then anyways. But while gaming or watching tv I can honestly say I don't like em. Thankfully I am content at around 60% brightness so the fans are rarely on (or quiet if they are running).

If wacom didn't bother with the cintiq engine upgrade port (seriously who uses that?) they could have designed this whole thing to not need small noisy fans but large quiet ones instead that run at a lower rpm, or ditch the fans all together and just have heat pipes or something. You can set the fans to low or auto but it's hardly any different at max brightness, and at lower brightness the LOW fan setting actually runs louder then auto does.

If their only real purpose is to keep the drawing surface cool, then it would be nice to have an option to disable them for people who want absolute silence or a new setting for "lower" cause low just isn't low enough. I doubt they are actually needed to prevent the device from burning up cause I used it all july and it was hotter n hell in here with no AC, and everything is fine.

DRAWING AND PAINTING-
Compared to the 22hd it's about the same experience, but slightly better. The etched glass screen has a slightly more toothy feel then the 22hd which is nice, and the parallax is improved. Drawing on a 22hd felt more like plastic on plastic. Even so, ultimately it's mostly the same experience so it's more about having that extra screen real estate and 4K UHD which is much nicer on the eyes then the old slightly blurry 1080p 22hd (it had aggressive anti-glare coating).
Some people said the new etched glass eats the felt pen nibs really fast, but I haven't had a problem with that? I do draw with a feathery touch though, which is one of the best things about a cintiq vs a cheap tablet (it will actually register your lightest of strokes). Doing art on the 24 pro is magnificent.

THE PEN-
8000 pressure levels. You'll notice about 10 of them.

The new pen is disappointing.
It's slightly lighter and thinner then the 22hd grip pen, but it still feels like a fat marker and has that slimy rubber grip which feels slightly sticky after long hard hours as your paw heats up and sweats. Even their new pen PRO slim has the rubber grip as well, so no thanks!

The old intuos 4 CLASSIC PEN is still IMO superior, even though it doesn't have 8000 pressure levels. I can barely notice the difference in pressure levels between them. 2000 pressure levels was already way more then you can probably perceive (those people who say they can notice a difference are probably just experiencing some kind of placebo\power of suggestion effect lol).
The classic pen is almost as light and about the same feel as a real pencil, and by not having a rubber grip it feels natural and uh.. not warm and sticky. I strongly recommend it and I hope they never discontinue it. It's the pen the display should really ship with (who wouldn't like it more then the grip pen?).

PEN HOLDER-
I don't see many people mention this in their reviews, and was trying to figure it out before buying, but yeah the 24 pro totally comes with a pen holder you can clip into in 1 of 2 spots on the top of the cintiq. Pretty handy. I was hoping it could be attached to the sides, but that's a minor gripe as it does work good up top.

EXPRESS REMOTE-
I expected this to be a big upgrade, but sadly it kinda isn't.
If it's been off for hours, it doesn't turn on when you click any button on it like it should have been designed, instead you have to awkwardly slide this really tiny and weird slider on the bottom to turn it on. It will automatically shut off after 15 minutes or so without use, and this is part of why it holds a charge that lasts a long time. I charge it maybe once a month though I don't use it much.
Why?
For serious work the keyboard is still much faster to use.

There is a multitude of buttons on the remote, but it is terribly awkward to hit most of them when you hold it with 1 hand and drawing with your other hand. In reality only a few buttons are actually comfortable to hit quickly while working. They did their best to put braille like patterns to help you feel out which button your thumb is resting on, but because there is no spacing between buttons I often end up hitting 2 buttons at a time instead of 1 like I wanted.
So when I want to go FAST like sonic, I can't. It's slow and cumbersome to use these buttons compared to the lightning speeds I attain with a keyboard.

The touch wheel is pretty bad just like I remember form the intuos 4, doing a horrible job at recognizing touch. I BADLY miss the superior old touch strip on the back of the 22hd, and I about cry every time I reach up to use it like I have for 7 years only to remember it's not there anymore...

I think the remote should be redesigned a little.
Touch strip down the middle of it. Buttons with some spacing between each key on the sides of the touch strip. Less buttons to hit sure, but are much more usable. The remote should automatically turn on by hitting any key on it- it shouldn't even have nor need a manual slider for power.

MAGIC MAGNETICALS-
I do love how the remote sticks to the bezel area left or right sides magnetically. That is really slick and professional. Though I find the magnets could use just a tiny bit more power, if the screen has been cleaned recently, it can slide down and eventually fall off especially if you tilt the screen down a bit, and the magnets are only on the middle (not top or bottom of the bezel area)

The charging usb cable works fine. It's really short, but long enough to plug into the side of the cintiq and still have the remote magnetized to the bezel area (this works to either side). I wonder if they could make it charge from the magnetic field someday in the future and just forget the cable all together.

IS THE REMOTE GOOD FOR ANYTHING?
yes.
For just light sketching when I don't need to use hotkeys very often, I love this remote, cause I and be wrapped up in a warm blanket on cold nights and have my left arm tucked away while still having access to some express keys.
The remote is a good idea, it just needs to be redesigned and improved upon.

4 TOUCH BUTTONS-
The only touch buttons on the regular 24 pro are the top right ones on the bezel for accessing the display settings or other wacom settings (and an onscreen keyboard button). They glow with backlighting and look great against the black bezel. I really like this design and I am kinda surprised they didn't expand on this idea more by adding touch express keys on the left and right sides of the bezel. A touch strip in this style on the front under where the remote sticks to would be about perfect for using your thumb on.

SPEAKING OF BEZEL-
I just love the nearly all glass front of this thing and tapered back. Only at the very edges is there finally a ridge where the glass meets the outer edge of the plastic chassis. It feels oddly very pleasant to grab this thing. When pondering the deep meanings of life I often find myself dragging my thumbs around the bezel area just cause it feels nice.

VESA ARM MOUNTS (the only way cintiqs should be used imo)-
The official wacom vesa arm mount is expensive, and seeing as how I already had a ergotron LX which I got with my 22hd back in 2012 (it still works good!), I decided to buy the required steel plate so the 24pro could fit on it. If you don't already have an arm mount, maybe consider the wacom one as it comes with everything you need and they claim it's more sturdy and stable (less shake when drawing on it- not that it's a major problem though).

Installation went well, cause it only fits 2 ways. Of course I got it wrong the first time, but no big deal. A few minutes to fix. =z
I did have to use a great deal of arm strength to tighten the ergotron enough to hold the cintiq up. While the 24pro is about the same weight as a 22hd, the vesa metal mounting plate adds some serious heft to it. Also make sure that whatever desk you are mounting this to is sturdy and heavy enough it won't topple over, especially as you move the cintiq around which can change the center of gravity and all that. All put together it's heavy.

TO VESA OR NOT TO VESA?-
Using an arm mount means you can put the screen in just about any position and angle you could ever want. Whether I am drawing, or gaming, or watching tv, reclined in my chair or not, I can always have the screen in the perfect position then easily push it back out of the way when done. I can't say enough how wonderful this is. It's a great reason to get a 22 or larger cintiq too just so you can do this. It's all part of bringing drawing to your comfort zone, and I don't know of a better way to achieve that.

FREE SOFTWARE-
The intuos and 22hd came with waaaay better software. The pro line just comes with 2 months of adobe rush and access to their photo library. Pretty lame. I am not even going to bother registering cause I could care less about this software.

DRIVERS-
I am impressed how well the 24 pro works compared to the 22hd. The pen handles the edges of the screen very well in every app I've tried, and stability is improved. I don't find myself having to save and reload my custom settings to fix odd problems anymore. The only bug I've found is sometimes upon booting up, it fails to load the drivers properly (pen does nothing) which requires a restart- a minor inconvenience. The other bugs I run into are the fault of apps and not wacom from what I can tell.

CONCLUSION-
There is no question...
Despite the potentially noisy fans, or the unpleasant glare like glow of the backlighting in dark scenes (the worst single problem), or the 4 dead pixels that only bother me if I remember they are even there...
The 24\32 pro still is the very best digital drawing\painting\modelling tool out there. I don't know of a better drawing surface besides actual paper.
I love working in 4k. It's amazing for doing art, but also fun for gaming and tv too. Paired with a vesa arm mount it will become your best friend that goes on incredible journeys through the digital world with you. I am very happy I upgraded from my 22hd.

I am already hungry for the next gen cintiq's that will hopefully fix the few existing problems and have other fun improvements like 100+hz, or 8k resolution. Those are probably some years away yet as wacom does not bring out a new line very often. If you want the best NOW in 2020, this is it, the pro line. Nobody else makes a 4k pen display that I can find, and wacom drivers have gotten to a point where they are pretty solid.

Even so, if you can live without 4k (you really can't once you see it- I call it the 4k curse), and are new to this sport thus not sure art will become your new life, definitely consider a cheaper model or different brand. 800$ is much cheaper then 2000$ if you decide art isn't for you. Do your research. I've been at this long enough to know what I want and need, and there is no question it's the 24 pro. Also, if you have a need for touch, definitely pay extra to have it. This purchase is something you'll live with for a number of years, so do it right the first time.

-----BONUS DVD SECTION-----

REFURBISHED OR NOT?-

You can get a refurbished cintiq pro on ebay, saving hundreds of dollars. But this is risky, as they may or may not have serious light bleed, any number of dead pixels\dust spots, and craziest of all, even scratches! You can only exchange those if there is something non cosmetic that is wrong. And each one sold is not individually shown, so you have no idea if you will be lucky and get one with no issues or 200 dead pixels.

I would definitely advise you all to just pay a few hundred more to get one on amazon so you can at least return it\exchange if something is wrong. I like how many refurbed 24 pros they have on ebay for sale up against how few reviews of this product are out there. This pro line definitely has some manufacturing problems, so I would take this seriously. I don't know how much we can fault wacom either for this generations problems. It must be really hard to make a 4k pen display, nobody else is doing it. I just hope the next gen cintiqs will be darn near flawless.

INTUOS OR CINTIQ-
All those people who say intuos is better... I don't get it. I've used both for years, and it's night and day. It's really hard to ink curves on an intuos. The disconnect that exists by drawing on a pad but looking up at a screen is not natural. It's not the natural way to draw and it isn't nearly as fun. You crazy people you! =)

title: No Coil whine/SB 2 and XPS 13 2-in-1 7390 compatible
text:
I was using a Monoprice USB C dock with my SB2 and recently purchased an XPS 13 2-in-1 for some graduate work I am doing. The Monoprice was great, worked with both machines, but a very noticeable coil whine existed and I tried changing cables with no luck(Pluggable long length docking cable(TB3 and USB C compatible). In my research of the XPS purchase, a lot of people talk about the coil whine that the older XPS 13's exhibited, detailing that some of the components on the motherboard were probably the cause and the only way to fix most of them was to replace the board.

This made me look for a different USB C dock to see if it might be the dock to blame. I also decided to look for the most discerning group - Macbook users - to see if there was a dock they preferred. That led me to CalDigit and until I ran across this new USB C Pro Dock, I thought I would have to spend a lot more. My research has paid off - there is zero coil whine in my setup now.

I would imagine my configuration is especially prone to coil whine, regardless of the laptop used. I have external Logitech speakers with subwoofer plugged into the headphone jack of the dock - meaning any whine is amplified. Then, I add a 34" 344x1440 monitor that has a Logitech Unifying adapter plugged in(more radio waves) in it. In the dock itself is a Jabra 370 adapter for my Jabra headphones(more radio waves) and also a Jabra Speak 710 - more audio components.

With all of this connected to the XPS 13 7390 or the SB2, no coil whine. Could not be happier! Charges both devices and works perfectly!

I am definitely recommending CalDigit for docks.

title: Get Real Quality for Slightly more.
text: 28 AWG CCA will not meet Cat6 TIA/EIA-568-B-2.1 specifications.  The electrical resistance will not allow Power over Ethernet (PoE) to work at any reasonable distance.  Amazon sells 24 AWG copper conductor CAT6 for just a little bit more and that is what should be purchased to ensure the Cat6 TIA/EIA-568-B-2.1 specifications are actually be met.  I should have read the specification more carefully and I note that the 28 AWG size is not mentioned in the description and is carefully hidden in the pictures.  In order to legally install Ethernet cables in walls IAW the National Electric Code which all municipalities use as a baseline, it must be CM or CMG rated.  CCA cannot legally display this rating.  Further CCA cannot legally use the UL certification marking either.  Also CCA is notorious for unbalanced resistance of the cable pairs which can cause problems with PoE applications. Cable Matters Snagless Cat6 Ethernet Cable has these certifications (not a CCA cable).

title: A very fast processor... when it actually runs.
text:
I bought this processor from B&H in the middle of January, and it (and its replacements) have given me nothing but trouble. Most of the time when I try to power up the system this is in, it won't even POST. If I do get it running, I can't utilize 64 threads or else the processor crashes and the system fails to POST immediately after. Sometimes it will crash when using 32 threads or less.

I tried 3 different motherboards, 2 different power supplies, and 2 different sets of memory (at the suggestion of a motherboard manufacturer) and finally RMA'd the processor. B&H handled things very quickly so kudos to them.

New processor arrives. Same instability problems. I figure it's possible I got 2 bad processors (though very unlikely) so I send the processor to AMD to be inspected and replaced if needed. After a few weeks, AMD sends me a replacement. I install the CPU in my system and, to this day, I continue to have stability issues with this CPU.

In addition to the various hardware troubleshooting I performed, I also tried various bios versions. Obviously, that didn't help either, else I might not have bothered with such a negative review.

I have built many computers, (including dual-socket systems), so my issues are almost certainly not user-error. I was really excited to have such a powerful processor and get away from Intel's overpriced and mediocre products. I guess I'll be sticking with Intel's underwhelming (but stable and reliable) CPUs in the future.

title: Lightweight monitor for work
text:
This review is for Uperfect 13.3 inch Full HD portable monitor. I have been using this monitor for more than 6 months and I carry the monitor with me most of the time. I have used the monitor with several Raspberry Pis and laptops, mainly for work purposes.

The monitor comes with 1 USB-C to USB-C, 1 USB-C to USB 2 (intended to be used with the power adapter which also comes with the box) and 1 HDMI cable. The user manual says the monitor supports Thunderbolt but my computer does not support it, so I use USB-C to USB-C cable for power and HDMI cable for display. I even find this combination pretty compact for my purposes.

The picture quality of the portable monitor is very good and it is very bright. The monitor have some controls on its left but I usually use operating system's interface to manage brightness and other settings. The monitor is also lightweight and it doesn't hurt to carry it within a backpack.

My work involves a bit of a coding and mostly reading, and this monitor is very convenient for my purposes. Adding a monitor to your setup always increases the efficiency of the work. Therefore, I would definitely recommend this monitor.

title: Cut the cord with confidence
text:
We dropped cable TV sometime back. The bill had become just sickening to look at considering what we were getting in return.

We have been using an indoor square antenna with a small amp. We had the little flat square antenna behind a picture on the wall.

I thought our indoor antenna was pretty impressive. We could watch all the local stations, but the reception was not always clear. We would get some pixelation and the signal was just not solid on some of the channels.

As soon as we open the box on this new RCA Yagi, we could tell that it was going to be a game changer.

It took just a few minutes to unfold the elements and we plugged the antenna into the TV and laid it on the living room floor. Did a channel scan, and picked up about 50 channels. The channels all came in rock solid and crystal clear.

My son and I took the antenna outside and mounted it about 15-20 feet up on the side of the house. We live outside of Buffalo, New York, so we decided to aim the antenna at Toronto to see what we could get.

When we did our channel scan, we had every channel available to us in the Buffalo area: NBC, CBS, ABC, FOX, Ion, CW, and multiple PBS channels.

All the channels were strong and clear.

From Canada we picked up CBC, CTV, French CBC, TVO, Omni, Citi TV, Global, and a couple more. It is really unbelievable because Toronto is 60 miles away!

We also picked up another 20 or so channels that were religious or were playing old tv shows and movies.

We are really happy with the quality and performance of this RCA antenna. It’s still hard to believe that for such a modest price we could pick up so many channels.

One interesting note: When we first set up the antenna, the local NBC station would not come in because we were aimed in the opposite direction. We move the antenna about 10 to 20° and then we were able to pick up everything.

We could not be happier.

title: Mostly Lovely Attractive Device
text:
Really I do love this radio--the sound quality to my ears is excellent, the radio reception just dandy using only the factory installed antenna. The primary reason for choosing this Crosley model is I still enjoy listening to my CDs, which I now can do as well as having the radio and Bluetooth. All this in one sleek looking package for under $150. Very good indeed!

Now the two reasons that I only gave four stars instead of five. 1) Yes the controls are difficult to read ie small--for those of us with older eyes. Ditto for the remote. My answer to this dilemma has been to memorize which buttons do what on the receiver and remote--or put on my glasses. 2) The clock does occasionally change to what can seem a random time. For instance it is 9:00am, I turn on the radio to listen to the local news all is well. Next at 10:00am I switch to Bluetooth to listen to a radio station in another time zone--frequently BBC Radio (listening live) in the UK, eight hours ahead of my time zone. When turning off the Bluetooth radio the clock may (though not always) have jumped to read Greenwich time, reset to eight hours ahead of my time zone! This is an interesting random "quirk" but not a issue for me as I don't use this radio/CD/Bluetooth as an alarm clock.

title: Very Strong and Can Be mounted on Drywall
text:
I installed the Mount-It! Heavy-Duty Speaker Wall Mount on either side of a TV in a corner about 8ft high to hold 12lb bookshelf speakers. Luckily they angled well enough with my speaker size to aim at the listening position. Here were my discoveries when installing.

-- STRONG: These are made of hardened steel and very strong. I used them for 12lb bookshelf speakers.
-- STUD INSTALL ONLY?: They only discuss installing onto studs or brick in the instruction. I did not have a stud where I wanted to mount and used drywall anchors for the 4 mounting holes. Its very strong with the weight and will no problem to install on drywall without a stud. See picture of drywall anchors I used.
-- NOT DESIGNED RIGHT FOR STUDS. The instructions ask that you install the mounts on studs. However the mounts hole spacing is to wide to fit on a standard 1.5" thick stud.
-- NEED LONG SHAFT SCREW DRIVER: The pivoting bracket will not allow the head power driver to get close to the screw when screwing into the wall. You will want a long shaft driver and ever then there you will be on an angle screwing into the wall.
-- MOUNTING PLATES: They are supplied with mounting plates for the back of the speaker and slide into hooks on the mount and then and screwed in to secure. The mounts were much too large to fit on either side of the banana jacks so I drilled my own mounting holes and overlapped the banana plug recess. See picture. This worked fine. I was surprised at how hard the steel was when I drilled the new mounting holes.
-- SCREWING SPEAKER INTO MOUNT IS A PIA. It provided with small allen head screws to secure the speaker to the mount. When the speakers are up high these are a PIA to screw in but doable.
-- BE CAREFUL IF MOUNTING IN A CORNER: when in a corner and needing a large angle to aim the speakers it the mounts were barely able to aim correctly. I needed a 30 degree angle and with my speaker size and the down angle also needed that was the maximum I could get before the speaker body hit the wall. This is very dependent on how you place you speaker mounts so be aware of this if you have an awkward install as I did. The speaker was 8.25"w x 8.25"d x 13"t.
