title: Good sound, questionable support
text:
This review is for the Hidizs AP80. It seems some of the other reviews are for the AP60, which is a very different device.

I backed the AP80 on Kickstarter, and it arrived on schedule. During the campaign, the manufacturer's representative promised explicit podcast and audiobook support would arrive in a firmware update. There's no indication that this will ever actually happen, since they have never mentioned it since the campaign ended. Just understand that what ships might be exactly what you will have for the life of the player.

Database Mode
Seems to work much as previous non-touch Hiby OS versions. The Genre menu remains a useless wasteland, since it has no hierarchy beyond Genre, then ALL songs in that genre. Artist still seems to be the Song Artist field, and not the Album Artist field. This makes compilation albums impossible to play without delving into the folder view. The database updates about as fast as the AP60II, maybe slightly faster. it takes about 5 minutes to parse my usual set of tunes (about 7000 mixed FLAC and MP3). Definitely faster than a Clip Zip, but you'll want to update the database only when you don't need the player any time soon. On the plus side, unlike the AP60II, you can turn off automatic database updates (AP60II claims to do this, but it updates anyway when you unplug it).

Playlists
Just as with every other Hiby-based player, external playlists are not easily integrated into the database mode. Since this is how all MP3 players worked until the bottom dropped out of the market in recent years, this is annoying. The Hiby R3 introduced the ability to "load playlist" from the /playlist_data directory, although you first had to create one playlist on the player before the OS would recognize the directory (can't create it yourself). I don't have an R3, but based on the discussions in its thread, it seems that I should be able to put standard M3U playlists in that directory, hit "load playlist" and have them actually work in the database mode. I loaded my 150+ playlists using this method. It took over 2.5 minutes. Since M3U files work just fine in Folder view, why would you use the database? Two reasons: the list of playlists in the database shows how many songs are in each list; and, if you use the folder view, you get the full file path shown in the "now playing" view, while the database just shows the song title - much easier to read since you don't have to wait for a:\music\Prince\Purple Rain\01 - Let's Go Crazy.mp3 to scroll, you just see Let's Go Crazy.

Replaygain
Replay gain is finally a setting in Hiby OS. It's hiding in the playback settings menu, which is found inside the Player function, and not in the root menu as in older non-touch Hiby versions. I haven't tried any songs that I know have wildly varying replaygain values, so I'm not sure how well it works, but it has three settings: off, album, and song. This matches the standard ReplayGain settings from the Sansa line of last decade. Yay, finally getting features that were standard in 2005!

Podcast/Audiobook Support
Still nothing. No bookmarking, automatic or manual. No speed/pitch control. No recognition that Podcast or Audiobook is anything other than a genre of music.

Resume Breakpoint
In the player, there is an option (off by default) to resume the place you were listening, or restart the song you were listening to, or not resume anything. This feature doesn't work like any previous DAP I've used, including the Hidizs AP60II. The AP80 does not jump back into the player when it starts - it starts at the menu. So, if you want to resume the track, you turn on the device, wait for it to boot, open the player option, then click the PLAY button to resume. This seems like a strange thing to do, and I'd really like to skip those extra steps. The same behavior is seen if you use the FM radio. Turning off the AP80 while the radio is playing does not mean the radio will be active when you turn it on. You'll start back at the menu, silently.

General interface issues
The touch targets in the interface are not well-calibrated or are too small. Typing anything on the T9-style keyboard is a massive frustration. The system will time out and move to the next character before you can get the right one, and then the backspace button doesn't respond reliably, etc. This is a problem throughout the interface - anything smaller than the main icons on the menu is likely to be hard to hit reliably.

The lists don't wrap around. If you are looking for ZZ Top, be prepared to scroll a while. Fortunately, the scroll is pretty decently fast, and responds well to the "fast flick" that has become common in this age of touch interfaces.

Conclusion
Tweaking the touch targets, getting podcast support, and making resume actually resume would turn this into a decent player into a really great one, for my purposes. Your mileage may vary. Someone should really look at the old Rio Karma and just copy it wholesale.

title: This review covers first use only, incl formatting the SD card
text:
STEP 1 - READ the owner's manual to familiarize yourself with what the Rove's four buttons do. The 4 buttons are "Menu", "Up", "Down", and "OK".

STEP 2 - Before using, you must spend a couple of minutes formatting the SD card. I purchased the suggested 128 Gb SD card and placed it into my Rove R1. I then plugged it into my laptop using the included PC cable. You have a couple of options when it sees the PC. Choose the "Use Camera Normally" option which is the same screen as what you see when on the road. Now you can go through the menu and select the "Format" option. Following directions from the excellent owner's manual, I formatted the SD card. It's now ready to go.

STEP 3 - I then attached it to my car's windshield using the included suction cup and power cable. It started recording right away. So simple to use. Works with the default settings right out of the box.

STEP 4 - Once back home I plugged the unit back into my laptop. This time choose the "Connect as USB Flash Drive" option. This allows the PC to see the SD card as if it were just another removable drive. I then copied the movie files from the SD card to my laptop and played them on my video player (I personally use Cyber Link Power DVD). You could also extract the SD card from the Rove unit and place it in the SD adapter that comes with the SD card when you purchase it, then insert the adapter into your PC to view the video files.

PRO - Highly impressed with this unit. This first use was daytime only. Crystal clear playback with no distortion or wavering. Good field of view. Able to read license plates clearly from several feet away. The microphone picked up my music clearly, although a bit quieter. The unit feels solid, yet light-weight.

CON - I had to use considerable force to insert the plug into the cigarette lighter. It was very tight. I also had to use considerable force to insert the camera into the suction cup mount. It is way too tight. I probably won't separate them again.

I will eventually go through each Video menu option, including the Camera options and the Playback options, and edit this review, if necessary.

title: very nice addition to mobile computing
text:
the short version:

i like it very much and would recommend it to anyone who is looking for one.

pros: small, light-weight (this is not the slim version), display is good, no setup is needed. one cable for both display and power
cons: none so far

------------------------------- the longer version --------------------
due to my work requirement, i spend quite some time at customer sites / plant floor. our development platform opens a lot of windows and i typically have three monitors at the office to manage the screen space. but working on the plant floor means no extra monitors (powers, cables, etc). i had wished to have a mobile monitor that can at least give me a dual monitors for some time.

after some research i settled on this UPERFECT Portable Monitor 13.3 Inch Computer Display 1920×1080 IPS Screen based on portability and cost.

the package comes with: monitor, usb-c to usb-c cable, usb-a to usb-c cable, hdmi to hdmi cable (both ends full size, not mini), charger, stand, instruction sheet, and a card for free gift. all cables are about 3-ft long and appear to be in good quality. the construction is metal, likely aluminum, not plastic.

there are two ways to connect to a laptop with included cables:
a) usb-c to usb-c . the cable delivers both video and power to the monitor
b) usb-a to usb-c, and hdmi-hdmi. the hdmi cable is for display, the usb cable is for powering the monitor either by connecting to an available usb port on the laptop or using the included charger.

i have a win-10 pro dell laptop which has usb-c, hdmi, and firewire for video outputs. i used the included 3 ft usb-c cable to connect the monitor to my laptop. it worked right away without needing additional drivers. it initially mirrored the main display. i then switched it to the extended desktop.

the text is crispy clear, color seems to be alright, response time is good. i opened various programs on that monitor and all seem to be good. photos look great, video display is top notch. there was no light leak around the edges.

because i used the usb-c to usb-c cable, the audio signal is automatically transferred to the 2nd monitor (intel chip). the sound quality is surprisingly good for general purpose.

i did, however, flipped the orientation in windows display setting. the usb-c port on my laptop is on the left hand side which is good as i am right handed, the input ports on the monitor is on the right-hand side. the 3-ft cable is little short when the monitor is set at the right side of the laptop.

i then tried connecting the monitor to my phone (huawei P20 Pro). the phone 'projected' a tablet mode to the external monitor by default, but it can be switched to the phone mode too, basically mirroring the display of the phone. while in tablet mode, the phone is used as a keypad. i can open multiple applications at the same time. although i am not sure i will use this mode very much, as the monitor does source its power from the phone.

game performance. i didn't try to play games using this monitor so not sure if the response time is good for games.

durability. i have used the monitor for only few hours so far. we will see how long it will last. for almost $200 i hope it can last several years.

title: Amazing Headphones!
text:
I don't write too many reviews but these headphones turned out to be an awesome buy, so I have decided to go for it.

Looks:
I got mine in Navy Blue (just to be a bit different). They look awesome! (see pic). I got bored of black Bose and Sennheiser, it was time for a change.

Pairing:
I see a lot of questions about pairing with laptops. I have the headset paired up with MacBook Pro running MacOS Big Sur and Samsung Galaxy S7 phone at the same time with no issues. I can take call from MS Teams on my laptop and pick up regular phone calls from my phone without unnecessary switching/clicking. Easy.

Sound Quality:
Amazing. On par if not better than that of Bose QC II's. I listen to all kinds of music while working. I like electronic music with lots of bass and this headset delivers. I will also listen to anything from metal to classical and all genres some through loud and clear. I have not messed around with the equalizer yet as I did not see the need. They sound very good in "default" mode.

Calling/Conferencing:
Again, I saw a lot of people complaining about Noice Cancelling being "off" while on a call. After doing some research, it turns out this is a "feature" which you can easily disable. All you have to do is open the Jabra Sound+ app on your phone and go to the "cog wheel" settings menu -> Headset Settings -> Call Experience -> Sidetone and turn it off (see pic). Done. You will no longer hear yourself and everything else going on around you while on a call. The Sidetone feature being on is my only con about the headset: this feature should be OFF by default as it's discouraging a lot of customers and probably causing people to return the headset when there's no need.
I do a lot of conferencing for work via Microsoft Teams from the MacBook and the headphones are excellent for it. I've actually done a test with a coworker of Teams and asked him about the sound quality coming from my headphones' microphone. He said: perfect. Regular phone calls are sounding good as well.

Comfort:
Super comfortable for extended sessions. I keep them on most of the workdays to either be in Teams meetings or listen to music. I don't feel the need to take them off at all. I found Sennheiser's cups to be too small. These are big enough and there's extra room for your ears. Sennheiser's comparable model also hurt the top of my head after only about an hour. No issues here. I had no issues with Bose QC IIs either, but at this price point, this headset wins.

Controls:
Easy and intuitive. Most controls are on the right ear: volume up and down, stop/start music and/or call, . Level of ANC on the left ear. Twist the right cup 45 degrees to turn the headset on/off. I like things simple and this is simple enough.

Features:
There are many. I personally love how the headset pauses the audio when taken off and restarts as soon as I put it back on. It also has all kinds of settings for going into stand-by mode. Battery life is amazing.

Don't overthink this one (like I did). It's a very high quality headset at a very good price point. If Bose is too expensive for you, go for this one without hesitation. I have to say I was not expecting a feature set and quality standard this high from Jabra. I was wrong.

title: AudioCast works great for multi-room sound via Spotify Connect
text:
I originally purchased two AudioCast devices and quickly purchased two more. The devices work very well and have completely replaced the four ChromeCast devices that I had been using for many years. My use case is “multi-room streaming via Spotify connect”. I cannot really comment on using either Chromecast or AudioCast for other services as I do all my streaming from Spotify.

First, let me say that I am an IT specialist with strong networking skills. I agree with other comments that this is not super easy for “non technical” people to setup. You need an understanding of how your device connects and maintains connections to WiFi networks. The app seemed to get confused, and I had to stop/start WiFi on the device several times and bounce the app.

To be clear… the issue occurred during setup and not during playback. The device must first be connected to your WiFi network before it can be used. To accomplish that you install the AudioCast app on your mobile device and then plug in the AudioCast puck. Your mobile device will then see a new WiFi SSID (WiFi network) awaiting connections. You connect your mobile device to the new WFi SSID, which means it is connected to the AudioCast device. At that very moment, your mobile device is not connected to the internet. That is because the AudioCast device has not yet been connected to your WiFi network and therefore has no internet signal. At this moment, my Samsung phone would recognize that it was connected to a WiFi device that did not have any internet connectivity. The mobile device would then disconnect from the AudioCast and reconnect to my WiFi network, which prevented me from completely the setup. Ultimately I had to turn off the Auto Connect feature on my phone so that it would stay connected to the AudioCast device during the setup process. That allowed me to set the WiFi SSID/Password in the AudioCast configuration and the rename the AudioCast to a custom name that matched the location in my home. I had to do this for all four AudioCast devices.

Once I got the device connected to my network, streaming via Spotify Connect has worked flawlessly. I see the custom names in both the AudioCast app and in Spotify. Furthermore, devices that do not have the AudioCast app do see the devices in Spotify Connect and can stream. Meaning my wife and friends can all stream from Spotify without installing the AudioCast app.

The multiroom feature works great. I am able to “pair” AudioCast devices and the streaming is in synch. My screen shots show pairing of Office with Main. That shows in the AudioCast app. Back in Spotify Connect you see just Main. When I stream to Main in Spotify I will hear music in both Main and Office. If I want to change the pairings, I can simply drag/drop the devices in the AudioCast app.

I do not have the situation of the AudioCast creating a “hidden” or “secondary” WiFi network. However, I do see in the AudioCast app has the ability to create a Personal Hotspot. I believe this feature will degrade the performance of music streaming and therefore I leave it disabled.

The audio quality is equal or better than the Chromecast.

The performance is superior to the Chromecast. Connecting to the service happens faster than the Chromecast ever connected. My Chromecast devices would constantly drop the connection. I have used the AudioCast for several weeks now and have not experienced any drops.

One difference between Chromecast and AudioCast is the ability to create predefined groups. With Chromecast you could use Google Home to add your ChromeCast to named groups and the groups would show as a device in Spotify Connect. The AudioCast does not allow you to make groups with multiple devices. The AudioCast allows pairing of devices under one device, but does not allow for the creation of different groups with different names. While I personally like the ability to create groups… that Chromecast feature is trivial and was not a decision point in keeping the AudioCast over Chromecast.

The one fear I do have is perseverance. Like… how long will AudioCast be in business. Will they continue to add services and improve the app. Will support get better and will the company stay in business. I suppose time will tell.

title: A good choice if you want to pick up VHF stations well
text:
I recommend this antenna if you have VHF stations you'd like to receive.

The channel number reported on your TV doesn't tell you if it's on VHF (2-13) or UHF (14-51), as stations generally retain their legacy channel number from their pre-digital assignments. It's not at all reliable to count on the advertised channel number to indicate UHF vs. VHF.

For example, "Channel 33" which sounds like UHF, is on RF channel 3 (VHF) in this market. And "Channel 3", a big once-VHF local, is actually on 35 UHF. That's not unusual, so check Antennaweb's reported "RF channel" on your local stations before you pick an antenna, and if you have a must-get channel on VHF, spring for a larger VHF/UHF antenna like this one if you want to be sure of success. I didn't, and ended up with needing a bigger antenna (this one) to do the job. Note that the stations I had trouble with were less than 30 miles away, so don't go small or believe the ridiculous advertising claims on range, especially on VHF.

The VHF elements are the larger parts because of basic physics. This one has two VHF elements, apparently a co-linear phased dipole. There are 3 VHF based TV stations in the area, and it picks up all three well. So for me it was a total success moving from the smaller antenna with only one VHF element.

For me, KVIE-6 (RF channel 9) was a must-have for news, and I needed this antenna's extra gain to accomplish it.
So it's an A+ from me, working great and pulling in 64 channels.

As an added bonus of cutting the cord, you'll be losing garbage news like (wretched 24/7 Cable news network #1 and wretched 24/7 Cable news network #2 and wretched 24/7 cable news network #3) and picking up real journalism with an unbroken record of high integrity and due care to be accurate like PBS offers. ABC, CBS, NBC national news are all definitely better too. Being well-informed is important, and ditching 24/7 cable news is the first step to being a better and more informed citizen, so there's patriotic virtue in cable-cutting besides just saving money. :)

title: Great telescope!
text:
I did a lot of research and watched a ton of videos before buying this scope. I found it was the best bang for the buck. I'm just a beginner but I didn't want a beginner telescope that I would need to upgrade later. I felt this was a good mid level telescope. I had to wait a week or so because of clouds to test it out but my first night out (I mean very first time even trying to look for anything ever. Complete beginner.) I looked up and found some bright stars. I was able to pull up celestron app and found it was Orions belt. Started star hopping and found Beatlegeuse. Even Mars. I could even see Orions nebula from my light polluted back yard in the city. Without the scope I can only see 10 or 15 stars. But when I look in the eye piece I can see thousands. A couple nights later I took it out again after waiting for more clear skies (it's rain season at the moment) the moon was out this time. We couldn't see as many stars because the moons light (I think) and was also a little hazy. But when looking at the moon the wife and I couldn't believe the details this telescope provided. From the naked eye, the moon was just a sliver. I will post a picture. I can't wait to take this bad boy camping in the mountains with no light pollution and see what's really out there. The scope came collimated already but with all the clouds lately I have been practicing collminating. Took a bit to get the hang of but Orion has good videos and I can collminate this scope in a couple minutes now. I found this scope easy to use and setup. I have seen reviews on other Orion listings bashing the Ez finder scope but I have no issues using it. Was easy to dial in and I just put the red dot on a star or object then look in the eye piece and the object is there. The Ez finder works great people!!!! Also, Orions customer service is 100%.

(Update a few days later)
Woke up at 4:30 AM because I found out that Jupiter, Saturn and Venus would be visible. Pulled up my app to know where to look then with the Ez finder I put the dot on Jupiter and looked through the scope and it was right there. Amazing. Unfortunately it was too bright to see any details but looked like a bright ball with 4 moons around it. I will be ordering a filter kit so I can see the bands and hopefully the storm. Next stop Saturn. Just as easy to find with the Ez finder. Saturn looked unreal. It's small but can perfectly see the rings. Was worth waking up early for. Went to back to bed before Venus could come over the horizon. I couldn't get a picture of Jupiter and Saturn because it is too hard being that zoomed in and this telescope really isn't meant for taking pictures. I did buy a cell phone mount adapter so I can get better pictures of at least the moon. I will post updated picture. If I manage to get decent pictures of Saturn and Jupiter I will come back and post it. This is the first telescope I have ever owned or used and in one week I have seen Orion and nebula. The moon. Mars. Jupiter. Saturn. If I stayed awake a little longer I could have seen Venus, maybe I will tomorrow morning. I definitely recommend this telescope.

title: In-Depth Review
text:
There’s a lot to like about the Montech Gamma 750 watt power supply. It has great specifications at a low price. The only cause for hesitation is that Montech is relatively unknown when it comes to PC hardware, at least here in the United States.

Build: Montech, like many brands do not manufacture their own power supplies. This unit is made by CWT, which is very well known when it comes to power supplies, making units for many brands, including Corsair and Enermax. That should build some confidence in the consumer; even if you are unfamiliar with Montech, you can be confident in the quality of the unit as it’s made by a reputable source.

One the outside, the all black housing is appealing and fits in with most builds. The yellow labeling looks nice, but can easily be removed if so desired. The flat ribbon cables are without a doubt difficult to work with, but they do look great and are all black. Inside, CWT has used Japanese capacitors, which are typically the highest quality available and the unit received 80+ Gold Certification. You will also find a single 12v rail, which is absolutely preferred over multi-rail designs. CWT included a relatively quiet fan; while it does not shut off completely, you would be hard pressed to ever hear it. In my opinion, it’s close enough to silent to give it that label. This is a good quality unit and purely from a build standpoint, checks all of the boxes: 80+ Gold, Japanese capacitors, single 12v rail, quiet fan.

The Let Downs: This is a very good power supply. The only real downside is it’s non-modular. The 750 watt unit has two 12v EPS connectors when most computers only need a single 8-pin. There are two pcie cables, each with a pair of 6+2 connectors for even the hungriest of graphics cards. Two strands of SATA connectors and one strand of Molex. My point is, that’s a lot of cables, especially if most of them go unused! While I can’t fault Montech, I never expected modular cables at this price in a 750 watt unit. But, I would strongly recommend this go into a case with a power supply shroud. Otherwise, you will find it very difficult hiding all those extra cables. And, if this is your first foray into ribbon cables, they do look nice, but they are challenging to work with. I would have preferred Montech opt for black cables with nylon sleeping instead. They look 90% as good as the flat ribbon cables, but are much easier to work with. If they could somehow squeeze semi-modular cables into their price point, that would be even better.

Conclusion: While Montech may be a relatively unknown company, they did choose a quality manufacturer in CWT. I can also say that Montech is trying to establish themselves with a strong Social Media presence and I have witnessed a very active Twitter feed. While I haven’t had to use their customer support, I did reach out to their marketing team and they got back to me promptly. This is certainly a good sign that they have some folks who are responsive to the community. If they continue to make decent products at a friendly price, they have the potential to gain some mindshare in the PC space.

If you found my review helpful, please press that button and consider following me for other tech and PC hardware reviews.

title: A great case for a specific purpose
text:
I’ve been very picky in my search for, what id consider the perfect AirPod Pro case. I was looking for a case that would be, a little water resistant, have the ability to keep the AirPod Pro latch shut, and be able to wirelessly charge my AirPod Pros.

This had no reviews at the time of purchase so i figured I’d give it a whirl.

Regardless of any functions, the case is aesthetically pleasing; big marks on that.

Pros:
The case advertises itself as water resistant. While I didn’t directly try that, looking at the rubber gasket that forms a seal once closed, I feel as though it would hold up to its promise on that. For my purposes, I’m simply looking for something that would keep my Pros dry in my pocket if I got caught out in the rain; this case would be something I’d take my Pros camping with me.

The latch is my favorite part of it. The lock has two steps to open it, one is a metal toggle that keeps the case shut and the other is a metal latch/button that you also have to press to open the case. I have no doubt that if I dropped this case that it would remain closed.

The case is wireless charging friendly. The back of the case is flat, some Pros cases I’ve run into before have a hinge that pushes the body of the case away from the wireless charger, this one has its hinge on the side, rather than the back, of the case.

The cons:
By far my largest issue with this case is how it holds your AirPod Pros. The Airpod Pro charging case just loosely sits inside this case. While this case does have some rubber or silicone pads within it, the Pros charging case rattles around within it. If there was someway that they could add a silicon sleeve so that there is no rattle, these would be perfect, but as is, I worry that my $250 AirPod Pros might be rattled to death.

I prefer wireless charging and this wasn’t an issue for me personally, but be aware that if you charge your Pros via wire, you have to remove them completely from the case. This would make me a little nervous as my Pros would not be protected by the case just so that I could charge them.

Lastly, and this might be a little nitpick. The hinge on the case seems suspect. Long term I’d worry about how brittle the plastic is and how easy it could be to crack the plastic hinge. For details sake, the hinge is the plastic top and bottom shells with a steel pin acting as the hinge pin.

I ended up settling on a different, silicon, case that you peel back from the top of the AirPod Pro case as it doesn’t let the Pros case rattle, won’t let the Pros case open unless you want them opened, and is mildly water resistant.

It was really only the AirPod Pros rattling within this case that turned me off from it so much.

No issues getting the receiver to quickly pair it right up and it was ready to go. I do love how thin it is and I love how quiet the keys are. It also has a very nice weight to it, more on the heavy side. It's heavier than it looks to be so thin. To me, that's a good thing, that I'd hope will mean it's sturdy, strong, built to last, and that it won't be sliding all around my desk from being too light weight. It's just what I'd been wanting. I'd tried MANY other keyboards from amazon that were all about this thin, but they were from more generic brands, and all of them had to be returned for pairing issues or function issues.

My only issues here would have to be: No on/off switch. Not a deal breaker for some, but it's just something I'd like to have, because for so many years, it's always been there. Use it or not, it was there. Another issue would be that I'm really surprised that with all of the wasted space on the top side of the keyboard, Logitech could have included a special battery and sold this as a rechargeable keyboard. The whole "gray strip" at the top comes off to reveal the extra space and also where the 2 AAA batteries are located. And I will hope that this keyboard performs like my other logitech keyboards, which means that it will have great battery life even using the 2 AAA batteries. Time will tell. Again it's just my opinion, so not a deal breaker. The keyboard doesn't have a lot of fancy gadgets or buttons, and I paid $50 for the keyboard and mouse, and I do like it, so I'm happy.

Only other issue here would be the mouse that comes with this...it is very small, very thin, and low profile. It is much too small for my preferences on how I want my mouse to feel, so I will continue to use my logitech M525 mouse happily. I think a lot of people will probably like the mouse though, and I read that a lot of people compare it to an apple mouse design, since its so small and sleek. It is ultra-quiet, you almost can't hear the clicks at all, so as long as it's not too small for your hands, you'll probably love using it.

So in short, if you'd like a thin and quiet keyboard with a number pad, soft, quiet keys that type just like a laptop, this is a very nice design and it seems to be working great right out of the box. I will hope to get many years of great use out of this keyboard, time will tell. Thanks for taking the time to read my review. I hope it was helpful in some way.

FYI, I made that decision after reviewing most of the bad reviews. My takeaway is that these newer kindle (7-10) only last about 18-24 months. I agree with those reviews. The 10 would have been my 5th Kindle since 2012. Batteries don't hold up like the early ones. The Wi-Fi quits working even though it is right next to the router and I have fast speed. Or, they just completely slow down even when not connected to the internet. These have all happened to me and many others. So if you don't mind replacing your Kinlde every 18 months - buy it at your own risk. Just remember, Customer Support does not have the tools to help you!

title: Amazing performance at an absolute premium
text:
The top-of-the line aircooled GPU, performs perfectly out of the box.

Thermals are about on par with the FE, so the extra $300 is really buying the EVGA label and aesthetic.

This was the first 30 series I could snag after months of trying every in stock notification on several sites for 3080 and 3090. I've always been fond of the EVGA cards I've had in the past and it would have been my preferred 3rd party seller even if I'd had full choice.

Can't say how much of an upgrade this would feel like coming from a 1080 Ti or 2080 Ti, but from the Radeon R9 390 I upgraded from, it feels like several generational leaps.

RTX has pleasantly suprised me. From the marketing prior to trying it I had thought of raytracing as a gimmick, but seeing it in games and the way the scene behind your character is reflected on surfaces in front of you (windows, puddles, shiny cars, etc) is subtle but psychologically impactful in immersing you in the world.

Shadows are the element next most improved by raytracing, looking a bit softer and more realistic than even those produced by the complex lighting systems of recent years.

This model directly uses 3 full 8-pin connections from your PSU, rather than being adapted to a 20-pin like the FE cards. The height is a true 3-slot card, but it is very wide and very long - definitely measure your case. My case door barely clears the power cables.

It is heavy too, so if sag bothers you there are riser/pole/stand things that support the front of the card, given that your case is long enough to fit that accessory.

I also bought an HDMI switch to 5 HDMI ports so we can easily switch between cable box, firestick, Wii, ps4, and our pandora box 6 without always hooking and unhooking HDMI wires from the projector.
*Note* This is by no means a 4K quality projector. it is a native 1080p which looks good even at 200”. If you want a 4K projector (not one that just supports it) it’s going to cost you a couple of grand, but if you just want something with good tv quality picture and good brightness so it can be viewed during the day in your living room, this is what you want. *When I say can be viewed during the day I don't mean outside in direct sunlight, but even with the sun shining in from 3 different windows with slightly see-through curtains it works great and we have no problem with viewing during the daytime, or anytime for that matter. The speakers aren’t terrible, but I use my surround sound which I recommended or at least some speakers. The fan being somewhat adjustable is a nice feature and to us, it runs very quiet. I really like that the vertical and horizontal keystone is controlled by the remote and not manually. It works very well to get nice straight edges easily. The only way to make the screen bigger is to move the projector back farther because there is no zoom-in feature on this. That’s the one feature I wish it did have, but it does have an up and down “backward zoom” to ensure your screen fits perfectly in the space you want it. We use this as our main tv over our 4K 70” smart sharp tv (which says something!) I’ve included a bunch of pictures that’ll help with getting an idea of the picture quality.
One other thing to note is *if you’re not getting any sound from your fire stick, cable box, or any other device it’s because of Dolby sound. Go to your audio settings and turn it off and you’ll be good to go.
Also,* if your video isn’t coming through or it’s skipping in and out of audio and video, try another HDMI cable. I had that problem when I received my projector but it was a faulty HDMI, changed it and it worked perfectly.
Very happy with my purchase and so is the family! 5 stars and highly recommended.

*2 months in and everything is still perfect! We use this every day and have yet to run into any problems. Great purchase and worth every penny!

title: Great value for money!
text:
[[VIDEOID:68042342bb6614d8ccc966e4fc00a162]] This is my take on the Bietrun UMKF01 microphone. I am an up and coming content creator on a streaming platform, I need a microphone that could accurately capture the commentary I provide when I stream video game content. So far this microphone gets the job done. It does not have the advanced noise cancelling features that more premium microphones have; but at this price point, I would gladly get this mic as an entry level purchase.
These are what I consider to be its pros and cons:

PROS:
-It is a cardioid microphone and it does pick up audio mainly from the front, some audio from the side and the rear
-It comes with a stand that rotates and is adjustable for proper positioning whether in content creation or meetings
-It uses micro-usb, this to me is a Pro because you are able to get a replacement cable if ever you lose the cable it comes with.
-Indicator LED, it lights up green when it is recording or live and red when it is muted.
-Has headphone jack for monitoring audio (Don't know what you sound like? plug a pair of headphones to do so; volume knob allows you to adjust volume while you monitor your own voice)

Cons:
-Plastic construction, it is what you pay for (the microphone has survived many falls from a 3ft table to hardwood floors)
-Short cable, it does not have that long of a cable (approximately 3ft in length)

Overall, this microphone is a good entry level microphone. If you are doing commentary work, meetings, or need a good quality microphone for the price, this is the microphone for you. If you are well versed in audio manipulating software, this mic is a great purchase as you can make the audio quality even better!

text:
This unit completely replaces the entire stock dash unit and it is very welcomed. It matches and looks like it could have been stock itself. Installation was very easy, only problem was the small clips on the lower backside of the unit that clip into the cars plastic bracket for the unit had to be shaved down a bit. Wasn't a problem for me but if you don't have the means to professionally do this, you could get the exact same end result by simply removing the clips, or even shaving them down with an box cutter or knife of some sort.

The unit was easy enough to setup once installation was complete., and the UI has continued to be fairly easy to use. Bluetooth works exceptionally well. There have been only two times where the unit connected with my phone and the music was playing, only to have no noise come from the speakers. Nothing helped this besides simply turning off the car for a few moments and restarting, allowing the unit to reboot. Like I said this only occurred a couple times and I've had this unit for about 6 months at this point. Im willing to forgive this because I use this unit every single day and it works amazing.

Now if you look up reviews for this unit on YouTube you will see a few different ones, all seemingly the same but with varying appearances in UI's. I've seen a review posted recently with a UI looking similar to my own but more vibrant and not as box like as depicted in this products pictures. As well as the AC info screen, instead of displaying a whole new screen while you're controlling the AC, only a portion of the screen shows the AC info. All I can say to that is do your research into what exact model you're buying. You can even contact Xtrons directly for that information Im sure.

Going off that, the customer service. Xtrons customer support has been absolutely phenomenal. Setting up this unit I had questions about altering certain elements to which they responded promptly and giving me very detailed instructions on how to fix my issues. The unit comes defaulted to reading temperature in Celsius. Xtrons support gave me instructions on accessing a hidden settings menu exactly for this problem.

10/10 product and customer support.

P.S. I'd recommend downloading an app called Square home on the unit. It allows you to customize the look of your home screen.

title: Sorta get what you pay for...
text:
So, first of all I was really excited to find this deal online. I was happy with the price point and the features that it had, and so I purchased it as soon as I could.

Got the first one sent to me, which took a week. But with everything going on, I get it. Non-essential. I got the first one installed, which was pretty easy and low and behold, it didn't work. The picture on the screen was reversed at first. Then it went to black and white fuzz and eventually just stopped working at all. Did a return on Amazon, and sent it back. Decided to get the same one again as the reversed picture seemed like a pretty good quality when I saw what little of it I did see.

Got the next one, another week later. Installed it and everything was fine. Seemed to work great and was pretty happy that the screen was showing correctly. This is where I started to get a bit disappointed.

The volume is...well, annoying. Let me try and explain. If you have the volume set to 1, it is too loud to be what I would consider "background noise". Meaning, with this radio, it's either listen to it and enjoy the music, or mute it and have a conversation. There is no "have a conversation while still having music in the background" setting. Volume 1 is literally too loud to have a conversation without raising your voice. And if you turn on the "loudness" setting (which you assuredly need to do), it's even worse.

Another annoying feature, is that you cannot get the time to display on the LED readout. Not the screen, but the little readout that is under the screen. If you have it on bluetooth, it simply says "BT". There are no other options. Not as big of a deal as the volume, but...annoying.

When you are using the Bluetooth feature to stream music, the forward and the backwards button work fine. I can go forward and backwards to play songs again if I want. However the pause button doesn't work for pausing the music. This means to pause music from your phone on bluetooth, you have to fumble with your phone and pause it there, rather than using the button on the front. Mind you, I am talking about the physical button on the front, not the touch screen. I generally have the screen closed unless I am watching a movie, so I haven't tested that button yet. However the play/pause button on the front should work, no? No, apparently not.

The microphone on this thing picks up the person that is talking to you on the phone. A lot. They can literally hear themselves in stereo over your mic when you are using the hands free calling. Which...sucks for them. Today, I had to put my ear buds in and disconnect from the radio Bluetooth just to have a conversation. Which...was sorta one of my required features, being able to talk hands free without having an earbud in constantly in the truck.

Finally, when someone calls you again, the LEDs on the front don't come through for you. Want to know who's calling? Better grab your phone and look at it, because the LED's tell you nothing at all. I assume the screen will tell you who's calling if it's open. As long as you've downloaded your phone book onto the stereo. I would hope at least. Guess I could test it.

Would I get this radio again? No. I would rather have saved up a little more money and bought something that was...not so annoying. Are these deal breaker issues for everyone? Probably not. For me? Eh...yeah, kinda.

I'm going to load some movies onto a USB drive and see if they will play on the USB port. My guess is that they will not and that I'm limited to DVD video playback only. title: Welp, it didn't work for me.
text:
It didn't work for me. I tried the scratch removal process several times and got no love. Granted, the packaging does say it can't fix deep or severe scratches, so it is a gamble to buy. But still, I can't tell and don't know if my scratch(es) are deep or severe or not. All I know is my disc isn't working properly and I see some tiny scratches on the surface. So, it's kind of a drag to buy a one-job product that you can't find out if it works or not until after you've spent your money on it. The packaging doesn't even say what this is product is actually doing. Is it filling in the scratches? Buffing them out? Polishing/softening them? How does it work? Give me the details. Oh well, who knows maybe it will work in the future if I have the issue again on a different disc. At least I have the cleaning solution bottle I can use for just cleaning discs if the scratch remover never works.

Oh! and I did have another issue with the instructions, which are hidden behind the product and clamshell bubble that you need to tear off, and which you may tear off the instructions with the clamshell since you don't know they're there until after you've opened and destroyed the packaging (excellent job right there Maxell packaging designers). Lucky for me, I only slightly tore a little of the instructions, and they were still readable. I scanned both sides and uploaded them here in case anyone accidentally destroys their package and needs the instructions. It would also have been nicer if the product came in the little box, like the main product image shows. With this clamshell packaging, once you open it, you now have two bottles and a bunch of cloths and no way to store them all together. I guess Ziploc bag plan B is going to be my storage container.

And here's another issue. An important detail that the instructions leave out, and that I don't know the answer to is, it says with steps 1 and 2, to place a drop and wipe the scratch remover on first, then with steps 3 and 4, spray the cleaner on the disc and wipe everything off. But, it doesn't note if you need to wait or not. So, how long do you wait between steps 1-2 and 3-4? Do you immediately wipe the scratch remover off? Wait five seconds? Wait five minutes? Wait a half hour? Who knows? What's this scratch remover even doing? Could that be why it didn't work for me? Did I wait too long to clean it off? Did I not wait long enough? Does it matter? We'll never know. Step 3 should really include the word, "immediately", or "wait 'X' seconds/minutes" for those that have never done this process before. Even if it doesn't matter, it would clear up any confusion or questions.

Another thing, the included wipes seem to leave a bunch of small fibers on your disc after the final cleaning. I'd have preferred a lint-free microfiber cleaning cloth that leaves nothing behind. The idea of putting a disc with small, loose fibers into a sophisticated disc drive mechanism scares me. I ended up just using a separate microfiber fabric cleaning cloth I had to try and dust all of the loose fibers off.

It's a shame large corporations don't actually try out and test their products and packaging as a consumer would before selling them.

title: BEWARE OF THE CANCELLATION TRAP!
text:
I am a full time captain guiding for the last 15 years, I have had many garmin products and have had good service from all of them so I purchased years ago an in-reach if my cell was able to connect with a cell tower in case of an emergency since I frequent remote areas by boat like everglades national park.
My complaint with it is that typing a message takes forever with having to select each letter from a panel of letters its really old software and I hoped I would never have to do it in an emergency!
Well last March 2020 I cancelled the service due to covid-19 because my business in Miami went to near zero as it still is today. The next month they billed me again so I called the credit card company and they refunded my money with proof that I canceled the service. The next month they did it again! So I called the CC company and they refunded my money again with proof! The next month they billed me again! So again I contacted the CC and they refunded my money all this time sending Garmin by e-mail PROOF/explaining that I cancelled their service in MARCH!
I thought the matter was resolved then 2 weeks ago (Sept 2020) I get an e-mail explaining that I owe them near $40.00 and they are going to send it to a collection agency from a Mr Q!!! Now my wife and I are really hot, so we start calling them and e-mailing them. The first thing they asked at garmin is "did you fill out the survey when you cancelled?". Well its been 6 months I don't remember but we did many e-mails back and forth and I dont care about their %&%$ survey just cancel my service! My point its easy to start the friendly service but horrible to get out of it for some like me.
Well I would call them and for some reason the "supervisor" would always be busy and could not help with my problem, so I told them to get use to me because I would be calling EVERYDAY since I don't like threats with my credit.
Well my last phone call a lady at Garmin said I now have a zero balance YAY after 6 months! I don't believe its the Garmin employees who are to blame (I can name them all who I spoke with) but COMPANY POLICY they are just following orders. Shame on you Garmin!
BUT here is the kicker!!! I got a final e-mail from Q which I would like to post here but believe they might delete this post saying "I never cancelled and I actually owe them the balance" BUT they are going to cancel the charge because they like being kind to customers! Can you believe that??? My wife told me not to post this until we get got that e-mail since they might revoke the credit, yes we dont trust them. Here I buy thousands of dollars worth of their products and they beat me up over $40.00.
The only reason they did gave me credit finally is because my brilliant wife who works for a law firm kept all the e-mails going back to march showing proof that we cancelled.
As I write this she is wearing a Garmin watch and I still have a Garmin depth/GPS on my skiff, however I wont be buying their products in the future due to the fact that I am still guilty and I need pity from no one especially when I am a customer not a friend. Shame on you Garmin and I feel bad for the Garmin employees who have to suffer from such terrible company policy with customers and I apologize to them if I was ever rude to them during my communication I just got sick and tired of the all the time my wife and I had to spend proving my innocence for less than $40.00

title: Amazing for $160
text:
Absolutely amazing. First, curtail your expectations of a $160 laptop. Entry smartphones cost about that much. This laptop has less ram and processing power, and memory, then my Note 9. However my phone was $1,000 new so, that's understandable.

Background: I have a Nintendo Switch for gaming, a desktop for heavy computing/VR, and a 55 inch smart TV with surround sound for media consumption. This laptop is for travel computing. Doing classes on Blackboard, writing papers on Google Drive, checking military emails and streaming movies from Netflix via the HDMI port.

For that, it works amazing. It does everything I ask it with zero issues.

Step 1: Lower your expectations. This is basically a chromebook, but I needed a computer running windows to check military emails.

Step 2: take it out of S mode.

Step 3: remove the bloatware. Go to add or remove programs and remove what you don't need.

Step 4: Install Chrome

Step 5: remove pinned programs from start menu and task bar

Step 6: In task manager, stop non essential programs from starting up

Step 7: Update the computer

Step 8: Install Avast antivirus.

All of these steps can be found on Google. The easiest thing to do is search "Speed up windows 10 laptop" and you'll find all of these tips. Do them. The computer is lightning fast now. Boot up in 20 seconds.

No, it won't play Farcry 5, or let you edit movies via Adobe Suite. Honestly, starting Microsoft office takes longer than I want, which is why I use Google Drive. Once you strip it down to the bare bones experience (Turning off OneDrive and Cortana), it becomes a pretty good device, with a 4hr battery, HDMI output and great browsing experience.

Bottom line: These earbuds are a great price, the range is decent and battery life is about 6 hours with constant use (which can be doubled if you only use one bud at a time).

At my job we aren’t allowed our phones in the work areas, but we are allowed to use Bluetooth headphones to listen to media. My cubicle is at the front of the room so I don’t really have a chance to put signal range to the test, but these work perfect for what I need them for. I keep the base plugged into my computer’s USB port, so they are charged overnight. Typically I start use around 9:30, and get the low battery beep around 3:30 (so about 6 hours of constant use). I typically use only one earbud so when that one gets low, I swap it for the other. They have 3 different size attachments and I’ve found that the shape enables them to work in either ear (I prefer to listen with my left ear, so that is a big plus for me). I needed cheap wireless earbuds to listen to my books at work. Nothing fancy. These fit the bill.

title: Very happy with this lens

The lens feels great in the hand. It's classic Voigtlander quality. Smooth focus. Satisfying clicks for the aperture. It's smaller than the 35mm/1.4 and fits perfectly on the Fuji with the Fuji adapter. It has a small hood attached which isn't too big but offers nice protection just the same. I personally also put a B+W clear nano "filter" on all of my lenses for additional protection.

There is some vignetting and maybe light purple fringing at times but that is why you buy a lens like this, for the character. If you want a lens without this uniqueness you can buy any of a number of more clinical and "perfect" lenses. If you want something that can help you grow in unexpected ways as an artist, you explore lenses like this.

Very happy! Highly recommended.

title: A Fantastic Remote for the NVIDIA SHIELD TV Gaming Edition
text:
I purchased this for my "NVIDIA SHIELD TV Gaming Edition" tv box, which came with an original remote control and a gaming controller.

However, the original NVIDIA shield remote control (that came with my shield) is a bad design when it come to volume control because it is TOUCH SENSITIVE. Even though they attempted to reduce the inadvertent touches by receding this volume control into a grove at the bottom of the remote, I found myself inadvertently touching it too often, which would either pause the YouTube video (I was watching) or unintentionally change the volume.

When I found out that the newer NVIDIA shields had a different remote control, that doesn't have this flawed volume functionality, I said to myself "Oooh, I want that!", but when it looked it up online, the price for that newer model's remote was ridiculous. So, I bought this remote instead.

I love this remote! I puchased the one without the keyboard on the back. I've had just about every tv box made, and out of all of them, I like the Roku's remote control the best, and I liked the Apple TV's remote the least. This remote control is very much like the Roku's to me. I can grab it and do everything I need to do without looking at it; I can feel what I need with my hand alone (no eyes). It is way better than the original NVIDIA shield's remote. Even the microphone works, and it has this additional button where you can toggle onto the screen a mouse-cursor which can be controlled by moving this remote in air. I don't use that much, but I think is pretty cool that you can toggle it off and on using a button that's on this remote.

The only thing, that would have been a little nicer, would have been if the remote control operated over bluetooth instead of a low-profile USB dongle. This is exclusively because the NVIDIA Sheild only has two USB ports and I already have one of those dedicated to a 256GB thumb drive that increases the storage capacity of my Shield. Luckily, I had an old USB 2 expansion hub available that I wasn't using for anything else. I was a little apprehensive using it instead of a USB 3 hub, but for me it doesn't matter: the only thing I used my one remaining USB port for is charging the game controller, which doesn't require USB 3 speeds. I may upgrade to a USB3 hub ultimately ( if I ever find myself doing more file transfers, which can use the extra speed). I plugged in this USB 2 hub and then plug this remote control's dongle into it, along with my game controller. When I did this the game controller buzzed like normal, indicating to me that it was charging as usual. So, this isn't a big deal; I wanted additional USB ports anyway.

Lastly, setup was as easy as it gets: 1) plug in dongle, 2) install two AAA batteries (not included). After this, it immediately worked.

I recommend buying this. Its a good value.

title: The only way to standalone Clone a Drive and no software is required to do a standalone CLONE
text: Great product!! For a quick off line Clone, simply put your old drive in the SOURCE slot and your new Drive [of equal or greater storage size] in the Target Slot with the POWER  rocker switch set to off on the back of the WAVLINK. [Note: No need to partition or format the Target drive and no need to connect the WAVLINK to your computer.] Plug the power brick of the WAVLINK into the power outlet and plug the other end into the WAVLINK. Place the WAVLINK Power rocker switch in the on position and wait for the two blue Source and Target front panel lights to illuminate blue. Press and hold the round WAVLINK front panel button and hold it depressed until you see both blue lights flashing.  Let go of the front panel button and quickly while the blue lights are still flashing, depress and release the front panel button to commence the Clone process. You should see the 25% blue light flash indicating that cloning is underway. This will continue through remaining percentage areas and blue lamps will flash as the cloning proceeds through 50%, 75% and finally 100% areas. Cloning is only finished when all Percentage BLUE lights are no longer flashing. The time it takes will vary depending on drive sizes and types but as a point of reference, copying from a 1TB mechanical laptop drive to a 1TB Micron SSD took 3 hours and 15 minutes. Place the WAVLINK Rocker switch in the off position before removing drives following the cloning process. Insert the Cloned Target drive in your computer and you should be good to go.

The problem was the moment i started typing. When looking at the back side, there are 4 rubber pads to prevent the keyboard from sliding around when using. I point them out in the picture. The problem is that the two outside panels are not supported by any pads on the very ends. The ends of the keyboard are hovering slightly above whatever surface it's resting on. (In the picture, the counter top). When I type on any keys that are on that ends panels (ie Q,W,A,Z,1,2,Tab,Caps,Arrow keys,Enter,Backspace), the ends of the keyboard flexes and taps against the surface with every keystroke. You can see the gap on the ends vs when it's pushed down on when typing in the picture. I feel like a rubber stopper or pad along the bottom at the very end would've solved this. I guess I could've gone to Home Depot and buy some rubber or felt pad but for $50, I felt this flaw should've been addressed.

I really wanted to like this because of the positive reviews and the portability. I like to travel as light as possible and this wouldve been perfect. It's only because of that tapping with every keystroke on both ends is what made me return it. It's my only complaint but a annoying deal breaker.

title: Great price for a great product from a great company.
text:
I was in the market for a gaming PC for a good while, debating on whether I should build my own or buy a prebuilt. Initially I was dead set on building my first gaming PC, and I did all of the research and found all of the parts I wanted on line for the best price. I believe the overall price for the part were around $1000 or so, and that doesn't count any warranty because I was the one building it (this is important for later.) Prior to making the investment in all of the individual part I took one last tour across the internet to see if a prebuilt could beat my build in pricing and power. Low and behold I stumbled across SkyTech gaming and their Legacy Mini. Obviously, you can see that it was the better deal because I purchased it about a month ago. Now I've had ample time with the product to be able to review it and spoiler; its pretty great.

The Legacy Mini is a microATX PC build. In short terms it means the PC is on the smaller side compared to the norm. All of the parts that are in the PC are as SkyTech advertised above and the build quality is well. I believe the parts were very well chosen for the price of the overall unit. It's essentially the same build I had planned out except with a different case and power supply. Using PC part picker, an online website that allows one to build and price a PC build all together, this build to the teeth cost $1077.76 and I believe I used a cheaper power supply and RAM. This goes to show that the price is worth it versus other alternatives. Also I could not find another company that was willing to sell a 1660 ti build similar to this cheaper than SkyTech. Before I go on about my experience with using the unit, I want to add that a PC building YouTuber named ScatterVolt recently released a video titled "Top 5 Pre-Built Gaming PCs for the Holidays! ($500-$2000)." Among those 5 gaming PCs SkyTech produced 3 of them.

Here is a summary of my experience with the unit. I am a college student who has a passion for gaming. I have always played games on an Xbox product and dreamed of switching to PC one day. So this gaming PC is my first and I would not have had it any other way. The unit shipped and arrived exactly when it was said to. Out of the box everything was nice and packaged. Pieces were kept safe from damage over the shipping period. Setup was smooth as can be, SkyTech includes a mouse and keyboard with each unit sold so no need to worry about those peripherals on day one. Boot up was smooth and easy everything started great and the unit itself lit up like an early Christmas decoration. The PC comes with most of the necessities already installed and ready to use (Chrome, Furmark, Geoforce Experience, etc.) It's fast, responsive, and does it all. I set up my Steam and Uplay accounts and very shortly began playing Rainbow Six Siege (my personal game of choice.) Rainbow Six Siege can run around 140 FPS in 1080p at high settings for me. The unit was able to shatter my expectation with the quality of the game. The benchmarks that SkyTech listed for the unit were very accurate. I tried PUBG as well and it performed just as advertised, which is fantastic. The RGB fans are just an addition that make the PC feel more customized and they work flawlessly and beautifully. One last note I want to add is in regard to the PCs ability to be upgraded. Simply it can and it can very easily. Not even a week after purchasing I installed a 2TB harddrive with ease. Eventually I'll upgrade the 16GB of RAM from 2400 hz to 3200hz which again is a very easy process. The case that was chosen for this build makes it rather easy to access all of the parts and interchange them for new ones. I do not believe I will need to purchase or build any other PC from this point forward, which is fantastic.

In summation, I have had the unit for more than a month and have used it almost everyday whether it was for school work, gaming, or streaming TV. I have not had a single issue with the unit. The CPU temperature even under stress has yet to exceed 70 degrees Celsius, which is great for a PC with air cooling. Overall I believe this PC and likely other PCs that SkyTech produces are fantastic products built with passion for people with a passion. If you are looking for a well built machine, whether its your first gaming PC or not, SkyTech has you covered. It's really not rocket science.

title: Probably the best current option for what it is, but temper your expectations
text:
Something like this has been a (relatively) long time coming. Fast NVMe SSDs have been with us for a few years now. I've spent more than a half year looking for a reasonably priced, sturdily built enclosure with a USC-C connector that could house what most people would only ever use for boot drives in desktops and some laptops. This is that (with some caveats).

I'ved just purchased and tested the unit. One thing I did not like (but it was not disqualifying) is the relative difficulty in swapping different SSDs in/out. With the thermal pad (stickiness and thickness), things are a little tight. If you are just going to place your SSD in this unit and not swap another in, this is no issue.

I've now done some tests with two modern NVMe 1TB drives . . . both capable of using four PCIe lanes of bandwidth. These are the Samsung 970 EVO and HP EX920. I have used both on a Asus-motherboard-based desktop where I see reads speeds from 2600MB/s to 3500MB/s, depending. For writes, the HP is between 1700-1800MB/s and the Samsung 2300-2500MB/s. Both are excellent drives that almost anyone would be happy with, as long as you plug them into capable M.2 ports. This was under three OSes (Windows 10, Ubuntu Linux 18.04 LTS, and a hackintosh install with macOS High Sierra . . . I am not able to get Mojave to work well enough with this hardware yet).

Directly connected . . .with this enclosure on a current Macbook Pro running Mojave (so TB3 with four lanes PCIe), I get ~780-790MB/s write, and 730-740MB/s read. I am still running some tests on my desktop, but it only has one USB 3.1 Gen 1 (5Gb/s) connection. I am guessing I will end with half this speed or less, but again, not quite the same OSes.

Connected through TB3 dock . . . if it matters to anyone, I have a Caldigit TB3 dock that I am testing with, too. Using this same Macbook Pro, when I have things connected to this TB3 dock (including a DP-connected 1440p monitor running at 60hz, and some usb peripherals), I get:
--on the downstream TB3 connection, ~610-615/MBs write and 595-600MB/s read
--on the USB 3.1 Gen 2 (10Gb/s) connection, I get ~510-515MB/s write and 625-635MB/s read (not yet quite sure yet why this would be a little bit higher than the TB3 connection)
--one the USB 3.1 Gen 1 (5Gb/s) connection, I get 230-240MB/s write and 260-270Mb/s read

So if you want the max speed possible (assuming your SSD can read/write data at this speed), hang it directly off a directly connected four PCIe lane TB3 connection. Right now, this seems to be the best option of its kind. Just do not expect speeds that you currently seen on modern motherboards (M.2 connector directly via four lane PCIe) with modern drives.

title: It's decent for a $50 headphone
text:
I love headphones so much that I buy at least 2 pairs every year. Friend of my recommended this, and it's the first time I bought a soundpeats product. There are pros and cons about this headphones, overall, it's decent for $50.

PROS:
1. Super easy to use. The earbuds turn on/off automatically when you take them out or put them back in the case. It connects really fast.
2. Bluetooth 5.0+TWS connection. I tested for about 4 hours and I didn't experience any drop sound, which is great. You can use either one earbud or both.
3. Battery life. I gave the earbuds a full charge before using and was able to get close to 4 hours of listening time
4. Button control. I like that you can control everything through the earbuds (volume, play/pause music, answering calls) and don't have to take out your phone.

CONS:
1. Design. It's definitely bigger than lot of the TWS true wireless earbuds on the market. It stick out quite a bit. If you are someone with a small face, it's doesn't look that good on you.
2. Fit. While it's comfortable to wear, it doesn't feel snug. I can't tell you how many times I accidentally knocked it off when I tried to tie my hair or adjust my earrings. I haven't tried to work out in this but I would imagine that it probably will fall off at some point.
3. Sound isolation. Because it's not a snug fit, quite a bit of outside sound can come through when I am walking down the street next to traffic. Yes, you can drown it out by turning up the volume, but you really shouldnt listen to music too loud

NEUTRAL:
1. Sound quality. When I read about how it has a dual dynamic driver (beryllium+composite), I was expecting a somewhat full and fun sound, like those you want to dance to. But what I got instead was a very clean sound. So when you listen to vocal, audio book or single instrument (piano, cello, etc), they sound fantastic. It gives you a crisp, true to nature sound. But if you listen to rock/metal or orchestra, which you want a somewhat full/surrounding sound, it's not there. So depends on what you listen to, you may either love the sound quality or just feel Meh.
2. Mic/call. It's not bad, it doesn't stand out compare to others

title: Didn't Like These At First But Have Grown To Love Them
text:
I would like to change my review of these speakers. After some glitches along the way, and the shock of them being so large and heavy, I decided to keep them and give them a try. Then I started doing a little digging around on Youtube.com for reviews and examples of other multimedia speaker systems, and I can say that these speakers sound much better than even more expensive computer speakers I've seen reviewers sample.

I have only ever owned really cheap $25 speakers. I was expecting to just be blown completely away when I first got them, so I was very surprised when they weren't as "loud" as I thought they would be. But as I learned from watching the YouTube reviews, louder isn't always better. These speakers can be turned up to full volume and still give out really powerful bass and vocals without distorting.

My initial reaction was after listening through a Bluetooth reaction as well. The connected to the comp sound is 100% better.

As for the design... well, they're a lot bigger than I would have liked for computer speakers, so please be aware they're very large. They're going to take up a lot of real estate on the desk. And Bluetooth isn't always reliable. But as for sound, I've really grown to enjoy the audio experience they provide, and I do appreciate a competitive landscape on audio. It's good to see mid-range priced speakers for people who can afford a little more but not the best.

And the boxing, it was really obvious that Edifier wanted this product to feel special, and that's nice to see from a smaller company. Everything was bagged up nice, good packaging, and even though it was a little difficult to get everything open, it seems like they were going for the "make you feel like you really bought something amazing" experience.

That said, I ended up keeping these speakers and enjoy them very much. Compared to some of the more expensive brands I've heard sampled on Youtube, these speakers aren't just louder, they're clearer as well. So thanks for that.

title: UPDATE: never stops freezing to buffer. Stay far away. Get a cheap PVR.
text:
UPDATE10: Once again putting the most relevant update at the top. Ive been running tests comparing watching a show over the recast to just streaming it over the internet. The recast never stops buffering, whereas the steam runs just fine. Can someone explain to me why its faster to beam this signal all across the planet than move it three feet from my recast to my tv? I guess "cord cutting" means wasting a lot of time before giving up and just mirroring from my phone like a normal person.

Also, i really hate this "weak signal" popup. Great, sometimes its a weak signal, i get it. Why disrupt autoplay for THAT? Why cant i turn this message off? Why does it stop autoplay? It should, at the very least, just go away on its own after a few seconds. So annoying.
----------------
UPDATE8: Putting this at the top because its most relevant. After months, ive kinda learned what the pattern with this thing is. It seems to always attempt to stream in hd. My modem doesnt seem to be able to handle that. Ever. Then, the device spends about 5 minutes stopping every couple seconds, more time stopped than playing, then eventually figures out that it needs to reduce the quality. Itll play fine at reduced quality for about 5 minutes, but then switch back to hd and repeat. Every time. Itll buffer for 12 seconds for one second of playback. Does that sound watchable to you? I guess to watch an hour show itd have to buffer for 12 hours? Fine. Do that. Whatever it takes so i can watch one thing.
Several solutions to this. 1) Allow me to record at low quality, 2) Allow me to select low quality playback, 3) Best of all would be if i could download an episode. Then itd never skip and i could actually watch one show in hd.

UPDATE9: Yeah, this thing is going into the back of my closet so i can use the antenna for other things. Shame. Ive lowered my review to one star. I kept going back to try, thinking maybe theres some time of day itll stream without stopping to buffer constantly? There isnt. Theres absolutely nothing i can do to watch something without skipping and ive trial and errored a lot. The fact is, there are just easier ways to watch all these shows. Kinda defeats the purpose of me housing the recording locally when it still must inefficiently go through a modem. Officially done trying and giving up. Cannot recommend to anyone for any price. Get a pvr that connects to your tv.
-----------------
ORIGINAL: Wow. I really wanted to like this product. For the cost, it doesn't really seem worth the value. With the annoyances, i might just recommend a 50 dollar pvr. It might not be able to know a shows title to record at times you dont set, but at least it'll friggin go.

Mine just arrived today and its been a day of frustration. I will update this review with all the issues later, but for now i just had to come and report the worst one: it sometimes freezes to load every second. Dude. Buffer more. Or let me connect it directly to my tv with an hdmi. This is ridiculous, and i frankly cant see ever using it while its lagging like this, and it seems like itll eventually just be relegated to paperweight until the firmware is finished.

One more thing. The app on the phone doesnt have the tv listings, it only displays whats currently on, so you cant find new series to record. Obviously they could include this, but it just seems to me like a shameless money grab to force people to buy a fire media player if they dont have one. So far i can't see any reason my phone cant do the things it forces me to do on the fire stick.

UPDATE: Sometimes when i try to set up a recording, nothing happens. Considering that the only feature of this thing is recording...

As ive said, there are many things you need a fire media device for, but you can only change the default recording settings on app for phone or tablet. Come on! Let me do everything in one place or the other!

UPDATE2: Sometimes completely freezes my fire stick. I have to mute my tv to silence the thing im trying to stop because none of the buttons do anything and i press stop or back or home repeatedly. A couple times, ive been on the verge of powercycling it when its gone to the home screen, only to still not respond to any buttons, so i have to powercycle anyhow. Sorry, did i buy a dvr or a chore? Nothing else freezes the stick. I got this thing 2 days ago and am seriously considering returning it.

UPDATE3: Yeah, this thing skips way too frequently. At this point, im setting it aside until im feeling in a far more patient mood. Amazon really dropped the ball on this one. A tb of space, yet 0 seconds of buffering. Whats the point of even seeing if its working from one moment to the next, and invite frustration? I guess what im saying is, because this is only transmitting over a local network, that means that the demands on the modem are probably ridiculous. Maybe if one has a top of the line modem, itd be fast enough. Youd think between the two devices it forces me to use, thered be enough memory to buffer a show. Netflix manages it, and they're not sending data locally.

Why is it so hard to hold down the alexa button and say "skip forward 200 seconds"? I mean, thats the main reason i got this thing was to skip commercials. Not to sit here waiting while it thinks and thinks and then freezes and no buttons do anything. It's almost like, instead of "skip forward", it thinks i said "do nothing and freeze up."

UPDATE4: Meh. Ive upgraded my review from 2 to 3 stars. I'd say it works, without skipping every few seconds, 10% of the time. The other 90%, i just give up and watch something else. Im not sure how i can ever catch up to watching the shows ive recorded, but im done devoting mental or emotional energy to this object.

UPDATE5: Today is a great example. Ive been trying to watch one episode several times over the course of the day. Itll be fine for 15 minutes and then lag like 10-20 times in a minute and i cannot take that. I dont know how else to say this: BUFFER LONGER. Its like, they didnt want buffering to last a long time all at once, so they dont seem to have ANY buffer and it just plays it as it loads. NO. Who wants that? Buffer for as long as it takes so you dont have to buffer again.

I definitely cant use this thing as i was planning. title: Dream Machine
text:
I just got my Triton 500 yesterday (with the 2070 Super, couldn't afford to go higher). I have to say this thing is incredible! I've been searching for a gaming laptop for awhile, and tried just about every one. This gaming PC has won the competition! It games like a dream. I can't believe it's a laptop! It games the same as my desktop PC, if not better.

The battery lasts way too long for a gaming laptop. 6 hours with the NVIDIA GPU engaged is insane (youtube and Amazon Video).

Everything is engineered way too smooth with too many choices (GPU choice toggle/coolboost/Preset Overclocking/etc etc etc). Every time I look for an option to change it's already thought of, and done correctly.

Even the design is beyond beautiful. The RGB is insane! This laptop screams elite gamer, but also dignified and classy at the same time.

Also, I have a unique heat issue. I have burn damage to my hands so I can't use a laptop where the surface temp gets too hot (G14 sole my hands up for days). I can't get my Triton 500 to get hot. The surface temp is nice and cool, and even the GPU hasn't gone over 75 degrees C even on CoD warzone with maximum settings.

Performance has been incredible. I've been maxing out warzone in every way I can imagine trying to get this laptop to reach a limit. It hasn't yet. The 300Hz refresh rate is a game changer. I went from 2-3 kills a game to around 6 just by being able to see them before they see me.

Thank you all for your hard work in designing a dream machine Acer. I don't usually pull this hard for a product, but for the first time in years I'm beyond impressed! It's so rare to see a product intentionally designed as a masterpiece, and Acer has done it! I've never tried an Acer laptop before, but I've instantly changed my status to Fanboy!
