title: "Inexpensive" often comes at a price
text:
The light works fine, and it's quite portable and simple to use. But it has some minor flaws that I'm still sorting out. However, the big problem is that the trigger is defective and I can't just get a replacement trigger. I have to return the entire kit for a replacement. That's incredibly inconvenient and means I'm going to be without a light for up to 6 weeks because of the time it takes to go back and forth to China. The only good thing so far is that the strobe has a sync port in the back where I can plug in another manufacturer's remote trigger.

But this speaks to the way things are manufactured these days. To keep costs down, equipment is manufactured with no overruns. That means no extra parts, no replacement parts, nothing to fix the equipment. If a tiny (otherwise replaceable) part malfunctions, the entire unit and all its accessories must be replaced. And the consumer must wait without equipment while their purchase rides a boat to China. But, that's the "price" you pay for cheap equipment... The price of Inconvenience.

title: Total crap compared to the $25 Wyze
text:
The picture quality is comparable to the WYZE cam - however that's where all similarities end. This camera has "thermal" sensors supposedly, but picks up falling leaves as "bodies". It was running down my phones batteries with its endless "alerts" to leaves floating down. Whereas Wyze cameras have a clear and very customizable software running the camera - this software is bare bones and instructions are in google translated English. "After opening, you can monitor the human situation who stands in front of the device and gives alarms." What?

Wyze cams give the capability to record when either sound or motion is detected, and to customize detection zones and sensitivity and to set a schedule if so desired. All wyze recordings are then placed in a folder called events - Zumimall DOES NOT.

Wyze places a highlight around motion, zumimall does not. Wyze is also compatible with Alexa, Zumimall is not.

Given that this camera is more than 3 times the price of the Wyze, has none of the features in a cheaper camera, and the only difference is that I need a cover to use the Wyze outdoors - this camera is a FAIL.

I'm too late to return or else I would have sent this back and been done with it.

I've attached the settings screenshots for each. I'm not sure if other security cameras are better than Wyze, but I do know Zumimall is not one - in fact, I wish I had never bought it.

title: The best compromise between value, comfort, and functionality in a non-MS keyboard
text:
Those of us who own Microsoft Surface tablets love and loath them.

We love them because they are powerful, thin, light, and fun to use.

We loath them because they aren't quite a laptop, even with the MS clip-on keyboard cover. The kickstand idea looks good on paper, but how many of us really use tablets as tablets and not like ad-hoc laptops? Without a keyboard, you are basically wasting 80% of the Surface's power. Just go buy an iPad if all you want is a tablet. You'll be happier with it if all you're doing is watching streaming video or reading books.

But if what you want is a modular tablet/keyboard combo to get you the power of a laptop with the versatility of a laptop, you really only have a couple of options.

a) You buy Micro$oft's keyboard/cover combo, which is decent enough, but doesn't really solve that painful kickstand problem when you try to use it as a pseudo-laptop...

or

b) You buy a bluetooth keyboard/folio combo, which is usually a major kludge and chock full of compromises. Performance suffers and the whole thing just looks cheap. Why spend $800 on a Surface when it winds up looking like you stuffed it into a cheap pleather case with a crappy bluetooth keyboard.

Enter option c) The Brydge 12.3 Pro+ bluetooth keyboard. This is the first and only (to my knowledge) keyboard that actually makes the Surface act more like a SurfaceBook. You slip the Surface into the clips that hold it snugly to the keyboard, you pair up the Bluetooth, you get typing. I'm typing this review on it, BTW. In the world of keyboard options the Brydge 12.3 Pro+ is...

a) An incredible keyboard (super comfortable with a decent amount of spring to the keys)
b) Well balanced (it has enough weight to keep the tablet part from tipping it over)
c) Seems very stable as far as the Bluetooth connection is concerned

The pros are obvious. For the first time the Surface behaves like a true laptop without the cheap pleathery case/combo feel.

The cons are a little tougher to define, but they get down to the central issue. If you want a true SurfaceBook, get ready to spring another $500 to get into the ballpark. This does not make the Surface a SurfaceBook. The surface doesn't "clip" into the Brydge the way the MS keyboard/cover clips onto the Surface. The Brydge uses small-ish tabs at the lower corners of the surface to "cinch" the Surface into place. They are silicone coated clips that provide a snug, but not "clicked" point of connection with the tablet. In other words, the tablet *can* slip free, especially if you do what I did and try to add a sticker to the back of your Surface to protect that beautiful aluminum case from scratches. Then, what you'll wind up doing is also what I did, cutting away pieces of that beautiful skin so the clips maintain perfect, flat contact with the back of the Surface. After I put the skin on and tried to clip the Surface into the Brydge, the clips failed to make perfect contact, so the silicone coating wouldn't grip and the tablet slipped right out.

But, if you do buy a skin and spend a few moments creating a template to cut the corners out before you apply it to your Surface, the silicone clips on the Brydge will maintain a reasonably snug connection with the tablet and you will have all the functionality of a slim, powerful laptop with a solid, author-approved keyboard.

Bottom line, the Brydge 12.3 Pro+ keyboard for the Microsoft Surface Pro line of tablets is an incredible value, a solid performer, and perfectly funtional. Just buy a decent skin for the back of your Surface and make sure the silicone-covered pads that hold the Surface in place have complete contact with the tablet case and you'll enjoy the best of both worlds. The tablet functionality of the Surface when you need it, and the keyboard comfort of a laptop for the 80% of real world purposes that we buy a Surface for in the first place.

Highly recommended.

title: It works...so far
text:
Buying aftermarket batteries for devices is, in my experience, akin to flipping a coin. I was certainly skeptical of this battery after reading about reviewers who had problems with fit, but it seemed like the most well-vetted choice. Well, suffice it to say that it works, with the caveat that it has only been a few weeks since I installed it.

The replacement process is not easy, nor is it particularly difficult, but an instructional video is worth watching. The battery I received fit perfectly, but I could see how if any dimension were a tiny bit too big, it would cause problems with fit. The battery seems to charge just fine, although there is no longer an obvious automatic charging cutoff. This may be a problem with the JBL speaker itself, however, as I can't see how a battery without any onboard 'smart' functionality could affect this.

The battery holds charge much like the original so far. If it maintains this for a year, I will be over the moon. So far, so good!

Finally, it's absolutely ridiculous that JBL itself doesn't offer a replacement battery for consumer replacement. It's really a (bad) sign of the times when an otherwise seemingly well-designed product becomes useless after 2 years of use and can only be 'fixed' by JBL for the same cost as purchasing a new speaker.

title: Do not buy new version of this SSD after 2021 - was excellent but now it's not
text:
PNY recently changed the TBW for this NVME SSD and I'm wondering if it's because they switched over to QLC instead of TLC previously. ADATA was caught doing this so I do not recommend buying any version of this SSD after 2021 because their TBW (for the 1TB version) has gone from 1665 to 360 which is an 80% decrease! I repeat: Do not buy this NVME SSD after 2021. I don't think Crucial, Sabrent or Samsung (they all make their own NAND) have resorted to these deceptive practices so get an SSD from them instead.

Old review:
There are 5 NVME SSDs that I consider to be the best bang for your buck. Samsung is off the list cause they're too expensive but their SSDs are extremely good and have a good warranty. Any of the below are great and have decent warranties (3-5 years). Buy whichever is cheaper as they all have Toshiba/Micron/Hynix NAND.

1. HP EX920 (hard to find in stock right now)
2. Inland Premium NVME
3. Sabrent Rocket NVME (Not Q version)
4. PNY CS3030
5. ADATA SX8200 Pro

The PNY CS3030 actually checks off a lot of my requirements:
-quad-core, 8-ch
-has DRAM (DDR4 for 1TB-2TB, DDR3 for everything below 1TB)
-TLC (better write capacity than QLC)
-5 year warranty
-3500read/3000write
-Phison E12 (all of the good consumer NVMe SSDs use this and it's excellent)

Please note that this does not contain an M.2 standoff so you may have to order one in case your motherboard or laptop doesn't have one. It is also doublesided but this will not affect most PCs or laptops unless yours is a really thin ultrabook like the Lenovo X1E which uses only single sided M.2 SSD.

title: Nice Ring Doorbell but confusing power requirements.
text:
The Ring doorbell-2 is a great product. But, a lot of Ring doorbell -2 owners, who do not have an existing wired doorbell, still want to power their doorbell-2 using a simple 18 Volt AC transformer. There are at least two Amazon vendors that sell a simple transformer that plugs into a standard 120 Volt house outlet that connects directly to the back of the Ring doorbell-2.

There is great confusion over (1) the need for a 25 Ohm resistor in series with a 18 Volt transformer as well as (2) the exact range of Voltage and Wattage requirements for the AC transformer.

Many people claim that their doorbell-2 works perfectly with an 18 Volt AC transformer rated at 500 ma connected directly to the doorbell-2, while Ring LLC claims that a 25 Ohm resistor is definitely required. Other owners claim that with or without the 25 Ohm resistor the indication that their doorbell-2 is wired to the transformer comes and goes (when wired to the transformer the circular light around the push bottom should remain on all the time and the App shows that the doorbell-2 is charging.

So, Ring LLC - exactly how do we use a simple AC transformer to directly power a Ring doorbell-2 and what specifically are the AC Voltage and Wattage requirements of this transformer?

title: Practical product, great service, flexible pricing
text:
I have been using this tracker + wifi product for a week and have ben impressed by its working. This is the only product in the market I found where you get both tracking feature + wifi hotspot. You have settle for one or the other usually increasing the total price. Additionally you are not locked on monthly data usage charges.

The 9.95 pricing only contains the tracking feature and additional data packs can be added on their website immediately when needed and as many times as you want. This gives flexibility to add data packs only when needed/travelling. There is also flexibility to choose how much data you want to buy 500mb/1gb/2gb etc to accommodate for the time left in the billing cycle (tracking billing cycle and data pack usage have the same billing cycle). When data packs are added, Wifi is automatically turned on when the car is turned on. When data pack is used up, wifi will turn off (but the tracking feature is ON of course permanently as long as the 9.95 fee is paid every month).

In case I don't want to connect to a OBD1 port of the car, I can also find many OBD1 adapters online that I can use to plug in a regular 12v cigarette lighter port or directly to a 12V battery. This makes it a great option for tracking RV trailer and hotspot usage if needed to be disconnected from the tow vehicle.

The android app is stable and after a little bit of learning curve can be operated easily. All alerts work correctly.

The service is prompt and courteous. A live human being directly calls you back and works through any setup process or issues as you speak on phone.

Works on ATT cellular network which is reliable at rural and urban coverage.

title: Not mostly metal
text:
My previous Cord Reel was one of the ubiquitous orange plastic type. Mine has K-100 molded into the plastic. The handle on it broke when it fell about four feet to a concrete floor. I was looking for something a little nicer.

As many reviewers point out, the tubing in the stand for this product is metal (seemingly plenty stiff and sturdy for the easy task), but the reel, cord clips, and turning handle are all plastic. While the plastic seems adequate to task, by direct comparison the reel side plastic seems slightly more flexible and no sturdier than my orange reel.

As to capacity, this will vary by brand (not all 14/3 cord has the same exterior dimension). My cord is 100 feet of Romex brand (yellow jacketed) 14/3. It fit my orange reel with a little room to spare. This Woods 22849 has the reel edges a bit farther apart, but the reel exterior diameter is a bit less than the orange. When I wound the Romex on, I had about as much spare room as on the orange reel. Possibly I was a bit sloppier at getting the cord on, so if I did better, there would be more room. If you are calibrated to the orange reels, I suggest you plan that this one has about the same total capacity, just wider and less deep.

Unlike others who found the clips unsuitable, I thought the one I used to moor the mid-point of my cable did just fine. I like that there is a second, so if I break the first I still have something.

For the first time on a cable reel, I am following the advice of many reviewers here to double over the cord, clip the midpoint into the reel, and roll along so you have both ends available, unrolling only what you need. This works. However, the people advocating this method should all warn you: THIS IS FORBIDDEN BY THE MANUFACTURER. Both the K-100 orange reel and this Woods 22849 carry sidewall instruction telling you to unreel the full cord length before use. The reason is safety. The mechanism is heat. For ANY extension cord, failure to extend it means the heat rise in the conductor coming from the load current interacting with the conductor resistance will make it hotter, as the heat has a poorer escape path. This, in turn, lowers the maximum safe current. As I am powering a modest line trimmer which runs intermittently, I believe myself to be safe. If you are running a space heater or other device which consumes a lot of power, don't do this. If in doubt, put your hand to the stacked-up cord after your setup has run for a while. If it has warmed up noticeably, beware.

title: Beast Mode Activate?
text:
This laptop is a beast. I literally haven't found a game in which I can't run at max settings and still get an amazing frame rate. This is all without activating the "Turbo" setting which automatically over-clocks everything on your laptop, and cranks up the fans to max speed to keep them cool.

This laptop is very sturdily made, and the backlit keyboard is a great addition, although you can not change the colors in this model.

Cooling System- The fans and the design do a great job at keeping this beast of a laptop cool, allowing amazing ventilation that blows out the back of the computer. They can get a little loud when running in the above mentioned "Turbo" mode.

Screen- Great looking screen. I have no issues about the screen.

---Con---

title: Excellent Wireless Headphones
text:
I've owned quite a few BT headsets over the years. This is my first pair of "wireless" ones.

The 1st impression is pretty good. The packaging is high quality. You could even say it's a little excessive. Skullcandy is aiming for high end of the headset market with these, while trying to keep the price down.

BREAKDOWN

SOUND
These sound amazing. I've seen some people complain about static, but I can hear none. These are some of the best headphones used, in regards to sound. It's not over the top in any aspect. Sometimes a maker will try to compensate for a lack of quality with crazy bass or some other trick. You will not find that here.

COMFORT
These are possibly the most comfortable earbuds I've ever used. They come with three sets of silicone tips, so you can match up the one that feels nice in your ears.

I was afraid they'd feel heavy in my ears, but that is not a factor.

BATTERY LIFE
They say you can get 12 hours of battery life. I've only tried twice, but I have not hit 12 hours. That being said, battery life has never been an issue. They lasted more than long enough for my needs. If you do run out, just pop the in the case, and they'll charge up again.

QUALITY
The overall quality is high. One thing that shows this is the charging format. All my other BT headphones, speakers, and earbuds use the old micro USB connection, and most are not fast charging. These use USB C. They could have cut a corner here, but they did not.

The charging case clicks shut. I've seen some that do not. This is a nice touch. You do not have to worry about throwing them in your bag and the case popping open.

FUNCTIONALITY
These paired with my Android phone with no issues. I've never had any issues with them connecting. You do need have both buds in for full functionality. If you want to wear only one so you can hear whats going on around you, the other needs to be in your pocket. You cannot leave one at home. This is not an issue for me, but I can see how it would annoy someone else.

These will not replace my hiking BT earphones. I would not use these to exercise or when excessive moisture could be a factor. That might be a turn off for some people.

VALUE
This is a tough one. These are nice and high quality. They are priced lower than some of their high end competitors (in some cases, much lower), but you can find cheaper, wireless earbuds that are not bad. So it boils down to this - If you are looking at high end earbuds and want to save money, buy these! If you are looking at wireless, but can't afford the high end ones - at least consider these. If money is the biggest factor - move on.

OVERALL
These hit the five star mark, but it's close. If 4.5 was an option, I've use that rating. These are not perfect. They are a few features short of being perfect, but they are perfect for how I plan to use them.

If money is the biggest factor, you need a pair that can take a beating, or you want the most advanced earbuds, move on.

title: Far better than other brands of similar price
text:
So, I'm really paranoid about getting bugs in trips and my stuff getting crushed in transit, but this is one of the most sturdy yet simple bags I've ever owned.

The overall design isn't too much, and what I mean by this is that there aren't a ton of unnecessary toggles, loops, fabric or other trash that bedbugs can hide in, and the seam work is great as it's very tightly woven. The zippers align well, although it's all dependent on where you join them (I'd recommend at the top of the bag for maximum closure). Also, with the bag being only a dark heather grey, some semi-gloss black with orange accents, it's pretty sharp looking for both business and casual wear.

While the main storage compartment isn't massive, I was able to fit a Switch, several mugs in boxes, an oversized hoodie, a PlayStation Vita and a pair of Bluetooth over-the-ear headphones with a bit of room to spare. The rigid construction of the bag allows it to retain its shape and rest vertically with no issues.

The sunglass compartment is excellent for other small electronics, like a phone or portable batteries, but I'm also confident that you could throw this bag across a room with glasses in it and they'd be perfectly fine.

The side pockets do leave a bit to be desired as far as non-intended use is concerned, but if you're only looking to holster a drink, they're sufficient.

The TSA laptop section is spacious, features a neat pocket window for a quick view, and works well for its intended purpose. It's also excellent for storing documents/paper/magazines if you're worried about them being folded or damaged, as again, the bag's rigid construction does well to prevent anything happening to your cargo.

All in all, for the price, I was much more satisfied with this bag in comparison to Swissgear bags in the same price range. This bag was much more sturdy, smaller (which helped when trying to stow under an economy seat, or when getting into crowded Japanese elevators and trains), and far more quiet, as I'm really bothered by bags that jingle like you're covered in keys or something. Highly recommended.

title: The only dive case with full touchscreen support on the market
text:
I purchased (directly from Divevolk) the SeaTouch 3 the moment they came out with an insert for the iPhone 11 Pro at the end of 2019. I took it on a scuba diving trip and tried it out over 15 dives with the maximum depth of 150 feet. Overall, it performed well.

The touchscreen:

The touchscreen is THE feature that makes this dive case unique and uniquely capable. With other phone cases one has to install an app and use Bluetooth to connect to and control the phone. These dive cases can only access a small subset of phone camera features. The ability to turn on and off the phone to conserve power while it's in the Divevolk case is a real plus, too.

The touchscreen is consisted of two plastic layers encasing some sort of a clear gel. I could not find any reference on the physics behind this design. Suffice to say that the touchscreen of the case is soft and thick. This makes swiping very difficult, especially around the edges of the screen. Making matters worse is the need to swipe from the bottom and top corner of the iPhone to access the home screen, control center, etc. To compensate, however, one should turn on Assistive Touch. Incidentally, one should also turn on Tap to Wake and turn off passcode or face ID for easier underwater operations.

The touchscreen registers touches well when dry. However, underwater it becomes unreliable and unresponsive at times. In particular, pressing the same spot, e.g. the shutter button in the camera app, would often not register after the first press. Pressing at a different spot on the screen and then go back to the shutter button often resolved the problem. Similarly, press and hold, e.g. to take video in the photo mode of the camera app, would sometimes lose the touch registration and stop. Swiping is nearly impossible underwater.

The durability of the soft touchscreen was of some concern as equipment on a dive often gets knocked around a bit. One should be mindful not to let sharp objects come into contact with the touchscreen.

Design principle:

Unscrew the grip and one can see a soft tube connecting the case and the grip compartment. I did not unscrew the 10 tiny screws holding the compartment cover. Presumably it contains a bladder. As pressure increases underwater, the bladder is squeezed and air is passed through the tube into the phone case. The pressure inside the case is equalized to the pressure outside. Since there is no pressure differential at the seal, a super tight seal is not critical as in other hard case designs that maintain one atmospheric pressure inside the case.

As the bladder is squeezed under water, sea water would have to enter not only the grip but also the bladder compartment. It appeared that after a dive the water drained properly, at least out of the grip. However, I observed some salt deposits after opening up the grip. It's unclear what goes on inside the grip compartment. The bladder, being sealed in the grip, is not meant to be inspected by the user. I hope that the bladder will maintain its flexibility and re-inflate properly over many cycles of deflation and inflation. I also hope that any water and salt deposits inside the compartment does not interfere with its operation. It's unclear what the proper maintenance procedure is and how durable the bladder system is over the long term.

Other features and issues:

The loop on the case for the hand strap is too small and is partially covered by the grip. It's really hard to thread the strap without opening up the grip. A second loop for a lanyard would be nice for secondary tether to further lessen the risk of losing an expensive phone.

title: Great way to get stereophile hi-fi music from your Home Theater system
text:
I have a Denon AVR X-3300w HT Receiver that is just great for home theater. I recently purchased the Parasound 275V2 amp to improve 2 channel sound using the L and R pre-outs from the Denon as input to the Parasound. Then I purchased a pair of ELAC UniFi bookshelf speakers, which are notorious for requiring a lot of 4 ohm power ( in fact the minimum impedance is about 3.4 ohms.) No problem for the Parasound which pumps out 150 clean watts/ch at 4 ohms down to 2 ohms. Match made in heaven. Tip: I increased the source output level of the Denon to the max (+12 dB) so that the Parasound can have all of the input voltage it can use. This was easy since all of my sources use ARC to go through my LG TV, so that I have only one source (TV Audio) going to the Denon. The overall result is very satisfying. Side benefit: The Denon runs hot and the Parasound runs very cool. By offloading the mains to the Parasound, the Denon does not run quite as hot, but I still use a cabinet fan. Now I have ordered the ELAC Uni-Fi Center speaker that the Denon will have to drive.

UPDATE 2/12/2020: I have since replaced the ELAC speakers with Triangle Borea BR03's and the sound is fantastic!

title: NOT compatible with 400 x 200 VESA pattern
text: Installed on LG C9 television and what a complete waste of time.  While the mount will attach to a 400 x 200 VESA pattern, the arm ends up running into itself so the mount will no longer lay flat against the wall... it sticks out about 6-7".  In addition, it also interferes with the vertical angle of the TV so you can't adjust it to tilt up at all so the TV is angled down.  In addition, for this LG, the bottom bracket on the TV covers inputs (ethernet etc) on the TV.  Sanus also doesn't include proper fasteners for this particular line of televisions.  They include one length of M6 fastener (L35) and the TV requires an L15-L20.  I had used Sanus' own compatibility checker on their website to ensure it worked with the TV.  It absolutely doesn't and I would avoid it for this or similar LG TVs and all 400 x 200 VESA mount televisions.  I called Sanus customer service and they informed me their compatibility checker only checks the VESA pattern and nothing else.  They offered to ship an additional bracket that corrects the problem by making it a 400 x 300 + pattern which adds another 3/8" or so to the bracket sticking out from the wall when it is in the fully retracted position (almost 4" total).  Long story short, avoid if you have a 400 x 200 VESA mount TV and especially if you have an LG TV with that pattern.  Also, definitely do not trust the Sanus compatibility checker, it's completely worthless beyond checking the VESA pattern.

title: Fantastic
text:
Background: I spec and integrate the highest resolution LCD’s produced in aerospace defense applications. LCD image performance is measured in hundreds of dimensions and environments. Sony is not a player in that space.

For home, I’ve been SID show and showroom shopping LCD, OLEDs, etc image quality for years. This year, I’m replacing a comparably sized exercise room 1080p LCD set. Sony has always been, to my eye, a superb comparative model and a $100 or so more than other competitors. Is the premium worth it?

This Sony X800H is an eye grabber across the showroom and on close inspection. It’s a phenomenal picture. Sony’s proprietary LCD foundries are unique in the industry. The Sony LCD foundry produces a distinctive LCD that is worth the premium price to the discerning.

Performance-wise, Sony reduced the native refresh rate to 60hz from 120hz last year. That’s quite practical as it will be some years before >60fps cameras are widely available at native 120fps. No matter, the 60hz to 120hz refresh is not discernible to the eye. The X800H imaging software can be seen to take care of latency artifacts at factory default settings … no viewing distance ghosting, inverse ghosting, blur or pulse-width modulation.

There is a comment regarding darkness, edge lighting, and illumination issues. The X800H is both edge and background light as best as I can discern without tearing it apart. It's uniform lighting no matter. Sony has always been the master of the best 'optical black' pixel to enrich the color pixel perception. The X800H is loaded with image quality controls. Image software quality defaults arrived set at factory default. It was perfect out of the box. Don't adjust anything. I rarely futz with default settings. No one should have to. The vast majority of image problems are video source input. Change the channel first and compare the image.

An old school key attribute is viewing angles … how many degrees left/right and horizontal/vertical are necessary to degrade the image. The viewing angles here are excellent. Viewing angles are a peek into the remarkable quality of Sony’s proprietary LCD foundry.

Sony’s software, firmware, Smart integration, and image processors are likewise Sony proprietary. Sony names these features like everyone else. Feature comparisons are mostly apparent in year over year Sony tech evolution.

Of course, the real story is in the final image quality. The X800H is one excellent viewing experience.

Better than advertised. Better than expected. In this size, the X800H is the benchmark, IMHO.

text: When i saw these i wanted to get them right away because they seemed to be the best deal that you can get if you wanted ANC, at least that's what i was after. After i bought them i charged them immediately which is sort of a flaw. Let me explain. It takes longer than desired to charge these things. The best time to charge them is overnight, but the tradeoff between charge time and play time is well worth the wait. I can spend most of my day heavily using this thing with ANC activated and it will last. Even after i am done using it i forget to charge it and when i use it the next day it still has like 50% battery life. Now onto the sound quality. The sound quality has some nice highs, but it leaves some desires for the lows. It still delivers the lows pretty well, but its not as rich as some others i've tested (ex. Skullcandy Crusher Wireless). Next is the main target for this device, ANC. The active noise cancelling to someone who hasnt really experienced it in depth before was amazing. I also heard from other people that it has a faint hiss when ANC is enabled, but it is really faint that your brain tunes it out after about 15 seconds. ANC delivers really well. For example, i played some music at around 50% volume and ANC on and i had my friend basically shout at me and i was only able to barely hear him. Last but not least comfort, another huge roll in wearing over ear headphones. Based on other razer products they have i had some worries about the comfort, but when i got them, they were actually really good. It doesnt clamp on your head, at least not hard so it has a nice feeling and my ears which are pretty much medium fit in the headphones and didnt touch the drivers as most people i heard from reviews have experienced. Overall, for the price the razer opus is honestly really great for the price and i would recommend buying it.

text: I purchased a pair of  AiLi TR16 Battery Capacity Testers after viewing Will Prowse's Youtube video review.  Three models are offered on Amazon by current sampler size: 50A, 100A, 350A.  I selected the middle, 100A sampler for use with two 100AH LiFePO4 batteries, however, I believe this product can be used with any chemistry rechargable battery of comparable size, or less.  It came with a clearly-worded instruction sheet, and application diagrams.  The shunt has adequately-sized terminals, and appears to be high-quality mechanically.  It uses a 5-wire communications cable to relay data to the control module.  Instructions state the cable can be extended by addition of similar wire in-line with the connectors.  I was very impressed with the voltage calibration accuracy, and the two I purchased, agreed exactly, in readings.  I own several types of DC watt-hour meters that only count up.  This instrument is quite different, in that it counts both up and down in terms of amp-hours of battery storage.  Once the user establishes and saves the low and high limits into the control module, the instrument can be used like a gas gauge in a car, to identify how much energy is available in percent ( % ).  I now have been using both purchase AiLi Capacity Testers full time for several weeks now in a solar application, and am very satisfied.

title: Easy enough screen protector at a good price
text:
I just installed the screen protector on my Tesla Model 3. The packaging was good and the protector arrived nice and secure. I liked that it came with with a cleaning cloth, alcohol wipes and dirt sticker remover.

I was initially concerned that the instructions would be difficult to follow as it the directions were mainly meant for Chinese readers. However, it was easy enough to follow the written directions and the pictures included in the guide. Aligning the protector to the screen was a little tricky. It requires holding down the screen with one hand while applying some pressure. You then add three stickers to the back of the screen, fold them over, and apply to the front of the screen protector. This part took a few times to get enough coverage on the front of the screen itself so that it wouldn't just fall out under it's own weight. Once I got this part down, it was easy.

Peeling off the film from the back of the protector that adheres to the screen was easy enough. Some air bubbles were left behind which were easy to remove. Note that some bubbles left behind took a bit more finesse to get out but luckily I didn't have to remove any part of the screen protector to reapply.

The protector looks good. I applied mine a bit too high so you can see the edge of it on the bottom. The one thing that I think would have made this better is if it came with some kind of bumper guard like some iPhone or Android phone protectors come with. This would make the install process much easier.

All in all, it took less than 10 minutes. I have no complaints. I just hope that when the car is baking in the sun and the cabin gets very hot, that the protector has no negative impact on the screen itself.

title: Sounds great and gets the job done
text:
I recently purchased a 2007 BMW X5. Its a very nice luxury vehicle. But as with all Bimmers, its iDrive takes center stage on the console, and is part of the car. Unfortunately streaming bluetooth audio wasnt common yet in 2007. Buying an aftermarket head unit is not an option because of the iDrive. That leaves my only options as paying an extraordinary amount of money to retrofit a newer iDrive, or find an alternative solution. Well, this device is that alternative solution. In the center console of the X5 is a line in audio jack, and a 12 volt plug. Using a 12 volt to USB adapter, I basically shoved all of the cables in the console, and placed the puck just outside it, in a nice placement near the iDrive knob.

I tried it out today. Sound quality is really good. Better than it was using a lightning to audio cable directly plugged in to the aux in. The three buttons, next/last/pause play work perfectly fine. My phone is paired to bluetooth for the phone in the bimmer. I made a phone call not knowing what to expect. It appeared my phone was using the bluetooth off this new device; but as a bonus, I had the call stats up on the idrive since its also connected. This means I can see the inbound caller, use my steering wheel buttons, etc. But I have the high quality audio off this device.

Its not a perfect solution. But at the price, its way better than my alternatives. It doesnt automatically kick off the last played song when I turn on the car (the 12volt source is switched, which is what you want). But its not too bad, because the iDrive will not default back to aux in anyways. So no matter what, I have to start the car, then switch over. At that point, I can click play on the puck, and off it goes. But when I exit the vehicle, the phone stops playing, which it wont do if its plugged in directly to the lightning (itll play until you unplug the lightning cable).

The only other alternative that would work is an aftermarket android unit that replaces the original iDrive panel. It can still do the idrive functions, but layers in all android apps. That of course can do bluetooth streaming. But even that is $500. This device was my last stop before going that route. It appears I have a satisfactory solution, so I will probably leave it as is.

title: Excellent - considering its size and cost
text:
It is amazing how in recent years the price of digital projectors has gone down and the availability has gone way up. Of course there are a wide variety of projectors on the market from the very high end used in professional military training costing tens of thousands, down to the consumer level.

This Luby is on the far consumer end of the scale and for that it is pretty good. It is important to evaluate it against the intended use - this is not for business meetings or even serious movie buff viewing. Rather, it is a small projector priced about the same as a pair of prescription reading glasses. Think of it as more like a toy, something you would set up for a slumber party of 10 year olds who are not going to be too critical.

In these terms it has adequate resolution and brightness for uncritical viewing. I ran it from the HDMI output of my computer, and it was easy to set up and focus. The brightness is only sufficient if viewed in a dark room. There is a remote and also the box contained a white cloth "bedsheet" to act as a quickly mounted screen.

This projector works by imaging a high brightness LCD mini display. Although it claims to be HD compatible, it seems to mean this is downsampled to a resolution around SVGA, 800X600 max. This can not be expected to yield the same image quality as a large flat panel TV. It has a mechanical keystone adjustment in case you can't point it straight to the screen.

A fun product, provided you understand the limitations and don't expect too much. If you are more serious about video, you can go up even a little in price and find better and better quality. There are literally hundreds of models at every cost and performance point, topping out at digital projectors for theaters. This almost-toy version is not in the sweet spot, you need to spend more, on the order of $500-800 to get good image quality.

title: Caveat Emptor
text:
I am now using my third Archgon Premium Aluminum External USB 3.0 UHD Blu-ray Writer Super Driver For Apple-MacBook (hereafter, APED) in about as many years. The first, used gently and regularly though not constantly, lasted about two years before simple DVDs began freezing or skipping on me. The second wheezed along not longer than about eight months, after which I received from Amazon an 80% refund after the product's return. I've now used #3 for about three months. So far, so good. I don't anticipate durability.

With such a checkered history of performance, why do I keep using the same product? First, I can't afford anything more expensive, which might or might not perform more dependably. Second, techno-geeks whom I trust have told me that they know of no product of comparable price that is better or more reliable. *Sigh.*

To answer some basic questions: 1. Yes, this product is simple to use, while it's young and useable: simply plug it, with or without its supplemental cable, into your Mac's USB port(s). 2. It is purportedly equipped to play DVDs or Blu-Ray discs from Regions 1–6. I have only made one, brief attempt with a Region 2 (U.K.) disc, with indifferent results. 3. Given its seeming fragility and short life expectancy, handle it with care. Keep it in its sturdy, zippered plastic case when not in use. I also place a saucer of milk out for it before retiring, in an attempt to keep it pacified. 4. Purchase a supplemental warranty for the product, when the manufacturer's own runs out. If my experience is typical, you'll almost certainly need it.

A closing lament: Had not Apple decided that (a) laptops must be designed as slender as onion-skin and (b) an entire nation, or world, of users would immediately quit their collected CDs, DVDs, and Blu-rays for Bluetooth streaming, we'd still have built-in disc players on our computers—and no need at all for finicky products like this.

UPDATE 32 DAYS LATER: That third Archgon I owned just croaked on me, after only four months of sporadic use (about one hour every two or three days). Last Tuesday, it simply stopped working when I tried to play a CD. I treat machinery with care: the unit was never dropped or mishandled in any way. It simply died after 120 days of intermittent use. I have now dropped my three-star rating to one star. For whatever reason—cheap materials or incompetent manufacture—I have found this to be an inferior product that I cannot recommend. I take no pleasure in this review, but I now have fewer saucers of spoiled milk.

SECOND UPDATE 84 DAYS LATER: In the interest of accuracy and fairness to Archgon, whose employees must put bread on the table like the rest of us, my third disc drive, which died on me 52 days ago, has been resuscitated by the IT wizards where I work. Last night I played both a CD and DVD with it. I haven't yet attempted one of my Blu-rays, because there's no point in pushing my luck. This is turning into a boring technological soap opera. Every day brings a new surprise and a little suspense: will the machine work this morning? For that unreliability I'll leave my rating at one star, placate the little gizmo with another saucer of milk, maybe laced with with bourbon. Strike that. The gizmo gets the milk. I'll take the booze.

FINAL UPDATE: One year and nearly two months after purchase, this product finally died on me. One evening I was using it to watch a DVD. I paused play, to paddle into the kitchen for my saucer of milk. When I returned, I could not coax the machine, never disconnected, into playing. It never again played another DVD. It was able to handle CDs, but, for its steep price, that was not sufficient. As for Blu-rays, forget it. I had long since given up on that capability.

I want to be very clear to anyone who reads this review and is trying to decide on a purchase.

1. This was my THIRD Archgon external disc player in as many years. I was willing to give the manufacturer full benefit of doubt and, during that period, was informed by some acquaintances that it was probably the best equipment I could hope for. All of these machines, all identical to the model under review, died within the space of a year, give or take.

2. Apart from one or two attempts with a Blu-ray disc, I never attempted any maneuver fancier than (a) playing a CD on this unit, through my laptop, or (b) playing a standard DVD in the same way.

3. I never abused any of these units. After use, or attempted use, all were safely stored in the enclosed zippered boxers that came with the unit. No unit was ever dropped, jostled, submerged in water or dumped in hydrochloric acid. All simply rested on my desk, without disturbance.

4. I can speculate about causes for my problem but can prove none. It may be that this unit is simply friendlier for PCs than for Macs. That theory is supported by the oddly designed cables that accompanied the unit. If that conjecture has basis in fact, then the manufacturer should transparently warn customers that its product is not dependably compatible with Apple/Mac. The plug-in cable connections from disc drive to laptop may have eroded across time—though, again, I was very gentle in plugging, never forcing things. One tech specialist I spoke with today hypothesized that the built-in laser for playing DVDs may simply have died: not once, but three times on three identical units. Who knows? Who cares?

I gave Archgon every chance to make good. Three times in three years it failed me. I have purchased my last Archgon product. I did purchase a warranty on the unit but by now am so frustrated that I'll waste no more time, simply eat all the money I wasted, and start fresh, moving in a different direction that satisfies needs and wants.

Good luck to you.

title: Very Good Speeds and Easy Setup
text:
I ordered this product which I thought was economical to do an upgrade on my network. Previously I had a Linksys E4200 V1 with two Rackspace Wi-Fi extenders (one with an ethernet port) and the other without. This provided good coverage except that the speed was unstable. With that configuration I had separate SSID for the 2.4GHZ and the 5.0GHZ Band as the extenders would take the name of the base router and add EXT or 5GHZ_EXT to denote the different frequencies. So, to sum it up, I had four SSIDs but they all used the same passwords. Because of this I had to change SSIDs on some of my devices depending on where I was in the house.
To begin this package arrived within 48hrs after purchase which was awesome so I didn’t have to waste much time before I could setup. Set-up was a breeze which took me about 35 minutes or so from start to finish (15 to actually do the setup and the other 15-20 minutes to redo my wires for the switch and the other wired devices I have). My house is two floors with almost 3800 sq feet (garage and back lanai included) and I got almost full ISP speeds from the garage, the back porch. I even got almost 60 Mbps from the mailbox out on the street. See the comparison in the pictures.

PROS:
Easy to set up
Package and item were light weight and did not take up a lot of space
Gigabit ethernet port on the main point
Apply was user friendly and easy to operate
One SSID for the entire house which was a welcome difference to my previous configuration
The network and frequencies seem stable and the speeds exceeded or was close to my ISP 100Mbps speeds and I only had 24 of the many devices at home connected and in use.

CONS:
I would prefer to have the option to choose whether to connect to the 5GHZ or 2.4GHZ. Seems the system automatically select the frequency. But not a big issue as the speeds is good.
Only one gigabit ethernet port on the main point (easily corrected with an inexpensive gigabit 8 port switch)
Can only access the system through the phone app. NOT able to access through web interface.
The biggest downside from my perspective is that it only had Mixed WPA/WPA2-PSK Security. The WPA2 is good but PSK is older (PSK) TKIP encryption which is not as secure and recommended for use if you have older that can’t connect to a WPA2-PSK (AES) network. Would be better if it had the WPA2-PSK (AES) or at least have that as an option.

title: Reception not even 25 miles, then amp dies - Total GARBAGE!
text:
I live on a ridge with DIRECT line of sight to THREE different mountain top TV transmitter locations less than 25 miles away, it only gets signal from ONE of them, and poorly at that, without the booster it's totally useless. 130 miles? LMAO, perhaps theoretically on paper or in a lab environment not in real life.

The thin thread of a likely unshielded wire is a joke, no doubt there is much signal loss as a result, per the package the piece of plastic sheet only gains you 5dB, with the signal booster you get a total of 25dB. Basic math - no signal amplified by however many times you want is still ZERO!!!

Setting it up is an impossible pain in the you know where, even if you return it to exactly the same place by way of a tape and paper clip hanger, it's won't get the same reception, so if you happen to find someplace it works well enough don't move it OR the wire, seems the placement of the wire has something if not everything to do with actually getting the signal.

I decided to compare it to an ancient set rabbit ears and with or without the booster the old antenna does far better, got all channels ... until the booster died a few weeks later. As I recall this piece of junk had a one year warranty but I don't see any way to contact the vendor so I guess I'm stuck having wasted my money since the POS booster lasted long enough to exceed the return date.

title: For the price, this is well worth it
text:
For the price, this projector is fantastic. Extremely easy set up, great picture and sound (if you’re not looking for heavy bass and surround sound). This isn’t a paid or discounted review by any means. I have been hesitant about dropping a lot of $$ on a projector on amazon for my first projector, without knowing what I’m in for. That said, the positive reviews have been solid enough to actually verify them.
I’m lucky enough to have a rented apartment that has a roof deck with enough space and a large wall that is almost begging for a projector to project onto. My landlord said that he has used the deck and wall to push movies on to it but I have been concerned about how much a projector would cost without being embarrassed about having friends over to watch a movie that looks like it was streamed from a potato with a heavy price tag.
This projector has been awesome and was discounted to 120 something and change. It was delivered a day early, took 30 mins to set up (my own camera tripod, laptop and positioning set up) and has been great.

Downside is, if you’re looking for a projector that can stream (AirPlay) media like YouTube, Netflix or anything else of that nature from your phone or mobile device.. it will not do that (copyright is a real engraved bitch with this). If you have an HDMI cable, you are set.

It’s literally plug in and play with that. The HDMI cable and power plug isn’t super long so an extension cord is recommended if you want space to set the projector up without having your head shading the screen.

It has solid sound, picture and has been flawless watching on a max dimension of 200” on the wall I have. It has great adjustments for focus and angle (providing you have a cheap tripod to have it at the angle you want) as well as sound quality.

Definitely worth the spend on a large space. My photo has lights on in the background and with the lights off, looks even better. I would recommend this projector for the price and quality, hands down.

Saying that, it has been 3 hours and I’m into my second movie. I will be back if I have any issues. If you don’t hear from me, this positive review will stand.

title: My new favorite tablet
text: I wanted to try it out for a while before leaving a review. My experience with other tablets are a Bamboo I had for a few years and an Intuos used at school. I struggle with tendonitis and some other hand issues (even after studying proper grips and techniques, sometimes too much work is just too much work) and using this tablet feels a lot more natural to me than the others I've used. The Huion pen has a better feeling weight distribution compared to the Bamboo pen, but it doesn't have the extra top button which some like to use as an eraser, in case that is important to you-I preferred to keyboard shortcut and use the tip anyway so I personally don't miss it- and it is not bulky like the standard Intuos pen. We were never provided with a slim pen option at school so I can't compare it with that. After the bottom half of my Bamboo quit registering, I thought it might not hurt to try something new. Any differing levels of pressure sensitivity haven't exactly been noticeable as I go about my work, but I can't speak for others who may use different techniques. The tablet is high quality and I'm kind of surprised that there's not really anything about the other tablets I miss compared to this one. The programs I use it with are photoshop(various versions), clip studio paint, nekosuke, blender(mainly to make tileable textures & other model painting- I haven't really done sculpting in a while, so not sure about that yet), and gimp. I ordered one for my sister too and she is doing a bunch of fun traditional/digital mixed media illustration with it as well.

title: There are better options out there
text:
I use this monitor as a second screen for my laptop. I mostly use it for email, text editing, that sort of thing. The picture quality is fine for that. However, I have three major problems, two of which are with the brightness:
1. The monitor doesn't automatically set the brightness based on ambient light and, when you change it manually, it doesn't remember your setting when you change it. That means you have to reset it every time you turn it on.
2. I can no longer change the brightness at all. The way you do it is with a dual-purpose scroll-and-select knob on the side of the unit. I can bring up the menu but can no longer select and change the brightness setting. The problem started happening two weeks after the last day to return the unit to Amazon. Very annoying.
3. All apps do not display and operate correctly. I use a browser app called Grammarly. It highlights text and provides suggestions for how to improve it. You cannot select the suggestion or click on the highlights using this monitor. If you move the browser window to the main laptop display, everything works correctly. It looks like there is a problem with the display driver.
I would return the item if I could. I was previously using an ASUS MB169b. I dropped and broke it. I had hoped to get something brighter, which this display was until the ability to change the brightness broke. I should probably have just gotten the ASUS again.
[Update] Resetting the display resolved the problem with not being able to change the brightness. As well, a Lepow engineer told me you can save the brightness setting, but only if you are using HDMI with an external power supply. If you are using USB-C, as I am, you cannot save the setting. This is very, very annoying. Every time the PC puts the screen to sleep the Lepow monitor forgets the setting. I got this monitor so everything can be powered by the PC (no external power connector required.) Very disappointing.

title: Functional, but frustrating and disappointing.
text:
Update 2019-08-20: I've gotten the radio working now, after discovering another problem with the documentation I found with the radio and the downloaded information. Two methods, "manual" and "software" are presented for setting the radio's frequency range, and they're presented as if they're "options" for configuring it. Turns out, they're not; they apparently address separate issues in the radio and are BOTH required. You can use the software to configure the VHF range to 136-174 MHz, and you can then read the setting and confirm that the radio has accepted it, but it will STILL overwrite any frequency you program or key in that's outside of 150-160MHz on VHF (a similar limit exists for UHF frequencies). To get around this, you must also do the "manual" process, holding down the first two soft keys while connecting power to the radio. No user feedback is given during this process, no confirmation message -- just do it, then turn the radio on.

So, having gotten the radio to work I've now tested it, and found it putting out only about 39 watts at high power. The SWR I got was 1.5, so I may want to tune my antenna a bit and see if that helps.

My original review follows.

~~~~
Turns out, this radio has been a miserable experience so far. I'm somewhat accustomed to poorly-written CPS software and confusing user interfaces, uninformative and actually misleading documentation, etc. on Chinese import radios. But this radio has taken these frustrations to a new level. And what I'm left with is a radio that silently accepts frequency settings in the amateur 2-meter range, but silently rewrites them internally to 150.0 Mhz. Any frequencies I've set that were above that (my company has 2 licensed frequencies that I've programmed), including UHF, work as expected. All of my local ham repeater frequencies are rewritten however, with no messages from the radio or the programming software that this is happening. Manually tune a channel's frequency directly on the radio itself to 147.5? Ok, no error, it's 150.0.

Apparently this is a common problem, and there are a number of conversations online about it, discussing various ways to use the "Factory" software to set the radio's frequency ranges. None of it works.

Using the Factory software according to the written instructions in the box (primary range as VHF, range B as UHF) makes the radio incompatible with the programming software; they're supposed to be vice-versa, UHF first. (No option exists in the CPS for VHF first, and if it doesn't match then the CPS will refuse to write to the radio.)

But even specifying the full VHF range, 136-174, gets reinterpreted by the radio as 150-160 after the Factory software finishes writing to it, and it won't accept any frequency below 150 from that point on.

I'm going to keep trying for a little while longer, and I'll update this review if I resolve the problem or decide to send it back.

title: Speed Tested: Not Gigabit. Not worth your money
text:
SPEED TESTED:
To get Gigabit speeds speed tests should be close to 1000 Mbps (-100 for overhead on the line). I had an old Cat 5 cable that was giving me 885 Mbps, but wasn't shielded and thought, hey maybe I can get ready for 10Gbps! on my network! So I got this Cat 7 cable.

Wrong move. Speed tests were giving me 95 Mbps- on the same port as the grey cable. So I decided to show 2 pictures side by side showing my OLD unshielded cable going faster than the new shielded Cat 7 cable.

RESPONSE FROM SELLER:
I asked the seller about this and they gave the general response:
Your speeds will vary depending on your router, your network, your ISP, etc etc.

POSITIVE NOTE:
-Amazon made the return super easy. QR code was scanned by UPS at their store and they took care of it all.
-The shielding on the cable was pretty nice and seemed like a sturdy cable! Way better than my old cable. But I like my cables for what's on the inside, not their appearance.

title: Worth the higher price. Much better than leather or silicone bands.
text:
I love this watch band and have already ordered another. It’s not an exact match to pinkish gold of the Fitbit but close enough for me.
Why 5 stars?
1. Sleep comfort: I purchased the Fitbit Charge 3 specifically to monitor sleep patterns so sleep comfort was important to me. I don’t even notice it during sleep whereas with the silicone and leather bands I was constantly adjusting them during the night.
2. Looks. It looks sleek and classy. I found that I’m not into matching my watch band with my clothing or even mood. I want a band that will go with anything.
3. Clasp. The clasp is easy to use. Two large buttons on either side of the clasp allow easy in and off. I have rhuematoid arthritis so this is important.
4. Daily Comfort. I also have fibromyalgia so comfort is key. It can’t be too tight or rough. This band is lightweight and the individual links are smooth. I hardly notice the watch is on my arm. It also doesn’t make my skin sweat underneath it as the silicone and leather bands did.
5. Links. I like linked watch bands over a leather or silicone band. Previously I’d worn a linked bracelet type watch for over 30 years.
6. Durability. I’ve only been wearing a it for a few weeks so time will tell. But in this time I’ve cooked, cleaned, played with grandkids and multiple big dogs and generally stressed it in daily use to the point where I have normal scratches on the clasp. So I have high hopes for long term durability.

There are a lot of power strips out there with USB ports, but this device as a USB-C USB-PD port which allows you to power higher power devices. It's only 30 W so it won't charge your Laptop, probably (there aren't devices in this price range that will) but it is useful for an assortment of devices, like cameras, that need more power than a normal USB port provides.

I'm not a fan of the power button. It's no deal killer, but it's easy to not realize the device has accidentally turned of. IN a new version of would love to see them remove the power button, and maybe add one more outlet (adding 2 USB-C ports is far harder than you imagine).

title: Excellent Barlow
text:
To my surprise, this barlow lens is very good. I was not expecting the build and lens quality to as good as it is for the price. What really surprised me is the optics. Very clear and has very little if any reduction in light transmission to the eyepiece, which I did not expect for such an inexpensive barlow. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a good quality barlow without spending a lot.

UPDATE: I just wanted to add an update on some testing and comparison I performed with this Barlow lens and a GSO Shorty Barlow. First, you will notice that SVBONY has reduced the diameter of the barlow element, compared to the GSO Shorty. The reason for this is to allow full insertion of the lens assembly into a scope with a diagonal eyepiece socket. That is a good thing, as it prevents the barlow lens from contacting the internal diagonal mirror and damaging it. With the GSO, the barlow cannot be inserted the entire way to the housing stop, since it will contact or damage the diagonal mirror. I thought that this diameter reduction may also reduce the light transmission, compared to the GSO, but in my testing that was not the case. I found the SVBONY optics to be a little brighter and clearer than the GSO. My only conclusion is because this particular SVBONY 3x barlow has a THREE element vs the two element in the GSO shorty. The only plus I have found with the GSO over the SVBONY, is the ability to remove the barlow element and thread it onto the eyepiece. That gives an option to reduce the magnification from a 3x to 2.5x, something you cannot do with the SVBONY. For me, that is not an issue and I would still recommend the SVBONY over the GSO brand, due to its better quality element and better fit into any scope.

title: Nice Clock with lots of fun Options
text:
Disclosure: I was given this product for the purposes of reviewing.

This little clock is pretty neat. I have been using it for a couple weeks now. I usually use my phone as an alarm clock and it took a little getting use to, to switch to an actual alarm clock. This one is not too large with some really neat features that make it a cool find.

What I liked:
It has both an alarm clock and a "sleep aid" so its like the opposite of an alarm, music set to a certain time to start in order to start preparing you to fall asleep. I didn't use that function a lot but found it pretty cool. It had pretty decent speakers installed at first glance, the tones, tunes and noises come out nice and clear loud. The light feature, especially being touch controlled is pretty neat as well. It has a couple settings for the brightness of the clock numbers which turned out to be really nice. Another reason I don't use digital clocks is the GLARING light in the middle of the night if you happen to wake up. This was nice as when it is set on its lowest setting it doesn't seem to bright in the pitch dark. The wake up feature starting a light and getting brighter and brighter until the time hits and the alarm starts is a good idea as well, slowly prepping your body to wake up. It also has lots of fun noise and music options as well.

What I wasn't too keen on;
First and foremost, these guys need to hire a native English speaker to translate their manual. It was difficult to read. I could puzzle out what they meant but it definitely was noticeable. Following on that, I found some of the more advanced options a little difficult to set up due to lack of proper instructions. I think if they expanded their manual and had a better translation of it, this would be vastly improved. A small thing too, the increase speed of the light getting brighter and the alarm sound getting louder seemed to happen too quickly. If they made that more gradual I think it would be a lot better.

All in all though, I like this alarm clock and will likely be gifting it to one of my school attending children to use for getting up for school. For the price, I think this is a pretty decent product and recommend it to anyone.

title: Much prefer the old version - here's why
text:
I am a fan of Noopel alarms - far superior to my previously purchased Sabres & GEs.

Just purchased this "new" version and am returning to rebuy another set of the "old" version (black base). The new version Noopel has a third switch position for "low" - whereas the "old" version was a simple 2 position switch - up for on & down for off = no mistakes.

The Sabres, GEs and other brands also have 3 position switches with "off" in the middle. Meaning you have to guess and check to see if you switched to "off" versus low. Since the switch is TINY and facing to the side where you can't see the switch position label - I found the 3 position style mistake prone.

The new Noopel is different from my Sabres & GEs whereas they both employed a "chime" as 2nd alert setting while Noople has a high & low, The high remains great, it gets your attention far better than my Sabres or GEs. But the "low" setting is without value as being so low as to be nearly useless.

Another fact to note if you are shopping - my old version Noopels gave me MUCH better battery life than Sabre or GE. Also Noopel only requires 3 LR44s rather than 4 with my others. Simpler because the LR44s are small, round, and hard to handle with guy hands often ending up rolling on the floor. Saves hassle.

So I am rebuying the "old" version & sending back the "new". Either are better than Sabre or GE IMO.

title: Problematic Installation
text:
Once it is on, the product cuts glare and the touch screen works fine. There are several issues however.
1. The size is so precise that if you are not perfectly lined up, the coverage is off.
2. They send you two screens, but only the sticky tabs to attach one.
3. The sticky dust cleaner they send for a 17" screen is smaller then the one I get for doing my phone.
4. After following their instructions, I went to peel off the outer layer (tab 2) as per the instructions. This peeled off the the screen, at which point I got more air bubbles (after I had gotten them all out) and new dust under it (after I had cleared all of that). So now I have air bubbles that I can't get rid off, and a couple of dust specs that are stuck to the inside of the glare screen (not the computer screen) so they are almost impossible to get rid off.

Overall, while the performance is good as in terms of still have a clear crisp screen with no glare, the exacting requirement to line this up perfectly, the sparsity of the application accessories, and the problems with peeling off the outer layer make this a problematic product.

title: Fits Apple Smart Keyboard but no slot for Pencil adapter
text:
This is a really good case, but it had one flaw that was almost a deal breaker for me and I originally planned on returning it. I tend to lose small objects and I really wanted a case to store the small charging adapter that comes with the 1st gen Apple Pencil. This case doesn't have a slot. The pictures look like there's a spot to hold it, but no, the space is to allow you to press the volume buttons on the side, which actually works very well. But, without the storage slot, I was ready to return the case.

But! I decided to keep the case. As you can see from my pictures, my case has now been gently loved and is well-traveled. The biggest benefit of this case is that I can attach and store my Apple Smart Keyboard together with the case. This feature is practically not available in any other case. In almost every other book-style or wallet-style cases, the adapters to connect the Smart Keyboard is covered and you have to remove the whole cover to connect your keyboard. In this case, there's a large side opening that exposes the connectors for the Apple Smart Keyboard. This feature allows you store your keyboard inside your case all the time and remove it easily whenever you don't need the keyboard.

I've attached two pictures of the case with the Smart Keyboard installed. As you can see, it fits snuggly. The magnetic clasp works really nicely when you want to close and put away your iPad and also snaps behind the iPad so it's not covering your screen.

Overall, it's a great case. I wish for 2 things: (1) there was a slot to store the adapter and (2) it came in just plain matte black for a more conservative look. Aside from that, I still recommend the case.

Oh, P.S. the ability to turn the iPad portrait mode for FaceTime calls or other applications is nice. However, I don't use it a lot. Others my find this more valuable.

title: Good but could be great
text:
This is sturdy and the only single mount 32" triple monitor stand I could find.

About monitor stands:
It is important to note that there are several different monitor stand types that provide different functionality. One needs to consider if their monitors will stay in place once mounted or need to be moved around. I was wanting a single mounting point drilled through my desk to minimize desk clutter and ensure stability and this stand fulfils that need. I didn't want a desk clamp as I figured that wouldn't work very well with 45lbs. of monitor weight and I didn't want a foot stand as that would have taken up a loot of space between my monitor and my keyboard.

The one consideration I had not decided on until setting this up and trying it out was wether I would wanted all my monitors mounted flat in a straight line or to have the side monitor angle in like a "v" shape. In the course of setting these up I didn't know if I would be able to angle my side monitors in to my satisfaction or not. What I discovered is that the arms on the stand are very long and very adjustable from an angle in perspective. I did see other reviewers were not happy with the arm length as they interfere with the wall behind the monitor when using their monitors. I don't have that problem with 32" monitors. The arms do not get in the way of my back wall. I call this out because for me the extra long arms is a good thing, but for someone with smaller monitors the arms would have to be bent and protrude backward limiting how close one's desk can be to the wall. Bottom line if you have 3 - 32" monitors this may work for you as it does for me.

The good:
Sturdy, reasonable price, can hold 3 x 32" monitors and slant inward.

The bad:
Adjustability has some issues. For my setup I was unable to align monitor heights. I have the side mounts up as high as they can go, the center mount as low as it will go, and I still have over an inch of alignment differential between the center monitor and the sides.
Additionally, I had to tighten the nuts on the side mounts very tight in order to keep the monitors from tilting forward once set in position. I was surprised by the amount of torque required to prevent them from continuing to slide down. I will be replacing the arm riser bolt with a longer bolt and nut and see if I can get an equal rise from my side monitors.

title: Important Update - Annoying Buzzing Sound Eliminated
text:
I need to begin by noting that for the last couple of years I have been spoiled by mostly watching on a 55” OLED I purchased for my bedroom and I have to note that it is unfair in my mind to base a projector against an OLED screen. Although to black levels on the projector are as good or better than any I have used it could not possibly compare to the OLED screen I had become so accustomed to. Otherwise I am impressed by this units performance given its price level. I also cannot compare it to the new laser projectors which are far above the price of this projector. I own a large number of projectors or er the last 15 years and although some of the HD/3D units are very close to the picture quality of this one they all fall a bit short. What they do not have is bluetooth, which I was happy to see is included in this one. After spending several days watching about thirty movies and barring myself from watching my OLED screen I can say this far exceeds my expectations. I have enjoyed it so much that I began to use my home theater more and have begun to upgrade my sound system. If you are considering a first time projector at this price point then I do recommend this projector. If you are looking to upgrade to 4K but are not able to shell out at least two or three times as much money for a laser projector then I also recommend this unit.

Update: After using for a few months it started making a loud buzzing noise whenever an image is projected. When it goes to no image it stops so its not the fan. Very annoying.

Update 2: After using this wonderful 4K projector for over a year I have experienced just one problem, that until just recently I had no idea what was causing it. The problem was a very loud and annoying sound from the unit, especially when projecting bright scenes. The sound is difficult to describe in words and the best I can do is that of n electronic buzzing. If you are experiencing the same thing you will know what I mean. The other day I just got so fed up with it I decided to try again to see if I can do anything to stop it short of opening the unit up and playing around with something I am no way qualified to do. I decided to just change settings to see if anything made a difference. After about half an hour of switching settings off and on I finally hit pay-dirt. I have always preferred the “Dynamic Mode” setting for color mode. I changed it to Cinema Mode and played a movie that I had just experienced the annoying sound and to my surprise it was gone. It turns out that the sound is evident only when in the Dynamic color mode. Although I prefer that color mode the trade off in eliminating the noise is worth it. I hope no one else has experienced this problem but if so I suggest this as a fix.

title: Alexa not built-in; hands-free functions don't work I'm sending this back
text:
I am extremely disappointed with this TV. The Amazon listing specifically says "Alexa built in" THIS IS A LIE

The TV must download the Alexa app to enable it, but it does not even add the correct skills and for some reason it cannot even control the most basic functions without a lot of work.

It took me three days to figure out I needed to add a more advanced skill to Alexa to change the channel but even still it cannot control the TV. Unlike the firestick I'd been using I cannot tell is something like "Murder She Wrote" or 'James Bond" and have it show me that show in Amazon Video. Instead it is DUMB saying "I cannot find that" or it does not open a James bond movie it goes to wikipedia or whatvever and gives me description of James Bond by Ian Fleming. Telling it "show me james bond on prime video" give me "I cannot find a skill to do that" or something else like that.

If I had a penny for every time Alexa on this TV said "I cannot do that" " I cannot find that" or "hmmmm, I don't know that" or instead of doing what it's supposed to do namely open the program or app it does something fully different I'd be rich.

The other complaint is that Echo Dot and Alexa app are blind to the TV. The Echo Dot initially malfuctioned and kept shutting itself off when I tried to control the TV. It would just go unresponsive for some reason. Amazon support was CLUELESS and kept bouncing me from one tech to another. Two and a half hours of useless tech support and I cut them off and went to bed in disgust. 4 of the techs came into the conversation blindly asking if the issue was regarding my FireTV stick instead of reading the conversation.

*That is ANOTHER peeve of mine* Amazon support was useless which in the past has not always been the case but they could not help me make Alexa on my phone control the TV. One had me de-register it and I had to restart nearly all my devices including modem, router, phone, echo dot, and TV to get to show up again.
Logging out and in about 20 times. I was also told they would RMA the Echo Dot for the issue of it shutting off. I used the factory reset on it and it works just fine. So they could not figure out what do just send it back.
I might just send the Echo back alright *for REFUND* but that's another review.

The remote of the TV has a Netflix button an Amazon button and a voice remote button. BUT the voice remote button IS NOT Alexa it's Google Assistant instead. It likewise is sketchy to control other than most basic functions of the TV.

So in essense there is no hands free option to control this TV. The remote acts like the Wii remote or a mouse with a pointer that some may like. I find it clunky and useless since in something like Amazon IT DOES NOT SELECT THE PROGRAMS. I still have to use the arrows. So again something that doesn't work.

Another thing the App selection absolutly stinks. 1/3 of the apps in the LG store are inexplicably oriented toward "the Indian subcontinent" as per their very description. Even though I'm in USA.

Two apps I used on the firestick Tubi and PlutoTV are inexplicably non-existent on the LG store and cannot be downloaded. As others have said major network apps (CBS, NBC, FOX), are not available for some reason too.

The TV itself has a good picture and was easy to hookup and setup except for the above.

LG is at least more than half the blame here.
Their ThinQ app is poorly written and when initially setup with Alexa (Alexa insists you install LG's app when you go to setup an LG TV in the Alexa app) it doesn't install or offer the correct skills. It installs ONLY the basic skill. But Alexa still doesn't use them so it's useless.

There are plenty of other brands that should actually work. I am tech savvy. I can work out most computer problems in good time but this is just annoying.

I'll just keep what I had; a working Hisense 40" TV from 2013 if I don't find something else I like.

That said I'm going to be sending this frustrating piece of junk back for refund.
