title: Good enough for the price range, some odd limitations
text:
I did professional audio recording for years, both studio and location recording. I've used many mics, typically professional equipment.

This is a relatively inexpensive mic intended for direct input to a computer, tablet, etc., via USB-A (if you just have USB-C ports you'll need an adapter). The mic is made to look like a professional broadcast mic, but it certainly isn't. However it's actually not bad if you understand its limitations.

The mic comes with a detailed spec page in the not-quite-fluent English user's manual, a tiny book in tiny type. The frequency response shows big rolloff in frequencies under about 150Hz and then flat as a ruler up to about 15,000 Hz. Frankly this is hard to believe. The curve is just too flat. But I don't have any of my own measurements to compare.

The sensitivity is good, about what you'd expect. The impedance is close to 600 ohms, which is ideal. The signal to noise ratio is rather poor, but it's not a thousand dollar mic, either. Maximum input is more than you should ever encounter with proper use.

There is a tripod mount that only works in a fully spread position, taking up a fair amount of desk space. There is no other mounting system, a major versatility drawback. You can't mount this on a mic stand and it would even be hard to use with a spring clip.

There is an off-on-volume control, the latter of which is not seen in pro equipment, for a good reason. Please, leave it all the way up and don't touch it. Control gain at the recording end (your computer) and do things the right way.

It's an electret condenser, a design that's been used for decades to get reasonable sound at a reasonable price. It runs from the 5V DC you get from your USB port, and the current demands are minimal.

BUT ... how does it sound? It's good for voice when used reasonably close-up, at perhaps 1-2 foot distance maximum. It is decidedly not for recording musical instruments which have any appreciable low range. No acoustic guitar, certainly no cello, and I wouldn't use it for a violin either. Some wind instruments like a flute might be okay (I didn't try that).

Really, this is good for podcasting, online conferencing, and similar voice applications. Actually very good. Do experiment with placement and angle. It is a cardiod pattern which means it's most sensitive in the direction in which you point it. This is not something to place in the middle of a conference table and expect to pick everyone up more or less uniformly. (For that find an omnidirectional mic.)

So bottom line, it's certainly not "professional" quality as the advertising claims. It's a decent, maybe even above average electret mic good for vocal use. It is a bit noisy but with decent signal input (not too low, in other words) that won't be a problem. Finally, the price is pretty good. Yes, you can get cheaper USB mics but they will be way worse.

So I go four stars for overall quality for the price.

title: Do Not Buy Into The Brand Name Hype - This Device Is Not For Powerusers
text:
tl;dr: This product is for 60+ year old grandparents who want to digitize some old home movies and refuse to undergo cataract surgery, who also have horror flashbacks to 'those **** kids filling up their 20GB hard drives by installing 'The Sims' expansion packs and need the file sizes to be as small and compressed as possible. If you require anything more technical or higher quality than that. Look elsewhere!!
Note regarding other reviews: The latest version of the software appears to have enabled automatic de-interlacing, which may not have been present in previous versions resulting in the motion artifacts many people have discussed. I have had none such artifacts, and in truth their de-interlace method appears to be very good. Like YADIF time based good. So no complaints there. Audio/Video sync is still atrocious. Highly variable over the course of a 2 hour capture. Average finding is audio becomes 0.4 seconds ahead of the video stream immediately. But infuriatingly this can change at any movement and I've had swings as high as a full second de-sync BEHIND the video stream, and then 30 minutes later it swings 0.20 seconds ahead of the video stream. I have to spend about 15 minutes re-syncing all the audio and finding where it starts to get off track and then re-encode the whole thing in Vegas.
Detailed analysis:
Now I purchased this (thank goodness used at 1/3 the MSRP) to digitize about 100 hours of Hi8 video. I have an old Pcie x1 Hauppauge capture card that's about 12 years old and only supports RFU Coax input, so I decided to get some newer tech. I've been a fan of the parent company Corsair for many years, but I was wary of the bought out 'Elgato' because it reeked of l33t gamer marketing within the streaming world. Much like the Blue Yeti microphone, I feared it was garbage tech that had been highly polished and heavily marketed to fake acclaim. This product is outrageously locked down. I was ONLY able to get the proprietary Elgato capture software to recognize both the audio and video streams simultaneously. Attempting to use this device with Sony Vegas, Pinnacle Capture, OBS and EVEN VirtualDub all yielded either video alone, audio alone or neither. Infuriating. So I succumb to installing the latest version of Elgato Video Capture. Now if you thought the hardware was locked down, this software puts the icing on the cake. Absolutely no settings in regards to capture resolution, file container, de-interlacing (or leaving interlaced), detelecine and most egregiously BITRATE. Absolutely no option to adjust above the native capture rate of 2Mbps video and 218Kbps AAC audio. I even recently put a request on Stackflow to try and adjust the XML or DLL files to allow for higher encoding capture rate. Please Elgato/Corsair, all I really want is a few more Mbps, 8 would be enough. It's the h264 codec. It's all baked in just let me change it. I've already recorded about 40 hours of video and I'm at the crossroads of taking out my old RFU Hauppauge capture card to do the last 60. The video quality is 'acceptable'. It's not atrocious, but it could SO EASILY be better with just a few more options of adjusting the software encoder. In all honesty, the $18 Chinese converters probably have much better comparability with the aforementioned softwares which would allow for much higher bitrate captures and far more expanded options.

title: These definitely increase signal strength, but placement and angle are key.
text:
We ditched the super slow DSL that we were restricted to (2Mbps down/0.5Mbps up) in favor of an LTE hotspot router via a company that primarily caters to people who spend a lot of time on the road or in a situation where conventional high speed internet is not an option. Since fiber internet is not available in our area yet I am using this until it is.

I just upgraded to these new Proxicast paddle antennas from the Panorama desktop MiMo antenna I was using to try and increase the strength of the signal to the local tower and my upload speed doubled while the DL speed jumped up a bit more than I was already getting when at peak speeds (from what I understand, most home internet plans have a cap of 10Mbps upload so this was a bit of a win for me because I tend to upload large files at times due to my business).

These are 5dBi (the Panorama is 4.5dBi) and I have some 9dBi antennas coming. I'm hoping those will be able to push me over the 30Mbps down mark because I really want to be able to stream content in 4K, which requires a minimum of 25Mbps. If not, these will definitely do. Still ten times better than I was getting before the service switch.

The main thing with these is that you have to play around with the angle and placement for optimal performance but once you have that dialed in you should be very happy with your increased speeds.

I stand by the quality of this tablet. It does a great job at all of the stuff that I need. Again, keep in mind I'm not an artist and I really use it for demonstrations and teaching.

I'm dropping the stars because of an issue with the software. The software used to map the buttons seems to have an issue with selecting multiple modifier keys. In Affinity Photo, for example, the keyboard shortcut for rotating the canvas is ctrl+alt+shift+up. When I map this keystroke assignment, it does nothing. However, keystroke assignments containing only a single key or a single key + modifier seem to work fine. I'm not able to really work the way that I need to without mapping those multi-modifier shortcuts. My advice to you is to think about what you want to map ahead of time and then plan accordingly.

ORIGINAL
I didn’t want to spend hundreds of dollars on a drawing tablet. I really just needed something simple to do simple illustrations and diagrams for my classes. The tablet buttons and touch features (sliders, volume, etc.) work like they’re supposed to. The same is true for the buttons on the stylus. The tablet itself is light and the pen is comfortable. The pressure sensitivity and angles work pretty well and I don’t really have any complaints. My Apple Pencil iPad Pro are a little easier to use in certain cases—but I’m really comparing apples to oranges. These two products serve different purposes and I don’t regret the tablet purchase at all.

The software for this drawing tablet is really nice. You can use it to change several features, such as button mapping and pressure behavior.

For most of us who are not professional artists, this will probably serve your needs very well. It’s a huge surface with multiple features for an amazing price.

title: Very easy swap for new life in my Samsung Note tablet!
text: My Samsung Note 8.0 tablet was still running on its original battery, and I had been noting that although it would still charge to 100%, it wasn't lasting anywhere near as long as when I bought it.  As this went on it was becoming evident that sooner or later the battery would need replacing. I reviewed a number of online videos on how to do the swap and it appeared fairly easy to do, so I did an online search and decided to purchase a replacement battery from JIAZIJIA. The price was very good and the shipping was quick and on time. The battery itself appears to be a Samsung, although it had a sticker with the seller's name applied over the Samsung name. In the world we live in today its almost impossible to tell if an item is genuine or not, and JIAZIJIA's ad for the battery never made the claim that it was made by Samsung, but there was also nothing to suggest it wasn't, either. Regardless, I was interested in putting in a good quality battery so I could use my tablet like I used to. It turned out that changing out the old battery was just as easy as the videos suggest. The case was relatively easy to open and close up again if you use the proper tools as viewed in the videos. The battery change itself was very easy: Just a few screws and one wire plug and it was done. The new battery readily took a charge and lasts like my original battery used to, so I'm very happy with my purchase, especially for the price this one cost. I want to thank JIAZIJIA for the good buy and good service. I also want to offer one note: Opening the case and taking out the screws is relatively easy, but as I said previously, that is only true if you use the proper tools! This battery does not come with any tools, and that's one of the reasons I chose this one over some other online offers. A number of other battery suppliers include the needed tools to safely open the tablet's case and deal with the screws (very small). I have all of the needed tools and so elected to save money on the purchase and just pay for a good quality battery. If you have the right tools already, then this is a great seller to deal with. But if you don't have the tools either borrow or buy them, or look for a good battery buy that includes them. I recommend doing business with JIAZIJIA.

title: Excellent for games, everything else is meh. Your USB C Laptop can't run this!
text:
All USB C is not created equal, this display can't be driven at full resolution over USB C on most laptops (no that thunderbolt doesn't mean it will work). Double check your exact laptop(s) supports this resolution over USB C before buying unlike me. To add insult to injury you can't configure individual brightness or color settings when running PBP mode so when you have to use USB C and HDMI you will not be able to get both sides of the display to look the same. Through software on the PC you can get close but not perfect. After 3 hours of adjusting I have it close enough where I can call it good enough for my work laptop.

I should also add, this screen has 0 ability to configure individual color settings that I can find and the on screen display is rather sub par for what a thousand dollars should get you.

Also with the two laptops I tested when connected to USB C and they are drawing power from the monitor the backlight will flicker unless the brightness is set the the highest (which is bright enough to tan under). This is a major issue as either you have to run off battery or figure out a way to disable charging via USB C on your laptop.

All that said the main reason I bought this was because I wanted 2x 27" displays to replace my old triple monitor set up and to be able to game in ultrawide. That this beast of a monitor does just fine with over DP hooked to my main pc on a gtx 1070 (soon to be upgraded). It should be noted though that a 1070 is /just/ powerful enough to push this many pixels and you will have to turn down game settings if you have a similar lever card. If you have anything less powerful and want to game on this monitor I would re-think.

title: Great laptop with a BIG hitting probem
text:
This computer is really GREAT in many terms. It has an amazing 4K display. 32GB of memory. Big SSD drive. Strong CPU and Dual graphic cards. One of them is NVidia. It is relatively lightweight, not so thick and got a compact size even with 15" display.
It has a one pretty prominent problem: HITTING.

It seems like Dell engineers are not really aware of the fact that computer generates hit. It seems like they didn't invest a single minute of thought to figure out how to properly dispense hit.
It's poor ventilation creates a so sever hitting problem that I would recommend you to stay away from this laptop.
Once hit is too high, which happens very quickly, the computer starts throttling. It makes it work is SO SLOW, that you will feel like you are working on a machine from the 80s.

Just copy some big file, open a video or Chrome with a bunch of tabs and hit starts building up. Very quickly you start hearing the ventilation starts working hard. Which is not a big deal, since it tries to clear the hit which it good. But once you stop doing the heavy action, it takes a VERY long time for vantillation to stop the noise. which strongly implies that it is VERY POOR in clearing hit.

I have Mac from my work. I do with it pretty heavy stuff. There are times when vantillation starts working hard, then after no more than a minute, it stops. It is doing a great job in clearing hit. It has never throttled.
This Dell is throttling all the time up to a point I simply cannot work with it anymore.

My suggestion: stay away from this laptop. Not because it is not GREAT, because Dell engineers simply do not understand a thing about building machines that know to properly deal with hit.

text:
Just received this flash today. Seems pretty solidly built. Really wanted to like it since I’m looking for a second flash unit for my Canon and was hoping for a cheaper option. However, the TTL on this just doesn’t work well. While I agree with other reviewers here that this thing has plenty of power, power without control is not very useful. I’m rating it as 2 stars, b/c the build quality is good and I did not try it in manual mode so I don’t want to dock a star for that. However, if you take a look at the two pictures (the properly exposed one with the Canon 430 EXII and the other with the GT65C), you will see that the exposure is way off on the Geekoto.

Both pictures are using the same camera, same lens, in AV mode at f5.6, and without exposure compensation on either the camera or the flashes. Both were taken with flash directly attached to the camera and no bounce or diffusion. Both photos were shot in RAW using the SL2 and only cropped and then converted to JPEG using Lightroom. No other changes. I also tried minus one on the Geekoto and it was still way too overexposed. Perhaps your luck will be better but for me, this flash just isn’t what I am looking for and I’ll be returning it.

****Update*****
Was contacted by the company. They have sent me another model so I can assist them in testing this item to see if this issue occurs again and if they can resolve the issue. I have tested it and the same overexposure issue is on the replacement model. I have forwarded this information to the company, including pictures, and hope they are able to resolve the issue on their end. I like this company. title: Works well. Using for two channels. Resistances are fine. Check your amp.
text:
There’s some confusion regarding the protection circuit. There is a 10-ohm resistor wired in parallel with all the circuits when selected. If you bypass it, in “Single pair direct” mode, it just wires the connected speakers in parallel. For example: I have 8ohm and 6ohm speakers on mine (only using two channels) the 6 ohm speakers measure 4.7 ohms on their own or direct through this box. With the protection circuit enabled, the amp “sees” almost 8 ohms (passive resistance). Selecting both pair directly shows a 3 ohm passive load (the 8 ohm pair measured about 6 passively). There is a noticeable but not particularly significant drop in sound level if you compare the protection circuit on/off while live.

Anyway, it works and it’s inexpensive but seems well built. It was able to accommodate good 14 gauge wiring, though I’d much prefer banana plugs to the dinky spring clamps, I can’t knock it for performance. If you have three or four pair of speakers or are running 4 ohm pairs, the protection circuit will come in handy. My amp handles the 3.5 ohm impedance of both fine so I don’t bother with it. It just complicates things for my wife and adds an unnecessary circuit, for my purposes.

title: No touch or FaceID sensitivity drop
text:
Purchased for my brand new 11" Pro and installed it shortly after receiving, playing with and getting a feel for the touch sensitivity and speed of the iPad screen. I did ever-so-slightly misalign the first protector (at least to my standards), so I considered it a practice run, removed it and tried again with the second protector included in the package. The instructions should be followed exactly, including the suggestion to perform the operation inside a somewhat steamy bathroom--this seemed to remove much of the dust from the air as they suggested. Avoid using towels as well immediately beforehand so their lint doesn't become airborne. Alternatively, if you have a legitimate industrial clean room on hand, use that!

After installing the second protector, I did have two small circular "spots" which were unacceptable to me, and the process for CAREFULLY lifting the nearest corners and removing the lint and/or re-setting the protector seemed not to have affected the stability of the corner's adhesion, which it sometimes does for some protectors I've used. As you can tell from the picture the protector is not "perfectly" oleophobic, but it does wipe clean easily.

Finally, most importantly, the FaceID and touch sensitivity seem not to have dropped at all, even immediately after installing the protector. This has been noted in a lot of places online, but in my case on an iPad purchased in Summer 2019 I see no difference. FaceID works every time, as one would expect with the full notch at the top. I haven't had a chance yet to test with the Pencil 2, but if I do and the touch sensitivity isn't acceptable I'll update this review. Overall a very good product so far after a couple of hours, especially for the price.

title: ESR takes extra steps to ensure satisfaction!
text:
UPDATE. Original review, unedited, below.

The protector didn’t fit well with my case (which I like a lot) and ESR’s reps talked with me to resolve the issues. Ultimately they refunded my purchase. Very happy with their engagement and focus on satisfied customers!

If you like the semi-matte “paper” finish for your screen, you’ll like this material. If you have a lower-profile case, it will probably fit fine also.

I’m still hopeful that ESR makes a couple of tweaks to their installation tools. That could elevate this product into must-have status. I am impressed with their customer service.

================================
The protector looks and feels ok once on. That said, the installation aids (the “installation tool,” card, and pull tab) are poor.

The tiny snap-together tool seemed like a good idea, but it doesn’t provide sufficient stability to provide good alignment. A larger 3- to 4-pin tool would be a big improvement here.

The included cleaning tools are a nice touch, but (1) they should include a second screen wipe for a 2-pack of screen protectors, and (2)...
THE CARD WILL SCRATCH THE PROTECTOR IF USED AS DIRECTED. Do NOT use the card to smooth out bubbles! ESR, swap out that paperboard for a material that won’t leave fine scratches in the film!

Finally, the stickers attached to the protector, meant to remove the backing film, are stuck to the protector, not the backing film. :-{ They leave most of their glue on the protector, and require solvent to remove. This may be a QC mistake from the factory, or a design oversight. In either case, this makes the post-install clean-up a frustrating mess.

title: Overly stiff, prone to kinks and tangles
text:
(note: I have the same complaint about their USB-C-C cable) While it is very inexpensive and seems sturdy enough, the problem with the JSAUX cable is it’s too stiff. It easily gets kinks which can keep a neatly rolled up cable from unwinding cleanly without tangles and knots and could wear it out prematurely. It doesn’t seem to be the nylon covering that is causing it, but more the wiring inside.

I didn’t think to review it until I got some Aukey and Anker cables to compare. Those are a lot less stiff, especially the Aukeys, and less problematic.

Secondly: The extra rubber strain relief behind the connectors seems like a good idea, since this is where it bends and breaks the most. The disadvantage is that it makes the cable too stiff (again) where it NEEDS to bend the most. Coupled with a hard metal connector that is also longer than normal, the inflexible section of the cable that protrudes from the device it is plugged into is noticeably longer than my other cables. This can be a make holding and charging your phone more awkward, or require more clearance in front of the device to allow it to bend (like when it is coming from a wall charger). By loose comparison, original Apple cables in my experience break the most but bend the easiest and soonest after the plug in point. I think there’s a trade off here between flexibility and strength.

title: Almost was gonna give it 5 stars but...
text:
This is my third exchange since I was within the return window, I don't want to deal with warranty replacement having amazon ship replacements is much faster with same day shipping.

I was going to give it 5 stars cause its my favorite dash cam yet, I used Rexing S500, then got the Rexing V1LG (two which I never had problems with, no glitchy software etc. Why did I go this with CHI[nese]COM camera this time? Well I tint my back windows in my SUV with limo tint, so the rear camera becomes useless when the sun starts to set, CHICOM camera has a waterproof exterior rear camera that is waterproof (I think? I coated all the seams with marine grade silicone just to be sure) seems to still work after first rain. The picture is nice and clear, for both front and back even at night, now I can have my windows tinted dark like my soul and have the camera outside that works decently at night.

Now the problems that frustrated me...

First one I got: it worked okay but would randomly shutdown and since the screen turns off I am not sure if it is recording, sometimes I would tap the screen it would turn on and it just stopped recording. I thought it was an SD card issue, I used a Sony 32G, then a Samsung 32g and then a Sandisk 32g, all freshly formatted by the dash cam, and the problem repeats itself, I also tried a reset and retried with all three cards, so I give up order a replacement, the firmware was 966_20181126

Replacement #1: This wouldn't even record more than a second or two and then it would stop for no reason, again, I cycled through all my SD cards, formatted through the menu, reset, tried all three cards again this was with the latest revision 966_20181226

Replacement #2 So far so good, no problem yet I will update if problems persist. has revision 966_1126

Areas of Improvement:
1. Better quality control, test the products with a few SD cards even some no name brand cards.
2. Better manual with a better translation from Mandarin > English, there are some weird phrasing which looks like it was just ran through google translate and printed.
3. Add an LED so when the screen turns off you know its recording because you see a blinking little red light.
4. Longer rear camera cable, in my Highlander it was just long enough, if this is installed in a larger car like an ford excursion or Toyota Sequoia, the cord may not be long enough.
5. Though you can turn off the chime, get a better chime or give us a few to choose from

Picture is of the rear camera mounted (under the N in highlander) , the roughness is from the silicone coating, I love it mounted here because if you are standing and you look down you can't see it because it is hidden. there is still room to open the drunk to the left, I was afraid if mounted could be ripped of or seen.

So far besides the issues I had because CHICOM doesn't believe in quality control I will be using this camera instead of my Rexing V1LG, which is still in good condition, the V1LG has more little options but not a deal breaker, the rear exterior camera makes up for it.

title: Great budget projector, brightness lacking, Lumens vs ANSI Lumens, which is correct?
text:
Update: 09/09/2020

This projector performs very well.

I did discover new info about it, and some drawbacks.
- It is manufactured by a company called HKTDC Sourcing.
- The model is the M8 according to their website
- They only rate the projector at 3000 lumens and contrast ratio is 2000:1, the rest of the functionality described on Amazon is the same. I feel duped.
- Dust on the inside of the lens is difficult to clean with a compressed air duster can. I found a very small amount of dust inside on the reflective mirror and lens. It was there when I bought it, not sure how else it got inside it since the air filter has never been removed yet.

***Most of these projectors have an access point like a clip on cover underneath the model decal where you can blow air inside to clean it, this unit does not have it.

- To clean the inside would mean taking it completely apart. There are 5 small screws on the bottom, but the casing itself is snap clipped together in addition. To take it apart risks breaking those clips and damaging the exterior case. The DIY in me knows that I could drill a small hole under the decal just to clean the lens and mirror, but I will refrain till I have to clean it. In reality it should not get that dirty unless the air filter is never cleaned.
- The way I cleaned the dust is used an air duster can with the air filter off. This did the trick and cleaned up the mirror and lens of the small dust specs. I reinstalled the filter, tested it and no issue.

The good:

This projector has very good features for the price range. It has both vertical and horizontal Keystone correction that can be accessed through the menu. It also has hidden ceiling mounts underneath the rubber feet. I bought a Vivo Universal mount for it. You can also change the orientation of the projection upside down reverse sideways whatever. The focal ring around the lens is very easy to move and smooth.

I was actually very surprised with the speakers on the projector. They actually sound pretty decent considering the size. It does sound a bit "boxy" and distorts at high volume. I'm not going to fault the unit for that since small speakers mean small sound. Still decent. On the topic of fan noise I do not think it is overly loud but reasonable for the size unit.

The bad:

The brightness I would say is the only negative of this projector. The other issue I have is the inconsistency of the marketing. Amazon's description states that it is 6800 lumens but the pictures showing the products say 6500 lumens.

My assumption is that the rating is in Lumens and not ANSI Lumens. I am not sure if this is even rated for ANSI lumens or what the equivalent would be. As you can see from the pictures, the brightness is a little lacking on a white wall. I have the shades pulled behind it where there are two windows and it is overcast not sunny out. In a regular lit room, I would say this projector is perfect for everyday use. My intention is to have it for the man cave downstairs. I would also expect the performance to be better in an almost dark room. If you were to use this projector outside you would most certainly not be able to see it too well during the day. At dusk or at night I'm sure this projector will perform very well. Judging by the lumens range stated 6500 to 6800 lumens, I would say that is a fair rating, most likely a typo in the marketing material. From the research I've done I would say that 6800 lumens is equal to roughly about 1,000 ANSI lumens. Knowing that rough rating, I would say this is perfectly suited for a dim/dark room or outside at night.

Summary:

Overall for what I paid for this unit I would say it is a great buy don't hesitate in purchasing it. This will certainly not light up an airport runway by any means in terms of brightness, but the performance is adequate for my needs.

text:
I use this device in Bluetooth TX mode, with USB connection to a Windows PC.

The only reason I bought this device was so that I could have an LDAC audio connection over Bluetooth from my PC to my Sony WH-1000XM4 headphones, as no standard Bluetooth hardware supports it on PC. Sometimes, upon initial power-up, the LED turns white indicating an LDAC connection, but as soon as I try to play any music, it instantly turns blue, indicating a regular SBC connection. Sound quality is consistent with a regular SBC connection, which I could just use my PC's build-in Bluetooth card for without having to purchase this BTA30.

Also, volume control from the PC doesn't work. Even though Windows shows the volume going up and down, there is no change in volume, unless volume is brought down to nothing, at which point it does mute audio. Muting audio is the only thing that works. The volume knob on the BTA30 device also doesn't do anything, so the only way to change the volume is to use the built-in controls in my headset.

I had high expectations for this device as the first way to experience LDAC on PC, but I have been thoroughly disappointed. I hope Fiio will soon release firmware updates to remedy the issues I listed, otherwise I will have to return this product.

11/29/2020 UPDATE: After working with Fiio support, they have indicated that the BTA30 can't output LDAC if the audio is going over USB from the PC, and they have updated the product description to note that. Using S/PDIF over coaxial cable, LDAC works well with my Sony WH-1000XM4 Bluetooth headset. The audio quality is excellent., I am able to control volume from Windows, and the volume control knob on the BTA30 works well. I am very happy with the product and the support given by Fiio.

title: Read this review if you're on the fence
text:
I've wanted a Recast for a while. I wanted it partially to be able to jump back if I missed something. The added benefit of jumping commercials is nice

But the real benefits I enjoy I did not realize I needed or put thought into their existence.

With my Recast setup, I have one antenna connected to one box. I don't necessarily need a long cable run. (Unless I wish to tune channels independently on another TV or device) Once Recast tunes them, I can wirelessly stream the channels wherever it is I'd like to view them. Which brings up a good point. I personally only need 2 tuners. If you've a family which watches a lot of TV, you very well might need the 4 if you'll utilize it in this way.

Once the antenna is connected to the Recast, on any device capable of streaming you can now view a Guide, what's currently on, & your recordings. So you now have off-air viewing capability on all devices which previously only had access to streamed content from online sources.

On my FireCube, FireStick, & FireTV, along side Pluto I can look through all of my live channels. For me it's I think 120 on Pluto and 28 off-air.

With the recent pricing, it is well worth the $$$ for me. Plus Amazon product support has always been amazing for me.

title: Introduced errors on the LAN connection
text: So first the good news, this was the only one of several 802.3BT injectors which successfully negotiated at the BT power level with my WIFI Access Point. Unfortunately, the LAN connection through the POE injector was not nearly as good. Initially I had issues with the network negotiating only 100M on the switch instead of the 5G link it should see. Disconnecting and reconnecting the LAN cable a couple times from the switch seemed to eventually fix that and the switch reported a full 5G link. Unfortunately, I started having horrible wifi performance, unexplainable buffering on media streaming. After lots of frustrating troubleshooting I discovered the switch was reporting network errors on the port. I tried swapping cables. They were all good. The errors went away after I removed this POE injector from the path. So basically this POE injector was not passing the network straight through but rather introducing errors. I'm very disappointed !!

title: Excellent Product
text:
I purchased this NAS to replace my very old Drobo Mini. A lot of research went into my decision to go with a Synology device and 3 weeks in I'm confident I had the right decision. This NAS ticks all the boxes:

- The disk management software is extremely easy to learn yet powerful

- I/O performance is great and can be even better with the 10gbe expansion card. I consistently get around 114 MB/s transfer speeds over gigabit ethernet which I know isnt the fastest speeds possible but it is sufficient for me.

- Running a single 1080p Plex stream barely ticks the cpu/ram which leads me to believe this NAS could easily run quite a few streams at one time.

Side note: I used Carbonite to keep my Drobo backed up to cloud however the only plan Carbonite has that supports NAS is their business plan which is double the price of the home plan and only supports a storage size of 250gb (vs unlimited). After a lot of frustrating research I went with Backblaze B2 to back the synology up to cloud and while its not finished, it has been working fine. In addition, B2 runs directly on the NAS so it doesnt need to be linked to a host to run.

title: Seems like it would work, if it fits
text:
This stand is sturdy as hell and will not fail you when you roll into the darkness. It will be steadfast and strong, a stiff-armed companion who will valiantly wield the Sword of Justice against all foes who stand in your way. That is to say, this is a stiff, strong, and heavy little contraption that seems like it would easily hold its shape no matter how heavy your monitor.

Only one problem. The stand's metal mounting plate is attached to the folding arm with a shank that juts out from the bottom. For many monitors, this design might not pose any problems, but the VESA mounting holes for my monitor and I'm sure many others are inside of a recessed section of the back panel. The shank therefore overlaps with the recessed section's edge and prevents the back plate from laying flush with the monitor's back panel, rendering the stand unusable.

A better but perhaps more expensive design would be to attach the back plate to the stand arm from the center.

title: Great sound for a great price!
text:
The Bluetooth stopped working on an old Pumpkin unit I bought here on Amazon two years ago for $240, and I needed a replacement. So, knowing these things don't have a great lifespan, I found this one for less than $100 and decided to give it a shot. It's fantastic!

THE GOOD
-Form Factor-
At first, I didn't like the form factor because it isn't a simple swap for the factory mounting brackets. But after trial and error, I eventually just used the OEM mounts, screwed through the brackets included with this unit, and it fits perfectly. Since you only need one screw on each side of the unit, and it's more like a tablet, you can adjust the tilt of the screen a bit. So, now I LOVE this form factor!

-Sound-
Then, once it was installed, I didn't like the sound. It seemed weak and there is no EQ app with the ability to control every minute detail of the sound. After tinkering with it for hours, it turns out the few EQ settings it has are all you really need, and the amp is quite a bit more powerful than my old Pumpkin, which means I can turn down the gain a bit on my external amps, leading to both a louder and clearer sound.

-Interface-
It's smooth, and quick. Comes loaded with Waze and Youtube and a default navigation app that looks and works really well.

THE BAD
It isn't perfect though. Its missing an input for an external mic, and no one has called me yet while driving, so I don't know how well the built in mic works. All I know is, I wish it came with an external mic connection. I also realized that the Key1 line on the unit is bugged. I had my external amplifier connected and it was constantly on, even when the car was off. To fix it, I spliced the remote wire into a 12v outlet and I'm good to go! The unit comes with a remote wire connection but I decided not to trust it after the Key1 mishap. There also seems to be a build quality issue with the screen bezel, some glue smudged on it.

VERDICT
I started off hating it, but within 24 hours I'm very happy about this purchase. Solid buy for $95. Would recommend to a friend. I also recommend it to people who have purchased older units - the Bluetooth is better quality, the Android version is better/snappier, and it's an affordable upgrade that will rescue you from the daily misery I used to feel with my old, slow Pumpkin unit.

title: Compared to Q Acoustics 3020i and Jamo S803s - Kef q150's are the clear winner
text:
I bought these in white for Father's day when they were on sale for $300. I also bought Q Acoustics 3020i's ($300) and Jamo S803's ($200) around the same time to audition them and see which pair I wanted to keep.

I ended up keeping the Kef q150s (and the Jamos).

All three are very good speakers which I think anyone would be pretty happy to have. All three look really good, which actually matters a lot to me- but I think the Kefs are the prettiest.

Build quality is similar across the board, I don't have any issues with any of them. The Jamos are certainly a step down from the other two, but they still look really sharp and nothing was concerning to me. Q Acousitcs may have a slight edge in cabinet construction over the Kefs, but all are pretty good.

The Jamo S803's are great- they have a dynamic signature that bumps up the highs and the mid-lows a bit. This is great for apartment-level listening, as I can have the speakers at a moderate level that won't bother my neighbors and still find the speakers fun to listen to. I found the Q-Acoustics very flat- to the point of being comparatively boring at the volume levels I prefer. The Jamo's don't play as deep as I was hoping- subwoofer absolutely needed. The Kef's actually got deeper than the other two by quite a bit, which surprised me because the driver is smaller if you don't count the massive surround. Anyways, the Jamo's give some energy to the higher bass, but fall off too quickly to satisfy me at least. Also, the Jamos are way less efficient than the other two pairs- they need more power. On the other hand, I have an amp rated to 20 watts per channel RMS that was capable of driving the Jamo's beyond a comfortable listening level for me in a mid-sized room. They are inefficient, but you don't need anything special for them to work.

The Q Acoustic 3020i's are also very good. I like the rounded corners. They are bigger than they look because these speakers are very deep. I think I like the proportions of the Kefs the best, but again, all three look nice and sound good. The 3020i's have a pretty flat sound signature and are certainly a bit more refined than the Jamos. Imaging and sound stage were similar between the two, however. Again, I kept the Jamos and not the Q Acoustics because I simply enjoyed listening to music using the Jamos more than when using the Q Acoustics. The 3020i's are probably "better" but I personally recommend the Jamos- even if they were the same price, but especially since the Jamos are quite a bit cheaper.

I was actually blown away to hear for myself how much better than the other two the Kefs are. In every way. I could truly hear the difference that the Uni Q (concentric) driver makes. The difference was apparent immediately - nothing sounded wrong or bad when I listened to the other speakers, but everything had more depth, space, and clarity coming through the kefs. Plus, to my surprise, these speakers got noticeably deeper than the other two. I still need a subwoofer to suit my own tastes, but these are much closer to the point where you don't need one, and for many genre's these would be perfect on their own.
Still, I think the imaging is the real standout feature of these speakers that makes me really love them. The speakers start to blend in to the background and it feels like the room is just making music when you play a well-recorded track with these positioned well. My brother in law has LS50's, and these get impressively near that experience for a fraction of the cost. The LS50s are better in every way, much the same as these Kefs are better than the other two pairs- but the Uni-Q driver is not just hogwash marketing malarkey.

At the sale price of around $300 (which these also hit during black Friday and much of the Christmas Season) the decision is easy. But at $550, it isn't clear cut whether the difference is worth the cost. That is going to be a personal decision. I would probably pick the Jamos for the best value. All three pairs of speakers are very good, but the q150's were the clear winner in my comparison.

Note: I tested these speakers in a living room, but I am going to put one pair on my desk eventually. However, for now I can't say anything about how the speakers compare near-field.

title: Keyboard is this laptop's downfall
text:
The device is good, but the keyboard ultimately made me return it as it became annoyingly unusable. First, it is a light, cheap-feeling, "bouncy" keyboard. I had an old Acer Aspire One netbook years ago that was similar in size to this and the keyboard had a much more solid feel. Second, the number keys don't line up where they would on a normal keyboard, so I was constantly pressing the wrong key when reaching for a number key. The "1" key is shifted right of its normal position in order to allow them to all fit. Finally, the Fn keys (F1, F2, F3, etc.) are part of the number keys instead of their own row, so you must hold down the "Fn" key at the bottom of the keyboard while pressing a number key to activate a one of the function keys. They could have easily fit a small row of separate function keys above the number keys if they had shrunk the mousepad just a bit, which is unusually large for this size device. There are other 10" laptops that have much better keyboard arrangements, which I would recommend over this device, especially if you are regularly using it for any amount of typing (like emails). These issues may seem insignificant, but ultimately they make the device annoying to use on a daily basis.

UPDATE: I ultimately returned this due to the keyboard annoyance. I reset the device back to factory default settings through Windows and repackaged it with all included parts and original packing materials. I knew there was a restocking fee of 15% which is common and expected for most non-defective electronics returns, but I was ultimately charged more than 30% of my purchase price as a restocking fee even though there was no additional wear and tear on the product and it was returned in as near to original condition as is humanly possible. I returned it within the 30 day window.

title: AM buzzes, very light and easy to tip
text: I listen to the radio almost all day and am always on the lookout for nice battery run portables so I can move around and take them as I need. On AM talk stations there is a constant buzz of static on every inflection and syllable making some stations too irritating to listen to...I'm talking the big, major stations, not some barely-there-im-amazed-I'm -picking-this-up station.  The dial is a nice bright glow I couldn't replicate via photos but that's my one selling point for you.  However, the radio itself without the pleasant wood front, is very, very light and made of plastic.  Any breeze or flap of a fly's wing will change the station since the dial turns like butter.  If it was "tighter" or heavier so it'd have some stick to its location it'd help.  The radio falls over easily since the wood front is the heavy side but the whole thing is super light.  If you lay it flat you're fine.  Sound, when you get a non buzzy station is very good.  I don't mind paying a bit for a good product but this is a light plastic mimimum radio to which a nice light laser etched wood front has been added and in my eyes it's way overpriced.  I adore any craftsmanship or creativity so thought the extra $ would be worth it since someone, they say, makes the wood additions but the dial is not good and the buzzing is maddening even just to listen to the weather to see if that apocalyptic storm is still coming in any minute like they tell us every day a cloud is in the sky.  I have purchased several cheaper, clearer color radios (I think we're not supposed to say who or what?....) that I'd say are better sound so I was a bit underwhelmed by this one.

title: Clean tight old-school bass
text:
I've been frustrated with modern Home Theater audio systems for a very long time. I hate the thin bright sound they produce and the missing bass that everyone tells me I need a subwoofer to add back. I've tried Klipsch, Martin Logan, JBL, many brands and sizes of subs and all of them give me too much deep deep bass and not enough of what I call musical bass that I miss. My latest sub was the Rel T9i. Even that was a disappointment.
I saw this sub and thought maybe this is the answer. I immediately loved the old-school sound it gives me. It has a strong output in the 50 - 200 Hz range meaning I can focus it on 50 -100 Hz and get back what I call bass without getting overwhelmed with < 50 Hz sound that i'd rather do without at the levels most modern subs produce.
The sound from this sub is tight and musical. I've replaced what was a bass knob with a sub level control that achieves the same thing.
I have it paired with Krell gear and Sonus Faber tower speakers. I'm feeding it 100 Hz and under - volume at around half and the sub blends well with the system. I'm considering buying another just wondering how i'd get it a signal.

title: Amazing Case with Huge Potential
text:
Pros/Thoughts
Had my company buy one of the RSV-L4000 cases to secure our Ubiquiti Controller in a rack since it started its life as a desktop. After opening it up, I immediately wanted one for myself. This thing is huge and the possibilities are endless, Want to do a 15 drive hot swap array while using an E-ATX motherboard and still have room for a full sized GPU, Done. Want to do a custom liquid cooled loop with double 360mm 80mm thick rads, no problem.
Cons/Thoughts
The fans that come with the case are very sub par I had read reviews about the poor quality of the fans both construction and performance. The molex connections are fairly cheap as the pins and sockets tend to become misaligned or pull out. Impossible to work with, No. I was able to daisy chain all the fans to test them out with little effort. The fans are utterly silent but move very little air I could imagine if this case was fully loaded it could quickly become a problem with temperatures, easy enough to replace with some Arctic P120's which go for $28 for a pack of five.
Bottom Line/TLDR
Overall I like the potential of this case if I had it my way I would build a file server one and a full custom loop gaming one. The fans suck, there is no doubt about that but they can easily be replaced. That's why I am giving it 4/5 rather than the full 5. I did not experience any quality control issues that others have had happen to them. Only regret is I didn't get the RSV-L4500 with the different front bezel and the three 120mm fan/HDD mounts instead.

title: Great Fast recertified PC but lack luster service and delivery
text:
I bought this PC as a replacement for a media server. First the good: the description and specs were correct and amazing for the price. I was a little hesitant that it would truly include a 1TB SSD, but it did, as well as the 32 MB of RAM. It came with a new basic USB keyboard and mouse and included a USB wireless adapter (the pc is not wireless without this), which I had planted to hard wire it anyway due to the purpose of the purchase. The casing was in great shape and came with instruction on how to setup and the 1 year warranty information.

Now the bad. When turning the machine on I got "No Bootable Devices Found" which i believe some of the reviews stated. I powered it off, grounded my self and slide the case open to check connections, everything we secure, not loose wires/connectors (it was shipped and handled by many people). Went in the Bios and there was nothing listed in boot sequence, but the BIOS did recognize the hard drive. I emailed the seller via Amazon and received a response a couple hours later asking for my contact information (my fault for not including), then waited a couple more hours. They finally called me back (not bad service per se, but a little slow for my taste). They had me try everything I had already tried, which I told them, and it ended up being that I have to reinstall Windows or ship the PC back for refund (not replacement). This is what is unacceptable. For me, I already had a Win 10 Bootable USB, so I chose to reinstall Win 10 myself, but the majority of consumers don't or wouldn't know how to do this themselves.

I asked if they checked each re-certified PC they sell and ship, and he stated it was automatic process, and no "person" verifies the PC. Looking at some of the comments, this simple step would save money the business pays in shipping PCs back. I even asked for a credit for the trouble for me to install Win 10, what was supposed to be installed already and tested, and he stated that I could get a refund if I wanted to return the PC.

Even thought the PC and pecs is a great deal, I would not recommend this company to anyone else.
Only giving three stars because the specs are great and once I installed Windows, the PC is amazing fast and just want my media services needed, but receiving a non working machine is unacceptable, especially when it can be avoided.

title: A good switch - provided you have certified cables and don't need tech support
text:
If you are not technically inclined, you may have trouble with this switch, as it has some caveats that you need to account for. That said, this is otherwise a very good KVM switch with excellent features (though I haven't figured out all of them yet). The user manual is available in PDF if you find the booklet in the box is not enough, but don't expect much from IOGEAR's tech support line. Not only will you get voicemail all hours of the day, but when you submit your issue online they do not respond. At. All. The switch works quite well however, and I do recommend it if you are able to troubleshoot issues on your own.

The included DisplayPort cables are trash, though. Sure, they look/feel good, well insulated and thick, but they are not DP certified and you will find yourself with flashing/blinking monitors, especially if you're using laptops connected to docks. Unplugging the monitors from the switch and plugging them directly into the dock makes the flashing/blinking go away. My monitors are not 4k, so I was not overdriving the switch or the DP channel from the computer. At first I thought the issue was the switch - I updated firmware, etc., but then I decided that maybe certified cables (found here: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B083C3ZZ9X/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o05_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) would do better. In short, they did, and the issue is completely gone. Do yourself a favor and buy certified cables.

I consider the cabling issue to be a minor issue, but that with the tech support issue cost a star. It still rates 4 stars because the switch is good quality and solid. Since getting the right cables, I have had zero issues with it. I do wish it would keep the EDID information on the ports of the computers you switch away from, because when you switch to another computer, the first computer then moves all of your open windows to the primary dispaly, and doesn't put them back when you switch back to that computer. This is annoying, but not the fault of the switch so much as a DisplayPort and Windows issue. I expect I'll eventually find a work around for this.

Anyway, the switch is quite good, and allows you to use MST/daisy chaining on your monitors, through the switch, and to your computer or dock, resulting in fewer cables being used at the desk, which makes for a bit neater workspace, allowing me to indulge my inner zen. If you're looking for a good KVM, this is a good candidate, just remember to buy certified cables and avoid the ones included in the box.

title: Good Product Concept: Needs Improvement
text:
I wanted this product for four reasons. First because it was a neckband device, which means the battery life is higher, and you don't have to carry around a charging case in your pocket, and not so prone to loss. Secondly, the neckband features retractable earbuds, which meant no dangling wires becoming entangled in shirt buttons or looped around each other. Third, the device featured a neckband speaker capability. This meant that, in private, you could conduct a conversation without putting the buds in your ear. A simple switch moved from private mode to speaker mode. Finally, I wanted a reasonable amount of clarity when talking or listening on the mobile phone.
The BCS1000 has proven OK in three of the 4 categories. The issue is the latency and echoing when in neckband speaker mode. This makes it impossible to use this feature if conducting a cell phone call. Both parties to the call can hear echoing. So, too much latency, and too much echoing. The device also does not feature active noise canceling. I have had multiple devices, and noise canceling is essential if you are using neckband or non neckband earbuds to make calls. This device and all others, without active noise canceling is unsatisfactory.
If I assigned an equivalent value to each of the four features that I believe are essential, (retractability, neckband, sufficient in-ear voice and sound quality, and a good neckband speaker function, I would take the price (about $100), and divide by 4. The Exfit people should sell this product for no more than $75.00, or fix the echoing and latency issues, and keep the urgent price point, or add decent active noise canceling and raise the price by about $40.00.
My rating for this product is 3 to 3.5 stars. With a decent neckband speaker, the rating would increase to 4 5 stars.

title: Does not support 5.1 surround from Dolby Digital Plus.
text:
Set up:
Seller: Links3C Technologies
HDMI Output to Mitsubishi WD-60735 rear projection TV.
Optical output to JVC DVD Digital Theater System TH-M05.
Input #1: Roku Ultra (2019)
Input #2: Panasonic Blu-Ray player DMP-BD605

I purchased this Avedio Links HDMI switch on 9/15/2020, and set it up the evening of 16th after I received it. So, it is too soon to review on durability.

This switch replaced an Etekcity®4K x 2K 3 Port High Speed HDMI Switch I purchased in February 2015. The Etekcity switch was working fine, but had no separate audio output.

I think we purchased the TV and Blu-ray player around 2009. I am sure the the JVC theater system is at least 20 years old, probably older. When I turn on the JVC system for the first time in the morning, I usually have to turn it back off and on three times before the powered subwoofer will stay on. So, it is old.

We got the original switch because the TV has three inputs, and the stereo has none. At the time, we had a Brighthouse DVR, the Blu-ray player, a Roku 3, and a PC tower all with HDMI outputs. Then and now, only the Blu-ray player and now the Roku Ultra goes through the HDMI switches.

The Roku is always on. When the Blu-ray player is turned on, it automatically takes over the switch to be viewed on the TV. When I turn the Blu-ray player off, the Roku comes back on (both switches). The PC is connected directly to the TV, but might change.

I used to connect the Blu-ray player to the JVC theater system with an optical cable for the 5.1 surround sound. On this Avedio Links switch, to get the 5.1, you have to use the switch remote to enable the 5.1 surround; it is not automatic. I did not find anything on the switch, itself, to turn 5.1 on.

The 5.1 surround from the Blu-ray to the JVC theater system still works through this switch. I do have a problem getting 5.1 surround from the Roku. However, the problem is with select apps.

5.1 surround worked on videos through Apple TV and Google play. I do not get 5.1 surround from videos through Amazon Prime, Vudu, Hoopla, and Youtube TV, and others. I do not have Netflix to check.

I think I found the problem with why 5.1 does not work with certain Roku apps. The paper instructions for this switch state, "This product does not support audio output of authorized Always Dolby Digital plus." Apparently, Amazon Prime and Vudu use Dolby Digital plus. It is, also, possible that some Roku apps may not support 5.1, at all.

I looked at a sampling of other HDMI switches with optical out. I did not see support for Dolby Digital plus. Some specifically stated that they do not support DD+. Some stated they support Dolby Digital, but no mention of Plus. Still, the movie sound is better through the stereo system as just stereo sound (2.1), than through the TV stereo speakers.

I think that this issue could translate to to problems with hardware, such as Blu-ray players, that uses DD+.

My Vudu and iTunes movies are linked through Movies Anywhere. So, the Vudu movies that do show in Apple TV, I can play in the Apple TV app, and hear it in 5.1 surround. If Google Play and Apple TV "upgrade" to Dolby Digital Plus, then I will lose the ability to listen in 5.1 surround. Once that occurs, if there is no affordable HDMI switch that supports DD+, the next step might be to upgrade to a new theater system with multiple HDMI inputs.

Overall, I like hearing the movie audio through our stereo system even if they are just in stereo, as opposed to the TV speakers. As long as it lasts, I will enjoy 5.1 surround on the few apps that support it. I am still a little disappointed that it does not support DD+.

title: Excellent Android Headunit with a few minor drawbacks
text:
Pros: It's essentially an android tablet. You can install anything from the Google Play store that you want. Netflix, Hulu, whatever.
Parking switch limiter only applies to the AV inputs, not any apps installed to the head unit itself (disclaimer... don't watch Netflix while driving!)
Sound/Call quality was great
Built-in mic has excellent quality
Easy to install (I had never installed a stereo or backup camera in a car... I learned how to do both from Youtube and installed this myself. Worked on the first try.)
Comes with it's own GPS unit. Does not need to drain your phone by using location services.
Comes with a WiFi antenna (but not WiFi service... you'll need to supply the WiFi to get any use out of this Headunit)
Touch screen is very responsive
After initial boot, boots very quickly
Fast processing power... I use to have an Atoto A6 and this was MUCH faster.

Cons:
Obviously translated from another language. You see it in the instruction materials and even in some of the head unit menus... it's legible enough, but not perfect English.
Occasional freezes in the Android OS require you to restart
Can't play audio (other than phone calls) from your phone via Bluetooth. You don't need to because you can install any apps you want directly to this unit. *This may be my user error. Correct me if I'm wrong*
Initial boot time is quite long, but this only happens the first time you boot and then if you ever do a full restart. Turning your car off just puts it to sleep and it will boot up instantly next time you start the car.
No built-in support for Android Auto (AA). You don't need it because you can run apps directly on the headunit, but the AA layout with large buttons can be nice. There is an add-on purchase you can buy to make it compatible with AA.
The depth of the unit can make installation difficult. Check measurements several times before purchasing this head unit.
This hasn't appeared to cause any issues yet, but this unit runs very hot. I'm hoping it can stand up to the summer heat. I installed in winter and we're just getting to Spring now.

Overall if you're looking for a head unit where you get full control, unlike a major stereo producer like JVC or Bose, this is what you want. Install whatever apps you want without worrying about parking switch limits (again, don't watch videos while driving!) It's an excellent unit for the price, but it does have a few drawbacks that are worth paying attention to. I'd buy it again!

title: Didn't work for me at all.
text:
I connected this, per the instructions, and didn't get even a bit of static. Double checked all the connections, changed antenna orientations, and so on... nothing.

I'm an electrical engineer, so I opened the thing up to have a look inside. I verified that the amplifier itself was in the antenna housing (where it should be). The little thing that goes between antenna and TV is just a power injector. I traced out enough of the circuit to find and verify the power rails in the antenna... and the voltages were all as expected.

What WASN'T as expected was the build quality: There was flux everywhere (I cleaned it off), and a large blob of solder in the middle (as best I could tell it was a crude attempt to fix or reinforce a trace). There looked to be a solder bridge too, which I also fixed. The circuit board was flexed upward in a bad way, too- because the RF connector was taller than the mounting posts.

The circuit was mostly passives- just one TO-92 package which was probably a voltage regulator, and one surface mount package (SOT) that was probably the gain stage?? No markings to know for sure.

The antenna itself was an aluminum loop in the housing, and the 2 radials/reflectors you can see in the product photos.

I gave up at this point. I've got a signal generator and can borrow a spectrum analyzer, but this wasn't worth the effort. It was clear that even if I did find the root cause of the problem, this was never going to be the antenna/amplifier I needed for my rural area. I salvaged what parts I could, and recycled the rest.

title: Works beautifully as an SIO2USB device at 125kbaud
text:
The actual chip is marked "FTO1", not FTDI. See attached photo, which I took with my digital microscope (see link below for that nifty and inexpensive device):
____________________________________________
https://www.amazon.com/Microscope-DEPSTECH-Magnification-Inspection-Adjustable/dp/B07FD6K6VL?ref=pf_ov_at_pdctrvw_dp
____________________________________________
All the pins are broken out, unlike many other such devices. It works beautifully, is packaged quite nicely in a little plastic jewel box. Comes with a nifty six-pin female/mail jumper kit, and I'm just happy.

I am using this as an interface between my Atari 800xl and my Toshiba laptop bench machine. The Atari is using the Toshiba as a peripheral suite at 124000bps and the device doesn't skip a beat.

Nifty leds show activity coming in and going out.

Not a genuine FTDI chip. It identifies itself as such in firmware for the purpose of working with the FTDI drivers, both devices I bought have the same serial number. This is not a problem for Linux or MacOS users.

For an SIO2USB device, connect Atari SIO Pin 3 to FTDI pin "RX" , SIO Pin 5 to FTDI pin "TX", SIO pin 7 to FTDI pin "RI", and SIO pin 6 to FTDI pin "GND". There are several peripheral suite programs available that utilize this device, APE, AspeQT, RespeQT, and AtariSIO (That is what is on the screen in the photo).

text: It works for Gmail sign in (very easy setup -thanks Thetis & Google), but Windows 10 only gives the option to save and use the key in the online Windows account. Windows doesn't make it easy. (*Edited once I got more information about Windows 10*) this is false. Local Windows is not an App. Online Windows is an App, so the key will only work with Online Windows 10. Just to set up the key as a default option to login to online-Windows, you have to use the Windows 2FA phone app first, and then it eventually allows you to make the security key an option in the default settings, but ONLY logging into the online Windows. I only gave it a rating of 4 because of the difficulty in figuring out how to make the default setting work. The lack of documentation, on the part of Thetis was disappointing, but not surprising, considering that Yubikey is the key that Microsoft recommends. Btw, Yubikey and even Windows Hello can't login to Local Windows either so in the end I think the Thetis key was the best option.

title: Great replacement for 8AH battery
text:
If you are wondering if you can replace the 8AH battery with this 10AH battery the short answer is YES! I did just that with little difficulty and you can too. I had two concerns;

1. Are the connections. ie voltages, on the bottom of the two batteries the same, and in the EXACT same locations?
2. As the 10AH battery is approximately 1 inch longer than the 8AH battery, will I have enough room to insert and remove the battery while mounted in the frame of my e-bike?

The answer to both questions, I discovered, is Yes! See the attached photos to get a better idea of how my bike frame compares to yours.

The 10AH battery ships with a battery holder, keys, and charger. The battery holder has two wires ready to be wired into the e-bike's controller. As I was really anxious to see how this new battery would work I chose to modify the original battery holder rather than take the time to rewire the new battery to the controller. Also, I didn't wish to tarnish in any way the new battery and associated components as I wanted to keep open the option of returning the new battery if things didn't work out. Modifying the old battery holder consisted of simply cutting it in half with a hack saw and smoothing the rough edges with a file. In the photos, I refer to the part I cut in half as the ”spine”. I disassembled the battery holder to make the cutting easier. See the attached photos of this process.

The ideal solution would be to install the new battery holder and wire it to the controller, but if you are not comfortable doing this then the “cut-in-half” solution will work quite well. It did for me. Before removing any screws use a felt tip marker and put a mark, let's say, on the top and outermost ends of the parts to help in reassembly. There is a complex shape to some of the parts and the marks will simplify putting it back together.

After cutting the battery holder (spine) in two remount them back in the bike frame, separating them by about 1 inch. Then tighten the screws, insert the new battery and you are good to go. After doing so I and promptly went for an 8 mile, hilly test ride around our community with plenty of juice to spare.

Soon I will install the new battery holder as this will be a fairly simple wiring job. In the photo of the open battery controller, the two wires (red and black) in the lower left are the wires coming from the battery that will need to be wired to the controller. The existing wiring connections are a pair of push together adapters. The new battery wiring does not include its half of these connections so I will replace all of them with connectors I can purchase at our local hardware store.

As the new battery has a 25% larger charge capacity you should be able to ride 25% farther or stay out 25% longer than when using the 8AH battery. Win-Win!

Can this battery harm your 250 Watt motor, not likely if you ride as you always have in the past. If now that you have this new-found capacity you decide to begin carrying heavier loads or tackle challenging hills like never before, then you might be asking for trouble. Just be real and have a great time.

title: How to Polarize this light
text:
This is more of a DIY how-to Polarize this light.

1.) Remove the 4 small Phillips screws on the back corners.

2.) Use a thin hard tool along the edge popping the plastic tabs apart. I used my Amazon Chase card that is made of metal but a knife or paint scraper should work (don’t cut your hand).

3.) remove the white plastic diffuser and use it as a template to mark your linear polarizer film.

4.) Cut the polarizer. I used a straight metal ruler and exacto knife on a self healing cutting mat. Scissors would also work. Do round the corners like the diffuser.

5.) reassemble the whole thing. Make sure the polarizer is on the outside. Remove the protective film on both sides of the polarizer. You will have to press with both hands to pop the tabs together.

I used the included tilt mount and screwed it onto a 1/4 20 selfie stick.

So why would you want to go through all of this trouble to polarize your led light?

When also using a circular polarizer filter on your camera or phone the result is a huge reduction in glare which in turn boosts contrast and saturation. This is especially useful in tattoo photography. The skin is more reflective than you may think.

Use 4700K - 5300K for natural noon sunlight temperature light.

title: Amazing sound, lasted 6 months, love the replaceable parts.
text:
I do not consider myself an audiophile. When I found the KZ ES4s, I was just looking for a cheap pair of earbuds to replace the apple ones I usually get. They are pleasantly bizarre. The detachable cord is great! Every earbud I've owned failed because of the cord. Now if the cord breaks I just might be able to replace it! This feature sold them for me.

It sounds really good. You can read all about that in the other reviews. I did not have any trouble with the included tips, I guess my ears are the right shape.

-------
UPDATE - 2 months later
I started off loving these, as you can tell, and two months in my appreciation for them has only grown. I've owned earbuds that cost me much more, but these occupy a higher realm, despite being less expensive. I'm thinking of ordering a second, backup pair just in case.

UPDATE - 6 months later
It took six months for these earbuds to break - I'm rough on my earbuds, so it doesn't get much better than that. I whacked one of the earbuds against the floor two months in, and three months later it broke open. I swapped the broken left earbud with it's twin backup, it works great. So now I'm using the right earbud and cable from the original pair, with the left earbud from the new one... they'll likely last longer because you can replace each part individually! I'm very pleased.

-------
Update 10 months later
Still in love with these! The replaceable parts proved a lifesaver once again. The cord of my first pair failed after a year, and I just swapped it out with the cord for my second pair. All earbuds should work like this, I'd be on my fourth pair without this great feature, and instead I'm on my second and going strong. I'm now using them with my Oculus Quest as well as my phone.
And I just got a third pair which I can mine for spare parts as well, even though I don't yet need it.
I'd hate to go back to other earbuds now.

title: Costly service fees and limited control kill what could've been a great solution!
text:
Let me start by saying I have considerable experience in enterprise networking, my entire smart home / home office environment was built using Ubiquiti products, and I've been a fan of the portfolio because of the many enterprise features they bundle into a responsible price point.

So with the pandemic resulting in a greater reliance on internet for home-based work and school this seemed like a perfect add-on to provide backup internet with plug-and-play interoperability. I really liked the concept of a low monthly recurring fee with additional costs tied to consumption only 'if needed and used' (as an alternative to the high monthly recurring fee from having a second ISP)

To be fair, integration and activation were simple and straightforward - however, after a few months I can only say that the concept is great, but costly service fees and limited control kill it.

Specifically,

- The service is locked to AT&T at a rate of ~$15/ month, which includes one Gigabyte of data transfer* while data transfer beyond that is an additional ~$15/GB* (* I understand that there is an introductory promotion right now that this fee is temporarily reduced to ~$5/mo)

- While you can control which networks / VLANs are allowed to use the backup internet (for example, if you have a network dedicated to video cameras, you can prevent streams from that network running up usage), you can't control what triggers a fail-over or a fail-back, or the times you want LTE backup to be active, which are in my opinion are essential given the costly usage fees.

By way of example, I noted frequent transfers to LTE backup in the middle of the night. As best as I could tell, those resulted from minor internet 'blips' that lasted some seconds (a few missed pings?) and would've otherwise gone unnoticed.

While the LTE was hyper-sensitive to fail-over it, at times it would nonetheless take a good while to fail back to my regular internet, running up LTE usage during that time. This most recently happened during my nightly cloud backup - and during that short 1am blip I wouldn't otherwise cared about, I quickly ran up ~2 GB of LTE usage.

Unfortunately, there's no way to configure failover to trigger occur during specific times (i.e. during school / business hours) or to be less sensitive, such as if the internet is out for at least 1 minute, or 5 minutes, rather than for some seconds.

Also, the options to force a manual failover are limited - I figured I could disable the LTE device in the UniFi controller to prevent failovers to it, then re-activate it anytime I was actually impacted by an outage - but disabling the device didn't seem to stop failovers to it. The only way I could stop those was by blocking traffic at the switchport. Similarly, the only way I could force a manual failback was to reboot the LTE.

Now the UniFi controller does allow you to set a monthly data usage limit between 1GB and 20GB (in 1GB increments), however it will only *warn* you when you exceed that limit but won't *block* further usage until that limit is exceeded by 2GB - so if you set a 1GB limit, you can potentially be billed for 3GB of LTE usage ($45) per monthly cycle - the circumstances I essentially woke up to.

All these arbitrary limitations seem to benefit Ubiquiti / AT&T while degrading its value and requiring a lot of effort to manage around. I'm already looking at alternatives.

Good luck!

This box arrived without a plastic shrink wrap and without tamperproof tape on the box. Lift the cover and you have access to the PCB. I returned the product for an exchange thinking this was evidence of someone peeking and maybe touching it with their static charged hands. New one arrived in same condition. So I give a zero for packaging.

It booted the first time and no issues. The documentation is excellent.

Notice their website did not list the bios installed on the motherboard. So updated the motherboard with the latest from their website. Big mistake. Now I can't enter the bios. Been posting trouble tickets for 3 days, no answer yet. This version of the bios is no longer on their website. Their online support says 3 to 7 days. A long time when you need help. The Q-flash functionality sounds great, but I need to strip down the motherboard (remove CPU, heatsink, video cards). Not a great option given the cost of the processor.
