title: High Quality Earphones
text:
This is a high quality bluetooth earphones. It has a crystal clear audio. The neckband is rubberized and pliable. It is barely noticable on your neck. The battery life is great. It's much better than most bluetooth earbuds. It is around 12 hours continuous use as advertised.

One thing I like about this earphone is that it paired well with 2 devices at once. Audio will still come from one device but once you stop that device audio, you can listen to the audio from your second device. If your device could not find the earphone, you need to clear the earphones device history by pressing and hold the power and - button simultaniously until light flash red and turn white.

One thing I want with wireless device is the ability to charge and use at the same time because it extends the durations of the device when the battery is dead. This earphones will shutdown when plugging in charger but if you turn it back on, you can use it while charging.

Now for the cons. The manual does not provide instructions on how the buttons work. It works similar to other buttons control. Vol+/Vol- with 1 press. Next/Previous with press and hold +/-. Power button on/off by pressing and hold 3 secs. Another cons is that I could not find the mics anywhere. It does not seem to have one. Pressing the power and hold for 2 secs does activate google assitance. And finally the last cons is that the connectivity is around 12 feets. It's when you'll notice connectivity problems. You can still hear at 20 feet but there will be a lot of interruptions. I have bluetooth earphones that works seamlessly at 20+ feets but battery life is around 6 hours.

Overall, if you use this device mainly for listening to music or exercising, this earphone is for you. If you are looking for an earphone for answering phone calls, this is not for you. Many people will dislike this earphones becsuse of the short wireless range. Dependings on where your phone is located, this earphones will not work every where in your house. This is not a problem for me so I gave it a good score.

EDIT: this bluetooth earphones interfere with wireless signals. My other bluetooth devices does not.

title: Works fine except the thermistor
text:
This is a YL-40 module with a PCF8591 ADC converter on it. I used a Raspberry Pi 4 to communicate with the module over I2C bus.
Using included "suitcase jumpers", on-board sensors can be connected to ADC inputs.
Jumper P4 connects thermistor to AIN1.
Jumper P5 connects light sensor to AIN0.
Jumper P6 connects potentiometer to AIN3.
Due to PCB error (no electrical contact or trace found), you need to solder a wire from other side of thermistor R6 to GND if you want to use the thermistor. (Both of my boards have this issue and others have reported problem online). If you just want to use the ADC/DAC, the 4 analog inputs and 1 analog output work fine. The potentiometer and light sensor work fine.

title: Great sound and mic (with bluetooth compatibility problem)
text:
First of all, this headphone (and most bluetooth headphones) have 2 modes: (1) Stereo/headphone (no mic) and (2) Hands-free/headset (both input & output). I suppose the idea is to have great sound quality when listening to music/movie (option 1). This option works fine for me and the sound quality is great. When you want to use the headset mode (option 2), the sound quality would be lower but you would be able to use your mic. So, when my order arrived, it initially worked really well for 2-3 calls (through Skype/MS Teams), then I could not get it to work in the headset mode anymore (no sound and the bluetooth's connection dropped when I started a call). The stereo mode (mode 1) still worked fine. I troubleshoot for hours, e-mailed Anker's customer service, and googled/read through many bluetooth headphone issues. I decided to exchange the headphone (with hope that the item I initally received was defective), but the second headphone had exactly the same problem. I tried it with 3 different Windows 10 laptops with no luck. I also had another bluetooth headphone that worked fine (with headset mode) in the same computer, so I know the laptop's bluetooth worked fine. I also tried this headphone with my phone (Pixel 3 Android) and it actually worked fine!

So it looks like this headphone has some compatibility issues with my laptops (maybe certain bluetooth device). To be fair, when researching I saw many other headphones (different brands) also had similar compatibility issues. I tried almost all the recommendations (uninstall bluetooth, update driver, turn on/off sound options, disable other speakers/mic, etc. etc.) but nothing worked out for me. I decided to return both headphones because I needed it for calls and not just the audio. I have to say that the build quality of this headphone is very good and the sound quality is excellent (especially considering the price). Anker's customer service had also been great: helping out with troubleshooting, exchange, and returns. I think Anker should identify and solve this bluetooth compatibility issue (because it seems to happen to other people too from the reviews). If you are going to use it with your phone or willing to try with your computer, I would recommend the product. It is a great product with one critical compatibility issue.

title: Great Value Gaming monitor
text:
Pros:
Only $200 as of writing this.
144hz refresh rate
1ms response time
8 pre configured monitor profiles

Cons:
No built in speaker

This Acer Nitro 24 inch monitor is a great steal for its value and quality. Many monitors with these specs cost well into the $300 range, but Acer captures all the needs of the modern 1080p gamer for only $200. I love the 144hz refresh rate. I've only ever used 60hz monitors and let me say 144hz definitely makes a difference when it comes to gaming. I played GTA V on this monitor side by side my old 60hz monitor and the image quality was astoundingly more sleek and defined. The monitor also has an eco feature which dims the brightness and makes colors easier on the eyes as you game late into the night. Another reason I went with this monitor is because of the reputation Acer has for good quality monitors. Other gaming monitors competing in this price range try and offer the same specs but do so at the cost of quality. I've had this monitor two months now and my brother who bought a Scepter brand monitor is already noticing dead pixels.

The only downside I can think of for this monitor is its lack of a built in speaker. For some people this may be a deal breaker, but you can honestly pick up $10 speakers on Amazon that would have the same quality audio as traditional built in speakers (which is what I did).

With all this in mind I expect to keep this monitor in use for the next several years until 4k gaming becomes a more realistic option for the casual gamer. Definitely worth the money.

title: Great gaming laptop overall for the money
text:
I have had this laptop for almost 3 weeks and have been putting it through its paces with general use, games, watching streaming videos, etc. before writing this review.

=======
Pros:
=======

* Cooling is MUCH improved over the 2018 PH315-51 model and comes factory under-volt by -0.125v which certainly helps.

* The screen bezel is a lot thinner than the older models. The screen just feels bigger now even though logically, on paper, a 15.6" screen is a 15.6" screen.

* Has a DisplayPort

* All USB ports are USB 3.0 (Instead of 2x 2.0 and 1x 3.0 as on the older model)

* Gaming performance is great

* Overall performance is great

* Boot time is insanely fast on the NVME drive. Around 10 seconds or so, if that.

* Screen is beautiful, colors are vibrant, the view angle is fantastic, and the 144 HZ refresh rate is great; although please see my gripe about discoloration of the top of the screen in the Cons section.

* The touch pad is nice and spacious

* It is pretty light as far as gaming laptops go. I've seen some people complain that this laptop is heavy; but coming from an older gaming laptop that weighed almost 15 pounds... The weight of this laptop is a major relief!

* The keys are back-lit which is great for low-light/night time computing/gaming

* The chassis is nice. The top (back of the screen) and the keyboard area is metal, while the bottom and the bezel surrounding the screen is durable plastic. I absolutely love how nice and cool the metal is against my wrists when I'm typing.

=======
Cons:
=======
* My biggest gripe about this laptop is that there is visible light/color distortion at the top of the screen that is very noticeable against dark backgrounds. This is very distracting if you're watching a movie and there's dark scenes, or if you like to play horror games where typically the environment is dark. I've noticed a lot of people calling this light bleed and I've seen multiple screenshots of the effect; but this isn't light bleed (Well, it might be in the technical sense of the word). You know how if you press your finger lightly against an LCD screen (I'm NOT recommending that you do this by the way), it discolors slightly around the area where you touched? That is what's happening here. Apparently the bezel at the top of the screen is pressing WAY too freaking tight against the top of the screen (From factory!) and causing the discoloration at the top of the screen. I can't imagine that this is good for the health of the screen. This NEEDS to be fixed.

* NVME drive is small at 256 GB. There is 237 GB usable, but realistically, there is less than that due to operating system install, so there is more around 130 - 150 GB of free space for applications, games, etc. You can load a handful of modest sized games or one huge game (Doom 2016 is around 80 - 100 gigs after patches and Final Fantasy XV is around 90 gigs after patches. Sheesh, game sizes are getting absolutely ridiculous!). That little drive will be hurting for free space in no time at all after a few games are installed. You will definitely want to add a spare drive to put games on. Acer claims that the laptop is expandable with a second NVME drive and a 2.5 inch bay (Which does include the connector you need for it in the package), but the entire back has to come off if you want to put a drive in internally, and you might void the warranty in the process if you do it yourself; so it's not a false claim, but it's a 'gotcha' claim. An external USB drive is the way to go if you want to remain on the safe side and don't want to pay a tech to put a drive in for you.

* Battery life is OK; not great, but not bad either. When not gaming it can get about 3 - 4 hours of light use. It is absolutely horrendous when gaming at approximately 50 minutes, give or take a few depending on the game. Although I will say that this is to be expected from a gaming laptop. It's a lot of power packed into a tiny device. You will definitely want to be plugged in if you want to game on it for any extended length of time.

* The webcam is horrible. It is -technically- HD in resolution, but only in resolution. The picture quality resembles early 2000s webcams. The video quality is something between a VHS recording and low quality grainy DVD. You'll either want to get an external webcam or pass this laptop up for a different one because this webcam sorely disappoints. It will work in a pinch though. I will note that it helps a bit to have a very well lit room if you want to use the webcam; even so, it's still pretty bad in my opinion. In the end it doesn't matter to me personally since I don't use webcam that often anyway.

* The sound quality of the microphone is not fantastic. It sounds like someone is talking through a tin can. Like the webcam though, It will work in a pinch. I don't use microphones that much anyway, so it isn't a big deal for me.

* The speakers sound piercing and tinny. No bass whatsoever. This is to be expected though, most laptops don't have the greatest speakers anyway. Use headphones or an external speaker system whether wired or blue tooth.

* Acer seems bent on making installing your own OS on this laptop as hard as possible; even if you want to install a different edition of Windows 10 (For example: It comes with Windows 10 Home but you want to upgrade to Windows 10 Pro). It is doable but be prepared to do a little digging and research to figure out how to do it. I would expect this kind of crap on a low end cheap laptop, but NOT on an expensive gaming laptop!

* UEFI/BIOS settings are bare minimal. You can tweak a few boot settings and that is about it. It is definitely NOT a power user's utility. Again, I expect this on a low end laptop, not a gaming laptop.

=============================================
Mixed Feelings that are neither Pro nor Con for me:
=============================================

* Although cooling is much improved over last year's model, for some games, you will want to turn the fan to max. Keep an eye on PredatorSense temps. I personally prefer to max the fans if I notice the temps getting higher than about 75, but that's just me.

* There is a very limited amount of USB ports if you're not counting the USB-C connector, there are 3x USB 3.0 ports. Invest in a powered USB hub if you need to plug in more than just a keyboard and mouse (Because who wants to game on a laptop keyboard and touch pad unless they had no choice?)

* USB-C connector is data only; does not output video

* There is no optical disc drive. Not a big deal since USB drives are cheap nowadays, but it would have been nice to have.

* You have to be slightly heavy handed on the touch pad but this may come down to user preference. Personally I'm fine with it and I'll be hooking an external mouse to it whenever possible anyway.

* Keyboard back lights are not RGB. They are solid blue/light blue in color, you can toggle them on or off, and set a few different levels of brightness on them. Not a big deal for me though; I'm just happy being able to see the keyboard in the dark.

* There is pretty minimal bloatware pre-installed, but it is no where near as bad as other computer brands. I would consider it a reasonable amount to be honest.

* The dual GPU set up can be confusing at first. A tip for anyone first time to dual GPU: If you're having trouble figuring out why some applications are performing badly and they don't seem to be using the nVidia GPU; close the program, then right click it, and chose Run application with GPU > High performance nVidia. You can also set up an application profile in the nVidia control panel for your program to use which ever GPU you want if you want the program to always run with that.

Despite some faults with this laptop, overall, I like this laptop a lot.

title: Simple, straightforward and easy to install.
text:
Our work Wi-Fi can be spotty sometimes and we run EVERYTHING on Wi-Fi now. From out point of sale to our music system... it's all wireless so if our Wi-Fi goes wonky, everything starts to act weird. Before switching providers I thought I would give an extender a shot first. I didn't want to go all in on an expensive item, so when I saw this model for less than $25 I went ahead and ordered it. It came today and so far, so good.

I was a little worried about the installation after reading the reviews here. But when I got it and opened the instructions I saw there were three methods that could be used. I went with putting the app on my phone and going from there. This unit was up and running in less than ten minutes. Most of that time was just me re-checking to make sure I didn't miss a step.

First I installed the app. Next I plugged the unit into an outlet fairly close to our router. Then after it was on and running I connected my phone to the TP-Link wireless connection. After that I added a password for the extender, then backed out and reconnected to the router Wi-Fi. That was it. The next time I have a moment I will connect all the devices to the extender but I checked their network connections and sure enough, I see the new network option listed and ready to connect to.

For reference, our business uses a local/regional provider called All Points Broadband. They use Cambium products, specifically cnPilot routers/access points. Our modem is pretty new (less than six months old) and is fairly reliable on its own. I just wanted to improve uptime to 99% or better.

If you are not technically inclined, just follow the quick start guide and this extender is a great, cheaper option to improve Wi-Fi coverage in your home or business.

title: Not perfect but a no brainer at $99!
text:
I almost gave these a 5 star. Oh so close. Not because they are 5 star buds or even close to perfect. They aren't. However, what these things do well, they do really well. I have been curious about JLab products for some time. Best Buy has been pushing JLab for a couple years now and, as a headphone junkie, I thought it was time to see if they could live up to the high value budget headphone hype. Here is the breakdown:

The Good:

-Sound: Surprisingly very good. Maybe a little flat but really not bad at all. Solid bass, a rich mid section, and plenty crisp highs. As far as I can tell, JLab didn't include any specialized codecs for these. You can make the sound your own with the JLab ANC app (more on that in a bit) with their robust EQ. Plus, these things get loud. Louder than most BT wireless buds. Overall, very well done.

-Battery life: The over ear loop design always allows for larger battery capacity and JLab takes advantage of that ability here. 15 hours on bud plus another 55 in the case. With ANC on, I am getting more like 11 hours or so of use but that is still class leading. So far so good.

-Bluetooth 5.0: It is here and gives you great range and easy pairing. The connection to my Note 10+ is super stable. I have had zero issues with them.

-Form Factor: I am not a big fan of the loop design for everyday buds. I much prefer to just toss buds in my ears. That said, these are active headphones made for exercise and this design lends itself to that. In my workouts with these I have found that they stay put and are very comfortable. You will want to kind of screw them into your ear as you wrap the hook back around your ear. They give you a bunch of tips including a soft Comply style tip. You should be able to find a good fit here.

-Charging: JLab has built in a cable charger to the bottom of the case. It is a little strange but, at the same time reasonably handy. You also have wireless charging onboard. I think I prefer to bring my own cable to the party but this works.

-Intangibles: IP66 waterproofing rating is here so you can sweat until your hearts content. There is no killing these with water. These also have proximity sensors which gives you auto pause. Pull off a bud and whatever you are listening to or watching pauses. These buds also give you a low latency mode meaning when you watch video what you are seeing should match what you are hearing. These things complete a solid package.

The Bad:

-ANC: I have some of the best buds in the business when it comes to ANC and I truly wasn't expecting that level here. The challenge for me here is that I don't really hear much ANC going on at all. That said, the buds themselves are extremely noise isolating so there isn't much sound coming in regardless. I just hope folks don't buy these for their ANC. You will hear noise leaking in during podcasts or lower volumes. When you crank up the jams, the world around you is pretty much gone. I will say that JLab have updated these once already and I see that I have another update pending so maybe they will update the ANC at some point. As I said, I didn't expect much on the ANC front and I didn't get much.

-The case: It is massive. While I like having 55 hours of battery in there, you won't love carrying this in your pocket. I would rather have a smaller case with 25 hours myself. That said it does have good strong magnets to snap in the buds to. The top is also magnetic. There is also 4 LED's that let you know how your doing on battery. I hammered the new Bose wireless buds for the same case issue. However, unlike Bose that provides a massive case (see photo) with only two more charges, JLab at least gives you a big battery back up. Not a complete fail just too big.

-Calls: Call quality isn't good. These are geared towards working out so this isn't a deal breaker for me but it's still too bad. If you need to take a call just get to somewhere quiet. In a pinch they work just fine. Just not something you would want in a daily use bud.

-The App: I was debating not hitting JLab for their app here as so many buds don't even have an app but, after spending some more time with it, I have too. They need a good software guy to go in there and clean it up. It is a sloppy mess. All the features you could want are there; the afformentioned EQ, the ability to update firmware, control ANC, ambient noise settings, and the ability to remap your controls though I can't seem to make that work. The updates are long and cumbersome. Everything is here, it just needs to be reworked.

-Conclusion:

So at $99, I was expecting flawed earbuds with little in the way of ANC and poor sound. Honestly, JLab is onto something here. I am glad I finally tried them. While the ANC is definitely barely present, the rest of this package is very good. From battery to waterproofing to sound quality, these buds punch WAY above their price point. I don't think I would recommend them as a stand alone daily earbud like a set of Airpods or Galaxy Buds+ but, as a set of buds for working out, JLab has an absolute homerun here. Well done to the JLab team!

title: Good Picture Quality and Looks Great
text:
I bought two of these for mother's day, one for my wife in the pearl white (stardust) color and one in dark blue (slate) for my mom. While the price is high, the packaging and everything else are premium, this is kind of the iphone of digital picture frames.

Pros:
- The frames seem to be of good quality. In one of my pictures you can see the power cable is a very nice fabric braided cable which feels nice and even comes with a suede and metal cable tie. Also, the stand is as far as I can tell a heavy piece of solid metal.
- I am a hobby photographer, so I take pride in some of the images that I've captured and this frame does a very nice job of displaying them with very good quality. The screen is not matte like most lcd screens, but not too glossy either. This is probably the best part of the frame.
- Once set up, you can easily have people add photos from their phones to the frame.
- There is also a camera for gesture controls. You can use it to change the images either forward or backwards, and you can also "like" a photo.
- The frame can automatically sense light in the room and turn itself off at night.

Cons:
- There is no off button in the app or on the frame. There are two settings: auto will sense the light in the room and if you turn off the lights at night, it will shut off automatically. However, it will stay on in the day which might be wasteful if you're not home. You can also set a timer, but the only workaround I have found is to set the timer to turn on at a certain time, then turn off 5 minutes later. So, not off, but off for all but 5 minutes in a day which is acceptable.
- When you send an invitation to others to contribute to the frame, it didn't send emails (as far as I can tell) to people to join, I needed to text them to tell them to install the app. Once installed and they logged in, then it would let them know in the app that they had been invited.
- If you're gifting this to someone who might have trouble connecting it themselves (like my mom), then you need to know a lot about their wifi network to set it up ahead of time. I'm pretty good, but I don't remember my mom's wifi network name exactly, so it was easier for me to give it to her and set it up at her house. This is not a big deal, but if you are sending this to grandma and you can't physically be there to help her, I might be worried.

Conclusion:
While the price is pretty steep, I think that the build and image quality seem to be worth it. The real question of value will be answered in time. I feel like if this frame can last for a few years, then it will easily justify the cost. However, if it doesn't last at least two years, I would probably not get another one. I think that this is a great option and it would be practically perfect if they would add an on/off switch in the app down the road. My wife and mom love it, and I think that this would make a great gift for anyone.

title: The JBL Bar 9.1 is awesome!! It has everything you ever want!
text:
****UPDATE 6/11/20

It looks like the Fire TV Stick 4K doesn't do Atmos with the JBL Bar 9.1. I don't think the Cube TV does it too. I just picked up a Shield TV 2019 and Atmos works on Netflix and Disney+. The system will tell you in the front that it's doing Atmos so don't believe on what you see just on screen on any app. The trick with the Shield TV is that you need to turn off Dolby Surround in the audio settings.

The Sonos Arc is out now and honestly it's a good system but overall this JBL Bar 9.1 fits my needs better. It's has Bluetooth, HDMI IN, chromecast, DTS-X, and fully wireless up-firing rears. If all you want to do is get a single sound bar setup and didn't want to spend more then $800 then get Sonos Arc as it's a great speaker just by itself. If you want more and want the complete package then just spend $200 more period.

US version doesn't get the 4 side caps after all. Which sucks and u wish you could just buy them separately. I'm still talking to JBL about giving them to me so we'll see. JBL should've included them in the first place, come on we are spending $1,000 on this.

******

I don't write a lot of reviews and honestly this is probably my first one ever on Amazon. I feel like I need to with this product just to defend it after reading the other reviews so far.

I got my unit about 1 1/2 weeks ago and so far it's been near perfect. There were some hiccups in the beginning but I haven't had any issues since. This is an excellent surround system period! Yeah it's true that this isn't a ture 9.1 system like one of the reviewer said but what it does have is 9 separate channels of sound though. It's all just marketing from JBL. I don't mind it being just a 5.1.4 system as all I really wanted were the up firing Atmos speakers. One thing that I do wish this had are some side firing speakers to make it 7.1.4 like the Q90R. That system is $1,600 though.

In the box I was missing the 4 side caps though but I think that was by accident maybe. I did reach out to JBL to see why it was missing. They didn't mention that it wasn't part of the US packaging. They don't have it in stock at this time but will ship them out to me once they are. I did get the mounting brackets though unlike the other reviewer. Also I didn't know it was supposed to come with micro USB cables as well but that's fine as I will just get some later on if I decide to hard power the rears.

I was able to calibrate my system just fine. It's a 2 stage process and takes a few minutes. I didn't have to do anything extra then what I saw in the manual. I do wish the remote had more buttons for Night Mode, Smart Mode (Hold mute for 5 secs, let go and hit VOL +), & Sound Mode (EQ modes if they did support it like the Bar 5.1). Yeah I do wish this system had more refine settings to mess with like the menu system on my Sony. It would've been great if it did have an app for it as well.

My TV does support Atmos but I plugged my Fire Stick 4K directly into the Bar 9.1. My Disney+ does show Atmos along with Vision. Netflix is showing Vision only but I wasn't aware that the app on the Stick 4K doesn't support Atmos. I'm looking to either get the Shield TV (2019) or the new Apple TV 4K whenever it comes out. The Stick 4K does support YouTube HDR though. I'm planning to upgrade my TV either this year or the next with eARC support and ATSC 3.0. I'm eyeballing the Sony 900H at this time.

The rear battery life have been great so far. I have been able to watch several TV shows and movies the night before then wake up to watch additional TV without charging them again. It does prompt you when they are low though so you could either charge them via micro USB or with the bar. I believe it does have quick charge but I'm not too sure. I do wish you could tell how much battery life is left though. You could however hit the power button to see the LED indicator, again app support would've been nice. Having no wires is awesome though and it's nice knowing that I could always hard wire them in the future if I wanted to.

Chromecast aka Google Cast + Airplay 2 support are great and was one of the main reasons why I got this unit over the Samsung Q90R plus I'm a Google fan! The bass is booming and I love being able to turn it up or down. I use this for music too over Bluetooth and casting, both sound awesome but casting will give you higher fidelity. Of course each peices of this setup won't sound as nice as a Sonos setup (~$1,800 total for ARC, Sub, 2 Ones) but it's not meant to be at almost half the price. Sonos doesn't have have DTS-X or HDMI INs though which are deal breakers for a lot of people out there. I does have support for Airplay 2 but I don't think you could Chromecast though. Having 820W on the JBL Bar 9.1 makes this system louder then the Q90R which was one of the main complaint about it.

Overall it's an awesome system that is near perfect. I'm still giving it 5 stars though because basically JBL gave us everything necessary in a modern system without any extra for a great price. Yeah this system will be on sale eventually at $800 or less but I couldn't wait and I'm glad that I got it now instead. They're still hard to find at this time though being sold out everywhere. If you could get one now you should. It's worth every penny like most JBL products are. Good luck with your shopping and thanks for reading my long review.

title: It's the Best for What It Is!
text:
When we decided we were going to invest in security cameras we knew a) we didn't want to be tied to "the cloud", b) we didn't want to worry about hardwiring or plugging into an outlet and c) we wanted to be able to keep it reasonably out of reach of anyone desiring to get their hands on it where it was mounted. This little Hiseeu unit (which reminds me of a one-eyed Minion) seemed to fit the bill perfectly; and it got a lot of great reviews - a lot of them punctuated with helpful in-depth details - which for me is a great selling point. So on the strength of that (and a reasonable price), we purchased two - one for the front door and one for the back yard. They arrived quickly and in perfect shape. Everything in the box was easily identifiable with the list on the enclosed instruction sheet. Though the instructions are written in English, they are not perfectly understandably written; however, with the help of illustrations and the fact that this is a relatively straight-forward set-up process, a little interpolation is all that is needed. That, and the fact that the app (which we accessed and installed through Google Play and is free) guides you with audio as well as visual instructions along the way makes for a very easy installation. Once the camera is activated and registered, basically all you need to do is mount the camera somewhere. I would recommend somewhere out of the reach of human hands that aren't carrying a ladder around! When you do decide on a spot, I strongly recommend against using the anemic 3M adhesive pads - the only fly in the ointment of an otherwise excellent product. The pads became our choice as a result of desiring to preserve the integrity our vinyl siding against any holes, which would be necessary (as we thought then) with the alternate mounting bracket enclosed, albeit a more secure method. The camera and the software played really well together for about a half a day. The next morning, I went to log in to the app and when the camera came on, I noticed on the live feed that it was looking straight down at the front porch, rather than from the position I had mounted it in the previous afternoon. No sooner had I made this observation than I heard a "thunk" outside the front door. The camera had fallen eight feet to the concrete below - a victim of the insufficient adhesive value of the pad to the siding. Well, having read other reviews, I was encouraged by others that needed to contact Saul - the guy to call when there's a problem. Through a short exchange of emails, Saul was able to send us a replacement camera (which arrived very quickly), while we mailed the non-functioning camera to the warehouse address.....it was as simple as that! Fantastic customer service! Thanks, Saul! I have since mounted the new camera at the front door utilizing the screw mount bracket instead, however I have mounted the bracket to a vinyl siding hook from Menards (Model Number: VSH56-24 Menards® SKU: 2850715) and then attached the hook to the siding - no holes. The particular hook I used is supposed to hold 56lbs., so I feel pretty secure with it holding an 8oz. camera. I ran out of time this weekend to mount the back yard camera, but I plan on mounting it the same way as at the front door, utilizing a vinyl siding hook, small machine screws, a couple washers and nuts (for mounting the bracket to the hook) - all stuff you can find for a nominal cost (under $10 total) at Menards or Ace Hardware or any hardware store. I haven't explored all the features of the camera yet, but it provides great video resolution to the phone app for viewing on your phone (which you can change between standard definition and high definition). Nighttime viewing is very good, too, though in black and white - which is perfectly fine and as expected. The intercom feature is excellent as well - very good audio, offering conversation between you and the individual(s) outside. I'm really looking forward to learning more about using these cameras. So far I have nothing but five stars for the cameras and certainly the customer service from Saul! A highly recommended, quality, home security device at a reasonable cost!

Update 9/5/19: got the other camera activated and then installed in the back yard and it was even easier having done it once already for the front door. Camera alerts me with the CloudEdge app very well; I was a little surprised when I got a notice that the back yard camera picked up some human activity this morning while I was at work - turns out the next door neighbor's lawn crew (probably 35 feet away) set it off. Actually, I am pleased that that happened so that I know what to expect for the range of activity picked up. Still a five star experience with these cameras!

title: Good design hampered by poor build quality
text:
I just picked these up from my mailbox less than an hour ago and I am returning them as I write this review. The design is one of the better ones for this type of product. It is actually comfortable to wear when sleeping on your side, but the problem is that the build quality is so poor that it cannot last more than a few months if not weeks of regular use. The speakers and the Bluetooth module are separate connected by a micro USB port. The cable to the speakers is the the cheapest, crappiest cable that I have seen on a product of this price. The cables are thinly connected the the male end of the micro usb with no reinforcing and so even just trying to get the module back into the band you can damage the connector. Just after 15 minutes of use I can tell that the cable is not seated correctly in the connector and will just continue to deteriorate so I am returning it. DO NOT GET THE WIRELESS VERSION. title: Very solid screen protector
text:
First the good. I am using this on a 9th Gen Fire 10. It is a solid screen protector. It is very clear, more clear than other screen protectors that I have use on phones and tablets in the past. When installed, you do not notice it, at all. It is almost like a second piece of glass. It is not as flexible as others. It is also a lot thicker. The touch and response is better then a regular screen protector. It almost feels like you do not have a protector on it. Exactly what you want in a screen protector. You don't want to notice it. I am very impressed.

Now the negative (or possible negatives). Most of these aren't negatives per se. They could be, depending on your circumstances. They were not for me. The protector is THICK. This could present problems with some cases. I have the ProCase Stand Folio folding case. It closes with the protector, but barely. I had the same case with a 7th Gen fire 10. That one closed a little better (It might be that the 9th gen is thicker than the 7th gen). There are several videos on the manufacturer's website, make sure you watch the right one. The descriptio0ns of the videos aren't really useful. In regards to installation: using the holding strips was new to me, but seemed to work well...ish. When the screen was installed there were large air bubbles. Unlike a thinner, more flexible screen protector, it is a little more difficult to push the air bubbles out, especially since it does not come with a plastic squeegee, like thinner protectors do. I was able to do it though, without too much trouble. The documentation that comes with it says that the bubbles will disappear in a few days, on their own. I didn't bother to wait to find out. I used my fingers to force them to the sides.

Overall it is a great protector that you don't notice, and had a great feel an response. I would highly recommend this to anyone with a 7th or 9th gen Kindle Fire 10. In my opinion, it is the best one on the market.

title: It's okay, but don't expect miracles for astrophotography
text:
I am pretty disappointed with this product. First, if you're planning on mounting a telescope on this thing - don't. It doesn't have a Vixen Dovetail bracket. You will have to bolt any telescope on directly, which is annoying. Also, it can't handle much weight. A 5lb scope or less. I tried putting my 130mm newtonian on this mount, and it can't handle the weight.

I tried using this for astrophotography using a Canon camera and a 300mm lens. The counterweight is too heavy even all the way up the counterweight shaft. You may need to invest in a smaller counterweight for a camera set up. That's a relatively easy fix, even though it is slightly aggravating to have to purchase more stuff. What was REALLY disappointing and aggravating was the sidereal tracking of this mount's RA axis motor. If you're looking to get round stars, don't set your exposures past 30 seconds. Even 30 seconds gives you oval stars. The RA axis motor is either not calibrated correctly or there's some other cause for the Dec drift and RA tracking errors. The mount isn't particularly steady, and the clutches on this mount are terrible. They do not hold well.

I have attached two images. The first is a 20 minute exposure showing the drift and tracking error, and the second is what a 30 second exposure of the same part of Orion's belt looks like. This was taken using a Canon Rebel T6 with a 300mm lens.

I attempted a return, but amazon won't accept a return for this item for some reason, so I think I may be stuck with this $180 mount. Don't make the mistake I did in getting this mount if you're looking to do serious astrophotography. Save up and buy a better mount/sidereal tracking system. If you're just looking to get some 30 second images, this mount might be okay for you, but don't expect miracles with this.

title: Used In My Zombie Containment Unit for Halloween
text:
[[VIDEOID:cabf2dfc94c5a5fcef6dd2523f72855d]] I bet you didn't expect to see a review with this type of usage of the monitor, did you. I built a zombie containment unit for Halloween a few years ago in which it used a monitor to give the illusion a zombie was trapped inside the unit. I used a very cheap monitor in the past and found that it looked okay when looking straight on at it, but any angle from the sides or from the bottom would wash out the image and the illusion was broken. Given that the "window" was about 5 and a half feet from the ground, anyone shorter couldn't view the video.

So, I found that I needed a type of monitor that had wide viewing angles so you can see it from off angles instead of just straight on. This monitor has an IPS board that allowed for these sharper viewing angles.

Here are some things that I looked for when researching a monitor to buy:

* Largest monitor I could buy for under $100 USD
* Lightweight as it would be hung on the inside of the "unit"
* Bright/vivid video
* Sharp viewing angles without loss of image quality
* at least 22" diagonal width. The previous monitor was only 15" so I wanted to get a larger size for more realistic size "zombiie" within.

This monitor checked off all the boxes. I also had a $15 Amazon gift card which softened the hit to the wallet.

Once received, I hooked up the power cord and an HDMI cable that went to a small digital video player that had a memory card which played the trapped zombie clip. I didn't attach the base as doing so would not allow me to mount the monitor inside the cabinet. This isn't a Halloween prop build video so any details of the unit is limited to the monitor itself.

I used a felt material inside the cabinet along the edges where the front of the monitor would be in contact with to protect the screen as this is a bezel-less screen on the top and sides. I didn't want any scratches! No bezels was the only real drawback to the monitor. Funny to think that as any other use would welcome no bezels.

Anyway, the clip I uploaded is the monitor integrated within the cabinet. I'm really happy with how it turned out and having this monitor has really took this prop a notch up.

Overall, I recommend this monitor if you are looking for a monitor with sharp viewing angles. Colors are good, no dead pixels on my screen and the price was right for the size. Other than how I use it, I can't say much more.

title: Don't fall for the fear mongering of other reviews
text: For starters always check sd cards with h2testw and if it passes that you're golden. Now, on to some other "issues" that people complain about. Formatted space of any storage will be less than the advertised, because of how storage manufacturers interpret storage space vs operating systems.  Then for the speeds, they are "up to" so check reviews that show the real transfer speeds. As for the green pcb on some of the sd cards, mine has it as well, but performance and capacity are in check, so it's just a manufacturing difference that has no implications. After all that if you still think your sd card is fake you can contact SanDisk with your sd card serial number to verify.

title: Nice keyboard, but...
text:
First the positive stuff. This keyboard is very compact and lightweight. It is very easy to use - just plug it in and go. Its battery lasts a very long time; like ,at least 12-16 hours of continuous use. The backlighting options are fun too. I like the green light, but can see how the red or blue lights would be nice in a room that is dark.

Now, the not so positive stuff. The mouse pad is super close to the keyboard, which is obviously a part of why the keyboard is compact. The problem is that my pinky hits the mouse pad often and ends up moving the cursor, sometimes causing me to delete an email i'm typing. When I'm typing an email and backspacing or using the delete key and my pinky accidently selects the email in the process, the email ends up being deleted. This is extremely annoying. Also, if I'm not looking at what I'm are typing, the cursor could end up anywhere in my document or email and then I have to figure out how to fix it. This can probably be avoided with a little time and training to keep the pinky away from the mousepad. Still, it's a pain. The mousepad should be moved above the keys or be made less sensitive.

The other big issue is that the keyboard does not register double letters. So, if you are intending to type "letters", you end up with "leters". I don't know if this is some sort of built in autocorrect feature, or if it's a product of the type of keys used but it's enough to drive one bonkers.

I would say the mouse issue is worse than the double letter thing, but they’re in close competition for being the most annoying issue with this keyboard. It's a shame because, otherwise, I really like it. I bought a full wireless keyboard with a seperate mouse. Not sure if I will return this one yet, but probably will.

With the stock cable, the sounds was very bright and tight, highs were piercing…with the upgrade cable the sound is much richer, bass improves and the sound stage is much fuller, you can hear little nuances that were non existent with the stock cable… I am very surprised
So for $16.99 is it worth it? I think so, it might not be the primary go to cable I will use with the ZS 10 Pros, but I think it will be great backup…

All manufacturers have defects but to be without this over a month and a half with no end in sight, buyers need to beware of this unit and the brand.

Despite having numerous Pioneer products over the years, this experience has been so terrible, I will NEVER buy another Pioneer product again and I recommend you steer clear of them as well.

Same as the 12" version, the unit was easy to install. The included plastic prying tool was very handy when installing and hiding the wires. The main wires you need to install/hide are usb power cable, rear/back camera video cable, and the GPS sensor cable. I had everything done in 30 minutes.

Testing:
The camera resolution was pretty good - both front and rear. you do need to adjust the front camera lens angle a bit to get a straight and leveled shoot. My highway and local street testing are both pretty clear. No shaking, no blurry, and pretty accurate color.

GPS function:
This is the main reason I bought this unit - the GPS sensor cable is long and I placed the sensor in the corner of dashboard on drivers side. It picked satellites with no problem. Now the video recordings (front and rear) all have a comprehensive driving data stamp - date, time, speed, latitude, longitude. Like it a lot. I did not need to calibrate the speed function - it is in sync with my speedometer.

All in all - very good - so far no compliant.

I will be using this one and install the prior 12” one on another car. GPS stamp on the video makes me feel much better now:-)

title: Tv works well but not the media player
text:
OK, so I've only had this for a day or so but that being said, I'm pretty impressed. Some background: I'm a cord cutter of about 4-5 years now; so, I'm fairly conversant with antennas, TV tuners, etc. I live halfway up a high rise on the upper east side of Manhattan with no line of sight to the World Trade building from whence just about every OTA (over the air) TV signal comes from. I use a Clear Steam Max-V indoor antenna purchased directly from Antennas Direst (highly recommended). This is my third (and likely last) indoor antenna and I get superb reception with it. Once in a while (like this morning), channel 2 (CBS here in NYC) will give me a problem. Now mind you the antenna is NOT connected directly to a TV but rather to a 4-5 year old 2 tuner model TabloTV box (TabloTV also highly recommended) which is then connected to my router. I tried the Tyler TV last night in the room where the Clear Stream is located. After a scan which only took a couple minutes, the Tyler picked up about 63 channels (actually more than the Tablo). Now mind you, the Tablo unit is 4-5 years old so the newer models may in fact have better tuners. I don't know. At any rate, right off the bat, I was impressed by the tuner in the Tyler unit. I didn't test all 63 channels for reception but I did test all the channels (networks) I was interested in. All of the networks (CBS, NBC, Fox, NET, etc.) came in fine. Now, you can't move around with the unit. If you do, it'll pixellate. So, I guess using this thing in a moving vehicle is probably contraindicated but then again I don't know that for sure. I did take it to other rooms in the apartment (away from windows and such) and the reception was still there, still good. I then took it down to the lobby and reception all but failed. Understandably as I was standing there under 22 floors of concrete & steel. Might as well have been in a bank vault. HOWEVER, I walked it out onto the street and the reception came right back. This morning when I tried it again, all was fine and here's the kicker: the Clear Stream couldn't pick up CBS-2 AT ALL(which has never happened before) but the Tyler could! (I don't know what the issue is with CBS-2. It might be a UHF/VHF thing or it might be weather related. As I'm typing this, there's a major storm approaching NYC from the west in which direction the Clear stream is oriented. Or, it could just be the tuner in the Tablo. I dunno.) But, to repeat, the Tyler unit had no difficulty picking up CBS! Pretty impressive, I'd say. I tried one of the other antennas on the Tyler: no change, good reception. I haven't run the unit long enough on the battery to comment on the length of the battery time. When I got the unit it must have been already partially charged 'cause it only took about 35-40 minutes to completely charge. I'm gonna take it out to a location further from the NYC transmission tower to see what happens and I'll edit this as needs be but right now I'm pretty impressed.
Update: 7/13/2020 - I took the unit to a location further from the lower Manhattan broadcast towers and as expected some of the channels were either unavailable or pixilated; however that being said it did start to pick up channels that were being broadcast from different towers; so, the bottom line is that your reception is gonna vary by locale plain and simple. Here’s why I lowered my rating: can’t get media to play on it. I tried a USB flash drive formatted as ex-Fat and a SD card formatted as Mac OS Extended. Both drives had the same MPEG-4 file (a movie without any DRM restrictions) on it. The unit wouldn’t recognize either drive. I emailed the vendor and while they were reasonably responsive in getting back to me they haven’t as yet (about 2 weeks now) gotten back to me with an answer or a fix. I’m gonna try playing with different drives formatted differently and if anything changes I’ll post it here but if you need a unit to play media you might wanna consider looking elsewhere.
Edit: final update - tried several different flash drives & SD cards formatted each differently, each with a different video (MPEG-4) file along with different photo files. Unit wouldn’t read any of the drives with any of the files. Never heard again from the vendor. Returned the unit for a refund. (Thank you, Amazon.) I suppose if all you want is a small (very small) portable TV this might work for you. And I will say that I was kinda impressed by the tuner but if you wanna play media on it, look elsewhere.

title: Pleased so far.
text:
I am reviewing these after 10 days of use.

BATTERY LIFE: By far the best battery life of any Bluetooth headset I have used over the past 3 years. They charge quickly and I used the first pair for approximately 12 hours at a fairly high volume before needing to charge them. (I use them at work and for safety reasons I can only have one earbud in place so the volume needs to be high enough that I can hear over the background work noise.) I purchased two headsets so that I could always have one charged and ready when the other battery died. These last so long and charge so fast, I probably could have purchased only one.

EARBUD SOUND QUALITY: The sound is ok for music, given the price point. I don't think it's mindblowing but I'm not looking for amazing sound here. I just want to hear music while I work and be able to make/take phone calls as necessary.

MIC SOUND QUALITY: Eh, this is why I dropped the rating to four stars. The mic can cut in and out for the person on the other end of the call. It doesn't happen all the time but it does happen more than my previous headset. It's not a deal breaker for me at this point but I will be monitoring it to see if it's getting worse and I find myself repeating what I said with more frequency.

COMFORT: The earbuds are fine in my ear. Nothing to really report here. The neckband rests comfortably as well. These will obviously be subjective based on each person's physical requirements. I will say that the neckband provides sufficient stability for using just one earbud without the earbud left dangling causing the whole headset to shift to one side. This is necessary for not having the earbud I am using pulled out of my ear or the mic pulled away from my mouth. This is also the lightest headset I've ever purchased.

RANGE: I've had headsets with longer range but that's a minor issue for me. I'm learning its limits, so if my phone is on the charger and I need to step away, I'll just make sure I put my phone in my pocket.

PAIRING: These were fairly easy to pair. Occasionally, the pairing is a little wonky and I will have to re-pair them mid-use, but I cannot say if that is an issue with the headset or my phone. Either way, it's an easy fix.

OVERALL: Are they the best headset in the world? They're one of the better ones I've purchased over the past 3 years. I tend to go through them fairly quickly with nearly constant use (minimum of 40 hours a week, often more), but by the time I need to get a new set, my old ones have been discontinued for a newer model, so I always end up shopping around. Often takes me 3 or 4 purchases before I find something I am satisfied with. I believe this will be the set I keep this time around, assuming they don't suddenly stop working in the 20 days I have left to return them.

title: Works perfectly
text:
I am extremely happy with my purchase. I have to say that I was a bit skeptical with how well this plug would work, especially with using it via Alexa, however I was pleasantly surprised. I was looking for a way to add more plugs in one area and not necessarily expecting the "Smart" feature to work well or at all. The item came quickly and packaged well. The unit itself is a bit on the large size, however it is flat so it can lay against the wall. If you have one of those outlet covers, you don't have to worry about it not being able to close. Mine closes right over the plug with no problem. There are 4 individual plugs, each of which you can program. I have not set individual scheduling times yet, however that feature does come up on the app. Currently I have 3 pond pumps running via this plug ( 145 gallons, 100 gallons, and a 20 gallon) so far so good!

There are simple instructions included but I will give you a quick run down:The plug took me about 15 mins to set up. Would have been much much shorter time, but I had mixed up my labels so I thought it wasn't working when in actuality it was powering something else on and off ( my mistake!!). Setup is a breeze (make sure you don't make the same mistake with mislabeling your plugs!!!). Download Smartlife, enter WiFi info, search Plug, plug into outlet, power off 10 secs, power back on, hold button until blue light flashes 5 secs, then wait for it to sync, and that's pretty much it. That all took maybe 5 mins. I then opened my Alexa app, went to settings, searched Smartlife, enabled sync, and was all set!! I am able to use voice command via my Echo show, Alexa App, or via the Smartlife App.

All in all I am so happy with my purchase. Would definitely reccomend.

title: Very Good Deal; Cheap Parts Mean There Is Risk That Something Won't Work
text:
This is a fantastic deal for a mid-range computer if you already have a monitor and speakers; it is not possible to build a cheaper computer with these specs from your own parts as of right now. I personally recommend you consider adding a graphics card and possibly another storage drive if you are planning to install...almost anything. The drive it comes with is small for a modern desktop computer. I used this graphics card: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01N2W8MJ9/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s01?ie=UTF8&psc=1 The computer has one PCIe expansion slot and requires a "low profile" graphics card. For the drive, there is no mount inside the case for an additional drive, but I think (think--not tested) that I see another SATA port that could be used. Personally, I may try to make another drive mount myself inside the case, but for anyone, it is very easy to get an external drive and plug it in; there are a lot of USB ports on the case! The RAM slots are completely filled, so there is not a quick way to add more (I'm not even sure the system will support more, mind). 16 GB is more than enough for standard home use.

I would not recommend this computer if you are planning to move it frequently, as the parts were not manufactured with much care. The connections from the motherboard are very cheap. On mine, most of the USB ports are slightly too small, and there is a worrying metal-on-metal sound as you try to jam something in. The HDMI port is slightly too big, and the cable falls out if it is moved. Not a lot of quality control, in other words. The mouse and keyboard are quite cheap as well. I think the scroll-wheel on the mouse will break soon. When my computer arrived, the back plate was out of place, so I had to pry it very forcefully into place to use the ports. This may or may not have happened during shipping. It also has some scratches that are extremely obviously painted over with matte paint which does not match the glossy style of the original finish. There was no dust.

So, bottom line, this computer is far cheaper than building it yourself. The parts are also cheap, which increases the risk that they may not work, so keep that in mind before ordering. It worked out for me, and I like mine a lot!

title: Makes Good On Its Promise of Simplicity
text:
This is a pretty slick plug-and-play video capture solution and I was genuinely surprised by how well it works. It's well worth the price of admission.

Packaging:
The ClearClick comes in a decently sturdy box. It includes printed instructions. So many products try to cheap-out by only hosting their instructions online, it's refreshing to have decent printed instructions included. It also comes with a Micro USB charging cable and a USB power adapter. Again, it's really nice that they included a power adapter when so many products like to cheap out and only include the cable.

What you need to provide yourself:
2 X HDMI cables (well, technically you only need one, but you're going to want two)
microSD card.

Features:
- Built-in monitor screen so you can see what you're capturing in real time - this also sort of eliminates the need for a second HDMI cable, as you could conceivably just use the built in monitor.
- Automatically adjusts capture resolution to input resolution. If you feed it a 720p source, it will capture in 720p, if you feed it 1080p it will capture in 1080p, etc...
- There's a little "cycle" button with rounded arrows which switches the device from capture to output mode so you can navigate the microSD card and play back your videos - meaning you can check the quality immediately rather than having to view the captures on a PC later on.
- Built-in battery so you don't have to constantly provide power to actually use the device.
- Encodes with H.264 and uses an MP4 container which means the videos it produces are pretty widely compatible with most reasonably current playback and editing equipment.
- Microphone input which will mix in Mic audio with the captured A/V stream so it's possible to do voice-overs during capture - more on that later.

Construction:
The box is made of hard plastic. All of the parts seem to fit together correctly. The ports all correctly line up with their slots etc... The HDMI, USB and phono ports all have a nominal amount of insertion and removal force. Nothing seems too tight or too lose. The microSD card slot is a push-push design, so in theory it should be easy to insert and remove the memory card, though in practice my larger hands have a bit of trouble installing the card because the little contour around the slot isn't wide enough for my finger to actually fit down into it, and the card slot has a little too much resistance to use a fingernail. The built in monitor is a slightly narrower aspect ratio than 16:9 so what you see on the screen appears narrower than what you're actually capturing.

Ease of Use:
All of the ports, sockets, slots and buttons are clearly labeled, so connecting and using the capture box is very straightforward. The record button has a traditional circle marking, the menu button has a traditional gear marking etc... Seriously, you can be up and capturing stuff in less than a minute after you take it out of the box. The whole process: insert a microSD card, connect input HDMI, Connect output HDMI, slide the switch over to "capture" mode and when the box boots up and shows your source on the screen, hit the circle button to start recording - that's seriously it.

The capture box will just write files to the root of whatever microSD card is inserted - there's no need to wipe the card before you insert it and it's not going to bother anything else you might already have on the card. That said, the capture box does have the ability to reformat the card for you if you like.

Options:
The device doesn't give you a ton of control over capture options, but it's not missing anything I'd call crucial. By default it records the date and time onto the video which I imagine most people will want to disable immediately. It gives you three choices for capture quality - which will have a significant impact on file sizes (and probably battery life).

Battery Life:
In my testing, the battery lasted for about 2 hours of capture.

Capture Efficiency - Size of card to length of recording
1080p video captured at 60Hz using the highest quality settings resulted in files that were about 6 minutes per GB. That works out to just over 6 hours of capture on a 64GB card.

Performance:
H.264 is about the closest thing that there has ever been to a universal standard video codec, and there are a ton of really cheap off the shelf microprocessors which can encode H.264 in hardware. Capturing in hardware makes for very fast encoding with low power requirements. I recorded several clips in 1080p at a full 60Hz framerate and this device had no trouble keeping up- there were no missed frames, no glitches, no loss of A/V sync.

That's not to say that it's perfect, however. I'm putting on my nit-picky hat here, so you shouldn't worry that the following criticisms significantly diminish this product's value. I'm more pointing out the difference between this and significantly more expensive solutions. There's a loss of color depth and plenty of artifacting during dark scenes which is typical for H.264 when using a fast encoder preset - some of the less noticeable image quality is sacrificed to maintain encoding speed. Since this device is capturing in real-time, that's almost unavoidable, and the image quality is the same as what you would get from something like OBS or other PC-based screen capture tools. What this means is that you're not going to get, say Blu-ray quality video, but it would at least be on-par with the quality you'd see on YouTube, possibly a hair better.

Testing and Results
To put this device through it's paces, I tested out several scenarios.

Test 1: capture video from an NES Classic. The NES Classic outputs 720p video and the device automatically detected and captured at that level. The video and sound all came through crisp and clear with no frame drops or audio sync issues.

Test 2: capture video from an NES Classic and use a microphone for voiceovers. The audio/video quality was identical to the first test, but it helped me to discover two things, first I need to practice more because I suck at voiceovers but more importantly, there's no way to adjust the capture volume of either the HDMI source or the microphone. In the resulting video, the sound output from the game very much overpowered the sound of my voice.

Test 3: capture video of my PC desktop. This video was 1080p @60Hz and was very smooth. Normally I use OBS or some other software-based screen recording tool and it's always a little complicated to get everything set up correctly, and the capture process is sharing resources with whatever you're doing, so if you fire up something that's process intensive, the recording and the task can interfere with one another. With the ClearClick, it was ridiculously simple to just plug the silly thing in and start recording. Again there was no stuttering, the mouse pointer didn't flicker or disappear, I didn't have to futz with certain windows being blacked out in the capture. It was just plug and play. I will probably be using this tool from now on to record how-to videos and other tutorials on my PC.

Test 4: capture video of a modern video game running in 1080p @60Hz. Again, recording was incredibly simple, and the resulting video was smooth with no artifacts or major problems. Here is where I was able to first notice some compression artifacts in very dark scenes, but the capture was still at least as good as any I've seen online.

Conclusion:
The ClearClick is a stupidly simple and elegant approach to video capture. I'm confident that even if I wasn't a technology junkie I wouldn't have any trouble operating it. It does a surprisingly good job capturing PC desktop video with the added bonus that it's not going to interfere with the performance of your PC while you're capturing. The resulting video file sizes are a little large, but they're easy enough to optimize with something like Pinnacle or Handbrake. It's a completely self-contained solution - there are no apps or logins or firmware updates, it just does one job and does it well. Update: I have noticed one annoying quirk of operation, though - it stops recording whenever it loses sync - this happens during resolution switches which severely limits usability for capturing things like retro game videos.

[Update] when trying to use this to capture video from a retro console, I stumbled across an extremely frustrating issue. It will completely stop recording whenever it loses video sync, this includes when a console is switching resolutions. Makes it impossible to capture from systems like Playstation and Saturn.

Pros:
- Completly self-contained, no accounts, no apps, no PC, no smartphone
- Comes with a USB power adapter
- Comes with printed instructions
- Plug and Play
- Battery means you can capture without external power (lasts for about 2 hours)
- Fast and high quality captures
- Has a microphone port for doing real-time voiceover

Cons:
- Stops recording whenever it loses sync (including during resolution switches)
- Micro SD slot can be annoying if you have large fingers
- Microphone capture volume can't be adjusted
- Stops recording whenever it loses sync

title: Check and confirm the product specification before you buy any product.
text:
Before my order, I compared the Huawei MediaPad M5 Lite Android Tablet with 10.1, Huawei MediaPad M5 Android Tablet with 8.4" and Samsung Galaxy Tab A 10.1 inch 128GB. Huawei MediaPad M5 Android Tablet with 8.4" has better display resolution, faster processor but smaller screen size and older Android version (8.0). Huawei MediaPad M5 Lite Android Tablet with 10.1 costs lower than Samsung Galaxy Tab A 10.1 inch 128GB but has lower storage size (32GB) and older Android version. The Samsung Galaxy Tab A 10.1 inch 128GB spec. has no RAM size listed. I checked Samsung WEB site it says 6GB RAM/128RB ROM. So I ordered the Samsung Galaxy Tab A 10.1 inch 128GB from Amazon.

After I set up the tablet and checked the storage configuration I found it has only 3GB RAM/128GB ROM so I chatted with Amazon customer support. He offered my either with a discount or return the tablet. Since I really do want the 6GB RAM (my old Asus Nexus 7 has only 1GB RAM and now runs like a snail) I returned the Samsung Galaxy Tab A 10.1 inch 128GB and ordered it from Samsung and hope I will own a 6GB RAM tablet. After setting up the new tablet agin I found it only has 3GB RAM with 128GB storage. So I went back to check the Samsung WEB site Samsung Galaxy Tab A 10.1 inch tablet spec. Surprise, previously the spec. was 2GB RAM/32GB ROM(storage), 4GB RAM/64GB ROM, 6GB RAM/128GB ROM, and now it is 2GB RAM/32GB ROM, 3GB RAM/64GB ROM and 3GB RAM/128GB ROM. Also the price for the 128GB version has being lowered. Amazon also lowered the 128GB version price. So I returned the Samsung order and reordered it from Amazon again(because I have some unused Amazon coupon balance) even this new Amazon order price is higher than the discount the Amazon customer support offered to me previously.

To the tablet itself. The screen is large and crisply clear. Even it does not have the highest resolution, it is still very good. The response time is very fast. The storage size is generous (128GB). If it is not for the confused RAM/Storage size spec. issue, I will give it 5-star review. And even it has only 3GB RAM, if its spec. is clearly specified at the beginning, I will still consider to buy it because It has offered the best choice in this price range.

As to the customer support. Both Amazon and Samsung online chat supports are great. Fast and responsive. Amazon support is especially great. The support staff is very courteous and offer solutions on the customer's stand.

The plan was to use it as an office 4k 60Hz monitor which also provides power, Ethernet and USB-A for this laptop. Happy to report that everything works as planned and as they described - I plug exactly one USB-C cable to my macbook and it gets power, monitor, wired network, keyboard, mouse and couple of transient USB devices like phones through USB hub. There are two things you'll have to do though.
1. Make sure you have USB 2.0 enabled in the monitor settings, this is actually default. USB 3.2 will limit your refresh rate to 30Hz and it's awful.
2. Get a better USB-C <-> USB-C cable. Unfortunately Philips screwed this up. They throw a cheap one to the box and it can't provide enough bandwidth to pass 4k@60Hz - you'll be stuck with those 30Hz. I've used another one, from my USB-C external SSD drive, and it work perfectly.

There is no need to install any drivers, hack anything or click anything while holding magic buttons. macOS recognized it immediately and you can choose default or scaled resolution up to full 4k as you wish, just like with built-in display. title: Good if you don't care about quality
text:
Upgraded my old camera and wanted a quick kit for a trip I am going on so I got this. Upon arrival I was excited to try everything out, had been picking things out individually and it was getting pretty pricey. Found this kit and figured I would give it a shot. It will be fine for a weekend, but there are many you will need to upgrade overtime.

The 0.43x Macro/Wide Angle lens is the best thing in this kit. Attached to a 200mm lens it takes really good macro shots. With more tweaking of settings I could see myself using this a lot.

The 2.2x Telephoto lens I couldn't get to work correctly. All my images came out blurry no matter what I tried. But I will have to play around with it some more, maybe my lighting was bad, it was an overcast day when I tried it out.

Backpack seems pretty decent, though I was hoping it was a little bigger to fit the tripod inside. The Tripod itself is VERY cheaply made, I don't really know if I trust it to hold my camera without falling apart.

Starter Cleaning Kit is a nice kit of stuff. The mini tripod buckles under the weight of the camera though if you have a lens on it, even the standard one. Not really sure the point of it.

Lens Hood Fits good, did it's job fine.

Did Not Test
Commander 3PC Filter Kit - Should Work Fine, No need to test
Commander 4 Pcs Macro Close-Up Kit - Other macro works great, didn't need these but might help with sharpness.
Memory Card Reader - Looks like cheap plastic, should work
Commander Wired Remote
Extra Battery (Generic)
Extra AC/DC Car/Home Worldwide Battery Charger
Commander Hand Grip Strap
Air Blower - No need yet
Lens Cap Keeper - Have a few lenses, got pockets for that.
USB Cable - It's a cable.

Missing Items
1 Sandisk 32GB Memory Card. Only got one, kit says it was supposed to come with 2. One I got was only 48MB/S anyways though, fine for photos but I like faster when I do video.
Cleaning Brush. - Got the Air Blower at least, but no brush pen.

tl;dr - Good kit if you need these things quick and don't mind cheap quality. Some items are pretty sturdy and do a good job though, so it all depends what your main focus is. But the main things I was looking for in the kit aren't up to standards I was looking for.

title: Every Car is Different
text:
Any serious audio enthusiast will tell you that the listening room is as important as the equipment. Rooms in homes can be tweaked, treated, rearranged to make the equipment sound better and integrate the speakers. Cars, not so much.
That's why I looked for an installer that had specific experience with Subaru Foresters, and asked them to recommend speakers in my price range. And that's how I ended up with these Focals, which really do sound spectacular in my 2015 Forester.
Every car is different. The size and angle of the windshield has a direct effect on up-firing tweeters installed in the dash, as does the amount of glass all around. The volume of the door cavity, and how far forward and how near the floor the speaker location is, directly effects bass extension and midrange projection. The shape and volume of the car's interior, the type of upholstery, the number of passengers... it all has an effect.
How can I know if other speakers would have sounded better? Without sitting in other Foresters with different systems, I can't. I do know how much better these sound than the factory speakers: worlds better. The difference between, say, average portable computer speakers and a very good hi-fi bookshelf speakers.
They are accurate to the source (as I can tell by playing a sampling of my own recordings). They add no perceptible distortion at normal volume. Their bass extension goes well into the bottom octave of a bass guitar or double bass, although it falls off by the lowest note. But there are no distortions or false overtones, no booming.
The high end is extended and clean (and will therefore reveal the flaws in low-bitrate streams and rips). I don't know the exact crossover frequency, but it's low enough to help pull the stereo image up off the floor and place it mostly in front of you. Midrange remains balanced and integrated, and only minor tweaks of my 10-bang EQ seem needed to dial the sound right in.
So are these the right speakers for you and your car? They could be. They are certainly high-quality, capable speakers that have great potential in the right vehicle. They will appeal to the listener who values accuracy and doesn't want speakers that add their own quality to the music. But if you can find an installer with extensive experience with your specific car and get a recommendation, you might benefit.

title: Too Dim. I Expected So Much More!
text:
I want to love this projector but I can't. This is a potentially great planetarium projector. There are things I really like about it but several things I dislike. I wanted to buy a star projector for my new baby's room and I purchased the Bliss Lights Sky Lite Projector. I loved it except that the stars are green (?) and the star patterns don't seem random or natural. I wasn't able to find many of these projectors that had white or even yellow stars. That's when I found the Sega Homestar Flux. Here are the Pros and Cons:

Pros:
- Accuracy. It has a disc included with a representation of the galaxy that is pretty accurate.
- The stars are white and not some odd colors.
- Though a bit weak I do like the comet feature.
- Subtle light. The projector has a light that is not overly bright. Even my wife who can't sleep with any lights on can fall asleep with this on.
- Auto Shut Off. It shuts off after 3 hours (but you can set it for a shorter time) which is great so you don't waste power if you fall asleep.
- Relaxing. A great way to relax and unwind especially if you pair it with the right kind of music.
- Sega offers numerous discs for the Homestar Flux.

Cons:
- Way too expensive. At $180-$200 this projector should wow me. I'd rather spend 75% less on a laser projector that is far brighter.
- Too Dim. As I said before the light from the projector is not overpowering which is fine in some instances however after I saw a video review stating that its 5 watt light was noticeably brighter than the classic version's 3 watt bulb I was ready to be impressed. It was very much a disappointment when I turned it on. Compared to the Bliss Lights Sky Lite Projector the Homestar Flux is very dim. I intended to use the Flux in tandem with my Sky Lite Projector to add a white starfield. Even on the dimmest setting for the Sky Lite it drowned out the Homestar Flux so you cannot use them together.
- Smaller Field of view. When compared to the Bliss Lights Sky Lite Projector the amount of coverage for the Homestar Flux was easily 20-30% less. The Sky Lite Projector covers the ceiling and about 2 feet down my walls in my 16'x18' bedroom whereas the Flux only covers the ceiling from the same spot. This was also very disappointing.

Overall:
My impulse was to return the Homestar Flux however I kept it because my wife likes it and can sleep with it on and I got it using Amazon gift cards (didn't cost me any money). With that said I believe Sega could improve this by 1) making it much brighter, 2) giving you low, medium & high settings for the light projection intensity; the highest setting should be twice as bright as it is now with the current lighting level being the lowest setting, 3) lowering the price to around $100. Someone else said this and I agree. If you could somehow combine the Sega Homestar Flux with the Bliss Lights Sky Lite Projector into one device you would have a great product.

Conclusion:
If at all possible before you decide to buy this product try to see one for yourself and also look at some laser projectors since many of them have better price points. If you want an accurate representation of the galaxy and the ability to view other discs of planets, constellations, etc. for educational purposes or to set a relaxing mood in your home and can afford it then this is your machine.
