title: Great Monitor for the Price
text:
I’ve been using this monitor a little over a week now, and my experience has been great so far. I previously had an older 720p portable monitor that was in dire need of an upgrade. Now that I work from home permanently, I spend a lot of time working from my kitchen table and a single monitor just won’t do and a standard monitor is too bulky and requires too many cords. I did quite a lot of research to find a suitable replacement that wouldn’t break the bank. Here are my thoughts:

Positives:
• True 1080p display with a very crisp image.
• Can be powered through the laptop USB-C port, though a separate charging cable is included if your laptop can’t handle it. I would think most laptops with USB-C should be able to.
• Very bright backlight, even when powered through the laptops USB-C port. I did think brightness was a concern when I first powered it on as it was fairly dim and the brightness setting said it was at 100. After messing around with the other settings and modes, it turns out it’s actually brighter than my laptop.
• There is a built in settings button. My previous portable display didn’t have this, but is very nice to have.
• Several connection types available. USB-C and USB-C to USB 3 are probably preferred since they don’t require additional power, but there is also a mini-HDMI port and an included mini-to-Standard HDMI cable. I have to use this to connect it to my 2015 MacBook Air, but this option does require the external power cable.
• Surprisingly thin and light.

Negatives:
• Sits a little low compared to my laptop, and there’s not an easy way to adjust the height with the included case/stand.
• It seems like when it’s plugged in through USB-C, it can’t quite figure out to turn off the display once the laptop screen goes blank from inactivity. I’m not sure if this is a screen issue or more to do with the settings on my laptop, but I haven’t really looked into it and I just unplug the usb cord at the end of the day, so not really a huge deal either way.

Overall, I am very pleased with this purchase, but will report back if anything changes.

I contacted Amazon because this item is basically still new-ish, given it went through no wear and tear at all and the use of it had been infrequent, and they told me to contact the manufacturer, Logitech. I've contacted Logitech and I'm waiting for them to get back to me, but fully expect the typical run around many manufacturers give you to avoid replacing a faulty product. For the price, this item should NOT be junk. But apparently, that's what I got.

Will update once I hear back from Logitech.

title: Know what you're getting into
text:
This is stacking case with integrated cooling for 6 Pi boards. There isn't much room for hats, and GPIO access is very limited. That said, it was a good match for my first multi-board project, and I went for it. The materials can be brittle, and like some other reviewers, my kit arrived with some breakage. Kudos to C4Labs, who sent me replacements via priority mail as soon as I contacted them.

Assembly is difficult, and made more so because the parts themselves aren't clearly marked in a way that helps you orient them. I had the entire case together before I realized that I had the side panels reversed, which meant taking it all apart again. What helped me during assembly was to use cellophane tape to hold pieces in place; it was still a challenge to build it, took a lot of patience and trial-and-error.

I'm happy with the results, although I probably would go with their larger case offering if I was starting over, because of the GPIO access. But it all came together, and I now have a kubernetes cluster on my desk.

title: Very Nice Wireless Earbuds for the Price!
text:
I recently upgraded my iPhone, which no longer has a separate jack for the supplied head phones. Since I keep the phone in a battery case (for backup battery), the USB connection will not work with the iPhone supplied wired earbuds. So I went onto Amazon in search of wireless earbuds, with no intention on spending big bucks for Apple Air pods, Bose or Samsung pods or buds, etc. I wanted something functional and inexpensive, but not cheap in quality or function. I found these little jewels for a little over $30, and I'm happy I did.

Sound quality? Very nice for the price. At high volume which is high enough for me, there is little distortion. I probably would like a bit more bass, but it's acceptable and the mid and high-range sounds are very good.

Fit and quality? Nice. They stay in my ears just fine. They come from the factory with the smallest ear caps installed, and I changed them out to the next size up. Fit nice and snug, but very comfortable and no issue with irritation. The buds are solid and appear well constructed. No annoying LED light flashing like some of the other options out there. I fly quite a bit, and nothing is more annoying that seeing people's devices flashing different colors. There is a tiny LED on each earbud to indicate status, but nothing annoying. Best of all, they have a low profile and fit almost flush with my ears. I didn't want earbuds that stuck out 1/4" to 1/2" like many out there, and you can barely tell they are in your ears looking head on. I like that, as well as not having a dongle hanging down like Air pods and similar.

The mic? It's fine. Haven't had any complaints from callers hearing me, but I really haven't put them to the test in a noisier environment than my home office. So maybe I'll update this review at some point with that info, or if something changes.

Pairing was easy, and I've paired them with both my iPhone and my iPad. Touch control is both nice and a bit of a curse. If you try to adjust the fit in your ears it's easy to bump the touch pads and change whatever you were listening to. But you get used to handling them around the edges. The touch functionality is nice and simple to use and remember.

Noise cancellation? Hard to say. I will note that if you fit them well to your ear canal that in itself is enough cancellation. I'm still playing with the best size ear cap to provide best fit and sound quality. I noticed that if you press the earbuds in slightly while in your ears, the bass sounds improve. Release that pressure, and you lose the better bass sound. So that is why I am playing with the different ear caps. Again, the fit is great, they don't fall out of your ears, and do not irritate my ears after wearing for a couple of hours.

Finally, the charging case. I like it. It is small in footprint, earbuds fit in snugly and the magnets they use to hold the buds in and the lid closed is perfect. The case has an indication of charge level, and my guess is that you'll get a few charges out of this case. It has the USB connection in, but not out so you can't use the case for charging other devices, like your phone. I don't care about that feature. I have other battery banks to do that. What was important to me was the charging of my earbuds and size and quality of the case, which I think we have a winner here. I did not test out the water-proof functionality.

Trust me. I did a lot of searching and compare on Amazon, including reading all the negative reviews on each comparable product. These earbuds had not only great reviews, but only a few negatives which I didn't find impactful or overly harsh. If you're in the $30 - $50 market for wireless earbuds, give these a serious look!

title: Fantastic budget notebook which can be upgraded with M.2 SSD.
text:
The Swift 1 SF114-32 offers exceptional battery life, has an elegant slim chassis, has decent performance, and a quality 14" 1080p IPS screen. This notebook has some impressive components and very good performance at an unbeatable price. While there definitely are some trade-offs versus other higher end notebooks this size, it is a great value.

Pros of this notebook include:
* Chassis is made completely of aluminum.
* Relatively fast performance with 64 gb eMMC flash storage.
* M.2 SATA SSD can be added.
* Significantly better performance than previous budget notebooks not based on Core processors.
* Bezels around the screen are relatively thin.
* Very good 1080p IPS screen. Good viewing angles. Outstanding contrast (1923:1). No PWM flickering.
* It is the size of most 13.3”notebooks and it weighs less than 3 lbs.
* Fantastic battery life (I get 12 – 14 hours when using wifi).
* Great range of ports for a smaller and thin notebook.
* Fantastic 2x2 WiFi performance with top of the line Intel wireless card (9650 - includes AC).
* Bluetooth 5.0. 800 ft. range!
* Large (3"x4") touchpad which performs very well.
* Nice keyboard with very little flex (though short travel).
* Does not get too warm even when running stress test.
* Runs quietly. Only passive cooling used.
* Speakers sound good even at full volume but are not very loud (common in notebooks this size).
* Fingerprint reader.
* Type C USB.

Cons of this notebook include:
* Small 64 gb eMMC flash storage. Though this can and should be supplemented with M.2 SSD.
* Windows 10 S. Limits software you can run on notebook. Upgrading to 10 Pro was painless, did not cost anything, and went relatively fast.
* Not a very bright screen (240 cd/m²).
* The ram runs in single-channel mode. Having it in double-channel mode would have added some performance.
* SD card reader transfer speeds are mediocre. I was getting 25 – 38 MB/s. They are adequate enough to play h265 1080p videos from SD card though.

All in all I'm very happy with this notebook. I feel it is quite the bargain at $305. There really is no other notebook at this cost with these kind of specs (not to mention chasis is aluminum and it can be upgraded with M.2 SSD) The N5000 gives a significant boost in performance over other budget notebooks and the processor comes close to the Core-i3 processors of the Broadwell generation in performance. While the screen is not as bright as it could be I'm very happy with how it looks and contrast is amazing. The icing on the cake is the fact that you can add more storage (and faster) to the notebook. I added a 500 gb SSD, cloned the eMMC drive, and then made the SSD my primary drive. It is significantly faster and I have a lot more space. I have installed Linux Elementary OS on eMMC drive and can now dual boot to either OS.

title: Good for $80, with a couple of flaws
text:
This is a more than decent sounding set of (almost) over the ear headphones that do NOT feature active noise cancellation. They isolate from outside sound, and they do a better than passable job of it. More than adequate for most users. Materials quality seems high and they are cleanly manufactured with no cheap-looking parts or rough edges.
Volume levels are plenty for my taste. You can have enough bass and volume to make your eyes vibrate and your ears ring. I can't relate to the people who state these have no volume in their reviews. Perhaps it's a difference in the source we're listening from. 90% of the time I'm listening to Spotify on my Galaxy S9, so not top quality audio, but still with these JBL's the notes ring out well in the mid-range and high registers. Bass responses can be clean, but if you get too much bass guitar mixed in with a lot of bass drum and the notes are coming fast, these 'phones get muddy on the low end. I give them a 3 for sound, which is great, IMO, for the $80 price tag.
The EQ fails to impress, but it's better than nothing. The presets in the app are worthless for my music, primarily modern and classic rock, blues and metal. Tinkering with the EQ helps, but I set several presets myself with widely varied patterns and could still switch between them with no discernible change in sound. How does that work? But still, for the money, they're getting it done.
The big deal breaker for me is that the housing of the cans themselves creak and pop every time I turn my head. I examined both sides and could find nothing apparent that would explain why they were popping. No warped parts, no breaks or cracks or missing pieces. They're just noisy due to their construction, as near as I can tell. An additional gripe is that once in my 6 hours of testing, they cut themselves off. I was walking and wearing them and they just stopped, even played the power-off tone. Opened the app and it said battery was 100% (after 2 hours of listening, so I have my doubts on that as well). I turned them on again and resumed listening for another hour without incident.
Which brings me to my last gripe. They aren't as comfortable as I would like. They're decent, but they do NOT go over my ears. They sit on my ears, and push in on my earlobes, and after about 20 minutes, adjustments must be made.
In the end, most electronics have quirks. The quirks I attribute to these JBLs can be lived with if decent sound and saving cash are your top priorities. My Sony WH-1000xm3s are the best out there currently. But they're at best, $200 more than these. You just can't have all the Sonys offer for 1/4th the cost. However, if these are in your budget, you could do a lot worse.

title: quality waterproof binoculars at a reasonable price
text:
Nikon Action EX 10x50 binoculars produce a beautiful, clear image at daylight, dusk or night. They feel solidly-built, weigh a hefty 34.2 oz and are waterproof and fogproof, which adds to the cost. The eyecups twist in for viewing while wearing glasses and twist out for viewing with bare eyes. These have a focusing ring and a diopter ring so you can focus left and right eyes individually. The lens caps can be attached to the included neck strap.
These binoculars satisfied my requirement of 10x50 binoculars with good quality optics for beginning astronomy. While Jupiter was at opposition during June 2019, I could see Jupiter and four of its moons with these binoculars, but with my old 7x35 binoculars, I could see only one of the moons.
If you don't need 10x magnification, consider the Action EX 7x50 model.

title: So far so good, has some quirks
text:
This is definitely a good "for the price" monitor, I use it for my recording studio and general internet with a top-of-the-line 2017 MacBook Pro. I thought this monitor was an especially good deal because the 2 TB3 ports and 2 USB ports spared me having to spend another $200 on a hub for all of the outboard gear I need to use with the MacBook. Interesting issue I had was a pretty bad hiss/crackle through the headphone port of my MacBook when it was plugged into the "laptop" Thunderbolt port on the back on the monitor. Looks like there has been a problem with headphone jacks/power supply interference with MacBooks for 10+ years, so this might not be the monitor's fault. I switched the laptop to the other Thunderbolt port and the noise went away. The MacBook is still charging via the other Thunderbolt port, so not sure what's going on with all that. The SSD I now have plugged into the "laptop" Thunderbolt port still works as expected and I don't notice anything odd like extra heat or anything. Fingers crossed I'm not setting myself up for a failure of some sort, I prefer my gear, especially brand new stuff, to be setup to spec, but again, for the price...

Update 12/23/20: There’s a headphone jack on the back of the monitor (duh). I ran my audio line out of there and there’s no interference with the MacBook Pro when it’s plugged into the 90w TB3 port on the monitor.

title: Amazing sound; superb customer service.
text:
I can’t say enough good things about this speaker and the experience I had with the vendor’s customer service.

The sound quality is amazing. As others have said, if you control the volume from your phone, you can really get it cranking. Also, very crisp and full sound. Gone are the days of big cabinet stereo systems, but this little guy fills that gap perfectly.

After about nine months, I started getting a single “busy signal” beep every two or three minutes. The speaker was fully charged - plugged in, in fact. I did some research and it sounds like the battery dies for some people. Some folks replace it themselves but accessing the battery is not easy.

Amazon put me in touch with the vendor since it has been so long since I bought it. I emailed them and told them what was happening and they replied and told me to make sure it was charged; I told them that it was and it was still doing the beeping sound. I also told them how much I loved the speaker and really hoped I could get it fixed.

So a few days went by and I didn’t get any response from them and I really wasn’t too worried about it. Next thing I know, I get a brand new speaker in the mail! If works perfectly with no beep! I was past the warrantee window and they replaced it anyway. So, top notch customer service, to say the least.

I’ve had had one or two other experiences with vendors replacing a faulty product. You really can’t ask for better than that when it comes to customer service.

I gave it two stars for the battery because, well, the battery in the first one started dying after a few months. If you happen to experience that problem, reach out the vendor (if it’s past the Amazon return window) and they should take care of you.

text: This is the third shower speaker I bought so far. I had great hope in this one considering it had a lot of great reviews and a great quantity of it as well. I was so excited to use this one when it came to my house and as soon as I opened it I, of course, read the user manual (and noticed the free warranty card in the box which you should use if you recently bought it) and realized I had to charge it for 4 hours until it really could be used. It was no big deal for me since I always take showers at night but after connecting it to my desktop, the speaker wouldn't skip any songs from my Spotify playlist which was strange. A simple turn off and on of the speaker did the trick and it could skip nevertheless it was worrying. So here I am listening to my jam in my shower and suddenly the speaker loses its suction and drops on my shower floor. This gave me a heart attack because upon reading the user manual, it explicitly states "Do not use the unit if it as been dropped or damaged in any way." (Typo included). The speaker was still fine but if you put it on max, the audio begins to cut off and come back on which was very annoying especially considering its happening on the first day I even got it. Also, the Bluetooth connectivity of the speaker was a bit weak since putting it behind the running water makes it cut out even though there are 10 feet between my desktop and the speaker as well as 2 doors. So much for the "10 meter" range the product claims. I am very sad and will probably never buy a shower speaker after this one because I am on the verge of returning this disappointing piece of plastic. Other people may have it lucky with their purchase but I'm pretty sure I'm forever cursed with forbidden shower speakers which is really a sad day for me.

The left side is the where the LTE SIM slot should be, right under the volume button. Similarly-looking to the SD slot, the LTE slot should have a tiny pinhole to eject the tray. Mine had a "blank" cover (no pinhole). I thought that perhaps TekZilla just put a cover on since the previous owner may have lost the original, however that's not the case. This tablet/laptop doesn't have the HP drivers loaded on it, so I downloaded and tried to install the HP Snapdragon X5 LTE driver (yes, from HP's Support website) - The install FAILED saying there is NO LTE device! TekZilla simply emailed me back saying "Sorry, but there is LTE". Bottom line is that the tablet/laptop they sent me doesn't have LTE. My lesson learned, your warning as a buyer.

title: Works as advertised
text:
Have now brought my Z2 SGP521 back to life! After cracking my original display (changing battery), my Z2 just sort of sat on the shelf until I came back Stateside. Installation is easy enough, there are plenty of YouTube videos How-To. I was just over zealous on removing the back third of the original.

The package was delivered promptly, and I can say the seller packaged it extremely well! Just remind yourself to be very careful unpackaging it. Don't go gorilla crazy when you unwrap the 10 feet of bubble wrap (not to include the shipping box). Also ensure you make a good attempt at cleaning out the previous adhesive. I used a spudgie and some alcohol and did the best I could. Technically you should disconnect the battery first, but hey, I live dangerously.

Connect the display cable and ensure the display works before putting new adhesive tape on. Important as the seller will not accept a return if it looks like you stuck it on first, then discovered it didn't work or have bad pixels. Mine was dead pixel free. If anybody remembers some of the first generation Z2 tabs had horrible pixel deterioration (like mine, I just lived with it).

While your display is active, lift it up and sort of move it around a little to insure your display cable didn't get damaged. I thought mine was and ordered a new one, but didn't need it anyhow. After verifying all is well, power down and install the new adhesive tape. Ensure the camera holder is in the proper position. Start at the bottom and after seating the bottom, gently lay the display down to ensure all 4 edges are seated properly, then press it in place. Again, don't go gorilla on it.

I can't tell if the new screen is of same vividness as the original, but it looks pretty good.

text: The company I work for bought me a Precision 7530 and a TB18DC dock.  The laptop is great.  The dock, no so much.  The dock is supposed to supply power to the laptop. The connector is two USB C plugs in one connector.  If bumped or tugged, it comes loose and you have to play the plug/unplug game again. title: Review of Akaso V50X - Pretty good value
text:
This is for the Akaso V50X only, with firmware from June 2019 V1 after testing for a few hours within a day of receipt of the camera. The camera works as described. Many options to adjust the picture quality. The underwater case worked in a poo, testing in the ocean will occur early next year, the reason for the purchase primarily. One thing they should have is a dust cover for the SD card and USB connectors, without the dust cover anything can get in there, I will likely put some tape there. Also, the SD cards absolutely must be formatted in the camera and not on a PC, the camera won't recognize the format and require you to reformat the card anyway. Also, if you try to use your camera formatted card in an Apple MAC memory card slot reader it will not recognize the format either. In order to copy the files from the SD card to the Apple computer (I did not test with any other type of computer) is to use a memory card to USB adapter and then the computer will recognize the external drive. You can also connect the camera to the computer with the SD card installed in the camera.

One other area that I think needs improvement is a better way to get the SD card in and out of the slots, us with bigger fingers will have problems, I used a dime which seemed a good thickness to help with this process.

Secondly, one software feature that would be handy is to allow for the video or picture to be taken upside down and flipped upright with an option so that using a monopod or selfie stick the shot can be taken with the camera mounted below the stick upside down.

Lastly, with the case in the waterproof enclosure and underwater there is no way to make camera setting changes, the camera has to come out of the enclosure or be above water for the remote or phone app to make a connection. I think a settings button available to the waterproof case and use of the up and down buttons would help here because there are times the lighting conditions underwater change and a setting change is required.

Overall, the camera performed quite well and as described and for the price is a great deal and with all the extra mount tools the only extra add on items you need are SD cards and maybe a monopod or selfie stick.

Great item and great idea to save and use an old security system that was $2000-$3000 to install.

text:
[[VIDEOID:cd76701c36e5180e43477a045c02c49e]] [The Disclaimer]
I am not an average user, I opted to not use the Side Mounted Inferred Lights, not because I think they are bad, but because I had a unique use for my project.

[The Review]
I have purchased a few lenses for my raspberry Pi's as I have worked on home security camera's for a few years now on the side. I have to say this one is my favorite. The angle is nice and wide which gives it better exposure and a better view, but the picture isn't so wide that it turns into a fish eye image which I like.

[My application]
I mounted mine in a dummy camera, did not have enough room in that chassis to put the the inferred light into which wasn't a big deal for me.

[Side Note/Details about Side Mounted Inferred Lights]
Side note, though I have not personally used these EXACT side mounted inferred (I know I called it Ultra Violet by mistake in the video, my bad) lights I have used this exact design a few times with other lenses and they work good. They push out a lot of light but they have their disadvantages to. The inferred lights get super hot, so keep that in mind if you are going to use an adhesive on them, OR you plan on keeping them someone near flammables in a hot and dry climate. They have a red dim light on them when they are in use (The sensor almost always has them running unless its really bright in the room) so if you are going for a stealth look I would recommend external inferred lights which is what I am using. The last disadvantage to these lights is they use very small bolts/nuts and need to be tighten delicately and evenly to get the best results. If you do not, you can have troubles with keeping a good connection but if tighten well and evenly they will stay on there and will NOT wiggle out.

If you use MotionEye OS like I do you are able to get better frame rates with Raspberry Pi Zero's W after tweaking a few settings so the video doesn't give the best representation of the motion capture of the lens.

title: This Lens is REALLY Good...
text:
I'll start by saying that I wasn't planning to like this lens. My main gripe when this lens was announced was that it wasn't an 11-24mm or a 12-24mm. While I would like Nikon to eventually release a wider lens, I've come around to the belief that they found a great balance in this lens.

The lens weighs next to nothing and doesn't take up much space in the bag thanks to its compact design that gets even smaller when you set the zoom to its storage mode (basically retracts the lens completely). Despite this, the actual build feels pretty solid and I can attest that the weathersealing is excellent. The main thing that really makes this lens stand out is the ability to take standard 82mm circular filters. As of this writing, this is the only ultra-wide zoom on the market that boasts both 14mm on the wide end and the ability to use standard circular filters. Tally up these things and it's probably the most practical ultra-wide angle zoom on the market.

All of this would mean little without performance and we come to a bit of a mixed bag here. In terms of sharpness, the 14-30mm f/4 S seems to be sharper across the frame at all apertures than the 14-24mm f/2.8G and it makes the 16-35mm f/4G look like a complete joke. The coatings do an excellent job at retaining contrast and mitigating flare. The color rendition is very accurate (images accompanying this review are uploaded with no color correction using the Camera Neutral profile). I haven't found any notable chromatic aberration to speak of either. That brings us to vignette and distortion.

You know that saying that "You can't have your cake and eat it, too."? With every lens, there's going to be some sort of trade-off. Generally speaking, high quality, well-corrected optics will result in the trade-off of a large and heavy lens. While this lens is razor sharp and excels in many optical aspects, the compact design of the lens meets its trade-off in the form of significant optical distortion and vignetting. People who use Lightroom probably won't even notice this because Nikon has worked with Adobe to automatically apply a software correction to the RAW file upon import to fix the distortion and vignette (I'd guess that it's about 2 stops at its most extreme on the wide end), but you'll definitely notice both if you're using any other RAW conversion software. So we have a bit of a controversy here. If the distortion and vignette is corrected automatically upon import in the software so you wouldn't even notice it, does it matter?

In my opinion, yes, it does. The reason is because any corrections that you're doing in software rather than optically is going to require interpolation of the data on your sensor and it will inevitably lead to SOME loss of quality. The same can be argued about the vignette where locally fixing it leads to less dynamic range able to be captured in those portions of the image. If you have a Z7 like I have, then the loss of quality is likely not noticeable for most purposes, but it's there and it needs to be acknowledged. Having said this, one can argue whether optical distortion or even a strong vignette are necessarily bad things. I know it sounds pretty stupid to say, but unless you're using this lens to shoot architecture, real estate (like I do), or other subjects with really straight lines, you're not really likely to notice even moderate levels of distortion or vignette as real world scenes are complex enough to mask those types of flaws. If you ARE shooting straight lines, then you're either going to have to live with software correction or look elsewhere. For me, the size, weight, and 82mm filter thread still make this lens much more desirable than a larger, better corrected lens. Admittedly, I cheat the system here by having a sensor with far more megapixels than I'm likely to ever actually need.

So why am I giving this lens 5 stars despite these flaws? There's a physical reality that you have to deal with for every lens. Because of this, I believe in judging a lens based on what it's intended to be and what the value of the overall package is. In this case, we have a lens that's extremely sharp, has excellent resistance to flare and CA, possesses great color rendition, is light weight, is compact, and can take standard circular filters while reaching 14mm on the wide end. This is an extremely high quality, 5-star package that's unprecedented in its combination of features. Yes there are flaws, but the only way to realistically solve those flaws would be to make the lens bigger, heavier, and likely remove the ability to take those circular filters. In my opinion, that's the realm of Nikon's upcoming 14-24mm f/2.8 S lens, not this one. This is going to be a choice between functionality (this lens) vs. unparalleled optical quality (a much bigger and heavier lens). I can definitely say that Nikon is making the decision a very interesting one by releasing such a good 14-30mm f/4.

text:

I am an IT professional, and usually find the iPad built-in software keyboard adequate for the many tasks I perform on the iPad. Where the built-in keyboard does not work quite as well is for a terminal emulation where you are accessing a computer/server remotely and want to be able to see as much of the screen as possible. Now on trips where I really don't want to lug around my full-sized notebook, I can perform every task I need to support my customers using the iPad and this great keyboard.

I haven't had it long enough to talk about durability or battery life, but it seems very well made and also seems to hold the charge very well. The keyboard automatically shuts down when you fold it closed, which certainly helps preserve the power and the folding of the keyboard to pack it away is a lot more intuitive than a switch on the side somewhere.

Also, this allows me to keep my more "stylish" iPad cover without changing to any of the cases where the keyboard is built-in. I've tried cases with the keyboard built-in, but they add weight and come with other limitations, when my need for an external keyboard is actually much less frequent than my need for a nice, lightweight iPad.

I give this keyboard an exceptional recommendation. I will provide updates on how it holds up over time.

text:
The only issue when I was trying to clone my HDD to this SDD was the SDD was not formatted for GPT to MBR or vice a versa, can't recall. So the cloning software would not do the process. Had to put SSD in another computer as a secondary and go into Disk mgmt and do this procedure. The cloning software will tell you what the SSD needs to be converted to if it needs it. This is just an example but do your research and choose the right format conversion. Example: How to initialize a disk drive using GPT
Click Start, type diskmgmt.msc in the Start search box.
Right-click diskmgmt.msc and click Run as Administrator.

Note: When a non-initialized disk is detected by Windows, select the Disk, choose GPT (GUID Partition Table) and click OK.
Verify that the disk status is Online, else right-click and select Initialize disk.
If the disk is already initialized, right-click on the label on the left and click Convert to GPT Disk.
Once the disk has been initialized, right-click the unallocated space and click New Simple Volume and follow the steps to complete the process.

After getting this process done it was smooth sailing from there. This SSD is pretty fast and along with memory upgrade i have increased benchmarks by 150%. Good luck.....

The first image shows the exact same area before the light comes on. The second and third photo show that area with the light on. The motion detection works very well. There are three settings:

1) Leave the light on from dusk to dawn
2) Leave the light in night-light mode after dusk and have it come on fully when it detects motion
3) Leave the light off until it detects motion. After dusk, once motion is detected, it will come on fully

Honestly the only odd thing I found is the switches that you have to use to change between these three modes. Instead of having a normal switch, this uses pushbuttons that are under the plastic. There are tiny pin-size access holes above each of the three switches. The light comes with a pin that appears to be slightly thinner than a paper clip that you use to slide into one of the holes so you can press the button. The second thing I notice is that the drive is much noisier than my old Seagate drive. It reminds me of those old school external hard drives that were essentially internal drives in cases. I also notice some lag time sometimes when I try to access a file and I have to listen to it wind up like a turbine engine before Explorer or my software can unfreeze and get to the file. This is probably my biggest complaint and I wish I had researched this more.
None of these negative features have made me deeply regret my purchase. I do have twice as much storage space now and the drive does look nice. I've also lugged this thing all over in my laptop bag and it seems to be holding up okay, so it seems relatively durable.
I will replace this as my primary work drive at some point because of the lag time but I will happily keep it as a backup drive.

UPDATE 07/05/19
I began having some reliability issues with this drive. It failed the Drive Check in WD Drive Utilities on more than one computer so after six months of use it looks like I need to replace it. My next drive will be a Seagate.

title: Seems good, with some quirks
text:
Pretty does what it says. I don't use it regularly since I view it as just something I need in case of emergency. But I have noticed two things with my unit.

One is that the blue battery level lights seem inconsistent. For example, I was playing the radio with all 4 lights lit. Turned on the light and it showed just 3. Turned everything off and then the radio right back on and it was back to 4.

A bigger issues is that the battery lights seem to wipe out AM radio. Every time any of those blue lights are on, I just get a lot of static even if it was already set to a local station. As soon as the blue lights go out, the station can be heard. Since it takes 30 seconds or slow for those lights to go out, that's a problem.

But it is more extensive than that. Because those blue lights can come on for another 30 seconds depending on things you do. For example, suppose you are listening to the AM radio and turn on the headlight. Well, the blue lights come on too so you can't hear the radio until they go back off 30 seconds or so later!

So, it does the job, but, unless mine is just flawed in some way, you'll need to be prepared to deal with these quirks.

Too long a review? Yea, too long a process to find the right adapter too. Save yourself the hassle and buy this one.

title: Problems with Raspbian and permissions

Permissions would get wonky with every reboot for files/folders on this drive, and some apps on the Pi constantly popped up "access denied" errors when trying to rename or move, despite all access granted. Different drives produced the same problems; problems disappeared when the same drives were used with a different USB solution (un-powered enclosure).

UPDATE: I've now used these with three different SSDs and a 2.5" HDD. None have played well with Linux. They format fine, mount fine, then when you've started using them, they start spitting back "directory not found" errors. Different cables and enclosures work fine with the same drives. I'm past the return date now... not happy.

It's a shame; I bought five of these to use for rack-mount Pi enclosures with easy external drive mounting. May try another brand, but four of these are going back; It would be five getting returned, but I destroyed the box opening one of them, and there may be some use for it with Windows... we'll see...

This cable caused me three days worth of grief; don't let it do the same to you.

title: ML1050ST+ Short Throw 1000 lumens review
text:
I initially tested in a room with ambient light and gave this projector 2 stars because it didn't do as well as I had expected based on other reviews but then I raised my rating to 4 stars after testing it in a dark room and experiencing the full capability of the projector and I could have raised it to 5 stars but you'll understand why I didn't if you get to the end.

I bought this to replace an excelvan CL720 projector that annoyed me with its truly obnoxious fan noise terrible image left edge to right edge brightness uniformity and the fact that the projector was incapable of focusing both the center and the outer edges of the image simultaneously. The Optoma ML1050ST+ gets all of that stuff correct right out of the gate. It is also brighter by a smidge over popular cheap 720P native projectors like the CL720 or GP100 or GP90 etc but don't expect to see a remarkable improvement in terms of picture brightness if you're upgrading from one of those.
Where this projector really destroys the cheap chinese projector versions is when you use it in a dark room. The black levels/contrast (when viewing in a dark environment) is ASTRONOMICALLY better than any of the native 720P offerings from excelvan, vivibright or vankyo. The color accuracy on the ML1050ST+ is also head and shoulders above the cheaper chinese projectors as well (thank god because there is no way to adjust the primary color levels either). It also does way better in terms of edge to edge picture focus and edge to edge brightness uniformity. It was really pleasant to see the outer edges at the right and left of the screen just as in focus and just as bright as the center of the screen (if not brighter).

This projector's light engine is wonderful. The power consumption is rated at 77Watts but that figure is misleading because that's what it uses ONLY in full bright mode and you can't use that mode because it looks truly horrific. In cinema and photo modes you would expect the brightness to be significantly lower than bright mode but that's just not the case. In reality the modes do more to change the color of the image and the fan noise level than affect brightness. Think of the modes like this. BRIGHT mode= highest fan noise + useless green picture, ECO mode = 0 fan noise (inaudible) + useless dark green picture. The next two modes: CINEMA & PHOTO mode= very low fan noise and exactly the same brightness as bright mode but just with accurate colors. (maybe I got a lemon but that's how mine works.) Anyway In these 2 usable modes the projector ONLY consumes 27 WATTS of power. YES you read that correctly just 27watts plus the lamp life is basically eternal and it doesn't get very hot so you can use this for extended periods like you would a TV set and it would actually lower your electricity bill(that's mainly why I bought it). Add that to the very low fan noise in all modes except bright mode(useless mode) which is probably less than 1/10th of the CL720 fan (possibly quieter) and then consider the colors are accurate the black levels are good the image focus and brightness is good and uniform and you can easily see why the cost is totally worth it right? Well not so fast. Here's the problem.

Two things will REALLY hurt the way this projector is perceived. The first issue is the PRICE$$$$!!!!. At $650 just about every other projector in that price range does native 1080P and that brings me to the second and the BIGGEST weakpoint of this projector. 720P native resolution REALLY hurts the picture quality and therefore the potential of this projector. Also, the black levels while good are not $650 "good" so just because of how much the item costs, you will constantly wish the black levels/ contrast was just a bit better. If your intended use for it is mostly TV show or movie viewing the tradeoff of brightness for black performance is a sketchy one and you never get the best brightness as well as the best black levels at the same time even in a dark room. It's REALLY close but not quite there and you'd be really happy as is if you paid $300 or even $400 for this level of performance but for $650 you'd constantlly wish you had better performance on screen.

I FIRMLY believe that optoma's decision to prioritize adding a headphone jack and the autofocus feature to the 1050ST+ over just simply making it native 1080P to take full advantage of the brighter light engine was just a terrible decision. You can live with the fact that the projector doesn't get super bright because in reality it only consumes 26-28 Watts in the only two modes that matter (cinema & photo). That's half the power consumption of a regular tv set while producing a much larger image; You can also live with the fact that it doesn't have world endingly amazing black level performance for the $650 you spent because it still does a very decent job in that regard; Even though you don't have to as these features are now present, You could have lived without a headphone port or autofocus, because you can work around all of these types of quirks and it only hurts the viewing experience SOME of the time. However, The lack of 1080P native resolution hurts the projector ALL of the time.

So in concluding, do I recommend it? Well it depends. I've decided not to return it but that may not be the best decision for you depending on your needs.

Does light weight/ small form factor/ portability/ very low fan noise & heat/ lower power consumption than the average laptop mean a lot to you? Are you satisfied with decent image quality that only lacks finer HD detail? Are you willing to pay a premium to have those features? Then this projector is perfect for you

However if you're after the best bang for your buck and you don't mind having a projector that's bulkier, or you don't care that the average projector consumes about 6 times more power than the ML1050ST+ and you can't stand to see an image that looks less sharp and lacks detail almost like a 480P image does, then you really should look at a different model.

title: It's just a different experience; an improved experience.
text:
I also own a Boston 10" VR-series sub and a Polk 12" (PSW505). While those, together, provide plenty of low-end for music and movies, it's a different kind of low end. Those two can get very loud, and some people love that. As an example, in the movie "Aquaman", during the battle scene toward the end, there is extensive, heavy LFE and with those 2 subwoofers, I found msyelf reaching back to the Polk to turn it down. It was just too much for my taste; "boomy" if you will.

With the PB3k, it's 'different'. I just set it in the android app to the 'Movie' preset, and leave it alone. I haven't yet had to turn it down, even during that same battle scene. It wasn't 'boomy', rather, it was sound that you felt, not heard. If you've never experience that, I'd highly recommend it.

My theater has always had plenty of low-end, from a volume perspective. It wasn't until I turned off the other 2 subs and let the PB3k run solo that I realized it's not about volume that makes the difference. It's about the 'type' of LFE that makes the difference. Not quality, but type. I think it's a subjective expereience; you may prefer the loud, boomy experience. I've recently found that I much prefer to feel the LFE vs hear it.

This is easily one of the best purchases I've ever made and would do it again in a heartbeat.

title: Excellent Carplay sound system
text:
I bought the newer YS102SL Starter unit and installed it on my Honda CR-V. Wiring and connections were fairly uncomplicated to do myself. The build quality is very good and the screen resolution is excellent with adequate brightness even in the sunlight. The manual says the unit will dim when the headlights turn on, but I have not been able to get this to work using either the dimmer or illumination wire from my car’s harness. It includes a screen protector which I installed since I knew nothing about the strength of the screen glass. I have an Axxess ASWC-1 interface for the steering wheel controls. It identifies the stereo as Pioneer/Jensen. The process was rather straightforward to map the buttons to the radio functions on the unit. The boot time is on the slow side at about 15s, but the backup camera activates much faster, so it’s not as noticeable overall. The sound quality is excellent - on par with premium sound systems costing hundreds more. There is no discernible noise when using just about any media. There is a full equalizer and additional bass, middle, and treble settings. I have noticed that the latter settings somehow reset to it’s default whenever you restart your car - even though the settings appear to have changed. I have to go back to the audio settings and tap on it several times to get it to wake up. Then I can lower the bass by moving it up or down and then back to the place where I last had it. The process is rather annoying. I talked to support about this and they are escalating the issue up the chain. The radio function leaves much to be desired as well. The interface has a magnifying glass icon that is supposed to search for all stations it can pick up - then you can add each to your favorites. I’ve noticed that it skips a lot of stations, so I have to go back manually and add them. The tuner works slowly, so this can be tedious. That being said, once you have your stations set up the radio works fine with stations having better reception than my factory unit. If you reset the radio, however, your favorite stations are lost. Thankfully, I have not had the need to do that in the week or so I have been driving with this. The bluetooth audio is adequate for phone calls, but there is a high pingy-ness almost like crackling when you play music. Media can also be played through the microSD slot. Movies and photos are very slow to load making it practically useless for that (which is not a good thing to do while driving anyway). MP3 files sound excellent from the microSD slot, but for some reason the first 1.5s of audio is muted when each track is played.

I use Apple Carplay on this unit and it works flawlessly. Very smooth and responsive with equally impressive sound. Honestly, I can’t overemphasize the sound quality on this - haven’t ever heard audio like this in a car stereo. It gives new life to my factory speakers. Going back to the factory audio settings doesn’t stop Carplay from playing music and stuff, which is a nice feature. You can’t use Waze or other navigation apps while playing the AM/FM radio, but these stations are generally streamable on your smartphone anyway while navigating.

Some of my minor complaints on this unit are things that can hopefully be fixed in a future firmware update:

The RDS info on the FM radio has a rather small font, you end up taking your eyes off the road too long to read it.

The date on the screen is fixed to day/month/year format. It would be nice to have the option for the American month/day/year format.

It does not appear that user images can be used for wallpaper, just the half-dozen stock images.

There are no guidelines built in for the backup camera. Atoto offers an aftermarket camera that has guidelines, but most car owners these days have OEM cameras already that do not have guidelines - they rely on the stereo to provide that.

An option for a shorter 2s warm boot like the A6 Pro would be good.

Bluetooth pairing does not have an access code. Sometimes I see random phones appear in the screen. It would be nice to have this more secure.

All in all this is an incredible bargain for premium sound at $140 Prime. Since this product was just released a couple months ago, it’s reassuring to know the manufacturer offers firmware updates, so we will have to see what improvements are added. I am going to keep it and highly recommend it for now. I plan to update this review in a few months once I have road tested it for a while.

title: Cheap storage is... cheap
text:
64 GB is a lovely thing to keep on a keychain. Except when it stops being 64 GB.

My first purchase of this product was completely corrupt and unusable. I thought it was an odd egg that slipped through. I returned it and had it replaced for free. The new one worked fine for some light file transfers at work for several months. I built a new PC and used Windows Installation Media Tool to reformat the USB with Windows 10 in a 32 GB partition (thank GOD I backed it up beforehand). Everything went perfectly fine - I'm typing this on my new computer. But then when I went to reformat the USB back to 64 GB of usable drive it completely broke. The full formatting process took 2 hours... A full format of a 1TB HDD takes maybe 2 minutes. After it completed, the drive behaved erratically, disconnecting from computers without prompting, taking forever (not a long time - literal eternity; the computer had to be powered off) to copy files, and throwing unknown errors sometimes while moving files. I attempted to reformat it again, but computers now no longer recognize it as having any storage space at all. I will not be trying my luck with a third. Buy something with a reputable name behind it or take regular backups so you don't risk losing your data.

It only has a built-in microphone. The night vision is good enough up to around 40-60ft. I connected this to my POE switch that is connected to my DVR/NVR. My DVR is a rebranded Hikvision. I did not have any issues connecting to this camera and updating the IP address to work with my system. I used the static IP listed in the instructions and connected to it via Chrome on my phone.  I changed the admin password and updated the IP address to one that wasn't being used on my network.  Restarted the camera and reconnect to it with the new IP I gave it. I added the camera to the DVR, made some minor changes to the audio and picture for my preferences and made some set points within the PTZ settings. You can also use this camera without a DVR and view it from anywhere via several different apps, Guarding Vision, Hik-Connect, Hi-Look. I think the preferred app is Guarding Vision. You will need to follow the instructions to add the camera to the Guarding Vision Platform Access within the app, add your own encryption password for viewing and once that's done you can view the camera from anywhere, as long as you have a Data or WiFi connection. You can also just use an IP address to connect to it from anywhere but that involves having some advanced networking skills. To many different scenarios to get into about that. You can set up motion alerts from the app, illegal login notifications and many other notifications at your own discretion. It has a slot for an SD card, I am not using it so I cannot say much about it besides it would record to it based on your recording preferences you set up in the app, all the time, motion only etc. If recording all the time, once it fills up, it would overwrite the oldest recording and continue recording, unless you tell it not too. Motion recording is the same way, once it fills up, it would overwrite the oldest recording. For those curious, ONVIF works great on this camera. I had no issues with mine. If you have a different DVR/NVR than Hik Vision, you need to verify that the version of ONVIF that comes with this camera will work with your DVR and/or NVR. I use this camera indoors to record while we are away from home. It is an indoor/outdoor camera but my usage needed it inside. I actually have mine set up to the smart home and it only comes on if the Alarm is set to Away Mode or if we manually turn it on. Its great for watching the dog while we are away too. For the $, this camera offers many options for you to choose from. I cannot speak for the longevity of it because I've only had it a couple of weeks but if something changes, I will update this review. Good Luck!

text: I’ve had the Marshall Mode EQ headphones for a few weeks now and am really happy with them. I use high-end over-ear headphones when I’m in an audiophile mood, but I was looking for some good quality, affordable wired earbuds to use at other times. After some online research, I narrowed my search to these, the Beyerdynamic Soul Byrd, and the 1More Triple Drivers. I listened to several songs in all three headphones (electronic, classical, indie rock), and the Marshalls had the most consistently solid audio performance. The sound is well balanced and articulate. The Soul Byrds felt like they were lacking in depth, especially the midrange, although they were the most comfortable of the three I tried. The 1More came in a close second to the Marshalls - great sound and excellent build quality, however I just preferred the sound signature of the Marshalls and how consistently good they sounded across all the musical genres I tested them on. Other strengths of the Marshalls are the comfort, fit, and aesthetics. Price wasn’t a huge factor for me, but I did find it interesting that the Marshalls are the most inexpensive of the ones I tested, which is nice. I have not tried the standard Mode version (without the EQ feature), so can’t make a comparison. I went with the EQs mainly because of some reviews I read on audiophile sites, and I figured having two options was better than one. Overall, I highly recommend these earbuds!

title: Scary At First, But Great When I Figured It Out
text:
At first I gave this company a 1-star review. It appeared that my watch had come already linked to someone else's account and if that's the case, there's no way to unlink it without that person's password. Along about 3am I sat bolt upright in bed with a realization. What if it was in demo mode? I searched the trusty internet and there was a great video on YouTube from a guy who bought a used watch that was in demo mode and how he cleared it. It's the easiest thing in the world to do. Five minutes later, my watch was set up to my account and was rocking along beautifully. Thus far, everything I've tried has worked beautifully, including the ECG (EKG) and the cellular function.

So why the 4-star review for a watch that I'm rapidly coming to love? It's because of the company. Sending the watch in demo mode with no documentation whatsoever was unprofessional. If they are going to sell refurbished watches, the watch should have a factory reset performed and be ready to link to the new user's account on arrival. This cost me quite a bit of distress until it dawned on me after hours of fighting with it that the watch might have been in demo mode. And at that, I had to research until I found the YouTube video. Was it worth it? I think so, but if you're wanting a watch that will come to you in the same state that it would have from Apple, this probably isn't the place to shop.

title: Pictures is ad are misleading.
text: The picture in the add shows a comparison of 3 camera systems.  The top is the 5MP, the second a 2MP, and the bottom a 1 MP.  They progressively get smaller (cut off part of the picture) and blurrier.  The blurry part is factual, but the smaller image displayed is NOT.  The top photo displayed appears to be the widest image, but in fact the 5MP camera (2560 x 1920) is a 4:3 ratio image, like old style (almost square) televisions.  The widest display should actually be the 2MP image, as the 1920 x 1080 is a full HD widescreen 16:9 image like all modern televisions.  It will not be as clear an image, because it has less data, but if you are expecting a wide screen image this is not the system for you.

title: This is going to be an amazing backup!
text: I am so excited! I am working from home now during the pandemic, and I set up some backup systems in place just to make that it goes as uninterruptedly as possible such as having a Jackery for backup power and putting some extra GB on my cell phone plan in case my home internet goes down. The one weakness of my setup was that the VOIP Cisco 8841 phone supplied by the company could not connect wirelessly. Sure enough, there was an internet outage at my home Friday, and I had to have coworkers take over my call responsibilities. No more! This morning I configured this in less than 5 minutes to the WIFI from my cell phone used as a hotspot. I just plugged the ethernet cable into the port on my laptop and easily followed the configuration instructions which were little more than going to the address in the instruction booklet and selecting the name of my hotspot network. I unplugged my router from my phone's power injector and plugged this into the power injector in its place. My phone recognized it was online and let me log in and make a call. Now I could theoretically work from anywhere my cell phone can get a signal! I powered the unit by plugging its USB lead into a small power bank for convenience. The lead from the AC adapter is short though you could always use it with USB extension if desired. There is also a hole that looks like it is where the power should go, but I didn't need and have not figured out how to use that.  So you can imagine how easy this is to configure if I am no brighter that that! Also, I just unplugged it for about 15 minutes, and when I plugged it back in, it remembered its configuration. text:
Context: I live in an apartment with a built in router, but it is located in a closet and that means I have terrible WiFi connection in my room on the opposite side of my apartment. That is why I bought this. I’m beginning to regret it. This is my horror story.

Access Point Setup: The directions state that after you plug this into an outlet, wait for the green light, and plug the Ethernet cable into a LAN port and it will automatically create a new WiFi hotspot to set up. Easy enough! I plug it in and wait. The WiFi hotspot never sets itself up. The router indicator never lights up. Instructions already unclear on STEP TWO. Trying to connect to their mywifiext router website never works. What a disappointment - but there is another way, as the prophecy foretells.

(Also a nitpick, the instructions say to plug in the Ethernet cable after the power indicator goes from red to green. You wait 10 seconds once it’s on, not a big deal right? Well the on-off button is on the opposite side of the Ethernet port, so if you are an idiot (read: me), you will press this button by accident several times trying to plug the Ethernet in, meaning you gotta wait for that stupid indicator to go green each time you make this mistake. Torture device. )

Extended mode setup: Okay so the Access Point setup is confusing, maybe this set of instructions will be easier. (Spoiler: no)

Press the WPS button and run to your router and do the same there. If it doesn’t work (which it won’t the first few times), try and try again. And don’t forget to not accidentally press the on off button which is right next to the damn WPS button on this extender (designed to be a torture device). After traveling between the router and your extender for what feels like a mile run that I haven’t done since college, the router indicator should finally show green.

By now the device should work in -extender mode- but you realize that it’s not any better than connecting directly to your WiFi in your room. No, you want what you -paid- for, you are an over achiever, you want that failed access point set up to work and you deserve it. So let’s try that again.

Access Point Set Up *Part Two: Return of the Sith*: So let’s type in that mywifiext website that the instructions say and try again. Will the website work? Of course not, dummy (read:me), you can’t use chrome for this, you need to be in safari. I’m glad the instructions totally fail to mention this so your cave man oogah boogah brain will keep trying in chrome expecting a different result each time.

Once the website works in Safari, the website will show a big purple button saying “New Extender Mode” - No! Why isn’t there a big fat purple button saying New Access Point? Fine, have it your way. Let’s press it. It forces you to create a new account and some privacy questions. Great, another data breach target. Let’s fill that out. It tells you the extender is successfully set up. Wonderful! Except I still want the access point setup! Clicking next will direct you to the net gear website. Not so fast. Let’s go back and see what the WiFi extender website looks like and see if there is something we can do about that access point.

Now, my instincts tell me to update the device firmware. Don’t listen to my instincts, you already know I’m an idiot. When you download the firmware, and begin to set the router up, chances are the download and installation will take longer than 5 minutes to install. And you know what happens when you idle on the router webpage for 5 minutes? YOU DISCONNECT DURING THE FIRMWARE UPDATE. IT BRICKS YOUR WIFI EXTENDER YOU SPENT YOUR WHOLE NIGHT SETTING UP. Ahem. So you repeat most of the steps from the very beginning and reach this point, and this time do not update the firmware. I mean you can, if you don’t idle - but I believe I have PTSD now and I don’t dare to try lest I be abused by this device and it’s poor instructions again.

The Extender webpage does not show any tabs or options to set up the Access Point at this point, by the way.

So if you know how to set up the Access Point, please bless me with your infinite wisdom because I am not smarter than a fifth grader, apparently.

I hope my review helped you make a decision on what device to buy. If I could travel time, I’d go back and stop myself from trying to install this and yeet it out the window. Or just tell myself to buy a different device entirely.

3/5 because it -works-, just not as easily as I hoped.

title: Works with my old H115i
text:
I bought the H115i back in 2016 (the original). When I got it, it only came with Intel and AM3 brackets. I believe Ryzen 1 had begun shipping right around the time I bought it and Corsair said they'd send out a free bracket to customers who recently purchased. I had just built my intel system and decided not to bother. Recently I went to Corsair's site to see if they still sold the bracket. While it is listed for $5, it says out of stock.

Anyway, this kit worked no problem.

Step 1: Snap on the bracket to your cooler. (It's a push and twist mechanism).
Step 2: Remove the two top mounted plastic brackets that are situated around the AM4 socket on the motherboard.
Step 3: Connect the included mounting stand-offs to the default AMD backplate (collar down, long side up).
Step 4: Connect your cooler to those standoffs and use the included thumbscrews to tighten. Ez pz.

I saved myself over $100 by continuing to use my H115i. It still works as well as the day I bought it. I believe I still have about a year of warranty left on it so I may as well use it at least until then.

title: Awesome outdoor PTZ camera for the price.
text:
I've been hunting around for a decent, inexpensive outdoor PTZ camera. Other models I'd tried claimed to have ONVIF compatibility but never did. So far, this camera exceeds the requirements I put in place with only some minor caveats.

First off, the design. The shell is made of plastic and is generally very light. While I'd prefer a metal case, the light weight of the case should make it easier to mount. The connections are all on a pigtail coming out the right side of the base. I'd prefer for them to be say receesed in the base or something, but nothing we can't work around! Other than that, the design is what you'd expect from a dome camera.

Next, configuration. Power comes from a 12v 1A transformer with a 5.5mm jack. The cord provided is very short but it's a common size and will be easy to replace with something longer. Plugging it up and connecting it to my network brings me to my next point I highly recommend this camera. Unlike others that require some APP to configure the camera, this one just works. It's assigned an IP address and then you can log right into it and begin configuring it as needed. While an APP is available for both Apple and Android, just log into the camera! Through the web config, it only takes a few minutes to enable WIFI and connect it to your network. I want to mention how this camera is truly ONVIF compatible. Some other cameras claim this but aren't. In the case of this camera, it's instantly picked up using ONVIF Device Manager and can be configured this way. Massive thumbs up from me!

Image quality is good and about what I expected from the camera. During the day, it's a little over saturated and too sharp. Tweaking tweaking the settings slightly improved the image greatly. Though what really sets this camera apart from similar models is the inclusion of flood lights. I've included a quick comparison of no lights, flood lights and then standard IR lights. Both uses of lights provide good images in the dark. Flood lights give you color at a shorter range with IR being black and white but showing more detail further out.

The PTZ control is very good too. My other indoor PTZ cameras have always been very choppy and nearly impossible to make minor changes. This camera on the other hand is much smoother and allows for very minor bumps in adjustment. It also will remember it's last location if power is lost! Something none of my other PTZ cameras seem to do (without additional settings).

All in all, I'm happy with this camera. I think my only real complaint is the how short the power cable is. But given the going price for this camera, you can add an extension still keep the price around if not lower than some similar cameras.

title: Excellent Value and Great Notebook Replacement
text: Although I had to pay extra shipping and import duties to ship this to Mexico from US I still think it is great value. My old faithful Acer Notebook has been and continues to damage HDDs I put in corrupting sectors on HDD. (I'm going to try an SSD in it.) I needed another Notebook to use and have available if the old Notebook dies on me. The EZpad fits the bill perfectly. I, also, air travel some so the size and weight is perfect. I chose the 2-1 platform as I really like using my old Surface RT, even with it's limitations, but Windows RT 8.1 is extremely limited in what programs (that I need) it will run. Even with 70 yr. old eyes I'm adjusting fine to the smaller screen and, once you become accustomed to the slightly smaller keyboard, you will appreciate how really good the EZpad keyboard is compared to other keyboards that work with the "tablets". I have the keyboard for the Surface RT and I've used many smaller form factor keyboards, over many years. The EZpad keyboard is by far the best feeling and working keyboard of all. Touchpad.... not so good. I use a small Verbatim wireless mouse. Initially the speakers were terrible. I could barely hear them with sound up all the way. I used a small bluetooth speaker and/or earphones just to hear. I found a fix for the speaker volume on Youtube. That improved sound significantly and proved the issue was not so much hardware but software. But still, don't expect a lot of volume. Being so used to 1 T HDDs it took a bit of adjusting for me with only 128 SSD. I did install a 128 flash card so basically have 256 storage capacity and I have set up for most of data to be stored on the flash drive. 4 gigs of ram is working just fine as long as I don't load up to many programs running at one time. One thing that works easily is projection to other devices. I plan on taking my EZ pad to friends' houses, and with my VPN (I'm in Mexico so I have to have VPN for FuboTV, Hulu, and others because they are restricted to outside of US.) projecting content to my friends TVs for Movie Nights. I will either project or use micro HDMI to their TVs. Yes.... EZpad does have micro HDMI out. It can also be used if I want to hook up a larger Monitor. EZ pad boots and loads extremely fast. It runs much faster than I expected. Screen is beautiful. I love my little EZ pad!!!

title: Good sound quality and volume but exceedingly poor control design.
text:
The Good:
iced a bit above rock bottom (really cheap) the overall sound and communications properties of this unit are significantly better. Even at 70 mph, the music is quite recognizable because the volume can be turned up to an almost painful level. Phone not as good at such speeds but good enough to answer and tell the person at the other end to wait a few seconds while you slow or pull over to continue the call. Several cheaper units I have used over the years (the last two in the same helmet) were basically unintelligible over 50-60mph. Call clarity is also great.

You get both a "boom" type microphone and a simple "wired" Velcro-secured mic about the size of a nickel. Tried both and the latter was vastly superior at cutting noise and good intelligibility (called and left myself voicemails with both mics to evaluate). Easy to install (but, I have done this a number of times!).

Battery life is phenomenal! have played music through the unit for a full sunup to sundown (about 12 hours) without a charge. Also, you don't have to unplug anything to charge the unit (most other inexpensive units I have used force you to unplug their headphone/mic connection and plug the charging cord into the headphone/mic jack to charge). Beware that there is no included charger but you do get a USB cable that you can plug into an automotive USB power adapter, a computer, or a USB battery bank. Seems to fully charge in about an hour.

The Bad:
What seems to be a volume control/function selector knob that is common to most other similar units is a totally bogus decorative rubber item. The only "functionality" about it is the mode button in the center of the "knob". The unit has a pair of very stiff buttons on top of the unit to control volume and to advance/replay your music playlist. Unfortunately, you have to press them "down" (parallel with the surface of the helmet to which the unit mounds) and it is nearly impossible to operate the buttons without either pulling the unit from the helmet (if you use the provided tape) or it slides out of the helmet if you use the provided sprint-bail mounting device. The solution is to "pinch" the unit between your thumb (on bottom) and index finger (to operate the appropriate button on top)...which leads to another problem. In doing so, your thumb naturally falls on the only button on the "bottom" of the unit which initiates a "fake" SIRI message for operating your iPhone. I say "fake" because in my case, you get a "SIRI" announcement whether or not you are connected to the unit with your phone...even if it's NOT an iPhone (of which my phone is NOT). You get the SIRI message even if NOTHING is connected to the device.

Almost impossible to turn off or on or operate ANY useful buttons (that you would normally need to operate while riding) while wearing even the thinnest of gloves. Easy to get around in the summer with fingerless gloves if you are so inclined but when cold weather sets in...well....

If it weren't for the fact this unit has good loud sound and excellent battery life, I would hesitate to recommend it. I have been using it every day for about a month and it's the controls that are frustrating and a potential deal-breaker for most (the bogus "volume knob" doesn't help things, either.

I haven't tried intercom to other riders or a passenger with this unit nor have I tried plugging in the charging cable and simultaneously operating while riding.

I can't give it more than three stars for overall rating because of the frustrating controls.

title: Solid hard drive
text:
I've bought 3 of these (a 1 TB version and two of the 2 TB versions). After so many failures with WD and Seagate hard drives, I decided I needed something more "sturdy." I've dropped one of these a couple of times on my hardwood floors (just a couple of feet from coffee table height) and unlike my earlier WD and Seagate hard drives, these little guys kept trucking along. I've been using 2 of these for the past 5 years and 1 of these for the past 4 years and none of my 3 have yet to fail. I'm sure that they will fail one of these days (that's what all hard drives do eventually), so that's why I duplicate my backups among these 3 hard drives (with more backups in the cloud just in case). I use the 1 TB version as a time capsule backup for my Mac and the other two 2 TB hard drives get used for long term backup, all encrypted of course (my files are duplicated on both so that when one hard drive fails, I still have a backup for my backup). Yes, I am paranoid about my data.

I am surprised by all of these reviews that complain about losing a ton of data because their hard drive failed one day. Of course your hard drive will eventually fail. You have to have a backup for your backup because all hard drives will eventually fail at some point. If you don't have a backup for your backup, you are playing with fire! Remember, it's not a question of whether your hard drive will fail, but rather, it's a question of when.

Anyways, to make a long story short, these suckers seem a good bit more reliable than my prior experiences with those cheap Western Digital and Seagate drives.

title: The best and only flash I need
text:
As a professional photographer, I rely on the flash that gives me speed, durability and accuracy. I was surprised that the Godox V860II has everything I need. It is on par with the high-end model of Nikon Speedlight without the steep price tag.

Upon unpacking, the first thing I noticed about the flash was that it is well built and has a solid weight to it. Although I haven't dropped it yet, I wouldn't be surprised that it would survive moderate drops.

As any photographer would know, the accuracy of the flash output is extremely important. I tested out the Godox flash for the proper balance between the subject and background and found the flash to be accurate in most scenes. The flash output can be increased by +3 to -3 stops with is useful to control the brightness of the flash. To do so you simply press down the function 2 button and move the dial. Besides the aperture and shutter speed, The Godox also recognizes Auto ISO setting. Which I find is one of the most useful features. When I shoot events, I leave the camera in Auto ISO so I can shoot in bright and low light scenes without having to manually change the ISO. The Godox flash knows when the ISO is changed and adjust the flash output accordingly for properly lit, well-balanced exposure.

Another awesome feature about the Nikon version of the Godex is the ability to sync at any shutter speed up to 1/8000 sec. Meaning that you can use it as a fill flash outdoor and shoot any shutter speed. I tested at all shutter speeds on my Nikon D750 and found the flash was evenly lit with well-balanced output at all shutter speed.

The Godox is super fast in flash cycle time. In iTTL mode, I was able to fire off my flash rapidly without delay. In manual mode with full flash output, it takes up to 1.5 seconds to charge which is still acceptable. The manual claims that it can fire up to 650 times in full power in a single charge which is a plus for shooting large events. However, it uses an ion battery instead of 4 AA, I would suggest that you buy at least one additional battery as a backup.

The flash can be fired off remotely through Nikon' camera's commander mode, or by purchasing a Godox flash transmitter. It also has an RTP mode where you can capture the subjects in motion by a series of flash.

There is only one minor drawback about the flash which is the noise from the motor when zooming the camera lens. The Godox is smart enough to know when you zoom in and out before taking a photo, so it would adjust the field of coverage accordingly. The motor does sound a bit loud which can be annoying when shooting in quiet surroundings.

The Godox kit cames with a flash bracket that is made of metal and is durable. For me, it's too bulky, but you can add Bowen accessories such as softbox or snoot to the bracket. The bonus flash diffusor that came with the kit is super handy though. I have it attached to the flash all-time for softer lighting.

Overall, I am extremely pleased with the Godox flash, With its versatility, high-speed sync, and flash output accuracy, it's the only flash I need for portraits and events.
