title: I think they are great, especially at the price
text:
Lot's of complaints about these. I guess people expect them to sound like $5-10K B&O home speakers. For what they are, I think they sound great. No noise cancelling, so if that is a must-have, look elsewhere. I like that they are open frame and not total in-ear. I wear them for road sports and want to be able to hear the cars around me. You can carry on a conversation with these and still hear the music. As for comfort, they fit fine. All the little up and down and twisty adjustment points make then pleasant to wear. And yes, even with sunglasses on top of them. I like that they have a cord. Makes them much harder to lose. Ever notice how many people are selling a single ear bud?

The cord is best in front. The plastic they used on it will stick to you neck in the back once you get even slightly sweaty. Then they kind of pull when you turn your head. Yes, the buttons are small and the center one could satnd to be bigger, but you get used to them and how to find them without looking.

The batter life is probably not what B&O would like you to believe unless you run them at incredibly low volumes. I think they state 5 hrs, but it is probably more like 3-4. Again, less time if you use mic. But they are simple enough to charge.

Look, these are way discounted from the original price, so alot of the complaints about them vanish when you consider how little you spent. I got the brown ones and think they look really classy.

title: Great monitor for the price point
text:
I picked up this monitor to use with my laptop. I wanted it wide so that I can have 2 windows, side-by-side, while I'm writing my reports. I also wanted a touch screen, and didn't want to spend a fortune. While it's not perfect, it meets all of my requirements. I've used it almost daily for over 2 months now and am very satisfied with this monitor's features and performance.

What I like:
-super light for its size, I can pick this screen easily and move it around if I need to
-the stand is solid and allows the monitor to be raised, lowered and angled to make it comfortable to use
-connection was easy. Some said they had problems, but I found the directions were easy to follow and I had it set up and connected within just a few minutes
-I mentioned it was touch screen, right? This feature has worked flawlessly for me. I love it
-No flickering. I'm highly sensitive to light changes on a monitor or tv. This is LED and it has zero noticeable flickering, so no migraines
-Screen quality is good for web browsing, document-based work, and even the occasional graphic work.
-the price makes this a great value

What I didn't like:
-graphics aren't crisp. This is the only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5. If you work primarily in graphics then this probably isn't the best monitor for you. If you work with text or browse the web it's hardly noticeable
-the port cover is difficult to attach. After the monitor is set up and all cords are connected, this is supposed to snap on over them, probably for a dust cover, or maybe to give a cleaner appearance. The problem is that it goes on the underside and back of the monitor, unless I detach the monitor from the stand, this area isn't easily accessible. I turned the monitor and tried to blindly get the tabs to go into the slots and then click into place against the cords, which resist against the cover. It failed and I left it there because it's far more trouble than it's worth, in my opinion. If they wanted a dust cover, then it should be a hinged door. This useless piece of plastic just sits there cluttering up my space

I also love the switch from the page turn sensor into actual buttons for page turns. I didn't use the feature on my Voyage because they weren't well aligned with my thumb while holding it (so I used the touch screen to turn the page). There are only 2 ways in which the Oasis is not better than the Voyage. My Voyage held a battery charge that would flabbergast even the Energizer bunny. I mean, it's unnatural how long the Voyage can go (in Airplane mode) before needing a recharge. The Oasis holds a charge pretty well in airplane mode too, but nothing like the Voyage. The Voyage also has the 6" screen instead of the 7", so can tuck more easily into a pocket. Overall, both are great Kindles, but I am very happy I took a chance on the Oasis (10th generation).

title: Best TV for Price, Picture & Gaming
text:

I've included pictures that were hard to capture with my S10 but this is simply the best device with a screen I have ever owned. God of War on PS4 PRO is the best HDR game I've ever seen. Gears 5 and Assassin's Creed Origins on Xbox One X are fantastic too.

Picture Quality on the X900H 55inch is on par with more expensive OLED TVs like LG CX9 (yes I know, the GOAT). Black levels and High Dynamic Range (HDR) are absurdly good and deep for an LCD-LED. These TVs are more durable and less prown to burn-in like OLED and can get brighter for bigger day rooms. I've never owned a SONY TV before and am blown away by the Color accuracy and brightness. You don't have to mess with settings if you don't want to but you can, AND HOW. You can tinker all you want in settings and you can't make it look bad.

The X900H is the only TV that will be able to handle both PS5 and Xbox Series X simultaneously as the 4 HDMI ports have 2 that are HDMI 2.1 capable (other competitors in this class, even sony itself, only offer one 2.1 capable port). This is the only choice for multiple system owners in the near future.
Movies on either the built-in tv apps or my PS4 PRO or my XBOX ONE X (4k Blu-ray player) look outstanding. Even my Switch in dock mode looks good! Color accuracy, black levels and HDR again blow me away. CINEMA, GAME or CUSTOM are the best 3 settings to choose from. Some apps have there own picture settings specifications like Disney+ (Dolby Vision Bright or Dark) and Netflix (Calibrated Mode). These 2 mentioned apps are only ones I've seen that have presets like that and I don't care for Netflix Calibrated Mode at all. It dims screen for some reason even in bright day conditions so I turned it off and went to custom instead (pictures included).
4k Blu-rays of 2001: A Space Odyssey or Avengers Endgame or Saving Private Ryan or 1917 all look amazing.

OS is ANDROID TV which I never had experience with but as a Galaxy S10 owner I assumed it would be good. But I didn't know it would be GREAT. It's so good you forget it's there. Easy interface to use. Not overcomplicated. Good fit for any user.

Other than a narrower viewing angle than others in this class and a hilariously long remote there's no complaints. It took 3 weeks to get the much anticipated firmware update but it came and it's good. I don't have PS5 or Series X Xbox so it doesn't really matter for me yet. But it will...so I'm happy it came. Easy to update.

I have a 14 year old Sony Bravia DVD Home Theater System that still is going strong without a thing wrong with it so I have confidence in Sony's build quality for years of good use.
Remote control is intuitive and easy to use without looking at it for every button press, it features google assistant so that's fun and the microphone is built into the remote so you don't have to yell to the tv. It's all very non dramatic to ask it something. Since everyone has Gmail, everyone has a Google account so signing into the tv for the first time with your username and password is not difficult or invasive. Did I mention the remote is Bluetooth? Or that you can pair you favorite True Wireless Earbuds to the TV? Or that the TV "sees" PS4 automatically and as such let's you use the x900h's included remote to navigate your PS4 (Sony+Sony)? Well, now I have.

This TV used to be $1400 until Sony slashed it to under $1k which was smart. It would be still be a good TV for $1400 but it's a GREAT TV for $999 (55in version). Please don't have any reservations about the SONY BRAVIA X900H, it's a fantastic unit.

Amazon delivery was great with no issues and arrived when it said it would and they even called me before coming. Setup was easy but I took my time and you may want help if you are nervous about doing it yourself. I mounted mine on a entertainment stand, but if you use the included feet they just pop in on either side so that's easy too. Make sure you have a wide enough stand to accommodate.

This is a GOOD BUY. NO REGERTS. You can stop looking now. SONY HAS GOT THE FUTURE SETUP NO ONE ELSE HAS. The future of console Gaming is here. SONY X900H is ready ALREADY. How many other TVs can say that?

title: Kindle itself is just OK; FreeTime (Amazon Kids) is a hopeless joke
text:
My daughter, a voracious, multilingual reader, is currently using one of my old spare Kindles, which I've loaded up for her with a large number of books from my own collection (many converted using Calibre from epubs etc.) in the several languages she speaks. The interface on the old Kindle (it's one of the original, non-touchscreen models, older than she is!) leaves a lot to be desired, though, so when it came on sale I figured the Kindle Kids Edition would be a nice upgrade for her. While she has a large number of books in her collection, I figured the 1 year FreeTime Unlimited (or, as it is apparently now known, Amazon Kids+ - though the Kindle still calls it FreeTime) would be a nice bonus, helping her discover new books -- especially since the pandemic has made trips to the library a thing of the past for now.

I just received the Kids Edition and have been trying to set it up for the past hour or so, and I'm realizing it was probably a mistake. The Kindle hardware itself is fine (although the display isn't as good as on the newer Kindles I have, the Oasis, the Voyage, or the Paperwhite). And the cover it came with is nice, I think she will like it.

But the FreeTime feature just doesn't cut it. The crucial thing I didn't fully appreciate -- THIS IS A MAJOR SHORTCOMING, TAKE NOTE BEFORE YOU BUY THIS! -- is that you can't add your own content (i.e. books not purchased from Amazon) to the FreeTime library.

It actually took me quite a while to realize that in order to connect the Kids Edition to a computer via USB at all, you have to exit the FreeTime library. Otherwise the computer doesn't recognize the Kindle. Even after I exited FreeTime, I found that the Kids Edition, for some reason, was not recognized by Calibre, but I was eventually able to copy my daughter's library to the Kindle manually (as with other Kindles, it appears as a USB disk on the computer). I then reentered FreeTime -- and realized to my shock that *there is no way to access books that have been downloaded via USB from FreeTime*. There is a page on the Amazon site to add books that the parent has purchased on Amazon, but no way to make available non-Amazon books already loaded on the Kindle.

Now, it *is* of course possible to exit FreeTime and use the Kindle just like a "grown-up" Kindle -- the regular home screen shows books that have been loaded via USB. But in this mode, the FreeTime library is not accessible. And while you can start FreeTime if you want to read books in the FreeTime librayr, the parental-control PIN is required to exit FreeTime -- that's a good feature overall, but very inconvenient if you want your kid to be able to read books form the regular home screen as well as using FreeTime. Basically, the Kindle Kids Edition has two mutually-incompatible libraries, the regular one and the FreeTime one, *and you can't move books between them*.

Since the main reason I got my daughter this Kindle is so that she can read books from our own collection (many of which are in Hungarian or German and aren't available on Amazon at all) ,I probably should just have gotten her a regular Paperwhite (with a nicer screen to boot); FreeTime looks like it's going to be too big a hassle to use.

title: Smooth Operator
text:
I have worked with GPS navigators from several manufacturers, including Garmin, Magellan and TomTom. Each unit has its strengths and weaknesses. My favorite GPS unit up this point has been another TomTom, an old Start 40 which served me well for several years. I was interested to see how much the series has changed since I got that older model. It has changed quite a bit – more than I expected. I like this navigator, though I can see a few things I’d change.

First off, I have the 6” model which is a beast. I am used to a 5” GPS which I have been using, and it took some time to adjust to the larger screen. This is not to say it bothers me; it just is enough of a difference to require getting used to it. If you are upsizing like that, be aware that it takes up more physical space and placing on the windshield might require replanning.

Out of the box, I powered it on, connected it to my WiFi network and downloaded over 6GB of updates. That’s a huge update. The map it holds is obviously the largest component to be updated, and it covers all of the US, Canada and Mexico. While it is nice to have all that coverage, I personally do not need that much map and would have liked the option of only having the US map on-board. That would cut memory requirements. My older model was limited in memory and the map grew until it could no longer fit; I can see the potential for that happening again.

For navigation, up to this point I have stuck with the default settings, except with the 2D/3D map setting.

My first trip with this unit was to work. I did not use it to navigate, I only used to to show the map as I drove. It found my fix quickly (one of the reasons I like TomTom navigators) and when I was driving it updated the map smoothly and quickly as I reached new features. It displayed road names, it showed the placement of certain POIs like gas stations, and because I was driving at sunrise the map switched from night mode to daytime so I got to see both maps.

I’ll state for the record, I am not fan of the daytime map’s default color scheme. I almost always use the 2D map, not the 3D one, and it uses a set of pastel colors that might be somewhat soothing on the eyes but they’re quite drab. I’d rather see a bolder map that makes features stand out more. Another thing this unit does not show is road symbols like the interstate shield, instead opting for just small-print words. I can live with that but I do prefer the symbols.

On the way home from work, I used the unit again, but this time to guide me on an alternate route. Friday afternoon traffic in this area is typically awful, and the route home is almost always snarled by at least one accident (sometimes as many as 4-5). I chose to follow a route I knew would take two hours to get home, though it moves the whole time. I loaded the first point into the GPS and it dutifully guided me there, taking me on a fairly optimal route. When I got there, I then told it to take me home and I was quite surprised – every other GPS unit I have used has tried to make me take a U-turn to go back the way I came to get back on the interstate (the source of the problem), but this one did not, instead taking me on a route that would connect me back to the interstate about 20 miles south. Knowing this was also a bad route traffic-wise, I made a planned turn in the middle of the route, skipping another 20 miles of interstate. Instead of insisting I turn around, the unit again adjusted my route and took me on almost the exact route I had planned to take anyway.

What impressed me is how quickly the unit rerouted me without trying to put me back on the original route it chose. This is quite different from most units. Normally I get “turn around when possible” or “recalculating” over and over – not this time.

I finally did let it put me on the interstate, about 5 miles from home. When I reached my exit is showed very clearly what lane it wanted me to use, and it was very obvious when I was to turn.

I use the American female voice that reads street names. She enunciates very clearly and is easy to understand. Many GPS units sound tinny or have a buzz when the voice is active, but this one does not. My old Start 40 sounded clear too and did not buzz. I think perhaps TomTom does a better job with designing their units for sound.

One thing I use my GPS for is speed tracking. When in an area where there are no posted speed limit signs, it is nice when the GPS shows the speed limit and your current speed. For this one, though, the speed display is very small. It’s out of the way which is good, but I’d prefer a larger display or at least some ability to make it bigger. If there is a setting for that I have not uncovered it yet.

My primary complaint with this GPS is actually the menu system, which I find to be very clunky and odd. I don’t like it, and preferred the older menu system. It is workable, regardless.

Most GPS units that offered traffic do so through a special antenna or attachment in the power connector. Rather than offer this, this unit instead gets traffic updates via your phone through a Bluetooth connection. This is a double-edged sword. On one hand, it does not require that the unit be plugged in all the time and it becomes much more portable. On the other hand, it means that it pulls data and if you’re in an area where there is no data connectivity your updates aren’t available. I’m still deciding if I like this arrangement or not.

This is a good GPS with a little room for improvement in a few areas. The screen real estate is nice, and it navigates very well (better than most others I have used). It enunciates clearly and updates en route smoothly and quickly. The menu system is a little clunky, and there are some display settings I think could be better. Overall, though, this unit gets the important things right. It’s a good unit at a competitive price.

title: Good quality, but very heavy fully packed
text: Here's my disclaimer: I tried this backpack and thought it was good, but realized when I did a test pack I can't comfortably carry it fully packed for any length of time. Turns out I am a suitcase/carry-on person for travel, but if I WERE to be a travel backpack person, this would be the backpack I use. I was very impressed with the quality: the shoulder straps are padded, and I particularly liked the chest strap to better distribute weight. Though it was a bit of a squeeze, I did get one pair of sneakers, three days worth of clothes (dress, jeans, tops, sweater, underwear), a small toiletry kit, my makeup bag, odds and ends bag, Kindle Fire, large wallet, crossword book, and my phone into the backpack. The zippers are sturdy and I never felt like the bag was going to split, and the outside side clips helped compress and hold it together. The front pockets could have been slightly better designed, but still fit everything I needed, and I liked the key clip. The inside zippered pouch could only fit thin things, but it is nice to have the separation. It's doable to get three-days worth of stuff in this backpack, but will be heavy and make you a wide load (I kept bumping into things, not used to how large it stood off my back fully packed). That all said, if you want to travel hands-free, this is a great backpack to use!

Be sure to press down firmly along the strip once adhered to the floor to ensure full adhesion.

Final Notes: This product has a strong rubber/vinyl smell at first. It will wear off after about a weak. You may experience some difficult curling. You can bend this backwards quite a bit to adjust it and once applied to the floor it will eventually flatten out. If you have time an space, I would suggest rolling it out and putting light weights on the end to let it flatten for a day before applying.

text:
I have been using the Brain Driver for more than seven months with no issues. It is small, lightweight, easy to operate, affordable, and a single battery will last for months--I guess this depends on the battery, but that has been my experience.

The headband that comes with the unit is useful to some extent, I guess, but it is cheap and not of the quality or sturdiness of a real athletic headband. Mine started unraveling rather quickly, but I had already ordered medical tape to replace it. The cheap bulk roles of medical tape are much more secure and allow you to use any of the montages. The headband is very limited in how it supports the varied montages, so depending on what you're trying to do it isn't going to work anyway.

The sponges last a long time too. I make sure to squeeze them out and let them air dry after every use. I imagine they could get funky very quickly if you don't, but replacements are readily available. I believe that making things last is just as easy.

I don't think I can opine on whether or not this will be useful for anyone else. It has been for me. I would definitely recommend it to anyone interested in tDCS as an affordable, dependable, and user-friendly option.

title: HP Knocks it Out of the Park
text:
I have been in dire need of a new computer for a LONG time. My laptop is about five years old and takes about 10 to 15 minutes just to power up completely. I already have the use of a laptop from my workplace, so I don’t really need a replacement for it. What I need is a desktop computer to use when my laptop is still at work and this need was enough to convince me to get the HP Pavilion 24-inch All-in-One Computer, Intel Core i5-9400T, 12 GB RAM, 512 GB Solid State Drive with Windows 10.

Taken out of the box, consumers will of course need to set this computer up and get it ready. I am happy to say that the set up is about as simple as it could possibly be- much simpler than the set up of other pc’s I have owned, which shows just how long it has been since I have gotten a new computer. In under 10 minutes, it was ready to use. It was so easy, I started to worry that I had forgotten something, but everything was good to go.

This computer comes with a nice size screen- about 24 inches- which is the largest I have ever had in my house. It does make it easier to see things and I like watching videos and movies- something I didn’t like as much on my laptop, which had a screen about half as wide. The resolution and colors are good, too. I watched a few online videos and was impressed by how vibrant the different colors looked and how life- like people and faces appeared.

Having a touch screen is cool and this is something new for me. I have never owned a touch screen computer before and while I like and support new technology, I admit that this is taking time to get used to. I still prefer to use my mouse out of habit, but this will likely change in due time. It really is much easier to simply touch a screen and it makes navigation faster.

About the only issue I have with this computer is the fees charged for Microsoft Office. You get a free trial period, but after that, you will have to pay for the service. Considering the price of this computer, Microsoft Office should be part of the deal. I get that these companies need a regular revenue stream and charging for services was bound to happen but I still think it should have been an exception with this computer, given its higher than average cost.

Getting rid of my laptop is a great relief. With my HP Pavilion 24-inch All-in-One Computer, Intel Core i5-9400T, 12 GB RAM, 512 GB Solid State Drive with Windows 10 computer, my power up time has been reduced to under one minute and I have a viewable screen that is much more vibrant than before. I’m still a little irritated with the whole Microsoft Office thing, but it’s not enough to lower my rating, which is an easy five stars for this excellent HP product.

title: Great image quality but keeps losing connection
text:
I purchased two of these 4K cameras along with another bullet camera from Amcrest, all of them PoE and connected to a Synology NAS using Surveillance Station. I also recommend getting the Amcrest AMCPFB203W Wall Mount Bracket for Dome Cameras, as the long pig tail can be hidden in the bracket and installation is very neat, specially when mounting on a wall (Note that I have included photos for the camera and the bracket, but the bracket has to be purchased separately). If you do not use the bracket, the hole in the wall needs to be one inch wide. Waterproof protection is very good, so cameras are ideal for exterior installation. They include an adaptor to protect the RJ45 connector from moisture. I did not use the cables included for alarm connection and sound, so I taped them and put them inside the wall mount bracket. To be extra sure that everything was waterproof, I just added a thin silicone sealing between the bracket and the wall.
If you understand the basics of networking (IP addresses, DHCP, port forwarding, DDNS, etc), cameras are easy to configure. I would stay away if you do not understand these concepts. Adjusting the angle of the lense is also very simple and there is a lot of flexibility in terms of angle, so the camera is good for installation on a wall or a ceiling. However, lense orientation can only be changed manually, not remotely.
Image quality is great, but if you are using 4K resolution you cannot go above 10 fps or image will stutter continuosly. Form my point of view, that's just acceptable for a security camera (I am not trying to film "Out of Africa" here...). Alternatively, you can drop resolution to get 30fps. Handling all the cameras with Surveillance Station is great (Synology). I am handling motion detection with the Synology software as well, as the camera software had a small area that was continuosly giving false alarms, but not a big deal. Night vision works really well, although I do not need to reach a long distance, just my back garden.
The main issue is that these cameras will lose connection once or twice a day. One of them reconnects immediately (less than 1 min). However, the other one does not reconnect until the camera is rebooted. After that, it usually works for a few hours until connection drops again. I have them configure to reboot daily, but this situation is not acceptable (both of them have the same configuration, same firmware version, just different IPs and ports). The third AMCREST camera (a different model) is also fine. It loses connection once a day but recovers it immediately.
I have had these cameras for a year to monitor a remote location. It would have been 5 stars if connection would not drop so often. A common problem reported in forums.
Update: Following feedback from AMCREST support I changed the PoE switch for a new one from a different brand, but the problem remains. One out of the two cameras is faulty and needs to be replaced (unfortunately warranty is over).

title: Before Buying, Check What is Supported!
text:
I'm mainly writing this review so others know that your chosen m.2 drive probably won't work with this board. Go to this product's webpage and look at Storage QVL to find the 78 m.2 drives that are supported. I was planning on using a 1TB capacity, however there are only 7 supported 1TB m.2 drives! For specifics, I couldn't get the BIOS to recognize my Crucial P1 1TB NVME m.2 (M key) or my Samsung 860 128GB non-NVME m.2 (B + M key). I tried updating the BIOS to the 1.20 version but it didn't change anything. I went with a SATA based drive since the supported m.2 drives are older models and are either unavailable or too expensive since they aren't made anymore.

I bought this because it was mATX and has integrated WiFi. It seems odd to me that there are still so few boards with this feature. I looked on pcpartpicker and there are only 2 mATX boards with WiFi that are below $130. I didn't like the sound of the BIOS on the other board, so I went with this one. I've grown to dislike the issues surrounding USB WiFi adapters, so integrated WiFi it is.

Another thing. I wanted to make sure to apply the right amount of thermal paste so I put some on and placed the Wraith cooler on it and secured it down, and then pulled the cooler off the CPU to make sure that amount was enough and then I would re-apply. Now, I don't have too much experience with AMD MBs, but when I pulled the cooler up, I noticed my CPU wasn't there anymore. Weird. It was stuck to the bottom of the Wraith cooler instead. The plastic MB socket that moves over to hold the CPU pins in place must not have much force. IDK if it's just this MB's design or if this would happen on all of them, but it was weird and unexpected. Everything works fine still.

For the 2 chassis fan headers, I connected 4 fans with some splitters to make it work. Only 1 of these is a 4-pin header. The other is 3-pin. There's also a CPU fan header, but that's expected.

I purchased two 8GB DDR4 G.Skill 3000MHz DRAM sticks. They are spec'd at CAS 16 and 1.35V, but this MB displays the 1.35V setting in red, warning that it's too much voltage with this XMP profile. The system boots with it at 3000MHz and 1.35V, but running a benchmarking tool from PassMark, the CAS latency is 58ns compared to the advertised 16. I moved them over to my main system to test the two sticks and they benchmark at 18ns CAS latency (same test on both machines: PassMark's Performance Test). I ran a burn-in test (PassMark Burn-In) for an hour on CPU, GPU, and memory and they all passed without error so it's stable, but this MB slows the memory way down. You can see the test results in my pictures. Same XMP profile at 3000MHz and timing config in both systems. Slow system has a Ryzen 2700X CPU (8core/16threads) and my main system is running an i5 8600K CPU (6 cores/6 threads).

The BIOS on this board have a lot of setting choices. Not too many for CPU overclocking, but I was surprised by the length of a lot of the menus throughout it.

Not a con, but there are 4 USB 3.0 ports on the rear ports of MB and some other stuff, but it looks bare back there. The I/O shield is plain silver metal and it appears it's covering the whole area. I don't like the look. Poor explain job on my part, but yeah, you'll see.

I've been using this board for 2 days now and I might update this review if anything develops with it further. The board works, but I'm planning on returning the 2nd one I bought for another build. Overall, can't use the m.2 slot and memory is slowed down to worse than DDR3 speeds.

UPDATE: I've been using this board for 2 months now. I got the m.2 NVMe drive to work by forcing the gen3 speed in settings. Don't leave on auto. It's under one of the AMD NC or something settings. But... it still refuses to detect my m.2 SATA based drive (M + B key). I changed the m.2 detect setting to enabled (only in 1.50 BIOS, not available for download at this time) which is supposed to force the MB to see it. Tried all speeds (gen1, 2, 3, & auto). Nothing worked. I had to use a 2.5" SATA SSD for that build.
I ended up not using the SATA SSD mounting location because it's nearly impossible to route a SATA cable to it. I only tried a data cable and gave up before trying to connect the power cable too. I just stuck the drive below with the PSU so it was hidden in case's shroud and the cables were all right there so it worked out well. Zip-tied it to the power cable so it wouldn't bounce around.

This board works for the price, but it's not great.

title: Do your research before leaving a negative review.
text:
First of all folks, scratching is not caused by the performance of your record player, it's caused by static electricity that is created from dust on a dirty record! So please, clean your vinyl and think before you start blaming the company when it's actually your fault.

Secondly, I am basing my review off of the versatilty, sound, features, and price of this product.

1. Versatility: This 6 in 1 really speaks for itself in this category, so not much needs to be said. It has the capability to play records, cassettes, cds, fm radio, and mp3 via Bluetooth wireless!. Amazing!

2. Sound.. This is a little more subjective. If you have an external speaker to connect, you are good to go. If not, I wouldn't expect booming bass and toned mids from a product this small, and anybody would know that by reading the size of the internal speakers.

3. Price... For what this thing offers, it's definitely worth a buy for the following reason...

Durability... It seems this item is hit or miss as to the condition it arrives in. Mine was perfect, but judging on the reviews, I would advise purchasing the warranty for an extra 5 bucks.

5. Features... cannot rewind on the cassette player, but full control of cd playback. Vinyl components are good quality, but it is a manual setup, so you just need to set the needle yourself, no big deal. FM radio comes in clear with all the stations I tested, but no AM radio is available. Bluetooth is fully functional, just pair your phone, ipod, or mp3 device and you are good to go.

Bottom line, get the warranty, use an external speaker for desired sound quality, and guarantee one of these rarities in working condition because there is nothing like these on the market. Awesome value!

title: Improvements BUT headlights alarm keeps going off, has odd sound, yet somehow also too quiet
text: [[VIDEOID:24c6d2e5535cc5228343e102556bda97]] For the price, it's still a good buy. A lot of improvements over the previous model I had, though some of the same flaws still, and 1 step backward. The mobile app lets you record your route, DVR or download recordings to your mobile device, and control the dashcam from your mobile device (or at least change settings). Not recommended to modify dashcam settings or functions while driving regardless, of course. The picture seems clearer. The night vision option is arguably better, yet I found myself wanting a little bit more artificial brightening for the night vision. This is STILL an excellent and easy-to-install option if you want a back-up camera on your car, with an even larger display on this model, although I can guarantee that the suction cup mount will fall, and I honestly ended up using glue to keep it up, once I found the right spot. That's not a knock on this suction cup as it's a knock on all suction cups, but if you are worried about resale, or have a lease, the suction cup can work for awhile. Including a mount option that hangs off the mirror would be better for many. You'll have to glue or use gorilla tape or both to keep the rear camera up. The dashcam records excellent video, again arguably better, and has some quick preset options, and better power management options. That said, the parking monitor is unlikely to last more than 2-3 hours or so in my experience, and you probably want some external battery with a foldout solar panel if you want that option if your car is parked at work or something. A lot of the above criticisms are ones I had of my previous model, except for the artificial brightening of the rear camera, so there are improvements. But this new model has 1 major step backwards in my opinion, which a firmware upgrade should be able to solve. The old headlight alarm would sound once, and had a clear, decently loud sound (okay, could have been louder). The new headlight alarm is such a quiet odd tone that you could easily miss it, except for the fact that it will keep going off, even when you have your headlights on. I recommend 2-3 headlight alarms at most when the camera has external power going to it, and using a different and louder tone. I personally don't care if you reuse some existing tone in the camera. But it's honestly so annoying that I'll likely shut off this feature, which sucks, because it's a really nice safety feature for anyone with an older car whose headlights don't turn on automatically. I'd still recommend it, but a firmware upgrade to address some of the above issues, if possible, and inclusion of a mount to hang it from the rear-view mirror would make this a great buy. Video included. Shot quick on a phone, so apologies for quality. I learned a couple things since shooting it too. (UPDATED) I went back to my old dash camera. Honestly, the night vision displayed was just not good enough. Went to 3 stars.

title: Great if you have a lot of EF Glass
text:
[[VIDEOID:c15633aba65de18ca82713c6ad2a0ef4]] One thing that hasn't been clear to me and I don't blame this on the manufacture Viltrox but on the many reviews out there. I didn't notice until I began to use the speed booster that it will only work with EF Lenses, not EF-S lenses. Yes, this should have been a given with the idea being that this will take a mirrorless crop sensor camera and turn it into a full frame camera.

Now on the subject of Full frame. I'm using this with a Canon M50. Which has a crop factor of 1.6. This booster gives a plus 0.71. Meaning that this crops 1.136. For example EF 50mm 1.8 with the adapter is an 80mm with the booster it is a 56.8mm and also drops the F down to 1.2.

The images and video were all shot using the Canon 50m 1.8 STM. the first image is with the speed booster with aperture at1.2. The second is with the booster at 1.8. The third is with the Canon EF-m to EF adapter with the aperture set at 1.8. The video is with the speed booster.

I have used this both for images and video. With video, I haven't really noticed any issues other than the motor makes does make more noise than usual and the autofocus seems slightly slower when changing the autofocus from one subject to the other. The 50mm is dead silent when used without the booster, so I'm guessing that this is the motor in the booster. When tracking I've noticed no issue beyond the focus motor sound.

Who should buy this and who shouldn't? If you already have a collection of EF Full Frame lenses, slap this thing on and Bob's your uncle. If you are just starting out and on a budget, the EF-M to EF adapter may be a better option because you can use both EF and EF-S lenses. EF-S lenses tend to be cheaper and THEY WILL NOT WORK WITH THIS SPEED BOOSTER.

title: The Cadillac of Worksite Radios - Big and Packed with Features
text:
The U4 radio/Bluetooth speaker is big in every way. If the size and weight don't scare you off you'll enjoy excellent sound and battery life.

I bought this to replace a Sangean BB-100 that was stolen and it is a definite improvement in terms of volume level and features. The BB-100 always seemed a little too quiet even if it did sound pleasant. The U4 is loud enough for the campsite and a backyard BBQ but not loud enough for dance party. It might be too quiet for a large worksite too. Volume about 75% can start to experience some distortion depending on the tuning and music. I am super sensitive about this though. My kids were bumping some trap beats at 90% and it didn't bother them one bit.

The treble and bass controls are a nice touch and let you custom tune the sound (which is optimized for outdoors by default). Sangean is always able to get very dynamic sound out of a single speaker, but you don't get the surround sound from many Bluetooth speakers (like Sony or UE).

The battery life with rechargeables (sold separately) is excellent. The U4 made it through a week-long camping trip with 30+ hours of use at varying volumes between 25%-75% without dying. It is nice that they recharge in the radio and that you have the option to use alkaline batteries or to just plug it in to an outlet.
You can charge things with the USB port when the radio/speaker is not in use. The power output is a low 1Amp (like phone chargers 10 years ago), so if you plug your phone in overnight it might charge it up.

It is great to have AM, FM, and Weather band included. Weather comes in handy when camping or areas with bad phone coverage. As others have noted the antenna is a little short, but if you wrap or connect a wire to the metal base of the antenna you can boost the FM and Weather reception. I wish Sangean had included an external antenna jack for us nerds. They do this on most of their other radios and it is helpful. The attached antenna is short so that it can fold down and fit against the top of the radio (which makes it easier to store and travel with).
The digital tuner and screen with RDS (the text that displays the station and song information) work well as do the preset buttons and other controls.

Pairing is easy and the addition of aptX is cool (for nerds, again) but I don't think you can hear the difference.

It is heavy but well-built and durable. During an attack you could probably wound a black bear with it. A grizzly not so much, but the radio would survive even if you didn't so be sure to include it in your will.

With the purchase of rechargeable batteries added to the cost of the U4 you will most likely wind up spending over $200. If you don't need the extended battery life, radio, and other features you can get a better pure all-weather speaker for this price. For my needs the U4 is great and I don't think there is another product out there that could do better.

title: Before You Buy READ....Paring & Power Issue
text:
The Power strips work ok BUT I have an Android and had a hard time installing and paring the devices to my wifi. So I took the advice of another Reviewer and downloaded the Smart Life App, after that and some playing with find the right distance game, the power strips paired well. And as an FYI, I bought 4 of them.

HERE ARE A FEW ISSUES WITH THE POWER STRIPS YOU SHOILD BE AWARE OF BEFORE YOU BUY:

1.) Use the Smart Life App to pair and install the power strips, forget the app that comes with the instructions.
2.) You have to be right next (literally) to your modern and plug the ppwer strip within 1 to 2 feet for a successful pairing.

AFTER THE POWER STRIPS ARE INSTALLED AND WORKING. HERE ARE A FEW ISSUES I AM DEALING WITH:

1.) When you turn off the Power Strip through the app, I noticed that the individual power slots would NIOT turn off the plugged in device. So I simply unplugged the device and moved it to another outlet on the power strip ( the power strip has 4 power outlets and 1 USB port) that worked for about 4 or 5 days of me remotely controlling the power Strip through the app.

2.) Did that for days, each time 1 of the 4 power outlets wouldn't turn off the plugged in device, so I would simply, move and plugged the device in another power slot until finally I used all the four power plugs slots up.

3.) SO now, I could not remotely turn off any device from the power strips, ITS WEIRD, you can turn the ENTIRE POWER STRIP OFF REMOTELY But whatever you have plugged in WILL STAY POWERED ON!! Again even if you turn the entire power strip off. I have/had a small space heater plugged into the power strip, which I could turn on and off to heat my small office but with the power Strip NOT turning the power off, the heater just stayed on, no good.

4.) What I ended up having to do is uninstall and reinstall the power strips...A pain in the butt, BUT so far it seems to work. So. If they ever fix this flaw, the power stops would be a great investment but at the moment, its severally flawed.. And this issue is happening with ALL 4 power strips I bought and not just 1 or 2, ALL 4 OF THEM. If you have the patience go for it, if not..I would not recommend.

title: Works PERFECT. It's... AMAZING, My research / buying experience
text:
This monitor truly lives up to its hype. After much research and some short on hand experience with the ultra wide monitors, I have finally decided on the colossal Odyssey G9. In this long review, I will also give you guys what table mount I used which is also available on amazon, and what dp cable I used as well. I am currently running this monitor on a Asus GX701 / 2080 MaxQ.

The production dates are of importance to this specific statistic. The pre-july models SHOULD come with a blue round sticker indicating QC was rechecked and the bottom portion of the box may have new tape over it. 8th and 9th digit of your serial number is used to determine the manufacturing dates in case anyone is interested. "N" Stands for 2020 and the number after "5,6,7" corresponds with the production Month which I am sure there will be more in production as the year continues.

The importance of these dates is purely statistical and the primary concern for issues would be the backlight bleeding and glitching issues with Freesync on. By no means this applies to everyone who received their monitors in proper working condition but to those affected out of the pool of collected results. Normally I shy away from these but investing north of 1k has my research instincts firing on all cylinders. With that said, I would like to put it in perspective to the enthusiasts who want it laid out in easier terms.

May production dates were a coin toss of near 50/50 as notified by the packaging serial number N5
June production models were the most affected according to the pool of collected serial numbers and reviewers.(N6)
July productions were the very least affected and research shows samsung revised their QC guidelines. (N7)

So your chance of having a fully functioning / no bezel separation model for the July production dates are high and as long as the carrier delivering your package does their diligence, you will most likely be in the clear. 
Again the issues mentioned above are purely statistical and based on a group of reddit members. Keep in mind, negative reviews happen more quickly than those who have positive experiences with the product. I am positive that there are many positive experiences not publicized and as I am writing this, the 52 reviews on amazon is not the whole population of G9 users.
My biggest issue was table size and after researching the specs, realized I will have little to no room for my keyboard and mouse pad. I decided to have a desk mounted solution which amazon carries and it has worked out perfect for me and my other ultra wide monitor without a hitch. I will be writing a review on that as well. Link for the mount here: https://www.amazon.com/WALI-Monitor-Adjustable-Capacity-GSM001XL/dp/B07NLMLLT6/ref=sr_1_5?dchild=1&keywords=heavy+duty+monitor+mount&qid=1601493145&sr=8-5

Now for the monitor experience itself! (Finally)
Holy SH! batman! The ever so small dream of being in the future like some sci fi movies you probably won't be able to enjoy on this monitor due to it's 32:9 aspect ratio.... well the dream is now finally a reality and it's great! Not to say this is my first experience on an ultrawide but with the 1000r curvature, this truly is more eye pleasing and has me on the hook. Some say the angle is too aggressive but I believe the general consensus would say, you will adapt my overly critical friend. Shopping on amazon and searching for Odyssey G9 issues was never so much easier on this monitor. The initial settings Samsung has it pre-set to did cause some ghosting but with a quick search on google, the issue was solved and understood. (adjust your response time to "standard" and ghosting will be gone). I have tested functionality with free sync on looking for glitches or screen tearing which I have not been able to replicate. I may have to do further testing and more adjustments in graphical settings in an attempt to replicate some of the issues however I am starting to believe this could be due to cable choices of majority users (factory Samsung provided cables). I am by no means a cable engineer but I have done plenty of research which shows a quick cable change to a more superior put these issues to rest. HDR mode functions without a glitch, 240hz settings with freesync (in monitor options) work fine again without tearing or flickering, however I do not believe my GX701 or the 2080's current software is capable of recognizing this monitor as a gsync monitor so further testing and updates will be provided as I dig deeper into this option filled monitor. 

Now the main reason why I opted for this monitor was 2 things. The curve, and future proof. This monitor is full of features where the future is headed. Upgrading the monitor would most likely be the least of my worries for any of my other future hardware changes. I mainly use my computer for productivity and I do enjoy good quality gaming such as COD / Destiny 2 which is not as demanding as some of the other games out on the market. This monitor is more or less perfect for my application and truly sets a new standard to my home office / man cave vibe. 

I do currently have a small hiccup but I do believe the upcoming firmware updates will take care of these issues. 
-Turning off the computer does not turn off the monitor. (every single monitor I have had in the past never had this issue and they were all samsung monitors on this specific laptop).
****fixed**** samsung's website has a software (not firmware) for this monitor. Installed it and everything went back to normal correcting this issue.
-Gsync functionality with my current graphics card 2080 max q (laptop) does not give me the gsync functionality. (software update waiting from nvidia, and yes my laptop has a built in gsync monitor)

In terms of Cable, I am currently using: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B087QJ4WHR?ref=ppx_pop_mob_ap_share 10ft cable as my laptop sits to my left and the monitor stand base to my right. The excess is just enough (wish it was 1ft longer) for proper cable management. 

Conclusion:I personally have no issues with Samsung's Odyssey G9. I have returned 1 prior to this as I purchased it from best buy and video caught the fedex driver dropping my package and the production date was N5 meaning May of this year with a blue QC sticker. I didn't even bother opening and brought it straight back in for the return. The one I am currently reviewing is a N7 (July Production date model) and with much confidence I opened this package with a smile and am very pleased with this monitor hence my 5 star review.

**UPDATE**

It has been well over a month with no additional software downloads or changes to my hardware. Everything works perfectly fine. I haven't heard any crackling noise and there is no light bleed.

Added some photos to help and entertain you folks of my set up!

I find that the device disconnects from my computer within 5 minutes of connecting, sometimes less. It makes it very difficult to transfer music to it. Maybe it's because I'm on a Mac. It will continue charging as long as its hooked up to USB, but has often disconnected in the middle of transferring music to it, so I have to transfer little bits at a time until it disconnects, and then I have to get it to reconnect by unplugging it, plugging it back in again, and waiting for the prompt to charge and listen or transfer. Sometimes it gets stuck and won't reconnect, in which case I try holding the power button to make it reboot, but it will take a few minutes to spin a circle of dots on the display as it thinks about it.

text:
I ordered the 'RALENO LED Video Lighting Kits With 75inch Light Stand, 1 Durable Handbag And 2-Pack 384 LED Soft Video Light, Built-in Lithium Battery 3200K-6500K Video Lighting Kits For YouTube Photography Shooting' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts.

I ordered this kit to add more lighting options to my photography gear. My first impressions were that this kit is pretty complete in the sense that you get two lights with A/C power cords, stands for both lights, two shoe mounts and a decent carry case. With that said, I was not so impressed with overall quality of all included items. However, for all that you get in this kit, I am still quite impressed. Although this kit isn't of the best build quality it most definitely has great value with all that is included. The lights themselves are smaller than I had expected and the highest brightness setting isn't as bright as I hoped, yet it still has a place, and has come in handy many times to ad a bit more lighting to some of my projects.

I love that it includes the soft case and that the lights themselves have screens on the back that will actually show the color temperatures as well as the brightness level. I have more expensive lights that just have knobs on the back to adjust these settings with no easy way to know what color temperature you are at. This in-of-itself is a huge bonus as far as I am concerned. With this set I an easily select the exact color temp for each light to match. The stands are pretty basic. They are lightweight and easy to set up and take down. I am not so impressed with the quality of the Hot Shoe adapters as they are hard to solidly tighten the angle down without feeling like I am going to break the plastic knobs. They do function however, and I do appreciate that they included these, otherwise you would not be able to adjust the angle of the lights. The soft carrying case is decent and does have some padding if you don't throw out the included foam inserts.

Overall I find this kit to be effective, and have found that even though I may criticize many aspects of it, I do find myself using it quite often because of how convenient and easy to use and set up. There is most definitely value to this kit and I think that it would make a great lighting starter kit as well as a kit to ad more lighting options to your current lights. I hope that this was helpful.

title: Top notch webcam vs all the others
text: I acquired 4 different webcams in the thirty to fifty dollar 4+ reviews range this week as the wife needs a higher quality webcam for work.  This unit is near the top of my list of quality cameras.  The manual focus feature is actually a really nice feature to have... all the others I tried out this week don't offer that feature.  Also, this webcam is plug-n-play with Windows (Windows auto-detects the needed device drivers and installs them the first time you plug it into a USB port).  The microphone is active right away (red LED indicating its powered on) and when you activate the video camera, a green LED lights up.  The picture quality of the camera is really good, it auto light balances well and colors and image quality are near perfect... definitely 1080p quality.  This unit also comes with the tripod stand which screws into the base and the cord is plenty long.  My only gripe is a lack of a lens cover to guarantee privacy.  If you get this webcam, get in the habit of unplugging it after use to ensure privacy or find something to cover it (postit note works).  Overall, this webcam is a good solution for someone wanting an upgraded webcam vs the 720 laptop lens that just don't visually look that great for video conferences.

title: Misleading product info
text:
I had to replace my old eTrex 20. I got the eTrex 22 rather than a used eTrex 20 in part because it advertised greatly increased internal memory, 8G. Well that is a flat out lie on Garmin's part. Out of the box, it has less than 1G memory available to download your own maps. The mapset I had installed on the 20 will not fit on the 22x! yeah sure it comes preloaded with a map but I won't be able to tell if it's as good as my old one for some time and I'd rather not find out by getting out in the back of beyond. I was expecting to be able to have my old map set which is very detailed for my corner of the world, and then the preloaded map for the rest of the country. Nope. That was pretty much the only 'improvement' of the 22x over the 20 and it isn't even real. Other than that it's great if it's just like the 20 but I am not happy with Garmin, this is bait and switch.

I've had a chance to take it out in the woods now. The built in map appears to be thorough, the couple of trails I've tried it on, but the symbology is very poorly done. Would not get a good grade in any cartography or GIS class. The trails are shown as a very thin faint dashed line which doesn't show well against the colored background used for National Forest land. I have to be zoomed in pretty far to see it. Water courses are all symbolized the same - the same thin blue line no matter how big the river or small the creek. This is very poor symbology. It's not communicating the information you have a right to expect from anything calling itself a topo map. So no I do not want to use the built in map (that takes up nearly all the 8 G of memory) as my primary map, yet there's no room left in memory to install the map I used to use on the previous version.

text:
If you use the TV as a stand alone, or connected to a blue tooth sound bar it works fine. The problem is that this TV is very very invasive. Wants to know way too much information about you, browsing history and so forth. I wanted just a high end quality set for movies and some TV viewing. The TV wants to do all the connections on it's own and seems to resist letting the operator set up the choices on ones own. Maybe this is saying something about where we have evolved as a society. The TV takes the fun out of playing with the gadgets and knobs. If you are brainless and want the computer in the TV to do all the work, then this is a great set. The menu is not user friendly. The remote is a little wand with little choice of functions. You have to load the app on your phone for more functions regarding the TV control. If you have any old school regarding video or audio, this is not for you. If you want to give your control over to skynet: this will work for you. If you are looking for a lifelike picture: it will take a lot of adjustment of setting to get you there. Life is not in a glossy shine appearance. Very disappointed in the set.

Update: less than 90 days into ownership, had to contact Samsung, let them take over TV, Channel List for broadcast disappeared, would scan, but no way to get to scanned list. Kept jumping back to Samsung TV. Even they could not explain. Took about 30 minutes in all to get the problem worked out. TV will turn itself on sometimes. The computer in this TV has some serious glitches. 48 hours after getting the channel list fixed, it has disappeared again. Unless you like talking to service people, then I can say Avoid The Samsung line. I used to be a fan of the product name. This has been a major disappointment. Picture is very good, but I should have invested in another brand.

Update: the TV updated itself. The update has made the broadcast channel list all but useless. It keeps turning itself on after it is turned off. Keeps changing it's mind when you push the return button. It is some kind of real glitchy. I recently replaced my cell phone: I did not return to another Samsung.

Latest Update: Now we find that if you use the Pandora app on the Samsung: the sound does not play. Pandora app works as it should: just no sound. From what information found: this is not an isolated incident.

title: Bad Customer Service
text:
I have used hyper 212 evos in PC builds for years, and have always recommended them to anyone looking for a cooling solution for their PC. I no longer recommend buying this product, or buying any Cooler Master product for that matter after my recent experience with them.

I picked one of these up for a PC build for my dad for his birthday. I've always found the performance of this heatsink to be good, and the price to performance ratio is unmatched. I usually pick up a second fan and set it up in a push/pull configuration to maximize performance. The problem is that when I went to assemble, I was missing parts. Specifically, I was missing the brackets for the second fan. The fan brackets are shown to be included in the manual (part 'N'), and having purchased this exact model before (and many hyper 212 evos over the years) I know that these are included and had to have been accidentally left out.

I figure, no big deal, I will reach out to Cooler Master and request the missing part. It took them over a month to respond to me, and when they did, their customer support agent tells me I'm wrong, they do not include additional fan brackets, and sends me a copy of the manual. At this point I'm frustrated, as having purchased this exact item before, I know what it comes with, and the manual they sent me clearly shows the parts I'm missing being included. I responded to them pointing out more clearly what part was not included, and I have yet to hear anything back. At this point, I'm not holding my breath for a response, and I sincerely doubt that they will ever be sending me the missing parts.

I ended up having to zip tie the additional fan to the heatsink. Although this works, it is not the most elegant solution, it is not the solution I paid for, and it is not what I had in mind when building this computer for my father as a gift. It feels incomplete, and although I don't think it bothers my father at all, it does bother me.

Although fan brackets may seem trivial, it is Cooler Master's lack of customer service that has left me with a very bad impression. I received an incomplete product, and when I reached out to them to make it right, they were unresponsive, unhelpful, and indifferent. I would be extremely hesitant to buy any of their other products as my experience has shown the lack of support behind them. What good is a warranty if it doesn't mean anything? Where would I be if I had purchased a faulty power supply or had my keyboard malfunction? I prefer to do business with companies that stand behind their products, and unless something changes, I don't think I will be doing business with Cooler Master any longer.

title: good Surface Pro accessory, great customer service
text:
I got this dongle so I could use my USB-C PD charger as my all-in-one travel charger, to power both my phone and my Surface Pro. The first dongle I received didn't work though -- it would light up when connected to my PD charger + cable and to my SPro, but the battery icon would not show that it was charging.

I contacted the vendor, and they went above and beyond. First of all, they walked me through some simple troubleshooting steps, to make sure the dongle was the issue (and not the charger or cable).

When we isolated the issue to the cable, they asked for my address so they could send a replacement. I asked if they could send it directly to me in the Philippines (instead of my US address), and they did, with the customer rep (Francis) even paying for the shipping himself.

And to top it all off, when the package arrived, he had sent me not just the dongle, but their USB-C to Surface Connect cable -- both of which are currently working perfectly. :)

I can't speak yet to the durability of the products, but they work so far. But I can definitely say that their customer service is top-notch. Always great to have a company stand by their products.

title: Value Greatly Exceeds Price
text:
Overall: Sufficiently fast, functional and durable. Corded peripherals, but long enough, and plenty of ports. No complimentary office programs. Tilts, but doesn't swivel, making it hard to see where to plug things in. Not a touch screen.
Hardware:
Energy usage is under 60 watts, even using high performance settings.
Outside width 21".
The already-attached 9-1/2" base is plenty stable, but is so slip-resistant that you can't twist the monitor without lifting. The button markings for power and brightness are tiny and unreadably dark.
The left side has 1 USB 3.0 and 1 sleep-and-charge. Of the 4 USB 2.0 in back (towards the left), one is missing the inner black plastic spacer, but it still works.
To see the Caps Lock light, you have to look almost straight down at it.
The bright plastic above the speaker is NOT a volume-control slider, but a logo. There are no physical volume control buttons, and the keyboard has no hot keys.
The microprocessor is not literally a 4-core, but 2 double-threaded ones, which is hardly different to the layman, but still an unethical claim. Although the speed is up there--my primary desire--multitaskers prefer more cores. What greatly cuts costs and limits crashes is the built-in graphics, which are fine for all but the most extreme video editing and gaming. Good luck finding that fast of a processor + that much memory + flash storage for less than triple this price, if new.
Software:
Clear written instructions for setting up the operating system. READ AND FOLLOW. Lenovo passes the buck to Microsoft concerning issues needing tech support.
Startup takes half a minute.
Despite Microsoft Office icons showing up in the start menu, you have to pay for them to work.
Not only are there minimum requirements for logging in, there are extreme restrictions on naming certain files and folders. These are nuisances for me, being a solo home user.
Nicely 64-bit, rather than x86 (32-bit).

I called the company & a ttech instructed me on how to change the settings. He said that once the brightness was reduced, the text should be fine. Not so.

I was able to reduce the brightness, but it still hurts my eyes. Reducing it further makes the screen look muddy, so not an improvement. And, the text is still not black. On apps that have some things written in grey, the text almost disappears.

I tried to see if I could adjust to it, but no, I can't. And that's too bad because the monitor does have some good points. The size (28") is perfect for me and the color is amazing. Really, the best I've seen. Unfortunately, I didn't get this monitor to look at photos--I got it t, primarily, to read text.

Here's the thing, if you have great eyes--which I do not--the less than black, not quite sharp, text may not bother you at all. And maybe the odd brightness won't make your eyes sore like it does mine. For me, it's a not go. Fortunately, Amazon is allowing me to return it.

title: Bose vs. Sony: use case matters
text:
Don’t write reviews often but I recently struggled with the decision between these headphones and the Sony wh1000mx3. I ended up purchasing both to test and landed on the Bose. First and foremost, these are both phenomenal noise cancelling headphones and most people would be happy with either. Just to name a few things I liked about each product and why I seemingly went against the grain and chose the Bose over the Sony’s:

Fit: both were extremely comfortable. I give a slight edge to the Bose as I received a little less clamping force. Mind you I have a larger sized head so most people likely wouldn’t perceive the difference.

Controls: I preferred the Sony’s controls only because I feel like everything is touch now and it felt natural. I know there is a cold weather issue but I’m mostly using these indoors in an office setting and occasional air travel. I also preferred Sony’s inclusion of usb c.

Sound(music): simply put my ears preferred the Sony sound. The Bose sound very good (neutral) but I preferred the sound of the Sony’s.

Phone: and here is why I chose the Bose. And this is where for me, my use case meant the Sony’s were not an option. The Sony’s were unusable on work conference calls. Even in a quiet environment other participants couldn’t hear me. The Bose were exceptional in this regard. Also, the ability of the Bose to connect to two Bluetooth devices simultaneously is invaluable (for my use case).

In summation, both are great headphones and you should really determine your use case before deciding. For me, the Bose voice quality and the seamless Bluetooth connectivity between multiple devices out weighed the Sony’s exceptional noise cancelling, controls, and audio sound.

title: Some problems ....
text:
1. this requires a button press to program with the Arduino environment. Just get a modern model that doesn't need this.

2. WIFI does not work out of the box. You need to put a hefty tantalum capacitor (5-10uF) across 3.3V and GND (last pins on 2 sides, opposite from USB). Otherwise the power surge from WIFI reboots the device instantly when you turn on WIFI. This is unacceptable. The capacitor should be on the board. In fact, there is a tantalum cap near the 3.3v regulator on the board, but it is probably too small (a cost cutting measure?) Why sell a WIFI board if WIFI doesn't work?

But after you do this (after struggling for a few hours figure it out), and once you've installed the USB driver and development module, you can make a simple WIFI web server. But spend a bit more on a better module.

title: A phenomenal budget CPU for $99.99...  when you can ACTUALLY buy it for $99.99
text:
The Ryzen 3 3100 is an excellent value CPU for the average gamer looking for a CPU that can handle the rigors of high fidelity, high FPS gaming... that is of course, provided you can actually buy it, for $99.99

For whatever reason, AMD has seen fit to jack up it's price by 30 USD, to $129.99, which is 10 dollars LESS than their Ryzen 5 2600. The 3100 and 2600 may butt heads in terms of real life gaming performance, but at a 10 dollar difference, I can't recommend someone spend 10 dollars less for 2 less physical cores and 4 less threads, especially with the advent of newer games that are more heavily reliant on multi-core processing.

In short, unless AMD re-lowers the price of the 3100 back to it's original MSRP of $99.99, do yourself a flavor and just buy a Ryzen 5 2600, unless those 10 dollars REALLY mean that much to you.

text: This is my second NAS, my first being a Synology 412+, their primary purposes are to act as a multimedia server for both music and video and as back up for my computers and in the case of my older NAS to now act as multimedia back up to this newer QNAP NAS which was purchased to allow increased capacity over Synology which maxed out at 16 TB (<11 TB in raid 5 conf.). title: Lots of compromises, but good ones
text: Let’s start with the obvious: this is not a Really Right Stuff 3-series pod with an Arca Cube on top—and that’s a good thing. There are times when light weight and compact size  trump rock solid stability. For those times, this is an excellent choice at an amazing price made by a quality company. Comes with everything you need in a tripod, including a small ball head with an Arca clamp and a hook for hanging weight or accessories. Folded up, it fits inside a Peak Designs 20L Everyday Pack. I am not a fan of ball heads, so I substituted an Arca L60 leveler, and it worked just fine. I am also not a fan of center columns—and this has a two-stage telescoping column—but the height has to come from somewhere. Again, if you’re driven by weight and size, you’re going to have to take your medicine. On a recent trip to Italy, I carried the PD20L for compactness and discretion. On most days, I carried two Hasselblad X1D bodies, an XCD 135+1.7TC, a Canon TS17, and an XCD 30 and 45. And this tripod. All *inside* the pack. The Hasselblad plus telephoto and TC push the limit on this tripod, but in light-to-no wind, it was fine. It’s easy to jostle, because it’s so light, but using the self-timer and/or a shutter release cable gives it a chance to settle down. Normally, I would carry a much larger, more obvious Shimoda photo backpack, but for discretion and maneuverability in large crowds, this was a great choice. Feels flimsy, but is well made. It won’t take the permanent place of my smallest Novoflex or RRS (I carry the most solid tripod I can fit in my case or backpack), and I am looking forward to comparing it to the incoming Peak Designs Travel Tripod. But it also costs between 1/5 and 1/10 of those other sticks. Compromises and all, that earns it 5 stars.

title: Upstream Bonded Channels too low power
text:
After trying to do self-install with Xfinity, I had to order an installation service from Xfinity. The technician did spend over 2 hours to check and update the cabling outside and inside. This didn't resolve the persistent upstream problem. His test modem confirmed that the cabling and internet connection was ok. His conclusion was that my SB8200 was defective. I did contact Arris before returning the modem to Amazon. We did repeat the Xfinity installation steps with the same results. I am disappointed with their support because they didn't identify the real problem.

After replacing the SB8200 with Motorola MB8600 all problems disappeared. The self-installation was fast and easy. My conclusion is that the SB8200 had too low power levels. With SB8200, the channel 17-20 levels were between 37 and 38 dBmV. With MB8600, the power increased to 40.0 - 41.0 dBmV.

title: Comes pre-formatted with space eating partition (and there's no tool to erase it for macOS users)
text:
Comes formatted with a stupid space eating partition. macOS diskutility can only see the larger portion and format *that*. I was annoyed that I needed to take time to look up how to format the drive, since it's partitioned in a unique way that means I can't just erase it using macOS Disk Utility

To fully format the drive you need to open the terminal and run "diskutil list" no quotes and find the device with the same capactity as your usb (ex: for me it was /dev/disk3)

BE EXTREMELY CAREFUL WITH THIS COMMAND, SINCE IF YOU SELECT THE WRONG DRIVE YOU WILL ERASE YOUR HARD DRIVE, NOT THE USB DRIVE. BACK UP YOUR FILES BEFORE RUNNING THIS COMMAND. CONSIDER VISITING A GENIUS BAR FOR ASSISTANCE IF YOU ARE NOT COMMAND LINE SAVVY - SHOW THEM THIS POST AND SAY YOU WANT TO REFORMAT THE USB WITH A SINGLE PARTITION.

Ok, warning out of the way. Now that you've IDed the drive (in my case /dev/disk3)

Then type the following and hit enter:

sudo diskutil eraseDisk FAT32 thirtytwogb MBRFormat /dev/disk3

(You will be prompted for your administrator password - sudo means "super user do" and is how one runs a command as the administrator on the command line. "thirtytwogb" is the name I gave my drive, you can pick a different one if you'd like)

You may need to use a different format if you want to save files >4GiB to the disk.

If you're not terminal savvy, just run the command above and then use the GUI disk utility app to reformat again as a Mac filesystem.

title: Minirig 3 vs. Denon DSB-250
text: These are both great speakers - no frills but focused on producing excellent sound.  In my opinion, both are superior to Bose and UE speakers in the same price range, namely around $200.  So, which is better.  It is a close contest.  The Denon is a solid brick of a speaker, about 8" long, square, and very attractive with the grey stripe scheme.  Solid in your hand, exudes quality.  It has rich, clear sound and surprising bass.  Denon is a serious AV company and it shows in this speaker.  Really crisp sound, no reliance on acoustic tricks or inflated DSP.  Battery life is great.  All in all a quality speaker for someone who values premium sound and wants no bells, flashing lights or gimmicks.  Now, the minirig 3.  I had read glowing reviews, but frankly I was doubtful a single driver in such a small enclosure could put out quality sound.  Boy, was I wrong.  The minirig 3 has amazing sound.  Clear sound with balanced bass.  And it can go loud.  Louder than the Dennon.  Frankly, it is amazing the quality of sound this little speaker puts out.  LIke the Denon, it is built like tank.  Industrial looking.  Only one button, on/off.  It also has an app for adjusting the sound, and like the speaker, it is all business.  Works well.  Comes with a case and charging cord.  While the Denon is impressive  as you might expect, the minirig will stop you in your tracks with its quality of sound.  It simply beats the Denon in all areas in terms of sound.  A good competitor for the minirig 3 is the Bose 500 Home Speaker.  Side by side the same about the same in terms of bass, soundstage and clarity.  Of course, the Bose is over twice as much, four times as big and is not portable.  So, if you are on the fence about buying a minirig 3, go to your local Bose store and listen the Bose Home Speaker 500.  The minirig compares well to it.  Why the minirig 3 is not on more best bluetooth speaker lists baffles me.  It trounces my Bose Revolve and Minlink II.  UE Booms are also inferior to the minirig 3.  It is the best bluetooth speaker I have owned, and I think that ounce for ounce it can compete against any speaker, wired or wireless.  Highly recommended.

text: There’s great value in using this smart digital photo frame to share pictures with my mom who lives far away. Setup is easy by following the included instructions to download the app from Apple or Google stores. The app allows multiple people to send pictures. A sender needs to download the free app, setup an account, and input a frame ID number (unique to the digital photo frame unit) for security. Then you can begin sending photos to the photo frame. title: Same quality as their previous AirPods case but, at a price that's fair.
text:
Previously, I had a DamonLight case for my original AirPods. For both, I was looking for a case without an additional back rubber hinge connecting the top & bottom. I didn’t want something that could easily break or, that might snag on something. This seemed like the right one. Additionally, the overall design of the case was simple and clean. No blatant logos or graphics.

Fit:
The material is a matte finish and the fit is next to perfect. If you follow the simple instructions (sent via email), it goes on without any issues. The charging port on the bottom is also a near perfect fit. It doesn’t obstruct my various (Apple & non-Apple) cables in any way. I was a little worried about the top piece slipping off from time to time but, it hasn’t moved since I put it on and these are in and out of my pocket and bags at least 10-12 times a day. I believe, after massaging the pieces on, you’re essentially rubbing out the excess air and it really seems to hold the pieces firmly in place.

Material:
The silicone has a soft-rubber feel to it. It’s not sticky at all. There's also no factory smell (like some cases can have). The case has some grip to it but, I have no problem taking it out of both, my dress slacks and jeans. It’s not a case that would protect you from a major drop but, it is great protection against scratches and thin enough to not make the case feel bulky. The case collects a small amount of lint (something I thought would bother me a lot before buying it) but, it isn’t as big a deal as I had originally thought. And it wipes clean fairly easily. Additionally, the charging light can still be seen through the case so, that’s a plus.

Price:
I bought this for $10. For the materials used and the thought that went into the design of it, I think paying $8-$10 is a fair price. (The original case for the older AirPods were $13 and that price was definitely too high.)

I’d definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a well-fit case with a clean design. If I have any issues down the line, I’ll be sure to give an update.

title: Works great!
text:
This turned out to be a great investment. Recommendations -
1) Set up with a turnbuckle on each end, with the turnbuckles extended as far as they can go. Buy turnbuckles about 8-12 inches long. Turnbuckles are not included in the package but can be purchased at a hardware or home improvement store. They can probably be bought on Amazon as well
2) Loop the cable on one end thru one of the turnbuckle's loop and fasten the cable together with 3 of the included clamps
3) Loop the other end of the cable thru the other turnbuckle loop
4) Have one person pull the cable as tight as they can while the other person fastens the cable together with the other 3 included clamps
5) Rotate the turnbuckles in the appropriate direction to tension up the slack
6) Cut off excess cable to desired length. Leave enough excess on one end in case you need to perform a redo

I only used 1 turnbuckle on one end and wish I had used 2. I will redo the setup in the spring. However, it has worked out very well allowing our puppy to freely roam the back yard with a 15 foot tether. My setup was 115 feet long.
