title: First impressions compared to the Echo Dot 3rd gen
text:
We only owned a single 2nd gen dot and 2 3rd gen dots. I saw the echo 3rd gen was new and on sale during Black Friday weekend for $60, so I grabbed one. We wanted another echo dot but after reading and watching reviews I decided to spend a bit more and go with a full blown echo.

The echo dot 3rd gens are amazing. They really are. For $22 on sale they are especially a no brainer. The sound quality is night and day compared to the 1st and 2nd gen dot. Like twice as good regarding sound quality and fullness and how loud it can get. Alarms will actually wake you.

After watching some reviews of the new big echo here, I was sold. Now and then we use the living room echo for some music while we clean or to just goof off and dance like idiots lol. While the dot did good, why not go fuller and louder with the big echo?

Well, it’s still an amazing unit. Does all the dot does, of course. However, while the sound is fuller and louder, it’s not going to blow you away. I guess maybe I overhyped it based on the reviews I saw and their reactions, but I was a bit bummed.

Yes, absolutely it’s louder...my totally unscientific measurement would be it’s like....15-20% louder and fuller sounding (deep, more bass, higher highs etc). I’m not sure what I was expecting. Maybe I’d be happier regarding sound with the “studio” version? I don’t know. I don’t regret the purchase, though. The extra volume is welcome and it definitely does sound better with music. Happy but I believe I overhyped. If I had the money, I’d def replace the dots with the full echos. Only pluses and no negatives other than being less amazing as I had made it in my own head.

title: Good Sound with Disappointing Battery Life
text: This device has very good sound reproduction with the option of adding more bass but not TOO much. Without the added bass it has very good flat response throughout the spectrum with good highs, midrange and bass. It is fairly light and travels well with the carrying strap. I only gave 4 stars for the "sound quality" because I believe it could have been just a bit louder. I went with 5 stars on "water resistance" because it has good seals around each of the speakers and the connections are protected with a heavy plug that requires a good amount of force to remove assuring that it has a very tight seal. The manufacturer claims the battery life is 20 hours depending on the volume. I was lucky to get around 10 hours even when I was running it low volume most of the time which is why I gave "battery life" 2 stars. Part of the problem, I believe, would probably be that it doesn't have an auto turn-off when it sits idle for more than 5 or 10 minutes. And it is constantly trying to reconnect wirelessly to the media device. My guess is that if you turned it off, every time you stopped playing media through it, it would allow the battery to last a lot longer.  All in all, it is a very good speaker for the money - just put it on the charger every night after use.

title: Plushy Home for Surface Book 2
text:
Edit: Over a year later and this bag is still in the same condition. It works great, has seen plenty of use, etc. I'm very pleased. I've bumped this from 4 to 5 stars because it's as advertised and beyond.

OG review--
Overall, this bag came as advertised. The first thing I actually noticed was that the handle seems to be made of leather/synthetic leather, which I'm not fond of. This appeared to be the best case on the market currently for the Surface Book 2, and -insert most of the rest of my review-, so I'll get over it, though.

I read some reviews complaining about the side zipper... I like it. I could understand if the pull was on the side but it's not, it's on the top. You actually have to pull the zipper pull up around the corner to the top of the case. This, in my opinion, would be rather difficult to knock out of place so much that you somehow open it up enough to cause damage to the contents of the bag.
It's a good zipper, not a cheapy one, as far as I can tell.

The inside where the device goes really is only going to be ideal for device storage. Don't expect to put paperwork, cables, your left shoe, grandma, etc. in there. I have the 15" Surface Book 2 and am able to fit it snugly inside this bag with the Surface Pen attached. I wouldn't add anything else to this compartment.
If you need additional space for bigger items, stop now, look for a different bag suitable for for device.

More on the device compartment: It's so soft in there. Seriously, like a baby blanket. I would sleep in there if I could... Anyway, I do have some concerns about devices bring hot and tucked away in this plushy heaven, but my device is actually pretty great so I don't have this problem. It is something to keep in mind if you often carry around a pocket-sized jet engine.

(Still on device compartment... Sort of?)
The corners of this bag have reinforcement, which is awesome. If you drop this, it should be pretty safe... I don't recommend dropping it. I did squeeze and prod at the edges quite a bit and it all seems rather sturdy, which makes me feel comfortable putting my $2k+ device in there.

Okay, now we'll talk about the front pockets. There are two. Neither are big enough to comfortably hold the detachable strap because of its shoulder pad. You can technically fit it diagonally into the bigger pouch but then there's really no room for anything else. I was annoyed by this, as I don't see myself using the strap as often but I like to keep things together.
Aside from that, the pouches are good for everyday use for general device/carry-with-you items. The bigger pouch is good for your charger, maybe a portable drive or battery, etc.
The smaller pouch has some inserts for pens and whatnot, so you can bring those items along. There's enough room for a phone charger or other small device/cables.
If you stuff these, they will push towards the device compartment of plushy goodness so I'd recommend storing your device screen towards you and not the pouches. Do bear in mind that these pouches are also shorter than the case itself, albeit not by much.

Now the exterior, handle aside as I covered that first...
The clips for the strap are plastic. I know this bothers some people. It does seem sturdy, however.
There is no luggage strap on this model.
It feels durable overall but not rugged.
It does appear to be water-resistant but I didn't heavily test.

I like this case. If that changes, I'll be back here updating this review.

title: Not bad for the price
text:
The Macally Wireless Bluetooth Keyboard is a good choice. It appears sturdy and the keys are responsive. The touch and travel of the keys are similar to those on the Apple Magic Keyboard. It sits nicely on desktop or on lap. The bottom panel is made of stainless steel and provides good support for the keyboard. Macally saves a bit of money, I suppose, by making the top panel of plastic. Bluetooth seems to work well; I sit with the keyboard about one or two feet from my MacBook Pro and have never lost connection. This keyboard goes to sleep a little too frequently for my taste. Perhaps this is to conserve battery life. And speaking of which, the battery life seems good. I charged it a week ago and it's still going well. I wish there was a way to check battery level, but sadly there is not. A useful feature is that there is a caps lock light to alert you when the caps lock is on. Unlike the Apple Magic Keyboard (which has the light on the caps lock key), the light is in the upper right corner, on precisely the opposite end of the keyboard from the key. That's kind of Windows keyboard thinking. Apparently Macally is trying to bridge the Mac and Windows world with this keyboard because they include an Fn key. They make room for it by making the Mac CMD key and the Option key half-size of those on the Mac keyboard. That's kind of a downside, and personally I feel they should make a choice: is this a Mac keyboard, a Windows keyboard, or just something trying to please everyone? But overall, it's pretty good and I will keep using it on my second Mac.

UPDATE 4/12/20: The internal battery seems to last about a week and a half, starting from full charge and without using the on/off switch. So if you turn the keyboard off every night, it will probably last quite a bit longer.

title: Wireless Backup Camera w/1080P monitor
text:
I work as a Service Manager for a auto dealer and I am very familiar with backup cameras and the OEM wired systems. I recently purchased a camper to use in the back of my pickup truck and I tow a boat behind the camper. I felt very uncomfortable towing the trailer because I couldn't see the boat or the trailer while driving. I looked at the wired system since my Lance camper was prewired for a backup camera, but I knew from experience that the wired systems were plagued with corrosion and connection problems that caused the camera image to be poor or fail entirely. I have a friend that recently purchased a new Lance camper and he purchased the new Voyager wireless system offered by the Lance dealer so I checked his system to compare it with a OEM wired system. I felt that the wireless system was as good or better that most wired system so I took a chance on the FHD 1080P system offered here.
It only took about 2 hours to install both cameras and the monitor - I mounted 1 camera up high to give a good view of the road and trailer while driving and the other camera down low to help with hitching the trailer and to get a better view of the tires and trailer load. The images are very good and the cameras are very easy to configure. The monitor comes with different mounts to make it easy to mount firmly on the dash or windshield. The image is so good I think I'll remove the windshield mounted mirror and mount the monitor in its place.
Great product overall.

title: Not great with the T90 or DT990. Ok with the DT770
text:
I bought these to replace the pads on my Beyerdynamic T90s as they're starting to show their wear after 5-6 years, I also own a pair of DT990s and DT770s.

Construction seems good, the foam was softer than I was expecting, though with how thick they are it's not a bad thing.

Comfort was generally good, though I'm not the biggest fan of the "Jerzee" material, it's a bit too slick and plastic like, I much prefer Velour. One nice thing is the pads are quite thick so they keep the earcup fairly far from your ear, which is great for people with large ears like me.

Audio wise is where these earpads fail for me.
T90: The second I put them on and tried them it was an instant change for the worse. No longer did the T90s have that extreme clarity and presentation of making me feel like I was at a recording in person, it now sounded muddled with a bass emphasis, with vocals receding to the back and just throwing the whole thing off balance.

DT990: Similar effect as the T90, though not as pronounced as the sound on these is already somewhat less forward than the T90s, but the thing the DT990s shined at was a clear presentation especially with female vocals which now sounded muddied and much more of a forethought than a commanding presence.

DT770: Going even further down the chain, these are already somewhat more recessed and closed sounding, though that's more of their inteded purpose, so the Jerzee pads seem a bit more natural for this sound signature, but they still close up the sound somewhat compared to stock pads, or another pair of velour pads I have.

Overall not a good match for Beyerdynamic headphones, and makes me wonder if they actually test these with all the headphones they list or do they just make a design, test it with one pair, find that it sounds decent and then just list anything it'll fit onto.

title: Plenty of Clean Dynamic Power
text: Outstanding stereo power amplifier with plenty of clean power on tap. The DPA-2 is very well constructed and feels solid in hand, it's heavier and more substantial than it appears in photos. I'm powering Elac Adante AS-61's with it and the sound is significantly better than using either my Denon AVR-3500H receiver or a Crown XLS1502 Drivecore professional amp. Power is similar to what the Crown offered, but much cleaner, punchier and with higher fidelity. The XLR and RCA inputs with a use selectable interface is very helpful as I can use RCA unbalanced for my home theater L+R main channels and XLR balanced for a streaming DAC for stereo listening. I really appreciate the nice screen with power level meters, it gives you a good feeling being able to see the audio levels. They do move slightly at zero volume, I did contact Elac and they assured me this is normal and the bars go up exponentially with watts, so the first couple steps are just tenths of 1 watt. I highly recommend the Elac DPA-2, I suspect it it more amplifier than I will ever need and will sufficiently cleanly power anything I throw it at and provide many years of usage.

title: Just received this.. here are some answers
text:
I just had mine come in and wanted to test everything out. I saw questions with no answers so I'll provide what I can now and update you as I test this out more.

* Slave mode - Yes... there is a button that has an "eye" on it. When pushed, the eye is visible on the display screen. It then waits for a flash to trigger it. The manual does not mention "slave" but I verified that even my on camera flash will set it off when enabled

* HSS (High Speed Sync) and TTL (Through The Lens)- NO and NO. The description says it does NOT support either which a lot of people seemed to have missed. I believe the Vision 5 does but the Vision 4 does not. If you are using HSS to keep a shallow DOF then an alternative is to use a ND filter or a variable ND filter. The ND filter will drop your stops of light; however, it won't effect colors and tones allowing a shallower DOF.

* Battery - I cannot verify yet as to how well it works.. I do not see a battery indicator and it says it will display when you are running low on battery and to charge it. This bothers me but I don't plan on going out with it uncharged for a long period of time.

* Modeling Light - There is a button to turn this on or off. The light stays on while it flashes (some modeling lights turn off briefly for the flash). 90% of the time, this will not be an issue to turn it on. It also is not adjustable.. so the brightness that comes out is what you get. You cannot lower it.

* Build Quality - It definitely feels sturdy. It has rubberized grip feeling and on the battery. Everything fits snug and is not loose

* Bowens - Has a Bowens mount on the front. You obviously have to take the beauty dish off for that .

* Features and Power - You can choose the Frequency function and have it flash x amount of times. It also is really bright when upping the output. Cycle time is also good. It also has an overheat alarm where it will beep telling you it has overheated and will not turn on until it cools down.

* Channels - There are channels you can set; however, I have not tried to control multiple flashes with the transmitter. I'm going to test it against my Neewer 16 channel (non-ttl) triggers.

I'll update more as I test it out.

title: Beast Mode
text:
I got a perfectly working Monitor! Read some of the other reviews on google and a few have noted that they get dead pixels and red or green lines across the screen but lets be real n think about it. Only those who get a bad screen take to the internet and post their experiences and everyone whos looking to get one just sees those reviews. The truth is Most people who get a working product dont tend to make reviews theyll just use it and never think to mention to the community how awesome a product is.

On to the review. I'm no monitor geek or know much about monitors, All I wanted was for the screen tearing to stop and to have smooth gameplay above 60fps without vsync on. Welp folks, we have a winner. I'm coming from the Samsung CF791 1440p Ultrawide 100hz and since my framerates were well above 100fps I did get some screen tearing and wasnt as smooth. With this monitor at 144hz everything is Milk! The IPS is GORGEOUS! I thought the samsung Quantum dots was nice but this... THIS is where the pixels are born! Colors pop and the HDR is also a HUGE bonus even though its not HDR10 WHO CARES! I opted for the 144hz Freesync over the 120hz Gsync model because it doesnt matter if you have 144hz monitor and over 144hz fps in game. I get no screen tear and everything looks buttery smooth. Not to mention $200 less.

Cons: Not really a CON for me but it will be for those who play First Person Shooter games. The input lag is 14ms according to my research. And I did research it because coming from a 4ms lag on my Samsung monitor I did notice something "different" when I was wiggling my open windows around but just BARELY. I don't notice it unless I actually do TRY to notice it but there is an every so slight delay in input lag. Again, I only noticed it when I first set it to 144hz and tested the response. But it my everyday use and RPG game play, I don't notice a damn thing. I'm sure you MIGHT notice the lag if you're a competitive gamer. But yea, that's the ONLY thing I thought is really worth mentioning.

title: "Renewed", but brand new, and a Great TV.
text:
The product we received was brand new. I don't think it was "renewed". If it was it was remarkably well "renewed".
The TV is great. Great colors, very bright. Samsung makes a very nice TV.
I bought the 82 inch model, and it is very heavy. Forget setting it up yourself. I guess it at around 120 lbs or so. There are two different locations that the stands can go in, one around 62 inches apart, and one about 52 inches or so. We bought a new stand that was 58 inches long, and the tv fit on it easily. Make sure your stand is at least 16 inches wide, as the stands are around 15 inches wide.
There is a quick set up guide that comes with it. It asks you to set the tv face down on a table, to install the stands. It warns you to make sure the table is larger than the tv, but with the 82 inch model, good luck with that. The way we did it was to lift the tv up vertically right out of the box enough so my wife could insert the stands in the holes they go into. The stands then snap into place, and stay there. We could then set the tv down on the stands. It is a great system Samsung has developed for the stands. No screwing a stand into the tv. Just insert the heavy duty stand into the hole (again, there are two holes on each side, choose the width you want for the stands) and you are done. Brilliant.
I also paired the TV with the matching Samsung sound bar, Q60R I believe. The sound on the TV is a little weak for me, only 20 watts. The sound bar is around 360 watts. It is so nice, as the sound bar is perfectly integrated with the tv. When you use the TV remote to adjust the sound, it automatically knows you have the sound bar....anyway, I'm not that tech savy, but it is so easy to setup. I got the "renewed" sound bar also, and it was indeed "renewed". Looks like it was repackaged. Works perfectly and looks brand new.
What a great system. Perhaps a little expensive, but so nice. Buy it "renewed and save 1000 bucks or so.

title: Great product to connect all your devices to your computer except it doesn't power the MSI GS65
text:
I am using an MSI G65 StealthThin 8Rf. I have a 27" ASUS monitor, several external drives, headphone, mic, etc. You can imagine the clutter of cables that are connected to this laptop. Each time I have to take my laptop with me (to work or meet a client), I have to disconnect all these cables. Ugh!

Looking for a docking station, I came across the CalDigit TS3. The reviews got me excited. Damn pricey, but if it can simplify my life and improve the management of all these peripherals, then the expense is justified.

The box came. The TS3, power adapter, power cord, a Thunderbolt 3 cable and the rubber feet. No instructions. The TS3 itself looks like it was built using fine materials. Classy looking silver finish. Unassuming,stealth on my desk.

The TS3 looked simple enough to get everything connected. I had to double check the voltage as I live in a country where we use 220V/60Hz. Yup, the power range covers that voltage. We're a global economy, shouldn't all appliances be supporting 100-240V and 50/60Hz?

I connect my monitor, all the external hard drives, headset and mic to the TS3. Connect the Thunberbolt 3 cable from the MSI G65 port to the TS3 Thunderbolt port where it says computer. Double check that folks.

Ok. Now the power adapter of the MSI, I removed as I expected the TS3 to provide sufficient juice to drive the MSI. Nope. It doesn't charge the GS65. Powered up the TS3. Started the laptop. The ASUS monitor comes to life. Yes! Test the audio and mic. Check! But wait....where are my external drives?

I disconnect one of the drives and reconnect it to the USB port of the MSI. It worked. Plugged it back to the TS3. Nothing. Oh no. Defective USB ports on the TS3?

A quick search in the CalDigit.com website led me to a page where you need to make sure that the Intel Thunderbolt recognizes your new thunderbolt device. Running Thunderbolt Control Center (see photo), showed my TS3, but it wasn't connected. I approved it for connection always. Once I got that done, all the external drives suddenly showed up in file explorer. Whew!

That Thunderbolt Control Center setup needs to be part of the documentation/instructions.

Am going to be working with this docking station for sometime and will give further updates in the future. For now, biggest benefit is that I only have two cables connected to my MSI laptop. The TS3 and the power cord. Clean and uncluttered. Might have to purchase a spare Thunderbolt 3 cable. Just in case this one breaks.

title: Excellent capability for the money
text:
I have this system setup with 9 POE cameras (5mp). The quality of the image is excellent. A few notes: the 3TB sounds like a huge amount, but with 5mp cameras set at highest setting with audio, it doesn't allow for more than about 6-8 days of recording storage. I had another 2TB hard drive (same type, brand etc. from an older NVR) that I mounted inside this NVR case- no problem. I have it all hooked up to a 4k 42" television through one HDMI cable. I have the NVR also hooked to my wireless router with a ethernet cable for remote access through my laptop or smartphones. I recommend not going small on your monitor or television. There are several options for display, which are great. I can watch all 9 cameras at one time, but with 9 cameras on a 42"- lets just say the individual camera feeds aren't huge... I like the fact that the audio monitoring comes through the one ethernet cable from each camera and also through the hdmi output to the monitor/tv. I did try a true dedicated widescreen computer monitor at first (34 or 35" screen), but it wasn't 4k and it was much more expensive than the 4k 42" tv. Advantage of the monitor- I could use my desktop computer and monitor the video feeds on the same screen by splitting the inputs. That didn't outweigh the disadvantage for me of the much more expensive screen and lack of 4k capability for future camera upgrades. It isn't clear on the description, but this NVR works with 4k cameras also. Also, while using my smartphone, I can review stored video feeds at up to 16x speed (audio only available on 1k speed). That makes it much faster if you want to review any strange situations.
So, when is that important: I had a situation where we were on a trip and my back hose bib (outside water faucet) came on during a storm. I couldn't tell for sure that it was on while looking at the video feed while gone, but sure enough, it was on when I got home. The water ran for 3 days. Was it a vandal? I sure thought so, but I went back to the camera feed that covered that area and backed it up. A plastic lawn chair on my deck had blown into the faucet at just the right angle and bounced off, but turned on the water. I wouldn't have thought that was possible, but it happened. Never would have believed had I not saw it with my own eyes.
My takeaways: I thought initially 4 or 6 cameras would be enough. To actually cover my house and detached carport took eight (8) cameras. The 9th is for my shop. You just can't do it with 4 or 6 cameras. The TV/monitor hardwire (hdmi) hookup only allows video review at 4X speed. Smartphone or laptop hooked up through my wireless router (or 4g) allows up to 16X review speed of stored video. Not sure why this is. Also, there is no phone number for tech support anywhere in the US. All tech support is via email. I am old school and I like to talk to a person. To me, that is the biggest downside. Supposedly, this only supports Reolink cameras. I haven't tried any other brands, but I may for the PTZ feature. I will update my review when I do. Why would I do that? Reolink only offers a 4x optical zoom camera at this time. Other makers offer up to 20x optical zoom. That would be nice. Also, the compression is a different standard (H264 vs H265). That may be why it doesn't work with other makes.
All in all a very nice, easy to set up system with audio and excellent video quality. Hardest part was running the wiring.
Any questions about my installation, please don't hesitate to message me.

Hope this helps.

UPDATE 11/17/2020
I saw some reviews that state this NVR doesn't work on 4k cameras. They make two versions of the RLN16-410. I do have the 4k version. Make sure when you order it, you go with the 4k for future upgrades. Also, I added an extra internal hard drive for as 3tb for 24/7 recording does only do about 4 days with 8 cameras. To me, I like the option of having 7 or 8 days and the fact that you can occasionally format one hard drive and not lose your settings. Only issue I have had is the firmware upgrades. I haven't been able to successfully do a firmware upgrade yet. Am going to contact customer support on this today.

title: Klipsch Delivers on its Refrence Premiere Name
text:
I’ve been a Klipsch owner for over a decade now. In that time I’ve had 3 different surround speaker lines, 2 subwoofers and the Pro Media computer speakers. I’ve heard many others but I just love the Klipsch sound. My most recent upgrade was from the Icon line (the Refrence line predecessor) to the Refrence Premier line. Last year I replaced my front channels (KB-15) with the RP-160m’s and they’re absolutely fantastic. It was a massive upgrade. The downside is that they exposed my KC-25 center channel for the midrange speaker it is. It’s not bad at all, it just couldn’t keep up with my new RP speakers. The center began to sound dim and subdued in comparison. The center should be leading but was instead being upstaged on either side. A stronger center was in order. As I began to search for a new center, I knew I was going to stay with Klipsch. The only question was which one would it be. Available space and price narrowed it down to the RP-500 and RP-600. The 500 was over $100 less and well reviewed so that was the choice for me.
After I received the speaker (bought from 3rd party seller IQ Home Entertainment) I wasted no time connecting it and trying a number of different movies and music. I instantly heard the difference between this speaker and my last. It’s as if someone were standing in front of the speaker before and now they moved out of the way. Voices are so much louder and clearer now. I can hear a lot more depth and breath in the voices now. Low and gravely voices are so much deeper and thicker than they were before. This is no doubt due to the much greater frequency range in the RP-500c. It’s able to go much lower and higher than my previous speaker. I’d have been disappointed had it only been a small difference but fortunately the price I paid has shown to be absolutely worth it. Everything just sounds so good now that I can’t imagine feeling the want or need for more. I was also pleased to see the build quality was on par with my new bookshelf speakers. Same color, same smooth feel and very attractive copper woofers. The only difference being the extra copper rings surrounding the woofer and the tweeter. The Reference Premier line is a huge step up from my Icons I’ve replaced. The extra cost is seen and heard through and through. Absolutely a premium look and feel.
To me, Klipsch means clear and clean audio that just makes you smile and feel good when you listen to your favorite music and movies. Hearing things as they were intended to sound. High end quality at an affordable price. The most important feature being fun. You’ll want to hear everything again while enjoying every minute of it. That’s what I want and expect from good quality speakers and Klipsch never disappoints me. Highly recommended.

2. Headphones are crap. You can tell they are cheaply made, poor quality. Fit in ear comfortably, sound is OK, but no markings for left or right side.

3. Requires a USB 2.0 slot for charging. Says this in the manual. Does that mean using USB 3.0 will kill it?

4. Interface is kinda 90's. Icons leading to menus. Pretty straightforward to navigate, but not pretty or sexy at all. Display seems to have a decent picture. Lots of surprising features including a speaker, ebook reader and image viewer. No bluetooth.

5. There are equalizer presets, but you can't customize. No Full Bass like my Philips GoGear Vibe that this is replacing. So you need a good, quality set of earbuds for the best rich bass sound.

6. The player itself seems solid and heavy - larger than I expected but still small enough for my case. It is thick and chunky, yet the buttons seem kinda flimsy. Good response though - no issues there.

Overall I think this is a decent if not good mp3 player, but only time will tell. If the thing lasts for more than a year, then it is an excellent value for the money. I will be using it hard over the coming months, and will report back here.

UPDATE 5-19-2019
I am returning the MP3 player. Earlier today it got stuck on the Charging screen. The power button was unresponsive and there is no reset anywhere I could see. The battery died about 12 hours later, so I plugged it in and it came on to charge. But then my laptop died because I forgot the thing wasn't plugged in. I guess that was the death knell for this mp3 player. Unplugged it, waited, plugged it back in - no response.

In the end the thing is too darn sensitive. My stupid Philips could change while in a USB 3.0 slot, and I could remove it, remove files from it, scan it, do all sorts of stuff and it never batted an eye. It finally died when the battery finally died, after getting a little flaky near the end.

But this player will malfunction if you breathe on it wrong or look at it crossways. Also whatever material they used for the back scratches SUPER easily, which pissed me off, because it is a point of pride for me to return something in the same physical condition I received it, and I had to turn this in with scratches. I only had it on soft surfaces like cloth or plastic. Nothing that should scratch metal. So be aware of these main points if you get this:

1. MicroSD cards will not work even when they should.
2. Super sensitive electronics.
3. Easily scratched materials.

I can not recommend this player. Revising my score. Back to square one...

title: I Don't Have That Warm and Fuzzy Feeling
text:
As some reviewers have pointed out, the Title of the item says Cat6 but if you look at the description it only says "Transmits data at speeds up to 1,000 Mbps (or to 1 Gigabit per second)". Further, other reviewers have pointed out that the connectors are not Cat6 connectors, but Cat5e connectors. After doing further research let me see if I can dispel some of these inaccuracies made by these other reviewers.

First, Cat6 cables are really only CERTIFIED at 1 gig (1,000 Mbps), but are able to support up to 10 gig (10,000 Mbps) at lengths 37 meters or less. Cat5e cables are really only CERTIFIED at 100 mbps, but can support up to 1 gig. Notice the use of the word "CERTIFIED" - I think this is where the confusion is regarding cable ratings. I believe this is what the manufacturer ACTUALLY means from their description stated above - that the cable is CERTIFIED at 1 gig, not that its maximum rating is 1 gig. Think of CERTIFIED as "guaranteed". The official spec for Cat5e and Cat6 GUARANTEE 100 Mbps and 1000 Mbps, respectively, but can support more (it's just not guaranteed).

Secondly, the connectors on this cable are not actual Cat6 connectors (see the pictures by other reviewers), but Cat5e connectors. However, the official spec says that the different Cat6 connector is only a RECOMMENDATION, not an actual requirement for a Cat6 cable. Simply put, Cat6 cables have the option to go with Cat6 connectors or can use the Cat5e connectors as long as the cable maintains the rating of a Cat6 cable. So just because it doesn't have the official Cat6 connector, doesn't mean it's not a Cat6 cable. Making a determination by looking at the connectors is not a sure fire way to tell if a cable is Cat6. Reviewers stating it is NOT a Cat6 cable based on the connectors are incorrect. The only way to truly tell if you are getting a Cat6 cable or not is to test with a network tester - something regular home owners don't have and aren't willing to drop another $75 to $300 dollars for. Cable manufacturers are basically on the honor system when it comes to their cables. If you want to feel warm and fuzzy about your cables, then buy from a known and trusted cable provider. Monoprice comes to mind but there are many others.

Thirdly, these cables are thin and while there is no AWG (American Wire Gauge) printed on the cables themselves or listed in the description, I believe these to be 28 AWG. I have numerous 24 AWG at my house and these Amazon Basics cables are clearly thinner. The higher the AWG, the thinner (or, smaller diameter) the wire. So a 24 AWG will feel "thicker" than a 28 AWG. Also, 28 AWG is a ratified spec for a network cable and was designed mostly to conserve space and increase airflow in IT rooms with crowded network racks and cable runs used by businesses with tens, hundreds or thousands of devices that need a wired connection. The regular homeowner doesn't even come close to this. However, 28 AWG has more signal resistance (the longer the wire) because it's thinner, so it's recommended to keep 28 AWG wires at a length of 15 meters (roughly 50 feet) or less. Again, most homeowners probably don't have this issue and shouldn't worry about it.

So, with all that being said above I ultimately returned these cables and here's why: I don't like it when I don't have that warm fuzzy about something I buy. I THINK these are Cat6 28 AWG network cables but I'm not absolutely sure. If the manufacture had listed more DETAILED specs and had a more clear description then maybe I would have kept these. Also, almost all of the network cables I buy have the the AWG listed on the cable itself along with the Cat type and some other details. These cables only have "Cat 6 Cable" listed on it. That's it. Nothing else. So if I'm trying to determine the gauge of a wire I need to know the differences between the different types of AWG - something most regular people don't know and for which I had to do research on to write this review. I'm a stickler for accuracy and being CLEAR about communicating your product. I should have read the other reviewers BEFORE I pulled the trigger on these. Instead, I got wowed by the price and didn't do my due diligence.

Will these work for you? Absolutely. Before I sent these back they were working for me. Most homeowners won't even need to worry about going over 1 gig speeds so whether this is a Cat6 cable or actually a Cat5e, most won't even know the difference. But I'm OCD about this stuff so don't let my review necessarily dissuade you from buying these. Use it as guide to become better informed and to be able to discern between reviews that are accurate and reviews that are CLEARLY misinformed because they don't have all the information about cabling specs and are just shooting from the hip.

title: GoPro Hero 8 Black: w/UPDATE !!!
text:
How did GoPro ever release this POS??? First time I used it for any length of time (at a local winery where our favorite band was playing), the damn thing crashed and locked up with the screen freezing... MULTIPLE TIMES!! The power switch will NOT function, nor does the start/stop switch. AND, it then gives an SD card error (SanDisk 128GB Extreme Pro Micro SDXC 275MB UHS-II Class-10 U3 4K), telling me that the ONLY WAY to fix the card is by FORMATING, which will then erase ALL data! WTF GoPro???

Not wanting to loose all my data, I disregarded the FORMATING requirement, removed the battery, removed the SD card, then re-inserted both and voila... the Hero8 came back up WITHOUT formatting! That is until the next THREE TIMES this POS camera locked up again!!! Each time it locked up, the recording I received was a completely frozen still image, while the audio kept recording (and the audio recording is FAR INFERIOR to my old Samsung S7 phone!)

PLUS... this camera has ANOTHER GLITCH... when held perfectly steady with the selfie stick's end set directly on our table, the damn thing will FLICK LEFT to RIGHT about one time every 10 seconds for NO reason (no movement of the stick occurred). What a mess. Go figure...

Until these serious problems are (hopefully) solved, this camera is seriously a DNB (Do Not Buy). Hopefully, I will have a future update that solves this problem, or the Hero8 and ALL the accessories I bought (three extra "Hero8" Batteries w/one Dual Charger, lens protectors, storage case, SANDMARC Pole and more = $800+), will be returned to Amazon. What would YOU do???

PISSED OFF in SoCal...

11/15/19 UPDATE:
As it turns out, for proper camera performance, you will need to update the original Hero8 camera's v00.15 software that's loaded from the factory which came with my Hero8, to the latest v1.20 to function properly (supposed to eliminate the Left to Right "image shake", and image Freezing/Lockup I experienced). It's a manual update that is very easy to do, and is easily downloaded from the GoPro website. If needed, simply "online chat" with the GoPro people and they will walk you through this required software update (which they did with me).

No idea why my new Hero8 wasn't already loaded with v1.20, but that seems to be the case with most all of them (I suspect too early of a release).

Ok... "so far, so good", and my rating goes from 1 star to 4 stars (if Amazon will let me increase my rating). The v1.20 software update seems to have eliminated the Left to Right "image shake", and image Freezing/Lockup problems I originally experienced. I performed a full one hour recording (one full battery), and there was NO image shake, NO lockup and NO image freezing. Seems all the Hero8 needed was this new v1.20 update and it was good to go. GoPro could have eliminated a LOT of complaints had they shipped the Hero8 with the v1.20 update, but as I said... this latest update may not have been available at the time of first release. Regardless, I feel the 10/31/19 release date should have been held back for a week or two until the original v00.15 could have been replaced with this new update. In any event, all seems well & good for now... until I get more recording hours on it!!!

title: A long and honest review.. not really impressed.
text:
I purchased this camera 6 months ago now, and I have spent a lot of time trying to talk with Vantrue and make improvements.. in the end, the answer was pretty much "get over it, we can't do anything about that." Overall, I am not impressed with the cameras or the support.

Pro's:
The Video 4k and turns out great most of the time.
The option for up to 256gb MicroSD card
The mounting dock is great. The usb cable plugs into the dock, and the camera slides on with a tilt latch to secure it, reducing cable clutter.
Support will respond relatively quickly, even though the responses are typically restating what you told them the issue was, and asking if that fixed it.. Example at the bottom.

Cons: You probably noticed the only pro was the video resolution.
The camera will NOT keep time. You have to start the car every 3 to 4 days, or the time will just pause and stay there.
The indicator LED is extremely bright.. Not sure why this goes unnoticed most of the time, but there is no reason for the indicator light to be so ridiculously bright.
The GPS modules that are sold separately are terrible. I purchased the small GPS as a way to keep the time up to date and show the speed.. the time will NOT update through GPS. Vantrue stated they disabled that and do not intend to bring it back.. If they can not update that, then the least they can do is to enable the GPS overlay (Stamp) to show on the video.. Currently there is only ONE way to get the GPS speed to show on a saved video, and that is to enable the Location Stamp. If the location stamp is disabled, GPS doesn't work. Vantrue's remedy is to download additional software onto a computer, and view the video through the additional software.. If you pull the video for review right after an accident, and install the SD card into a phone or similar device, the GPS speed shows 000mph.. if you enable located, you get a long stamp of your location plus the GPS speed that is relatively accurate, overlayed directly onto the video.. without extra bloatware. After alerting Vantrue of this, and making numerous videos showing them the issue, they stated that the location stamp should not be required and that they would update it in a firmware patch. After the latest firmware patch, nothing changed.
Firmware patches.. they don't just correct a feature, they actually go through and reset every setting you have changed. anytime you update the firmware, you have to reset every single setting to your liking.. minor inconvenience, but annoying all the same.
Since most users don't even register their products for warranty, I am assuming most people won't realize that the vantrue website is incredibly frustrating to get working, and once you log in for the first time, there is very little information to assist in setup of the device. You can download your firmware updates from their website, which will reset everything you like about the camera.
Capacitor doesn't last. We are use to batteries, that allow devices to sit for a while and record while you are in the store for a short visit, but the capacitor in the vantrue X4 UHD camera does not stay charged, just like most capacitors. The capacitor dies off almost instantly, which is not good if your car does not provide power to the cigarette lighter plug after it has had the key turned off. Vantrue suggests that users buy their external, "always on" charge kit that gets installed separately. Again, this is not a decent solution, this is just a way to sell more unnecessary bloatware items to users, and it will drain the battery on the car while it sits. if you remove the camera from the dock, whether it be GPS or not, it will immediately shut off until you provide it with power..
The camera feels like cheap plastic.

Overall.. I would rate this camera much higher if it weren't for all of the flaws. I will be looking to offload this camera in the near future in favor of any other company that puts some thought behind their product. While the support person tries, there seems to be a language translator involved, and the topic is completely lost most of the time. After buying two cameras (one facing forward, one facing rearward) as well as two GPS mounts and the MicroSD cards to go with the systems, I can say that if the camera was in the $125-150 range, I would be much more comfortable suggesting that users buy it with the awareness of the design flaws. I will give vantrue a try again in the future.

I will also continue to update the firmware, and see if the camera improves. If it does improve, I will make sure to revise this review.

"the blue indicator led is extremely bright, and in future models it would be good to use an LED that is a little dimmer so that it isn't distracting when the user is driving" ... "The blue indicator led flashes to let you know it is recording. It is mean't to show that there is activity..." ... "yes.. it is way too bright, and should not be so bright. there is no reason for it to light up my entire car interior at night" ... "the blue indicator LED is flashing to tell you there is activity. You can turn the screen off in the settings.. the options are 30 seconds, 1 minute, 2 minutes or 3 minutes.." ... "the screen isn't the problem... the screen turns off after 30 seconds. I understand you can not change the led that is already in this version, but in the future, it would be better to make it so it isn't so bright." .. "did you try changing the screen settings? the blue led is flashing to tell you there is activity and that the camera is recording..." ... "........wow..." title: High Failure Rate.  (I think these may only be designed for 3 volts)
text:
I have to agree with others on the high-failure rate of this product.

At first they seem to work, but I've purchased a total of 20 sensors and only 6 are still working (4 of those haven't been used, yet). I used these with an Arduino project; Powered them directly from the Arduino (5v pin) and after being on for a few days (2-4 days) sensors would fail - this happened multiple times. (See my theories on this below.)

HOW THEY (ARE SUPPOSED TO) WORK:
The sensors work by bouncing IR light off an object and triggering an output when the light is received by an IR detector (a phototransistor). There is a power LED and a "status" LED. The power LED remains on while there is power. The "status" LED lights when an object is being detected.

These sensors do not utilize a modulated IR light system (think TV remote control). They are relatively simple in that they just detect IR light. Since IR light is emitted by lots of sources (incandescent lights, LED lights, probably some / all fluorescent lights, the sun), exposure to these light sources will trigger the sensors. If you can hide the sensors from receiving direct ambient light (using them inside a project box or under some kind of shroud), they will be more reliable. (Too much exposure to ambient IR light sources renders them useless. Increasing the sensitivity also increases the effects of ambient light).

DISTANCE:
As for distance, I only used these to detect objects from 1-2 inches inches away, however they do not seem capable of detecting much further than that. Adjusting the potentiometer does increase sensitivity / distance, but only a VERY SMALL AMOUNT before the sensor just locks its output low (The power LED and the status LED remain on) until you adjust the sensitivity back down. (I suppose the potentiometer is able to adjust the sensor's op-amp reference voltage out of the range of the phototransistor's output so the output just gets stuck on.)

REPEATED FAILURE:
As I have stated above, these sensors seem to fail permanantly and repeatedly. When they fail, the power light stays on, but they stop detecting objects. So far, 14 sensors have failed, each one within a few days of powering them up. In my project, I had been powering them from the 5v pin of an Arduino for several days at a time. (The Amazon details claim these will work from 3-5v range.) I started to wonder if they were "burning out" so I tried connecting them to the 3.3v output instead. All sensors (I have 5 running at a time) are currently working after 3-days as I wait to see if any more fail.

WHY (I THINK) THEY FAIL:
What I noticed while trying to adjust the sensitivity of a failed sensor (before I knew they were in fact dead), is that adjusting them too far, turns on the status LED / ouput just as it would on a working sensor. This led me to wonder if it was only the IR emitter that is failing and not the detection part of the circuit. I believe have have proven this to be the case by shining an external IR LED and even a TV Remote (though its output pulses IR light so expect pulses) on the sensor and it responsed as it should. I wonder if whatever resistor they are using on board is not enough to power the LED from 5v. (Don't know if the LED burns out or the resistor, as I haven't bothered to dismantle and repair these $1 sensors.) I am hoping that the 3.3v source will prevent the sensors from failing further. A bit more time will tell.

For the time being, suffice it to say that "you get what you pay for," indeed. For the price, they are good for experimenting, but it would seem they aren’t built to last (or perhaps just not to work at 5 volts).

So first off, let me say that the Motion adjustment for these are awful. We get alerts every time a bug flies by, if it's foggy and the mist rolls under one, when it changes from night time to day viewing, when a cloud passes over, etc., etc., and this is with it set on about 7 which is really low.

Secondly, having those other two pigtails coming off makes hiding the wires a nightmare. I also bought some of the extra cup brackets for easier mounting as that's what I do with all the cameras I've installed for the City where I work. Trying to shove all those wires in there is next to impossible. I didn't use their cups as they are $26 each and you can find plenty of them on Amazon in a 4 pack for not much more which work fine. Well, they work on the bullet cameras they work but not on the dome cameras. There's another thing that's hokey on mounting. I wish I would have never bought the kit that had those with the kit.

Lastly, maybe. The kit is misleading as to which cameras you are getting as it says 4MP and 5MP in different ways that is confusing and apparently written by someone trying to cram as much verbiage in a short span as possible. I apparently got the 4MP cameras after spending 2 weeks looking over a dozen companies of kits and a group of this company. I also had bought 2 separate 5MP bullet cameras so I would have 6 total. Why on earth would I want a 4MP kit and then add 2 5MP to it? So now I'm stuck with this thing.

Ok, another lastly. The web page browsing for the cameras within your own network is AWFUL. It looks like it's maybe 1990 software that was written for Windows 98. Trying to work with it at the DVR itself isn't really that much better but about normal for most. I pre-wired my house with Cat6 for 8 cameras total and did not use the cables theirs came with except for cutting theirs down to make short cables. That was a pain as well....the twisting is non-existent.

Bottom line, I wish I wouldn't have bought this now and just went with the Revo brand that we primarily use around the city in various buildings like the 3 fire stations, court building, sanitation dept, code enforcement, and the swim center. They cost more money but boy is their interface better (and it's nothing to write home about). Do your research and if you order these, make sure you get the right resolution cameras so they don't look like these that I am stuck with.

ARRRRGGGGGG!!!!!!!!!!!

text:

However I've noticed a significant decrease in quality over the past few years. I think the keyboard issue is pretty well known, however I've experienced other issues beyond this in terms of durability. The materials, including the exterior, just seem to be made cheaper. Even the cords are coming apart (frazzled) quicker. The software generally appears to be stable in quality, which is good.

I'm actually a little embarrassed to admit this, but I've gone through three MacBooks in two years. I just get the cheaper Air version now because of this. It isn't worth the time and hassle and lost labor for me to try and work with Apple on fixing the broken units. Their repair process is quite laborious and not end user friendly (by design, my cynical side thinks).

Anyhow, buying cheap MacBooks is my new normal, as I've become so engrained in their ecosystem that changing ships would be brutal. Thanks for listening to my TED talk.

title: Very convincing!  Provides great security for our rental
text: We are currently renting a beautiful home in a great neighborhood, but sadly the neighborhood is a target for burglary (we even had our car stolen last year). While we would love to install a fancy real security system, because we are renting, we don't want to spend all that money until we're in our own home. This is the PERFECT solution for the meantime! It looks totally legit and the red light is just the touch that puts it over the top! Looks like a real infrared camera! There are just a few things that could be better. First, it only comes with screw mounting options which will limit where you put it. Since it's fake (and subsequently lighter weight than a real camera) I really wish they had included a stick mount option or some form of clip instead of just screws. I opted to take off the screw plate and shove the arm directly into a gap between the stone and the eaves of our roof. It's in there securely and looks legitimately like it could be drilled in to the house and hard wired. Anyone casing the neighborhood looking for easy targets would definitely see it (day or night) and probably wouldn't come back! We haven't had any porch pirates, vandalism or other issues since we put this up and I feel so much more at ease! The only other thing I would say by way of constructive criticism is that they include a big sticker meant to be posted somewhere to act as a further deterrent, but it just screams "fake". My advice is just to use the camera itself and throw the sticker away. I appreciate the thought with that but the execution is bad. Oh, and we've had ours up for a few months now and the 2 AA batteries are still going strong to keep the red light on. It has stayed in place and continues to function in snow storms and single digit temperatures. I can definitely recommend this "camera"! If this has been helpful to you, please click the helpful button below so it can help other people too! Thanks!

title: Truly the Best OTA Antenna Available!
text: Let me start by saying I researched a lot of OTA antennas before discovering this new Marathon Plus Whole-House unit.  Aside from being specifically designed to replace my cable service and power multiple TVs, I was interested in the new technology it offered - especially because many antennas that I read about claimed to be “New for 2020” yet they had reviews from several years ago (how can they be truly new?).  Now to the details about this Marathon Plus unit: excellent packaging, comprehensive well-written 10 page instruction manual, everything included to mount or place the unit indoors or outside, and excellent engineering/construction.  It took about 15 minutes to connect this in place of my Spectrum service to deliver over 40 channels to all 4 of my TVs, and it outperformed the reception maps I had referenced.  BTW: the Free Signal TV website also has a reception map portal for aiming guidance (and they sent me an email after ordering with their own aiming recommendations based on my location – find another antenna company doing that!).  We are now watching all our local and regional channels for Free in stunning HD and streaming other programs that we used to pay a lot of money for with Spectrum. All I can say is the extra expense of this unit is well worth the money.  You get what you pay for with antennas – and in my opinion, having a unit that truly utilizes the latest engineering and design makes the Marathon Plus the best choice to cut the cord.

title: Beautiful piece of junk
text:
I'm a huge fan of Synology NAS units, but this has been the most frustrating piece of network equipment I've ever purchased. We purchased three for three branch offices, and all three were huge disappointments. The VPN works great, occasionally, but it inexplicably stops working for no apparent reason. Our site-to-site tunnels among three offices were completely unreliable, up one day, gone the next, and the SSL VPN service is similarly frustrating.

I must have spent dozens of hours fiddling with settings to coax the thing to do its job, a total waste of time. We replaced these with PfSense routers, and the difference in reliability has been night and day. Find another option.

title: Nice product
text:
These microphones are good and stiff for intended use. Appear to be well made. I'm going to be using them in a full face helmet.
Update. I've had a chance to try these out. They work great. (Full face helmet and rigged one for my half helmet headset also) I'm using these as a work around for my 2011 Harley Ultra Limited. I did not want to buy the Roadtech GPS to interface with my phone and corded headset, but still needed to be able to take an emergency call. As a general rule, I do not recommend riding a motorcycle and talking on the phone. I bought this mic, a USB c (my phone requires this setup, your phone may use different style) to headset and microphone splitter. Run a jumper 3.5mm trs cable from splitter adapter "headset" into aux port AND run a 3.5mm trrs from splitter adapter "mic" to the mic mounted in your helmet. I ran the mic cord through the loops of the corded headset. Note: This ONLY works from the aux position on the Harmon Kardon.
Update: Well the microphone finally went out. Evidently the wear and tear of using them has took its toll. I am using them in an unconventional manner...just hoped I might get a year out of them. Not saying product was bad but more just putting out what to expect if used like I did (on a motorcycle).

title: The buttons don't work very well
text:
I have two of these. I use them via Bluetooth. There's a lot about them that I like: Connection is reliable, battery life is good, pairing is easy, pairing with three devices and switching between them is easy, comfortable to use, all of that is great.

But on both of these mice, after only a year or two of moderate use, the left click button has stopped working reliably, particularly with operations where you hold the button down, like click-and-drag. Despite the fact that I hold the button down, multiple release-and-press cycles often occur, resulting in things being dropped in an undesired location, actions being completed earlier than desired, and unwanted single or double clicks occurring.

It's infuriating. Despite the displeasure, I was going to give this a two star review, because of all the other things I like about this mouse. But just writing it down has renewed my frustration and I'm giving it one star, and really it should be zero, because essentially I can't use this mouse.

---
Edit: I contacted Logitech for support. Unsurprisingly, both mice were purchased more than a year ago (16 and 17 months ago), which is beyond the one year warranty. I'm very disappointed in such a big brand with apparently shoddy quality, and refusing to stand behind their products. I think I'm done buying Logitech products.

title: Was Hoping for More Speed, got Less
text:
I was disappointed in just how flimsy it felt when I took it out of the package. I had a CAT5e cable connecting a flat screen to my internet modem/router. WI FI speeds had been unacceptable to get a good 1080p + picture for streaming. CAT5e wired connection increased this speed by only about 10-20% on average, but my router was still only putting out just about half of my internet bandwidth to the TV. My download speed averages 30MBs to the router, but the TV only received about 15MBs on average. I replaced my 2 year old router and it had no effect. I replaced the cable because as the ad says it is "faster than CAT5e/CAT5." But I ran a dozen or more speed tests with the new CAT6 flat cable - and if anything the speeds might have been slightly slower. In fact the fastest speeds I had hit out of the group were actually with the CAT5e, which managed around 18.5MBs on 2 occasions (and sometimes dipped down to around 12.5). The new CAT6 posted speeds ranging from around 11.5MBs to 17.5MBs. And this is with a cable that is shorter - 50 feet versus about 75, which should have give the new cable a small advantage. CAT6 is supposed to use a slightly larger wire, and the modular plugs have a slightly different internal design where the 8 wires are staggered instead of all in a tight row. It is supposed to result in less signal loss and less cross-talk. But somehow *this* CAT6 cable actually seemed to be about 1MBs *slower* than traditional CAT5e. It was fairly cheap, but it didn't do what I hoped it would and actually cost me a lot in time and effort. And now I am debating crawling around under my house again to put the old wire back in place. I could have lived with it if it hadn't actually slowed me down.

PS. I let Jadaol know about my problem, and while they made excuses saying speed depends on many factors besides the cable (ignoring the fact in this exact application CAT5e was faster than their CAT6!) they promised to send a replacement cable if I gave them my order ID. I have now given them my order ID 3 times, and they haven't responded any more. "Kindly provide us your Amazon order ID if you are interested in a replacement and we will take care of the rest for you."

Because of this, and because there seem to be so many problems finding a decent ethernet patch cable now, I tried to dig a little deeper. Numerous brands of cable on Amazon seem to have four star plus ratings - but then look at the 5% or 10% of ratings which are terrible: people who actually test the speed of their new cables often have the same complaint as me - it is slower than the speed they got with their old cable, or fails quickly after installation. Our code (EIA/TIA standards for Category 6 cables require 23AWG) here states CAT6 wire is supposed to be 23AWG minimum (with 22AWG preferred for CAT6a) - Jadaol claims to be using 30AWG, even for their CAT7 wire! 23 AWG has a diameter of 0.0226 inches, while 30AWG gauge wire has less than half that diameter at 0.0100!!! So they are using wire which will have FAR more electrical resistance and will break much more easily than true CAT6 ethernet cable. (Please note for wire gauge smaller numbers mean thicker wire for some reason!) No wonder people are calling these cables from multiple companies fakes, and finding they can't perform or hold up. These are basically counterfeit cables.

title: Overall great, but a couple of issues Amazon should fix
text:
So far so good! Once it gets set up right, it is amazing. I have been avoiding buying a soundbar in hopes of finding something like this. And the Studio more than satisfied. For now one speaker is enough in my apartment living room.

It is so good, that I now plan to upgrade to a second speaker to get surround sound in a couple of months when I get a house. The bass rumbles! The midrange is all there and the highs are clean! I can hear dialogue very well over the sound and it’s a huge upgrade from the decent TV speakers I have been using.

My main complaint right now is that the Fire TV 4K remote will not pair to the Studio. The instructions in the Alexa app show that you can pair the remote to it, but this isn’t possible. I called customer service after many tries, and the very nice customer service guy at Amazon said this isn’t functional right now. He said there is no notes about if this will ever be functional.

That means you have to control the volume with your voice, even though you can still control everything else in your Fire TV with the remote. Come on Amazon, please fix this ASAP! The volume is so good on the speaker that you have to yell at Alexa just to turn the volume down. And it pauses the volume and it’s just awkward. Fix this!

Also, I don’t love how the speaker will unpair from the Fire Stick when you play your own music through the speaker even when using a skill. You have to reconnect either manually through the Fire Stick settings or figure out how to exactly tell “Alexa pair to xxxxx’s Fire TV” without messing it up. This should be seamless or continuous. Please make this easier!

Overall it’s a great experience! If those two issues are fixed it will be a 5* system.

title: As good as or better my Swaros
text: I also own the newest Swarovski EL 8.5x42 and SLC 8x42, and have found that the Leica Noctivid 8x42 has better eye relief than either of the Swaros, despite the fact that the reported eye relief values suggest that it shouldn't.  I believe the issue is that Leica measures eye relief from the eyecup (the "usable eye relief" for eyeglass wearers), whereas Swarovski measures from the glass (without subtracting the space taken up by the eyecup).  As a result, when wearing eyeglasses I get the fullest, most immersive view from the Noctivid.  The sharpness and contrast of the Noctivid seem to be as good as for the Swaros, while also seeming brighter.  I've seen no chromatic aberration whatsoever.  The ergonomics are great.  I only have two minor issues: (1) The rubber of the lens caps rubs on the glass very easily and causes smudges that have to be cleaned off quite frequently; in  25 years of birding I've never owned a binocular with this problem.  I replaced the top lens caps with a Vortex cap, and that completely fixed that issue because the Vortex covers are deeper and don't touch the glass, but the objective lens covers are of a proprietary design that are hard to replace with a non-Leica cover.  (2) While the focus knob is very smooth and uniform, it is touchier than on the Swaros (different gear ratio?), which takes a little getting used to.

title: Easy to assemble and lots of light! Reviewing 16" square portable studio XD.
text:
I had a little trepidation about assembling it because of some of the reviews so I was pleasantly surprised when it zipped up over the frame easily. The zippers seem sturdy and there were no really tight spots. I was very careful to make sure the frame rods were fully seated in the corner pieces. The frame rods are sturdy and fit snugly into the corner pieces so it isn't likely to come apart.
I am so glad that I sprung for the XD that has 4 light strips. I got a difficult piece of jewelry (that has dimension) to test with 2 light strips and 4 and sure enough there were shadows with 2 lights mounted on top that disappeared when I installed the second 2 light strips. These I placed as one suggestion portrayed facing the back. The lights snap onto the frame securely and I like how they click when they pivot if you want to change the direction the strip is pointing.
I'm also glad I got the 16" square model because it is manageable and doesn't take up a lot of space.
I photograph my jewelry with a smartphone and really need to get closeups. This was impossible from the top or through the front hole(s). With the extra light strips in the front, there is enough light that I can leave the front open and get the phone in for the closeups I need. I do have to turn up the exposure when I edit the photos but they come out amazingly crisp and colorful for a phone!
The backdrops come rolled up with the frame rods and are nice and thick with no marks and stay in place from the get go tucking behind the frame to keep from rolling up.
I really cannot complain about anything. I cannot say I would want to take it apart and reassemble it but that was not a requirement for me anyway. I assembled it on a piece of tile board so I can move it if I need to.
I don't know if I'll use the dimmable lighting feature but I'm glad to have it.
Lastly, the velcro for the openings is ferociously strong.
My only concession is a binder clip to hold the front open. The zippers seem sturdy enough but I would not want to be constantly zipping them over the front corners. All zippers wear out so I have them zipped down a couple inches in front and carefully turned the front up and secured it to the zipper binding (careful to avoid the zipper!) along the top with a binder clip so I can easily let the front down after a session.
It is nice that the power supplies have a power switch but I have both plugged into a power strip and turn the lights on and off with the power strip switch.
All in all worth the extra money. SO glad I got the 4 light strips. I'm very happy with it!
Now I need more props and more interesting back drops so I can construct little scenes for my jewelry photos.

title: Base Kindle gets an upgrade
text:
The pros: I like that you have a choice of colors and that it comes with a front light. It's small and easy to carry around. If you've never had a Kindle before or never had one higher than the base, you won't notice the 167 ppi difference between it and the Paperwhite and the Oasis.

The cons: If, however, you're like me and you have an Oasis, you'll immediately notice how much less crisp the letters and pictures are.

Don't get me wrong. It's a good price for a starter Kindle, especially with lights now. For someone who's looking for the best reading experience they can get without spending too much money, it's a good choice.

However, for a few dollars more, they can get a Paperwhite with better resolution, waterproofing, and more storage (2x more for the base Paperwhite model).

So what should you get? If you're more concerned with saving money, go for the Kindle Basic. Otherwise, about thirty dollars more gets you a big improvement.

title: DO NOT BUY THIS SYSTEM - TOO DIFFICULT TO RESET PASSWORD
text:
Avoid the ANNKE systems, unless you want 24 hour delays in resetting your password, or other customer service support. Customer service is accessed via email in a time zone 12 hours away (opposite of USA) - so, you must wait until the next day for customer service response by email.

If you forget your password, or it is corrupted, you must request a secure code via email to reset it. And... if you're system date and time is off, you will not be able to reset it, until you realize it is off - since, ANNKE's secure code generator provides a secure code unique to each day - of course, the user manual does not explain any of this.

So... if you do... buy it... MAKE SURE TO RECORD YOUR UNLOCK PATTERN AND YOUR PASSWORD... AND... DO NOT ALLOW ANYONE ELSE TO CHANGE THESE. If you're system is not connected to the internet, check your system date and time frequently to make sure it's correct.

And... of course... remember that all such products made in China are totally insecure... if... connected to the internet. They are all manufactured with chips, which allow the manufacturer and Chinese agencies to monitor your activities (e.g. HUAWEI example).

Just don't buy it!

title: Good, sturdy design for the price.
text:
I just bought this USB C-to-C to replace one that had frayed at the plug-to-cable strain / connector. I found it by sorting price lowest to highest and this was near the cheapest. First, it's braided, which always feels like a sturdier cable to me and less likely to have issues than rubber or plastic jacketing.

Second, to me the make or break feature of a charging cable is that plug-to-cable strain or connection point. As you can see in the picture, this cable has a nice sturdy base to the plug going down the length of the cable about 1/2 inch. To me, this will hopefully lead to less issues if the cable trails at a 90 degree angle to the plug; say to reach up from the outlet low on the wall to my phone on a table or counter.

Charging shows the fast symbol on my battery meaning it's pulling the good wattage, because as my old cable started failing, my phone would alert me it was charging slow. This cable seems to get the 5V at 3A rate a C-to-C should give you. Haven't run any precise tests or anything, but no red flags it's substandard. It's a new purchase, so I don't know how it'll hold up for the long run, but initial impression is that it has good design and materials for the money. I don't regret buying it to replace the crappy one that failed.

title: Great for ergonomics, video calls, and a little more desk space
text:
I was excited to get the Skrebba Laptop Stand. For years, I've used a low-profile plastic stand that fits in my backpack and lifted my laptop slightly off the desk to provide some ventilation. However, in these days of home-based video calls and makeshift offices, it was time to upgrade to something more ergonomic.

The Skrebba Laptop Stand is lightweight and sturdy. The part of the stand that holds the laptop is well ventilated so heat dissipates nicely. I like the industrial design, coloration, and finish of the stand as well.

For video calls, the stand unfolds to a nice height so my camera is closer to eye-level, rather than looking up at my nose. It's a subtle thing, but it helps me to look more professional.

Ergonomically, I'm able to fold the stand in such a way that helps me to position my hands in a way that prevents carpal tunnel.

Because the stand lifts my laptop off the desk, I've also been able to reclaim a little bit of space.

I have one piece of constructive feedback: Although the Skrebba Laptop Stand is adjustable, I wish that the joints were able to be user-tightened. It's not likely that I will fold and unfold this stand often, but I can see it getting loose over several months.

Otherwise, this is the perfect stand for me at the right time.

text:
Dear Amazon,

Can you please have your Kindle Product Management Leadership review the following feature requests for the next Oasis release?

1. USB-C - Duh?! As has been ubiquitously pointed out, it is indeed extremely baffling that micro-USB passed muster in 2019 for a top of the line Kindle when USB-C is everywhere and is the de facto standard. Why?! I am fairly certain that it is not because of technological complexity or price. Please fix this embarrassment in the next generation Oasis please. Did I say "PLEASE"?

2. No Ads - Seriously! Again we are talking about the top of the line Kindle! I shouldn't have to pay $20 extra for an ad-free experience. Best way to repackage this is to offer this as a opt-in option and you can market this to promote personalized notifications to enhance the user experience. That gives the user a choice and takes money out of the equation.

3. Charger - Again for a premium product, you expect the user to shell additional dollars to buy a charger? This should be bundled in!

4. Higher Storage - I get the same storage in Oasis that I would with a device that is priced at 50% a la Paperwhite. There has to be greater number of differentiators between the two models and higher storage on Oasis is one way to do it, It would be useful for people who use a lot of audio books. How about a 128 GB or 256 GB option?

5. Better format compatibility - Think about the possibilities! When everyone else is supporting EPUB, why can't kindle? What better way to attract non-Kindle users? Downsides are not much because of the ecosystem lock-in that Amazon already enjoys by a great degree against its competitors. At the very least, native Kindle software should support seamless conversion options for unsupported formats.

6. Battery life and issues: Another differentiator with Paperwhite could be longer battery life with Oasis. Also there seem to be several reported issues with the battery and it would be nice to do a root cause analysis of that and fix them.

7. External storage: Wouldn't it be nice to have a SD card option?

There are several others but they are lower priority for me such as bigger screen (7" seems like an ideal size to be able to hold it one hand), color screen (for comic book lovers), audio jack (for people wanting to use a wired headset), additional bundled options (magnetic case, case with keyboard, multi-plug global adapter, etc.)

I am sticking with my Kindle from a decade ago which still works like a charm. I would love to upgrade in a heartbeat even if all you do is just #1 above.

So why three stars? After all I have not bought or used the product. I trust the positive reviews of the product enough to declare that this is a high quality product but I do know that the above missing features doesn't qualify this to be a 5 star (or even a 4 star) product for the price.
