title: Effective ANC, But Lack Bass and Volume
text:
Summary: These earbuds lack deep base and don’t play loud. ANC is effective, but if you don’t need it then Anker Spirit X earbuds are a better headphone for less money.

Update 7/11/19: I tested the noise cancellation on a recent flight with mixed results. The ANC (plus the passive noise reduction inherent in earbuds) was effective enough for most music (rock, jazz, pop) since this music has a fairly consistent and loud volume. However, it did not work well enough for music with quiet passages such as solo vocals and some classical where the airplane noise became intrusive.

Update 4/7/19: What about power woodworking such as sanding?
Unlike vacuuming, the ANC was not effective enough to even hear the music while sanding. Not even close! However, combining a hearing protector earmuff over these headphones worked very well to suppress almost all outside noise.

Update 3/20/19: What about for vacuuming?
Kenmore full size: It works! Although not an extremely loud vacuum, I find the whine of any vacuum irritating, and so I vacuum while wearing hearing protector earmuffs. Inserting the earbuds blocked some noise passively. Somewhat to my surprise, ANC did make things quiet enough (not completely quiet) for enjoyable music WITHOUT turning up volume. Vacuum = Kenmore Progressive inteliClean on high speed; Music = Copland: Quiet City, and Tom Waits: Closing Time.

Hoover hand-held/rotating brush: Does it work? Well, sort of. This devil is really noisy - it rattles and shrieks! Worse still, I clean carpeted stairs on my knees so the Hoover is only 2 feet from my ears. With ANC on, I have to turn up the volume a bit, and music is less satisfying. However, ANC works well enough that I will probably do the stairs this way next time.

Original review:
PRO
- Good overall sound.
- Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) works fairly well for noisy environment.
- 10 hr play using ANC. Charge time = 2 hr.
- Fits under most hearing protector earmuffs (for mowing lawn).
- Nice storage bag with zip compartment for USB cable (see picture).
- Responsive customer service
CON
- Unable to play very loud.
- Deep bass is a bit weak even with bass boost on.
- Doesn’t have wings to help it hold firmly in my ears.
- 2X price of most Bluetooth headphones (currently).
NEUTRAL
- Magnets hold earbuds together when not in use.
- Bluetooth 5.0 and aptX.

Comparison (see picture)
1. These: Anker Life NC “necklace” style headphones (Bluetooth 5.0),
2. Sony WH-CH700N over-ear phones with ANC (Bluetooth 4.1),
3. Anker Spirit X earbuds (Bluetooth 5.0),
4. Paloview Earflow “necklace” earbuds (Bluetooth 5.0).
5. LG HBS700 “necklace” earbuds - formerly very popular.

Deep Bass
There are problems with deep base and there shouldn’t be. I tested deep bass (using Pixel 3XL phone) with reverberating organ (Copland: Organ Symphony, E.Power Biggs from LP), large drums, rock (Linkin Park: Crawling), and synthesizer (Inception soundtrack: Dream Is Collapsing). Paloview and Anker Spirit earbuds were very good in deep bass response and equaled Sony, but the Anker Life NC (with 12mm drivers) failed to deliver much deep bass. I suspect that the difference in bass might be a design difference. Both Paloview and Anker Spirit X earbuds have wings and ear clips (see picture) that grip my ears, while I really have to work at getting Anker Life NC firmly into my ear. I tried different ear-tips and different insertion techniques, and although it feels like they are firmly in my ear, if the seal is weak then it will affect bass. Disappointing. Sony has great bass so it shouldn’t have anything to do with ANC.

Loudness
Neither Anker headphone plays as loud as the other headphones. On the Inception soundtrack (unusually quiet) I actually maxed out the volume. Although I did have enough volume, another person might not. Could this be a design decision to prevent hearing damage from excessive sound or perhaps the firmware needs fixing?

Soundcore App
Originally, the Paloview earbuds were lacking in deep bass, but the Paloview app updated the firmware fixing the problem. Can the lack of bass in Anker Life NC be corrected? The Soundcore app allows boosting bass, setting max volume, and to customize the action of the buttons. The bass boost setting does improve the deep bass somewhat, but is a little heavy handed.

Sound Quality
All of these earbuds (except LG) had excellent overall sound quality - not much else to say. Qualcomm aptX is supported, but I couldn’t hear any difference. I’ve read that aptX is not necessary on well designed headphones. The Anker Life NC has a button to toggle Normal/ANC/Transparency. I did not hear any downside to the ANC mode. Transparency is supposed to boost outside sounds, but I did not see any advantage over just pausing the music in Normal mode. The old LG earbuds just don’t measure up, and I didn’t test them further.

ANC Theory
Turning up volume to overpower noise risks damaging your hearing. Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) headphones listen to ambient sound (noise) and then create an opposite sound-wave canceling that noise. In principle, this could work perfectly, but current technology only removes mid frequencies. [Confusingly, some companies claim ANC when it only cleans up sound on a phone call (uplink style).] Passive noise reduction can also be important since earbuds and over-ear headphones physically block some outside noise. Note: no brand of ANC works well enough to safely use while mowing the lawn (but earbuds can be used under an earmuff hearing protector).

Noise Reduction
My concern is listening to music on an airplane without turning up the volume (average airplane, economy class). Paloview and Anker Spirit X (snugly fit into the ear) passively reduce a fair amount of outside noise, but Anker Life NC lacks wings to hold them in place and was not as good. Unfortunately, ANC is not effective for voices or screaming babies (both Sony and Anker Life). Sony ANC was fairly effective for reducing background roar on several recent flights, although I did not feel it was enough for comfortable music listening. I have not flown since receiving the Anker Life so I compared them to Sony in an environment simulating an airplane (noisy fan). I was surprised (Sony has been doing ANC for years) to find the Anker ANC was BETTER in removing the roar type noise. Good job!!

Note: I will be flying in the next several weeks, and I will test Anker Life NC in real life conditions - I will update this review ASAP.

title: Got the Job Done
text:
Just moved into a small 1 bedrm APT, and needed Ethernet to run thru the wall to the other APT where the tenant has Gigabit FiOS. Wifi from their new Quantum Gateway is extremely poor which is heavily known, and being a Gigabit connection I DEFINITELY knew better than to use WiFi. I knew I had to be hardwired. I've only ever been on a 25/25 from Comcast when I lived in Florida, and my Uncle here on Long Island had 150/150 but I never experienced a Gigabit connection so just had to have it.

I wanted to go with 75ft but I played it safe and went with 100ft. I ended up having about 20 feet left over which I coiled loosely and used the supplied velcro clip to neatly store the rest behind my desk. I also ordered the Darller 200 Pack of the nail in cable clips which made the job look nice and clean.

I wanted the install to be as neatly as possible without noticing a ethernet cable s I got the cable in white. I ran it along the baseboards, up and around the doors behind the TV stand behind the fridge in my APT that goes right into her APT into a closet, and continued running it along the baseboards up and around her bedroom door behind her dresser into the router. Cat5e is rated at 1Gbps up to 100 meters which is 328 feet so that means a 100 foot cable can carry Gigabit speeds no issue. However, this is a cat6 cable which is rated 10Gbps at 55 meters which is 180 feet, and this cat 6 is backwards compatible with 5e AND 5 even though no one in their right mind would use direct cat5.

it took me 30 minutes to run and clip the wire between both apartments. Cake walk! Overll I'm pleased with the cable at the price, and with prime 2 day shipping. You can't go wrong.

title: Best router product I have ever owned and support is excellent.
text:
I purchased Linksys Velop as an early adopter when the mesh router was first introduced. I installed a three node configuration in a large two story home over 5500 square feet. It eliminated every dead spot.

As I grew my smart devices (30+) and extended my need outside to the backyard to stream video and music, I added two nodes making the total five. The bandwidth was and continues to be excellent, no delays no contention.

I will admit that initial support from Linksys was very difficult as the mesh network configuration was complex, the nodes were at different firmware releases and the app had some nuances and errors that needed to be resolved. But unlike other consumer electronic products, Linksys Velop stayed committed to their product and employed a continuous improvement process and has improved the app on both the phone and the computer and the technicians are very skilled, knowledgeable and most of all very patient. When solving a problem, it requires walking through the house to each node to restart after changes are made to the primary node, so the process for problem resolution can take time, but in the end it is resolved.

If you want ideal WiFi coverage indoors and out, consistent performance (I am receiving download at up to 400 mbps and upload of over 22 wireless), and with excellent customer support that continually improves, this is your product. Just understand that as you grow your mesh network, it does require your patience and you will be best served if you make the effort to better understand the technology, the details of the app and settings as you will be able to make changes yourself and solve problems more effectively. While it is the future for home wifi, for coverage and performance for challenging homes, it is for sure the present. I am confident you will be very pleased.

title: Fantastic Monitor - Exceptional Quality
text:
The screen is nearly bezzless on the three sides, outside of the bottom which houses the front firing speakers, looks comparable to others, it's actually stylish looking, rustic to a degree. I had the AD27QD and sent it back for this, had it for nearly a month. Gigabyte does an amazing job with support of their monitors, mine was 1.08, eight firmware updates. IMO, it's the Swiss army knife of monitors, that said, I'm glad I sent it back for the BenQ, this just looks better overall. I also love the true stereo sound for music and YouTube. Gigabyte's offerings all had a degree of noticeable back light bleed, IPS glow, especially the flash-lighting on their VA panels, my gosh, BenQ has none of this. I don't think that's on Gigabyte, it's the poor 1500r curved panels they are likely getting from Samsung. The response time is exceptionally similar to AD27QD. I would have bought the Aorus FI27Q-P if it weren't $649, it was my first choice overall, though now using the EX2780Q, can’t imagine it would have been as good, this monitor is flawless from an image quality perspective!

+ HDRi is actually legit, I typically don't even care for HDR much, it's nice to have, though sometimes I prefer to play without it, just played Ghost Recon Breakpoint, Xbox One X and used 1440p@120hz, VRR with HDRi and it looked tremendously better than my experiences the Aorus CV27Q and AD27QD. I was really surprised by how natural it looked, not overly colorful where everything appears cartoonish. It actually made the game more realistic looking, grass and foliage appeared much more detailed and natural green tones. Modern Warfare looks incredible on this monitor, plays great, very responsive and incredibly detailed looking. This monitor is capable of 1440p@120hz, VRR and HDR all checked at the same time for the Xbox One X, though unfortunately X will only use the HDR if you have it upscaled to 4K, either way looks great. I played both and prefer the 1440p mode with HDRi. PS4 Pro is able to be played in 4K HDR (upscaled), PC gaming was great as well.

+ Super dark backlight, ZERO discernible back light bleed, VA like, very, very pleasantly surprised.

+ Looks as good if not better than my LG 32UD99 which is one hell of a monitor in its own right.

+ Colors look great, playing the new Age of Empires II DE was a truly mesmerizing experience, this monitor truly has some damn good looking, saturated, yet natural colors.

+ Audio is the best I've heard on a monitor, my LG actually has great sound as well, it's right up there, though the EX has more depth of sound, with the included sub-woofer. Great for YouTube, Spotify etc.

+ Exceptional uniformity throughout, medical grade black, white and grey, pure.

+ Image response time is very good, going to test this more to see how it performs in fast moving games.

+ Clear AG coating, not coarse, smooth, natural look.

+ Included controller is fantastic, super handy and the audio wheel on the left, smart setup.

- Would only let me select 10bit color with 120hz, vice 144hz. This is an issue to me, the Aorus CV27Q would let me use 10bit color at 165hz, zero issues. I don't get this, supposedly the BenQ has DP 1.4, so it should be able to do this, very disappointing. Checked the manual, it only support 120hz with 10bit color.

- Color vibrancy is nowhere near as good as the enhance color options on something like the Acer XV273K, which IMO, is the pinnacle of image quality if not for some of its quirks. I'm referring to the method of pushing the vibrancy beyond the default, really no need to, looks great at 10.

- Comes in the smallest box I've seen for a 27-inch, looked like a lego set arrived, crazy how small compared to the Acer for example, though it did come with no issues, so guess it works.

- The Stand!!!!!

title: pretty KooL stuff
text:
I use this with my alienware M15 I purchased last year, its a good laptop. But I don't like how hot it gets when gaming. I understand that CPU's are capable of handling 100C temps, but I also know that not all surrounding components can, and keeping any computer running as cool as possible prolongs its life. For the last year I have tried to fix thermal throttling using intel XTU, and Throttlestop software. I was able to stop or limit the thermal throttling happening in the CPU, but temps would still stay around 88C spiking occasionally to 100C. I then opened the laptop and changed the thermal paste to the best stuff on the market. temperatures were still 80s with spikes, only difference is when I stop gamming he temps come down really really fast. So that said to me I just need more air it the only limiting thing in the laptop left. So I starting my long research on cooling pads. For awhile I decided they were probably worthless, and forgot about it. After looking around more I decided to get the Kootek, because it had good reviews and results for years past, seems these days there are tons of cooling pads on the market. The one thing I can say for sure is they are all cheap and have varying reviews ranging from great to this thing sucks. Why no company can make a good cooler is beyond me seems like it should be hard. But if your gonna do it, get something cheap like the Kootek, and make sure the fans in the cooling pad will align with the intake fans on your laptop, which is why i bought this verses the Havit, which has many many more reviews. the Havit's fans simply wouldn't work for my laptop, as my intakes are at the bottom rear of the laptop, the kootek has two small fans that line up almost perfect with the intakes on mine, and the top of the middle fan as well.
All this being said my temps have been running in the 65-75c range, with spikes in the higher 80s now, so it does seem to make a difference, I also notice on some games that aren't as intensive temps are much more even across the board, with no spikes. the Kootek is cheap feeling, and no doubt made cheaply but its working, I cant speak to longevity as i have only had it about a week now, it is fairly quite, its quitter than laptop fans on full blast for sure. If your intakes are located where the fans are I'm sure it will make a difference for you, if not look for another one.

Someone Will probably start a class action lawsuit against Bose for this product. Bose should offer refunds for this horrible product.

I did a side-by-side comparison to my Bose SoundLink Revolve+, and a friends Harman Kardon Onyx Studio 3; before downloading the Bose Music app. The speaker was not louder or better than my Bose SoundLink Revolve+, And the $129 Onyx studio 3 sounded better. I was shocked. Then I recalled a review saying that a prior firmware update had crippled the sound on this device. So I installed the Bose Music app and it downloaded an update to the speaker firmware, and this Bose home 500 sounded completely different and much louder than before. title: IronWolf drives are the best NAS drives I've used
text:
UPDATE: This week I finally has my first IronWolf Pro drive fail. By chance it was the newest drive I put in my server. It was also my largest drive (16 tb). There were unrepairable corrupted sectors (according to seagate tools). I contacted seagate and I was walked through the process of returning the drive and having the data recovered. They were not difficult to deal with. I'm leaving my review at 5 stars. I have however ordered another 16tb drive as a quick replacement to the one that died (amazon will get that drive here at least a week before seagate would get a replacement here). If that drive dies prematurely and or the 16tb replacement seagate sends me back dies again then I will start removing stars with the caveat that, maybe the quality control or tech associated with drives larger than 14tb, arent ready for the masses. I've been running 5 other 14tb ironwolf pro drives 24/7 for many many months longer than the 16tb drive and they're all quick, silent and uncorrupted.

Original:
I have 3 of these 14tb IronWolf Pros. Ive bought 10 of the 8tb IronWolf (regulars). I currently only have 5 of the 8th drives installed and running. I havent had a single issue with any of the drives. Some of my drives are 4 years old. Some are 8 months. They all run 24/7 with a 60 second reboot, once or twice a week.

Anyways I began buying these 14tb drives a year and a half to two years ago. They are more expensive dollar for dollar (by tb) than the 8tb drives but when you have a ton of data and your running out of sata ports on your motherboard or internal hdd slots in your tower these are the way to go.

As I said before they are reliable. Not a single DOA drive and not a single breakdown. I get on average about 170 mbs drive transfer rates.

Fast, quiet and reliable, cant ask for much more.

Before I got iron wolfs I bought some other seagate drives (not NAS). TOTAL GARBAGE. Seagate almost lost me as a customer there, but I gave ironwolf a chance and I'm glad I did.

title: Great bang-for-buck
text:
I purchased this webcam to work from home. My laptop has a built-in webcam, but as I'm using a docking setup with two monitors, it was annoying to shift my entire arrangement to participate videoconference meetings.

Long and short: This suits me perfectly for my needs -- teleconferencing from home, several hours a day. Easy to set up, good exposure, nice contrast, doesn't oversaturate, and the audio works well. If you're looking for something under $100 and don't need the uber-res, gamer-preferred, high-end webcams to stream, record, and post to YouTube your Minecraft gaming adventures, this is a solid solution.

Details: I'm using a state-issued Dell Latitude 7290 (8GB RAM, 1.9 GHz CPU) running Windows 10 Enterprise.

Experience - Install and Activation: Very straightforward. Out of the box, I simply plugged it into one of the USB ports on my dock. I didn't need to install any drivers (I'd have known, because all our state-issued laptops are administratively locked; can't install anything without admin support), and the webcam was recognized by Skype, WebEx and Zoom. Note that I did have to tell each of those platforms to use the webcam because I have two detected by the system.

Apologies if the info below is too pedantic:

- Skype: Go to Tools > Video Device Settings, and select "Logitech HD Webcam C525" from the drop-down.
- WebEx: When you join a meeting, select "Logitech HD Webcam C525" from the "Select Video Connection" drop-down. Same for audio, if you're calling in from computer.
- Zoom: Go to Settings > Video, and select "Logitech HD Webcam C525" from the drop-down.

Experience - Audio and Video Quality: My team members, with whom I meet almost daily, quickly noticed the difference in video quality and commented on it. It's a definite improvement over the built-in webcam. I really like the "I'm tracking you" feature. If for some reason I shift my position in the frame, the webcam adjusts. Given I'm trying to work with four pets in the house, this happens a lot (because they all apparently can sense when I'm in a videoconference, and that is THE TIME to try to get into my lap).

- Hue: I notice I look a mite greener than usual. The camera does lean toward the cool side of color temp, but I'm not bothered by that much. Turning on and off various lights helps warm things up a bit. Not a big deal for me.

- Exposure: I'm truly happy with this. I face three tall, broad windows looking onto my back yard. The webcam readily adjusts to the level of sunlight hitting my face at any given time.

- Saturation: I think it's a good balance -- not too undersaturated, not too clownish. I've worn things from dark shirts to pale blouses and multicolored jackets; no oversat or undersat so far.

- Artifacts: Four days in with frequent, daily use, no issue with streamers or artifacts.

title: Does the job, but it's not easy
text:
This glass and touchscreen replacement does the job, but it's definitely not an easy task. Note the pre-installed button makes things a bit easier, but if you want to your touch ID to work, you'll need to preserve and use your old button (and swap it with the one attached to this new glass).

The two major difficulties I found in installation are these:

1. Removal of the original glass is always difficult. This isn't a problem with the replacement glass, but an unavoidable property of the iPad. Wear safety glasses, and wear gloves when removing the old glass.

Cover the entire original screen in tape to prevent glass bits from going everywhere. You're probably going to shatter the old glass. This isn't a big problem, but try not to damage anything else in the process. Watch a YouTube teardown video-- maybe a couple of times. Finally, after removal make sure to remove all bits of old adhesive and tiny bits of glass where the new glass will contact-- THIS IS CRITICAL. Small bits of glass in the old adhesive will create pressure points that will break your new glass after all of your hard work.

2. Here's where some product difficulties come in: The new glass has plastic strips that need to be peeled off to expose adhesive that holds it in place. Some of these strips are around the fragile ribbon cables, and there's also a large sheet of protective plastic that needs to be peeled from the back of the glass during installation. You must keep even the smallest bits of dust off of that surface while tilting the glass into place while getting the ribbon cables to tuck neatly inside the iPad.

THE CRITICAL PART HERE: prep the new glass before plugging in the cables by carefully removing the (probably blue) plastic strips from the edge adhesive. Then remove the adhesive protection from the cable going to the button. Stick that button cable to the surface-- you will probably need to lift the edge of the large back-of-glass protection sheet where the button cable lies (DO NOT STICK IT ON TOP OF THE PROECTIVE SHEET). Stick it down, then let the back-of-glass protection sit back down on top of it.

The ribbon cables themselves have some (probably white paper) strips covering their adhesive. Do these next. Remove the strips, but BEFORE FOLDING THEM ONTO THE SCREEN BACK SURFACE lift the edge of the large back-of-glass protector so the ribbon cable pieces can stick into place (they MUST NOT stick to the back-of-glass protector sheet that you remove just before you fold the glass into place). Be very careful, as the adhesive section of the ribbon cables must stick very neatly and flat onto the back of the glass in order to fit well. IT IS VERY EASY TO TEAR THE THE RIBBON CABLES NEAR THE ADHESIVE SECTION. If this happens, portions of your touch screen may not function.

Once you've stuck the adhesive base of the ribbon cables into place, carefully plug in the cables, plug in the screen and replace the 7 screws (3 tiny ones in the metal plug cover on the display cable, 4 larger ones on the corners of the display panel). You'll need to be holding/leaning the glass upright (approx. 90 degree angle from plane of iPad-- don't lie 180 degrees flat-- bad for cables). Have the iPad lying on a table with a small box or object to lean the glass against.

CLEAN OFF ANY DUST SPECKS on the back of glass and display surface, then fold the glass into place. Do not force anything-- you'll just shatter the glass. Be patient. 10 minutes here will save you a couple of hours redoing the entire thing.

DO NOT apply pressure at any particular point on the glass-- apply pressure over a large surface to get the adhesive to stick in place. Pressing the entire iPad face-down, gently, on a firm surface that won't scratch is best. A firm rubber matt or cardboard will work. Make sure there is no dirt, grit, or bits of glass on that surface, and make sure your glass is lined up and is seated within the aluminum border before pressing.

I'd say expect about a 50% success rate if you're fairly careful and experienced with this kind of work but don't replace screens regularly (which is my case-- I've done this a few times, but not regularly). Don't rush. Don't tear the ribbon cables. Clean the edge contact surface well. Don't drop your sharp tweezers on the lithium battery 😁 (not kidding).

title: A beautiful, sleek, stylish, powerful machine with so many problems.
text:
I am a year into ownership and felt that it was a good time to put down some thoughts on the year.

The Good:
The computer is one of the nicest pieces of hardware I have ever experienced. Everything on it seems deliberate and precise. The keyboard has a wonderful feel and typing on it is an absolute blast. The trackpad is so nice to the touch and incredibly accurate. The body feel of it is a great matte finish. It is powerful (i7, 1060) enough to do most everything I need it for.

The screen is bright and clear. I find myself doing double takes at the video clarity. I have all the accessories that I thought would be useful. Pairing mice, Xbox controllers, headphones and other Bluetooth accessories is a snap.

The Bad:
Right out of the gate my computer was having blue screens of death (BSOD). I tried reinstalling windows, resetting, taking it to Microsoft to see if they could do anything. They ran their diagnostics on it and everything checked out. Unfortunately, since I purchased it on Amazon through a third-party seller, neither Microsoft or Amazon would replace the unit due to it being purchased through a third-party and the third party seller just said: "take it to Microsoft". Yes, I should have checked whom I was buying it through, but it was not clear as the third party seller was defaulted and the actual Amazon seller was on the other seller's page. Microsoft wound up replacing it with a refurb! 2300 dollars for a month of problems and then a refurb. Awesome! The screen detaching from the keyboard was a bad idea. Mine doesn't set right and sometimes doesn't recognize the keyboard or the graphics card.

Conclusion (TLDR):
Don't buy this unless you are okay with paying this much for something that has common issues with both hardware and software. If you do still want to buy it, make sure you do so through Amazon or Microsoft as third-party sellers won't help at all with the issues you will face. I'm stuck with it, I use it every day. I love it, I wish it had fewer problems.

title: Mic sounds as good as my Rode Videomic and a lot smaller
text:
I have been using a Rode VIdeomic in my vlogs for a while. Loved it but it was big enough that my "dead cat" often was visible in my video. I figured this was worth trying for $20. I can't tell the difference in the sound.

Lots of reviewers said the dead cat cover is useless as it only installs over the mic element. Well it can work just fine. I fed the foam pop cover inside the dead cat with just the opening sticking out. Carefully worked the mic into the opening making sure the foam slid on properly. Then let the dead cat o-ring clamp down on the mic element. Problem solved. I now have a dead cat on the mic that is not loose and doesn't rub on the mic element. I can't believe no one else figured this out. I figured it was worth a try since that is how the dead cat on my Rode mic was installed. Now that you know how it works......"you're welcome"

title: Best TN i've tried to date
text:

Using this on an Nvidia graphics card, G-sync works perfectly with no hiccups, although you'll need to enable it yourself.

I dont have any kind of equipment to test the 0.4ms response time, and every other company out there I doubt that it is actually THAT low. However this is easily the fastest response time monitor i've tried. and thats coming me, who's owned the alienware 240hz, LG 240hz, the PG279Q IPS, as well as a few others. Buttery smooth and is immediately noticable.

Colors are not quite to IPS level, but they are really closing the gap. This defintiely isn't the grainy crap TN panels that plagued the market a few years ago. I'll gladly take the SLIGHTLY worse colors in trade for a much better response time and no risk of backlight bleed/IPS glow with this monitor.

title: Good hardware
text:
I bought the FiiO BTR3K mostly for use paired with a Boltune BA002 transmitter which is connected to my TV. The BTR3K works: it sounds good, maintains a stable bluetooth connection, and allows me to use aptX LL or HD, depending on how I configure the Boltune transmitter.

I have run into two problems so far, neither of which is a big deal for me - but they might be for you:

Although the Android version of the FiiO Control app works fine, the iPhone version of that app didn't work at all for me: it can't recognize that the BTR3K is connected, even though I am able to make calls and play music through the device. This is not really a big deal, since the app doesn't do anything essential - it's just for tweaking some options such as codec preferences.

The other problem is that the BTR3K doesn't work with the microphone in my Apple Earpods: the person on the other end of the call just hears some high-pitched squealing. However, it does work with a Sennheiser wired headset that I have, and the mic built into the BTR3K itself also works well, if I connect regular headphones/earbuds to it.

Bottom line: this works very well as a receiver, but if you want to use it for phone calls on an iPhone you may have (solvable) problems.

title: Excellent system. Works great once you understand it.
text: I couldn't believe that this included "everything I need" for the price, but it does: Dongle which converts "White, Red, Yellow" signals - to USB, in addition to an excellent software package which makes it easy to capture video - and then to *edit* that video: yes, this product includes a good video editor. Once I got out an old VHS tape player, hooked up the wires (OK. I had to have my own "Yellow, White, Red" wires - to come out of the VHS player - then connect to the dongle included in this product), connected the USB to my computer, and fired up the capture / editing software, I was able to start saving off all of the old family videos on VHS. Now they're in digital and I can burn them to DVD or just save them as a digital file anywhere. All of that said, there were a couple of start-up things that I had to learn. The instructions say to carefully download a driver. In my case, I'm running Windows 10 - and Windows 10 already had the driver (or automatically downloaded it), point being that I was able to totally skip that step. Next thing was that the video editor has a feature to "start / stop including this video" - as part of a "multi-cut edit". It's a great feature: after capturing, I can just watch the video on my computer, and click to start excluding - then click again to start including - on and on - until I'm done and I click the "go ahead and edit it all down" button - and it just clips out all of the stuff I wanted to throw away. It's great. My problem was that it was counter-intuitive to me: I kept clicking to "clip this out" but that meant "keep this" and vice versa. Once I understood which way the software worked, it works great.  The only other problems I've had - have to do with getting the correct kind of DVD blanks for my computer's DVD burner, but that has nothing to do with this package or its software. Bottom line: Nobody knows just how long our VHS tapes will last. They're just magnetic dots on tape. They will slowly demagnetize over time. Don't lose your priceless, unique family videos: instead, buy this system and get them into digital, shareable form.  One final remark: Remember that you're taking this video from VHS tape. VHS tape has a kind of grainy resolution that is no fault of this product. If you doubt, then hook your VHS player up to a TV and be reminded of just how BAD our video was - before HD and UHD, and 4K and 8K and..... point being "don't blame this product for VHS-quality video. That's the best that can be done - unless you get some kind of separate video-enhancement software which up-converts". That may exist, but don't expect this very-amazingly-priced product to do that.

title: Exactly what I was looking for
text:
I have been looking for a product exactly like this for several years. I am a business traveler and I have to be on conference calls constantly. These are comfortable and the sound quality for calls is simply fantastic. I enjoy the fact that they have some noise canceling capacity, but do not put you into total isolation the way high end dedicated NC headphones will.

Here was my criteria
1 - Must have a mic boom. These headphones met that criteria. I wanted a mic boom because I've always felt that walking around with a bluetooth device and talking to "nobody" makes you look crazy, especially in airports. These provide a great visual indicator that you're talking on a phone. Bonus: Putting the mic vertical puts your call on mute.

2 - Active noise canceling on the mic. Plantronics provides near perfect clarity, even in noisy environments. I tested these by using a leaf blower in the driveway while talking to my wife over my cell phone. She could hear me clearly and barely heard the blower. I was thrilled to be able to use these in an airport without issue.

3 - Sound quality. These are not up to Sony or Bose quality, but those high end headphones can't touch the call quality of the Plantronics. I really enjoy that they're more than good enough.

4 - Portability. The ear pieces turn flat, but do not hinge down like my Sony headset. They're still flatter and smaller in the case than the Sony's.

5 - Multidevice. I use these with my Galaxy Note 10+ and my Ipad Pro. They switch effortlessly between the two devices without intervention.

I'm giving them a 5/5 on Amazon because they are exactly what I wanted and more. If I was reviewing these for a tech site I'd give them a 9.5/10. The only possible improvements are making the ear pieces modular so you could go from stereo to mono and possibly providing a bit more bass for listening to Spotify. These are fantastic headphones for a business user and weary traveler.

title: Comfortable, durable (and just about perfect with two cheap, simple mods)
text:
I've been using this sling exclusively for more than two years. This is great if you want to carry two cameras. Holds plenty of weight - I carry a Sigma 100-400 mounted on the left side and I barely notice it. Puts all the weight of the cameras on your hips rather than your neck or shoulders.

I love it but how you carry your gear is subject to personal preference. This will work well if you value these criteria: dual-body carry, quick access, weight off your neck.

Two tips/tricks for success with this sling:

1. Mount your cameras left loop and bottom screw. Get a two-pack of camera screw loops. (Something like this - https://www.amazon.com/Zecti-Release-Install-Olympus-Panasonic/dp/B07F592F8M/ref=pd_cp_421_3/143-9441404-3457115.) If you use both the strap loops, the sliders on this sling will constantly be in your way if you use the viewfinder. Mount it left and bottom instead, and you'll be golden.

2. Get a two pack of small carabiners or clips if you plan to be active with this sling. Pass a carabiner through one of the mount loops so you can quickly secure the camera by clipping to your belt loop. This will keep the cameras from swinging if you're running, stooping down a lot, etc.

I've been very happy with this sling. It's reasonably versatile, folds up easily, and is durable. Quality product and a good price.

Jan. 5, 2020 update - This sling is still in near perfect condition after almost three years of heavy use. Clips and straps are tight as the day I bought it. I've been upgrading equipment, getting progressively heavier. The sling handles everything like a champ. Highly recommended. Outstanding value, provided you follow the tips above.

title: Made a critter sprayer, works perfectly
text:
I heard a tapping noise one morning and found several buzzards on my back patio, pecking at the sliding glass doors. After quickly checking my pulse, I realized they weren’t here for me. Wife was not cooking, so… wrong house? Turns out they think there are other buzzards in the mirrored glass. I chased them off, but they kept coming back. And they’re messy.

This PIR switch was just what I needed. I didn’t want to hurt the birds, so I decided to use this PIR switch to build a motion activated sprayer. It has adjustment pots for both sensitivity and duration, and now when critters come onto my porch, they get sprayed with water for about 1 or 2 seconds at a time until they leave.

I love that I can adjust the length of time they get sprayed. Most switches available in 12-24V can’t be adjusted down past 30 seconds, which is way more than I needed. This one goes all the way down to one second, which is just what I needed. You could use this for lighting in a cabinet or safe, and adjust the time to any length you want.

It’s super sensitive, and I’ve seen it chase away everything from squirrels to raccoons to buzzards. But I also like that you could reduce the sensitivity if you only wanted to spray maybe dog, or even mother-in-law-sized things.

This isn’t waterproof by any means, but it was easy to seal from the elements with a little silicone. Mine has been rained on many many times with no problems.

The back pops off easily so you can adjust the pots on the circuit board for sensitivity and duration with a small screwdriver.

Love it, and would order again.

Pros -

+ Adjustable for sensitivity and duration.
+ Highly sensitive – effective on things as small as birds.
+ Can reduce duration to as low as one second, much shorter than almost any other switch available.
+ Perfect for any trigger from 12 to 24V.
+ Flat ends allow use of zip ties, or there are screw holes in tiny side wings.

Cons -

- None.

title: A necessary component for a radio upgrade.
text:
In order to replace my useless, broken Ford Focus factory radio, I had to also purchase a dash kit as you cannot use an aftermarket radio with the factory dash kit. This added A LOT of cost to this endeavor, but I digress. I was looking at 3 different dash kits and of the three, Maestro's brand was the most expensive by far. Additionally, if you wanted to also connect the steering wheel controls and OBDII capabilities you also needed a pricey module sold by Maestro (not included with dash kit).

I could have paid a bit less, but in looking at the kits I preferred the KIT-FOC1 because it removed the 4.3 inch mini screen that Ford had installed and allowed the radio itself to come through higher in the dash kit. The kit also allows you to add 2 USB ports, 1 HDMI port and an AV input plug via the dash kit. Along with this, it makes use of some of the space to give you a little cubby hole you can stuff things into, which the original Focus dash sorely lacked.

I was fortunate to find a seller on Amazon with a pretty big price drop compared to most other sellers. This softened the blow on my wallet for doing this job. The install went fairly well. The kit itself fit into the dash about as well as you can expect it to. If you look at it closely, the edges have a bit of a gap around the kit, but it is not readily noticeable and does not impact the install or use.

The one negative I would give for this kit involves the button for the locks/hazard lights. This piece of the dash feels incredibly cheap and upon installing, the lock portion of the button works fairly well, but the hazard lights can be turned on, but you have to muck with the button a bit to get them to stop. Other than this, the dash kit worked out really well.

title: Light leaks! Quality control issues. Easy fix
text:
I have two of these Leica M to Nikon Z adapters. The first one felt like it was built well and the lens clicked in firmly.
The 2nd one, the lens feels loose and I'm noticing now that there is some rotational play in the mount both at the lens side as well as the body. This is NOT the case when using Nikon's own S lenses on the z mount as they are super firm.
This is an issue because you will feel the lens move if you're turning a stiff focus ring.

Another offender is the light leak. The example picture is 6 second exposure with the lens cap on at f16 (to rule out lens cap leak) so you wont see it this bad normal shooting. However, on a sunny day it will be creeping into your shots affecting it a little.
The solution for the light leak is a rubber o ring 42mm inner diameter, 52mm outer diameter with 5cm width. It removes all light leak.

The lens moving around in the adapter.. no fix there as the tolerances are just not as tight as they need to be.

title: Decent value. Be sure to set to Dolby Digital if using ARC!
text:
Setup is easy. I only plugged in HDMI, so ARC would be the only signal to the soundbar. Fired it up the first time and had no sound. First I thought my cable didn't work with ARC, but I read and discovered any and all HDMI cables work with ARC. I also found that ARC only works with Dolby Digital. My TCL Roku TV was set to auto detect, so you'd think it would recognize the situation of the HDMI/ARC being the only audio out, but it didn't. I had to set it to Dolby Digital and all worked fine after that. I think a new one comes with an HDMI cable, but this renewed one did not. The sub comes pre-paired so all you have to do is plug the power in and turn it on. I do wish there was a way to turn the sub off with a switch, otherwise it's always on. The bubble wrap was taped to the soundbar in one area and left a kinda large sticky residue patch, but it happened to be on the backside so I haven't bothered to clean it off just yet. The remote has woofer +/- buttons but there is no indication of how the sub is set in the range or how many clicks it takes to go from low to high. There is no definition I can find for the difference between the 3 sound settings, ASC, Cinema, or the "bass-blast" one. So just gotta push the buttons and listen. With my TCL TV set to control the soundbar's volume through ARC, a single click changes the volume by 4 out of 100 instead of 1 like the TV normally would. I assume the soundbar's volume just has 25 settings, and 100/25=4, so there you go. The sound could be fuller for 300 watts RMS. I made a 2.1 shelf system in my garage that has 300 watts max and it sounds stronger and bassier than this supposedly more powerful LG 2.1 soundbar. But it does sound way better than the super crappy tiny itty bitty speakers the TV came with. Heaven forbid a TV come with decent speakers these days. Every time I've bought a TV since 2004, the sound gets worse and worse.

Small update: I paired my phone to the bluetooth and played some music. It sounded better than the sound from the TV, so I think the TVs output is just kinda weak.

text:

Some problems i have noted:
-The kit does not come with a case or a lens cap for the front lens. I recommend getting a 67mm lens cap as the front lens scratches easily. there are some scratches on mine, however they seem to be superficial and do not affect picture quality. I have noticed that the other seafrogs listing for this housing does come with a neoprene case.
-The rubber glare reducer does not stay on the housing well, and tends to float around and get in the way. That being said, it is not needed, as I am able to see the camera clearly even at the surface. I took it off entirely after the first 3-4 dives.

I was looking for the USB-C version of this monitor to replace my UltraFine while also being non-mac-specific, but this monitor was not made for macs at all.

The first issue is that it mounts a something called CRP DISABLD and if you unplug it (or if your laptop sleeps) without ejecting it, your Mac will return an improperly ejected error. Asking Amazon Q&A and LG support gave me no support, saying "it's not the monitor!". Well, it is. I have nothing else attached and I've tested this with multiple macs.

The second issue is that you can't control the monitor's volume with your keyboard controls.

The third issue is that LG's support system is terrible and I have no idea how to respond to their reply except by calling someone.

Overall, I do not recommend this monitor if you have a Mac.

title: Overall, very impressed
text:
Ok, so as a consumer I try to stay very unbiased and try to not be brand loyal. So I'll give this review as unbiased as I can. Also, I'll include a summary at the end if you dont want to read my long review. Also, also, I'll be comparing them to airpods in many ways as they were made as a direct competitor.

So I'm going to break this down into materials and design, connectivity, sound, fit, and features.

Design and Materials:
Starting with design, this is subjective of course, but I personally really like how the buds look. Comparing them to the airpods, I think that the more subtle design paired with more colors is really appealing and will draw in more people. That said, airpods have become sort of a meme and their design has become very mainstream. The case is also well designed. It looks better than the airpod floss case, in my opinion, but it isn't as satisfying as the airpod case. That said it is easy to open and looks clean, especially the matte black. Now onto the build quality. The earbuds themselves are very light, but this is okay as you want to basically forget they are in your ear. That said, the buds dont feel cheap. The materials are very nice and they feel good in hand, and head. The case is a similar story. Light but substantial enough that it feels well made. Like I said, I also love the matte finish on the case.

Connectivity:
So much like the airpods, all you have to do, on Samsung Phones, is open the case and after a moment the buds pop up and boom, your connected. This remains the same after you first connect, just open the case and by the time their in your ears, you're connected. The range is okay. If you go more than about 15 feet, give or take, they start to break out. But if you have your phone on you, you're good. I also havent really had any stuttering or anything like that, just clear audio if you're in range.

Sound:
So this is possibly the most important category. Now I dont pretend to be an audiophile but I have listened and own a fair number of headphones. So with a package this small, I kept my expectations low. But when I got the buds, I was actually pleasantly surprised by the sound. Songs like Hotel California are really well balanced. Vocals are really clear and highs are also clear and clean. However, where the buds lack heavily is in bass. Rockstar sounds alright but if you need crazy bass, fully wireless earbuds are not for you. I mean, the driver is really small so you cant really expect earth shattering bass. But I know kany people love their bass, as i do too, and you may miss it with these. However, that isn't what these are for. The galaxy buds are made to be convenient, small earbuds, and as a result, audio suffers. That said, I think the audio will be very good for most people, as long as you can live without some bass. Again vocals are great and highs are clear and crisp.

Fit:
So possibly the best feature that the buds have that the airpods dont is the fit. This is because you get three different wing tips and ear tips in the box. This means that most people will be able to find a combination that fits them well and comfortably. Contrast that with the airpods which dont come with anything and the either fit or they dont. Another important difference between these and airpods in the in ear design. This means you get very good sound isolation which you will either like or not like. However, Samsung has included an ambient sound feature which works pretty well. The fit overall is superb, though. Once you get the right ear tips, you honestly forget that they are in your ear. They are also very good for working out because of how small they are and how well they fit, I mean, they wont come out of your ear, they go in your ear very well. Again, this is a mixes bag with airpods as if they dont fit you, they can easily fall out.

Features:
Wrapping up this review is features, and there are quite a few. So starting with controls, you have a touch capacitive panel on each earbud. The controls work well but I'm not a huge fan of the implementation. A single press only play pauses, a double press only skips, etc. The only customization you have is with the long hold. You can either have that trigger a voice assistant, volume or toggle ambient noise. I wish you could go deeper into controls and, for example, have play pause on the right with a single press, skip on the left with a single press, volume up and down by holding down on left and right, and ambient noise as a double tap. And who knows, software may change and make this possible. Another thing I dont really like is that, unlike the airpods, you cant take one bud out to pause the music and put it back in to resume it. Again, this could change with software. Speaking of software, the galaxy wearables app has a decent amount of customization, better than apple at least, and I hope to see Samsung continue to improve it. One thing that you can use with the app is the ambient noise toggle. I actually really like this feature and it works pretty well. The microphones do a pretty good job of amplifying voices and it works at a good distance too. The fact that they can charge wirelessly is also a big plus, especially for Galaxy S10 users with the reverse wireless charging. Other small features are USB-C, decent battery life, good quick charging (1.5 hours from 15 minutes of charging) and the overall convenience and size of the package.

So overall, the Galaxy Buds are made very well and look quite nice too. The pairing process is very solid, especially on Samsung and the range is good for mose people. The sound quality is pretty standard for this price range and lacks on bass but has clear mids and vocals as well as crisp clean highs. The customizability of the fit is amazing and means that the buds will fit most people. Finally, the buds' controls could be better but they have plenty of other great features like wireless charging. Overall, a very solid package and for $130, what are you waiting for?

title: Good Idea, But Still Needs Some Improvement.
text:
I bought this keyboard for my new iPad 11. The keyboard comes in three parts, the canvas case with the rubber frame to hold the iPad, the rubber keyboard cover and the detachable keyboard.

The canvas case is heavy duty canvas, durable. The rubber casing that holds the iPad in place is flexible and durable, making it easy to put the iPad in and take the iPad out. It doesn’t have a place to put the Apple pen that I can see, but it definitely provides protection on all four sides of the iPad including the back. The case is held shut by a magnetic flap that seems to work well. When using, the iPad fits atop of small grooves in the lower part of the casing. These are there to hold the iPad in place when you are using. There are three grooves to adjust the iPad at different angles. I haven’t had any issues with the iPad staying in place.

The keyboard is plastic with the keys bright lit red when in use. Love the backlit color. You do have to be a bit careful as the keys can be easily removed from the keyboard if hit wrong. I tried removing the rubber cover and my fingernail hit the key wrong and off popped the letter piece. It snapped back into place pretty easy, but definitely had my heart pumping when it popped off. The keys are fitted atop the keyboard and have opening around the keys, but the rubber keyboard covers seems to provide protection quite well. Pairing was a bit difficult. It took several tries before I could get it to pair and I’m finding that I am having issues with getting the keyboard to consistently stay paired. I turn the keyboard on and I have to keep manually having to go into the settings to connect it, rather than it connecting automatically when turning the keyboard on. Often, after first turning on the keypad, the cursor will move down the page without touching the keys or there will be delayed typing. You’ll type a few words and they appear a few seconds later, if they appear at all. I am finding that the keyboard doesn’t always respond at the time I type.

The keyboard doesn’t hold the charge for long, so I have to charge it more than I’d like. The cord provided is short, so unless you are really close to the receptacle and have a ledge or something to put the keyboard on, you have to leave it close to the floor or on a kitchen counter. There was no AC adaptor supplied with this keyboard, so unless you have your own adaptor, the only option to charge is through the back of a computer, but remember the cable is short, there’s no possibility of using it while it charges.

This vendor contacted me long before I received the keyboard, so they are really responsive. That is definitely a plus. They have kept in contact to ensure that I was pleased with the keyboard. I don’t often find this the case with most vendors, so this is refreshing to see a company stand by their product.

title: So far great, specific game experiences reviewed
text:
I am coming up from a bad experience with an MSI-AMD 460. I will never buy another MSI product again, it died after 18 months of very light use, and MSI didn't pay the mail it rebate and customer service ignored me.

- Shipping
I do not have prime. It still came in 4 days despite the 10 day estimate.

- Call of duty online at 60fps and 1440p.

It went so smooth on default settings I maxxed out several subsettings, still nice and smooth.

There is a percentage slider on the graphics options. I turned it up to the 200% max and it lagged horribly, went down to 130% and the picture is crisper than 100% setting and still smooth. At 150% picture was even better, but the slight lag was still too much. So 130% when the default is 100% was the best setting.

Wii Dolphin emulation.

The old MSI-AMD 460 just could not handle Wii emulation at all. Completely choppy and laggy and unplayable. RX2060 not only handles it at 1440p at full settings, but the "fast forward" key plays the game at 2.5 speed and it is still quite smooth.

Noise and Fit in My Mid Tower
While bigger than most graphics card, it fit just fine in my very standard size midtower case, and there is still room for 2 more PCI cards.

Noise: did not notice any noise at all, the quiet hum of my ac more than completely blocked it. No noise at all with AC off watching movies.

If this is your first high end card: you need to plug it into the power supply as well as the PCI slot! I was so confused why it wasn't working at first, all my previous cards got enough power from the PCI slot.

My only negative: Nvidia demands registration and e-mail in order to even download the driver, and tries to get you to install a lot of bloatware on top of the 500meg driver. This is becoming common, doesn't mean it isn't obnoxious.

My PC itself is a 2014 model with a x77 motherboard and Win7. No problems at all with this late 2019 GPU.

When you are thinking about the benefits of upgrading, keep in mind this new card is very power efficient, less money on your electric bill, and creates less heat you need to AC away. $10 a year saved on electricity for five years isn't nothing!

title: Awesome Replacement for 3700X Stock Cooler
text:
I've been running a Ryzen 7 3700X with the stock Wraith Prism cooler. It was doing an okay job. Most of the time my max running temps were in the upper 60's or low 70's, with the occasional split-second spikes up to high 70's or even low 80's while gaming. So the stock cooler was doing well enough, and I'm not OC'ing my CPU.

But the smaller fan of the cooler did generate more noise than I cared for, so I decided to try out this air cooler. I've always admired the Noctua products for a while, but I never bought them because of the brown and tan color scheme. When I saw this all black edition, I decided it was worth a try. Because I'm not OC'ing, I didn't feel the need to go with a twin-tower design, and this NH-U12S had gotten some great reviews.

It arrived today (next-day shipping FTW!) and it was literally the fastest and easiest cooler install I've ever experienced (I've previously installed a total of 2 air coolers and 2 AIO coolers in previous systems). For the AM4 boards, the required hardware was minimal--two brackets, 4 spacers, and 4 screws. That was it since it utilizes your existing backplate. I love that it comes with additional fan clips and rubber mounts for adding a second fan if I want. But based on the current temps, I don't think that'll be necessary.

Now my system runs around 7-10 degrees cooler. Cinebench R20 multicore maxed out my temp at 68C (with ambient temp of around 25C), which I think is pretty darn good, and even those infamous Ryzen CPU temperature spikes are only popping up to very low 70's. I couldn't be happier, as I didn't expect significantly better performance--I just wanted it to run quieter.

I definitely recommend this for anyone looking to replace their stock cooler for a Ryzen 3000 chip.

title: Great little antenna, but 120 mi. range is exaggerated.
text:
Impressive.
I just acquired a settop box for digital OTA conversion. The antenna that came with the box was decent, but not great. While it picked up almost all the channels available in my area, several of the lower band channels came in with heavy pixalation and intermittent freezing. On occasion, I received the "No Signal" notification when tuning in to them.
I swapped the panel antenna with this post antenna, and was immediately amazed! NONE of the channels available over the air were diminished, and NONE of the channels freeze or experience pixelation. I do experienct intermittent drop in signal, but this is not unique to any antenna. On every channel, sound is well in sync, and clear. Setup was identical to most antennae of this type, and it was imply a matter of swapping the connection with my old antenna with this one. The longest broadcast in my area is about 55 miles away, and this one picked it up with no issue. There are a number of air broadcasts inside of 120 miles, but none of them were picked up. I have to deduct a star for this, since the claim of 60-120 miles was not substantiated with physical reality. As impressive as this little post antenna may be, a manufacturer should not make claims that are not substantiated by execution. Looking at a map of broadcast availability, there are seven channels that can reasonably be expected to be found by this antenna that were not. I'm not that disappointed, since those are in areas that I have little interest in viewing.
I'll offer four stars for performance. Unsubstantiated claims are a disappointment, for me. You can reasonably expect about a seventy mile limitation in actual performance.

title: Amazing! The description leaves out a lot of good stuff
text:
I just got it up and running and the software customized a bit to fit my own preferences. Amazing! There is a bit of tech knowledge required but the instructions at the ThingPulse website are pretty complete. I built and programmed mine to use it specifically as a weather display but as a display for other projects, it's very cool and the weather station software can serve as a starting point for lots of other projects.

It's also not just the main display you see in the product photo. The main display has a carousel display band of data that animates through the forecasts for the coming days. Tap the display and you get current conditions. Tap it again and it does tabular forecasts for a few taps. Again and you get a machine status page. This thing packs a lot of information into a small package and is very attractive doing it.

The daughterboard for the Wemos D1 Mini Pro is bigger than the one illustrated at the ThingPulse website. The kit I received had a daughterboard the same size as the TFT display with the same spacing mounting holes.

There were a few libraries I had to manually load that aren't called out in the instructions but the Arduino compiler will call out the header files it doesn't know and you just knock them down one by one and add them.

One other thing is my development environment is running under Linux Mint 19.1 and I didn't need the Winchiphead CH340x / CH341x com port drivers. Not a fan of loading drivers into Linux from untrusted sources. Having the capability already there was nice. Mint could talk to the board just fine once I installed the Boards Manager library for the ESP8266.

I removed the SD card socket and built mine low profile to fit it into a slimmer case but you don't have to if you want to build it full height. All the parts needed are supplied build full height but I used two layers of double-stick foam tape stacked to space up the non-connector end of the display. It's more secure and sturdier than just having the connections at one end cantilever the board out.

I'm just going to make a nice box to put it in and set it out to start using it.

If you have a bit of tech/programming familiarity this is a heck of a kit. The display is a bit small but that will make for a much less obtrusive weather station. Cheap for the price.

title: Unmatched quality and design and performance.
text:
Very nice antenna quality the way they used to be years ago.
5/8 wave over 5/8 wave, is an old design that works and performs very well. Using it as a base antenna with a radial kit.
Trimmed the base rod slightly to get a perfect SWR 1:1
Hears and talks as good as a full size 5/8 wave.
Browning makes very nice antennas at a very reasonable price.
UPDATE:
Purchase a 2nd one for use on my VW.
Again, got a perfect matching SWR.
Got an NMO magnet mount from browning have installed it to the rear just before the hatch.
Now this antenna has quite a bit more wind load at higher speeds due to the size of the rod and the matching center load.. and I would recommend getting the larger 5 1/2 in magnet base as they'll be considerable more wind resistance at higher speeds and the smaller mag bases will probably fail.
Antennas that are matched for a specific band perform much better, and over the years I've never found a dual band antenna that didn't struggle with the SWR accordance to its ground plane a car can provide.
There is no perfect ground scenario you can provide that won't aggravate a dual band antenna.
But you dual banders would probably argue with me till the cows came home but they'd all be emptied of their milk at sunset before I opened the gate.
It's not a perfect world out there when it comes to radios and antennas and there's always challenges to overcome and that's the beauty of it as you'll never be fulfilled with boredom.

title: These babies are AWESOME
text: My wife and I like totally different kinds of TV. I like content with a lot of action that usually means lots of noise. title: Flimsy
text:
Used this to install a Samsung sound bar under a 65" Samsung TV. Not sure if this can really be used properly with a 65" TV and an average size sound bar. The instructions are very confusing as they give several different mounting options but no explanation of when to use which. I ended up just using the two longer bars (at an approximate 45 degree angle) because the shorter ones weren't sufficiently long if the longer ones were mounted 90 degrees vertically. This method of install is shown as an option in the manual. The problem is that you can only attach the TV end of the bracket to one VESA hole instead of the preferred two (each). With the weight of the sound bar and attaching to the back of the sound bar, it causes the bars to flex and the sound bar ends up pointing slightly downward. It also makes it very difficult to center the sound bar under the TV and get it parallel to the TV (one side protrudes more than the other).
While these may work in most scenarios, I think they are too small to be used properly with a 65" TV. Each of the longer brackets should be firmly attached to both VESA holes and the smaller brackets should extend outward from the larger ones (as they show in their picture). This would provide more stability and rigidity, but his is impossible with a 65" TV, the brackets just aren't long enough. I'm still not convinced that the smaller brackets could sufficiently hold the weight of an average sound bar without bowing and having the sound bar tilting slightly downward.
Anyway, not too many affordable options out there and you definitely get what you pay for with this one=not much.

title: Brilliant receiver
text:
After adding an HDR projector, I realized that my crazy daisy chain of HDMI workarounds on my Logitech Z906 wasn't gonna cut it anymore.

Bought the AVR-S740H. Re-connected all the Logitech's speaker leads to the receiver's. Connected a 3.5mm to RCA adapter for the subwoofer. Now the Z906 only deals with subwoofer output from the receiver, and the receiver handles the rest of my audio.

I've got 4 HDMI devices, and they work like a charm. This includes an Apple TV 4K, which passes 60hz 4K HDR to my BenQ HT5550 projector just fine, and an X9S, which sends both 4K HDR and 3D to my projector, again with no problem. Windows 10 doesn't seem to "detect" a full 60hz on 4K output, but my Nvidia management software detects it just fine and I can get 4K output from my PC, through the receiver, to the projector, again, just fine.

Cons - Any menu stuff does not get "composited" onto my screen. That is, if I want to change settings on the receiver, I basically have to pause whatever I'm watching. Only 5 HDMI inputs on the back and 1 on the front, if that's a concern for you.

Pros - Feeds my speakers fine, HDMI switching is fast, 100% compatibility across all my stuff, and cuts down dramatically on my cables. For about two-fiddy, the price is great.

title: Fantastic left-handed case
text:
I've been looking forward to this case for a long time. My computer sits to the left of the monitor, which means that the majority of cases won't have a window on the right side and even if they did all you would see is the backside of the motherboard.

So the trick is finding a case in which the motherboard is either inverted, lying flat, or standing on edge. Enter the Silverstone RL08. The RL08 mounts the motherboard inverted (compared to standard), which means the pcie slots are towards the top, and the CPU towards the bottom (the ports still go out the rear of the case). It also comes with a right-side tinted TG side panel that showcases your components.

Supposedly the inverted-arrangement provides for better heat management, and although I didn't perform any testing to verify this claim, it sounds like it should work - but the bigger factor is probably what components you have and how you set up your fans. I have 240mm AIO watercooler on the CPU, which is mounted to the front of the case as an intake. I also have a 120mm AIO watercooled graphics card which is mounted on top as an additional intake. I then have a single 120mm fan on the rear of the case as an exhaust.

I had to take a star off the final score, due to some minor issues:

Even with an ITX motherboard, it was difficult to fit all my components in. The case supports up to an mATX-sized motherboard, but if you have multiple graphics cards in there you're either A) not going to mount any fans to the top or B) going to hit the 5.25" drive cage.

The case also supports full-sized ATX PSUs, but it's an extremely tight fight to put in a PSU, the 3.5" drive cage, and have a front-mounted radiator. Luckily I have modular cables for the PSU so I was able to fit everything in the small gap between it and the drive cage.

The case is really well constructed, looks fantastic, and comes with many high-quality touches you'd expect from a case at this price point.

My only (minor) recommendations for v2 of this case would be:
1. Full mounting rail for the 3.5" drive cage to allow for more space between it and the PSU
2. Make the 5.25" drive cage removable to support multiple long graphics cards
3. Recessed mounting rails for the top fans so that the magnetic filter sits flat when domed screws are used
4. Captive thumbscrews!

title: Good but rough around the edges
text: So first off let me say I wish I could have given this 3.5 stars but that's not an option and I'm hoping people read this before purchasing. I bought this strap for my Sony A7Riii after seeing many glowing youtube reviews on the strap.  Overall the build quality seems good but in one way almost too good because the material is not supple.  As you can see in one of my photos the stiffness of the strapping tends to open up large loops that tend to make the strap unwieldy at times. Another small issue is that the locks also tend to slide with a heavy lens while walking along, they look like aluminum but they may be a plastic material.  Once wearing the strap though I find it very comfortable, it's just folding it up and stowing it in my bag I really dislike.  Recently they had a recall on the anchoring buttons so I went online to get the replacements.  It took a long while to get them and when they did send them (hard to believe but I scanned the slip from the post office), they sent them with insufficient postage so I had to go to the post office and pick up my package and pay what was owed, about 5 dollars. No huge deal, I paid it but I feel the company is likely having some growing pains or disorganization, still I like that they are developing innovative products.  So, one caveat of the new anchors at least on my  A7Riii is that the material part no longer fits through the eyelets without using these metal clip rings.  Not only do I feel the metal clips may not be super strong but in the wind if you're doing video they rattle around and make noise, not that I use the onboard mic often but it's clearly audible if you do.  I thought of cutting one of the strings on the buttons so it'd be a single strand and then knotting the end but I'm not sure the material would hold a knot safely.

title: Asus does not stand behind their products anymore!
text:
I made the mistake of buying this board from Newegg last month as they were one of the few retailers that had them in stock. It has been a disaster. The board doesn't work right, the 2.5 gbs port is dead out of the box, the bios ezflash cannot connect to a server to update, it won't sleep nor will it restart when windows commands it to do so. My board didn't even come with a chipset fan cover.

Many times I have to hit the power button multiple times in order to get it to post. I contacted Asus and they won't replace it with a new board even though I purchased this board new in the box expecting a fully functional product. They are offering me a used board as a replacement, you know, a refurb that someone else had problems with that they rma'd back.

Don't buy into a headache like this and go get a Gigabyte motherboard instead! I will never buy another Asus product because of how they've done me with this board. Look at the dialog I had with them at Newegg.

Pros:
Pretty to look at.
Has WiFi 6
Lots of sata and usb ports

Cons:
Doesn't always boot when I push the power button forcing me to power off then on again
Doesn't always restart when windows tells it to.
The reset button doesn't work.
Only two m.2 slots.
My board doesn't have a chipset fan cover!!!
Doesn't recognize that an AIO is plugged onto the AIO header forcing a post stop since no CPU fan is present.
Expensive!

Overall Review:
I've run Asus boards with all of my builds for many years now so it was natural that I used one for my 3900X. I regret buying this board over the Gigabyte model, especially at this price point, as the bios is immature and the board doesn't perform consistently. I even updated the latest bios, 1201, immediately after installing it which hasn't help matters any.

When I hit my power button I expect for it to post and boot into Windows but this board has other ideas. When I hit my reset button I expect for the board to immediately reset and begin posting but not this board forcing me to hold down the power button to stop it.

I also run an EVGA 360 AIO plugged to the AIO header and the bios will halt during post forcing you to run through the menu and tell it to discard the settings so it will continue to post. I got tired of this and moved a case fan to the CPU header, the one in the middle, so the board would stop doing that. How sorry is that? In a world where people run AIO's instead of traditional air coolers the bios should be smart enough to know the different and continue posting.

My board doesn't even have a chipset fan cover! I tried creating an rma so I could get one and their system says that there's already an rma for this board and I bought it new. Asus really dropped the ball with this board and I cannot recommend this board and suggest that you look elsewhere, especially at this price point. I wish that I"d went with Gigabyte this time. Do yourself a favor and DO NOT BUY THIS BOARD!!!!! Next time I'll start by looking at Gigabyte and AsRock boards!

ASUS Response:Dear Gregory P,

It's unfortunate to hear you're not completely satisfied with your motherboard. Please make sure your front panel connectors are in their correct orientation, mixing positive and negative can leave the function inoperable. You can set your "CPU Fan Speed" to ignore under "Monitor" in BIOS to avoid any further error messages regarding the CPU fan header. If the issues persist, feel free to contact me if you have any technical or general questions. You can reach me at cl-adrian@asus.com. Your case for reference is N200103255.

Thank you for choosing ASUS!

Best Regards,
Adrian
ASUS Customer Loyalty – US Support

title: A good edition to your Ring security needs
text:
This is obviously a very specific product that is only used for Ring devices. This does only a few things. It extends your WiFi to other Ring products and sends notifications for said products.

I purchased this to enhance my WiFi for the Ring 2 Video doorbell. Ring has a spectrum of WiFi strength ranging from -0 to -99, -99 being the worst signal and -0 being the best. My WiFi is in the back of the house so my original WiFi strength was -63. I thought by adding this chime to the setup would boost the signal enough to get a better sound and video quality. While it did boost WiFi strength to -46 (after testing out different outlets) it didn’t much improve the doorbell. Albeit the distance between my doorbell and WiFi was cut in half by the chime addition.

Like the Ring, the chime was easy to setup. Less than five minutes using the Ring app. It can be custom controlled meaning you can use it solely for extending WiFi range, or notifications for movement or actual rings, or both.

The chime only takes up one outlet and provides plenty of space for the other outlet if you plug it into the top.

So, with a little bit of time finding the sweet spot in your house to extend the WiFi, the chime does a decent job boosting that signal.

If I get any more Ring security devices I’ll be adding the efficacy of this chime in a later update.

I give this product four stars because it does what it says it’s going to do and does so fairly well. Normally I post that if I’m looking for something in the future I wouldn’t do much more research into other products while giving a four star review; however, because this product is Ring specific I’ll be required to purchase this item again.

title: Signal strength is very good, but not great.
text: I purchased this wifi router to replace my aging (8-yr old) EA6300 dual band wifi router.  Now that my household streams TV via PC or Roku devices, I wanted something that was more robust for streaming.  I was also hoping for a sizable boost in strength, as this product is advertised to cover a 2,000 sq ft household.  My home is under 1,300 sq ft.  While the signal strength is slightly better, it's nowhere near what I had hoped for.  That's likely due to the placement of the router and the structural elements around it.  Short of upgrading to a "mesh" system, which is considerably more expensive and would require running Ethernet cables through walls to really take advantage mesh network features, it's likely the best I can do given the current state of technology. The set up and interface is similar to the EA6300, with the exception of the band steering, dfs, vlan, and airtime fairness options.  While I like the band steering feature, I would have preferred greater control over the channels used for each band.  Unfortunately, to take advantage of the band steering feature, you must allow the router to "automatically" chooses the channel for each band.  Interference from my neighbors' wireless access points limit the amount of channels that work in my home, and the router has a habit of choosing less than optimum channels.  Of course, you can opt-out of the band steering and designate the channels for all three bands, but now you have to connect to multiple bands manually.  The band steering works more like a mesh system, which IMHO, is much more convenient.  Life seems to be full of these compromises, doesn't it?
